Observed 2026-09-30 via authenticated GitHub API reads of beamfall/corvint main. Public organization repository is eligible; main ruleset 23699808 requires go-product, ci-control-plane, doc-gates and allows merge commits, but has no merge_queue rule. Published ci.yml only triggers pull_request and push(main). Published ci-control-plane.yml accepts only workflow_run.event == pull_request and posts status on PR head SHA. Owner approval remains required for enablement and live merges. Owner clarified that the requirement is test adequacy over combined queued changes, not just queue admission. The reported live observation plus exact native branch confirms this behavior; retain a runnable isolated regression in the owning repair.

This is recovery, not a durable fix. No SID revival, direct claim edits, fake failure transition, shortened fence, dummy owner or fabricated receipt is acceptable.

acceptanceCriteria: Done looks like: `ledger/go-test` reachable on both branches (drop it from `.PHONY` or give the off branch its own recipe) plus a regression asserting the ledger-off gate command list contains `go test ... ./...`, and no gate step that can resolve to "nothing to be done" without the receipt saying so.
body:
Migrated from docs/agent-memory/bugs.md (entry dated 2026-09-22).

`Makefile:21` lists `ledger/go-test` in `.PHONY`, and the only `ledger/go-test` recipe lives on the ledger-on branch of the `ifeq ($(CORVINT_GATE_LEDGER),off)` block (`Makefile:51-60`). GNU make does not search pattern rules for a phony target, so with the ledger off `ledger/go-test` matches no rule and make reports `Nothing to be done for 'ledger/go-test'` — the whole-tree `go test -p 1 -timeout 30m -count=1 ./...` step is dropped while `gate` still exits 0. Reproduce: `env CORVINT_GATE_LEDGER=off make -n ledger/go-test`. Only the ledger-off path is affected — the default ledger path runs the suite through its own partition. Observed at `main` (cd9fec9) and at 82a113a; it voided the 0.6.0 candidate's recorded full-gate receipt, which passed in 4m13s without running any Go test. Done looks like: `ledger/go-test` reachable on both branches (drop it from `.PHONY` or give the off branch its own recipe) plus a regression asserting the ledger-off gate command list contains `go test ... ./...`, and no gate step that can resolve to "nothing to be done" without the receipt saying so.
title: gate: `CORVINT_GATE_LEDGER=off make gate` silently skips `go test ./...`

Migrated from docs/agent-memory/tests.md (entry dated 2026-09-22).

`internal/trace.TestStableMetadataIncludesChangeTime` (`metadata_unix_test.go:31`) chmods 0600→0400→0600, `internal/authoritystore` `PLE-V0-003 configuration witness detects restored bytes` (`repository_metadata_test.go:33`) rewrites identical bytes then `Chtimes` the mtime back, and `internal/cem/gitauth.TestAuthorityBindingRejectsObservedNamespaceAndModeDrift/restored_modification_time` (`authority_binding_test.go:187`) does the same for an authority binding; all three then require `Ctim` to differ. Under a Linux container on ext4 at 82a113a all three FAIL ("ctime-only metadata change accepted", "restored content/mtime hid change time", "observed drift accepted") because the operations land inside one coarse ctime tick; all three PASS on Darwin/APFS. The implementations (`metadata_linux.go`, `metadata_darwin.go`) are correct — the assertion is clock-granularity dependent. Done looks like: each of the three loops or waits until `Ctim` actually advances before asserting (and `t.Skip`s if it never does), so the result does not depend on host filesystem timestamp resolution. Note the underlying product limitation the tests were written for: a restore completed within one ctime tick is genuinely invisible to the witness.
title: trace + authoritystore + gitauth: three ctime witness tests assume ctime advances between adjacent syscalls

body:
Migrated from docs/agent-memory/ideas.md (entry dated 2026-09-19); widened by the owner on 2026-10-11.

Original recommendation (owner-accepted): `make gate-affected` (local) and `tools/corvint-pr-tests` (CI) plan the same selection through different drivers. A single runner would take a base, plan through `corvint affected`, select, run, and fall back to the full suite the same way on a laptop and a hosted runner, with CI adding only the trusted-pin admission.

Widened scope (2026-10-11): Corvint calls the test runners itself through registered per-runner adapters that receive only the selected targets and use the runner's native target filter, so each session builds only what its tests need (Go first; cargo, swift, dotnet, gradle and Playwright each need their own adapter qualification). Sharding becomes selection-aware: the default keeps the AFP-V0-022 complete-universe partition intersected with the run set; an experimental balanced placement partitions the run set itself so narrowed runs use every shard, with a `verify-shards` fan-in that proves exactly-once coverage. Every run writes a bounded `corvint-test-run/0` receipt.

Spec: docs/specs/session-test-runner-v0.md (STR-V0-001..016, proposed). Qualification is tied to the current driver's identity, so the call sites move only after the STR-V0-013 parity report, and the CI switch needs AFP-V0-016 consent and a new AFP-V0-030 forward epoch. AFP-V0-028..030 admission and the AFP-V0-029 shadow bar are unchanged. Balanced placement promotion and non-Go adapters are separate follow-ups, not required to close this ticket.
title: test runner: one `corvint test` that selects from the diff, builds only what is needed, shards, and falls back alike locally and in CI

body:
Filed on 2026-09-22 from a review of https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate (head d277088, 2026-09-22).

Corvint has no threat model document. Only four specs mention threats in passing (`docs/specs/test-claim-qualification-v0.md`, `docs/specs/mcp-test-validity-profile-v0.md`, `docs/specs/local-observability-dashboard-v0.md`, decision 0320). The product invariants that are security-relevant (secret-screened learning, tainted sources never satisfying a basis in V1-0090, read commands never mutating, no network on the default path) are stated in AGENTS.md and scattered specs but never enumerated as threats with a named mitigating invariant and a priority.

Substrate keeps a prose threat model (`docs/threat-model.md`) whose priority table has one row per threat: id, priority, threat, mitigating invariant, suggested concrete mitigations, notes. `hack/export-threats.py` exports the table to `docs/threats.json` and `hack/verify/threats.sh` fails when the JSON drifts from the Markdown. The invariant column is the useful part: each row names a property that, if held, removes the threat, rather than a specific fix.

Proposal: add `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` with that table shape for Corvint's own boundaries (local repository data as untrusted input, provider records, learned traces, host adapters, the optional console, the MCP surface), a generated `docs/threats.json`, and a `threats-check` step in GATE_STEPS next to `decision-numbers-check`. Each row should cite the spec requirement ID that carries its invariant so `docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv` and the registry cannot disagree silently. The JSON is the natural input for the security-review skill.
title: docs: machine-readable threat registry with a drift gate

acceptanceCriteria: `.golangci.yaml` with the standard preset plus misspell exists, every exclusion carries a reason, and a `golangci-lint-check` GATE_STEPS entry runs it with a pinned tool version.

`make gate` passes on the commit that introduces both steps, either clean or against a recorded ratchet count that a later run may only lower.
body:
Filed on 2026-09-22 from a review of https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate (head d277088, 2026-09-22).

The Corvint gate runs `go vet`, `cross-vet` and `check-go-format`, and nothing else over Go or shell source: no staticcheck, no misspell, no shellcheck. Nine scripts under `script/` carry `# shellcheck disable=` comments as if a shellcheck gate existed, but none is wired into `GATE_STEPS` or `.github/workflows/`.

Substrate's `.golangci.yaml` is a reasonable starting template: golangci-lint v2 `default: standard` (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused) plus `misspell` with `locale: US`, every exclusion carrying a one-line reason, QF quickfix rules suppressed, generated paths excluded, `errcheck` off in `_test.go`. `hack/verify/shellcheck.sh` and `hack/verify/golangci-lint.sh` are each one short script.

Caveat: the first run will surface a backlog across a codebase this size. Scope the ticket as: add the config and the two GATE_STEPS entries, pin the tool version the way `check-host-package-versions` pins others, and either clean the findings or record a ratchet count the way `script/diagnostic-coverage.count` does, so the gate is green on the first commit and only forbids regression. The tool must be an offline, pinned binary; the default local product cannot grow a network dependency (invariant 7).
title: gate: standard-preset golangci-lint and shellcheck steps

Owning spec: docs/specs/task-context-packet-v0.md; evaluation contract: docs/specs/retrieval-eval-comparability-v0.md.

body: Filed 2026-09-23 from the owner's request that Corvint support JetBrains, made while reviewing JetBrains Air (jetbrains.com/air). Invariant 7 (AGENTS.md) holds: no hosted service, UI, daemon or network dependency on the local path. Scope under decision 0373: a JetBrains host is a companion FALLBACK row, never a Core claim, because every JetBrains agent surface reaches external tools only through MCP. Junie (IDE plugin and Junie CLI) reads `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` in the project and `~/.junie/mcp/mcp.json` for the user, with the `mcpServers` shape {command,args,env} for stdio servers (junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli-mcp-configuration.html, junie-plugin-mcp-settings.html); Junie has no hook or lifecycle support, so no native lifecycle adapter and therefore no FULL tuple is possible today (agent-harness-integration-v0: FULL needs a shipped, tested native adapter). JetBrains AI Assistant configures MCP servers under Settings | Tools | AI Assistant | MCP with the same `mcpServers` JSON and stdio/Streamable HTTP/SSE transports (jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/mcp.html). JetBrains Air runs Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie plus custom ACP agents from `~/.jetbrains/acp.json`; Corvint is not an agent, so ACP is not the integration point, and Air agents receive MCP servers through the IDE/Air MCP settings (jetbrains.com/help/air/select-agents-and-models.html, jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/acp.html). Guidance reaches Junie through `.junie/AGENTS.md` (highest precedence) or the root AGENTS.md combined with the playbook (junie.jetbrains.com/docs/guidelines-and-memory.html). Deliverable: `integrations/jetbrains/` with (a) a project-scope `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` example and an AI Assistant MCP settings example that launch `corvint-mcp` over stdio against the repository, (b) an AGENTS.md guidance snippet telling the agent to call the Corvint task-context and `cem report` tools before editing and to treat their output as untrusted data, (c) a README that states the FALLBACK label, the reasons (MCP-only, no hooks, no IDE plugin), and the degradations that stay open, and (d) a new `(jetbrains-junie, mcp, <Junie version>, <corvint-mcp version>, macOS)` entry in integrations/compatibility.json with hostVersionEvidence recorded from an actual Junie or AI Assistant session on a Core platform. Depends on V1-0191 because the row is meaningless while `mcp-server-unavailable` is a global degradation. Non-goals: a Kotlin IDE plugin (EXTENSION-ECOSYSTEM.md row 8 keeps it behind the deferred VS Code editor projection contract, vscode-extension-v0.md), an ACP server, any Air cloud integration, and any Core or FULL claim; broadening to Core needs an owner amendment of corvint-1.0-product-and-release-v1.md and decision 0373.
title: hosts: support JetBrains (Junie, AI Assistant, Air) as a companion FALLBACK host over `corvint-mcp`

acceptanceCriteria: corvint-tasks records a policy change through an OWNER or OPERATOR mutation with its own receipt, or the owner records a decision naming another route for the release-checklist gate.
The corvint store's release-checklist gate runs `script/release-checklist --pre-promotion` (or the decided replacement) and `corvint-tasks receipt audit` stays OK afterwards.
`corvint-tasks release readiness` on a candidate with every other gate attested reports gate:release-checklist from a real attestation, not as structurally missing.
body: Filed 2026-09-23. PR #117 (V1-0189) changed the release-checklist gate argv in .taskman/policy.json to `script/release-checklist --pre-promotion`. corvint-tasks treats that file as a projection of the journal, and its transaction model writes intent/policy.json only in the INIT operation (corvint-tasks internal/transaction/model.go), so the edit could not be adopted: every store read and mutation refused with INTENT_DIVERGED on intent/policy.json until the projection was restored to the journal bytes (sha256 501ae5be...). The corvint-tasks SPEC says policy changes are OWNER/OPERATOR mutations, but no such verb is implemented. Until one exists, the release-checklist gate still runs plain `script/release-checklist`, which cannot exit 0 at any commit (V1-0189 BUILD-LOG entry), so gate:release-checklist can never be attested and every release candidate stays BLOCKED on it. Needs an owner decision on the route: a policy mutation in corvint-tasks (separate repository), or a recorded decision that changes how this gate is attested.
title: The release-checklist policy gate cannot run --pre-promotion because corvint-tasks writes policy only at init

acceptanceCriteria: A preregistration amendment adds mention-anchored orientation tasks with frozen expected evidence before any run.

This ticket records that amendment and a sealed run that scores prompt-mention orientation.
title: Amend the daily-loop preregistration with prompt-mention orientation tasks

acceptanceCriteria: A spec amendment defines how a caller supplies bounded commit facts and how rows for a named commit are pinned.
Frozen cases cover a reachable commit, an unknown commit and an ambiguous prefix, and the compiler itself still reads no history.
body: Filed 2026-09-23 from V1-0192. LCP-V0-013 resolves a commit mention only as a prefix of the bound commit; any other commit reports anchor-evidence-unavailable because the prompt compiler reads no history (LCP-V0-011). A prompt such as `revert 1a2b3c4` therefore gets no evidence. Resolving it needs Git facts acquired by the caller under a bound, pinned to immutable objects, without making the compiler read history.
title: Resolve task mentions of commits other than the bound commit from caller-acquired Git facts

acceptanceCriteria: TJAA names the Playwright plan's outcome for a changed helper that no spec reaches, in its own unknown vocabulary or as an explicit bounded exclusion, and says why.

body: Filed 2026-09-23 from V1-0204. AFP-V0-020 now names a changed unit that no test reaches as NO_SELECTABLE_TEST in every plugin. The Playwright plan (TJAA) builds on the shared TypeScript graph and widened to the full relevant suite on any shared-graph unknown. V1-0204 keeps that widening tied to the graph's other unknowns, because a full E2E suite cannot exercise a helper that no spec reaches. So an unreached changed helper still leaves the Playwright plan BOUNDED with nothing selected for it. This ticket decides whether the Playwright plan should report that helper, and how.
title: Decide how the Playwright plan reports a changed helper no spec reaches

acceptanceCriteria: The taskLexicalTerms doc comment in internal/contextindex/taskcontext.go describes the term table's actual tokenisation: termCounter.count (termtable.go) splits a body identifier at a lower-to-upper camelCase boundary, so `stripFinalNewline` is not one body token.

acceptanceCriteria: An edit to a spec pinned by a use-case contract receipt that does not touch the receipt's claimed sections no longer fails TestUCV0ProfileMigration, or the failure names the exact repin command.
Two open PRs that both edit docs/specs/daily-change-evidence-workflow-v0.md no longer force each other to regenerate conformance/use-cases-v0 receipts and ledger.json after every merge.
The receipt still detects a substantive change to the evidence it attests; the chosen binding is recorded in the use-case conformance spec and BUILD-LOG.
body:
Filed 2026-09-23 while fixing CI on PRs #127, #130 and #133. conformance/use-cases-v0/receipts/*/contract.json pins the whole-file sha256 of docs/specs/daily-change-evidence-workflow-v0.md, and implementation.json pins source files such as cmd/corvint/local_completion.go; ledger.json pins each receipt's digest. Any edit to those files fails TestUCV0ProfileMigration (subject-digest-mismatch, conformance/use-cases-v0/main.go:363) even when the attested behaviour is unchanged, and repositoryRevision is only pattern-checked (:332). Every DCW-editing PR must repin, and each merge forces the remaining PRs to repin again. A mechanical repin (recompute subject digests, set repositoryRevision to HEAD, update ledger digests) was needed on four branches. Options: bind to requirement IDs or section digests, or ship a repin make target with a clear failure fix line.

Recurrence 2026-09-24: the tripwire reached main. Commit 793fc8a (decision 0376) edited docs/specs/daily-change-evidence-workflow-v0.md (sha256 44e9b24d... -> c7a069c3...) without repinning, and PR #140 merged it at 2026-09-24T12:15:46Z while its go-product job (Actions run 35997202483, started 12:08:38Z) was still in_progress; artifact-integrity and go-interop had passed. main then failed TestUCV0ProfileMigration for UC-CHANGE-CONSEQUENCE, UC-EVIDENCE-CARRYING-COMPLETION and UC-TASK-ORIENTATION until PR #145 repinned them (merge 72c614a, 12:45:43Z; same mechanical repin as 5675e30). PR #143, prepared independently in another session, carried byte-identical files and merged 20 s later as a content no-op, so two sessions spent the same repin. So a docs-only edit can merge the break before the job that runs go test reports; whether go-product is a required check was not verified.
title: conformance: use-case receipts pin whole-file digests, so every DCW spec edit forces a repin

acceptanceCriteria: A spec amendment to learned-trace-admission-v0 defines the observation record, its support count, citation pinning and the staleness rule, with requirement IDs.
Frozen cases cover consolidation of agreeing rows, a stale observation after a cited blob changes, and an observation never outranking project-owned authority.
The skill-export projection either consumes observations or explicitly excludes them, stated in the spec.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 from a review of vectorize-io/hindsight (MIT agent-memory system; README reviewed via summary, paper arXiv 2512.12818 and code not read). Hindsight consolidates related facts into 'observations' that keep exact quotes, a proof count and supporting evidence, and refines rather than overwrites them. Corvint analog: group admitted learned-trace rows that support the same route into one observation carrying its support count and the pinned blob citations of every supporting row; mark it stale (not authoritative) when any cited blob changes at the bound revision. No LLM extraction, no new mutable store; admission, secret screening and the LTA held-out gate still govern, and project authority still outranks it (invariant 3).
title: learning: consolidate repeated admitted traces into pinned, support-counted observations that go stale when cited blobs change

acceptanceCriteria: A spec defines the closed question set, the packet shape, the tree-hash key and invalidation, with requirement IDs.
A frozen evaluation compares standing-answer packets with on-demand packets for byte cost and evidence parity at the same revision.
Read commands serve a standing answer only when its key matches the bound tree; otherwise they fall back to on-demand compilation.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 from a review of vectorize-io/hindsight (MIT agent-memory system; README reviewed via summary, paper arXiv 2512.12818 and code not read). Hindsight's 'mental models' are standing answers to predefined questions, rewritten as data arrives and served without retrieval latency. Corvint analog: a closed set of recurring questions (e.g. how to test a path, what governs a path) answered by deterministic packets built at `index --if-stale` time as derived state keyed to the tree hash, never rewritten by an LLM and never outranking live evidence. Relates to V1-0023 (compact evidence summaries).
title: index: precompute deterministic standing-answer packets for recurring task questions, keyed to the tree hash

acceptanceCriteria: A spec amendment to task-context-packet-v0 defines the RRF ordering (constant k, per-relation rank source, deterministic tie-break by slot order then path) as an experimental alternative to TCP corroboration, with requirement IDs.
A two-arm run (corroboration vs RRF) on the decision 0027 history-backed corpus reports gold rows at ranks 1-5, 6-10 and in the top 20 with the same samples in both arms.
A decision promotes RRF, keeps it opt-in, or kills it from that reading, recorded in BUILD-LOG; slot admission, caps and packet membership are unchanged in either arm.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 from a review of vectorize-io/hindsight (recall fuses parallel channels by reciprocal rank fusion). Rescoped 2026-09-24 by the owner after recording the current state: the task-context packet is slot assembly, not one ranked list. `compile` admits capped slots in evidence order (pair, mentioned, definition, reverse-import, reference, cochange, sibling, test, lexical fill; internal/contextindex/taskcontext.go:237-283), and `corroborate` (taskcontext.go:338-352, decision 0027) reorders by the count of other relations that would have admitted a path, +50 score each. Candidate: replace that count with reciprocal rank fusion over each relation's own candidate ranking (every row a generator produced, not only the admitted one), keeping slot admission, caps and the one evidence row per path unchanged. Evaluation corpus: the history-backed unseen-task runs decision 0027 used (benchmarks/results/cw-trial-unseen-corvint-v1-rank.json and the held-out development run). Out of scope: git recency as a fused channel. CORVINT_CONTEXT_RECENCY (TCP-V0-035..038, decision 0369) already reweights the lexical and cochange slots and cannot be measured on the frozen bench, which rebuilds snapshots as one commit; that follow-up waits on a history-preserving corpus.
title: retrieval: replace the corroboration count with reciprocal rank fusion over the packet's relation rankings, measured on the 0027 corpus

acceptanceCriteria: A decision records the chosen public benchmark, its licence and why it measures Corvint's job.
A one-command harness reproduces Corvint's published numbers from pinned inputs on a clean machine without network after fetch.
Published results separate self-run from independently reproduced numbers.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 from a review of vectorize-io/hindsight (MIT agent-memory system; README reviewed via summary, paper arXiv 2512.12818 and code not read). Hindsight's main adoption lever is a public benchmark result (LongMemEval) reproduced by independent groups, plus a live results page with per-configuration accuracy, latency and cost. Corvint's external validation remains open (V1-0014, V1-0019). Candidate: choose an existing public code-context retrieval benchmark (verify which exist and their licences first), ship a one-command local harness with pinned inputs and published results, and invite independent reruns. Corvint self-results stay labelled as self-use, not independent validation.
title: eval: publish a reproducible public retrieval benchmark harness that third parties can rerun

acceptanceCriteria: A frozen retrieval corpus keeps real commit history per sample, with its provenance and licence recorded, so recency features are not 1 everywhere.
The CORVINT_CONTEXT_RECENCY off/on arms are rerun on it and decision 0369's opt-in status is revisited from that reading.
Only then is git recency evaluated as a fused channel alongside V1-0219's ordering.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 when V1-0219 was rescoped to RRF vs corroboration. Decision 0369 keeps CORVINT_CONTEXT_RECENCY opt-in because the frozen agent_retrieval_bench rebuilds each snapshot as one commit, so every ranked list was identical off and on (BUILD-LOG 2026-09-23, V1-0089). Fusing recency as a channel is unmeasurable until a corpus keeps history.
title: eval: build a history-preserving retrieval corpus so git recency can be measured and fused

acceptanceCriteria: The owner confirms the rewrite plan and disables the ruleset for the force-push.
git filter-repo removes only that trailer; the rewritten tree of main is byte-identical.
Every pinned SHA is repinned or its evidence regenerated, and receipt audit, doc checks and the full gate pass on the new main.
Open branches are rebased, the ruleset is restored, and the effect on v0.7.0/v0.8.0 is recorded in BUILD-LOG.
body:
Filed 2026-09-24 after the 0.8.0 release. Commit ac80244 on main carries `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` (cherry-picked from 366d526, merged in PR #70), which lists the claude account as a repository contributor. It is the only such trailer on main. The owner chose on 2026-09-24 to release 0.8.0 first and rewrite later. Measured blast radius at 444f62c: the `main` ruleset (pull_request, required_status_checks) blocks a direct force-push; 500 of 551 commits get new SHAs; 65 of those SHAs are pinned in 109 tracked files (60 .corvint/changes CEMs, 17 .taskman tickets and the release file, 15 use-case receipts, 10 daily-loop benchmark receipts, docs); v0.7.0 (678c1b1) and v0.8.0 (516439f) contain the commit, and published tags are never moved.

Owner instruction 2026-09-29: remove Claude as a contributor when preparing the 1.0 release. This task is required for v1-0. Reassess the current history and evidence blast radius before proposing the rewrite; the measurements above are historical. This scheduling instruction does not execute or approve a specific force-push plan. Retain the existing rewrite approval, evidence regeneration, published-tag preservation and verification criteria.

2026-09-29 isolated rehearsal identified a concrete N-1 selector blocker: hosted .github/workflows/release-gates.yml:192 uses ancestry-based prior-tag selection and produces no tag on rewritten main while published tags are preserved. Evidence /tmp/corvint-v1-delivery-20260929/history-rewrite/n1-selection-checks.json and N1-PATCH-PLAN.md. An isolated reviewed repair will accept a paired explicit prior tag and exact tag-object identity, retaining default ancestry selection and failing closed on absent, unsafe or stale references. Lifecycle prior-release archive selection is separate from accepted Core v0.8.1 compatibility replay; core-n1-replay is outside make gate. Historical immutable SHA evidence remains historical; do not bulk rewrite references. No specific force-push or publication approved/executed.

2026-09-29: N1 predecessor repair independently reviewed, sealed at 3086a4ca5285a082eed78da159045b7a2cc8ffd0, integrated locally and PR349 pending CI/auto-merge. New owner private-spec/public-consumer requirement V1-0471 supersedes the executable scope of the earlier contributor-only rewrite proposal. Retain its backup method and historical evidence, but do not execute its old main-only lease. Combined approved paths/history/refs scope, fresh rehearsal/maps and exact final approval remain required; historical tag preservation versus historical document removal must be decided explicitly. See /tmp/corvint-v1-delivery-20260929/history-rewrite/PUBLIC-PRIVATE-SCOPE-ADDENDUM.md.
title: 1.0 release: remove Claude as a repository contributor

acceptanceCriteria: The owner promotes v0-5 to v0-7 in order, or records a decision on how published pre-releases relate to store promotion.
v0-8 reaches candidate and readiness reports its gates.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 after the 0.8.0 release. `corvint-tasks release readiness` for v0-8 is BLOCKED only on candidate: the release record lists no missing tickets although six scoped tickets were OPEN (V1-0016, V1-0023, V1-0154, V1-0191, V1-0195, V1-0201), and `release candidate` refuses because its predecessors were never promoted (v0-5 is candidate only; v0-6 and v0-7 are not candidates). 0.7.0 and 0.8.0 were published as GitHub pre-releases without store promotion. Promotion is owner-only. Route chosen in decision 0381 item 10: v0-7 follows v0-5, v0-9 follows v0-6 and v0-8, promote v0-5, v0-7, v0-8, then v0-6 after V1-0011.
title: release chain: v0-5, v0-6 and v0-7 were never promoted, so v0-8 cannot become a candidate

acceptanceCriteria: The installed corvint binary runs the daily change, check and seal steps as subverbs of the existing Core verb dogfood; no new root verb is added.
script/dogfood-change.sh, dogfood-check.sh and dogfood-seal.sh become thin wrappers over those subverbs and keep their make targets and environment inputs.
dogfood finish no longer executes repository scripts, reads the repository VERSION file, or builds cmd/corvint; it runs from any Git repository with only the installed binary.
A test runs change, check, seal and finish in a temporary non-Corvint repository with no script/ directory and passes.
The daily-change-evidence and local-completion specs carry numbered requirements, failure modes and rollback for the move.
body: The adopter daily path only works inside Corvint's own tree: internal/localcompletion/finish.go runs bash <root>/script/dogfood-check.sh and dogfood-change.sh, and those scripts resolve the repo from their own location, read VERSION and fall back to go build ./cmd/corvint. On any other repository (Beamfall, V1-0184; untouched repositories, V1-0019) the path cannot run. Owner decision 2026-09-24: make it portable first, ship in 0.9, then run V1-0184 with that binary.
title: dogfood: run the daily change, check and seal path from the installed binary so it works outside Corvint's tree

acceptanceCriteria: An owner-accepted rule either forbids path:line citations into BUILD-LOG (cite the entry heading instead) or makes the log append-only at the end, and the mixed ordering is resolved.
line-citations-check or a sibling check enforces the rule.
Existing BUILD-LOG line citations are converted.
body: Filed 2026-09-24. Decisions such as 0375 cite `docs/BUILD-LOG.md:<line>@<anchor>`. BUILD-LOG is newest-first, so every new top entry shifts those lines and line-citations-check fails until the citation is repinned. On 2026-09-24 PRs #153, #158, #159 and the V1-0236 branch each had to repin 0375 lines 13 and 40, and parallel repins produced merge conflicts in the decision file. Some recent entries are appended at the end instead, so the log's ordering is also mixed.
title: docs: BUILD-LOG path:line citations shift whenever an entry is added at the top, forcing repins in unrelated PRs

acceptanceCriteria: The work rebind existing-adoption refusal prints fixed text plus at most the bounded worksource or Git status reason (the WQO-V0-051 vocabulary), never raw Git stderr.
A test drives rebind with Git stderr containing a C1 or ESC byte and a long payload and asserts neither reaches the output.
work-queue-observation-v0.md states the bound for this line.
body: Filed 2026-09-24 during the #156/#157 review (PR #159). internal/worksource/git.go:212-217 wraps a failed qualified Git acquisition as `qualified Git acquisition failed (<argv>): <err> <stderr>`, keeping up to 64 KiB of Git stderr, and cmd/corvint/work_adopt.go:225 prints it after `corvint work rebind: existing adoption is unqualified:`. Git stderr can carry repository-controlled bytes (paths, config values, terminal escapes). WQO-V0-051 bounds the SOURCE_UNQUALIFIED line to fixed text; this rebind path has no such bound.
title: work rebind: the existing-adoption refusal prints up to 64 KiB of raw Git stderr

acceptanceCriteria: A test in script/dogfood-change_test.sh binds a change, reorders two same-count hunks (for example by a rebase that swaps their order), reuses the old ordinal plan, and shows today's result before the fix.

dogfood-change refuses a plan whose rows were written for a different hunk order with a named refusal, or binds rows to hunk identity (path and patch digest) rather than ordinal; the test passes after the fix.
body: DCW-V0-019 (PR #134, decision 0376) refuses a citation plan whose row count differs from the prepared map (stale-nine-of-ten, stale-ten-of-nine). Decision 0381 item 6 names the remaining gap: a plan written for an earlier hunk order that has the same number of rows still covers every hunk, so citations can attach to the wrong hunks without a refusal. Unreproduced; criterion 1 reproduces it. Split from V1-0173. Not a 1.0 blocker (decision 0381 item 6).
title: dogfood-change: a stale ordinal citation plan still binds when hunks are reordered but the count is unchanged

acceptanceCriteria: The session-start digest emits at most the P0 tickets plus a count per priority and the read command (`corvint-tasks roadmap`) instead of every OPEN ticket.

Measured SessionStart additional context stays under the host's inline limit (no persisted-output overflow) on the current store; the before and after byte counts are recorded in the ticket completion.
body: The SessionStart context observed 2026-09-24 was 11.4 KB, overflowed to a persisted file, and was mostly a list of all 100 OPEN tickets emitted by the operator-global hook `~/.claude/hooks/agent-memory-digest.sh` (outside this repository, so touchPaths is empty). It spends the agent's attention budget before any task exists and contradicts evidence-explains-its-inclusion. Lesson 33 of the source recommends a small router plus progressive disclosure. Source: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch, Phase 14 agent-workbench track, reviewed 2026-09-24.
title: session-start: cap the task-store digest so the hook stops injecting every open ticket

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded control schema (owner, proving evidence, retirement condition) is defined in DOGFOOD.md or a cited spec.
Each existing dogfood step and AGENTS.md hard rule is listed with those three fields, or explicitly marked as having no retirement condition with a reason.
At least one control whose retirement condition is already met is identified or the audit records that none is.
body: Controls (gates, dogfood steps, AGENTS.md rules) accumulate and none carries a stated condition under which it may be removed; `retire` in docs/specs refers to migrations and code paths, not controls (inferred from file names, confirm when starting). Lessons 46 and 54 of the source require each promoted control to carry one owner, the verification that proves it, and a retirement condition, so the rule set can shrink as well as grow. Source: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch, Phase 14 agent-workbench track, reviewed 2026-09-24.
title: dogfood: give every gate and promoted control an owner, proof, and retirement condition

acceptanceCriteria: DOGFOOD.md records the destination order and requires each friction finding to name the earliest layer chosen and why a lower layer was not.
The recorded friction findings of the last three dogfood-sealed changes are classified against the order, and any finding that became instruction prose but fits an earlier layer is filed as a ticket.
If a fingerprint is added to self-observations, the change cites SOL-V0 requirements and does not feed ranking, evidence or authority.
body: Dogfood friction findings and operator corrections currently tend to become instruction prose. Lesson 46 of the source orders destinations: test or evaluation, scope or permission policy, automation, canonical example plus validator, instruction with a scenario check, human decision record; and deduplicates repeated corrections by a stable fingerprint. `self-observations.jsonl` is a candidate carrier for the fingerprint but must stay outside ranking, evidence and authority (invariant 4). Source: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch, Phase 14 agent-workbench track, reviewed 2026-09-24.
title: dogfood: route each friction finding to the earliest layer that prevents recurrence

acceptanceCriteria: Every `dogfood status` and `dogfood finish` result either carries at least one next action or a named reason code for having none, covered by a test for the frontier-UNAVAILABLE case.
The local-completion spec states the requirement with a stable ID traced to that test.
body: `internal/localcompletion/types.go` carries `NextActions` with `omitempty`. Lesson 40 of the source holds that a handoff without a next action is a status report. The session-start event observed 2026-09-24 reported `frontier: UNAVAILABLE (frontier-authority-unavailable)` with no next action. Whether finish and status always populate NextActions is not yet confirmed. Source: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch, Phase 14 agent-workbench track, reviewed 2026-09-24.
title: dogfood finish: always emit a concrete next action, including when the frontier is UNAVAILABLE

acceptanceCriteria: A pull request that adds a refusal code no spec names fails CI.

CI runs the Makefile's documentation checks that are gate steps (spec-requirements, requirement-definitions, traceability-tests, decision-numbers, line-citations, error-code-ownership) on every pull request.
body: Found while preparing 0.8.1 (decision 0381 item 11). PR #160 added 26 dogfood change/check/seal refusal and step codes that no spec named, so `make error-code-ownership-check`, a GATE_STEPS entry, failed on main from 7739f60 on. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only go test, go vet and go-archive-gate, so no PR check saw it; the release gate would have. PR #165 adds the owning spec section (DCW-V0-020).
title: ci: pull requests do not run the documentation gate steps, so unowned error codes reached main

acceptanceCriteria: A go-test step that fails in one resolved package records a pass for every other resolved package that passed, keyed as GL-V0-001 requires, and a rerun on the same tree runs only the failed package plus the unresolved set.
gate-ledger-v0.md amends GL-V0-002 for per-package records, with a test that a failed package is never recorded.
body: During the 0.8.1 release, one flaky test failed the go-test step. GL-V0-002 records only a step that exits zero, and the 101 resolved packages run in one go test invocation, so the rerun repeated about 100 packages that had passed on byte-identical inputs. Parsing go test -json per package would let a failed invocation still record the packages that passed.
title: gate-ledger: record each resolved package's pass even when the go-test step fails

acceptanceCriteria: Each package moved to the resolved set declares its out-of-package reads so gate-affected-select can bound them, with a test that an undeclared read keeps it unresolved.
The unresolved count and the wall time of a one-file change's gate are measured before and after, with cmd/corvint's split or bound recorded in BUILD-LOG.
body:
The 0.8.1 gate partitions 101 packages under per-package keys and 129 unresolved under the tree key (tests read paths via os.Getwd, `..` or git that the affected-plan index cannot bound). Any tree change reruns all 129; cmd/corvint alone takes about 591 s (V1-0226). The owner asked on 2026-09-24 why Corvint cannot already name only the tests a change needs.

2026-10-01 measured CI investigation: at clean public main adf8358220769b8d6724ad27d27625602b8a7c62, native gate-affected-select -unresolved inventories 159 of 284 root packages. A controlled newline-only edit to internal/behaviorfalsify/receipt_test.go gives Corvint 141 provider packages and selector 171 packages, scope UNKNOWN. The exact PR #416 merge replay selects 245 of 287 packages. These are advisory counts, not proof of safe omission or measured runtime savings. Owner again requested Corvint to test only what needs testing in CI. Current generic pins remain empty, and enabling them serializes the selected suite on shard 0; qualification/execution-profile work is separate. Existing acceptance criteria and authority remain unchanged. Independent read-only review checked counts against actual receipts; evidence /private/tmp/corvint-ci-approval-findings.json and GitHub run 36878582999.

2026-10-01 AFP-V0-023 (PR https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/pull/438, branch claude/ci-affected-selection at 8f7a8ba8 on origin/main 2aec8fec): the project-owned .corvint/test-read-scopes.json declares measured read scopes for 99 root-locating test packages (75 entries), so planner and selector select them through DECLARED_READ_SCOPE instead of the rule (d) floor; an invalid declaration fails closed to the full run. Full CI runs declared packages under the Landlock wrapper .github/testconfine (ABI>=2), so a too-narrow scope fails rather than under-selects. Replay of 16 recent merges: mean 200->166 packages selected (-17.1%), 5023->4543 package-seconds (-9.6%). Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-01-declared-test-read-scopes.md; CEM .corvint/changes/6eec96cac12c30d6ccecbeec9659716d72e392c7.cem.json (52/52 supported, dogfood-check PASS, sealed); focused tests pass; one independent review, both should-fix findings fixed. NOT_RUN: hosted confined full CI run (needs admin ci-control-plane approval for .github at the exact head), make gate. cmd/corvint is NOT declared and stays selected through import edges and its own reads; six packages were rejected (fail only confined) and 15 env-limited packages were NOT_RUN, all staying on the floor. Keep open until the hosted confined run passes and the remaining unresolved set is re-measured. Follow-ups V1-0633..V1-0636.

2026-10-01 hosted run of PR438 at 8f7a8ba8 (run 36917489536): all four go-product shards failed. Every confined failure was a nested go build (adapter, fixture or CLI under test) failing 'error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128' because the Landlock ruleset denies .git (intended: git reads are the unbounded class) while Go stamps VCS by default. tools/gate-ledger also failed unconfined: TestGoTestKeysResolvedPackagesPerPackage copies the tool's sources and omitted the new readscopes.go (the earlier 'fails either way' diagnosis was this PR's own defect). The derivation masked the VCS failure: its snapshot had no .git and set GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false. Fix d22fbe14: the wrapper appends -buildvcs=false to GOFLAGS for confined binaries only (testconfine.ConfinedEnv, TestConfinedEnvTurnsOffVCSStamping_AFPV0023); .git stays denied; the fixture copies readscopes.go. Re-verified in a real clone with .git, GOFLAGS empty, GOPROXY=off and the revised wrapper (golang:1.27.1 linux/arm64, Landlock ABI 4): all 99 declared packages identical per-test outcomes confined vs unconfined, 5179 outcomes, 33 skips; declaration and replay unchanged. Fix CEM .corvint/changes/684cce0f64c6fe63c5a69dde0b715f9e50eeccce.cem.json (10/10 supported, check PASS, sealed); PR438 head 5e7dfab15bde1f48b501e5a35b45db9ca9b164ed. Hosted rerun and admin ci-control-plane approval still pending; keep open.

2026-10-01 floor attribution and behaviorfalsify fixture: re-attributing the 16-merge replay by planner witness shows the unbounded-reader floor still costs about 1,817 package-seconds per merge after AFP-V0-023; internal/behaviorfalsify is about 796 of them (UNBOUNDED_READER in 14/16 merges, about 910 s per serial run), then tasks/authority 307, doccorpus 168, tasks/store 124, cmd/corvint-go-test-provider 105, tasks/intent 45, analyzernativebridge 35. Cause for behaviorfalsify: the test helper repositoryRoot walked up from os.Getwd and ran git on the real checkout, which the AFP-V0-023 wrapper cannot confine because it denies .git. PR https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/pull/449 (branch claude/behaviorfalsify-hermetic-fixture, head 3e996c6c on origin/main e5d96823) replaces it with a disposable committed fixture repository; test-only. Evidence: tests pass (43 s, -race 126 s), vet clean, corvint affected with only docs/specs/README.md dirty no longer selects the package, independent review no blockers, CEM .corvint/changes/ecb3236e84a17dd90645b731da714f7233ae2d60.cem.json (4/4 supported, check PASS, sealed); expected saving about 796 package-seconds per merge (about 17% of 4,543), NOT_RUN make gate. PR438 hosted confined run passed at 5e7dfab1 (all four shards, Landlock ABI 7); only the admin ci-control-plane status remains. Same git-on-real-checkout class still keeps doccorpus (TestCorpusSelfDocumentation), companionrelease and conformance/release-artifact-v0 on the floor; they need hermetic fixtures. cmd/corvint-go-test-provider fails unconfined in the golang:1.27.1 container (execution authority changed: post-run revalidation, in three qualification tests), so it cannot be compared there yet.

2026-10-01 floor read scopes (PR https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/pull/452, merged into claude/ci-affected-selection at b6e38e47): declared measured scopes for internal/doccorpus (examples/documentation-corpus/, after moving its self-corpus test to internal/doccorpus/selfcorpus), cmd/corvint-postmerge-metrics ([]) and cmd/corvint-analyzer-c-jni (go.mod, internal/analyzernativebridge/); all outcomes identical confined vs unconfined. Docs-only probe: 64 -> 62 packages selected, 36 -> 34 UNBOUNDED_READER. Expected saving about 150 package-seconds per merge (estimate from the attribution; replay not rerun). Rejected: tasks/authority and tasks/store (store opens /; new ticket), companionrelease (.git; V1-0643), console (reads root), release-artifact-v0 (.agent-evidence). NOT_RUN (fail unconfined in the container): cmd/corvint-go-test-provider, internal/authoritystore, internal/dashboard/source, internal/lspstdio. NOT_RUN make gate. PR438 now waits only on the admin ci-control-plane status at b6e38e47.
title: gate: bound the 129 unresolved test packages (cmd/corvint first) so a tree change stops rerunning all of them

acceptanceCriteria: A consumer recomputes the plan, approval and raw-report digests from retained artifacts alone, with a conformance fixture that does it.

Missing, tampered or stale plan, approval, raw report, assertion outcome, setup, unrelated, cleanup or bound evidence reports invalid_control, not_run or not_supported, never killed, each with a test.
The receipt schema is versioned, bounded under BBF-V0-010, deterministic, and screened for credentials and undeclared environment values; BBF-V0 amends BBF-V0-002 for the new bindings.
body: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/167 (adopter integration against the installed 0.8.0 companion). Checked against internal/behaviorfalsify/types.go at 2a8d1ec: the Report binds plan_digest and each AttemptResult keeps the parsed HookReceipt (plan_digest, target/runner identity, attempt/retry, native_receipt_sha256, target/unrelated/setup observations, artifacts), hook and cleanup process evidence and workspace before/after digests. Missing: an approval record distinct from the plan digest (Execute takes approvedDigest as a bare string), the raw hook-receipt bytes with their digest, canonical plan bytes or a documented recompute path, the companion's own tool/schema/revision identity, and an explicit list of omitted or unsupported fields. Companion work under proposed/experimental BBF-V0; post-1.0 per decision 0381 item 9 (not a Core-verb correctness failure).
title: behaviorfalsify: approval-bound receipt that retains raw hook-report bytes and names omitted fields (issue #167)

acceptanceCriteria: AFU-V1-001..005 and 007..010 are implemented with the named tests in the spec acceptance matrix.
AFU-V1-036: flows inputs are Lstat-checked before open and every write is root-confined without following a symlink, with FIFO, swap and symlink tests.
Export is read-pure and import(export(request)) reproduces the request's canonical bytes.
body: Decision 0385 (issue #175), spec docs/specs/application-flow-understanding-v1.md. Core-owned model parts that e2e-safe reads. In progress on branch claude/afu-s1 (036 hardening committed efc2628).
title: flows S1: intent model, export/import, review anchors, input and output hardening (AFU-V1-001..005, 007..010, 036)

acceptanceCriteria: AFU-V1-011..014 adapter fixtures cover a retry-passed test, a timed-out attempt and a failed negative control.
AFU-V1-012: every attempt's duration, failure, anchor and attachments are retained, with a regression test on a two-attempt Playwright report.

The daily adopter path requires DOGFOOD_INTENTS_FILE entries with exactly one `## Requirements` heading (OCM-V0-001, internal/lrfrepo/ocm.go:556 `invalid-requirements-section`; docs/DOGFOOD.md Inputs table), so no Beamfall change can reach `complete: true` and V1-0184 cannot produce `beamfall-dogfood` receipts. Routes: (a) add a Beamfall requirements spec first, then change against it; (b) extend OCM intent reading to a repository-declared form (ADR decisions or roadmap acceptance blocks) under its own spec; (c) allow an intent-free daily path whose OCM rows are NOT_PRODUCED but still complete for the three Core use cases. Filed 2026-09-25 from the pre-1.0 expert panel review (main report or Beamfall/corvint-tasks addendum; confirmed by at least one verifier). Finding text: **F2. A pending redo blocks reads, can be cleared only with the primary on the intent branch, and readers report in-flight writers as crashes.** - **Severity:** medium. - **Core:** no. - **Location:** `tasks-src/internal/store/redo.go:52` (`requireBranch` before redo) and `store.go` `settled()`. - **Failure:** - After a C2 crash, `queue status`, `ticket list`, `roadmap`, `ticket show` and `gate list` return NOT_RUN REDO_PENDING. `release list` still works. - An agent on a feature branch cannot recover, because the retry is refused with INTENT_BRANCH_MISMATCH. - Under a concurrent writer, 14 of 60 reads returned REDO_PENDING with crash remediation text. - **Fix:** - Add a branch-independent `recover` verb, since redo only replays committed bytes. - Have readers try a non-blocking flock and report WRITER_ACTIVE when it is held. - Name the branch precondition in the remediation text. - **Votes:** 1/0/1. - **Known ticket:** none.

Audit addendum 2026-09-26 (STO-01), source 2961076fc0b78bfab743578f2ef5c17006be058a: A returned I/O fault or interruption after the UNPAUSE receipt is published and before barrier deletion/head advancement. This occurs even when all staging slots are cleaned. The committed receipt remains pending. Retrying unpause returns REDO_PENDING; generic mutation redo refuses the null post with UNSUPPORTED. Supported commands cannot settle the journal, so store use requires manual recovery. This is an acknowledged implementation-slice limitation, not a claim of corruption or violation of a recovered accepted task-store contract.
Source: internal/tasks/store/redo.go:121; internal/tasks/store/barrier_test.go:151; internal/tasks/store/barrier_test.go:172; internal/tasks/cli/cli.go:117.
Verification: "PASS: GOCACHE=/tmp/corvint-go-build-cache GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/trace ./internal/tasks/store -run TestAppend(RecoversInterruptedRetention|InterruptedRecoveryRemainsRetryable|RetentionPostPublishSyncFailureRecoversOnRetry)|TestApplyMigrationAtCandidateLimit|TestTMV0009_AS11_BarrierPublicationReturnedFaults. Existing barrier test provides deterministic returned-fault reproduction; no process-kill or power-cut experiment."
Correction: Extend explicit task-store recovery to a receipt-authorized barrier deletion: delete only the exact preimage, accept already absent postimage, refuse any third value, sync deletion before head advancement. Include this scope in the recover work for V1-0309.
See .agent-evidence/2026-09-26-comprehensive-audit.md and .agent-evidence/audit-20260926/ for original evidence. This addendum does not claim implementation or promotion.

body: Filed 2026-09-25 from the pre-1.0 expert panel review (main report or Beamfall/corvint-tasks addendum; confirmed by at least one verifier). Finding text: Unverified (low severity or beyond the per-reviewer cap; not examined by a verifier): - go-runtime:cmd: help text labels Core verbs experimental/alpha/Go-only (`cmd/corvint/help.go:218`); unknown flag reported as "unrecognized arguments" (`taskcontext.go:39`); adapter stdout write and CPU-profile close errors ignored (`host_adapter.go:852`); empty `--root` resolves to cwd (`main.go:642`). - go-runtime:kernel: contextindex kills the Git process group after Wait (PID-reuse hazard gokernel already fixed, `internal/contextindex/git.go:229`); snapshot eviction uses an unstable sort on tied mtimes (`snapshot.go:455`). - git-integrity: repo-owned `core.bigFileThreshold` steers range impact into a binary refusal (`range_impact.go:471`); symlink entries indexed as source with link target as content (`git.go:392`). - proof-soundness: `ciMapHeader` returns nil on unparseable JSON (`interop/cem01-go/ci.go:194`, V1-0133); `validateSpan` message promises start>=0 but checks end>=1 (`wire/map.go:302`). - red-team: corvint-mcp returns repository-authored text unframed in `structuredContent` (`cmd/corvint-mcp/main.go:223`). - wire-contract: mixed snake_case/camelCase key conventions frozen; `affected` unknowns as `CODE: detail` strings; experimental profiles frozen as wire identifiers. - retrieval: medium, Swift `impact` returns only the changed path with `git diff --check` as the only verification (`impact.go:150`); PPR off by default (`ppr.go:11`); lexical reason strings show inconsistent idf (`taskcontext.go:1108`). - rts: medium, impact ranks tests below every non-test importer so direct tests fall outside the limit (`impact.go:196`, V1-0263 root cause); V1-0264 appears fixed in code but is still OPEN (`internal/dogfoodflow/flow.go:399`). - admission: orientation receipt has no binary identity (`use-case-conformance-v0.md:50`); V1-0011 and V1-0184 OPEN after promotion. - agent-systems: `frontier-authority-unavailable` hard-coded on every receipt (`local_completion_event.go:471`); `adapter claude-source-handoff` labelled Core but experimental and file-writing (1.0 spec:113); compatibility tuple timeout disagrees with hooks.json; corvint-mcp answers standard `initialize` with -32601 unless the legacy flag is set (`internal/mcp/server/server.go:211`). - landscape: medium, no stable MCP surface in 1.0 Core (1.0 spec:60); Claude Code adapter README links a missing anchor.

body: Filed 2026-09-25 as a gap left open by decision 0394, which accepted IDX-SNAP-V0-024 (panel blocker B9, PR #219): a tracked path whose Git bytes are not UTF-8 is an index exclusion, not a repository refusal. query --task and prove --task still refuse with unsupported-query-history when commit history holds a non-UTF-8 path. The refusal is frozen under GPK-V0 with oracle parity, so a fix needs a GPK amendment that keeps parity (for example, skip the path in query history learning and disclose it) or an owner decision that the refusal stands.
title: B9 gap: query --task and prove --task refuse unsupported-query-history on a non-UTF-8 path in history

body: Filed 2026-09-25 as a gap left open by decision 0394, which accepted IDX-SNAP-V0-024 (panel blocker B9, PR #219): a tracked path whose Git bytes are not UTF-8 is an index exclusion, not a repository refusal. The context packet has no exclusions member for any reason, so a non-UTF-8 path excluded from the index is disclosed only in the impact and prove receipts. A fix adds a bounded exclusion disclosure to the task-context packet under a spec amendment, or an owner decision records that impact and prove disclosure is enough.
title: B9 gap: the context packet does not disclose non-UTF-8 path exclusions

body: Filed 2026-09-25 from the pre-1.0 expert panel review, main report §4 Disputed findings (scratchpad review/out/panel-report.md). Finding text: `affected` excludes the owning package and its importers with `NO_DEPENDENCY_PATH_TO_DIRTY_UNIT` when the dirty path is unowned (rts, two findings: `//go:embed` asset and deleted Go file; each 1/2). Agreed and reproduced: changing `internal/gokernel/host-schema.json` or deleting `internal/testsupport/hostload.go` leaves the packages that fail to build or panic excluded with an affirmative reason, while a RUNNABLE advisory command over ~32 coincidental path-literal readers is emitted; `tools/gate-affected-select` selects them correctly. `Owns()` (`golang.go:89-90`) accepts `.go` only; `seed()` (`select.go:266-273`) never seeds the directory owner; readers run after traversal (`select.go:131-132`). body: Filed 2026-09-26 (owner: "ticket the cache trim"). The host disk filled (2.7 GiB free of 1.8 TiB): ~/Library/Caches/go-build held 88 GiB, /tmp/corvint-go-build-cache (Makefile CORVINT_GOCACHE, also used by script/dogfood-change.sh and script/dogfood-bind-range.sh) held 40 GiB, and /tmp held 386 go-build* work directories (4.5 GiB, 289 older than a day) from interrupted builds. acceptanceCriteria: Each listed runner either uses the shared sanitized Git environment (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1, system and global config isolated, empty credential helper) or carries a recorded reason it must inherit the caller's environment, with a test for each runner changed.
Every surprise status read uses the isolated shared implementation.
Configuration changes after loader completion cannot execute clean/process filters or alter repository state.
Dirty-worktree refusal and clean committed-range receipts retain their intended behavior.
body:
Found 2026-09-26 at 2961076f while following up the appflows runner review finding (V1-0254). Core and MCP reads use sanitizedGitEnvironment (internal/gokernel/repository.go) or boundedGitRunner (internal/liveverify/affected/dirty.go). These runners do not: internal/dogfoodflow/check.go:116 and internal/dogfoodflow/flow.go:142 (os.Environ plus LC_ALL=C), internal/lspprovider/provider.go:170 (inherited environment), internal/releasecandidate/candidate.go:292 (isolated config but no GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH), internal/tasks/store/release.go:208 (inherited environment). In a partial clone a missing object can be lazily fetched from the promisor remote, and user or system Git config (hooks, fsmonitor, credential helpers) applies. None of these are Core read verbs, so invariant 4 is not directly breached; V1-0349 covers the Core and MCP reads. Decide per runner whether to reuse the sanitized environment.

Audit addendum 2026-09-26 (SEC-03), source 2961076fc0b78bfab743578f2ef5c17006be058a: After snapshot/build isolation has completed, touchsurprise.Render calls requireCleanWorktree, which executes raw git status against live repository metadata. This runner disables fsmonitor but does not use gitstatus.Status or neutralize repository clean/process filters. A metadata change between the isolated check and this second read can bypass the intended no-filter execution boundary. Static filter configuration is already rejected by the earlier loader: this is a concurrent-change defense gap, not a demonstrated ordinary-path command-execution issue.
Source: internal/touchsurprise/touchsurprise.go:43; internal/touchsurprise/git.go:51; internal/touchsurprise/git.go:97; cmd/corvint/surprise.go:120; internal/gitstatus/status.go:488; internal/contextindex/snapshot.go:649.
Verification: {"method": "Source inspection and existing regression tests only", "test": "TestSurpriseWritesNothing and TestSurpriseRefusesDirtyWorktree pass with ordinary fixture configuration. The existing surprise package has no filter/config-change regression.", "reproduction": "NOT_RUN: no command-running fixtures or metadata-race demonstrations executed."}
Correction: Route this status call through the shared gitstatus.Status isolation and preserve its safe refusal semantics; avoid a later raw status command with weaker boundaries.
See .agent-evidence/2026-09-26-comprehensive-audit.md and .agent-evidence/audit-20260926/ for original evidence. This addendum does not claim implementation or promotion.
title: Git runners outside the Core read path inherit the environment without GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH or config isolation

Exit 0.", "unitTests": "NOT_RUN; end-to-end scratch reproduction executed instead."}

body:

body: Found 2026-09-26 while diagnosing the v0-6 gate load flakes. Seven runners SIGKILL the child's process group (kill(-pid)) only after Wait has reaped the leader: internal/contextindex/git.go:231 (deferred terminateProcessGroup), internal/doccompiler/process.go:85 (deferred), internal/cem/gitrun/gitrun.go:250 (killDescendants after the reap; gitrun_unix.go:16-17 says the kill happens before the reap), internal/liveverify/mutate/shared.go:43 and gotest.go:180 (after Run), internal/taskman/process_unix.go:37 (after Run), internal/worksource/git.go:214 (deferred cleanupGitProcess), and internal/releasegate/git_unix.go:59 (after Wait). Once the leader is reaped and no descendant keeps its group alive, the group ID can name an unrelated process group whose leader reused that PID, so the sweep can kill it. The window is narrow (a reused PID that is also a group leader), so the severity is low. internal/gokernel/process_unix.go already fixes this with waitGroupLeader, which signals the group while the exited leader is still unreaped (waitid WNOWAIT) and falls back to the old order elsewhere. V1-0312 lists only the contextindex site among its unverified items.

acceptanceCriteria: A new daily-loop harness revision pins the preregistration digest in a committed file (as benchmarks/untouched-repository-v1/preregistration.sha256 does) instead of trusting --prereg-sha256 alone.

Each loop step runs with a scrubbed environment: every DOGFOOD_* variable and host Git configuration (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, HOME) is set by the harness, so an omitted-input variant cannot inherit the value from the operator's shell.
The L3c re-encoded control changes the committed CEM bytes (noncanonical re-encode) and fails the row if the commit status is nonzero, so the control cannot pass as a no-op.
The bind git add and commit run with check=True, and a failed bind makes the loop row FAIL with the git exit status instead of continuing.
The frozen daily-loop-v0 harness and its preregistered digest are not edited; the fix lands as a new preregistered revision with its own seal and a build-log entry naming the old defects.
body: benchmarks/daily-loop-v0/harness.py at d22b9ef0 has four defects found while building the V1-0019 chi case-freeze harness, which fixed the same shapes. (1) harness.py:586 compares preregistration.json against the operator-supplied --prereg-sha256, and the corpus and harness digests are then read from that same file, so no committed value pins the preregistration. (2) harness.py:385 starts from dict(os.environ): a DOGFOOD_* input that a variant omits (L5, L6) can still arrive from the operator's shell, and host Git configuration reaches every step. (3) harness.py:411-412 run the bind git add and commit with check=False, so a failed bind continues to the next dogfood-change and check. (4) harness.py:458-464 re-encodes the CEM with canonical() and commits with capture_output and no status check; a CEM already in canonical form yields identical bytes, the commit fails with nothing to commit, and L3c then checks the unmodified tree. The harness digest is preregistered, so the fix is a new harness revision, not an in-place edit (decision 0423 non-goals). Filed under the owner rule that known bugs are fixed before the next release.
title: Fix the daily-loop-v0 harness: pinned prereg digest, scrubbed env, checked bind commit, real L3c control

acceptanceCriteria: A dogfood change rerun whose citation plan the committed map already carries leaves a compact (non-indent-2) committed map byte-identical and the worktree clean, and dogfood check then passes (a cmd/corvint test that fails before the fix).
A pass that adds a citation still publishes the cited map.
DCW-V0-019 names the rule and its trace row names the test.
body: Observed in the V1-0019 chi smoke-006 run (loop control L3c-reencoded-control): after the bind, the committed .corvint/change.cem.json was rewritten as compact JSON with identical content and committed on top of the bind. The rerun of `corvint dogfood change BASE` then ran the same citation plan again; `cem cite` re-publishes the map in its indent-2 encoding even when every citation is already carried, so the sidecar was left modified. cem-status failed excluded-artifact-mismatch (target-side bytes differ from the verified input), local-outcome failed record-index-failed, and `dogfood check` refused dirty-worktree. The CEM contract fixes strict JSON, not a byte encoding, so a committed map whose content the pass does not change must stay byte-identical. Fix: in the dogfood change cite pass, when a produced pass leaves a map that decodes to the same JSON value as before the pass, restore the pre-pass bytes.
title: Keep a committed CEM map's bytes when a dogfood change rerun cites nothing new

acceptanceCriteria: A context index build over a repository whose .gitignore (or a nested ignore file Git reads) is not a regular file refuses promptly with a named code instead of waiting for the git deadline.

body: observeRepository (internal/contextindex/index.go:380) runs git status through readStatusSnapshot. When a repository's .gitignore is a FIFO, git status blocks reading it and never returns (reproduced 2026-09-26: git init; mkfifo .gitignore; git status is still running after 10 s). The build then waits for gitDeadline (internal/contextindex/git.go:24, 30 s) and fails with a timeout instead of a prompt, named refusal. V1-0367 bounds Corvint's own readIgnoreFile to regular files; the git child still opens the FIFO.
title: Context index build blocks on a FIFO .gitignore until the 30 s git deadline

acceptanceCriteria: A Git call that exits 0 while its output reader is starved for several seconds returns its output instead of a WaitDelay failure.
A descendant that keeps Git's output open still fails the call within a bounded time, and a test pins both cases.
A signal-killed or pipe-drain failure is reported as such, not as "returned non-zero exit status -1".
body: internal/contextindex/process_unix.go:25 (and process_other.go, process_windows.go) sets command.WaitDelay = time.Second. os/exec starts that timer when Git exits, so if the goroutine copying stdout into boundedBuffer is not scheduled within one second, Wait returns exec.ErrWaitDelay although Git succeeded. On a starved host (load 400-650, swap full) this turns successful Git calls into failures: 37 contextindex test failures were WaitDelay only and pass on single rerun, and the c-flakes dogfood-change local-outcome step failed twice with record-failed. tracerecordrepo recordIndexError (adapter.go:604-627) then renders the empty-stderr, exit -1 failure as "repository changed while reading local traces: ... returned non-zero exit status -1", which names neither the signal nor the pipe drain. worksource/git.go:157 (one minute) and cem/gitrun pipeDrainDelay already treat the drain bound as a hang detector held in a variable that tests shorten; gokernel, doccompiler, taskman and liveverify/mutate still use one second.
title: A one-second pipe-drain bound fails successful Git calls on a loaded host

acceptanceCriteria: A descendant that keeps a subprocess's output open still fails the call within a bounded time, and the existing held-pipe tests keep passing.

A doccompiler, taskman, liveverify mutation or work executable binding subprocess that exits 0 while its output reader is starved for several seconds returns its output instead of a WaitDelay failure.
Each changed bound states that it detects a held pipe and is not a latency budget.
body: V1-0390 raised the Git pipe-drain bound in contextindex and gokernel from one second to one minute. The same one-second os/exec WaitDelay remains in internal/doccompiler/process_{unix,other,windows}.go, internal/taskman/process_unix.go, internal/liveverify/mutate/process_{unix,other}.go and cmd/corvint/work_executable_binding.go:287. os/exec starts the WaitDelay timer when the process exits, so a successful subprocess fails with exec: WaitDelay expired before I/O complete whenever the goroutine copying its output is not scheduled within one second. That was observed for Git calls on a host with full swap and load above 400. The groupreap adoption in V1-0373 kills a leftover group before Wait, which closes held pipes, but does not help a starved reader. work_executable_binding has tests that depend on the value.
title: One-second pipe-drain bounds outside Git acquisition fail successful subprocesses on a loaded host

acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether internal/worksource and internal/contextindex Git runners adopt groupreap.Wait (signal the group before reaping the leader) or keep reaping first, and the decision states how VPO-V0-010 and WQO-V0-005/015/032 treat a descendant that holds the output pipe.
If they adopt it, those requirements and their tests are amended in the same change; if not, the rationale is recorded next to the runner.
body: From the V1-0373 group-reap change on claude/rc1-git-runner-hardening (5cd9419a). groupreap.Wait (internal/groupreap/groupreap_unix.go) waits for the leader with waitid WNOWAIT, SIGKILLs the process group, then reaps. It is adopted by gokernel, doccompiler, cem/gitrun, releasegate, taskman and liveverify/mutate. internal/worksource/process_unix.go (Setpgid) and internal/contextindex Git execution are not adopters: their specs treat a descendant that still holds the output pipe after the leader exits as incomplete output (VPO-V0-010, WQO-V0-005, WQO-V0-015, WQO-V0-032), and a pre-reap kill would close that pipe and change the outcome. Owner question: should these two runners move onto the same order, with the requirements amended, or keep reap-first with the reason stated? Related behaviour change in the adopters: when the leader has exited but a descendant holds stdout, they now return the leader's status instead of ErrWaitDelay or a timeout.
title: Should worksource and contextindex Git runners signal the group before reaping, like groupreap adopters?

title: Packages fail to build on freebsd, openbsd, netbsd and solaris

acceptanceCriteria: An over-limit plan or trace reports a fixed code that names which bound was exceeded, with the limit and the observed count.

body: Observed while binding the 2026-09-26/27 integration changes on origin/main (PR #276 and earlier). internal/dogfoodflow/change.go:719 marks the OCM link plan NOT_PRODUCED invalid-ocm-link-plan when it has more than 256 rows, and internal/trace/record.go:22 caps a trace at MaxTracePaths = 200. A change that touches more files than that cannot bind in one pass; the only workaround is splitting the change into several PRs by hand. The refusal names the plan as invalid rather than naming the bound that was exceeded, so the operator has to read the source to learn why. Proposal: report the exceeded bound by name (rows or paths, limit and actual count) and document the split route in docs/DOGFOOD.md, or admit a directory-prefix row that covers many paths as one row.

acceptanceCriteria: The test's timeout is a hang detector that does not expire on a loaded but progressing host.

body: internal/observations/observations_test.go:442 starts 24 copies of the test binary under one context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), 10*time.Second). On a host at load 200 or more (12 CPUs), process start and the barrier wait alone can exceed 10 seconds, so the context kills helpers and the test fails although Append serialization is correct. Seen 2026-09-27 in a local run for the V1-0293 fix: the test failed after 12.26s with observations_test.go:463 context deadline exceeded, raised by command.Start while the helpers were still being started. Fix: derive the bound from t.Deadline() (or use a much larger fixed bound as a hang detector), and keep the serialization assertion unchanged.
title: TestAppendSerializesConcurrentProcesses fails under host load: 24 helper processes share a 10-second context

acceptanceCriteria: A Git probe that expires on its own bound during a dogfood event reports a time-bound code, not dogfood-event-unavailable.
LCP-V0-008's code list and its test cover that path, or the spec records why unavailable is correct.
body: internal/gokernel/repository.go:24 fixes gitDeadline at 10 seconds; on expiry the probe returns repository-probe-timeout (repository.go:161). cmd/corvint/local_completion_event.go:147 maps an error to dogfood-event-deadline only when the event context itself expired, so a probe that times out on its own bound reaches the generic branch at :156 and reports dogfood-event-unavailable. In production the 1600 ms event deadline always fires first, so the gap is reachable when a caller supplies a longer event deadline through dogfoodEventDeadlineKey, which the cmd/corvint tests do (local_completion_claude_test.go:132 uses 10 minutes). On a loaded host TestDogfoodEventReadOnlyEnrolledStopAndPrompt then fails with dogfood-event-unavailable, which reads as a product fault instead of a time bound (seen 2026-09-27 at load 200 to 290 on origin/main 3cd473ba plus V1-0295). Fix options: map gokernel repository-probe-timeout to dogfood-event-deadline, and/or let the tests' longer event deadline also lengthen the Git probe bound.
title: Git probe timeout inside a dogfood event reports dogfood-event-unavailable, not a time-bound code

acceptanceCriteria: A SubagentStart adapter event returns a bounded packet as additionalContext, or a named degradation code, and never blocks the spawn.
The host-adapter spec gains a requirement with a stable ID traced to a fixture test, and compatibility.json records the new surface.
A recorded trial compares `corvint surprise` for subagents with and without the packet on at least one frozen task set.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner's request to research Corvint integrations with large productivity gains. The Claude Code plugin registers SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse (Edit|Write|NotebookEdit), Stop, PreCompact, PostCompact and SessionEnd (`integrations/claude-code/plugins/corvint/hooks/hooks.json`), but not SubagentStart. SubagentStart cannot block, its input carries `agent_prompt`, and it accepts `additionalContext` (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Every Explore or worker subagent therefore re-reads the repository. Proposal: map SubagentStart to a bounded `corvint context --task <agent_prompt>` packet through the existing `corvint adapter claude-code` path, advisory only, with the same budget and degradation codes as user-prompt. Any productivity gain is a hypothesis until measured; `corvint surprise` and `corvint necessity` supply the measure.
title: hosts: inject a task-context packet at Claude Code `SubagentStart` so subagents do not start cold

acceptanceCriteria: The adapter answers Read/Grep PreToolUse with `defer` plus bounded additionalContext or a degradation code, covered by a test that it never emits deny or ask.
The spec states whether hook-driven unplanned-read recording is admitted under AGENTS.md invariant 4, with a decision reference.
Measured p95 hook latency on the Corvint repository stays under the configured hook timeout.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner's request to research Corvint integrations with large productivity gains. PreToolUse returns `additionalContext` and a `permissionDecision` of allow, deny, ask or defer (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). A Read/Grep matcher could add, at the moment a file is opened, its owning spec, covering tests and co-change neighbours from the index snapshot, and could feed the unplanned-read ledger without the operator marker. Corvint holds no authority to block a read, so the adapter must always return `defer`, never `deny` or `ask`. Open questions: the 2 s hook timeout against index load, and whether the ledger write stays inside invariant 4 when driven by a hook instead of the marker. Any productivity gain is a hypothesis until measured; `corvint surprise` and `corvint necessity` supply the measure.
title: hosts: point-of-use context on Claude Code `PreToolUse` for Read and Grep

acceptanceCriteria: The Stop adapter output lists selected tests, unwitnessed ranges and mutation verdicts for new tests, or NOT_RUN with a reason for each missing part.
A fixture proves a tautological new test is reported as killing no mutant.
The spec records how the mutation budget fits the hook timeout, with a stable requirement ID.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner's request to research Corvint integrations with large productivity gains. Agent-written tests that pass regardless of the code under test are an expensive failure. Three existing verbs answer it: `corvint affected` (tests this diff needs), `corvint witness` (changed surface no test exercises) and `corvint prove --mutate` (test-kills-mutant rows; up to eight single-operator mutants per changed file under a 30-minute invocation budget). Proposal: the Stop adapter composes them into one advisory done-list, running `--mutate` only for test files added in the session to stay inside the hook timeout or deferring it to an explicit command. Advisory only; it must not block Stop or claim authority. Any productivity gain is a hypothesis until measured; `corvint surprise` and `corvint necessity` supply the measure.
title: hosts: `Stop` hook reports the done-list: affected tests, unwitnessed lines, and new tests that kill no mutant

acceptanceCriteria: A documented flow runs a wave of at least three agents from the task store with disjoint leases on the Corvint repository.
An Edit on a path leased by another agent yields an advisory warning in a fixture test and never a deny.
The recorded run reports the merge conflicts between wave branches, compared against an unplanned wave.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner's request to research Corvint integrations with large productivity gains. `corvint work propose-wave` groups work by footprint and `corvint lease` records path leases (`internal/scopelease` enforces nothing). Proposal: a host-facing flow that takes the `.taskman` queue, proposes a wave whose impact footprints are disjoint, hands each item to a worktree agent with a held lease, and warns through PreToolUse Edit `additionalContext` when an agent edits a path another agent leased. Warnings only; no block, and lease state stays out of ranking, evidence and authority. Any productivity gain is a hypothesis until measured; `corvint surprise` and `corvint necessity` supply the measure.

acceptanceCriteria: A context packet for a subject reserves every tracked AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md) on the path from the repository root to the subject's directory, closest first, each with its own evidence row.
