body:
Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Observed: `corvint context --task ... --subject apps/fetfinder/components/WorkspaceProfileCardHeader.tsx` on the MeVille clone (Corvint 0.8.1 build 82) cited only the root `AGENTS.md` as governing; `apps/fetfinder/components/AGENTS.md`, the scope document in the subject's own directory, was absent from all results. Cause: `internal/contextindex/taskcontext.go:1212` fixes the precedence to root-level names and states that no other nested instruction path is eligible. The AGENTS.md convention (agents.md) says the closest file takes precedence, and Codex and Claude Code both load nested files. This contradicts invariant 3 (project-owned authority first) on any repository that scopes instructions per directory, and it will surface in V1-0019 untouched-repository validation.

2026-09-28 reviewed local outcome: Local implementation a5e9e29b is independently reviewed on codex/bug-fix-batch, bound CEM 494689566f90609650ce93f9c0355deaba697c84. Tracked subject-ancestor AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md selection, sibling exclusion, subjectless root precedence and bounded uncertainty regressions PASS; focused units, CLI, vet and locators PASS. Keyed completion and strict dogfood check PASS. Integration verified: PR #320 merged at e9a261d26bd5915e1c4a8d10519a6355b34c5946, reviewed head e09eed3a2d036341215c4537d5707939fdf7be3f is on origin/main, and all 11 CI checks PASS. Compatibility repair preserves unchanged frozen root-only output. TCP-V0-008 and REQUIREMENTS.tsv are updated; all three ticket criteria are supported by focused tests and independent review. Separate next-candidate release qualification remains pending outside this scoped bug ticket. Completion evidence SHA256 a364dc362f0527ce18e9b8931a80df610a2a1aff795ec64d26d0d952c929d73d.
title: context: a nested AGENTS.md in the subject's own directory is not admitted as governing evidence

body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). `internal/contextindex/parse.go:197` classifies AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` as instructions, but no Go source reads the `applyTo` glob, so a path-scoped Copilot instruction is treated as repository-wide or not at all. Not recognized: `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (alwaysApply / globs / description modes), `.kiro/steering/*.md`, `.windsurf/rules`, `.clinerules`, Codex `AGENTS.override.md`, and `@path` imports inside CLAUDE.md. body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Hosts resolve instruction files differently: Codex walks root to working directory, one file per directory (AGENTS.override.md > AGENTS.md > fallbacks) and stops at project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB default); Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md exists at or above the working directory, loads subdirectory files lazily and expands @imports (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory; learn.chatgpt.com agents-md). A packet can state, per host, the load set, files present but ignored, and truncation, so an agent and reviewer can see instructions the host will never show. Depends on nested-file admission.
title: context: report which instruction files each host would actually load for the subject

acceptanceCriteria: A governing row whose content contains zero-width, bidi-control or tag characters carries a named warning and is downgraded from authoritative, covered by fixtures.

body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Instruction files are a known injection path: the Rules File Backdoor hid instructions in invisible Unicode (pillar.security), and AGENTS.md injection exfiltrated credentials in Codex (backslash.security). Corvint elevates AGENTS.md, specs and decisions to top authority, so a poisoned governing file inherits that authority. No invisible or bidi character screening was found in internal/contextindex. A second gap: a governing file modified in the working tree or in the change under review (an agent granting itself authority) is not distinguished from committed authority in the packet or the CEM.

acceptanceCriteria: go-archive-gate-test and gate-receipt-test read modes with GNU stat first and pass on GNU/Linux and macOS.
error-code-ownership-check builds per-directory patterns with no empty alternative and passes under mawk, gawk and BSD awk.
check-host-package-versions.sh fails with `jq is required` when jq is absent.
Every gate step after go-test passes in golang:1.27.1 with jq, and the hosted release-gates ubuntu-24.04 full gate passes on the next candidate.
body: Observed in release-gates run 36344236053 (ubuntu-24.04 full-gate on 7075454e, job 108690109484): `make gate` stopped at go-archive-gate-test with `FAIL: a run that recorded its own witness did not pass`. Cause: script/go-archive-gate_test.sh:74 and script/gate-receipt_test.sh:79 read a mode with `stat -f '%Lp' X 2>/dev/null || stat -c '%a' X`. GNU `stat -f` is --file-system and takes no format, so it prints file-system status for X on stdout and exits 1; the fallback's mode is appended and never equals 700/600. Deterministic on every GNU/Linux host since the initial snapshot; only the macOS gate had reached these steps. Running every later gate step in golang:1.27.1 found two more portability defects that hosted ubuntu does not hit: script/check-error-code-ownership.sh:108,114 build alternations with `a[k] = (k in a) ? a[k] "|" x : x`; mawk creates a[k] before evaluating the right-hand side, so every pattern leads with an empty alternative and 363 non-code strings are reported unowned. script/check-host-package-versions.sh reads versions with jq and, without jq, reports a misleading stale bump for every package.
title: Gate scripts fail on GNU/Linux: BSD-first stat, mawk alternation order, silent missing jq

acceptanceCriteria: rewrite_cem and every other mutation return False when the loop never bound, and the variant is HARNESS-FAILURE with the run and receipts still written.

body: Observed in V1-0019 run-001 on Corvint (benchmarks/untouched-repository-v1/corvint, harness f24533a1...): every positive loop run was refused by dogfood change, so no .corvint/change.cem.json existed, and loop_rehearsal's L3c control (reencoded -> rewrite_cem) opened the missing file and raised FileNotFoundError at harness.py:564. The run exited 1 with only the started marker, no run file and no receipts. The comment above the mutations says a mutation that did not happen makes its variant HARNESS-FAILURE; rewrite_cem does not honour that. Also: `run --work DIR` refuses when DIR does not exist instead of creating it (smoke 8, first attempt). A harness change is a new numbered preregistration deviation; earlier runs stay.
title: Untouched-repository harness crashes when the loop's bind never happened instead of recording HARNESS-FAILURE

body:
Owner intent: make the LSP integration world class and use Corvint capabilities to provide the best possible information across use cases. This extends, and does not reopen or overstate, completed Go milestone V1-0476. Owner decision: BOTH upstream language-server enrichment for agents and a Corvint editor language server. The direction is accepted; technical profiles and qualification thresholds remain proposed. Current evidence: Go/gopls-specific provider, definition/reference expansion, fixed bounds, external evidence separated from ranking; no broad multi-language or outcome qualification. Existing V1-0168 workspace-loading and V1-0167 error-redaction tickets remain separate work and must be dispositioned with evidence. Do not treat every Corvint command as mandatory runtime work or claim support for every possible use case; define tested profiles and explicit unsupported cases.

# Bidirectional LSP quality plan — V1-0477

Owner decision: BOTH upstream language-server enrichment for agents and a Corvint language server for editors. This direction is accepted by the owner's chat response; technical profiles, language order, performance thresholds and promotion remain proposed. Existing Go integration V1-0476 is delivered and stays experimental. This plan is not a delivery claim.

## Product boundaries

Use one shared evidence compilation interface behind CLI/MCP and an optional native-Go stdio editor companion. The editor starts and owns the companion session; shutdown, EOF, cancellation and interruption retire its descendants. Core remains usable as one terminating native-Go binary with no required daemon, network service, account or new database. The companion and each upstream provider require a separately explicit deployment/execution profile. Do not turn on every Corvint tool for every request.

Maintain two distinct snapshot identities: immutable Git evidence (repository/root, object format, commit/tree/blob) and live editor overlays (session, canonical document URI, monotonically validated document version and content digest). Never label overlay text as committed evidence. Corvint context for committed content remains usable separately when a live view cannot be represented. Results identify their snapshot; stale/out-of-order responses cannot replace newer results. Close/save/reopen, branch changes, renames, root changes, generated files and Unicode positions need fixtures. Git status alone is not an editor buffer identity.

Compile applicable facts through existing trust boundaries: project-owned specs/instructions retain authority; upstream semantic facts, history and inferred relationships remain labelled evidence. Expose relevant definitions/references/types, impact, governing requirements, tests and actual test observations, CEM/OCM/frontier gaps, source documentation and explicit uncertainty. Learning/ranking changes require their own accepted contracts and frozen evaluation; never silently turn separated LSP evidence into a ranking input. Test suggestions, formatting/refactoring/rename edits and code actions are proposals, not permission to execute commands or modify files.

## Stages and dependencies

1. Contract and baseline: freeze the numbered capability/session/profile spec and requirements-to-tests matrix. Inventory languages, server versions, editors and workspace types; distinguish consumed, delegated, Corvint-enriched and unsupported capabilities. Register public representative fixtures plus a held-out corpus without reading protected existing holdouts. Define numerical quality/resource/latency targets from a recorded baseline before implementation or promotion; include baseline language-server-only and Corvint-only arms.
2. Upstream adapters (after 1; reuse V1-0168 and V1-0167): capability negotiation, executable/config identity, workspace loading, URI/encoding boundaries, cancellation, errors, no silent installs/downloads, and hostile response bounds. Repair loading and redact diagnostics before treating provider availability as success. Expand beyond Go only through independently qualified language/server/workspace tuples. Proposed first cross-language candidates are TypeScript and Python; order is not yet accepted. Adapter metadata maps each method to advertised support, limits and degradation reason, not a blanket language-supported boolean.
3. Shared snapshots and evidence joins (after 1): implement and test the immutable/overlay model, shared semantic query interface, provenance, stable identities, duplicate/conflict handling, budgets, invalidation and trust-preserving joins. Reuse existing Core/index contracts rather than adding a second authority store. Cross-language/framework links require witnessed evidence; absence is unknown. All consumers see the same underlying facts for the same admitted snapshot and request, though transport projections can differ.
4. Editor LSP companion (after 2 and 3): initialization/capability negotiation, document sync, request cancellation, diagnostics lifecycle, shutdown/exit/EOF, multi-root isolation and position encodings. Expose negotiated standard features through qualified upstream delegation and Corvint enrichment; expose Corvint-only evidence via documented namespaced extensions or editor commands. Capability matrix includes navigation, hover/signatures, completion, symbols, diagnostics, call/type hierarchy, semantic tokens/inlay hints, rename/refactoring/formatting and code actions; advertise only actually implemented/tested subsets, and keep edits version-checked and client-applied. Verify real VS Code and a second independent LSP client; existing VS Code integration is deferred under its own contract and is not reopened implicitly.
5. Agent integration (after 2 and 3): bounded task-specific semantic requests in CLI and MCP through the shared engine, explain selected providers/features and omissions, avoid unnecessary fan-out, preserve committed default output and cancellation/cleanup. A richer/longer-lived opt-in profile is explicit; ordinary CLI reads do not require the editor server. No automatic model calls, test execution or learning. Compare joined semantic evidence to prior packets with authority and uncertainty invariant tests.
6. Qualification and promotion (after 4 and 5): deterministic conformance plus real repos/workspaces, cross-language boundaries, missing dependencies, dirty buffers, rapid edits, branch/root changes, malicious/oversized output, provider crashes and cleanup. Freeze correctness/coverage floors, stale-result rejection, cold/warm p50/p95, memory/CPU, query/token cost and task outcomes per declared profile. Compare upstream-only, Corvint-only and combined arms. No world-class/superiority claim from synthetic parity, implementation presence or native evidence linkage alone. Publish supported/degraded/unsupported tuples with measured limits, rollback and explicit failed/unrun evidence. Keep parent open until delivered, integrated and qualified.

## Existing evidence and documentation

Current code: internal/lspprovider/provider.go, internal/lspevidence/context.go, docs/LSP.md. Governing boundaries: AGENTS.md invariant7, docs/specs/deployment-neutral-index-platform-v0.md, docs/specs/external-evidence-provider-v0.md, docs/specs/task-context-packet-v0.md, docs/specs/vscode-extension-v0.md. Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/387
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

`go run ./tools/qualify-opencode` (commit `25730ea`, OpenCode 2.0.19 on darwin/arm64) passed only on the third of three consecutive runs on the same machine. It then keeps OpenCode `UNQUALIFIED` until a manual retry. The two failures had different causes:

1. **Focused gate:** `TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts/GOC-V0-008…` failed in `integrations/host-adapters.test.mjs:101` (`CRB-V0-012 OpenCode exact transport, unicode bounds, receipt and env`) with `assert.equal(result.ok, true)`: `false !== true` after about 2017 ms. The machine was busy (a Docker lane reset was running), which suggests a fixed ~2 s bound on the fixture round trip.
2. **Native cleanup gate** (next run, machine idle): `observed command cleanup incomplete` listed three processes (`PPID 53543`, started during the run). They had exited by the time I inspected them a minute later, which suggests a race between the 20 ms observer and child exit.

Run 3, with nothing else changed, passed all 14 conformance groups.

## Request

- Make both bounds robust under ordinary load: an adaptive or longer deadline for the CRB-V0-012 round trip, and a short settle or retry window before declaring cleanup incomplete, while still failing on true survivors.
- Or have the tool report a transient/retryable classification distinct from a real failure, so wrappers can retry safely.

## Why it matters

The qualification record is bound to the exact `corvint` binary, so every source update needs a new run. Flaky runs silently drop an otherwise working host integration to `UNQUALIFIED`.

## Environment

macOS 26.7 arm64, Go 1.27.1, Node 24.11.1, OpenCode 2.0.19, Corvint `main` `25730ea`.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/388
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Make Corvint the system that keeps documentation, end-to-end tests, and follow-up work in step with every merged change. After a change request merges, one repeatable workflow should:

1. read the merged change, its description, and the linked work item with its parent hierarchy (for example, story → epic);
2. decide which documentation is stale, which behaviour lacks asserting tests, and what looks wrong;
3. open or update **one follow-up work item** that tracks the outcome;
4. open a **reviewable documentation change request**;
5. open a **reviewable test change request** for missing end-to-end coverage, with proof that the new tests are stable and actually assert;
6. **raise findings** (possible defects, scope mismatches, coverage gaps) where people triage them;
7. republish any derived corpus once the documentation change is approved.

Everything the workflow produces is a draft for human review at first. Specific content classes move to automatic merge only once measured correction rates earn it.

## Why Corvint

Most of the evidence engine already exists: revision binding (`status`, `record`, `witness`), drift detection (`docs flows check`), external evidence providers and fail-closed test selection (EEP-V0..V2, ETS-V0), test-validity receipts, `behavior-falsify`, and Tasks. PRS-V1-015 already requires automatic documentation that detects drift, previews updates, supports explicit apply, and never publishes itself. The product loop in `PRODUCT.md` ends with "merge-time independent re-verification → knowledge delta". Today every adopter has to assemble that loop by hand from CI YAML, scripts, and agent prompts, and each one invents its own containment, idempotency, and fail-closed rules.

## Scope boundary

Core stays as decision 0373 defines it: local, no network, no daemon, no authority. Anything that talks to a network, holds credentials, runs an agent, or writes to an external system belongs in a separately qualified companion, the way Tasks does. Core supplies deterministic, source-content-free records. The companion and the CI host act on them.

## Agnostic by design

- **Work tracker:** any tracker, through a connector contract. No tracker's field model is assumed.
- **Forge:** any forge that has change requests.
- **CI host:** any CI host. The trigger, runner, secrets, and schedule stay with the host.
- **Agents:** any coding agent. Corvint defines what an authoring step may read and write, and verifies it afterwards.
- **Stacks:** any language stack that Corvint's analyzers and providers cover.

## Sub-requests

- [ ] #389 corvint delta, one read-only source-content-free record for a merged change
- [ ] #390 range and path impact for non-Go languages (impact accepts only .go today)
- [ ] #391 closed-vocabulary intake for untrusted change context (descriptions, linked work items and their parents)
- [ ] #392 work-tracker and forge connector contract (read hierarchy, idempotent follow-up item, gated findings, draft change requests)
- [ ] #393 scope attestation for authoring agent steps in automated workflows
- [ ] #394 acceptance verdict for new end-to-end tests (repeat, falsify, validity in one record)
- [ ] #395 replay historical merges through the post-merge workflow with recorded writes
- [ ] #396 per-content-class evidence for earning automated merge
- [ ] #397 corpus republish from an approved documentation revision with provenance and parity
- [ ] #398 reference CI host templates and host adapter contract for the post-merge workflow
- [ ] #399 documentation corpus parity to replace bespoke corpus builders and servers

## Acceptance (for the umbrella)

- A reference workflow processes a merged change end to end with outward writes stubbed. It produces the follow-up item, the documentation change request, the test change request, and the findings as recorded requests, and it matches labelled expectations on a replay set.
- Replaying the same merge twice produces no duplicates.
- Untrusted text never reaches an authoring step except as validated closed-vocabulary fields.
- No authoring step can see a credential that performs an outward write.

Umbrella gap check 2026-10-05 at origin/main 8a35775a (lane claude/v1-0535-umbrella-acceptance; no code change; verdict CLOSE_WHEN_DEPS_LAND). Passing tests (go1.27.1, -count=1): internal/postmergeworkflow, postmergeconnector, intake, cmd/corvint-intake, stepverify, plus a focused postmergehost run.
(a) Proven: TestReplayActualRecording MATCH for follow-up and finding requests; TestReplayMismatchBasis; TestReplaySeparatesHumanVerifiedMismatches; PMC-V0-005. Missing: docs/test drafts through the workflow (PMR-V0-005 draft-scope-validation-unavailable; /1 follow-up-not-integrated; no /2 producer) and a historical replay set. Owners: V1-0542, and V1-0545 for the CI host run (PCH-V0-003/014).
(b) Proven: TestReplayTwiceIdenticalRecording, recording-not-idempotent refusal, PMC-V0-006/007. Missing: the repeat with drafts (V1-0542).
(c) Proven: binding/hash-only adapter Request; hostile title absent; PMC-V0-003; CVI-V0-005..007; TestNativeActualIntakeDeltaThenFollowUpRefusal. Missing: a real authoring consumer (V1-0542).
(d) Proven: environment sentinel in TestReplayActualRecording, ASS-V0-005, PCH-V0-007 TestAuthoringEnvironmentHasNoWriteCredential, TestHostEnvelopeCompleteEnvironment. Missing: physical isolation and a hosted run (V1-0545, PCH-V0-011/014).
When V1-0542 and V1-0545 land, rerun the replay over the historical set with drafts, twice, on the reference host, and record one evidence-only build-log entry mapping (a)-(d). The COVERAGE_UNKNOWN effects blocker remains.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/389
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Add a read-only Core command that produces **one source-content-free record for a merged change**. It should combine what a post-merge workflow currently has to collect from several commands.

## Requested capability

`corvint delta --base FULL_SHA --head FULL_SHA [--previous-generation FILE] [--provider ...]` prints one canonical JSON record containing:

- **Revision binding:** base, head, tree, the changed-path digest, and the Corvint build.
- **Documentation drift:** spans that are stale, retired, unchanged, or newly added, using the same identity rules as `docs flows check`.
- **Affected tests:** in-repository `affected`, plus cross-repository selection through registered EEP/ETS providers. When coverage is incomplete, the record says `run-full-suite` and names the missing evidence. It never returns a silent subset.
- **Uncovered behaviour:** flows or units touched by the change that have no asserting test link. Each entry names the gap type and its denominator.
- **Work-item keys:** extracted with a configurable pattern from commit metadata. The keys are opaque identifiers; no text is copied.
- **Unknowns:** everything Corvint could not classify, listed explicitly.

## Constraints

- Class `R0` (or `R0+SOL`) in the sense of `AUTOMATION.md`. The command makes no network calls and writes no state.
- No source excerpts, diff bodies, or ticket text appear in the record, only paths, identities, digests, enums, and counts.
- Output is deterministic for identical inputs.

## Acceptance

- A schema and conformance vectors are published.
- Given a fixture merge, the record is byte-identical across two runs.
- Incomplete provider coverage yields `run-full-suite` with the reason.
- A downstream workflow can decide "no-op, docs-only, tests-needed, findings" from this record alone.

## Why

Without this, a post-merge workflow has to call `status`, `affected`, `witness`, `docs flows check`, and one or more providers, then stitch the results together itself. Each adopter reimplements that join, along with the fail-closed rules that make it safe.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/390
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

`corvint impact` and the `corvint_impact` MCP tool accept only `.go` paths; the MCP input schema enforces a `.go` suffix. Repositories whose product code is Ruby, JavaScript, or TypeScript cannot get revision-bound impact evidence for a change. Flow documentation (`docs flows generate`) already recognizes several constructs in those languages: Ruby methods and jobs, literal Rails routes, JS/TS functions, and Angular registrations.

## Requested capability

- Range impact (`impact --base`) and path impact for the languages that already have analyzers (at least Ruby, JavaScript, and TypeScript), with the same receipt shape and explicit `unknown` entries for dynamic dispatch.
- A per-language capability table in `impact --help` and in the MCP tool description, so callers know what is covered.

## Acceptance

- Conformance fixtures for each added language, including negative cases where dispatch is dynamic.
- The MCP schema admits the new suffixes.
- Unsupported constructs appear as unknowns, not as absence.

## Why

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/391
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Provide a contract for turning **untrusted change context** into validated closed-vocabulary records before any authoring step sees it. Untrusted context here means change-request titles and descriptions, commit messages, and linked work items together with their parent hierarchy.

## Problem

A post-merge workflow needs to know what the change intended: the claimed behaviours, flags, migrations, the tests the author says they added, and whether the description matches the diff. It also needs the same for the linked work item and its parent (for example, acceptance criteria on a story and scope on an epic). That text is third-party input. An agent that holds write access and reads it directly can be steered by it.

## Requested capability

- **A published intake schema.** Every field is an enum, a repository path, an identifier, or a count; free text is forbidden. Suggested fields:
  - `intent`
  - `claimed_behaviours[{kind, path}]`
  - `flags[]`
  - `migrations_claimed`
  - `tests_claimed[]`
  - `description_vs_diff`
  - per-work-item `alignment`, `acceptance_criteria`, `concerns[]`, and `parent_review`
- **A validator.** It rejects free text, checks that every path exists at base or head, and normalizes ordering.
- **A reader-step contract.** It states what a reading agent may access (the raw input, read-only), where that input must live (outside the authoring worktree), and what it may write (exactly one intake file).
- **A containment battery.** Hostile fixtures, such as instructions embedded in descriptions or requests to create items or run commands, must produce output identical to their neutered twins apart from the `concerns` field. The battery also runs mutants of the input builder that must be caught.

## Constraints

- The schema and validator are deterministic and local, so they can be Core or a companion.
- Fetching the raw text is the connector's job (see the connector request), not Core's.

## Acceptance

- Schema, validator, and conformance vectors are published.
- The battery runs in CI and fails when a builder mutant leaks prose.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/392
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Define a companion **connector contract** for work trackers and forges, so post-merge workflows can read context and write outcomes without being tied to one vendor.

## Requested capability

**Read**
- A merged change request: identity, merge and base commits, changed files with status, author, and timestamps.
- A work item and its full parent chain up to a configured hierarchy level (for example, walking `parent` until reaching the epic level). The connector returns raw content only to the intake step (see the intake request).

**Write**, performed only by deterministic steps and never by an agent tool call
- **Upsert a follow-up work item.** Look it up by a stable key, such as a label derived from the merged change. Create it or update it. Set its parent to the resolved hierarchy item and link it to the source item. The body is rendered from a fixed template that interpolates only identifiers, enums, paths, URLs, and counts. Include a no-op rule, so changes with nothing to do create no item.
- **File findings.** File them against policy gates: an allowlist of classes, a per-change cap, a requirement that the cited path and line exist at the merge commit, and a rule that security-shaped findings are routed to restricted triage. Filing must be idempotent.
- **Open or update a draft change request** on a branch derived from the stable key, with a generated body.

**Client modes:** `live`, `recording` (writes the requests to a JSONL file), and `dry-run` (prints them). This lets whole workflows be tested without credentials.

**Credentials:** each connector declares the minimum scopes it needs. The contract states that credentials are available only to the writing step.

## Acceptance

- The contract, a conformance kit, and at least two reference connectors of different kinds are published.
- Running the same upsert twice yields one item.
- The recording mode's output is stable across runs.
- Tests show that a rendered body cannot contain strings outside the whitelist.

## Why

Every adopter currently writes this glue by hand: tracker field discovery, lookup by label, parent linking, and caps on findings. Without a contract, the parts that matter for safety (idempotency, a text whitelist, credential separation) are reinvented for each project.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/393
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Attest what an **authoring agent step** was allowed to do, and verify afterwards that it did only that. The step should be containable by any agent or host.

## Problem

In a post-merge workflow, an agent edits documentation or tests, and trusted steps then run generators, validators, and builds from the same worktree. If the agent can edit those scripts, fixtures, or policy files, the next trusted step becomes arbitrary code execution. Adopters currently hand-write `git status` pathspec gates and guarded-file lists in CI YAML.

## Requested capability

- **A step declaration.** It lists the paths the step may write and the paths that must not change, such as scripts, CI config, fixtures, schemas, policy, and agent instructions. It also lists the read-only checkouts and the environment keys the step may see. The declaration must not include credentials that perform outward writes.
- **`corvint step verify`.** Given the declaration and the pre- and post-step state, it produces a receipt that passes or fails and names every out-of-scope write, every modified guarded path, and every modified read-only checkout. It binds the receipt to commit, tree, and dirty digest.
- **An optional pre-step check** that the host did not expose undeclared environment keys to the step.

## Constraints

- Local, read-only verification, which fits Core rules. Enforcing it (stopping the job) is the host's decision.

## Acceptance

- Fixtures for each violation type.
- A receipt that downstream steps and change-request bodies can cite.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/394
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Provide a single **acceptance verdict for newly added end-to-end tests**, combining repeat runs, falsification, and validity into one record that can be attached to a change request.

## Problem

When an agent writes a new browser test, a reviewer needs three things proved: the test is stable, it actually asserts the behaviour it claims (it fails when that behaviour breaks), and it cleans up after itself. The pieces exist (`corvint-js-test-provider` receipts, `corvint.test_validity`, `behavior-falsify`, `playwright-minimize`), but each adopter wires them together differently.

## Requested capability

`corvint tests accept --new <spec paths> --repeat N --environment <label>` (as a companion), producing:

- per-test run results over N repeats with retries disabled, including durations and cleanup outcomes;
- a falsification result per test, where a mutated response or DOM condition must make it fail, and a test that still passes counts as non-asserting;
- test-validity axes, with Strength filled from the falsification result;
- an order-dependence probe when repeats disagree;
- one verdict, `accepted`, `rejected`, or `blocked`, with reasons, bound to the test-repository revision and the product revision it ran against.

The environment must be recorded, including the Corvint build.

## Acceptance

- A test known to be non-asserting is rejected.
- A test known to be flaky is rejected, with the order-dependence evidence attached.
- The verdict renders into a change-request body without needing further tools.

body:
Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/399
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Make Corvint's documentation corpus a **drop-in replacement for a bespoke documentation corpus builder and MCP server**, so a project can retire its own builder and serve the corpus through Corvint.

#31 delivered the generic revision-pinned compiler and MCP. #339 delivered lossless import of existing corpora, including sharding, typed records, and a parity report. What's left is **query parity, scale, and a switch-over path**. Adopters who already have a bespoke corpus server can then move their agents and the post-merge workflow (#388) onto Corvint without losing any answers.

## Gap today

The `docs corpus` CLI reads include `info`, `validate`, `search`, `get`, `trace`, `related`, `journey`, `stability`, `locate`, `coverage`, and `gaps`. The corpus MCP exposes only `docs_info`, `docs_search`, `docs_trace`, `docs_find_related`, `docs_get_journey`, `docs_get_stability`, and `docs_unknown`. Typical bespoke documentation servers also answer the following:

- **Locate code for a concept.** Given a phrase, return the flow, the source paths, and the anchors.
- **Claims by source file or symbol.** Given a path, return the typed claims with line anchors and trust status.
- **Flow details.** Return a flow's sections, entry points, and related flows in one call.
- **Dependency tracing across flows.** Report upstream and downstream flows for a change.
- **Coverage and gaps.** Report test coverage by flow and journey with a named denominator. List the gaps by type: missing asserting end-to-end tests, no tests, missing manual cases, stale journeys, and stale anchors.
- **Test recommendation for changed paths.** Map paths to flows and reviewed test links, and recommend the full suite with named missing evidence whenever coverage is incomplete. This should share the ETS-V0 semantics.
- **Navigation and UI evidence.** Return routes, screens, and selectors tied to flows.
- **Vocabulary resolution.** Map business terms and aliases to flows and features.
- **Intent comparisons and "why".** Return ticket or change history, separating recorded intent from observed behaviour.
- **Trust envelope on every answer.** Include the content status (generated or verified), the source and corpus revisions, stale state, retirement by age or by merge distance, citations, and limitations.

## Requested capability

1. **MCP parity for existing CLI reads.** Expose `get`, `locate`, `coverage`, `gaps`, and `validate` over MCP.
2. **Typed query tools.** Add tools for the capabilities listed above, over the typed records that #339 already preserves: claims, eight-section flows, test-link roles and confidence, coverage membership, ticket history, and intent comparisons.
3. **A uniform trust and retirement envelope.** Return it on every response. Report empty results as "not documented", never as "does not exist".
4. **An indexed artifact profile.** It must handle large corpora (tens of thousands of claims and thousands of symbol anchors) with bounded memory, and each build must be byte-reproducible.
5. **Parity harness for switch-over.** Given a bespoke server's recorded question set and answers, run the same questions against Corvint and report per-tool agreement, missing answers, and extra answers. The same output supports a side-by-side period before the old server is retired.
6. **Serving.** The local stdio transport stays as it is. Hosted serving should be available as a separately qualified companion transport with an embedded artifact and no live source access, consistent with decision 0373.

## Acceptance

- MCP exposes every CLI read.
- The typed query tools have conformance vectors.
- The parity harness runs against a recorded question set and reports agreement per tool.
- Two builds of the indexed artifact from identical inputs are byte-identical.
- Every response carries the trust envelope.

## Why

A post-merge workflow (#388, #397) has to republish the corpus that agents query. While that corpus is served by a bespoke builder and server, each adopter keeps maintaining a second system with its own provenance, trust, and gap semantics. If Corvint's corpus reaches parity, Corvint can be the single place where documentation evidence is compiled, checked, and served.


Part of #388.

Owner exploration request 2026-09-30: "I'd like you to explore them. Current evidence: docs/CHANGE-EVIDENCE-MAP.md:140-197 already has typed evidence roles, structural supported semantics, coverage and bounded mutation witnesses. docs/specs/ocm-v0-dogfood.md:42-65 enumerates scoped requirements. Browser behavior falsification already supplies criterion/assertion-bound controls and outcome classification. The accepted hypothesis catalog docs/specs/applied-intelligence-breakthroughs-v0.md:54-68 already describes missing-test generation with fail-before/pass-after or registered mutation qualification. Tasks external review binds canonical acceptance, candidate, gates and reviewer-attested claims, while its CEM/OCM fields remain unsupported/null (docs/specs/corvint-tasks-external-agent-review-v0.md:36-40,71-79). Do not advertise any of these methods as new inventions or universally adequate proof.

Hypothesis: portable criterion-experiment records can preserve useful experimental evidence across task planning, candidate review, integration and later edits. The record joins exact canonical acceptance revision/claim identity, CEM patch/hunk group, reviewed expected observation, same oracle package and constructed execution trees, configuration/toolchain/runner identities, all original attempts, valid registered wrong alternatives, contradictory observations and unresolved cases. Ask which registered wrong alternatives remain compatible with the current evidence and use that bounded set to select the next useful test. Absence of a surviving registered alternative never means absence of all bugs.

Prototype first as a separate experimental adapter packet beside canonical CEM 0.2; do not invent a promoted cem/0.4 wire or change frozen vectors. Keep CEM reference-only/local/source-content-free, deterministic consumer offline, execution in a separately invoked contained runner. No default LLM generation, daemon, hosted database, account or new queue. An opt-in Tasks policy may consume exact criterion coverage and experiment receipts bound to acceptance/generation/candidate; existing command gates, independent review and integration remain required. Semantic mapping and oracle authority remain reviewer-attested with independent owner-accepted criterion evidence, not inferred from implementation outputs. Preserve all old completion receipts as history; subsequent stale applicability produces maintenance proposals in the existing queue, not retroactive erasure or silent reopening.

Use separate behavioral relations for repair, preservation and new behavior; no universal fail-before rule. A base-incompatible imported test is unsupported comparison. Controls must compile, reach the expected assertion, preserve declared setup/unrelated criteria and clean up; crashes or unrelated failures do not count as kills. Equivalent controls are applicability unknowns. Freeze selection before execution and retain all requested/rejected/omitted/applicable/executed denominators and retries. Any candidate/oracle/dependency/config/acceptance/policy change initially invalidates current applicability; selective reuse awaits qualified exclusion witnesses. No global causality claim.

Independent bounded native Codex critique (Astra/medium, 2026-09-30) supports a prototype of lifecycle evidence but found no established product superiority. It specifically required stronger oracle authority, exact base/candidate execution-tree bindings, denominator controls and a matched stronger-testing baseline. No product tests or comparative trial were run during this exploration. Installed Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build163 and Tasks build202; official check observed v1.0.0-rc.1 and tasks-dev-20260929.2, with publisher identity NOT_VERIFIED and broad qualification absent.

Related existing work V1-0499 (bounded mutation), V1-0501/V1-0195 (proof review), V1-0504 (synthetic tour), V1-0197 (receipt bundle) stays open/unchanged. This is a comparative research question spanning lifecycle evidence, not a replacement for those delivery tickets.

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/420
Direct owner requested fixing newly filed GitHub tickets on 2026-10-01 in the ongoing all-issues batch. Preserve original complete issue intent below. Independent baseline confirms the reported behavior; no source repair or live policy/store migration performed. Core rc.1 build163; Tasks developer build202.

## Summary

The queue policy accepts `retries.admissionsPerRevision`, but the retry-exhaustion checks ignore it. A queue cannot change its retry budget, even after the #412 hand-off accounting fix (PR #414).

## Evidence (main @ d693d28)

- `internal/tasks/intent/policy.go:257` parses the field: `p.AdmissionsPerRevision = boundCount(rt.Field("admissionsPerRevision"), 0, wire.MaxAdmissionsPerRev)`. `wire.MaxAdmissionsPerRev` is 3, so the policy cannot raise it above 3.
- `internal/tasks/transaction/lease.go:36` defines `MaxRetries = 3`. Exhaustion uses that constant, not the policy value: `internal/tasks/transaction/lease_handoff.go:20` (`exhaustedAttempt`), and the plan and retry-recovery paths noted in #412.

## Impact

Our multi-agent queue (361 tickets, 3 lanes, up to 16 concurrent external agents) loses a retry whenever an agent session dies or its lease expires. With HANDOFF/REVIEW_RETURNED, clean hand-offs are now free, but crash or expiry still uses a retry. The budget of 3 cannot be tuned, and every exhaustion needs an OWNER `ticket reopen`.

## Request

Wire `retries.admissionsPerRevision` into the exhaustion checks, in claim, preview and owner recovery alike. Allow a policy value above 3 within a documented bound, or document that the field is informational and reject values other than the constant.

Follow-up to the last comment on #412.
title: GH #420: corvint-tasks: retries.admissionsPerRevision is parsed but never enforced; exhaustion still uses the hard-coded MaxRetries = 3

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/421
Direct owner requested fixing newly filed GitHub tickets on 2026-10-01 in the ongoing all-issues batch. Preserve original complete issue intent below. Independent baseline confirms the reported behavior; no source repair or live policy/store migration performed. Core rc.1 build163; Tasks developer build202.

## Summary

PR #414 (#412) added retry-free HANDOFF and REVIEW_RETURNED releases. `docs/TASKS-EXTERNAL-AGENTS.md` doesn't mention them, and an adopter has to read `transaction/lease_handoff.go` to learn the preconditions. Two common hand-off shapes also can't qualify.

## Undocumented preconditions (from `verifyHandoff`, main @ d693d28)

- The claim must use `--stage implement` or `--stage review`. A claim without a stage, or with `--stage integrate`, is refused (`TICKET_STATE`), and REVIEW_RETURNED needs `review`.
- The attempt must be in phase BUILT or CHECKING, with a submitted `CandidateTreeOid`, `ScopeCheck == WITHIN` and no pending effects. Otherwise it is refused with `MISSING_EVIDENCE`.
- The ticket acceptance revision and policy must not have changed since the claim. A `policy update` while attempts are live makes every in-flight hand-off fail with `STALE_POLICY`.

`grep -n -i "HANDOFF\|REVIEW_RETURNED" docs/TASKS-EXTERNAL-AGENTS.md` returns nothing.

## Hand-offs that can't qualify

1. **Work outside the queue repository.** Our agents write matrices, reviews and test code in other repositories; the queue repo only tracks `.taskman/`. To qualify, an agent must `submit` the tree of the claim's `baseCommit`, which changes no paths. It can't submit `HEAD^{tree}`: an integrator commits `.taskman/` while it works, and those paths fall outside its declared scope. Submitting an unchanged tree only to unlock the accounting is a workaround, not evidence.
2. **Integrate stage.** Integrator and full-suite-baseline attempts on a reserved `integrate` lane can't hand off cleanly at all.

## Requests

- Add a hand-off section to `TASKS-EXTERNAL-AGENTS.md`: stages, the submit requirement, reason codes, refusal codes, and the effect of a policy change on live attempts.
- Provide a supported hand-off for attempts whose work lives outside the queue repository, for example `release --reason HANDOFF --evidence <ref>` with no candidate tree, or an explicit "no tree" submit.
- Decide whether the `integrate` stage should get HANDOFF, and document the decision either way.
title: GH #421: corvint-tasks: document HANDOFF/REVIEW_RETURNED releases for external agents, and support hand-off without a candidate tree and at the integrate stage

Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/422
Direct owner requested fixing newly filed GitHub tickets on 2026-10-01 in the ongoing all-issues batch. Preserve original complete issue intent below. Independent baseline confirms the reported behavior; no source repair or live policy/store migration performed. Core rc.1 build163; Tasks developer build202.

## Summary

Per-command `--help` is inconsistent in `corvint-tasks` (main @ d693d28). External agents learn flags by trying `--help`. When it errors, they guess flags or read source, and in our queue the guessing has cost retries.

## Observed

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `corvint-tasks ticket create --help` (and other `ticket` mutations) | OK: operation and `payloadKeys` |
| `corvint-tasks policy update` (no args) | usage text in warnings |
| `corvint-tasks plan preview --help` | `ERROR`, warning `unknown plan flag` |
| `corvint-tasks release --help` | `ERROR` `MALFORMED: argv: unknown flag --help` |
| `corvint-tasks submit --help` | `ERROR` `MALFORMED: argv: unknown flag --help` |

Top-level `corvint-tasks help` lists usage lines. It doesn't list the `--reason` values that `release` accepts for hand-offs, though `HANDOFF` and `REVIEW_RETURNED` do appear in the general `releaseReasonCodes` list.

## Request

Make `--help` a read-only, `OK` outcome for every subcommand. Return that command's usage, flags and, where relevant, its accepted reason codes. `release` should spell out its hand-off preconditions (see #421).


## Observed public-main composition after PRs #424 and #416

acceptanceCriteria: A generation-fenced heartbeat records lastHeartbeatAt without extending the work lease.
Queue and attempt reads distinguish fresh, stale, and unobserved holder signals; stale does not free reservations or prove physical quiescence.
Focused compatibility, stale-generation, TTL and journal tests pass; independent review and linked immutable change evidence are retained.
body:
## Problem

A dead agent's attempt blocks its ticket, and its demo-pool lane, until the work lease expires. Nothing in the queue tells other agents whether the holder is still alive.

Attempts carry one long work lease (60 minutes in our program). When an agent host dies (crash, context exhaustion, host process killed), `queue status` still shows its attempts as `RUNNING` until `expiresAt`. A coordinator then has two options:

- wait for expiry, which blocks the ticket and lane and still costs a retry when it is reaped; or
- guess that the holder is dead and release the attempt on its behalf.

Observed on 2026-10-01 (build `main-d693d28`): an OpenCode orchestrator host exited and took its sub-agents with it. For about 40 minutes the queue held 8 attempts whose holders were dead, two of them with allocated lanes. Successive coordinator sessions could not tell the attempts were orphaned. Some coordinators chose to treat them as live, so nothing ran; others released them, at the risk of cutting off a live agent.

## Request

A liveness signal separate from the work lease, for example:

- `attempt heartbeat` (or `renew --heartbeat`) with a short TTL, such as 5–10 minutes, and `lastHeartbeatAt` shown in `queue status`/`attempt show`;
- a derived state such as `STALE_HOLDER` once the heartbeat TTL passes while the work lease is still valid;
- optionally, a holder-supplied liveness token (host session ID or PID) recorded on claim, so that a supervisor can check it.

Coordinators could then release only provably stale holders, and keep their retries through the `HANDOFF --evidence` path, instead of guessing.

body:
## Problem

An agent can't see how much of a ticket's retry budget is used until a claim is refused with `RETRY_EXHAUSTED`.

On `main-c4de689`, `ticket show <id>` returns `currentAttempt`, `eligibility` and `nextAction` but no retry accounting. Neither does `plan preview`. Per-attempt `retryCount` is only visible through `attempt show` on a known attempt ID, and that is lost once the attempt ends. Now that `retries.admissionsPerRevision` is configurable (#420), operators also need to see how close each ticket is to its limit.

## Request

Show retry accounting on `ticket show`, and summarise it in `plan preview`/`queue status`:

- `retries: {charged, limit, remaining, byReason: {EXPIRED, RELEASED, FAILED, ...}}` for the current acceptance revision.

This would let coordinators prefer hand-off releases for nearly exhausted tickets, and raise an alert before exhaustion rather than after.

## Problem

There is no read-only CLI for the live queue policy. `corvint-tasks policy --help` lists only `policy <update>`, and `policy show` fails with `policy needs the verb update`, on both `main-d693d28` and `main-c4de689`. To prepare an update (`--expected-policy-version N --file PATH`), operators read `.taskman/policy.json` directly. The help also doesn't say whether the file must carry the incremented `policyVersion`, or whether the store assigns it.

## Request

- `policy show` (and `--help` for it) that prints the effective policy, its version and SHA-256.
- In `policy update --help`, say how `policyVersion` in the file relates to `--expected-policy-version`. Optionally add `policy update --dry-run` that validates the file and shows a diff against the live policy.

body:
## Problem

`ticket create` can't create a ticket with a chosen, human-meaningful ID, and its help suggests that it can.

On `main-c4de689`:

- `corvint-tasks ticket create --help` lists `[--target TICKET|LOCAL --expected-revision N]` in the shared usage line.
- `ticket create --target BT-002 --payload-stdin` fails with `MALFORMED: targetId: CREATE names no target or expected revision`.
- Without `--target`, the ticket gets the next queue-prefix ID: `ticket:flowproof:main:FP-0001`.

Our program names work packages by board ID (`BT-001`, `F0-5`, `FL-016.matrix`). Imported tickets keep those IDs, but a ticket created through the CLI cannot. So agents and dashboards must map `FP-0001` back to `BT-002`, in the title, the BOARD and the prompts, and that mapping can drift.

## Request

- Let CREATE take an optional explicit ID or alias, validated against the queue's ID grammar and refused if it collides. Or support an `alias` that `ticket show`, `claim` and `plan preview` accept.
- Fix `ticket create --help` so it doesn't show `--target` for CREATE, or explain `LOCAL`/`localToken` there.


Source: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/430
Source cf4c8a39 already accepts localToken in CREATE payload; confirmed defect is misleading CREATE help and poor discoverability. Preserve the existing collision and queue grammar checks.
title: corvint-tasks: ticket create can't set a meaningful ticket ID, and --help implies --target works for CREATE

acceptanceCriteria: Decision recorded: qualify the store state dir instead of the Git common dir, or keep the common dir with a stated reason, with the TM-V0-010 text updated to match.

body:
Observed 2026-10-01 while qualifying a Codex host for `corvint-tasks dispatch` (V1-0475; PR stacked on beamfall/corvint#436).

Every store mutation calls `authority.Qualify(repo.CommonDir)` (internal/tasks/store/*.go). That writes an O_EXCL probe `.taskman-qualify-<pid>-<random>.tmp` directly in the Git common dir (internal/tasks/authority/qualify.go:45), while the journal lives in `<common>/taskman`. A sandboxed worker host therefore cannot grant only the store's state directory.

Reproduction (codex-cli 0.153.2, macOS):
- run `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<repo>/.git/taskman"]'`;
- have the worker run `corvint-tasks ticket claim`.

Expected: the claim succeeds, because the store's own state directory is writable.

Actual: the claim fails UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM, because the probe in `<repo>/.git` is refused. It succeeds only when all of `<repo>/.git` is writable. That root also lets the worker write refs and objects, which widens what an operator must grant to a sandboxed agent.

Idea: qualify (and probe in) the directory that actually holds the store state, `<common>/taskman`, creating it first if TM-V0-010 allows. Alternatively, document why the common-dir root is required. This changes the TM-V0-010 qualification root, so it needs a spec amendment.
title: Tasks store: qualify the taskman state dir so sandboxed hosts need not write the whole Git common dir

acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce or bound the race (e.g. run with -count=200 under CPU load), and record the outcome.
If confirmed: the producer acquisition is synchronized with the observer (barrier or fifo), so the test cannot miss the window. The fix is verified with a repeated run under load.
If not reproducible: the ticket is closed with the evidence, and the CI failure attributed elsewhere.
body:
Suspected flaky test (not yet confirmed as a defect). Observed 2026-10-01 in CI on beamfall/corvint#434 (head 0bce80fe, run 36914793900, job go-product-shard (1)):

    work_materialization_unix_test.go:189: actual producer did not acquire scratch under observer ownership
    --- FAIL: TestWorkActualProducerInterruptedScratchCleanup (2.18s)

#434 changes only internal/tasks/dispatch and docs; this test (cmd/corvint) is unchanged since the public snapshot.

Hypothesis: the poll loop in cmd/corvint/work_materialization_unix_test.go (~lines 156-180) globs `corvint-work-source-*` every millisecond and SIGSTOPs the group once a path appears. A fast producer can create and remove its scratch directory between polls and exit, so `acquired` stays empty. The comment there already names the race with a normally completed short acquisition; the loop narrows it but cannot close it.

Expected: the test deterministically observes the producer holding scratch (e.g. the producer blocks on a test-controlled barrier or fifo after acquisition), or it records a skip-with-reason when the window was missed. It should never fail on timing.

Actual: an intermittent FAIL on a loaded hosted runner. The failed jobs were re-run.
title: Suspected flake: TestWorkActualProducerInterruptedScratchCleanup can miss the producer's scratch window

acceptanceCriteria: The check result for each component states the relation between installed and available builds, or UNKNOWN with a reason, without the caller comparing strings.

body: Observed 2026-10-01, darwin/arm64. `corvint-update check --allow-network --component tasks` returned installedVersion 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202, installedBuild 202, availableTag tasks-dev-20260929.2, freshness RELEASE_OBSERVED, action check. `--component core` returned installedBuild 163 and availableTag v1.0.0-rc.1. Neither result carries an available build number or a comparison outcome. For Core the tag matches the installed version string, so the reader can infer it is current. For Tasks the installed version string and the dated tag share no comparable field, so an agent cannot tell from the check whether an update exists, whether the local build is newer, or whether apply would be a downgrade. Expected: the check states the relation (for example CURRENT, UPDATE_AVAILABLE, LOCAL_NEWER, or UNKNOWN with the reason). Actual: the relation is left to the caller. No update was applied in that session for this reason. Also observed: installedVersion for tasks embeds the whole JSON command result of `corvint-tasks version` as a string instead of the version value.
title: corvint-update check does not say whether the available release is newer than the installed build

acceptanceCriteria: `queue status` and `plan preview` read no receipt below the retained checkpoint when one is usable, proved by a test that counts receipt reads.
A checkpoint read returns the same selected records, sequence and head binding as the complete audit, and any unusable checkpoint or unsettled journal yields exactly the complete audit's answer.
Reads never create, replace or delete the checkpoint; `receipt audit` and every writer keep the complete audit.
Measured before/after wall time on the live store is retained in the build log, with the checkpoint read's detection limits stated in the spec.
body:
## Problem

GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#446. `queue status` and `plan preview` replay the whole receipt chain on every call. On this store at 1,829 receipts a build of origin/main e5d96823 took 4.5-4.9 s for `queue status` (three complete audits plus an attempt inventory scan); the issue reports 9-22 s at about 1,350 receipts under load. The cost grows with history and widens the window in which a concurrent writer moves the snapshot.

## Change

1. One memoized journal audit per read command; projections reuse the capture's intent digests.
2. A writer-retained derived checkpoint (`taskman-audit-checkpoint/0`, sibling of the state directory). Reads rebind it to its receipt, walk only later receipts with the unchanged validators, verify every projection, and fall back to the complete audit on any doubt. `receipt audit` and every writer stay complete.

Spec: CAL-V0-059..061 in docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md.
title: corvint-tasks: queue status and plan preview cost scales with receipt history (GitHub 446)

acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether and under which durability and rebinding rules a writer may skip the receipt prefix.
If accepted, mutation cost at 2,000 receipts is measured before and after, with duplicate-request and fork counterexamples still refused.

Delivers beamfall/corvint#641 (owner, 2026-10-06: writer cost must be milliseconds, not seconds): a heartbeat, renew or claim write on a synthetic store of at least 13,000 receipts completes in milliseconds (median of 5 well under 1 s, measured with the load band recorded), and stays flat from 3,000 to 13,000 receipts.

receipt audit is unchanged; removing the derived checkpoint forces the full audit, documented in the spec and --help and covered by a test; the checkpoint is bound to the chain head and the refresh-versus-write race is tested.
body:
## Observation

Found while fixing GitHub 446. After CAL-V0-059..061 reads resume from a checkpoint, but every mutation still walks the whole receipt chain: `store.Mutate` runs a request-index lookup audit and then `reader.Audit`, and lease writes run `AuditForWrite`. At 1,829 receipts one complete audit is about 1.1 s on this host, so each write costs 1-2 s and grows with history. A read that meets a pending receipt also falls back to the complete audit.

## Request

Decide whether writers may resume from a durable, verified checkpoint (the read checkpoint is deliberately best-effort and not write authority), what must be rebound for request-id replay detection (the read checkpoint omits `requests/`), and how often the complete audit must still run. Merge the two audits in `store.Mutate` where the protocol allows.

## GitHub 494 follow-up (2026-10-03)

Source: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/494 (created 2026-10-03T22:45:27Z). Reporter observed claim/heartbeat/release elapsed times of 10-41 seconds with about ten workers and 5,750 receipts on main-32aa5a3; idle read calls took 0.31-0.61 seconds. Twelve of 23 worker sessions in the 22:00 hour reportedly timed out; memory pressure (about 7 GB compressor, substantial swap) is a confounder. The report does not identify the exact executed Tasks binary. Local inspection uses official Tasks build 202 and immutable source dd8cc0ca918a80faaa041c98a783de11550b2bcc; this is not proof of reporter-runtime parity.

Deduplication: this ticket owns the existing history-scaling/performance decision. V1-0626 concerns retry visibility, not proof of a no-attempt charge. Do not call the issue's EXPIRED/no-start report a confirmed accounting defect without matching request, receipt, attempt and generation evidence. Distinguish a claim committed before caller timeout from a claim that never committed.

Current source evidence: internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:69 invokes AuditForWrite on a cache miss, before lock acquisition; internal/tasks/journal/audit.go:109 still performs a complete audit. Its cache is in-process, so one-shot CLI calls do not share successful audits. internal/tasks/store/mutate.go performs request lookup and a second complete audit while holding the writer lock. These source facts support investigation, not latency attribution under the reported workload.

Next proof: a disposable representative 5k-receipt/10-worker reproduction, phase timing for preflight/audit/lock/write, exact binary and host conditions, same-request replay and cancellation at pre/post-commit boundaries, and an honest documented latency envelope. Do not bypass full writer verification or promote the best-effort read checkpoint to write authority. Preserve the original acceptance criteria and qualify any changed durability/rebinding contract independently. No load test was run against the canonical live queue.

Additional bounded source observation: `leaseWrite` at immutable dd8cc0c internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:224 allows up to 16 prepare/commit rounds; `SNAPSHOT_MOVED` invalidates the whole preparation and triggers another full audit. Concurrent independent writers can therefore amplify preparation cost even though lease audits are outside the lock. Measure restart count as well as lock wait; a global-lock-only diagnosis is unproven.

Found while fixing GitHub 446. With a usable checkpoint `queue status` takes about 0.25 s on this store (860 canonical paths). Share one intent-tree observation between the outer snapshot probe and the journal capture, without weakening the two-capture movement check.

acceptanceCriteria: `queue status` and `plan preview` started inside a writer's receipt-to-head window succeed on the new head once the writer finishes, within a bounded wait, instead of reporting NOT_RUN/REDO_PENDING at once.

A moved snapshot is paused on and re-read within the same budget; only a writer that outlives the budget ends REDO_PENDING or SNAPSHOT_MOVED, and that failure names the wait and says the read is retryable.
The waiting read writes and locks nothing (product invariant 4): the store is byte-identical after a read that gave up.
Covered by maintained tests in internal/tasks/snapshot and internal/tasks/cli, with the spec requirement traced in docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#433 (owner, 2026-10-01). Reproduction: about ten agents running corvint-tasks mutations concurrently; a read-only `corvint-tasks queue status` or `plan preview` returns NOT_RUN with code REDO_PENDING (also SNAPSHOT_MOVED, per the issue comment); retrying about two seconds later succeeds. Version: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202 on Core at ff3da727e95a1999cbc4a58a471cdd498693f902. Expected: a healthy store with a writer in flight is not a failed read; the condition is retryable and the reader should wait it out. Actual: snapshot.Reader.Read reported a probe-level REDO_PENDING at once and retried a moved snapshot three times back to back with no pause, so a read landing in the section 5.2 window between receipt link-in and head rename, or straddling consecutive commits, failed. The issue's `outcome: ERROR` came from the external dispatcher; outcomeFor already maps both codes to NOT_RUN. Fix: spec requirement CTS-V0-006 (docs/specs/corvint-tasks-store-init-v0.md), bounded patience with backoff in internal/tasks/snapshot/probe.go, build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-01-tasks-read-waits-for-in-flight-writer.md, branch claude/i433-read-redo-pending. Related: V1-0309 (panel F2, readers report in-flight writers as crashes).

body:
Owning GitHub issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/464 (reported against main-25ba271). Reporter evidence and requested behavior:

## Problem

`corvint-tasks dispatch` (`main-25ba271`, workState kind `command`): when the dispatcher receives SIGTERM while the work-state command is running, the command's context is cancelled. The tick still continues with every ticket's work state set to `UNKNOWN`. On the next start, every ticket flips back.

Observed 2026-10-01 at 23:04Z on a 365-ticket queue:

```
alert   work state command: context canceled
state   MX-5 changed: status OPEN→OPEN, work state NONE→UNKNOWN, plan BLOCKED (...)→BLOCKED (...)
...     (one line per ticket)
stopped dispatcher stopped; 2 worker(s) left running for the next dispatcher
started ...
state   MX-5 changed: ... work state UNKNOWN→NONE ...
```

In total there were 704 spurious "state changed" events in `events.jsonl` from one restart. They drown real transitions for subscribers such as our timeline and notifier.

## Request

When the dispatcher is shutting down (context cancelled), skip the rest of the tick: don't apply `UNKNOWN` states and don't emit change events. More generally, consider not emitting per-ticket `state` events when the only change is the work state moving into or out of `UNKNOWN` because of a reader failure; one `alert` line is enough.

body:
Owning GitHub issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/468 (reported against main-25ba271). Reporter evidence and requested behavior:

## Problem

`corvint-tasks dispatch` parks tickets that are making real progress, when that progress lives outside the queue.

The progress fingerprint (CAL-V0-057, `Fingerprint` in `internal/tasks/dispatch/roster.go`) covers the ticket's status, revision and work state, plus attempts that carry durable work: a candidate, gates, reviews or a durable phase. A worker that does a session of real work and then hands off with the clean external hand-off `release --reason HANDOFF --evidence <ref>` (#421) leaves none of those. Its work is commits on a WP branch, documents and an updated status file, and the hand-off records no candidate. The dispatcher counts the run as "no progress", cools the ticket down, and parks it after `parkAfter` runs.

Observed on 2026-10-01 at 23:38Z (`main-25ba271`): `INV-1`, a multi-session inventory WP, was parked ("3 dispatcher run(s) made no progress"), although each of those sessions committed partial inventory and rewrote its status file. Every long-running WP in a program like ours hits this eventually.

Our workaround is in our `workState` command: it appends a variant suffix (`work~3` and so on), derived from the WP status file's mtime, so that a changed status file changes the work state. Every role then has to list all the variants.

## Request

Let the program declare progress explicitly. Any one of these would do:
- the `workState` command may return `{"state": "...", "progress": "<opaque token>"}` per ticket, and the token is folded into the fingerprint but never matched by roles;
- count a hand-off whose `--evidence` reference differs from the previous one as progress, possibly behind a per-role `progressOnEvidence: true`;
- optional `progressPaths` per role (like `activityPaths`), whose content hash is folded into the fingerprint.

body:
## Summary

Agents holding a lease must heartbeat and renew while a long command (test suite, image build) runs. `corvint-tasks` offers `attempt heartbeat` and `renew` but nothing that does this around a command, so every orchestration writes its own guard script in the agent's shell. In a multi-agent program these ad-hoc guards repeatedly failed: shell/Python syntax errors in generated guard code (the command then never ran), guards that outlived the command, and missed beats that let the lease expire mid-run and fenced the hand-off (`FENCED`, then the lane stayed allocated until reap).

## Request

Add a command such as `corvint-tasks run --attempt ID --generation G --timeout SECONDS [--lease-minutes N] -- COMMAND...` that:
- heartbeats before, during (default every ~4 min) and after, and renews so the lease covers the timeout plus cleanup;
- runs the command in its own process group and kills the group on timeout or when a beat/renew is refused (fenced/expired);
- returns the command's exit status with distinct codes for timeout and lost lease, and records a receipt of the outcome.

## Evidence

2026-10-02, native queue with ~10 concurrent agents: two review/integrate sessions ended with "bounded runner failed before executing: SyntaxError" in their own guard code, and earlier BT-002 attempts expired mid-Playwright and had release refused as FENCED. We now ship a small external wrapper (a stdlib script with tests), which suggests this belongs in the queue tool.

Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/497; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
`corvint-tasks dispatch` has static caps (`globalCap`, per-role `cap`). When the host is saturated the dispatcher keeps launching workers, queue mutations slow to minutes (see #494), sessions die on claim/heartbeat timeouts, and every timeout wastes a session and can charge a retry. The operator can only lower the caps by hand and reload, which cannot track load that changes hour to hour.

Observed (main-32aa5a3, one 10-core macOS host, ~11 concurrent OpenCode workers plus a Docker VM): load average 50-170 on 10 CPUs, swap 67-70%, 12 of 23 worker sessions in one hour lost to claim/heartbeat timeouts.

## Request
Native, optional host-pressure throttle in the dispatch config, e.g.
```json
"pressure": {"loadPerCpuHigh": 5, "loadPerCpuCritical": 8, "swapHigh": 0.8, "swapCritical": 0.9,
             "calmLoadPerCpu": 3.5, "calmSwap": 0.7, "ticksToChange": 2,
             "levelCaps": {"1": 5, "2": 3}, "exempt": ["pinned"]}
```
- Sample load/swap each tick, apply hysteresis, and cap NEW launches of non-exempt roles at the level cap. Running workers are never stopped; pinned/critical-path tickets and review/integration roles stay exempt.
- Show the level, inputs and held tickets in `dispatch status` and as an event (`throttled`).

## Workaround in use
A steward script computes the level and `workState` emits `hold-load` for excess authoring tickets. This works but duplicates logic that belongs next to the launch decision.

Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/498; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Releasing a pool attempt leaves the member QUARANTINED ("logical attempt ended; physical safe reuse unproved"). Freeing it needs an agent to run the lane's reset + health and then `pool confirm-safe`. We spent many LLM sessions on this: they hit the 120 s tool limit during the 3-5 minute reset, `confirm-safe` itself timed out (#494), and lane-2 stayed quarantined for 30+ minutes repeatedly, which blocked the critical-path ticket (a G2 review needs that lane).

## Request
Let a pool definition declare how safe reuse is established, and let Corvint do it:
```json
"members": [{"id": "lane-2", "safeReuse": {"argv": ["scripts/demo-env/reset","--lane","2"], "verify": {"argv": ["scripts/demo-env/health","--lane","2"], "expectExit": 0, "expectStdout": "ready_for_mapping: true"}, "timeoutSeconds": 900, "maxAttempts": 2, "env": "file:lanes/lane-2.env"}}]
```
- `corvint-tasks pool sweep [--member M]` (and an option for the dispatcher to run it automatically) runs reset then verify, records the evidence, and applies the confirm-safe transition itself, with an idempotent request id and a bounded retry.
- On failure the member stays QUARANTINED with the captured exit codes and logs attached to the receipt.

## Workaround in use
`tools/fp-lane-sweep.py` (reset, health, confirm-safe with retries, verifies FREE via queue status because a timed-out confirm-safe may still commit), started by a steward loop.

Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/499; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Some tickets make no progress for many consecutive sessions on the default model, while a stronger model would likely finish them. Today the operator watches the event log and hand-edits roles. We built this in an external work-state script, but the dispatcher is where it belongs.

## Request
A role-level escalation ladder keyed on consecutive no-progress sessions per ticket:
```json
"roles": [{"name": "matrix-worker", "model": "A", "escalate": [{"after": 3, "model": "B"}, {"after": 6, "model": "C", "notes": "operator-visible"}], "deescalateOnProgress": true}]
```
- Count trailing `finished ... no progress` sessions per ticket from the dispatcher's own events; any progress resets it.
- Surface the current tier and streak in `dispatch status`, emit an `escalated` event, and let a worker at the top tier attach a typed NEEDS-OPERATOR request (see the escalation request).
- Per-tier caps so a stronger, scarcer model is not flooded.

## Workaround in use
`workState` returns `t1-`/`t2-` prefixed states and duplicate roles per tier (cap 1 each, separate role-claim slots).

Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/500; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
`corvint-tasks dispatch` and the supervisor script are long-running, but nothing restarts them after a crash or reboot, and the surrounding helper loops (health, steward) have the same gap. We found that a killed steward loop stayed dead indefinitely and a reboot would have stopped the whole program silently.

## Request
`corvint-tasks service install|status|uninstall --program P` generating and managing the OS unit (launchd LaunchAgent on macOS, systemd user unit on Linux) that keeps the supervisor/dispatcher alive, honors the existing stop file/drain, does not kill adopted workers on restart, and exposes liveness in `dispatch status`. A documented hook for registering extra helper commands to keep alive would cover site-specific loops.

Pitfall we hit: a launchd job that starts processes and exits kills them unless `AbandonProcessGroup` is set; the generated unit should handle this.

## Workaround in use
A LaunchAgent running a keepalive script every 2 minutes that restarts the supervisor, steward loop (also when its log is stale) and health loop.

Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/501; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Operator guidance to a ticket's next worker has no first-class channel. We prepend notes to the ticket's status file. Over a few days one ticket accumulated 9 stacked, partly contradictory operator notes ("owner must reopen" after reopen was refused; a 40-call cap beating an 80-call override). Workers burn their budget reading them, and some obey stale ones. One whole review session was lost this way.

## Request
`corvint-tasks ticket note set --target T --text ...` / `note clear` / `note show`, with these semantics:
- exactly one CURRENT note per ticket; setting a new one archives the old (still readable via history);
- shown in `ticket show` and in the claim result so the worker gets it without reading files;
- timestamped by the queue (never the caller), so notes cannot be future-dated (which workers distrusted twice);
- optional `supersedes` check against a revision to avoid racing edits.

## Workaround in use
`tools/fp-note.py`: archives all older top-of-file operator notes to an evidence file and writes one CURRENT line.

Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/502; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Workers escalate by writing `NEEDS OPERATOR:` into a status file. There is no type, so infrastructure failures and real decisions look the same. In practice most escalations were claim/queue timeouts (#494), which parked tickets and made workers set `needs-human`, while real product-scope questions were mixed in. The operator has to read files to tell them apart, and nothing clears the request when it is answered.

## Request
`corvint-tasks ticket escalate --attempt A --kind decision|infrastructure|scope|blocked --question "..." [--options a,b]` and `ticket answer --target T --text ...`:
- `infrastructure` escalations are retried by the dispatcher (bounded) and never park the ticket;
- `decision`/`scope` appear in `dispatch status` and a queryable list, and an answer is delivered to the next worker through the claim result (see the ticket-note request);
- the park decision uses the kind, and open escalations carry age so stale ones are visible.

## Workaround in use
A steward script greps first lines for claim/timeout wording, removes the line, resets the state and tells the worker to retry.
