Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/503; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem (semantics unclear, verified on main-32aa5a3)
After claim timeouts consumed all six retries, `ticket show` reported `retries: charged 6, remaining 0, exhausted: false`, status `OPEN`, and `plan preview` showed the ticket SELECTED. `ticket reopen --role OWNER --expected-revision 6` was REFUSED with `TICKET_STATE`. One unambiguous state. Either `remaining=0` means exhausted (status RETRY_EXHAUSTED, reopen allowed, not SELECTED), or the field is not shown as 0 while the ticket is still claimable. `ticket show` should include a `claimable: true|false` plus the reason, and the reopen refusal should say which condition failed.

body:
Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/504; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Review verdicts (G1 matrix review, G2 lane review) exist only as markdown headings and bold lines in per-ticket status files, and the scheduler parses them. The parser misrouted tickets three times: prose "No G1 PASS is claimed" read as a pass; author sections titled "G1 RETURN repair dispositions" read as newer RETURNs, so a resubmitted matrix kept going to authors (10 of 24 sessions without progress); and a second RETURN that arrived after a resubmit line was invisible to the worker. Each cost many sessions before it was noticed.

## Request
Record verdicts as queue-native gate results (`gate record --ticket T --gate G1 --verdict PASS|RETURN --attempt A --reasons ...`), plus a `resubmit` event from the author, and expose them to `workState` (`gates: {G1: {verdict, generation, resubmitted}}`) so routing needs no text parsing. Related: #394 (acceptance verdict for new tests) would be a natural producer of the G2 record.

## Workaround in use
One parser module with regression tests built from the real misroutes.

acceptanceCriteria: A table-driven test runs each shipped hook adapter (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode where hook-based) under: corvint binary absent, index unavailable, empty stdin, malformed stdin, stdout closed before write, and a host deadline shorter than the adapter's internal budget.

Every case exits with the host's non-blocking status and emits a FALLBACK or degradation code naming the cause; no case returns a blocking exit code, hangs past the host deadline, or writes outside the declared local ledgers.
The adapter's per-invocation process spawns are counted in the test and no adapter spawns a login shell.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from the owner's request to learn from claude-mem (github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, shallow clone at bfc50259f64a, 2026-10-03). Its plans/17-hook-wrapper-contract.md groups 25+ user reports where a hook blocked or looped the host: a login-shell PATH probe on every invocation (250-420 ms on macOS, 1-10 s on Git Bash), exit 2 on an unreachable worker turning the Stop hook into an endless wake loop, a global cross-session failure counter that escalated to blocking, printf write errors on a closed pipe, empty stdin silently disabling capture, and synchronous SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks whose internal budget equalled the host wire timeout. Their remedy is a contract: the wrapper resolves nothing it can cache, spawns nothing it does not need, never writes to a closed pipe, and cannot return a blocking exit code for an availability failure. Corvint adapters already degrade to FALLBACK (see completed V1-0286 and open V1-0607/V1-0396 for deadline reporting), but there is no single cross-host matrix proving the non-blocking property under each failure. Proposal: one table-driven conformance matrix run against every shipped hook adapter. This is an idea, not a confirmed defect: no Corvint hook has been observed blocking a host in this session.
title: hosts: fail-open conformance matrix for every hook adapter (worker absent, empty stdin, closed pipe, cold start, slow PATH)

body: Filed 2026-10-04 from the owner's request to learn from claude-mem (github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, shallow clone at bfc50259f64a, 2026-10-03). Its plans/18-observer-response-pipeline.md documents silent data loss because every non-conforming LLM reply fell into one bucket that confirmed the claimed batch: prose instead of XML, auth/model/transport errors arriving as assistant text, context overflow, empty replies, schema drift, and a hard-coded max_tokens truncating 76% of responses; history buffers were also unbounded. Their remedy is one explicit classifier with one policy table mapping each output class to {preserve batch | confirm batch | abort with reason}, plus a budget on every history and buffer. Corvint mostly avoids LLM-authored evidence, but some paths ingest host or model output: daily-loop and harness task observations (open V1-0369 is an instance: the cost gate accepts unmatched and failed task observations as savings), doccompiler admission of generated documentation, and any learning inputs. Question: is there a single inventory of these ingestion points, and does each refuse or abstain on an unrecognised output class instead of accepting it?

The reused run id and tree id are retained as an artifact.
The fraction of main commits with a completed or reused result is reported before and after.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 during a CI audit (Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163, Tasks build 202) at origin/main e5d47da8; hosted run https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/actions/runs/37198363933 (4 shards, 295 packages, 5635s summed package time, race steps 1924/1647/1397/1264s). Idea. Every merge to main reruns the full 33-minute suite, and 30 of the last 65 main push runs were cancelled by cancel-in-progress, so about half of main commits have no completed CI result of their own. When the pushed commit's tree id equals the tree of a PR merge ref that already passed go-product under the same workflow and runner identity, the result is evidence for the same immutable content. Proposal: a trusted first job compares tree ids and records the reused run; otherwise run in full. Separately decide whether main pushes should queue instead of cancel so each merge keeps a result. Related: CORE-GITHUB-MERGE-QUEUE-COMPATIBILITY-1.
title: ci: reuse a passed PR result on the main push when the merged tree is byte-identical to the tested merge

acceptanceCriteria: The workflow triggers once per PR head, has a concurrency group and uses the pinned runner and environment guards.
Either the job is folded into go-product or its distinct purpose is stated in the workflow.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 during a CI audit (Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163, Tasks build 202) at origin/main e5d47da8; hosted run https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/actions/runs/37198363933 (4 shards, 295 packages, 5635s summed package time, race steps 1924/1647/1397/1264s). Confirmed by reading .github/workflows/intake-containment.yml at e5d47da8: it triggers on both push (all branches) and pull_request, so a PR branch push starts two runs; it has no concurrency group, uses ubuntu-latest rather than the pinned ubuntu-24.04, and sets none of the GOPROXY=off/GOWORK=off/GOFLAGS guards the other jobs use. It tests ./internal/intake and ./cmd/corvint-intake without -race; both are in the root module and already run with -race in go-product. Whether the non-race run is an intended separate signal is not recorded.
title: ci: intake-containment runs twice per PR push and repeats packages go-product already runs

acceptanceCriteria: A check fails when the number of unbounded test packages rises above a recorded ceiling.
The ten most expensive unbounded packages have declared, Landlock-enforced read scopes or a recorded reason they cannot.
Selected seconds as a share of the full suite is reported for each PR and retained.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 during a CI audit (Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163, Tasks build 202) at origin/main e5d47da8; hosted run https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/actions/runs/37198363933 (4 shards, 295 packages, 5635s summed package time, race steps 1924/1647/1397/1264s). Measured with installed Core build 163 on a clean clone: corvint affected --base FIRST_PARENT over the last 20 first-parent merges selected 144 to 193 of 295 Go packages, 86% to 92% of summed test time, scope UNKNOWN every time. A merge that only adds two .corvint/changes CEM files selected 147 packages: 141 UNBOUNDED_READER and 6 PATH_LITERAL_READER. The 141 unbounded units hold 4213s of 5635s; the largest are internal/testacceptance 953s, appflows 348s, companionrelease 224s, tasks/authority 206s, extevidence 194s, tasks/store 171s. So activating selection today would save about 10%. The count has grown from 103 (V1-0081) and 129 (V1-0246) to 141. Proposal: (1) a ratchet check that refuses a new test package with no declared read scope or an increase in the unbounded count; (2) bound packages in order of hosted seconds, not package count; (3) report selected seconds per PR in the step summary as an advisory shadow metric. V1-0246, V1-0081, V1-0649, V1-0634 and V1-0635 own the bounding mechanics.
title: affected: ratchet unbounded test readers; they hold 75% of CI test time and keep selection at 86% for a docs-only change

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the seven listed memories is classified with its chosen layer (product change, refusal text, helper/make target, check, or out-of-repository host limit) and the reason a lower layer was not chosen.
Every in-repository item has a merged change or its own filed ticket, and each merged change has a test or check that fails on the original friction.
The owner deletes or shortens each memory whose workaround is no longer needed, and the remaining memories name the ticket that would retire them.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from an owner-requested review of michael-denyer/pstack-claude (lesson: encode a repeated lesson in structure, not in more instruction text). Claude Code sessions on this machine carry per-project memory files that exist only to work around Corvint, Corvint Tasks or shell friction, and each new session re-reads them and still trips on the first attempt. Current workaround memories (~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/memory/): (1) corvint-tasks-payload-canonical: mutations refuse non-canonical JSON (key order, whitespace, unsorted set arrays) instead of canonicalizing or naming the exact fix; (2) corvint-tasks-ticket-create-payload: create needs all 20 closed keys with no emitted template, and enum values (kind, effects.coverage) are discovered by MALFORMED refusals; (3) corvint-tasks-intent-branch and corvint-taskman-store-routing: mutations need the primary checkout HEAD on main, and the projection carry from a feature branch is a manual multi-step recipe; (4) line-citations-check-reads-head: the doc citation check reads HEAD, so uncommitted edits are checked against stale content; (5) dogfood-bind-amend-breaks-trace: amending after the first bind pass breaks the trace store; (6) interactive-rm-cp-aliases: zsh rm/cp aliases prompt and hang non-interactive agent shells, so repo scripts must call command rm/cp; (7) codex-cli-headless-lanes: the required Codex model flag and the draft-PR refusal hook. Related: V1-0242 (route future friction to the earliest preventing layer) covers the policy; this ticket is the concrete backlog of existing memories. Each item should land at the earliest layer that removes it: product behavior or a clearer refusal, a repository helper or make target, a check, or a documented host limit when nothing in this repository can fix it.
title: Encode agent-memory workarounds as Tasks/dogfood behavior, helpers or checks, then retire the memories

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded decision chooses repository test, local read-only doctor, V1-0413 extension, or no check, with the reason, and names how host-file findings stay local, uncertain and non-authoritative.

If a check is chosen, a fixture reproduces both 2026-10-04 contradictions (draft-PR rule against the refusing hook, merge-approval rule against a merge-preauthorizing memory) and the check reports each one.
The check reports UNKNOWN, not a pass, when a host file it needs is absent or unreadable.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from an owner-requested review of michael-denyer/pstack-claude (it pins skill rules with tests and checks that skill references resolve). Two contradictions between instruction layers reached agents on this machine before anyone saw them: (a) AGENTS.md standing publication approval required draft pull requests while a machine PreToolUse hook refuses the draft flag (V1-0640); (b) AGENTS.md said merging needs explicit approval while a saved Claude Code memory and ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (2026-10-03 standing merge preauthorization) told agents to arm or perform merges. Both were resolved by hand in an uncommitted AGENTS.md edit on 2026-10-04. Agents meet the conflict at run time and pick one side silently or ask. Spike: decide whether and where a check belongs. Candidates: a repository test over AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule pairs with a small table of known host-side settings; a read-only local doctor command that reads the host hook and memory files the owner points it at; or an extension of V1-0413 (per-host instruction load set) that also reports disagreeing rules. Host files outside the repository are not Git-pinned evidence, so any finding from them must be labelled local and uncertain (invariants 1 and 2) and never become authority (invariant 3).
title: Detect contradictions between project instructions and the owner's host hooks and agent memory

acceptanceCriteria: A benchmark over a representative 87KB receipt and a 13KB native report is retained before and after.

Every existing secretscreen match and redaction test passes unchanged, and a differential test shows the faster path returns the same match set as Pattern on a retained corpus including all current positive fixtures.
internal/testacceptance and internal/behaviorfalsify hosted race times are retained before and after.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 while diagnosing V1-0715 (Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163) at origin/main 2ffb4c53, darwin/arm64, go1.27.1. Confirmed measurement, optimization. secretscreen.Pattern scans at about 1 microsecond per byte: one MatchString over an 87,204-byte encoded behaviorfalsify EvidenceReceipt took 101-113ms, a 12,673-byte native report 14ms; under -race the same scans took 2.15s and 0.3s (about 22 microseconds per byte). Pattern.MatchString instead of FindAllStringIndex made no material difference (96ms vs 101ms), so the cost is the NFA over the large case-insensitive alternation, not match collection. behaviorfalsify.VerifyReceipt re-encodes and screens the receipt on every call: plan preimage, every hook and native byte field (raw text, each decoded JSON string, each key=value), then the encoded document again with the same bytes as base64; one verify of a 4-attempt receipt took 462ms without race. A CPU profile of TestPTFV0ParentCompleteAttemptOutcome under race attributed about 47% of samples to secretscreen.writerMatches. Expected: screening cost that does not dominate receipt verification. Candidate directions, none evaluated: a sound literal prefilter that proves no alternative can match before running Pattern; screening each retained byte field once per verify rather than raw plus base64; avoiding the masked copy in writerMatches when no PASS marker is present. Any change is security-sensitive: it must not reduce what is detected.
title: secretscreen: Pattern scans at about 1 microsecond per byte and receipt verification rescans the same bytes

acceptanceCriteria: A run with a TMPDIR longer than 128 bytes passes or skips with a clear reason, not an identifier-length failure.
The same tests still pass with a short TMPDIR.
The two failing tests are named in the fix with the identifier source.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Two internal/tasks/store tests fail when TMPDIR is long (e.g. /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-.../scratchpad/...) with 'identifier longer than 128 bytes'. They fail identically on main at the BASE 4b10a021 era and pass with a short TMPDIR. Reproduce: GOTOOLCHAIN=local TMPDIR=<path longer than ~100 bytes> go test -count=1 ./internal/tasks/store/. Expected: tests do not depend on TMPDIR length, or skip with a clear reason. Actual: failure from an identifier derived from the temp path exceeding the 128-byte bound. Which two tests and which identifier is not yet recorded; the cause (a path-derived identifier) is an inference from the message.
title: internal/tasks/store tests fail with 'identifier longer than 128 bytes' when TMPDIR is long

acceptanceCriteria: Failing tests are named from a reproduced loaded run.
Fixtures use condition or event waits, or deadlines scaled without weakening what is asserted.
The tests pass 20 consecutive runs under a saturating load.
body:
Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. The PSR (pool sweep, PSR-V0-*) store tests in internal/tasks/store flaked on a heavily loaded host and passed when run alone. Item 11 (#498 store tests sensitive to host load: PSR reconcile/dispatch tests in internal/tasks/store) appears to be the same family and is merged here; confirm when diagnosing. Suspected, not confirmed: timing-based waits or fixed deadlines in the fixtures. Related prior load-flake tickets: V1-0395, V1-0455, V1-0636. Reproduce: run go test -count=1 ./internal/tasks/store/ concurrently with a CPU-saturating load, then rerun alone. Expected: deterministic under load (event/condition waits, not wall-clock). Actual: intermittent failures under load, pass alone. The failing test names were not retained.

Additional evidence 2026-10-04: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, origin/main b46a3e27, corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202. `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=1 -run TestPSR ./internal/tasks/store/` was run three times while three concurrent agents were running Go test suites on the same host. With TMPDIR resolved to the non-symlinked /private/var/folders/zc/wb4tdm4x0c9dpkmkn8rdg9rw0000gn/T/, it failed only TestPSRDeadlineRetryMatrix/retry-success (8.08s; pool_sweep_lifecycle_test.go:326: commands reset=2 verify=0; package 172.4s). With TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/td, run straight afterwards, all PSR tests passed (138.5s). With the default symlinked TMPDIR, there were 49 UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM failures, which are V1-0753, not this ticket. Inference, not confirmed: the deadline-retry matrix belongs to this load-sensitive family, and the long resolved path played no part, because V1-0723's identifier error did not appear.

Additional evidence 2026-10-05: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, batch branch 4390ee3e (PR #570). The TestPSR* tests in internal/tasks/store timed out while running concurrently with other packages and go vet. Rerun alone they passed (85s), and the whole package passed (353s). This names the failing family as TestPSR*; individual subtest names were not retained.
title: PSR pool-sweep and reconcile/dispatch store tests are sensitive to host load (merges item 11, #498)

acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction shows which bytes differ between branch and main serializations.
A test or check fails when a committed INDEX.json is not in canonical form.
INDEX.json serialization is identical across generators, or a make target regenerates it deterministically.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Observed on PRs #513, #516, #517 and #518 on 2026-10-04: merging main into the branch re-escapes docs/specs/INDEX.json entries (spec index), so INDEX.json conflicts need manual keep-both resolution. Suspected, not confirmed: the generator/serializer escaping differs between branches (e.g. HTML escaping or non-ASCII forms) so identical entries differ byte-wise. Reproduce: branch from origin/main, add a spec entry, merge a newer main that also added one, inspect the conflict. Expected: serializer output is canonical and stable so independent entries merge cleanly, or a documented regeneration command resolves the conflict. Actual: whole-entry diffs in INDEX.json. Related: V1-0515, V1-0029.
title: Merging main into a branch re-escapes docs/specs/INDEX.json entries and forces manual keep-both conflict resolution

acceptanceCriteria: A test fails when the busy() guard is removed.
A test shows a sticky role keeps its tier after progress outside a session.

The 'model only in activity path' subtest asserts something that fails on the defect.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. PR #518 (#499 escalation ladder, ticket V1-0696) review findings. LOW-A: progress between sessions during cooldown resets the ladder but keeps the NoProgress backoff count, so the next no-progress session can park the ticket on the base model. This interacts with the open parkAfter owner question. LOW-B test gaps: (1) no test covers removing the busy() guard; (2) nothing checks that a sticky role keeps its tier after progress outside a session; (3) the 'model only in activity path' subtest is regression-only (cannot fail on the original defect). title: Escalation ladder (#499/PR #518) review LOW-A/LOW-B: ladder reset keeps NoProgress count; test gaps

acceptanceCriteria: Back-to-back merges to main each end with a completed (not cancelled) required-check run.
Pull request runs still cancel superseded runs.
The change names how the bridge precondition reads check state.
body:
Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Suspected and partly verified read-only: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 8-10 declare concurrency group '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}' with cancel-in-progress: true. For push events to main the group is the constant ref refs/heads/main, so a later merge cancels the in-progress run for the earlier main commit. When merges land close together a merged main commit can end without completed required checks, blocking the primary-main bridge precondition 'T required checks green'. The actual cancelled runs were not enumerated here. Expected: every main commit gets completed required checks (e.g. group by github.sha for pushes, or cancel-in-progress only for pull_request). Actual: earlier main runs cancelled. Related: CORE-GITHUB-MERGE-QUEUE-COMPATIBILITY-1.

Confirmed 2026-10-12 with the merge queue enabled on main (ruleset 23699808): queued merges land every 8 to 14 minutes while a full main-push CI run takes about 25, so each merge cancels the previous main push run. Push run 38295017392 on main commit 8fb53b265e1e2a46eb7fe8534c16c4bc288a96bc (PR #840) and push run 38295889750 on 21758ccd84d154114fb0bcef00fd98762ba408d3 (PR #847) ended go-product failure with SHARDS_RESULT=cancelled after the next queued merge pushed main. The same commits carry go-product success from their merge_group runs (38292100504, 38292857291), so the queue gate held, but each main commit now shows a failing go-product check run. merge_group runs are unaffected because each queue branch is its own concurrency group. V1-0760 (reuse the queue run on the push) would shorten but not remove the window.
title: CI for main pushes is cancelled by the workflow concurrency group, so merged main commits can lack completed required checks

acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether creation/retirement ownership can be proven and by what mechanism.
If adopted, a test fails when a leader group not created by the parent Owner is enabled.
The spec's known-limit text is updated or removed accordingly.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. The c443 transport adapter's gitstatus.EnableOwnedWorker proves only process-group leadership of the worker, not that the parent Owner created or will retire the group. This is a known limit recorded in docs/specs/aggregate-local-outcome-v0.md (PR #524), which is not in the local checkout at this base, so the symbol was not re-verified here. Expected: ownership evidence binds the group to its creating Owner and its retirement path. Actual: leadership only. Idea: define what proof would close the limit and whether it is worth the cost.
title: c443 transport adapter gitstatus.EnableOwnedWorker proves only process-group leadership, not parent Owner creation or retirement

acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction or reasoned demonstration shows which hazard is real.
Existing tests using the helpers still pass.
One shared helper replaces the copies with a bounded timeout and no detached maintenance.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Suspected, partly verified by read: internal/liveverify/affected/golang/golang_test.go:137 defines runGit, which runs exec.Command(git, -C root, ...) with os.Environ() plus fixed identity/config vars, CombinedOutput, no context or timeout, no process-group cleanup, and no auto-maintenance disabling (gc.auto/maintenance.auto). Near-identical helpers exist at internal/liveverify/mutate/mutate_test.go:125 and internal/liveverify/pymutate/pymutate_test.go:134 (those return output). Hazard (inference): three divergent copies drift; a hung git blocks the package until the test timeout and background auto-maintenance can race t.TempDir cleanup, the failure class of V1-0351, V1-0427 and V1-0662. Expected: one shared hardened test helper (timeout, group cleanup, maintenance off). Actual: three copies. Needs verification before changing.
title: Duplicated runGit test helper (internal/liveverify/.../golang_test.go:137) inherits the environment with no timeout or maintenance guard

acceptanceCriteria: The owner states the helper's purpose, opt-in mechanism and relation to V1-0598.

An opt-in mocha test helper was noted during work, but the repository has no detail on it: git grep for mocha outside docs/build-log finds nothing, and the only related ticket is V1-0598 (Mocha execution has no matching affected-test runner registration), which concerns runner registration, not a helper. acceptanceCriteria: 'corvint-tasks help ticket' returns ticket-verb usage.
'corvint-tasks ticket --help' lists verbs instead of an ERROR.

body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. acceptanceCriteria: The docs give a clone recipe with no 'git remote set-url'.
The recipe is shown to complete the dogfood loop up to bind in a fresh clone.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Agent subagent fresh-clone setup is blocked by the auto-mode classifier on 'git remote set-url origin' (flagged as 'Remote Repoint'). The documented plain-clone dogfood loop needs a remote. Suggestion: document a clone recipe that needs no repoint, e.g. 'git clone <url>' directly so origin is correct from the start, in the dogfood docs (docs/DOGFOOD.md) and agent instructions. Expected: the recipe completes without any remote rewrite. Actual: the repoint step is refused in auto mode and the session stalls. Related: V1-0272, V1-0182.
title: Document a plain-clone recipe for agent sessions that needs no 'git remote set-url origin' repoint

acceptanceCriteria: A process-exit path (os.Exit after an adapter watchdog or dogfood event deadline) kills every live child process group the adapter started, including git spawned by gokernel, gitstatus and contextindex, before exiting.
TestAHI044HookAdaptersFailOpen's slow-git case reports Git outliving the adapter by under 100 ms across -count=5, and the outlived bound is asserted rather than logged.
No new daemon, no login shell, and no change to the hook exit status or stdout contract.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 while building V1-0711 (AHI-044 fail-open matrix, branch claude/v1-0711-fail-open-matrix, base be98482b). When the adapter watchdog or dogfood event deadline abandons a git read and main calls os.Exit, exec's asynchronous context Cancel (process-group SIGKILL, internal/gokernel/process_unix.go) has not run yet, so the git child and its descendants survive the adapter. Reproduction: go test -count=3 -run TestAHI044 ./cmd/corvint/ with the slow-git PATH shim (logs pid, /bin/sleep 5, exec real git). Observed: 'Git outlived the adapter by' 3.763s and 3.772s (codex Stop / slow git on PATH) and 4.801s (claude-code session-end / slow git on PATH); every other case 0-43 ms. Expected: no child outlives the adapter process. Impact is bounded: the reads use --no-optional-locks and V1-0711 removes the private status scratch at exit (gitstatus.CloseScratch), but a hung real git would keep running after the host considers the hook finished. Spawn sites with Setpgid are many (gokernel, contextindex, cem/gitrun, worksource, ...), so the fix is a shared live-group registry consulted at exit, analogous to gitstatus.CloseScratch.
title: hosts: git children abandoned by an adapter deadline outlive the adapter because os.Exit beats exec's group kill

acceptanceCriteria: A failing package in a full pull-request shard is visible on the pull request (annotation, summary or a non-required check) before the shard finishes its remaining packages.
The required go-product check and the executed package set are unchanged.
Time from run creation to the first visible failure is measured on retained failed runs before and after.
body: Found while delivering V1-0716 (2026-10-04). Affected-first ordering moves the first failing package earlier inside a shard (replay over 12 failed runs: summed package time to the first failing package median 8.7 to 4.9 minutes), but `go test` still runs every remaining package, so the check result and the log only reach the author when the shard ends. Idea: stream the `go test -json` output through a small protected filter that writes a GitHub error annotation or step-summary line as soon as a package reports fail, without changing the exit status or the package set. Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-04-ci-affected-first-order.md. Hosted effect NOT_OBSERVED.
title: ci: surface the first failing package of a full shard before the shard ends

acceptanceCriteria: TestWorkspaceBranchRootAndHealthy passes 20 consecutive runs under the same contention.
The cause of the load-dependent failures is identified from a reproduction under CPU contention, or the suspicion is closed with evidence.
body: Suspected defect, not confirmed. Observed 2026-10-04 on macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1, Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163) while running affected packages for V1-0714 and V1-0716 with host load averages between 45 and 130. Run 1 (V1-0714 worktree): internal/lspstdio hit the 30m package timeout. Run 2 (V1-0716 worktree at 99e13a88, 43 packages in one go test invocation): TestWorkspaceBranchRootAndHealthy subtests root, healthy and save failed at workspace_guard_unix_test.go:93 with `healthy initial: map[error:{"code":-32801,"message":"Overlay definition unavailable"} id:2 jsonrpc:"2.0"]`. Both times `go test -count=1 ./internal/lspstdio` alone passed immediately afterwards (14.7 s and 9.5 s). Neither change touched the package. Expected: the test passes or reports a deadline; actual: an overlay definition request is answered as unavailable under contention, which suggests a fixed wait or a readiness race in the test or the stdio server. Hosted CI occurrence: NOT_OBSERVED.
title: tests: internal/lspstdio TestWorkspaceBranchRootAndHealthy fails under host load (suspected readiness race)

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded decision states whether the Claude Code adapter gains a function-hook module, with the host versions observed and the early-access limit retained.
If accepted, the host-adapter spec gains requirements with stable IDs covering coexistence with the command hooks, no double delivery, and the untrusted-data envelope on every new injection surface.

A prototype hooks module passes `claude plugin validate` and `claude plugin test` on a host that has them, and a live session shows the stale-snapshot degradation as an operator-visible status with an explicit refresh action.
compatibility.json records the function-hook surface separately from the command-hook PASS, as NOT_RUN until a black-box lifecycle run exists.
body:
Claude Code now loads function-hook plugins (mods): a hooks module named in hooks/hooks.json under `modules`, exporting register(on, options), with in-process hooks ($, e, next), a 10,000 ms per-dispatch budget, $.process.run, $.ui (status, toast, pane, AbovePrompt band), $.command.register, $.clock timers, $.state/$.store, and events the command hooks do not expose (prompt.context, prompt.section, session.compact, tool.call, tool.check, turn.complete, agent.spawn, classic.*). Observed 2026-10-04 in the desktop session engine 2.1.286 (declaration file written by the engine); the API is labelled early access and moves between releases. The `claude` on PATH is 2.1.267, has no `plugin test`, and its `plugin validate` reads only the manifest of the shipped plugin.

The shipped corvint@corvint plugin (adapter 0.2.x) is seven command hooks at a 1-2 s timeout calling `corvint adapter claude-code <event>`. Friction reproduced in the same session: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit both degraded with `corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale`, and the only remediation is prose asking for a manual `corvint index --if-stale`.

Candidate uses, each needing its own spec decision: (1) an operator-visible status entry and a /corvint command or button that runs `corvint index --if-stale` as an explicit, operator-started action, so invariant 4 and the no-automatic-refresh rule hold; (2) session.compact to carry the compaction pin in-process and verify it on the way up, replacing the PreCompact/PostCompact pair that has no live cycle evidence; (3) tool.call on Read/Grep and agent.spawn for the point-of-use and SubagentStart ideas already ticketed; (4) a read-only pane rendering the last packet, degradation code and frontier state. Constraints to settle first: the module has no Node and no DOM, so it stays a thin shim over the Go binary; the mod path must coexist with the command hooks for hosts without function hooks and must not double-fire; untrusted repository data must stay enveloped when it enters prompt.context or session.append; a mod carries no Frontier authority.
title: hosts: evaluate a Claude Code function-hook module (mod) for the corvint plugin

body: Filed 2026-10-04 from the V1-0712 output-class inventory (docs/build-log/2026-10-04-v1-0712-output-class-inventory.md), source origin/main a2615609. Confirmed from source, runtime NOT_RUN. The writers of the two private ledgers enforce closed contracts (unplannedread HookPostToolSession: closed tool set and projectpath containment; observations Append/validateWriterContract: closed kinds, codes and validObservationPath). The readers do not re-apply them. unplannedread foldRow (unplannedread.go:804) skips non-JSON rows without counting them and treats any row with an empty kind as an unplanned read, so {} adds an empty path and {"path":"../../x","bytes":-5} adds an escaping path with negative bytes. observations readRow (observations.go readRow) re-validates only proof and adapter-degradation rows; a hand- or agent-written file-change event with touchedPaths ["../../x"] becomes a Miss, and rows failing strictJSONObject or renderedKeysLineSafe are dropped uncounted. Both read through io.LimitReader(maxFileBytes+1) (128 KiB) and do not report that an over-cap file was cut. slotlearn ReadLabels (slotlearn.go:50) unions both outputs into labels without re-validation, and ServingSlot defaults unknown or empty paths to the definition class. The held-out gate (LTA-V0-009..012) still decides admission, so poisoned labels can steer which proposals are scored but cannot bypass the gate. Invariant 4 says the ledgers are inputs to learning only through this step, so the step should admit only rows the writer could have produced.
title: Ledger readers admit rows the writer refuses, and those rows become slot-learning labels

acceptanceCriteria: The attempt-runner spec (docs/specs/corvint-tasks-attempt-runner-v0.md) or code states the non-file stdin contract under a cleanup HOLD, or a non-file env.Stdin is gated so the os/exec copy goroutine cannot read it after run returns
The output-gate wording says later child writes are refused (survivors may see EPIPE) rather than that copying stops
body:
## Observation

Independent review of PR #527's race fix (commit f0853500, gatedWriter in internal/tasks/cli/attempt_run.go) passed with LOW findings only. Two of them are follow-ups:

- Under a cleanup HOLD the leader is left unreaped, so cmd.Wait never joins os/exec's stdin copy goroutine. A caller that passes a live non-file env.Stdin and reuses it after run would race with that goroutine. Today cli.go defaults stdin to strings.NewReader("") and the tests pass bytes.NewReader(nil), so it hits EOF at once and there is no race now. This is a latent hazard, not a confirmed bug.
- After shut(), a refused write makes the copy goroutine close the pipe, so group survivors that keep writing get EPIPE or SIGPIPE. The spec sentence says the runner "stops copying"; "refuses later writes" would be more exact.

Version: PR #527 head 6f208e1c. Expected: the stdin contract is documented or gated. Actual: it is undocumented.
title: attempt runner: document or gate non-file stdin under cleanup HOLD

acceptanceCriteria: The cause of 'descendant did not start' at 0.17s is identified
TestVerificationCancellationCleansDescendant only accepts a complete, parsed, nonzero pid (for example, keep polling while the read is empty or Atoi fails), or the fixture writes the pid atomically
The test passes repeatedly under load (for example -count=50 alongside parallel packages)
body:
## Observation

CI go-product-shard (1) on PR #525 (head ddc47ed0, run 37211690574, job 111466247269, 2026-10-04) failed `internal/localcompletion` TestVerificationCancellationCleansDescendant with `lifecycle_unix_test.go:96: descendant did not start` after only 0.17s. The PR does not touch internal/localcompletion, and shards 0, 2 and 3 passed.

## Suspected cause (hypothesis, not confirmed)

The test polls `.git/descendant.pid` for up to 3s, but breaks on the first successful `os.ReadFile` and ignores the `strconv.Atoi` error. The fixture writes the file with `sh -c 'sleep 30 & echo $! > .git/descendant.pid; wait'`. The redirection creates or truncates the file before echo writes it, so a read in that window gets empty content, pid stays 0, and the test fails at once rather than waiting out the deadline. The 0.17s failure time fits this: it is far short of the 3s deadline.

Expected: the test waits for a complete pid. Actual: an empty read ends the wait early.
title: localcompletion: TestVerificationCancellationCleansDescendant fails early on an empty pid-file read

acceptanceCriteria: A pull request whose own unbounded-readers-check passes cannot leave main failing that check after merge, or the failure is detected and attributed before the merge completes; retained evidence shows the case of an unbounded test package added to main after the pull request's last CI run.
body: Confirmed 2026-10-04 at origin/main 6bf78ff76889519d43b34cc2a5dfbf42b72e9ba9 (merge of pull request 530; macOS and a clean detached worktree, go1.27.1). Reproduce: `make unbounded-readers-check` on that revision. Actual: `unbounded-readers: 56 test units are selected on every change, above the ceiling 45 in .corvint/unbounded-readers.json`, exit 1; the check is a doc-gates step, so every pull request based on that main fails. Expected: main passes its own required gate. Cause: the ceiling was measured on the pull request branch; eleven unbounded test packages (cmd/corvint-cem-candidate, cmd/corvint-test-runner, internal/cem/gitauth, internal/cemcandidate, internal/testrunner and its dynamic, mobile, native, platform, registry, sql subpackages) reached main after the branch's last CI run, and the pull request merged without a run against the newer base. The immediate break is repaired by declaring read scopes (build log 2026-10-04-unbounded-reader-merge-skew), but the same skew recurs whenever a package that is unbounded merges while another pull request's passing check is stale; with the ceiling equal to the count there is no slack. Options to weigh: require branches to be up to date before merge, a merge queue, or have the main-push run report the skew with the offending packages. Related: V1-0719, V1-0728.
title: affected: unbounded-readers ratchet breaks main when an unbounded package merges after a pull request's last CI run

acceptanceCriteria: An intent file that adds or changes requiresPool or requiredRoles on an adoptable record is adopted through a composed REFINE whose post record carries the file's value, or the spec states the ADOPT_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD refusal as the contract.

Focused tests in internal/tasks/mutation cover add, change and remove for both keys.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, branch claude/502-escalations-record-key (issue 502 record-key slice) from origin/main cd70ba0a. composeAdopt (internal/tasks/mutation/adopt.go) maps differing fields onto REFINE, PRIORITIZE, SET_DEPENDENCIES, SET_GATES, SET_EFFECTS and holds, but has no case for requiresPool or requiredRoles, although the REFINE payload admits both (mutation.go refine keys). Before the 502 slice, differingFields and adoptCovered iterated only the canonical record's keys, so an intent file that ADDED requiresPool/requiredRoles to a record lacking them was reported adopted with the key silently dropped; a file that changed an existing value was marked Present with no value composed. The 502 slice iterates the union of keys, so such files are now refused ADOPT_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD (TestIssue502_AdoptRefusesUncomposedAddedKey) instead of silently dropped. Expected: ADOPT_FILE composes a REFINE carrying requiresPool/requiredRoles (adding, changing, and if REFINE supports it, removing), or the refusal is documented as the contract. Actual: refusal (after the 502 slice) / silent drop (before).
title: ADOPT_FILE cannot compose requiresPool or requiredRoles edits although REFINE accepts both

acceptanceCriteria: A test establishes whether an IMPORT record can carry requiresPool/requiredRoles; if it cannot, the ticket closes with that evidence.

body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, found while adding issue 502 escalation-reference preservation to importer.record (branch claude/502-escalations-record-key from origin/main cd70ba0a). importer.record builds the next IMPORT revision from importer.TicketKeys only; requiresPool and requiredRoles are not in TicketKeys, so if an IMPORT record carries either (set by REFINE), a re-import with a changed block writes the next revision without them. Both keys are in ticket.AcceptanceRelevantFields, so chain() also bumps acceptanceRevision on that silent removal. This is suspected from reading the code; no reproduction test exists yet. Whether REFINE on a shadow IMPORT record can set these keys at all needs confirming first. Expected: re-import keeps tool-local optional keys the export cannot carry (as it now keeps escalations and createdAt), or refuses. Actual (suspected): keys dropped and acceptance revision bumped.

acceptanceCriteria: A push to main whose commit a successful merge_group run of CI already tested in full skips only the root race invocation, as AFP-V0-024 does for a pull-request result; any other case, including a failed, cancelled, partial or differently-sharded queue run, runs FULL.

tools/ci-reuse-plan tests cover the admitted merge_group case and each refusal, AFP-V0-024 is amended in the same change, and one hosted main-push run after a queue merge is retained showing REUSE with the queue run id.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 while adding the merge_group trigger (pull request 552, AFP-V0-026). With a merge queue on main, each merge runs the complete suite on the queue commit and then again on the main push of that same commit, about an hour of four shards each time. AFP-V0-024 reuse does not match: tools/ci-reuse-plan admits only runs with event pull_request whose head_sha is the second parent of the pushed merge commit, and the docs-plan reuse step in .github/workflows/ci.yml queries only event=pull_request for that parent. The queue run has event merge_group and head_sha equal to the pushed commit itself, so the tree is identical by construction. Expected: the main push reuses the queue run of the same commit. Not yet observed on a hosted run: the queue is not enabled, so whether a merge_group run retains the same per-shard tested-tree records (the record step is currently conditioned on pull_request) and whether the pushed commit id equals the queue commit id under merge method merge must be confirmed first; the record step needs to run for merge_group. Keep every failure path FULL. Related: V1-0717, V1-0752, V1-0728, CORE-GITHUB-MERGE-QUEUE-COMPATIBILITY-1.
title: ci: reuse the merge-queue run of the same commit on the main push

Pre-existing, suspected defect, found 2026-10-05 during the V1-0697 / #500 fix round (branch claude/v1-0697-fence-drain at ad54459d, clone /private/tmp/claude-501/corvint-v1-0697-r2). acceptanceCriteria: The operator-notes spec's rollback section states that full journal audit decodes every historical intent/policy.json POST, so once an accepted policy names NOTE_SET or NOTE_CLEAR (an explicit policy.roles.OPERATOR row or an OWNER row), a binary without those operations fails audit even after a later policy drops them, independent of whether any note was written.
Rollback guidance after such a policy keeps the operation vocabulary and ExplicitGrantOperations and disables only the writer.
A native witness (grant, revoke, audit with the grant removed refuses the historical row) or an explicit NOT_RUN is retained.
body: Found while fixing the same hazard for issue 502 (PR beamfall/corvint#575, commit ec81e4cd, test TestIssue502_OperatorAnswersThroughExplicitGrant). docs/specs/corvint-tasks-operator-notes-v0.md 'Rollout and rollback' says rollback before any note is written reverts the writer, CLI, codec and stage-slot changes. But a policy naming NOTE_SET/NOTE_CLEAR can be committed before any note exists. internal/tasks/journal/records.go validates every historical POST and calls intent.DecodePolicy on intent/policy.json; policy decode checks each role row against intent.Operations and PolicyGrantable (internal/tasks/intent/policy.go:224). A reverted binary therefore fails full audit on that historical policy. Expected: rollback guidance conditioned on whether any accepted policy named the note verbs. Actual: conditioned only on whether a note was written. Version: origin/main 10570f60. Suspected doc defect; the decode path is confirmed by the #502 witness for ESCALATE/ANSWER, not yet witnessed for the note verbs.
title: Operator-notes rollback ignores historical policy audit: a policy naming NOTE_SET blocks a plain revert before any note exists

acceptanceCriteria: A test makes a mapped write to an audited store file after the lease-path audit and before the lock-held commit, and the lease write refuses or fully re-audits. Run it on Linux tmpfs and macOS APFS, or record why a platform is not covered.
If the path is shown to be safe, the evidence for that is recorded and the ticket is closed as not a defect.
body:
Reported 2026-10-05 by the V1-0645 lane (claude/v1-0645-writer-checkpoint at e9001205, parent 4ba43576). It is a suspected defect: the lease path was inspected but no reproduction has been run.

V1-0645 r2 (Codex P1) confirmed that inotify on Linux arm64 tmpfs, and kqueue on macOS APFS without msync, miss writes made through a memory mapping. The lane reproduced a mapped projection committing through Mutate when the content check was forced to pass. Its fix makes Mutate always take a fresh inventory, and reuse the merged audit only when every file the audit read matches by digest and size.

The lease path has not had the same fix. internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:156 passes the audit's observation.Files into guardedLeaseInventory. Under the lock it appears to rely only on Check and the head digest (the lane cited lines 397 and 436), so a mapped write after the audit could go undetected.

Expected: a lease write refuses or re-audits when any audited file's content changed through a mapping. Actual (suspected): the reused digests are accepted.
title: store: lease writes may reuse audit digests that miss mapped (mmap) writes (suspected)

acceptanceCriteria: A paired benchmark against the V1-0645 baseline shows a measured saving, recording host, load and run count.
The mapped-write test TestCALV0070_MutateRefusesMappedWriteAfterMergedAudit still fails closed.
body: Proposed 2026-10-05 by the V1-0645 lane (e9001205). After the r2 mapped-write fix, every Mutate takes a fresh inventory, and reuses the merged audit only when each audited file matches by digest and size. Pinning or caching the inventory's file reads (for example by open-file identity plus size/mtime, verified by digest) could recover part of the cost the fix adds back. V1-0645 measured median Mutate at 5,494→3,151 ms on macOS and 4,019→2,547 ms on Linux with the fix in place.
title: store: pin inventory reads now that every Mutate takes a full fresh inventory

acceptanceCriteria: The package passes under the gate's TMPDIR on darwin, or each affected test skips with a documented skip that names the environment requirement (protected ancestors, socket path length).
The root cause of protected-authority-unavailable under /private/tmp is named (fixture or product), with a test that distinguishes them.
body:
Suspected defect, root cause not diagnosed. Reported 2026-10-05 by the pstack-claude agent optimization session; pre-existing on origin/main and it makes `make gate` fail on this host (Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1). Not caused by the V1-0750/0751/0325 batch.

Repro: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/td GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/authoritystore/`. TestEvidenceFilesystemAuditRejectsTamperingAndExtraAccess (evidence_darwin_test.go:138 'valid: protected-authority-unavailable', also :149), TestEvidenceRecheckDetectsReplacementAndCancellation and TestMemoSuccessCannotReplaceFinalViewAudit fail with protected-authority-unavailable. Deterministic on origin/main ee925a4b and 8a35775a, c0a8b4ba and batch 2c36814d.

With the default long TMPDIR (/private/var/folders/...), TestDarwinReciprocalSocketWitness instead fails with 'bind: invalid argument' (unix socket path over the length limit). So no TMPDIR passes the whole package on this host.

Hypothesis: the fixture's t.TempDir root fails the evidence audit's ownership/mode checks under /private/tmp (sticky world-writable ancestors). Related but distinct: V1-0753 (tasks/store PSR, symlinked TMPDIR ancestor), V1-0601 (MTP socket path length), V1-0033 (completed ctime witnesses).
title: tests (suspected): internal/authoritystore darwin tests fail under every TMPDIR on Darwin 25.6.0 (protected-authority-unavailable, or socket bind: invalid argument)

acceptanceCriteria: 50 consecutive passes of TestPSRRequestConflictAndOrphan under -count on darwin.
The timing dependency behind 'new explicit request never executed' is named, and the test waits on an observed event rather than a deadline.
body:
Suspected flake, reported 2026-10-05 by the pstack-claude agent optimization session; pre-existing on origin/main, seen once in a full `make gate` run on the batch head. Failure: pool_sweep_lifecycle_test.go:635 'new explicit request never executed'.

Repro: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/td GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=8 -timeout 30m -run 'TestPSRRequestConflictAndOrphan' ./internal/tasks/store/` — 2/8 failures on origin/main ee925a4b, 0/8 on c0a8b4ba, 0/8 on batch 2c36814d (Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1).

Related: V1-0724 (PSR store tests sensitive to host load, general) — this ticket names one subtest with a count-based repro; close it into V1-0724 if the same timing dependency is the cause. V1-0753 (symlinked TMPDIR) is distinct. Evidence 2026-10-05: (1) pstack session at bc87a4dc (claude/v1-0325-intent-worktree + origin/main ee925a4b), TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/td, go test ./internal/tasks/... ./cmd/corvint-tasks/...: live-unknown-gone failed at pool_sweep_lifecycle_test.go:539 'strconv.Atoi: parsing "": invalid syntax', all other packages passed. (2) orchestrator batch trees 9708c91c and 2d39568b (claude/batch-2026-10-05), TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/v7t: same line-539 failure in the full store run, and -count=3 -run TestPSRRequestConflictAndOrphan failed again on both (2d39568b also failed request-and-policy-fences) while another session ran PSR loops on the host. Inferred, unconfirmed hypothesis: psrAwaitMarker returns once the marker file exists but the reset child creates it before writing its PID (non-atomic create-then-write), so the test reads an empty file; the earlier line-635 'new explicit request never executed' symptom may share the timing window. Fix direction: write the marker atomically (temp file plus rename) or await non-empty parseable content.
title: tests (suspected flake): tasks/store TestPSRRequestConflictAndOrphan/live-unknown-gone fails 'new explicit request never executed'

acceptanceCriteria: Every coded refusal carries an explicit retryability fact owned by Tasks, and the documented retryable set names each code and the condition under which a retry can succeed.
A test pins the classification for every code in internal/tasks/wire/codes.go, so a new code cannot ship unclassified.
Fencing codes (an attempt really lost) are never marked retryable.
body: Callers currently pattern-match result codes to decide whether to retry; the Flow-Proof runner killed healthy runs by treating LOCK_TIMEOUT as fencing, and now retries LOCK_TIMEOUT, SNAPSHOT_MOVED, STALE, REDO_PENDING, STORAGE_FAILED, HEAD_MOVED and JOURNAL_SATURATED by its own list. Requested by the owner in a beamfall/corvint issue 494 comment (2026-10-05T02:44:57Z, Flow-Proof fleet data point on main-cd70ba0: ~8,900 receipts, 13 concurrent sessions, pooled claim LOCK_TIMEOUT at rank 13; heartbeat/renew LOCK_TIMEOUT while the lease was FRESH was misread by the client as fencing). Needs a wire-contract change (taskman-command-result/0 or a successor profile) with a spec requirement, so the retryable set is owned by Tasks rather than each client.
title: corvint-tasks: mark each command result's retryability explicitly (retryable: true) and document the retryable code set

acceptanceCriteria: queue status reports the number of registered waiting writers and the caller's would-be rank, read without taking the preparation lock, or NOT_OBSERVED when it cannot observe them.
Any estimated wait is derived from recorded per-mutation cost with its basis named, or omitted; it is never presented as a guarantee.
A test with N registered waiters shows the reported rank and that the read writes nothing.
body: Supervisors cannot see admission pressure until a mutation fails LOCK_TIMEOUT after the 30 s preparation budget. Requested by the owner in a beamfall/corvint issue 494 comment (2026-10-05T02:44:57Z, Flow-Proof fleet data point on main-cd70ba0: ~8,900 receipts, 13 concurrent sessions, pooled claim LOCK_TIMEOUT at rank 13; heartbeat/renew LOCK_TIMEOUT while the lease was FRESH was misread by the client as fencing). queue status (internal/tasks/cli/cli.go queueStatus) is read-only and must stay lock-free (Invariant 4); the rank and wait must be reported as observed facts or NOT_OBSERVED, never invented. V1-0645 (writer cost) reduces the underlying cost; this ticket makes the pressure visible.
title: corvint-tasks: expose current writer-admission rank and an estimated wait in queue status so supervisors can back off before queueing

acceptanceCriteria: Bump the gemini-cli version everywhere it is pinned (gemini-extension.json, hooks/corvint-hook.mjs ADAPTER_VERSION, compatibility.json if present) and `bash script/check-host-package-versions.sh` passes on the branch.
Establish whether CI runs check-host-package-versions; if it does not, wire it into CI so a stale host package version fails the build.
body: On origin/main, `bash script/check-host-package-versions.sh` reports integrations/gemini-cli/gemini-extension.json last bumped at 4a2fe22786d12ac647d414061e6b060321924257, older than the shipped content change at f802b22dc584f47ca0d921dc65d56928b8860de5 (V1-0711 AHI-044 fail-open matrix, merged via beamfall/corvint#531). Expected (AHI-020): the gemini-cli manifest version advances whenever its shipped content changes. Actual: the gate exits nonzero for gemini-cli and CI did not catch it, so its wiring is unverified. Observed 2026-10-04 on 3e72363c / 1912550e by the V1-0773 session. Related but distinct: V1-0452 (OpenCode coverage). Update 2026-10-05: work started in beamfall/corvint#590 (branch claude/gemini-cli-version-bump, gemini-cli 0.2.5 -> 0.2.6 in gemini-extension.json, gemini-cli/compatibility.json and integrations/compatibility.json; check-host-package-versions passes for gemini-cli). Keep OPEN until the CI acceptance criterion lands: the CI doc-gates job does not run the script, only make gate does; wiring it needs a fetch-depth 0 checkout and cannot land until OpenCode is current on main. OpenCode is also stale on main since 88334a0c (V1-0746); beamfall/corvint#589 (V1-0773, OpenCode 0.7.8, stacked on #580) fixes that.
title: Gemini CLI package version is stale on main: check-host-package-versions fails (AHI-020)

body: `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./cmd/corvint/ -run TestHostAdapter` failed once on 2026-10-04 (Go 1.27.1, darwin/arm64) at host_adapter_javascript_test.go:92: "harness ended before descendant witness: <nil>", in the V1-0773 worktree whose change touches only the OpenCode plugin and JS tests. Three isolated reruns of `-run TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHarnessInterruption` passed (two on the change, one at base 3e72363c). Suspected load-dependent race; not confirmed or reproduced on demand.
title: tests: TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHarnessInterruption flakes under load: harness ended before descendant witness (suspected)

acceptanceCriteria: With opt-in policy `pools[].priorityAdmission: true`, an explicit `claim --ticket X --pool P` is refused (BLOCKED, `RESOURCE_COLLISION`, detail naming the yielded-to ticket) when free eligible members of P are no more than the number of OPEN, claim-eligible, higher-priority tickets with `requiresPool == P` and no live attempt. Ordering is (priority, order, ticketId), the same as planLess.
With the flag absent or false, claim bytes and receipts are identical to today (N-1 replay test).
`plan preview --pool P` and `claim-next` produce the same decision as the explicit claim for the same snapshot (a property test over generated pool/ticket states).

The read stays pure: plan preview writes nothing and runs no probes (CAL-V0-034). When `requiresPool` on a competing ticket is not observable, the claim is not refused on its account, and the read reports the gap as NOT_OBSERVED.

acceptanceCriteria: An explicit writer verb (proposed `pool wait --ticket T --pool P --holder H --ttl-seconds N`, N ≤ policy max) records one WAITING entry in `pools.json` with ticket, priority snapshot, arrival seq and expiry. It is idempotent per request ID, and there is at most one entry per ticket and pool.

A freed member is allocatable only to the head waiter, ordered by (priority, arrival seq), until the waiter claims, the entry expires, or the waiter's ticket stops being eligible. Other claims get `RESOURCE_COLLISION` naming the head.
Expired or ineligible entries never block. `reap` and pool sweep drop them under the existing fencing. A crash between the wait and the claim leaves no stranded member.
`plan preview` and `queue status` show the waitlist (ticket, priority, age, expiresAt) as read-only data.
Opt-in `pools[].handoffGraceSeconds` (default 0) keeps a clean HANDOFF's member reserved for the same ticket's next generation for at most that long. Grace expiry is fenced like a lease.

Issue #1067 case: a higher-priority ticket whose LIVE attempt is waiting for a member can hold a durable reservation (registered by attempt and generation); a freed member goes to it before any new claim or acquire, its next attach returns ACQUIRED, and the reservation ends with the attempt (optional same-ticket hand-off grace).

acceptanceCriteria: In the default plan, a ticket with `requiresPool == P` is SELECTED only while the count of earlier selections requiring P is below P's currently free eligible members. Otherwise it is DEFERRED with `RESOURCE_COLLISION` and blockers `[P]`, and it **does not count** against `maxActiveAttempts`. It is not BLOCKED merely because the plan was not run with `--pool`.
A fixture with capacity 16, 8 live, 6 pool-waiting and 28 lane-free tickets selects 8 lane-free tickets (reproducing the #584 numbers).
Plan output reports the number of resource-deferred selections, per pool. This is additive, under the profile decided in D1.
`claim-next` and explicit claim still admit exactly what the plan selects (CAL-V0-008/014 parity test). The `--pool`/`--stage` plan path and pool exclusions (CAL-V0-065) are unchanged.
When member state is unobservable (no `pools.json` proof), the plan reports pool availability as NOT_OBSERVED and defers. It never selects on an assumption.

acceptanceCriteria: Optional record key `executionPrerequisites: [{ticketId, obligation: COMPLETED|GATE_PASSED, gateId|null, stages:[...]}]`, bounded like dependencies. It is validated for existence. It is excluded from cycle detection, completion checks and `requiredGates`. Legacy records round-trip byte-identical.

A claim, claim-next or plan for a listed stage reports `PREREQUISITE_UNSATISFIED` (or the code chosen in D4) naming the prerequisite. Claims for unlisted stages are unaffected. `ticket blockers` explains it.
A GATE_PASSED prerequisite whose gate result is not observable yields an unknown (NOT_OBSERVED), not satisfied and not a hard refusal, following the dependency semantics at `view.go:146-152`.
The Core taskman decoder, import or re-import, and ADOPT_FILE accept and preserve the key, with regression tests mirroring V1-0754/0758/0759.
`ticket refine` can set and clear it under the existing writer and receipts. Completing a prerequisite changes no other ticket's record.

Retry accounting is unchanged (V1-0566 tests still pass).

acceptanceCriteria: The TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement cleanup never dereferences a nil cmd.Process, so a failed or pre-start expiry fails only that test instead of panicking the dispatch package run.

The test's expiry no longer depends on a 50ms wall-clock deadline being still open when readerStart runs (for example a controlled clock or an explicit gate), and it passes 50 consecutive runs under -count on darwin at high host load.
body:
Confirmed bug (test defect), observed 2026-10-04 by the #502 claim-delivery session on batch b77ba895 + claude/502-escalations-claim-delivery (tree fb1ea54a), Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1, host load average 179-214 from concurrent gate runs.

Failure in a full `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/tasks/...`:
- reader_test.go:132 'expired retirement admitted work: context deadline exceeded calls=0'
- then panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference in os.(*Process).signal via cmd.Process.Kill() at reader_test.go:110 (t.Cleanup).

Cause (from source): the test gives stateCommand a 50ms context. Under load the context expires before the reader process starts, so readerStart has set `cmd` but `cmd.Process` is nil; the cleanup guards only `cmd != nil && !collected.Load()` and calls `cmd.Process.Kill()`. The panic aborts the whole internal/tasks/dispatch test binary, hiding every later test result.

Expected: the cleanup guards `cmd.Process != nil`, and the expiry case is driven by an observed event, not a 50ms deadline.
Actual: wall-clock-sensitive assertion plus a nil dereference that crashes the package.

Repro: run `go test -count=1 -run TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement ./internal/tasks/dispatch` under heavy CPU load; it passed in isolation (1.5s) at load ~187.

Related: V1-0724 (PSR store tests sensitive to host load).
title: tests: dispatch TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement panics in cleanup (nil cmd.Process) when its 50ms deadline expires under load

acceptanceCriteria: A crashed owner between dispatch and FINISHED no longer strands the attempt: either a combined attempt+program transition or a takeover rule admits a bound, stopped, quiescent attempt, and an unproved stop still fails closed.
TestCALV0074_NoExecCrashTakeover is updated to cover the recovery and the retained refusal; the noExec WAITING settlement is either cancelled or documented as intended.
body: Known limit retained by V1-0755 (Claude Code supervised host, issue 354, review round r5; lane branch claude/v1-0755-claude-code-host). If the program owner process dies after dispatch and before it writes the FINISHED record, the program stays SPAWNING or STOPPING. The attempt keeps its claim and reservation, and a replacement owner is refused at internal/tasks/transaction/program.go:106 with "prior program owner not proved stopped". Witness: TestCALV0074_NoExecCrashTakeover/stopped in internal/tasks/store/program_claude_host_test.go, which pins the current refusal. Related observation: non-cancelling noExec paths settle the attempt to WAITING without cancelling it. Expected: a crashed owner's attempt can be recovered without manual store surgery, still failing closed when stop is not proved. Actual: the attempt stays held until its lease expires or the owner intervenes manually. Candidate fixes (an owner design choice): a combined attempt+program transition, or a takeover rule that admits a bound, stopped, quiescent attempt from STOPPING.
title: tasks: owner crash between dispatch and FINISHED leaves a supervised program SPAWNING/STOPPING and blocks takeover

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded decision states whether the Codex host's stream decoder must refuse duplicate and case-aliased members, with the threat model it relies on.

body: Raised by the V1-0756 lane on 2026-10-05 and confirmed from source in the batch tree (claude/batch-2026-10-05 at 3ec6eeab plus V1-0701). V1-0755 and V1-0756 make the Claude Code and OpenCode supervisor stream readers refuse duplicate members and case aliases (exactMembers/aliasFree in internal/tasks/supervisor/hosts.go). In the V1-0756 review, a duplicate member let `"accepted":false,"accepted":true` pass, let a repeated `type` hide an `error` event, and let repeated token objects merge into usage that looked complete. The Codex host decoder, DecodeEvents in internal/tasks/supervisor/events.go:19, still uses json.Unmarshal into a map at lines 28, 51, 89, 96 and 117, so the last duplicate wins and case aliases are not checked. Expected: either the same refusal as the other hosts, or a recorded reason Codex output is exempt. Actual: no check and no recorded decision. This is a suspected defect: whether Codex's JSONL output can be shaped this way by a hostile turn has not been verified.
title: supervisor: Codex stream decoder accepts duplicate and case-aliased members that the Claude Code and OpenCode hosts refuse

acceptanceCriteria: Measured runner-minutes for 100 consecutive CI runs (before and after) split by event and conclusion; cancelled share is reported from the GitHub jobs API, not estimated.

Expensive go-product-shard work for a pull request does not start while a newer push to the same pull request is expected or already queued, or the agent/batch workflow pushes only after local focused checks pass; the chosen lever is recorded with its rollback.
Main push runs that are cancelled by a later main push remain covered by AFP-V0-024 reuse or the merge-queue run; no main tree loses its full-suite evidence because of the change.
Required checks go-product, doc-gates and ci-control-plane keep their current semantics; no test is narrowed by this ticket.
body: Observed 2026-10-05 during an owner-requested CI audit, Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163, origin/main d524530f. The last 100 runs of .github/workflows/ci.yml (2026-10-04T23:29Z to 2026-10-05T10:46Z, about 11 hours) consumed 7063 runner-minutes by the jobs API: pull_request cancelled 45 runs / 2255 min (31%), push cancelled 16 runs / 846 min (11%), pull_request success 27 / 3076 min (43%), pull_request failure 5 / 571 min, push success 6 / 288 min. So 42% of CI spend produced no result. The cancellations come from repeated pushes to the same branches (claude/batch-2026-10-05 and claude/502-escalations-claim-delivery were each pushed about 15 times) with cancel-in-progress; each cancelled run had already started four 75-minute race shards, often 5-40 minutes in. Expected: an abandoned push costs at most the cheap jobs (doc-gates, docs-plan). Candidate levers: agents push batch branches only after local focused checks; start go-product-shard only after doc-gates passes; or debounce shards on synchronize events. Distinct from V1-0616 (narrowing), V1-0617 (balance) and V1-0760 (merge-queue reuse). Delivered in PR beamfall/corvint#611 (AFP-V0-027): a ci:batched label skips go-product-shard for batch constituents and fails go-product, so constituents land only through their batch; the label was created on 2026-10-05 with owner approval. Six-shard rebalance cuts superseded-run waste per cancelled run (run 37303691592: wall 22.4 min vs 45.3 min). The after-measurement of 100 consecutive runs split by event and conclusion is not yet observed; hosted constituent behavior is NOT_OBSERVED until a batch uses the label.
title: ci: cancelled runs consume 42% of CI runner-minutes; stop abandoned pushes from starting race shards

acceptanceCriteria: The amended and new requirements match decision 0431 items 1 to 9 and its failure modes, with final IDs assigned and the decision's provisional-ID sentence updated to cite them.
Each new requirement has a traceability row naming its planned test or hosted evidence, NOT_OBSERVED where nothing exists yet.

body:
Suspected flaky test (not yet confirmed as a defect). Observed 2026-10-05 on a loaded macOS host in a scratch clone of claude/502-typed-event-stage (base b1e37605, Go 1.27.1), during `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/tasks/store` (984s package run):

    --- FAIL: TestCALV0078_SupervisedRunAfterCommitIsNotRetryable/refresh-STOPPED (5.53s)
        program_gate_retry_test.go:149: implement: ... Phase:BLOCKED_RECOVERY ... Quiescence:SURVIVORS ... native transition refused: ... Outcome:VALIDATION_FAILED ... Detail:MALFORMED: transaction: program transition

The failure is in the setup step `w.RunRole(ctx, "implementer", "")`, before the injected fault point, so the case under test never ran. The subtest passed with -count=3 in isolation and in a full rerun of the same package set (844s).

Hypothesis: under host load the supervised implementer run observes surviving processes at quiescence, enters BLOCKED_RECOVERY, and the following program transition is refused, so the fixture never reaches BUILT. That would be a timing dependency in the fixture's quiescence observation, not a CAL-V0-078 defect.

Expected: the implementer step deterministically reaches BUILT, or the test reports a skip-with-reason when the host cannot prove quiescence. It should never fail on timing.

Actual: an intermittent FAIL before the fault point on a loaded host.
title: Suspected flake: TestCALV0078_SupervisedRunAfterCommitIsNotRetryable implementer step can end BLOCKED_RECOVERY under load

body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: keep the existing Go test suite as the source of truth and derive evaluation records from go test -json output instead of hand-authored eval rows (product invariant 6). Tests are not uniform (different packages, subtests, repeat counts) and no aggregate gate is computed; instead hold strict: (a) stable identity per package, test and subtest path, bound to the immutable tree; (b) non-duplicating, idempotent writes on rerun; (c) provenance naming the command, toolchain, platform and tree. Payoff: flaky tests (V1-0768, V1-0771, V1-0815, V1-0724, V1-0779, V1-0796) gain a durable cross-run identity and history, so flake rates are measured, not remembered. Related: V1-0245 (gate-ledger per-package pass recording). Any ledger must respect invariant 4 (read commands do not mutate) and must not feed ranking.

body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: Phoenix keeps a checked-in REVIEW.md using RFC 2119 keywords in sections Always check, Patterns to flag, Security and Skip, with concrete test-backed rules (e.g. a privileged operation needs a regression test asserting its location and required permission). Corvint has no repository rubric; Codex review prompts are hand-written per lane, so review criteria drift between lanes. Proposal: a project-owned rubric that the CEM reviewer report and Codex review prompts both cite, so review findings trace to a stable rule ID (invariant 3: project authority outranks syntax and learned traces). Candidate rules from this session: bounded reads, NOT_RUN never reported as passed, test temp paths under the 128-byte gate argv limit, no unbounded os.Getwd inheritance, error-code ownership.

body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: Phoenix specs open with a matrix of where each claim was verified (backend versions, interpreter versions), distinguish the language floor from the product support floor, state that behaviour was executed rather than reasoned about, and declare anything outside the matrix unverified. The spec plus its conformance tests is the authority; user docs are a curated derivative. Corvint records platform gaps in build logs and NOT_RUN lists (e.g. V1-0804 Linux-only helpers, platform qualification under V1-0697), but not in a uniform spec header where agents read first (the Agent digest). Proposal: an optional, machine-checkable Verified-on block in the spec digest (OS, arch, Go toolchain, host type, date, evidence pointer), validated by the spec index, with absent rows meaning NOT_RUN.

body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: Phoenix ships evaluators for user friction (corrections, retries, frustration), tool selection, tool invocation and tool-response handling, mostly LLM-judged. Corvint analogue, deterministic and local only: from agent session records compute re-reads of the same file, reads outside the planned set (the unplanned-reads ledger), retried commands, abandoned or reverted edits, and time to first relevant read. Use them as evaluation outputs to compare context packets (pairwise A/B arms for the same task, as in the multi-arm CEM trials), never as ranking, evidence or authority inputs (invariant 4; SOL-V0-001, SOL-V0-007, SOL-V0-010). Benchmark each metric against labelled sessions before trusting it, per the Phoenix rule that every built-in evaluator is benchmarked.

body: Issue 502 was delivered twice from base d524530f: on main by #610 and #612 (kept), and by the lane claude/v1-0699-escalations-rest (head 2d16ae3b, reverted from the batch branch claude/batch-2026-10-05b because it duplicated main). body: Decision 0427 / build-log 2026-10-01. No sealed retrieval partition remains (decision 0307: v4 retired, v5 and v6 consumed). The sibling explain-away rule (GPK-V0-040) is validated only on the development corpus and on probes; a window-licence floor variant was tried and not adopted (decision 0427). Authoring guide from the retrieval review: preregister a pool of about 15 repositories never indexed by Corvint and pick 5 by a committed coin (hash of a named future upstream tag); author on a machine without the corvint binary using only source and git grep; about 30 positive cases (task of at most 15 words from an issue or commit subject, never symbol names; expected files and symbols; 1 to 3 decoys each with a one-line reason: nearest-name same-file sibling, adjacent declaration, same-named symbol elsewhere) and 10 out-of-scope probes that are within-repository near misses (a feature the repository lacks beside ones it has; never a misspelling of a real behaviour, never a cross-repository transplant: the 45 transplant probes recorded in the build-log answer READY 22 times on declarations that legitimately carry two task words); a preregistration digest over the case file, the five metrics and their bars (top-5 above the exact-search baseline by at least 0.1; must-exclude over all emitted results 0; abstention precision at least 0.8 and recall at least 0.7; latency at most 5 s per case), exactly one run, and one appeal route: a second person may void one decoy as mis-authored before seeing any other output, after which that case is development.

acceptanceCriteria: The 10-pair development variance run and the frozen pair count are recorded in a build-log entry before the held-out selection is drawn.

The three-arm report is committed unrepaired and README's CEM row is rewritten from its summary.arms, seed_coverage and contrasts with the wording decision 0427 names for a positive and for a null result; the row says agent reviewer, never reviewer, until the reviewer-projection ticket's human leg runs.
body: Decision 0427 / build-log 2026-10-01 / CRT-V0-004, CRT-V0-005, CRT-V0-007, CRT-V0-008, CRT-V0-012 as amended. The 2026-09-04 pilot's treatment carried no evidence and three of its five changes had gold no arm could cite; it answers nothing about CEM. Procedure: accept or amend the CRT-V0 amendments; draw a 10-pair development run first to estimate the between-change variance of the per-change delta; freeze the pair count from amended CRT-V0-008 (about 55 pairs for a 20% relative reduction from a corrected control miss of 0.50 with two repeats); select with `cem-trial select --partition heldout --exclude tools/cem-trial/testdata/pilot/tasks.json` under the reachable-gold rule; run once with `--arms control,treatment,seeded --repeats 2` at a fixed model and effort; preserve the first report unrepaired at benchmarks/results/cem-reviewer-trial-first-run.json. Read the result as retrieval (seed_coverage.fraction) times adoption (1 - miss_given_suggested); a fraction below 0.5 is retrieval-limited and supports no claim about the map. body: Decision 0427 / build-log 2026-10-01. The 24-case development corpus carries no must-exclude selector, so the sibling class of blind-v6's forbidden hits was invisible during development, and the 45 cross-repository transplant probes measure the wrong thing (declarations carrying two task words in their own names).
