acceptanceCriteria: A spec amendment (CEM-PILOT or a new reviewer-projection spec) states the projection's contract, the no-fabrication invariant for quoted spans, and the SARIF mapping; the projection and export ship with focused tests and an independent human review of one real PR using them.
The human leg is preregistered (reviewers, changes, sealed gap counts, primary outcome, stopping rule) in a decision before recruitment, and its result is recorded whatever the sign.
README's CEM row is rewritten from the human leg's paired interval with decision 0427's wording, and never before it.
body: Decision 0427 / build-log 2026-10-01. The product review found that `cem report` cannot help a human reviewer today: it is an author worklist, it carries identifiers, OIDs and ranges but no cited text (CEM-PILOT-007 forbids source and diff bodies, though a byte-bound quote of a pinned span is evidence rather than prose), it is not hunk-anchored, and it says what kind of thing was cited but not what property of the hunk it constrains. Build `cem report --for reviewer` (or `cem review`): unknown hunks first grouped by file, each with a suggested basis from `context --subject` labelled suggested-not-cited; supported hunks with the pinned span quoted inline (bounded, headed path@oid:lines and relation); a falsifier line per supported hunk derived only from cited metadata (test name and `affected` selection, or requirement ID); evidence drift since the last sealed CEM listed above supported; mechanical hunks collapsed; SARIF export with one `note` per unknown hunk and one `warning` per drifted citation (ties to V1-0419 and V1-0195). Then the human leg: about 8 reviewers, about 12 sealed Corvint changes with known post-merge defects or missing tests (ground truth counted before recruitment), each reviewer sees all 12, half with the projection and half with diff plus git grep, counterbalanced Latin square, primary outcome recall of sealed gaps in a 20-minute box, secondary time-to-first-gap comment and calibration; stop and report null if the paired effect is below d 0.5 after 8. Observational per-PR telemetry (unknown count at review time against post-merge fix commits touching those hunks, reviewer time-to-first-comment) is logged to a sealed ledger never read by ranking and labelled single-author single-repository.
title: Reviewer-facing CEM projection (unknown hunks first, inline pinned spans, SARIF) and the human within-subject leg

TestSERVICE500_HelperRecordIsBounded (`openat var: not a directory`), TestSERVICE500_LogSinkRotatesWithinTwoFiles (all bytes dropped, LOG_IO_ERROR openat var), TestSERVICE500_LogSinkDropsBeyondBufferWithoutBlocking (dropped 101, want 100), and TestSERVICE500_LogSinkIOErrorIsReportedNotBlocking blocks on an unread gate send until `panic: test timed out after 30m0s`. acceptanceCriteria: Under a 10240 descriptor limit on darwin, TestCALV0026_AuditInventoryParityAndFallback and TestCALV0026_GuardedInventoryPopulated5000 pass.

WatchChanges never fails for store size alone; files beyond a bounded descriptor budget are still checked for content writes, mode changes, replacement and removal, proven by a maintained darwin test that forces a tiny budget.
Stores within the budget keep the existing kqueue behavior, and the agent-leases spec states the budget and the fallback's limit.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64 and GitHub macos-15, 2026-10-05, release candidate da78c1572211a85e6c9944adb98350d69964eb9b (1.0.0-rc.2 candidate 2). authority.WatchChanges on darwin (internal/tasks/authority/change_guard_darwin.go) opens one O_EVTONLY descriptor per watched directory and regular file under the state directory and intent tree and holds them until Close. Go raises the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE only to min(hard, kern.maxfilesperproc), 10240 on the hosted runner. Expected: lease reads, lease preparation and recovery work on a store within the wire bounds. Actual: WatchChanges returns `too many open files`; readLeaseProof, prepareLease and prepareLeaseRecovery fail (Mutate already degrades). Reproduction: `(ulimit -Hn 10240; ulimit -Sn 10240; GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=1 -run 'TestCALV0026_(AuditInventoryParityAndFallback|GuardedInventoryPopulated5000)' ./internal/tasks/store)` fails at audit_inventory_test.go:96 and guarded_inventory_test.go:671; passes at 24576. Hosted evidence: release-gates run 37381427566 job 112004121660. The darwin guard is new since v1.0.0-rc.1, so this is an rc.2 regression.

acceptanceCriteria: On darwin, a lease Check under the writer lock does work independent of ticket count when the store exceeds the regular-file descriptor budget, shown by a maintained test or measurement at a budget below the store's file count.
Changes to over-budget files are still detected at least as strongly as the stat-tuple fallback of V1-0841.
The agent-leases spec's descriptor-budget paragraph no longer records the locked-scan limitation, or records the accepted replacement bound.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin, 2026-10-05, branch claude/rc2-darwin-guard-fds (V1-0841 fix). The V1-0841 fix tracks regular files beyond a process-wide kqueue descriptor budget (half the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE) by an lstat tuple, and vnodeWatch.changed re-lstats every over-budget file on each Check. Lease commits call Check while holding the writer lock (internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go around lines 419 and 462), so once a store exceeds the budget each commit performs two lstat sweeps proportional to the overflow file count under the lock. CAL-V0-026 requires locked work not to grow with ticket count. Expected: locked Check is O(1) in store size. Actual: O(overflow files) beyond the budget; within the budget unchanged. Before V1-0841 the same store refused with too many open files, so this is a bounded degradation, not a regression from a working state. Found by independent Codex review of commit b7094faf. Candidate directions: sweep before taking the lock and only poll kqueue under it, rely on directory events for atomic-rename writes, or raise the budget. Follows V1-0841.
title: Darwin change guard re-stats over-budget files under the lease writer lock

acceptanceCriteria: The S0E normal-exit-lingering-descendant-contained case passes in the hosted macOS-15 full-gate job of the Release gates workflow.
With a Git that rejects --attr-source placed ahead of /bin and /usr/bin in the shim PATH, the case fails before the fix with git-diff-failed after 8 operations and passes after it.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, hosted macos-15 runner, 2026-10-05, 1.0.0-rc.2 candidates da78c157 (Release gates run 37381427566) and 7a83f52d (run 37403195661). TestStableS0EPublicCases/normal-exit-lingering-descendant-contained failed on both with code git-diff-failed, stage repository, 8 attempted operations; it passes on the local release host. Cause: the S0E harness shim sets PATH=/bin:/usr/bin and execs the verifier's Git argv, whose binary is the bare name git. On the hosted runner that resolves to Apple /usr/bin/git, older than the Homebrew git 2.55 the verifier uses, and the canonical diff's --attr-source global option is rejected, so the product correctly reports a failed Git. The local /usr/bin/git is 2.54, which hides it. Expected: the shim runs the same Git as the verifier. Fix: resolve the binary with exec.LookPath before handing it to the shim. Reproduced locally with a fake pre-2.40 git first in the shim PATH. This supersedes V1-0843's fork-refusal attribution for the hosted failure; the stderr side-file diagnostic stays.
title: S0E lingering-descendant shim runs /usr/bin/git instead of the verifier's Git on hosted macOS

acceptanceCriteria: TestGoTestRunsUnresolvedAfterResolvedFailure fails on the previous goTest and passes with the fix: a resolved batch exiting 3 still runs and records the unresolved packages, and the step exits 3.
docs/specs/gate-ledger-v0.md GL-V0-004 states that a failing resolved batch does not stop the unresolved packages.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, tools/gate-ledger at origin/main b7b21205, hosted macos-15 Release gates run 37358656556 (1.0.0-rc.2 candidate 0ae3f88d), 2026-10-05. goTest returned the resolved batch's non-zero status before running the unresolved packages, so the log shows PARTITION 129 resolved / 184 unresolved, 206 ok, one FAIL (internal/tasks/service timeout) and no RUN go-test-unresolved line. The next candidate then failed on cem/verify, localcompletion and tasks/store, which the first run never executed. Expected (GL-V0-004): ledger/go-test runs every package go test ./... would, so one run reports every failing package. Actual: a failing resolved batch hides every unresolved failure. Fix: run the unresolved packages after a failed resolved batch (unless it was killed by a signal) and exit with the resolved batch's status.
title: gate-ledger go-test skips the unresolved packages when the resolved batch fails

acceptanceCriteria: A decision amends 0415 for the -k flag and the schedule.
A dispatched or scheduled Release gates run whose full-gate fails one step still runs every later GATE_STEPS step, and the job still fails.
The scheduled run checks out main's head and names its artifacts with the nightly label.
body: Context: 1.0.0-rc.2 needed four candidates (0ae3f88d, da78c157, 7a83f52d, b7b21205); each of the first three failed only the hosted macos-15 full-gate job. make gate stops at the first failed step, so go-vet, cross-vet, interop-gate and every later step never ran on hosted macOS for those candidates. PR CI is ubuntu-only and release-gates.yml runs only on owner dispatch, so four macOS-only defects that landed after rc.1 (V1-0841, V1-0842, V1-0843, V1-0846) were first seen at release time. Expected: one hosted run reports every failing gate step, and macOS regressions surface within a day of landing. Change: full-gate runs make -k gate (exit status unchanged: non-zero on any failure, receipt only when every step passes), and the workflow also runs on a nightly schedule against main. Amends decision 0415; a .github/ change merges only after an admin posts ci-control-plane success (decision 0390).
title: Release gates: keep the hosted full gate going past a failed step and run it nightly on main

acceptanceCriteria: Each child case is reproduced under a saturating load (or bounded by a recorded count of passing runs) and its outcome recorded per child id.

Each reproduced test-timing case waits on the condition it needs, or uses an injected clock or a deadline scaled without weakening what is asserted; budget assertions that measure performance report a retained measurement instead of failing under shared-host load.
Every case that turns out to be a product defect (for example a real survivor in V1-0768, or the V1-0771 race) is filed or linked as its own ticket, not closed here.
The repaired tests pass 20 consecutive runs under a saturating load.
body:
Umbrella for load- and timing-sensitive test failures, merged 2026-10-06 at the owner's request from 19 tickets, which are archived with a pointer here. Each child's original record (reproduction, host, load, revision, failure text) stays readable with `corvint-tasks ticket show <id>`; read it before working that case.

Children (test and observed failure):
- V1-0226: benchmarks/runner and internal/behaviorfalsify each failed once under load (test names not retained)
- V1-0455: TestExperimentalKernelAdapterContext: 250 ms kernel deadline
- V1-0636: liveverify/affected TestSelectionOnTheLiveDirtyWorktree: 100 ms select budget (343.5 ms observed)
- V1-0638: cmd/corvint TestWorkActualProducerInterruptedScratchCleanup: 1 ms poll can miss the producer's scratch window (CI, #434)
- V1-0724: tasks/store PSR pool-sweep and reconcile/dispatch tests are load-sensitive (general)
- V1-0727: a liveverify wall-clock budget test (name not retained)
- V1-0736: lspstdio TestWorkspaceBranchRootAndHealthy: Overlay definition unavailable at load 45-130
- V1-0738: tasks/authority TestGH494PreparationAdmission: 100 ms LOCK_TIMEOUT under full-suite load
- V1-0762: cmd/corvint TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts fails at ~60 s in a loaded run
- V1-0763: liveverify/affected TestIncrementalSelectionMeetsTheLiveBudget: p95 173 ms against 100 ms
- V1-0764: opencodequalification TestPassiveWitnessSettle/AHI-032: live descendant at the settle deadline
- V1-0766: tracerecordrepo TestAggregateOutcomeNativeAdmissionSizes/513: TempDir RemoveAll (.git not empty), 2/5 runs
- V1-0768: tasks/cli TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun: SURVIVORS, 2/15 on base ce4ae150 (real survivor not excluded)
- V1-0774: integrations/host-adapters.test.mjs:812 AHI-032: ESRCH asserted before the killed child is reaped
- V1-0779: tasks/store TestPSRRequestConflictAndOrphan/live-unknown-gone: 'new explicit request never executed', 2/8
- V1-0794: dispatch TestCALV0053_ReaderExpiredBeforeRetirement: 50 ms deadline, then nil cmd.Process panic in cleanup (confirmed test defect)
- V1-0796: tasks/store TestPSRSweepSuccessReplaySuccessor 'not freed' 2/3 in isolation; TestPSROrphanEarlyInitializationCleanup also reported
- V1-0815: tasks/store TestCALV0074_HostSwitchAndRollback: MALFORMED program transition under load (same symptom as V1-0771)
- V1-0817: tasks/store TestCALV0078_SupervisedRunAfterCommitIsNotRetryable: implementer ends BLOCKED_RECOVERY/MALFORMED under load (same symptom as V1-0771)

Common pattern: a wall-clock budget, poll interval, lock timeout or settle deadline in a test trips when the host is saturated (load averages 40-200 from parallel agent gates), and the test passes alone. The release candidates run `make gate` on a loaded release host, so these failures can fail a candidate without a product regression.

Not merged, still open separately: V1-0771 (suspected product race behind the MALFORMED program-transition refusals; V1-0815 and V1-0817 are its symptoms), V1-0825 and V1-0831 (unlocked-read races), V1-0703 (mixed clock in a fixture), V1-0665 (pre-lock map read), V1-0582 (bounded-blob fixture startup), V1-0662 (detached Git writers in fixtures), V1-0391 and V1-0397 (rc.2 fix lanes). A case found to be a product defect while working this umbrella gets its own ticket.
title: Test reliability umbrella: load- and timing-sensitive test failures (merges 19 flake tickets)

acceptanceCriteria: A maintained test or measurement at two store sizes shows that the work done under the writer lock in a lease commit does not grow with ticket count (CAL-V0-026).
Checkpoint recovery semantics are unchanged: a crash after the lease commit still recovers the same canonical state.
body: Found 2026-10-06 while fixing V1-0845 (branch claude/rc2-darwin-guard-locked-scan, commit e0fa13eb, base b7b21205, Darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1). After V1-0845 moved the darwin change-guard Sweep outside the writer lock, `commitLease` in internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go still calls `retainCheckpoint` while it holds the writer lock (journal/checkpoint.go:64 encodes, store/guards.go:119 writes). Retention traverses, sorts and encodes the whole canonical map, so locked lease work still grows with ticket count, contrary to CAL-V0-026. Expected: locked work independent of store size, for example by retaining the checkpoint after the lock is released or making retention incremental. Actual: O(store) work under the lock. Inferred from source, not yet measured; the V1-0845 spec and build log record it as the remaining store-size cost.
title: Tasks lease commit retains the checkpoint under the writer lock in O(store) time

acceptanceCriteria: When the dispatcher observes its launched worker process has exited and the attempt is still RUNNING, it retries `release --reason HANDOFF` itself with a bounded backoff.

Once the lease has expired and the release has not succeeded, the dispatcher reaps the attempt and quarantines the pool member exactly as reap does today; an attempt already FAILED/FENCED is treated as resolved, not as needs-owner.
`needs-owner` is reported only when both the release and the reap fail; a dispatcher config switch (default on) disables the automatic path.
Maintained tests cover worker-exit with live lease (release), with expired lease (reap), with an already fenced attempt (no needs-owner), and with the switch off.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#622 (orchestrator triage; reporter observations on main-2fff511, not reproduced yet).

When a dispatcher-launched worker exits and its attempt is still RUNNING, the dispatcher only reports `needs-owner` and leaves the attempt RUNNING and the pool member ALLOCATED until a human acts. Six occurrences in about 24 h on program flowproof (main-2fff511); the reporter runs an external steward.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch: release (HANDOFF, bounded retry) or reap a worker's RUNNING attempt when the launched worker exits, before reporting needs-owner (issue #622)

acceptanceCriteria: When explicit `--exclude-member` values are supplied, generations with no recorded member are treated as covered by them (the caller asserts the author set) and the claim proceeds, recording that the legacy generations were covered by explicit exclusion, not by recorded members.
Without explicit exclusions the refusal is unchanged (never silently unfiltered).
The integrate-stage behaviour when there is no implement generation at all is specified and documented; if nothing exists to exclude, the claim is not refused for it.
Maintained tests cover mixed legacy/recorded generations with and without explicit exclusions, and integrate with no implement generation; the leases spec states the rule.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#623 (orchestrator triage; reporter observations on main-2fff511, not reproduced yet).

`claim --stage review --pool P --exclude-authors` refuses the whole claim with INDEPENDENCE_UNVERIFIED when any earlier generation has no recorded member (claimed before V1-0788). Explicit `--exclude-member` values supplied by the caller do not help. The same flag on an integrate claim with no recorded implement generation also refused.
title: corvint-tasks claim --exclude-authors refuses INDEPENDENCE_UNVERIFIED when any prior generation predates recorded pool members, even with explicit --exclude-member (issue #623)

acceptanceCriteria: A ticket whose current workState is a hold does not count against the planner selection window; it is reported with a distinct deferral reason, not SELECTED.
Tickets that are actionable are selected up to the window as before; the decision is deterministic for a given snapshot and workState observation.
When workState is unavailable or UNKNOWN, behaviour is unchanged (fail closed, no silent widening).
Maintained tests reproduce the starvation (held tickets filling the window) and show the actionable ticket selected after the fix.

title: corvint-tasks plan: tickets held by the program's workState still occupy the maxActiveAttempts selection window, starving others with LIMIT_EXCEEDED (issue #624)

acceptanceCriteria: A batch form (for example `ticket refine --batch --payload-stdin` taking `[{target, expectedRevision, payload}]`) validates every entry before writing and applies them in bounded chunks, releasing the writer lock between chunks.
Each entry keeps its own CAS check and receipt; a failed entry is reported per entry and does not partially apply that entry; the result lists every entry's outcome.
Replay with the same request id is idempotent (CAL-V0-065 style).
Maintained tests cover all-success, one stale expectedRevision, malformed entry rejected before any write, and a claim committing between chunks.
body:

title: corvint-tasks: batch ticket mutation (refine many tickets in bounded chunks that yield the store lock) (issue #625)

acceptanceCriteria: Priority admission considers waiting claims across stages: on a tie in priority, the earlier waiting claim wins, and a review/integrate claim for a ticket that other open tickets depend on is ranked ahead of a new implement claim.
The ranking is derived (no new stored state) and deterministic, consistent with the V1-0784 contract; the spec states the cross-stage rule.
`dispatch status` (or the claim result) exposes the waiting claims considered and the admission decision.
Maintained tests reproduce the reported order (review waiting, implement arrives, member frees) and show the review admitted.

title: corvint-tasks priorityAdmission: a waiting review-stage claim for a higher-urgency ticket loses the freed member to a new implement claim (issue #626)

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint-tasks run --attempt` gains a detached mode whose command survives the launching session's exit while the attempt lease is held, keeps heartbeating, and stays fenced (killed if the attempt is fenced or reaped).

acceptanceCriteria: The dispatcher excludes a detached supervisor from a worker's stopped tree only when its recorded PID and start identity match the run record; a mismatch or missing record keeps today's behaviour.
The heal hand-off of an ended worker defers (or transfers the holder) while a detached run for that attempt is RUNNING and live, within a stated bound; otherwise it releases as today.
dispatch status / reports show each attempt's detached run state (RUNNING, FINISHED, SUPERVISOR_LOST) read-only.
Maintained tests: a dispatcher-launched worker exits while its detached run continues and a successor attaches to the outcome; a forged run record does not exempt a process.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

V1-0856 (beamfall/corvint#627) added `run --attempt --detach` and `run --attach`, but dispatcher integration was deferred (docs/specs/corvint-tasks-attempt-runner-v0.md, Detached runs, remaining work). Under the dispatcher a detached run is still stopped: CAL-V0-056 `refreshTree` adopts children of recorded members by parent PID, so the setsid supervisor can be counted in the worker tree and stopped, and the heal hand-off releases an ended worker's attempt, which fences the run within one beat. Both changes need an owner decision on identity-verified exclusion of a recorded supervisor and on deferred hand-off or holder transfer.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch: adopt detached attempt runs (CAL-V0-056 refreshTree exclusion, heal hand-off fencing, run status in reports) (follow-up to V1-0856 / #627)

acceptanceCriteria: On Darwin the memory signal is the kernel memory-pressure level (kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level), or the swap-out rate, not the swap used/total level; a high but static swap level alone no longer holds level 2.
The signal that set the current level is reported (reason: memory/swap/load) in dispatch status and the throttled event.
An unavailable signal is NOT_OBSERVED/uncertainty and does not fabricate calm or pressure; Linux behaviour is unchanged.
Spec CAL-V0-068 (agent-leases) is updated with numbered requirements, and maintained tests cover a sticky-swap sample with normal pressure level dropping the level.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

GitHub beamfall/corvint#636 (main-2fff511). CAL-V0-068 pressure throttle on Darwin (source darwin-sysctl-host) sat at level 2 all day: load 63.4 on 10 CPUs and swap used 0.85, while the Colima VM had a load of 2.5 on 8 vCPUs and memory_pressure showed 39% free. vm.swapusage used is sticky on macOS, and the load average counts Virtualization.framework vCPU threads. title: dispatch pressure throttle: macOS sticky swap level and VM-inflated load average pin the throttle at level 2 (issue 636)

acceptanceCriteria: release and attempt heartbeat accept a caller-chosen bounded --lock-wait SECONDS (bounded maximum, documented) and wait on the prepare lock instead of returning LOCK_TIMEOUT after the default wait.
Re-submitting an evidence HANDOFF release after LOCK_TIMEOUT with the same request ID is safe: it either commits once or replays the committed receipt, never a duplicate or a conflict.
No path silently converts a plain release into a HANDOFF; any fallback that keeps HANDOFF accounting requires the caller's explicit intent and the original evidence.
Spec requirements are added and maintained tests cover lock contention with --lock-wait, same-request-ID replay after a timeout, and the absence of a retry charge on the replayed HANDOFF.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

GitHub beamfall/corvint#637 (main-2fff511, 6-10 concurrent workers, journal head about 12,500). Evidence-form HANDOFF releases return the retryable LOCK_TIMEOUT on .git/taskman.prepare.lock (35 status files, 66 lines). A retry with a new request ID usually succeeds, but when it also times out, workers fall back to a plain release (FL-002 gen 2646, receipt 12144). That charges a retry and can quarantine the pool member, forcing a lane reset of 3-5 minutes. Related: #494, #545, V1-0645.
title: corvint-tasks release --reason HANDOFF returns LOCK_TIMEOUT on the prepare lock; the plain-release fallback charges a retry and quarantines the lane (issue 637)

acceptanceCriteria: With two or more divergent projections, the journal reader's refusal names the same path and the same code (INTENT_DIVERGED or JOURNAL_FORKED) on every run, chosen by a documented deterministic rule (for example the byte-smallest path).
A maintained test with at least two divergent projection files, repeated (e.g. -count=20), asserts the identical refusal path and code each run, and fails on the current map-order iteration.
No change to the refusal for a single divergent file or to the success path.
body: internal/tasks/journal/records.go (Reader.projections, about line 557) ranges over the `canonical` map and returns the first mismatch it meets. Go map iteration order is randomized, so with two or more divergent projection files the refusal names A.json on some runs and B.json on others, and the code can switch between INTENT_DIVERGED and JOURNAL_FORKED depending on which path is visited first. Read commands must be deterministic for identical stores. Reported by the rc.3 corvint-tasks performance lane on base origin/main 855077fc (observed on base code, not introduced by that lane); the map iteration was confirmed by reading the source at claude/rc3-batch-2. Fix: iterate in sorted path order (or collect all mismatches and report the first in canonical order).
title: corvint-tasks: journal projection refusal names a nondeterministic path and code when several projections diverge

On PR571, the affected section in `corvint review --base` reports `selected: []` with provider EMPTY_SELECTION, marks every changed source UNINDEXED_SOURCE_PATH with 'immutable source inventory incomplete', and claims NO_REPOSITORY_GATE_DECLARED ('no Makefile gate target or AGENTS.md Verify block'), although both exist. Cause: reviewGuidance (cmd/corvint/repository_guidance.go:429-480) runs affected.Build over a GuidanceSnapshot capped at 4096 entries / 8 MiB (internal/genesis/guidance.go:30-36); this repository has about 7265 files, so 2742 inventory entries and 3418 sources are never read. This violates product invariant 2 (missing evidence must produce uncertainty, not invented certainty).

acceptanceCriteria: The spec records the unit-level frontier design with numbered requirements, failure modes and rollback before implementation.

A plan whose changed root packages are not imported, directly or transitively, by any open nested module carries no nested-module unknown; a plan that changes such a package keeps it, naming the nested module.
An unreadable nested module or import graph keeps the plan-level frontier open (fail closed).

body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Found by the V1-0867 lane (branch claude/v1-0867-nested-frontier, d5128a48, base 3dc863bd). V1-0867 (AFP-V0-028) closes the go:nested-module-frontier only when no nested module can reach the root. In this repository tools/local-authority requires and replaces the root module (github.com/Beamfall/corvint => ../..), so every Go plan stays scope UNKNOWN on that frontier, even when the change touches no package local-authority imports. Its imports are internal/authoritystore, internal/localauthority and internal/cem/... Moving the frontier to unit level, attached to the root packages that an open nested module imports directly or transitively, would drop the unknown for most plans. This is a reachability design change that needs a spec decision.
title: affected: attach an open nested-module frontier to the root packages it imports instead of the whole plan

acceptanceCriteria: A spec defines a read-only plan-time adapter event (host-neutral, Claude Code ExitPlanMode first) whose output carries resolved anchors, affected checks and governing authority with the usual uncertainty and abstention rules.
The event never blocks or approves a plan on its own authority; it reports evidence and degradations only, and is not an input to ranking or learning.
A frozen evaluation measures whether plan-time evidence changes plan scope accuracy before it is advertised.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Idea from reviewing backnotprop/plannotator (2026-10-06): it hooks Claude Code's PermissionRequest on ExitPlanMode so every agent plan passes a review step, with diffs between plan revisions and structured feedback returned to the agent. Corvint already injects context at SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, but nothing evaluates the plan itself, which is the cheapest moment to catch a wrong scope. A plan-time event could resolve the plan's file and requirement anchors, attach affected-plan impact and governing authority, and flag plan steps that touch paths outside the declared scope, all read-only and advisory.
title: Plan-time hook: attach Corvint context and impact evidence when an agent submits a plan (ExitPlanMode), before code is written

acceptanceCriteria: A spec defines a versioned, strict snapshot format bound to base/head SHAs and the CEM digest, produced by a pure export function; the diff bytes come from the bound commits, never from the live worktree.

Chapters reuse V1-0408 ordering and cite the evidence that placed each hunk; a snapshot whose binding fails verification is refused, not rendered.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Idea from reviewing backnotprop/plannotator ADR 006/007 (2026-10-06): guided reviews are exported as one small self-contained HTML file holding a strictly versioned JSON snapshot (guide, the exact diff captured when the review job starts rather than at export, provenance), rendered by a pinned, content-hashed viewer; export is a pure function. That matches Corvint invariant 1 (evidence pinned to immutable Git content). Corvint's reviewer report and CEM are already immutable, but there is no single portable artifact a human reviewer can open offline, and no importance-ordered, chaptered walkthrough with per-chapter reviewed state. Ordering work already exists as V1-0408 (order review by AI-authored, unwitnessed hunks); this ticket is the export and walkthrough format.
title: Portable immutable review snapshot: one self-contained file binding the diff, CEM, reviewer report and a chaptered walkthrough

acceptanceCriteria: The leak is reproduced or the cause is confirmed, and every test-created keeper socketpair is close-on-exec under ForkLock like production.
A keeper whose test process exits is gone within a bounded time; a maintained test, or a cleanup in the test that spawns the keeper, proves it.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Observed 2026-10-06 on the owner's macOS host: process `cem01-go.test __cem01-stable-keeper/1` (pid 5049, parent launchd, alone in its own process group, state SN, 0% CPU) had been running for 4 days 23 hours from an already-deleted go-build directory under /var/folders/.../T. It exited on SIGTERM when the owner asked for cleanup. stableKeeperMain (interop/cem01-go/stable_process_darwin.go) blocks reading fd 3 until the owner end of its socketpair reaches EOF, then kills its group; so the owner end stayed open somewhere for days.

Suspected cause (inferred from source, not reproduced): the darwin keeper test (stable_process_darwin_test.go, around line 270) creates its socketpair with plain syscall.Socketpair, without syscall.ForkLock and CloseOnExec, unlike production at stable_process_darwin.go:268-274. A child process started concurrently by another test can inherit the owner fd and keep the keeper alive after the test exits. Which test run produced pid 5049 was not observed.
title: cem01-go darwin keeper test helper can outlive its test for days

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded decision: either the limitation is accepted in CAL-V0-117 with its operator rule, or the token is monotonic and a test shows a restored older token no longer rebinds an old checkpoint.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session.

Observed 2026-10-07 in Codex review round 3 of V1-0645 (c05766af, PASS with this explicit limitation). The checkpoint carries the SHA-256 of the `.writer-checkpoint.invalidated` token current at publication; consumers use it only while the digests match. Deleting the token alone (absence is the empty token) or restoring an earlier token value can make an older checkpoint match again. The build log documents coordinated removal with no refresh running. Expected: decide whether to accept this as an operator-only limitation or make the token monotonic (for example a counter bound into the checkpoint, never reused). Suspected risk only; no failure observed.
title: V1-0645: writer checkpoint invalidation token is not rollback-resistant (deleting or restoring the token rebinds an old checkpoint)

Documented limit. One retirement pass scans at most 4,096 dispatcher worker directories and 1,024 attempt directories (CAL-V0-144 / ATR-V0-015, proposed). With a larger backlog, the same first entries can be rescanned every pass and later ones are never reached.

Expected: a resume cursor (or rotating start) so every directory is eventually visited within the per-pass bound.
title: Worker and run retirement scans stop at 4,096 / 1,024 directories per pass, so a larger backlog can starve

queue status omits the retries map unless asked, with the wire contract updated in the same change.
--help is terse by default; reason codes and preconditions remain available behind an explicit verbose flag.
docs/TASKS-EXTERNAL-AGENTS.md tells agents to request summaries instead of printing full JSON.
Maintained tests cover each selector, refusal of unknown fields, and byte bounds.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#650 (owner: get it fixed and merged).

Observed on a 370-ticket queue: queue status 63 KB (retries map 64 KB of JSON), plan preview 120 KB, release --help 5 KB, attempt show 5 KB, ticket show 4.5 KB. 24 h of agent sessions returned 9.5 MB from 2,324 calls. Every byte stays in the agent context and is resent each turn.

Ask: a compact mode (--fields or --summary) on those reads; queue status without the retries map by default; terse --help by default with long reason codes behind --verbose; agent guidance in TASKS-EXTERNAL-AGENTS.
title: corvint-tasks: compact agent output for queue status, attempt show, ticket show, plan preview and --help (beamfall/corvint#650)

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatcher worker can end its session while its detached run continues, without the dispatcher stopping the supervisor or releasing the attempt (V1-0858 criteria).
When the detached command finishes, the dispatcher launches one session for the same ticket and role with the run outcome in its launch context, exactly once per finished run.
run --attach --wait returns one compact line.
Maintained tests: worker exits, run continues, run finishes, successor launched once with the outcome; a forged record neither exempts a process nor triggers a launch.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#651 (owner: get it fixed and merged).

Observed: agent sessions stay open only to poll long detached lane commands (1,644 sleep/tail polls and 2,555 context checks in 24 h); each poll resends 100k-190k tokens of context, and sessions hit their context stop mid-wait and lose the run. Depends on V1-0858 (dispatcher adoption of detached runs), which this delivery must include.

Ask: a worker starts run --attempt --detach, records its next step and ends; the runner keeps the attempt heartbeated; when the command exits the dispatcher relaunches a session for that ticket and role with the run outcome (exit status, receipt, log path) in its launch context; optionally a compact attach wait.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch: relaunch the ticket's session when a detached attempt run exits (beamfall/corvint#651)

acceptanceCriteria: Optional per-role and per-ticket sessionsPerDay and tokensPerDay budgets are enforced at launch over a rolling 24 h window; a held launch emits an event and appears in dispatch status.
Per-worker token totals from bounded parsing of host usage output are recorded in the ledger and the finished event; unparsed usage is reported as unknown, never zero.
dispatch status shows the model and effort each worker ran with when the configuration declares them.
Maintained tests cover budget holds, window expiry, malformed usage lines and the ledger encoding.
body:

acceptanceCriteria: One corvint-mcp process serves several repositories that the operator declares at startup (repeated --root or a roots file, each with a short alias); authority still comes only from operator startup arguments, never from client roots or request data (MCPV0-015 intent preserved).

Every repository-scoped tool takes a required repository alias when more than one root is declared; an unknown or missing alias is refused with a stable code; one declared root keeps today's single-root bytes and conformance vectors unchanged.
The tool list is sent once regardless of repository count; measured tools/list bytes and process count for 1, 3 and 10 roots are recorded against today's one-server-per-repo setup.
Repository bindings open lazily on first call, at most a bounded number stay open (least-recently-used close), and an idle server does no background work.
Each result stays bound to its own repository and revision identity (invariant 1); results from different roots never mix.
An accepted multi-root authority profile spec amends MCPV0-001/MCPV0-015 before implementation is called done; the same option is evaluated for the test-validity, docs and corpus servers.
Maintained tests cover alias routing, refusal of undeclared roots, the bounded open set, and single-root byte parity.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from an owner request: when several repositories are in use, agents run one Corvint MCP server per repository, and the owner asked to combine them into one server that routes to each repository.

Today MCPV0-001 makes corvint-mcp own exactly one --root, and MCPV0-015 says multi-root support later requires an accepted multi-root authority profile. So N repositories mean N processes and N copies of the same tool schemas in every agent turn.

Orchestrator recommendation: in-process multi-root routing in corvint-mcp, not a proxy that spawns one child per root (a proxy keeps N processes and adds lifecycle and error-forwarding work). Expected saving: tool-schema tokens drop from N times to once per turn; measured numbers come from the token-usage audit and the acceptance measurement. Spec acceptance is human-owned.
title: corvint-mcp: serve several operator-declared repositories from one MCP server instead of one server per repository

acceptanceCriteria: A holder can bind a second ticket's attempt to an allocation it already holds (claim --pool P --share-allocation ID or an equivalent verb); the binding is recorded in receipts, pool occupancy and attempt show.
The member stays ALLOCATED until the last bound attempt releases and is quarantined once per batch, not once per ticket.
Fencing: a bound attempt's lease cannot outlive the allocation; releasing the holder with attempts still bound is refused or hands the allocation over, as the spec states.
Sharing is bounded (a maximum number of attempts per allocation) and refuses foreign holders, other pools and stale allocations with stable codes.
Maintained tests cover bind, ordered and reversed release, refusal paths, crash recovery and journal replay.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#653 (owner: get the new GitHub issues fixed and merged).

Observed (Flow-Proof, 2026-10-07): each flow session claims a pooled lane, prepares it (image refresh, health, global setup: 4-5 min), runs one flow's tests and releases it; release quarantines the lane, which needs a 1-3 min cleanup reset. 97 flow sessions in 24 h paid this separately, about 11 of 96 lane-hours plus orientation tokens. The workaround claims extra tickets without --pool and records the shared allocation only as status text, so the queue cannot audit which allocation ticket B used.

Ask: a supported way for one holder to run several tickets on one allocation, with auditable binding, one quarantine per batch, and fencing.
title: corvint-tasks pool: bind several attempts to one held allocation for lane batching (beamfall/corvint#653)

acceptanceCriteria: An evicted pack or sectioned-snapshot mapping is unmapped once no in-flight Index still uses its bytes (for example a reference count or runtime cleanup), never while it is in use.
A long-lived process cycling through more than four snapshots keeps a bounded number of mappings; a maintained test proves the bound and use-after-unmap safety.
The contract is recorded in the owning index-snapshot spec.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from the V1-0938 multi-root MCP lane (suspected, pre-existing).

Observed in code at 79536edd: internal/contextindex/pack_reader.go retainPack (about line 544) and snapshot_sectioned.go retainSectioned (about line 390) delete an evicted mapping from the 4-entry ring cache without unmapping it, and no finalizer or runtime cleanup was found in internal/contextindex (the only Munmap is the failure path in snapshot_sectioned_mmap_unix.go:26). Expected: a long-lived process such as corvint-mcp (now possibly serving several repositories) keeps at most the cached mappings. Actual (inferred, not measured): every evicted mapping keeps its address space until exit. Clean file-backed pages are reclaimable, so RSS impact is unmeasured. Unmapping on eviction may be unsafe while an in-flight Index still references the bytes.
title: contextindex: evicted pack and sectioned snapshot mappings are never unmapped in long-lived processes (suspected)

acceptanceCriteria: After a full `go test -count=1 ./internal/tasks/dispatch` run, no process started by those tests remains (checked by process group or a recorded pid list).
Each test registers cleanup that stops and reaps its host and worker processes, including on t.Fatal paths.
A maintained check fails if a dispatch test leaves a descendant process alive.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from the beamfall/corvint#651 lane (branch claude/gh651, base 79536edd, head 5d1f7167; go1.27.1, darwin arm64).

Observed by the lane after `go test ./internal/tasks/dispatch`: TestCALV0127_Reload* leaves orphan `sleep 300` processes and TestCALV0143 leaves its host.sh worker running. acceptanceCriteria: A turn.completed event whose input_tokens or output_tokens is null makes ObservedUsage report unobserved.
A repeated or case-folded usage member makes ObservedUsage report unobserved.
Maintained tests cover null, repeated and case-folded counters on the supervised Codex host.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from the beamfall/corvint#652 lane (branch claude/gh652, base 79536edd, head 58f843f2; go1.27.1). Confirmed by reading the code.

internal/tasks/supervisor/events.go ObservedUsage decodes `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` with json.Unmarshal into uint64. A JSON `null` decodes without error and leaves 0, so a turn.completed event with null counters is reported as KNOWN zero usage. The usage object is a map, so a repeated or case-folded member is silently collapsed. Expected (matching CAL-V0-157 in the dispatch budget parser): null, repeated or case-folded counters make usage unobserved, never zero. Actual: 0 is reported.
title: supervisor: ObservedUsage reads a null Codex usage counter as 0 and accepts repeated or case-folded usage members

internal/tasks/dispatch/config.go DecodeConfig uses encoding/json with DisallowUnknownFields, which still accepts a repeated object member and keeps the last value (for example two `budget` members on one role, or two `roles` arrays). The lane's new budget members refuse repeats, but the outer configuration does not; this predates V1-0937. Expected: a repeated member anywhere in a dispatch configuration is refused as malformed, so an operator never runs a config that differs from what they read. Actual: the last value silently wins.
title: dispatch: DecodeConfig keeps the last value of a repeated JSON member instead of refusing it

acceptanceCriteria: In one clone, a stage-2 `dogfood begin` after a stage-1 seal either succeeds and keeps the stage-1 generation archived, or refuses with a documented next action.
A regression test covers begin after a satisfied, sealed enrollment whose target is an ancestor of HEAD.
docs/DOGFOOD.md describes the staged-binding route for over-cap batches.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session while binding the rc3 batch (beamfall/corvint#650 to #653) in three stages; installed corvint from PATH, go1.27.1, darwin arm64.

A batch over the 256-hunk or 256-obligation cap (V1-0394, V1-0522) must be bound in stages: bind and seal range BASE..M1, merge the next range, then bind M1-seal..M2. After stage 1 ended satisfied and sealed, `corvint dogfood begin --plan STAGE2 --session-key K` in the same clone refused with `{"code":"prior-completion-stale"}` (internal/localcompletion/lifecycle.go:77): the satisfied stage-1 enrollment is bound to its old target, so it no longer evaluates as satisfied once HEAD moves on. The refusal carries no next action. The only non-destructive route was a fresh clone for each stage; `dogfood cancel` would discard satisfied evidence. Expected: a sealed, satisfied enrollment whose target is an ancestor of HEAD is archived as a completed generation and lets the next stage begin, or the refusal names the supported route.
title: dogfood begin refuses the next stage of a staged binding with prior-completion-stale in the same clone

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatch config can declare shared prompt fragments once and reference them from any role prompt; the rendered prompt is byte-identical to the equivalent inline prompt, and its digest is unchanged.
Unknown, unused-by-policy, cyclic or oversized fragment references refuse at load with a stable code and name the role and fragment; the per-role rendered prompt keeps its existing byte limit.
A config without fragments loads and renders exactly as before (regression test).
The leases spec carries numbered proposed requirements, traceability and rollback for the fragment syntax.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/656 (2026-10-07). A dispatch config with 21 roles repeats a 6-8 KB rules block in every role `prompt`; adding one 250-character rule pushed dispatch.json to 270046 bytes and `dispatch status` refused it with LIMIT_EXCEEDED (file larger than 262144 bytes, internal/tasks/dispatch/config.go MaxConfig). About 86 KB is text repeated in at least 15 roles. Ask: a top-level fragment map that roles reference and that expands at render time, keeping the rendered prompt and its digest exactly as before; alternatives are a role promptFile or a raised cap for the config file only.
title: dispatch config: shared prompt fragments so repeated role rules exist once (issue 656)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec defines the note record, anchors, revision pinning, STALE rules, delivery, write/supersede/retract path, byte caps, secret screening and non-goals, with numbered requirements and rollback.
A note can be recorded with anchors and provenance; supersede and retract keep immutable history.
A note whose path anchor's content changed since its pinned revision reads as STALE; unchanged anchors read as CURRENT; an anchor that cannot be resolved reads as UNKNOWN, never CURRENT.
Claim output (or an explicit read) delivers the notes whose anchors intersect the claimed ticket's declared paths, as a compact projection under a byte cap with omitted counts; reads never mutate.
Note text is secret-screened on write and is labelled untrusted agent-authored data on delivery; notes never feed ranking, evidence or authority.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/655 (2026-10-07). Sessions rediscover the same how-to knowledge (how to reach a screen, which helper does a task, required setup, stable selectors) per ticket because it stays in the ticket's own notes. Adopters work around this with keyword-matched local stores that have no staleness, no anchor binding and no provenance. Ask: a Corvint-owned cross-ticket note record; each note binds to anchors (source paths or symbols, route or flow IDs, test files) pinned to the revision it was written at; a note becomes STALE when an anchor's content changes and stays marked until re-confirmed or superseded; notes whose anchors intersect a ticket's scope are delivered on claim (and later through corvint_query) as a byte-capped compact projection; writes record attempt, generation and evidence path as provenance, and supersede or retract with a reason over immutable history (as operator notes, ON-V0). Optional promotion of repeatedly confirmed notes through skill-export (LTA-V0-006).
title: Shared, anchored agent know-how notes across tickets: bound to source, stale on change, delivered on claim (issue 655)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec (extending AFU-V1 / DCP-V1) defines the screen graph, node/edge records, revision pinning and STALE rules, import-graph test join, projections with byte caps, scaffold and overlay seam, with numbered requirements, non-goals, failure modes and rollback.

Compiling a fixture app with router definitions, flow steps and a Playwright suite yields deterministic screen nodes keyed by app plus route template with resolved hierarchy; ambiguous or unresolved routes are reported as unknown, never guessed.
A spec that reaches a screen by clicking (no goto) is attributed to that screen through the import graph; an anchor whose content changed since the pinned revision reads STALE.
map_screen, map_flow, map_find and map_scaffold return results under their byte caps with omitted counts and an explicit full escape; no projection is unbounded.
map_scaffold drafts a spec skeleton with imports resolved against the fixture test repository and the closest asserting spec cited.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/657 (2026-10-07). Agents writing E2E tests for a large web app spend much of each session working out how to reach and drive a screen, although the facts exist across corpus navigation research (one MCP navigation search returned 135283 characters), router state definitions, the Playwright suite (page objects, workflows, scenarios, specs that click through from home), legacy visit URLs and learned run facts (issue 655). An adopter-side compiler joins these heuristically into per-screen cards (1.6 KB) and scaffolds (3.5 KB) with no revision binding. Ask: (1) a screen graph compiled from router definitions with real hierarchy resolution; edges from flow steps and test sequences; each node aggregates permissions, flags, data preconditions, page objects/methods, workflows, scenarios, steps with selector strength and source/test anchors, every element pinned to its read revision and STALE when an anchor changed; (2) test-suite join by import graph (spec -> page object -> screen), not URL; (3) capped projections map_screen/map_flow/map_find/map_scaffold with byte budgets and a --full escape; (4) scaffold from the graph and the closest asserting spec with imports resolved against the real test repository; (5) learned overlay attachment point for run-verified steps (issue 658) and know-how notes (issue 655). Extends AFU-V1 navigation and DCP-V1 corpus; never raises candidate research to behavioural truth.
title: Application map: revision-pinned screen graph compiled into the docs corpus with capped MCP projections and spec scaffolding (issue 657)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec defines the binding from PWP receipts to map elements, the status lattice (VERIFIED@rev, UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD, CONTRADICTED, unverified), evidence-based selector strength, delivery and the OCA-V0 authority limit, with numbered requirements and rollback.

A passing receipt whose test IDs cover a step binds it VERIFIED at the receipt's app revision with a receipt reference; an agent-declared binding whose test ID is absent from the receipt refuses with a stable code.
Changing the step's app source anchor makes it UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD; a failing receipt hitting the step makes it CONTRADICTED; unknown or unresolvable revision never reads VERIFIED.
Map and navigation queries return per-step verification status within their existing byte caps; reads never mutate.
Verified status never upgrades candidate research into behavioural truth or feeds ranking or authority.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/658 (2026-10-07). Corpus navigation research is candidate (source-backed, never browser-verified) and says it must be verified before use, yet adopter sessions run those steps daily against a pinned demo with passing Playwright runs and manifests; nothing feeds back, so a weak selector stays weak after 50 green runs and a step broken at the current revision is not flagged. The adopter workaround is an honour-system JSONL with no receipt binding, revision or expiry. Ask: a verification overlay where a passing Playwright external-provider receipt (PWP /1-/3 with app identity) binds to the screen/step/selector it exercised (derived from spec anchors or agent-declared and checked against the receipt test IDs); each element carries VERIFIED@<app revision> with a receipt reference, UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD when its app source anchor changes and CONTRADICTED when a failing receipt hits it; selector strength upgrades only from evidence; map and navigation queries return per-step status. Verification never turns candidate research into a behavioural claim beyond 'worked in this run at this revision' (OCA-V0). Builds on the issue 657 application map.
title: Run-verified navigation: bind passing Playwright receipts to map steps and selectors (VERIFIED@rev, stale on source change, contradicted on failure) (issue 658)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec amendment defines tsconfig/jsconfig discovery, baseUrl/paths/extends resolution, extension and index inference, type-only edge strength, UNKNOWN for unresolved bare specifiers, and bounds (extends depth, config size), with numbered requirements and rollback.
On a fixture with baseUrl and wildcard paths, impact on a page object lists every spec importing it through an alias; a regression test fails without the change.
An import resolved only through an extends chain resolves; a cyclic or over-deep extends chain refuses or reports UNKNOWN, never guesses.
An `import type` edge is reported as type-only; an unresolved non-package bare specifier makes the impact result incomplete (UNKNOWN), never silently complete.
Index build and impact on a large TS repository stay ms-scale per query; config parsing is bounded and cached per index build.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/659 (2026-10-07). `corvint impact` on a TypeScript page object in an E2E repository finds only relative-import dependants; about 28 specs importing it through tsconfig baseUrl/paths (`import X from 'lib/pages/...'`) are missed, so test selection from a page-object or helper change is empty instead of failing closed, and the application map (issue 657) cannot reuse the import graph. Ask: resolve module specifiers through the nearest tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json (compilerOptions.baseUrl, paths with * wildcards, extends chains), index files and extension inference (.ts/.tsx/.d.ts) per TypeScript bundler/node resolution; report `import type` as a weaker edge; report unresolved bare specifiers as UNKNOWN rather than silently dropping them. Related: V1-0283 (workspace-package importers).
title: impact: resolve TypeScript tsconfig/jsconfig baseUrl and paths imports; unresolved bare specifiers UNKNOWN, not dropped (issue 659)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec defines map_plan input/output, step resolution, shared setup, session and navigation optimisation rules, data handoff, byte caps, fail-closed UNMAPPED/STALE handling and the authority limit, with numbered requirements and rollback.
On the issue-657 fixture map, a multi-step plain-language request yields a deterministic typed plan under its byte cap, reusing one session per app and skipping redundant navigation.
A step with no mapped flow or with STALE anchors is reported UNMAPPED/STALE with the exploration needed; the planner never invents a path or reports full confidence.
Per-step confirmation reflects receipt-bound verification status (issue 658) and never upgrades candidate research into behavioural truth.
A drafted spec skeleton has one test.step per action with the expected outcome assertion named; available from the CLI and the corpus MCP.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/660 (2026-10-07): 'test this edge case where you do 5 things in different parts of the website in a row, and using this corpus you know exactly how to do it in the most optimal way possible'. Adopter workaround plans each step to a researched flow, one shared data setup (proven registry scenario, API clients for remaining entities), one browser session per app, direct-URL navigation without redundant re-navigation, per-step confirmed methods/selectors/asserts, data handoff between steps, and UNMAPPED gaps; it drafts a Playwright spec with one test.step per action. Ask: (1) map_plan(steps[]) over the issue-657 map with byte caps and typed per-step results (flow, screen, navigation, methods[confirmed], selectors[strength,verified], asserts, produces/consumes, confidence, unmapped), also via CLI; (2) confirmation from receipts (issue 658); (3) fail-closed composition: UNMAPPED or STALE steps are named with the exploration needed, never an invented path; (4) test-validity on the composed test's receipt checks each test.step asserts an outcome and cleanup ran; (5) stored plans anchored for impact re-selection (needs issue 659); (6) learning loop feeding confirmations and notes (issue 655) back to the map.
title: Scenario planner over the application map: plain-language multi-step requests to a fail-closed E2E plan (map_plan) (issue 660)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec amendment defines the filter, the timestamp fields and their derivation, lastCompletion, windowed counts and the advisory stalled signal, with numbered requirements, failure modes and rollback.
`ticket list --status COMPLETED,OPEN` returns only matching tickets with stable paging; an unknown status refuses with a stable code.

statusChangedAt/lastAttemptEndedAt are derived from receipts deterministically; queue status reports lastCompletion and 1 h / 24 h completion counts; a store with no completion reports null, not a guess.
Dispatch status and events report sessions since the last state change per ticket and emit a typed advisory stalled signal past the configured N; it never holds or blocks dispatch.
Reads never mutate and stay bounded: on a 15,000-receipt store, queue status and filtered list complete in milliseconds without a full receipt scan per call (measured).
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#661 (build main-0b45b05, 2026-10-07): an adopter queue completed no ticket for about 46 h while the dispatcher ran about 170 sessions, each reported as finished (exit 0, progress recorded); finding this needed a scan of about 15,000 receipts. `ticket list --status COMPLETED` refuses MALFORMED (list takes only --offset/--limit/--summary/--fields); records carry no status-change timestamps; `queue status` has byStatus counts only; dispatch never surfaces repeated sessions on one ticket without a state change; loop detection (#587/#609) is opt-in and keyed on candidate trees, so it cannot see evidence/status-only programs. Requests: (1) `ticket list --status S[,S]` plus --fields access to statusChangedAt (or completedAt) and lastAttemptEndedAt; (2) `queue status` lastCompletion {ticketId, at, receipt} and completions per 1 h / 24 h window; (3) dispatch status/events: sessions per ticket since its last state change and an advisory typed `stalled` signal past N sessions with no status transition (not a hold). Must stay ms-scale on large stores (no full receipt scan per read).
title: Queue throughput visibility: ticket list --status, transition timestamps, lastCompletion and a stalled signal (issue 661)

acceptanceCriteria: The owner records a decision on the V1-0015 -> V1-0014 dependency edge, and the store reflects it (edge corrected, or the exception recorded).
V1-0014's milestone and priority are confirmed or changed by the owner.
Whether complete-manual should refuse or warn on an unsatisfied COMPLETED-obligation dependency is answered; if yes, a fixes ticket is filed with a reproduction.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session while counting the tickets left before 1.0 (corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202, corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 build 360).

Observed: V1-0014 (Qualify independent proof producers and consumers; EXTERNAL, P0, milestone post-1-0) is OPEN. Its only dependent is V1-0015 (Ship a digest-pinned portable CI verifier; milestone v0-7), which carries a COMPLETED-obligation dependency on V1-0014 but was itself completed by complete-manual on 2026-09-23 (PR #75 and #88, decision 0356). So a COMPLETED ticket has an unsatisfied COMPLETED dependency. V1-0014 does not gate 1.0: V1-0020 and V1-0021 depend on V1-0015, which is already COMPLETED. A naive transitive walk from V1-0021 that traverses completed tickets reaches V1-0014 and misreports it as a 1.0 blocker.

Questions for the owner: (1) Is the V1-0015 -> V1-0014 edge inverted or obsolete (the portable verifier ships first, and independent qualification consumes it), so the edge should be removed or reversed? Note that set-dependencies is refused on COMPLETED tickets. (2) Is V1-0014 correctly post-1-0 with priority P0, or should it be re-prioritised? (3) Should complete-manual refuse, or at least warn, when a dependency with obligation COMPLETED is not COMPLETED? This is a suspected tooling gap, not a confirmed bug: the manual disposition may be intended to override.

Owner answer 2026-10-07 to questions 1 and 2: remove the edge; V1-0014 is not needed for 1.0 (it stays post-1-0). Done the same day: V1-0015 was reopened, its dependencies were set to none, and it was re-completed with its original evidence digest and reason plus a note (revision 5). Question 3 (should complete-manual refuse or warn on an unsatisfied COMPLETED-obligation dependency) remains open.
title: Owner question: V1-0015 completed with an unsatisfied dependency on open V1-0014 (post-1-0); fix the edge, and should complete-manual refuse?

acceptanceCriteria: complete-manual on a ticket with an unsatisfied COMPLETED-obligation dependency commits and emits a warning naming each unsatisfied dependency and its status.
No warning when every dependency is satisfied; the receipt/mutation contract is otherwise unchanged and the warning is deterministic (dependencies in canonical order).
A maintained test covers both cases; the governing Tasks spec records the requirement.
body:
Owner decision 2026-10-07 (V1-0978): complete-manual should warn when the target ticket has a dependency with obligation COMPLETED whose ticket is not COMPLETED. The completion still commits (the manual disposition may override); the warning makes the override visible.

Reproduction: in the corvint queue, V1-0015 (dependency: V1-0014, obligation COMPLETED) was completed by complete-manual on 2026-09-23 while V1-0014 was OPEN, and no warning was emitted. Synthetic: create ticket A (OPEN), create B depending on A with obligation COMPLETED, then run `corvint-tasks ticket complete-manual --target B ...`. Expected: outcome OK plus a warning naming A and its status. Actual: outcome OK with only the actor-binding warning.

Versions: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202; corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 360). Likely code: internal/tasks/mutation/ (COMPLETE_MANUAL apply/verified) and internal/tasks/cli/mutate.go.
title: corvint-tasks complete-manual: warn when a COMPLETED-obligation dependency is not COMPLETED

Recovery needed the old binary run with --once and launches held. Code: internal/tasks/dispatch/ledger.go. Versions: corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 360); corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202; reporter on main-0b5096c, macOS arm64.

body: Follow-up from the V1-0947 lane, 2026-10-07. Confirmed by measurement: with CORVINT_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT=pack or sectioned (opt-in; the default gob path does not map), evicted mappings are never unmapped; deleted snapshot files keep their disk blocks while mapped. Unmapping on ring eviction, and runtime.AddCleanup on the retained packFile, both SIGSEGV under the V1-0947 guard test (TestEvictedMappingsStayValidForEscapedAliases), because Symbol.Path, Symbol.Name, Source.Text() and doccorpus-retained Source values alias mapping bytes without keeping any owner alive. V1-0947 bounds mappings to distinct files by reusing the mapping of an unchanged file; this ticket covers releasing mappings at all. Design options: an explicit lifetime (lease or Close) with copy-out wherever an alias can outlive it, or heap-backed/copied bytes within the pack spec's 8 MB heap limit. Versions: corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 360); corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202; darwin 25.6.0, go1.27.1.
title: contextindex: lifetime-bounded unmapping of pack/sectioned snapshot mappings (lease or Close plus copy-out), follow-up to V1-0947

acceptanceCriteria: With the opt-in flag the project's reporters run and produce their outputs in the same run, and the provider receipt is still retained and accepted by test-validity.
The receipt binds the original reporter list; without the flag behavior and bytes are unchanged.
The PWP spec records the requirement and its limits; a maintained test covers both modes.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#670. Since #665 test-validity abstains with no-retained-evidence unless the run goes through `corvint-js-test-provider e2e --retain`, whose controlled config replaces the project's reporter list. An adopter's own reporter writes evidence manifests its gates need, so they must run the 25-minute suite twice or lose one side's evidence. Coordinator decision: implement the issue's first option, an opt-in flag (e.g. --keep-reporters) that appends the provider reporter to the project's original reporter list and binds the original reporter entries (and config digest, already PWP-V0-002) in the retained receipt. The default stays replace-only; the qualified tuple and sensitive-input policy guarantees must hold, and anything the provider cannot observe about extra reporters is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than trusted. Ingest from foreign JSON/blob reports is out of scope. Versions: corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 360), reporter on main-0b5096c; corvint-tasks build 202.
title: Playwright provider: opt-in additive reporters so retained test-validity evidence coexists with project reporters (GitHub #670)

acceptanceCriteria: With the policy key absent or false, WORKER add is refused exactly as today.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#671. Know-how notes (KHN-V0, #655) are writable only by OWNER (OPERATOR via explicit policy row); decisions 0443/0444 grant WORKER nothing, so dispatched workers who learn navigation facts keep an unscreened local store. Coordinator decision: add an opt-in policy key (e.g. knowHow.workerAdd, default false) that lets a WORKER run `ticket know-how add` only on the ticket where it holds a live attempt, only with anchors inside that attempt's effects.touchPaths (or a policy-declared prefix), with the existing 1024-byte, 4-anchor, 32-entry caps and secret screen, recording attempt and generation (V1-0964). Every other WORKER write stays refused with a stable code. Versions: corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 360), reporter on main-0b5096c; corvint-tasks build 202.
title: Know-how notes: policy-gated, ticket- and touchPath-scoped WORKER add grant (GitHub #671)

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatched worker whose attempt stays LEASE_EXPIRED past the configured grace has its attempt reaped, its allocation released through quarantine and cleanup, and the worker signalled TERM then KILL, covered by a test with a non-renewing worker.

Workers within the grace, or that renew, are untouched (test).
body:
Filed 2026-10-08 by the orchestrator.

GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#674 (owner, 2026-10-08, main-0b5096c, 4-member demo-lanes pool, load 20-40 on 10 CPUs). A dispatched worker that is still running but no longer renews keeps its expired attempt: queue status shows holderStatus LEASE_EXPIRED with phase RUNNING, the pool allocation stays ALLOCATED, and the ticket is blocked as ATTEMPT_LIVE. Observed holds of 50-75 minutes past expiry. At 10:22Z three of four members were held by expired attempts, and no ticket completed for six hours. #622 covered the exited-worker case only. Today the only remedy is an external operator reap. Expected: after a configured grace (for example roles[].expiredLeaseGraceSeconds), the dispatcher reaps the attempt (allocation follows quarantine then cleanup), signals the worker TERM then KILL after idleSeconds as for the wall-time limit, and records a lease-expired event. Optional: deliver a stop-and-hand-off notice first when the adapter supports message injection.
title: Tasks dispatch: reap a running worker's attempt and stop the worker once its lease has been expired past a grace period (issue 674)

body: Suspected defect, not yet reproduced. On 2026-10-08 about 12:00 UTC the owner reported a macOS privacy prompt asking to allow corvint-tasks to access the Music folder (owner wording: 'why is corvint-task asking for permisson t to my music'). At that time the orchestrating Claude Code session had run read-only corvint-tasks ticket show/search/receipt audit and four ticket grant-approval mutations from /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint, and five agent lanes plus a dogfood bind were running go test for internal/tasks packages in /private/tmp/claude-501 worktrees. acceptanceCriteria: ticket create and ticket refine with empty touchPaths and resources report an explicit whole-repository warning (or require an explicit opt-in) in the command result, with a stable code.
queue status and plan preview name tickets deferred only because of the whole-repository serial fallback.
Spec amendment with numbered proposed requirements, failing-before/passing-after focused tests, independent review and sealed change evidence; GitHub #679 closed by the merged PR.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#679. ticket create accepts effects.touchPaths=[] with no resources; the planner then falls back to serialFallback WHOLE_REPOSITORY and the ticket stays DEFERRED/RESOURCE_COLLISION behind every live attempt with no warning at create time or in queue status. Observed in an adopter queue on 2026-10-08: a P0 ticket was deferred until ticket set-effects added four touchPaths. Proposal: warn (EFFECTS_UNBOUNDED) or require an explicit whole-repository opt-in on create/refine; list fallback-only deferrals in queue status / plan preview; optionally --effects-from <ticket>.
title: corvint-tasks: ticket create with empty effects silently serializes against the whole repository (GitHub #679)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec (human acceptance required) defines the input/output contract, grouping and isolation rules, determinism and fail-closed check, with non-goals, failure modes and rollback.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#681. Add a corvint test-plan consolidate projection (or MCP consolidate_tests) taking variations (ids + route/screen/setup anchors) and existing tests from test-validity, returning: groups sharing fixture state + screen + user that can be ordered steps of one test; variations needing isolation with the reason; existing passing tests that already witness a variation; duplicate variations. acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec (human acceptance required) defines fault derivation, the single-step-failure pass rule, revision binding, --all-steps semantics, UNPROVEN abstention, non-goals, failure modes and rollback, consistent with the existing test-validity contract.
After acceptance: implementation with focused and hostile tests, a real Playwright qualification and sealed change evidence; GitHub #682 closed by the merged PR.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#682. The test-validity strength axis needs a negative control (with the witnessed outcome altered, the named assertion step fails); today each control is hand-authored per variation (~3,600 controls in one adopter queue) and not reusable across revisions. Proposal: corvint test-validity negate --spec S --test T --step <title> reruns the test with a fault injected for that step's observable (Playwright network fault rewriting the response recorded in the passing run's trace, or a DOM fault hiding/altering the asserted element); PASS only when the named step and only that step fails; result stored on the strength axis bound to the revision; --all-steps covers every step in one run via expect.soft; steps with no derivable fault report strength UNPROVEN (manual control needed).
title: test-validity: generate step-level negative controls by fault injection (GitHub #682)

acceptanceCriteria: A receipt written for a runner-killed run (timeout or SIGKILL, exitCode -1) decodes, or is refused with a specific named code, rather than a generic malformed-receipt refusal.

body:
Found by the V1-0597/0613 SwiftPM lane on 2026-10-08 (Corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 build 360, branch claude/v1-0597-0613-swiftpm).

Observed: when the runner kills a run (PROCESS_TIMEOUT), the receipt records exitCode -1. The receipt decoder refuses that receipt; it fails closed, so no wrong result is accepted, but a timed-out run's receipt cannot be read back.

Expected: a killed run's receipt round-trips, or the refusal names the killed-run case.

Candidate site (suspected, not confirmed as the decoder path): internal/testrunner/validate.go:118 rejects ExitCode < 0.

Reproduction: run a SwiftPM fixture with a 30 s timeout that hangs (lane evidence /private/tmp/claude-501/swiftpm-td/live2/), then decode the receipt.
title: Test runner: receipt from a killed run (exitCode -1) is refused by the receipt decoder

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed AMAP spec amendment (human acceptance required) defines DI-constant resolution, the fail-closed cases and the name_from anchors.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#685, follow-up to #669 (V1-0981, AMAP-V0-016) on main-ecfff8e. On an adopter AngularJS admin app, appmap build still reports 153 of 176 states non-literal-name: the state-name table reaches the router function as an injected parameter (const Routes = ($stateProvider, StateConstants) => $stateProvider.state(StateConstants.X, ...)) registered with .constant('StateConstants', T), not via a static import. Ask: resolve a router-function parameter or $inject entry N through a .constant('N', T) registration in a tracked file where T is a wholly readable table (object literal, or a const/enum that file imports); fail closed (state stays non-literal-name) on multiple registrations of N for the app, a non-literal name, or an unprovable T; record the .constant line and table declaration as name_from anchors.

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed KHN spec amendment (human acceptance required) defines repository-qualified anchors, prefixed scope matching and per-repository freshness, with fail-closed handling of unknown aliases.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#687, follow-up to #671 (V1-0987, KHN-V0-021..023) on main-ecfff8e. ticket know-how add pins --anchor blobs at --commit (default HEAD of the working directory) and finds the task store from the working directory; a WORKER add also needs every anchor inside the ticket's effects.touchPaths. Programs whose queue lives in one repository while tickets touch others (touchPaths namespaced by repository prefix) cannot add WORKER know-how: from the store directory only queue-repository files can be pinned, from the work repository the store is not found, and repository-relative anchors never match prefixed touchPaths. Ask: name the anchor's repository (--repo ALIAS=ROOT as appmap build does, or --anchor ALIAS:path pinned against that root's HEAD), match WORKER scope against touchPaths with the same repository prefix, and compute claim-time freshness against that repository's HEAD; alternatively a store-location flag plus a documented touchPath-prefix-to-root mapping.
title: know-how: WORKER add unusable for multi-repository programs (GitHub #687)

acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether a /0 step-negation join (LPCV-V0-068) must also bind helper and support files, or records the spec+config-digest binding as an accepted limitation.

acceptanceCriteria: Decide by verifier contract change (with Python-oracle/divergence adjudication) whether a Go t.Run case anchor on its parent func header line is admitted; record the decision and either implement it in extractableGoClaim (internal/lrfrepo/ocm.go) or keep OCM-V0-018's unsupported boundary.

Align or document the parent-test derivation in internal/lrfrepo/ocm_goindex.go (anchor position) versus extractableGoClaim (last Test header ending before the anchor line), with a test pinning the agreed rule.
body: Found by the V1-0520 lane (2026-10-08, base f33ea8ef, lane head 67a0a8e2). An inline layout such as `func TestX(t *testing.T) { t.Run("case", ...) }` yields only the test claim: candidate listing (ocm_goindex.go:135) derives the parent from the anchor position, while the verifier (ocm.go:874 extractableGoClaim) takes the last Test header that ends before the anchor's line starts, so a same-line anchor has no parent and the candidate is dropped (claim-selector-out-of-range). V1-0520 kept this as the proposed OCM-V0-018 boundary and fixed the misleading hint. Expected: either the capability (needs verifier/authority change and oracle adjudication) or a documented single derivation. Actual: two derivations that agree only because enumeration filters by the verifier. Suspected latent mismatch, not a confirmed bug.
