acceptanceCriteria: Each listed site signals before the reap or carries a documented, tested reason; a regression test per changed site; the audit outcome for the three audit-only sites is recorded.
body:
Found during V1-0373 (batch L, 2026-10-08, Core v1 line at origin/main 38fcf067). After V1-0373 the groupreap adopters signal before the reap, but other spawners still signal a group after Wait has collected the leader, so a recycled group ID can be signalled or misjudged.

Sites (paths at 38fcf067):
- cmd/corvint/work_runner.go:200 defers workKillGroup(command) after command.Wait() (work_process_unix.go).
- internal/tasks/store/pool_process_unix.go:125 probes, then kills after the reap (check-then-act).
- internal/releasegate/git_unix.go processGroupGone sends signal 0 to the group after the reap; harmless but can falsely refuse on group-ID reuse.
- Needs a pre-reap audit: internal/tasks/store/gate_process_unix.go killGate, internal/tasks/dispatch/process_unix.go:111, and the kill(-pid) sites in dashboard/repository and opencodequalification.

Expected: every group signal is sent while the leader is still unreaped (waitid WNOWAIT, as groupreap does), or the site documents why the post-reap signal cannot hit a reused group. Actual: post-reap signals at the sites above.

Independent review of b2a0b8c6..032246d2 (2026-10-09; installed Core rc.2 build 360, Tasks build 202):
P2: new WaitResidue reuses Darwin QuietProof, which maps kill(-pgid,0) EPERM to ProbeQuiet. XNU killpg1 skips zombies and returns EPERM when no member is signalable, including live members denied by credentials/MAC. With those members closing inherited pipes and a successful leader exit, WaitResidue returns false and the work runner can pass. Expected: ambiguous permission failure is residue/unproved; distinguish zombie-only groups with a process-table observation. Source witness: internal/groupreap/groupreap_unix.go:35-43 and owner_waitid.go:25-35; apple-oss-distributions/xnu bsd/kern/kern_sig.c killpg1_callback/killpg1. This is a source-confirmed ambiguity inherited by the new API, not a live privileged fixture reproduction. Acceptance: separate zombie-only and denied-live-member tests, preserve fail-closed result.
P2 test gap: TestV11036PoolPostReapObservationSendsNoGroupKill records only poolGroupSignal calls. Original removed post-reap calls were syscall.Kill and killGate, neither routed through that seam; restoring those exact calls bypasses its kill assertion. Expected: negative control restores original code without additionally rerouting it. Build-log discrimination claim requires that qualification. Source inspection only; no unsafe raw post-reap mutant executed.
Validation: focused Darwin tests and race tests pass for all five packages; Linux/Windows cross-builds pass; FreeBSD library builds pass but command build hits unrelated internal/cem/publish openBoundedInput undefined. Linux runtime NOT_RUN. No implementation changed by review.
title: Remaining process-group signals after the leader reap: work runner, pool probe, release gate

acceptanceCriteria: procgroup ignores CLD_TRAPPED/CLD_STOPPED/CLD_CONTINUED waitid reports (shared helper with groupreap or an equivalent check) and a Darwin test stops then continues a leader and observes no early exit.
body:
Found during V1-0373 (batch L, 2026-10-08). internal/procgroup/process_posix.go:38 waitProcessExitUnreaped calls waitid(P_PID, WEXITED|WNOWAIT) and returns nil on any errno 0. On Darwin, waitid can report a stopped/continued child despite WEXITED (golang/go#19314; observed on Darwin 25 as si_code CLD_STOPPED). internal/groupreap/waitid.go (stateChangeOnly) now polls past si_code 4..6; procgroup has the same pattern without that check, so a SIGSTOPped leader is treated as exited and terminateProcessGroup escalates to SIGKILL of a still-live group.

Confirmed by code comparison at batch L (b26aea28); no procgroup runtime reproduction yet.
title: procgroup waitProcessExitUnreaped treats a Darwin waitid stop/continue report as an exit

acceptanceCriteria: Inventory of Setpgid spawners reachable from adapter/hook paths; each is recorded in the live registry or documented as unreachable from an exiting adapter; the xcrun owned-worker case stays inside the worker group; a test proves an adapter exit kills a recorded non-Git group.
body:
Found during V1-0734 (batch L, 2026-10-08). After V1-0734, KillLive at adapter os.Exit kills child groups recorded in the groupreap live registry. Other spawners that create private groups with Setpgid (tools, testrunner, tasks and others) are not recorded, so if the adapter watchdog or event deadline calls os.Exit while they run, their groups outlive the adapter. Related residual windows recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-08-batch-l-integration.md: a foreign reaper (ECHILD) can collect a recorded leader before KillLive, and platforms without waitid keep a post-reap signal. Review P2 (lane-0734): internal/gitstatus/executable.go:78 creates a private group even after EnableOwnedWorker(), so on Darwin with /usr/bin/git an xcrun child escapes the enclosing worker group.

Independent review dad48885..cc2378cb (Darwin, 2026-10-09): P2 at internal/procgroup/process.go:361. On ECHILD, the newly registered leader remains in liveGroups throughout BeforeStop and group cleanup, unlike groupreap.waitHeld immediate failure release. A concurrent exitProcess can therefore signal a reaped/reused numeric PGID even after failed observation is known. Scratch Go overlay reproduction: Run a shell exiting 0; AfterStart uses Wait4(pid) to reap; BeforeStop first confirms waitProcessExitUnreaped(pid)==ECHILD then inspects the live registry under its mutex. TestReviewECHILDReleasesBeforeStop fails: reaped leader remains registered after ECHILD, during BeforeStop. Expected: failed observation promptly releases the record and performs no numeric termination, with regression coverage. Correct build-log line 103 immediate-release claim. Existing focused Darwin race tests pass; TestAHI049ExitProcessKillsProcgroupGroup fails on base overlay in 60.06s and passes at head. Windows vet passes. This confirms stale registration, not observed actual PGID reuse.
title: Adapter exit does not kill Setpgid groups outside the groupreap live registry

acceptanceCriteria: Spec amendment in docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md: numbered proposed requirements for pool acquire/release on a live attempt (fencing by attempt+generation, waiting/queueing like a pooled claim, independence and exclusion rules applied at acquire time, release quarantines the exact allocation, lease/heartbeat/run/gate use the current allocation, replay returns the original receipt-bound allocation), failure modes and rollback.

CLI `corvint-tasks pool acquire --attempt ID --generation G --pool ID --request-id ID` and `pool release --attempt ID --generation G --allocation SHA --request-id ID` implemented through the transactional writer, with focused tests per requirement including stale-generation refusal, double acquire, release of a foreign allocation, and an attempt that completes while holding an acquired member.
Existing `claim --pool` behaviour unchanged (regression tests pass); GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#696 answered and closed after merge.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#696 (2026-10-08). A pool member can only be allocated by `claim --pool`; an attempt cannot acquire a member later or return it early. Adopter measurement on a 4-member pool: after authors claimed with --pool, about 70% of 688 held member-minutes were idle (vs ~21% when a runner claimed lanes only for commands), and sessions saw no free lane while members sat idle. The workaround (release HANDOFF then reclaim with --pool) costs two queue writes, a new generation and session context, plus a quarantine sweep (median 2.5 min) per cycle. Request: just-in-time `pool acquire` / `pool release` on a live attempt, with lease, heartbeat, run and fencing using whatever allocation the attempt currently holds and #480/#586 independence/exclusion rules applied at acquire time.
title: corvint-tasks pool: a live attempt can acquire and release a pool member (just-in-time lane use, #696)

acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction with a large receipt journal shows `pool confirm-safe` no longer decodes the full receipt history under taskman.prepare.lock: either it builds on the writer checkpoint (as `queue status` does) or the history read happens before lock acquisition with a revalidation under the lock; a focused test or benchmark pins the bound (e.g. receipts decoded or lock hold time independent of journal length).

Concurrent heartbeat/claim during confirm-safe no longer exceeds the 30 s preparation acquisition on the reproduction; existing pool safe-reuse semantics (V1-0695, V1-0674) are preserved; GH #701 is closed with the evidence.
body: beamfall/corvint#701 (2026-10-09, corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.0, Corvint main a5527cf42, macOS, ~10 concurrent clients). With a queue of about 21,100 receipts (.git/taskman 265 MB, writer-checkpoint 1.4 MB), `corvint-tasks pool confirm-safe --member lane-3` ran for more than 4 min at ~22% CPU. It was the only holder of taskman.prepare.lock and prepare.slot.00. A sample was dominated by wire parser, journal.Reader.step and snapshot.DecodeReceipt, which is a full journal decode rather than a checkpoint-based one. `queue status` takes 0.61 s by comparison. Concurrent confirm-safe, claim and heartbeat calls failed with LOCK_TIMEOUT after 30 s (rank=3, then rank=8). A caller timeout killed confirm-safe at 240 s before commit, so the lane stayed QUARANTINED and the work was lost. Expected: confirm-safe derives state from the writer checkpoint as queue status does, completes in seconds, and does not hold the prepare lock while decoding history. Entry point: internal/tasks/cli/lease.go.
title: GH #701: pool confirm-safe replays the full receipt journal while holding taskman.prepare.lock, starving heartbeats/claims with LOCK_TIMEOUT

acceptanceCriteria: Both waits ignore si_code 4..6 reports and return only on a real exit; a focused test per package SIGSTOPs a child, asserts the wait does not return, then SIGCONT/kills it and asserts the wait returns without reaping.
body: Found during V1-1037 (lane 2026-10-09, base 986cec7c). internal/dashboard/repository/process_wait_darwin.go (~line 73) and internal/testsupport/pipedrain_unix.go (~line 122) call waitid(P_PID, WEXITED|WNOWAIT) and treat any errno 0 as exit. Confirmed by code inspection; no runtime reproduction yet.

acceptanceCriteria: An accepted spec slice defines the Corvint Claude Code mod: surfaces, events, version gate (Claude Code 2.1.287+ terminal, 2.1.286+ desktop), and fallback to the existing hooks.json adapter where mods do not run (claude -p, Agent SDK, VS Code panel, cloud, WSL).

body: Claude Code now supports mods: in-process JS plugins that can draw panes, prompt bands, toasts and status lines, add slash commands and tools, and guard or annotate tool calls (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview). They are not sandboxed and run with user permissions. Corvint's Claude Code adapter today is hooks.json command hooks with 2 s timeouts; this session repeatedly shows corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-deadline degradations and large untrusted JSON envelopes injected into model context. Candidate uses: (1) status line and band showing context coverage, degradations, dogfood lifecycle and v1.0 ticket counts instead of model-facing JSON; (2) a pane for roadmap, readiness and CEM/review state; (3) /corvint commands for context, affected, tasks; (4) deny-only PreToolUse guards, e.g. push before dogfood-seal; (5) compaction pin verification shown to the user; (6) async event dispatch to avoid the 2 s deadline. Needs a spec (invariant 8), security review of an unsandboxed in-process module, and must keep the hooks.json path as fallback. Not on the 1.0 critical path unless the owner says so.
title: Claude Code mod adapter: user-facing Corvint status, panes and deny-only guards

acceptanceCriteria: After a core binary update that changes the index engine key, the next SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hook in an already-indexed checkout does not degrade with dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale; either the updater rebuilt the snapshot for live heads, or the hook started one bounded background refresh and said so.

Any automatic refresh writes only derived state under the Git common dir's corvint/index store, honours the existing eviction bound, never runs inside a read command's own path, and records its outcome (built, skipped, failed) visibly.
A regression test covers update-then-hook on a fixture repository; the governing spec records the requirement, non-goals (no permanent daemon), failure modes and rollback.
body: Observed 2026-10-09 on darwin-arm64 in /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint. At 21:42 the installed corvint was replaced by Corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 404) (engine key cd22c042fc84a53e) from build 360 (engine a7293de93d52e9e6). A snapshot already existed for the main checkout's HEAD tree 0cb16f6e0edeb09b390768f14102e11085419a65 under the old engine (sha1-0cb16f6e...-a7293de93d52e9e6.gob), but snapshots are keyed by engine, so every subsequent Claude Code SessionStart (including source=compact) and UserPromptSubmit hook degraded: 'Corvint FALLBACK degraded: corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale ... Refresh the snapshot once, outside the hook: corvint --root ... index --if-stale'. The user saw this after a compaction and asked why and whether it could happen automatically. Running the suggested command took 2.0 s wall (6359 sources) and cleared it. Expected: a binary update does not leave every session degraded until a manual reindex. Candidate designs: (a) corvint-update apply --component core rebuilds snapshots for live heads (it is already an explicit operator mutation); (b) the SessionStart hook, on a stale snapshot, launches one detached, bounded 'index --if-stale' and reports it, without blocking the hook deadline; (c) reuse an old-engine snapshot when the engine change does not alter the snapshot encoding. Invariant 4 (read commands do not mutate) and 7 (no permanent daemon) constrain (b).
title: Index snapshot goes stale for every session after a core binary update until a manual corvint index --if-stale

acceptanceCriteria: Measure btime stability on a GitHub Linux runner and record the result.
Either keep btime with a tolerance or migrate identities to a stable boot identifier, with an explicit compatibility decision for persisted ledgers, markers and run records.
A test proves a live process keeps a matching identity when btime differs by one second.
body: Suspected defect found 2026-10-10 while diagnosing the PR #725 dispatch flake (branch claude/dispatch-detached-rig-flake, commit 0c77b817). Linux process identities are linux:<btime>:<starttime> (internal/tasks/supervisor/identity_linux.go). In a docker golang:1.27.1 VM, 3000 samples of /proc/stat btime gave 1789760570 1076 times and 1789760571 1924 times, so a live process's identity can stop matching its recorded one. Under stress this produced: DeferralIsBounded 'released [claim]' after endWorker; SupervisorLostHandsOffWithoutRelaunch handing off without a SUPERVISOR_LOST alert; and an index-out-of-range panic in newDetachedRig (leader identity mismatched, empty tree, worker accounted ended while running). Production consequence: a running worker can be treated as ended/ORPHANED and a detached supervisor can fail verification. internal/tasks/service/descendants_linux.go:248 and internal/postmergeproof/procfs/procfs_linux.go:25 already use /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id. Fixing changes a persisted identity format (ledger, markers, run records), so it needs a migration decision. Frequency on GitHub runners: NOT_OBSERVED. Expected: identity of a live process is stable across reads. Actual: it can flip with btime rounding.
title: Suspected: Linux process identity uses /proc/stat btime, which jitters by one second between reads

body: Found 2026-10-10 by the CI audit (report /private/tmp/claude-501/gotmp/ci-audit.md; 60 ci.yml runs; main run 38055182050). PR wall median 39.8 min, critical path always go-product-shard 0. acceptanceCriteria: `corvint-update check --component tasks` reports installedVersion as the plain version string (e.g. `0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.407`), not the full `corvint-tasks version` JSON envelope.

body:
Observed 2026-10-10 on darwin-arm64. `corvint-update` built from origin/main 284c4312, `corvint-tasks` build 407.

Repro: `corvint-update check --component tasks --allow-network`.

Expected: installedVersion is the short Tasks version, matching how Core reports `Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 407)`.

Actual: installedVersion holds the entire `corvint-tasks version` JSON result (formats list, warnings, etc.) escaped into a string, a multi-kilobyte field. installedBuild (407) is correct. Related but distinct: V1-0639 (check does not say whether the available release is newer).
title: corvint-update check reports the Tasks installedVersion as the whole version JSON envelope

acceptanceCriteria: A single commit with more than 256 hunks, each cited, binds and passes dogfood-check without restructuring history, or docs/DOGFOOD.md documents staged binding as the supported route with the exact steps.
Any new bound is stated in the refusal fix text and covered by a test at the bound and one past it.
No hunk becomes uncited or cited implicitly: the CEM still reports supported=hunks, unknown=0.
body: Observed 2026-10-10 (corvint-tasks build 407, origin/main 556fef97) on the store test-speed lane (PR beamfall/corvint#735). The change was one test-only commit with 279 hunks, mostly one-line t.Parallel() insertions across 51 files. Pass 2 of `make dogfood-change` refused `cem-cite: invalid-citation-plan` with fix text 'at most 256 rows' (internal/dogfoodflow/change.go:1005); the same 256-row bound applies to DOGFOOD_OCM_LINKS (change.go:1018). Expected: a large, mechanically uniform change can be bound in one pass with every hunk still individually cited. Actual: the only route was rebuilding the branch as two commits with byte-identical final tree and binding each in a fresh clone (two bind and two seal commits). Workaround cost roughly one extra agent cycle. Options to decide: raise the bound with a measured limit, allow one row to cite a hunk range for the same path and evidence, or document staged binding as the supported route in docs/DOGFOOD.md.
title: dogfood-change: the 256-row citation plan cap forces large mechanical commits to be split and bound in stages

acceptanceCriteria: programWriter and leaseAudits exclude per store root, with a test showing two stores proceed concurrently and one store still serializes.
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/tasks/store/ passes; local wall time before/after is recorded in a build-log entry.
A CI run records the shard wall time for internal/tasks/store against the 700s target; a CI -parallel change is made only if that measurement supports it.
body: Follow-up from the store test-speed lane (PR beamfall/corvint#735, decision B two-stage bind). That change added t.Parallel() where safe; the package test took 821s locally and CI is estimated at about 1,100–1,250s, missing the 700s target. Two package-level locks serialize unrelated stores: `var programWriter sync.Mutex` (internal/tasks/store/program.go:18) and `var leaseAudits struct{...}` (internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:30). Tests on independent temporary repositories still contend on them. Proposal: key both by store root (for example a map of per-root mutexes), preserving the in-process exclusion each provides for a single store. Then measure whether CI should pass `-parallel` explicitly for this package. Unknown: whether any production caller relies on cross-store exclusion; confirm before changing.
title: Tasks store tests: process-wide programWriter and leaseAudits mutexes cap test parallelism in internal/tasks/store

acceptanceCriteria: A test or code citation establishes whether barrier and reconcile writes remove orphan staging slots.
The failure row states the observed behavior; if it changes requirement text, the change follows spec-driven acceptance.
body: docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md:5803 (killed writer between first staged artifact and head) says 'Barrier and reconcile writes do not recover: another writer must run first.' internal/tasks/store/barrier.go:72 calls redoPendingFor(repo, session, request.Operation), which suggests barrier does redo a pending receipt. Suspected stale text, not a confirmed bug: it is unverified whether redoPendingFor also removes orphan descriptor-less slots (the CAL-V0-019 recovery) or only redoes a linked receipt. Found while reviewing V1-0825 (CTS-V0-008, decision 0490, PR beamfall/corvint#734). Resolve by reading the barrier path and, if needed, a focused test with orphan slots.
title: Leases spec failure row may wrongly say barrier writes do not recover orphan staging slots

acceptanceCriteria: refresh refuses a log with a malformed line, a truncated final event, or a started package with no terminal outcome, with a test for each.

body: tools/ci-shard-costs/main.go: the advisory `check --advisory` path (report, line ~375) reads each log through observeStream, i.e. scan(..., strict=true), which refuses non-JSON lines, damaged events and packages that start without a terminal outcome. The table-writing refresh and plain check path (line ~96) reads through observe, i.e. scan(..., strict=false), so a truncated or damaged shard log can still feed the committed cost table (AFP-V0-040 lane, PR #730 merged). Expected: any input that updates .github/cishards costs is held to at least the advisory report's standard. Suspected defect from review; no corrupted table has been observed.
title: ci-shard-costs refresh/check scans shard logs non-strictly while the advisory report is strict

acceptanceCriteria: TestUPDV0004PartialArchiveCancellation passes 200 consecutive runs with go test -count=200 -run TestUPDV0004PartialArchiveCancellation ./internal/update, including under a concurrent full-package run.
The test still proves a partially read archive body is closed and the apply is refused on cancellation, without depending on a wall-clock deadline elapsing after the archive request starts.
body: Observed 2026-10-10 while working V1-0639. TestUPDV0004PartialArchiveCancellation (internal/update/update_test.go:509) fails intermittently with `archive body not partially read and closed: <nil>`: 4 of 40 runs at origin/main 64b5d174 and 3 of 40 on the V1-0639 branch (darwin/arm64, go1.27.1). Cause (inferred from the nil body): the test bounds apply with context.WithTimeout(500ms), and under load the installed-version probe plus release discovery consume that budget before the /archive request is made, so the interrupted body is never created. Expected: the test cancels only after the archive body has been partially read (e.g. cancel from interruptedBody.Read after the first chunk) so the assertion does not race the deadline. Actual: a timing-dependent failure that can fail CI for unrelated update changes.
title: TestUPDV0004PartialArchiveCancellation is flaky: 500ms deadline can expire before the archive request

acceptanceCriteria: The cleanup-confirmation contract change, if any, is recorded as an owner-accepted AHI-050 amendment.
A deterministic test reproduces the slow-reap timing and passes with the fix.

body: Observed in release-gates nightly run 38052349384 (2026-10-10, macos-15): host-adapter-test and cmd/corvint TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts returned corvint-process-cleanup-unconfirmed where timeout was expected, in a different OpenCode subtest each time. Not reproduced locally (2/2 passes at load ~94, RC3 lane F, PR beamfall/corvint#739). The failure first appears after the V1-0371 commits 7a4078b8, fd48aee7 and c05bf0a4, which narrowed cleanup confirmation to an ESRCH-only probe; the earlier check also accepted EPERM after the leader exited. Inference, unconfirmed: the hosted VM reaps zombies slowly, or the 100 ms reap timer fires before close. A fix (bounded re-probe, or EPERM-after-reap acceptance) changes the AHI-050 contract and needs an owner decision. Related to V1-0849 / V1-0762 but a new regression, not load flake. Blocks a green nightly for 1.0.0-rc.3 (decision 0491).
title: OpenCode host adapter reports corvint-process-cleanup-unconfirmed on hosted macos-15 since V1-0371

acceptanceCriteria: A PR touching a Go test file that fails `GOOS=windows go vet` fails PR CI before merge, shown by a test PR or a fixture run.

body: Two Windows cross-vet breaks reached main within two days: V1-1092 (prompt_fragments_test.go missing its darwin||linux tag) and b0b82698 from V1-0825 (`undefined: stubStageSleep` in a tagged test helper), both caught only by the nightly release-gates run and fixed in RC3 lane F (PR beamfall/corvint#739, 30bb2a06 and 6ab011ab). PR CI builds for Windows but does not vet test files. Proposal: run `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` (or `make cross-vet`) in a PR job, ideally only when Go files change per the affected plan. A .github change needs owner consent per decision 0390.
title: PR CI should type-check test files for Windows so cross-vet breaks stop reaching main

acceptanceCriteria: set-effects and claim emit a warning (not a refusal) naming the key and the suggested directory key when an exact PATH key is a directory in the tree, with a test.

body: Found in RC3 lane C (V1-1090, decision 0493). CAL-V0-021 makes a PATH key without a trailing / exact, so a key naming a directory covers nothing beneath it; submit later refuses OUT_OF_SCOPE (now with the cause named, CAL-V0-024 amendment). set-effects stores keys verbatim and claim reserves them without any warning. V1-1090's first acceptance point expects set-effects to agree with the submit rule. Proposal: a non-refusing warning at set-effects and claim when an exact key names a directory present in the base tree, suggesting the key with /.
title: set-effects and claim should warn when a PATH key without a trailing / names a directory in the tree

acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic test shows the Gemini hook reporting cleanup unconfirmed for a zombie group on the base and confirmed after the fix, or a retained run shows the hook is not affected.
Any contract change is recorded as an owner-accepted AHI amendment.
body: Found in lane H (V1-1116, PR beamfall/corvint#745). Proven locally on Darwin: a process group whose members are unreaped zombies answers kill(-pid, 0) with EPERM, and libuv runs timers before the poll phase that reaps the leader, so a single probe after a stalled termination turn sees EPERM and reports cleanup unconfirmed. #745 fixes the OpenCode adapter (bounded EPERM re-probe, proposed AHI-052). integrations/gemini-cli/hooks/corvint-hook.mjs (cleanup check near line 354-364 at main 3beedd98) still makes one `process.kill(-child.pid, 0)` probe and returns error?.code === "ESRCH" only. Suspected, not reproduced on hosted CI for Gemini. Any fix changes the AHI-050 contract for Gemini and needs owner acceptance like AHI-052.
title: Gemini CLI hook cleanup confirmation uses a single signal-0 probe that a zombie process group answers EPERM

acceptanceCriteria: The pre-commit pass refuses the same verify commands the post-commit pass refuses, with a test.

A verify file whose go test command used `-run '^(A|B)$'` passed the pre-commit dogfood-change pass and was refused only on the post-commit bind pass, after the CEM commit, forcing a rebind. Expected: the same validation on both passes, so the refusal arrives before any evidence commit. Exact refusal text is in lane H's transcript; reproduce with a verify file containing an anchored alternation -run pattern.
title: dogfood-change accepts a DOGFOOD_VERIFY_FILE `-run '^(...)$'` command pre-commit but refuses it only on the post-commit pass

acceptanceCriteria: A measured trace shows the git calls one enrolled Stop makes before and after, with duplicates removed.
Stop results are unchanged on the existing Stop tests.

body: Found in lane G (V1-1120, PR beamfall/corvint#746). One enrolled Stop evaluation makes about 12 git calls, repeating rev-parse, status and ls-tree: about 0.37 s CPU against about 1.5 s wall under load. acceptanceCriteria: An owning spec (index-snapshot-v0 or agent-harness-integration-v0) records the chosen automatic refresh mechanism as numbered requirements with non-goals, failure modes and rollback, accepted by the owner.

After a content commit or a main move in an enrolled repository, the next hook event after the refresh completes reports a fresh snapshot with no manual `corvint index --if-stale`; a regression test covers commit-then-event.
Concurrent triggers start at most one refresh per tree; a failed or killed refresh leaves no partial snapshot and the hook still fails open with the stale code and the manual argv.
The hook event itself stays within its declared work bound; the refresh runs outside it and exits when done (no permanent daemon).
body: Observed 2026-10-10 on the Corvint primary checkout (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 local build from origin/main 3beedd98; corvint-tasks build 407; Claude Code adapter). Reproduction: after main moves (a merge or fetch-and-checkout) or after any content commit, every Claude Code hook event (UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, PreCompact) reports `Corvint FALLBACK degraded: corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale` and tells the user to 'Refresh the snapshot once, outside the hook: corvint --root <repo> index --if-stale'. The user had to paste the notice and the agent had to run the command by hand; it built the snapshot for tree bd9760a0 in about 3 s and evicted one old snapshot. Owner feedback: 'this should be automatic.' V1-0286 (COMPLETED) fixed the cause naming and the remediation argv (IDX-SNAP-V0-012, decision 0049 keeps the hook from building synchronously inside its 1.5 s work bound) but left the refresh manual. Expected: when the hook observes a stale snapshot it (or an installed host lifecycle step) triggers a bounded, detached, single-flight `index --if-stale` outside the hook deadline, so the next event finds a fresh snapshot without user action. Candidate shapes, to be decided spec-first: (a) the hook spawns a detached, lock-guarded `index --if-stale` child and still fails open for the current event; (b) an opt-in git post-commit/post-merge/post-checkout hook installed by `corvint init`/adopt; (c) SessionStart triggers the refresh in the background. Constraints: product invariant 4 (read commands do not mutate repository or trace state) and invariant 7 (no permanent daemon) apply; the snapshot is derived state under .corvint, so the spec must state whether a hook-triggered refresh is admitted and bound its CPU, concurrency (one refresh per tree), disk eviction and load behaviour (HLQ envelope from V1-1120).
title: hooks: refresh a stale index snapshot automatically instead of asking the user to run index --if-stale

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#772, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: V1-1129 (#769, same pool acquire error mapping).

## Problem
`corvint-tasks pool acquire` refuses with `LOCK_TIMEOUT` ("preparation acquisition exceeded 30s") when several agents mutate the queue at once, even when a pool member is FREE. Unlike `release` (which accepts `--lock-wait SECONDS`, 1..300), `pool acquire` has no `--lock-wait` flag, so callers cannot ask it to wait for preparation admission.

## Observed
With ~7 concurrent agent sessions on one queue, 4 of 26 `pool acquire` calls in a 4-hour window returned `ERROR ["LOCK_TIMEOUT"]` (phase=registry or phase=queue). In one case a member was FREE the whole time; the session backed off for minutes before retrying, leaving the lane idle.

## Expected
`pool acquire` (and ideally every mutating command that goes through preparation admission: claim, renew, submit, pool confirm-safe, pool release) accepts `--lock-wait SECONDS` with the same semantics as `release`, and `--help` lists it.

## Workaround
Callers retry the same request id after a short sleep on `LOCK_TIMEOUT` (idempotent).
title: pool acquire has no --lock-wait; LOCK_TIMEOUT under concurrent agents while a member is FREE (GitHub #772)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#773, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: V1-0968, V1-1077 (appmap).

## Problem
`flows appmap build` accepts exactly one router dialect (`ui-router-states/0`). Applications that mix an AngularJS shell with server-rendered pages (Rails-style `routes.rb`) and component-router islands (React Router `createBrowserRouter`/`<Route>` trees) get no screens for those surfaces, so the screen graph, test join, scenario planner and consolidation planner all read those screens as missing (not UNKNOWN), which is not fail-closed for the whole application.

## Proposal
Add two dialects with the same literal-only, fail-closed rules as AMAP-V0-002:
- `rails-routes/0`: `get/post/resources/resource/namespace/scope/member/collection/root/mount` with literal arguments; named route helpers become state names; `constraints`, `defaults` and lambdas read UNKNOWN; `draw` partial files followed one level.
- `react-router/0`: object-form route arrays and JSX `<Route path element>` trees with literal `path`, nested via `children`/JSX nesting; `lazy`, computed paths and spreads read UNKNOWN.
Also a manifest-level "app coverage" summary: router files matched by a declared glob but not listed in `routers` (today a manifest silently caps at 64 routers).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fixtures per dialect: nested resources, namespace + scope, shallow routes, JSX and object routers, index routes, splats.
- Every non-literal construct produces a named UNKNOWN reason; no screen is guessed.
- A route file present under a declared glob but absent from `routers` is reported as `router-not-declared`.
- Template collision keys are shared across dialects so URL lookup works on mixed apps.
title: appmap: router dialects for server routes and component routers (beyond ui-router-states/0) (GitHub #773)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#774, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
RVN-V0 binds a passing Playwright receipt to *steps* of one flow. Suites still re-prove the same screen-to-screen transition (login -> dashboard -> section -> sub-screen) in dozens of tests because nothing records that an edge is already proven at a revision, and nothing lets a test declare "I depend on edge E being proven" and enter by deep link instead.

## Proposal
`corvint flows appmap edges --map FILE [--receipt FILE]... [--revision REV]` emitting `application-edge-ledger/0`:
- Edge identity = (from screen, to screen, trigger kind: goto | click selector | redirect | form submit) keyed by stable element IDs.
- Each edge row: PROVEN@REV (with the receipt/test key and the step that crossed it), UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD (an anchor on the edge's lineage changed), CONTRADICTED, or UNPROVEN.
- A `--require EDGE_ID` mode for tests: a test may declare `proves:` and `assumes:` edge lists (annotation or sidecar); the ledger reports assumed edges that are not PROVEN at the evaluated revision, so a suite can fail closed.
- Coverage summary: proven/total edges per app and the cheapest test (fewest steps) that proves each edge.

## Acceptance criteria
- Deterministic ledger digest per revision; capped projection with omitted counts.
- An edge proven by one receipt is reported once with every other test that also crosses it listed as `redundant-crossers` (count + keys).
- Changing a template or selector anchored on an edge flips it to UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD.
- `assumes:` an UNPROVEN or stale edge exits 1 with the edge list; no browser is launched.
title: appmap: navigation-edge coverage ledger with proven-once receipts (GitHub #774)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#775, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: V1-0249, V1-0255 (flows run evidence).

## Problem
Edges in the application map come only from static evidence (flow-step and test-sequence). Real navigation (redirects, guards, modals that change URL, hash routing) is only visible at runtime. Playwright already writes traces and URL events, but no producer turns them into map-keyed evidence.

## Proposal
`corvint flows appmap observe --map FILE --trace FILE|DIR [--revision REV]` reading Playwright trace zips (or a reporter JSON with `page.on('framenavigated')` events) and emitting `application-navigation-observation/0`: ordered screen visits (URL resolved through the map's template lookup, hash prefix aware), observed edges with the triggering action (from trace action metadata and locator), redirects, and URLs that match no screen (`unmapped-url`). Output is consumable by the edge ledger and by `--receipt` verification.

## Acceptance criteria
- Secret-shaped query values and form input values are redacted before output.
- A URL matching several screens reads UNKNOWN with candidates; zero reads `unmapped-url`.
- Observed edges never alter static nodes; they are overlay facts with the trace digest and app revision.
- Fixture with a guard redirect, a hash-routed app and a modal route.
title: flows: record Playwright traces into screen visits and observed edges (GitHub #775)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#776, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
`corvint-playwright-minimize` minimises suite-interaction *failures* (predecessor sets that break a test); it does not find redundant steps. Large E2E suites commonly repeat the same UI navigation prefix (log in through the form, open menu, click section, click tab) before the step under test, multiplying run time and flake surface even when a deep link or stored session would reach the same state.

## Proposal
`corvint test-plan prefixes --map FILE [--ledger FILE] [--tests FILE]...` (read-only): for each spec, derive the ordered screen/edge sequence from the map's test-sequence edges, page-object calls and observed traces; compute shared prefixes across specs; flag each test whose prefix (a) only crosses edges already PROVEN elsewhere and (b) ends on a screen with a FRESH deep-linkable template, with a suggested replacement (`goto(template with params)` or a session fixture), and the estimated saved steps.

## Acceptance criteria
- Output lists `{test, prefix_edges, proven_by, entry_template, saved_steps}`; tests with UNKNOWN joins abstain with reason.
- A prefix is never flagged if any edge in it is the test's own assertion target or carries a state change (`changes` non-empty / write effect class).
- `--check` mode exits 1 when a new test introduces a flagged prefix (lint gate).
title: Playwright prefix-dedupe lint: detect tests that replay a proven navigation prefix (GitHub #776)

GitHub beamfall/corvint#777, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: V1-1023 (test consolidation planner, GitHub #681).

## Problem
Follow-up to #681 (consolidation planner).
`test-plan consolidate` groups *variations* by context (spec, app, setup, screen, user, org) but needs a hand-built `test-consolidation-input/0`. Teams want the inverse question answered from the existing suite: "which assertions across all tests run against the same screen in the same data state, so they can be checked once in one test?" Building that input by hand is the blocker; REUSED is unreachable from real provider documents in V0.

## Proposal
1. `corvint test-plan extract --map FILE --tests-root DIR` producing a draft `test-consolidation-input/0` from specs: each `expect(...)` becomes an assertion anchored to the screen where it runs (from the map join and preceding navigation), its setup/scenario import, acting user fixture, and read-only vs mutating classification of preceding actions; anything unclassifiable is a missing anchor (abstains).
2. A `--group-by page-state` view in `consolidate` that prints, per (screen, setup, user, prior-changes digest), the assertions from different tests that could share one visit, with the reuse blockers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Extract is deterministic and anchors every assertion; non-literal locators read unknown, not dropped.
- Assertions after a mutating action are keyed by the post-change state, never merged with pre-change ones.
- `check` on a committed plan detects drift when a spec adds or moves an assertion.
title: test-plan: page-state assertion grouping (one-shot tests per screen state) (GitHub #777)

GitHub beamfall/corvint#778, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
A screen graph is only useful for "enter directly" if each screen's template actually loads by URL for the declared role and data state. Abstract states, required resolves, parent-only params and guard redirects mean a template is often not a valid entry. Teams keep hand-maintained "URL that loads" lists that drift.

## Proposal
- Static: `flows appmap entries --map FILE` classifying each screen `deep-linkable | requires-parent-params | abstract | guarded(permission/flag) | UNKNOWN`, with the minimal parameter set and the shortest PROVEN edge path from an entry screen.
- Runtime (opt-in, trusted local app, read effect only): visit each candidate entry with a declared fixture/session and record `loads | redirected(to screen) | error`, emitting receipts consumable by the edge ledger.

## Acceptance criteria
- Runtime mode refuses any screen whose entry is not effect class `read`.
- Results are revision-bound; a template or guard change flips the result to UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD.
- Projection lists per screen: entry URL template, required params, guard, last verified revision.
title: appmap: deep-link validator (entry paths per screen) (GitHub #778)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#779, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
`corvint impact`/`affected` select tests through imports; `flows impact` maps changes to declared flow intents. Neither answers "which screens and navigation edges does this change touch?" for template, controller, directive or route-file changes, so navigation proofs cannot be invalidated precisely and UI test selection falls back to all-or-nothing.

## Proposal
`corvint flows appmap impact --map FILE --base SHA [--ledger FILE]` emitting `application-map-impact/0`: changed paths -> anchored elements (screens via router/lineage anchors, steps/selectors via their anchors, templates/components via the contextindex import graph from the screen's declared component/template) -> affected edges -> tests that cross them (from join, test-sequence edges and receipts). Unknown hops are listed; any UNKNOWN reachable from a changed path forces a `full-suite-required` verdict for that app (fail closed).

## Acceptance criteria
- Router-file change invalidates the screen and all descendants (lineage).
- Template/component change reaches screens through declared component bindings; unbound templates read UNKNOWN.
- Output joins with the edge ledger: edges flipped from PROVEN to UNVERIFIED_AT_HEAD are listed with their cheapest re-proving test.
title: impact: source change -> affected screens and edges -> tests (GitHub #779)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#781, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: V1-0254, V1-0191 (corvint-mcp).

## Problem
Each MCP server is bound to a single `--root` at startup. Programs that run many agents in linked worktrees (one per task or lane), each at a different revision, end up sharing a server pointed at the main checkout. Every `impact`, `query` or `status` answer then describes the wrong revision, often a dirty one (`worktreeState: MIXED`), and agents can't tell.

## Proposal
- Accept an optional `root` (a linked worktree of the same repository) or `snapshot`/`revision` argument per tool call, validated against the server's repository identity.
- Or support a root-discovery mode that resolves the caller's cwd/worktree per call.
- Echo the resolved root, commit, tree and `worktreeState` in every response.

## Acceptance criteria
- Two calls that name different linked worktrees return answers bound to their own commit/tree.
- A root outside the repository identity is refused with a typed error.
- When no per-call root is given, the response flags whether the bound root differs from the caller's worktree, if that is known.
title: corvint-mcp: serve a per-call worktree root or snapshot instead of one root bound at startup (GitHub #781)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#782, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
`test_validity` in discover mode returns `no-retained-evidence` / `source: none` when no provider run has produced receipts. Adopters call it per spec for weeks and get hundreds of identical abstentions. Nothing tells them that a provider (such as the JS test provider) must wrap their normal runs, or where it expects receipts.

## Proposal
When discover mode finds no evidence, the abstention includes:
- the producer command(s) that would create it;
- the expected evidence path;
- whether a qualification for that provider exists on this host;
- the age of the newest receipt for the repository, if any.

## Acceptance criteria
- An abstention with `source: none` always names at least one producer and one expected path.
- If receipts exist but for another revision, the reason is `stale-evidence` with the receipt revision, not `no-retained-evidence`.
title: test-validity: say which producer is missing when discover mode abstains with no-retained-evidence (GitHub #782)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#783, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
On a root with `worktreeState: MIXED`, `impact` answers from an older committed tree plus whatever is dirty. When the paths an agent asks about are not among the dirty paths, the answer looks authoritative but describes a revision the agent isn't working on. Today only `freshness.state: mixed-worktree` hints at this, and callers ignore it.

## Proposal
- Add a top-level `warning` (or an abstention under a strict profile) when MIXED and the requested paths are not a subset of the dirty set, naming the commit the answer is bound to.
- Offer a `--require-clean` / `strict` profile that abstains on MIXED.

## Acceptance criteria
- A MIXED root with clean requested paths returns a warning that names the bound commit and the dirty count.
- The strict profile returns an abstention, not a result.
title: impact/affected: warn or abstain when the worktree is MIXED and the queried paths differ from the dirty set (GitHub #783)

GitHub beamfall/corvint#784, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. 

## Problem
Adopters file issues, add workarounds or holds tagged with the issue number, and later upgrade. When the fix lands, nothing prompts them to remove the workaround, so bypasses and holds outlive the fix by days or weeks.

## Proposal
`corvint changes --from <build-sha> --to <build-sha> [--refs-file FILE]`:
- list the issues and PRs closed between two builds, with a one-line summary and any new flags or commands;
- given a file or glob of adopter text (configs, prompts, scripts), report every `#NNN` reference whose issue is now closed in the target build: "workaround may be removable".

## Acceptance criteria
- Deterministic output from build metadata, with no network access when the source checkout is present.
- References to closed issues are listed with file:line and the closing PR.
title: Upgrade adoption checklist: issues closed between two installed builds, keyed to adopter workarounds (GitHub #784)

GitHub beamfall/corvint#785, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: V1-0869 (frontier-authority-unavailable emitted on every event), V1-0243.

## Problem
Session hooks report `degradations: frontier-authority-unavailable` on every session in repositories that never produce verified CEM/OCM artifacts. Adopters can't tell whether it is a fault, a misconfiguration or expected, so it is either ignored or chased.

## Proposal
- Document what produces frontier authority, what is lost without it, and the minimum steps to enable it.
- Have the degradation carry a short `reason` (e.g. `no-verified-cem`) and a docs link.
- Optionally allow an adopter to acknowledge it as expected so hooks stop repeating it.

## Acceptance criteria
- The degradation payload includes a machine-readable reason.
- The docs page lists its causes and remedies.
title: Document `frontier-authority-unavailable` for adopters who don't produce CEM/OCM artifacts (GitHub #785)

GitHub beamfall/corvint#786, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: GitHub #705, #685 (appmap di_constants re-export reading); V1-1131 (#773 router dialects).

## Problem
On an adopter AngularJS/Angular hybrid app, `di_constants` scoped to the registering file still leaves the table unresolved. The result is 153 states `non-literal-name` and only 10 of 23 screens resolved, with one `di-constant` unknown `not-read-whole`. The shape:

```ts
// core-downgrade.module.ts (in di_constants scope)
import { RoutesConstants } from './routes'          // directory import -> routes/index.ts
...
.constant('StateConstants', RoutesConstants)

// routes/index.ts
export * from './routes.constants'

// routes/routes.constants.ts
export enum RoutesConstants { CLUB = 'app.club', TEESHEETS = 'app.club.teesheets', ... }  // every member a literal string
```

The #705 fix reads one level of `export ... from` behind the registering file's import, but apparently not when:
- the import specifier is a directory that resolves to `index.ts`; or
- the re-export is a star export (`export * from`) rather than a named `export { X } from`.

The same shape appears in a second app in the same repository (`not-read-whole`, 65 `non-literal-name`).

## Proposal
- Resolve directory import specifiers to `index.{ts,js}` (TypeScript module resolution), within the same bounds.
- Follow `export * from` one level when exactly one star-exported module declares the imported name. Ambiguity (several star exports declaring it) reads UNKNOWN with the candidate paths.
- Make the `not-read-whole` unknown say which hop failed (directory index, star export, non-literal member, other).

## Acceptance criteria
- A fixture with exactly the shape above resolves every state name and parent through the enum.
- A fixture with two star exports declaring the same name reads UNKNOWN `ambiguous-reexport` with both paths.
- Existing #685/#705 fixtures compile to the same bytes.
title: appmap: injected constant table behind a directory import with `export *` reads `not-read-whole` (follow-up to #705) (GitHub #786)

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#787, filed by the owner 2026-10-11. Related: application-map-manifest/0; V1-1138 (#780 adopter qualification).

## Problem
`application-map-manifest/0` requires the `specs`, `page_objects`, `workflows` and `scenarios` directories to lie under `tests.root`, and `tests.root: "."` is refused (`appmap-invalid-manifest: tests.root must be a repository-relative directory`). A common Playwright layout keeps specs in `tests/` and page objects, workflows and data builders in `lib/`. Both are top-level siblings in a dedicated test repository, so no single subdirectory contains them all. Adopters must either leave specs out of the join (no screen→spec links) or restructure their repository.

## Proposal
Accept `"."` as `tests.root` (the whole aliased test repository, or the whole root when no alias is given), keeping every other bound and the dirty-root refusal scoped to the declared directories, not the whole tree.

## Acceptance criteria
- `tests.root: "."` with `specs: ["tests/e2e"]` and `page_objects: ["lib/pages"]` compiles and joins specs to page objects.
- Dirty-root detection for an aliased test repo considers only the declared directories (and the manifest), so unrelated untracked files don't refuse the build.
- Existing manifests compile to the same bytes.
title: appmap: allow `tests.root` to be the repository root (specs and page objects in sibling top-level directories) (GitHub #787)

body:
Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#792.

## Problem
The obligation ledger (TOL-V0-003) only accepts `<PREFIX>-<n>` ids, so adopters with existing id schemes (`AREA-12-V03`, `M001`, `ABC-12.V4`, `V7`) cannot use the ledger, native preflight (TOL-V0-025..027), run-batch/qualify or expected-fail crediting without renumbering.

## Chosen design (issue option 2)
Keep the native numeric `id` and the wire shape. Add an optional `alias` per obligation (1..64 bytes, `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*`). Refuse duplicate aliases and aliases colliding with a native id, with named refusal codes. Preflight and witness/qualify/expected-fail crediting accept the native id or the alias as a whole token; everything recorded stays keyed to the native id. Native id grammar unchanged.
title: obligations: optional adopter alias per obligation, accepted by preflight, witness, qualify and expected-fail (GH #792)

acceptanceCriteria: A worker whose only non-ignored children are sleeping with no CPU-time advance since the previous tick is stopped with reason IDLE after idleSeconds; a child that is runnable or whose CPU time advanced still marks the worker busy; each with a focused regression test (run with -race).
The owning spec carries numbered requirements for the busy-child rule, marked proposed pending owner acceptance.
body:
Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#793. Refs #793.

Observed: `corvint-tasks dispatch` never stops a worker for `idleSeconds` when the agent host keeps long-lived helper processes (agent server child, MCP servers) in the worker's process tree. `busyChild` treats any non-leader member whose `comm` is not in `idleIgnore` as busy regardless of activity, so `LastActive` is refreshed every tick and the IDLE branch is unreachable. 0 IDLE kills over ~670 kills with idleSeconds 900; a hung worker (log silent 25+ min, all members sleeping <0.5% CPU) ran to wallSeconds.

Expected: a worker whose log, activity paths and child processes show no progress for `idleSeconds` is stopped with reason IDLE. A child counts as busy only when it is runnable or its CPU time advanced since the last tick, not merely because it exists.

Workaround: list helper command names in `idleIgnore`.
title: dispatch idleSeconds never fires when workers keep long-lived helper processes (GH #793)

Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#800.

body: Confirmed in review of 469344d29396d7003f10bd7796c950feeca8304c (V1-1164), source unchanged at d6cab15d78a1f7359fa90307954746e86fda168d. internal/appmap/effects.go:576-577 accepts a function keyword without proving the complete argument is a function. Reproduction: define reset = () => localStorage.setItem('x','1') and check = reset before the test; between page-object constructions use test.step('reset', function() {} && reset), expect.poll(function() {} && check).toBe(1), expect(function() {} && check).toPass(), or expect(function() {} && reset).toThrow(). Temporary Go-overlay fixture probes using fixtureRepo/effectSpec/build verified two sequence edges, then observed navigation-only for all four despite the argument evaluating to reset/check. Expected unknown with effect_call callback. Existing TestANLV0035StepEffects passes and covers only direct names and pure inline callbacks, not these compound arguments. Direct expect(reset).toThrow()/toThrowError() probes yield unknown callback. Tested with go1.27.2 (repository pinned go1.27.1 not present); Core 1.0.0-rc.3 build 407 / Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.407. Review probes used scratch overlays, no source edits.
title: appmap: inlineCallback admits function expressions selecting named callbacks

acceptanceCriteria: TestLocalOutcomeTracePathLimitKeepsAdmissionReason passes with TMPDIR under a symlinked ancestor (macOS /var/folders, or a /tmp-based TMPDIR).
go test ./internal/dogfoodflow passes with TMPDIR=/tmp/<dir> on macOS.
The macOS nightly job no longer fails on this test.
body: Nightly macOS failed TestLocalOutcomeTracePathLimitKeepsAdmissionReason (internal/dogfoodflow/change_test.go). The test used t.TempDir() directly as the evidence root. recordWithClosedStages publishes the aggregate through aggregateReadFile, which starts with dogfoodoperation.CheckParents and refuses any symlinked ancestor; macOS TMPDIR (/var -> /private/var) has one, so localOutcome returned aggregate-publication-failed instead of the admission reason. Reproduce: TMPDIR=/tmp/x go test -run TestLocalOutcomeTracePathLimitKeepsAdmissionReason ./internal/dogfoodflow (macOS). Expected: pass; actual: aggregate-publication-failed. Product behavior is correct (refusing symlinked ancestors is intended); the test fixture is wrong. Fix: resolve the temp root with filepath.EvalSymlinks, as aggregate_worker_test.go already does.
title: Nightly macOS: dogfoodflow trace-path-limit test fails under symlinked TMPDIR

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint-js-test-provider e2e --help` (and the provider docs) state that results Playwright reports for dependency (setup) projects bind only when each setup file is also passed with `--test-file`, and that `--test-arg` and `--test-file` are independent.
The `test-file-unbound` / `report-identity-unknown` refusal names the unbound anchor file(s) in its detail.

Either an opt-in that binds dependency-project files Playwright reports is specified and tested, or the owner records the explicit --test-file requirement as the accepted contract; a regression test covers a setup-project run.
GitHub issue #807 is closed by the delivering PR.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#807 (opened 2026-10-11 by the owner while qualifying an external Playwright run with `corvint-js-test-provider e2e`).

Expected: a Playwright run whose config uses project dependencies (setup projects) binds every reported result, or the refusal says which file is unbound and the help documents the rule.
Actual: results for the setup files are refused as `report-identity-unknown` / `test-file-unbound` unless each setup file is also passed via `--test-file`, even though every result passed. `--test-arg` (what Playwright runs) and `--test-file` (what identity binds) are independent, so passing only the target spec to both is not enough. The requirement is undocumented and the refusal does not name the anchor file.

Version: Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 407). Related: V1-1196 (GH #794, provider help).
title: js-test-provider e2e: setup-project results refused as test-file-unbound unless each setup file is passed via --test-file (GH #807)

body:
Found while merging origin/main 01f95dbe4 (#804, DCW-V0-042 admitSealedCEMs) into the V1-0632 S1-S3 batch (beamfall/corvint#808, merge 92db2b33d).

acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce or bound the Linux race in which groupreap reads /proc/<pid>/status for a member of the owned group and finds no Threads line, so quiescence is reported unproved after a clean exit.
Treat a member that exits or becomes a zombie during the /proc quiet proof as quiescent or re-probe it, without accepting real residue; keep refusal when residue exists.
TestRunProcessReapsDescendantBeforeDelayedSideEffect passes repeatedly on Linux CI (for example -count=50) with focused procgroup tests and independent review.
body: Suspected flaky test, observed once in CI on beamfall/corvint#808 (run 38178767381, job 114586863420, go-product-shard (3), ubuntu, go1.27.2, head a8c05c4f45a8971665ee97d2eada7c739a0e0d14). internal/procgroup was not changed by that PR. Actual: TestRunProcessReapsDescendantBeforeDelayedSideEffect (process_test.go:129) failed after 1.01s with Err process-cleanup-failed: prove owned process group quiescence: owned process group quiescence unproved: groupreap: /proc quiet proof unavailable: no thread count for 66079; ExitStatus 0, WaitCompleted true, PipesDrained true, DescendantCleanupStatus owned-process-group. Expected: a descendant that has already exited (or is exiting) is proved quiescent, or the probe retries, so the test passes. Hypothesis (inference): the /proc/<pid>/status read races with the process exiting, so the Threads field is missing. Not reproduced locally (Darwin host has no /proc). Distinct from V1-1055 (signal-0 probe after pgid reuse).
title: procgroup /proc quiet proof fails with no thread count for an exiting group member (CI flake)

acceptanceCriteria: WriteStable validates bundle map, path/digest/role closure and bounds before mutation; a traversal or mutated path cannot write outside the created bundle, and failure leaves no artifacts in the parent.

Stable bundle file reads refuse FIFO substitutions without blocking and retain regular-file/symlink identity checks before and after reads; run a reached-path substitution control with owned-process retirement.
Directory enumeration uses bounded incremental reads and refuses excessive entries before allocating the full directory.
Add stable write failure cleanup and complete refusal-result/caller-root argv tests; keep CEM-V1-060..064 traceability claims bound to their actual assertions.
body: Observed reviewing V1-0632 S5b at b08dce919185fc49b79038f93ac82c2595961fb4, range a8c05c4f45a8971665ee97d2eada7c739a0e0d14..HEAD, host go1.27.2 darwin/arm64, installed Core 1.0.0-rc.3 build 407 / Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.407. (1) stable_bundle.go:148 trusts mutable StableArtifact.Path: CollectStable a valid bundle, set first path to ../../leaked and append that artifact again. WriteStable returns publish-failed on the duplicate, removes bundle, but leaves 154 artifact bytes in parent/leaked. os.Root confines to parent, not the newly created bundle. (2) stable_bundle.go:305 opens with blocking root.Open after Lstat. Disposable overlay probe repeatedly swaps a regular file and FIFO; 2000 regular-file reads complete normally, raced helper prints READ_LOOP_ENTERED then blocks until the three-second watchdog kills it. SameFile is after the blocking open. (3) stable_bundle.go:237 uses fs.WalkDir; Go 1.27.2 rootFS.ReadDir invokes f.ReadDir(-1), allocating the whole directory before callback maxStableEntries. A huge flat directory defeats the intended resource bound. Probe source retained in /private/tmp/cem-s5b-review.Ipn6p3/probe_test.go and overlay.json. Existing receiptbundle/CLI unit packages and selected cmd/corvint export tests pass. Expected: validated exact stable closure, writes only under the new bundle, complete rollback, bounded/nonblocking admission, test refusal result equality and caller-root cases. Actual: the above two runtime probes and directory-walk source demonstrate gaps. No source repairs made.
title: Stable bundle APIs permit path escape, blocking FIFO substitution and unbounded directory admission

acceptanceCriteria: On macOS with multiple installations sharing com.google.chrome.for.testing, getApp called with one exact .app path returns a binding for that application or a bounded actionable error within the caller timeout.
The timeout_ms supplied by the caller bounds getApp wall time; a 20000 ms request cannot block for several minutes.
Display-name and bundle-identifier ambiguity remains distinct from binding failure and returns the candidate paths promptly.
A regression test covers an exact-path app launch/bind with duplicate bundle identifiers and verifies that failed binding does not leave the launched application running.
body: Confirmed unified-computer-use macOS binding defect observed 2026-10-11 while verifying a native HTML select. Reproduction A: cua.getApp("Google Chrome for Testing") against a headed Playwright browser stalled for about 443 seconds and was user-interrupted; no keyboard input was sent. A later bundle-identifier lookup correctly returned immediate ambiguity with three installed app paths, which is separate expected behavior. Reproduction B: with no fixture server running, cua.getApp called with the exact Playwright 1.60.0 app path /Users/russelllewis/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1223/chrome-mac-arm64/Google Chrome for Testing.app and timeout_ms=20000 returned Computer Use server error -10005 timeoutReached after about 486 seconds; the binding variable remained undefined. The exact app process was launched near the end of the wait and had to be retired explicitly. Environment: macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, Chrome for Testing 148.0.7778.96. Expected: exact path selects one installation, returns a native App binding promptly, honors timeout_ms, and cleans up a launch when binding fails. Actual: multi-minute unbounded stall and orphaned launched app. This is a tooling defect, not evidence about Beamfall product behavior or native-select Escape handling.
title: macOS computer use exact-path getApp stalls and ignores timeout

body: Confirmed review defects in V1-0632 S5c at aca36474e5acd923dcbdfcec21b5776bacce9e06, range a8c05c4f45a8971665ee97d2eada7c739a0e0d14..HEAD. Runtime go1.27.2 darwin; installed Core 1.0.0-rc.3 build 407, Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.407. Disposable Go overlay tests used the existing public sealed positive fixture and were removed afterward. 1) internal/console/chain.go:331 selects strict parsing after permissive encoding/json decoding: injecting an additional "Spec":"cem/0.3" after "spec":"cem/1.0" leaves wire.DeclaresStable=true and ParseStable rejects unknown member, but decodeSealed admits profile=cem/0.3 with two hunks. 2) internal/witnesscollapse/stable.go:101 DeepEqual rejects an emitted report after Canonical and json.Unmarshal because verification References criterionBindings changes from []wire.StableCriterion to []interface{} (and untyped hunk values change representation); reproduction returned report-mismatch with no semantic edits. 3) internal/doccorpus/cem_stable.go:36-37 returns nil receipt for {"spec":"cem/0.3"}; the error is corpus-stable-refused but REFUSED/no-claims/full-verifier-result envelope required by CEM-V1-076 is absent. acceptanceCriteria: Redact secret-shaped URL payloads and credentials before saving events and cover selector-embedded inputs; preserve safe route identity and typed-value exclusion.

Bound complete serialized documents to the loader's 4 MiB input limit and abstain visibly on overflow; support or explicitly bound directory ingestion above 64 tests.

body: Review of 645304a2fb71065f9061d8d8d866600d703e84c6..3d68f7e8a2b3ed0fdba61207b18c361187d3ede6. Installed Core 1.0.0-rc.3 build407; Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build407. Qualified dependency inspected: Playwright 1.61.1. Confirmed: (1) navigation-events.cjs:44,86 persists raw URL userinfo and token query values; a read-only in-memory recorder probe captured both, violating the review's no-secrets-recorded invariant even though observe later redacts them. (2) navigation_events_test.go:99 folds redirect chains before comparing; :110 explicitly expects two producer visits vs one trace visit. Raw same-run visits/edges do not meet issue #814 acceptance; ANL-V0-042 proposes a weaker normalized comparison. (3) navigation-events.cjs:52 bounds only event count and individual URL length; a recorder probe with 1100 URLs below 4096 bytes produced 4452878 serialized bytes, exceeding observe.go:155-157's 4194304-byte limit. (4) every test goes into one outputDir; observe.go:146 rejects more than 64 JSON files, including the documented 80-test overhead shape. Static correctness gaps, not requalified live: (5) files from filtered/skipped tests and attempts with no context persist across runs; no run cleanup or metadata distinguishes them. (6) writing occurs only through runBeforeCloseBrowserContext; Playwright 1.61.1 Browser.close does not invoke it, and subsequent context.close returns for an already closed context, leaving otherwise passing tests without an events file. Node tests: 5/5 passed outside read-only sandbox; synthetic golden byte identity passed, live JSON hash prefixes/suffixes match build log. Go/live browser reruns NOT_RUN. Corvint impact rejected range binary content; affected plan retains UNKNOWN language/ownership frontier. No source repairs in review.
title: Issue #814 review: navigation-events secret persistence, trace parity and loader limits

acceptanceCriteria: Regex literals after control-condition parentheses cannot generate phantom legacy cases; every real it appears once.
Unsupported or continued assertions, including template-substitution assertions and withContext chains, are extracted or retained as case-bound unknowns.
Supported JavaScript literal escapes decode correctly or remain explicit unknowns; they never silently change expected values.
Precondition fixture order preserves hook/case execution order; a reordered setup cannot receive parity-candidate against the old order.
Nested case setup/visit/intercept calls and noninline or conditional hooks are discovered or cause case-bound uncertainty; no empty/invented precondition set establishes parity-candidate.
Precondition canonical text hashes to its emitted SHA256 even above 240 bytes; visited URLs remain available to crosswalk scoring.
Malformed registries and missing/stale mapping-review or target-assertion evidence refuse or remain unresolved, never reviewed parity candidates.
Keep old command output bytes and BehaviorLegacyCase wire shape unchanged; add adversarial regressions and retain focused tests plus independent review.
body:
Read-only review for beamfall/corvint#811 at HEAD a1a09bbcd04d64a02574d217e49117e9f45973b0, base 645304a2fb71065f9061d8d8d866600d703e84c6. Confirmed by a CLI compiled from this HEAD using go1.27.2. Installed discovery tool: Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 407; Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.407. Review fixture-result SHA256: 71268a3c6383d18433367b0375808ca24cc4660c4b9673c2a0820b9fb7b4c036.

P2 reproductions:
1. behavior_legacy_lex.go:137 returns false for a regex after a control condition. describe('s',()=>{ if (ready) /it('phantom', () => {})/.test(value); it('real',()=>expect(1).toBe(1)); }); emits phantom and real.
2. behavior_legacy_lex.go:167 legacyEscape maps '\x41' to x41 and '\b' to b without unknown.
3. behavior_legacy_discovery.go:733 stops expect chaining at first call: expect(x).withContext('context').toBe(1) emits withContext|x|context and silently drops toBe. expect(x).to.be.a('number').and.equal(1) drops equal(1).
4. behavior_legacy_lex.go:208 discards substitution code: const value = `${expect(x).toBe(1)}`; expect(y).toBe(2); emits only y and no unknown. Standalone Cypress .and assertions are also omitted without unknown.
5. behavior_legacy_discovery.go:560 sorts fixtures: reversing cy.visit('/before');cy.task('seed','A') produces identical lists and parity-candidate against copied old target.
6. behavior_legacy_discovery.go:617 and 625 skip nested known case precommands: cy.then(()=>{cy.task('seed','A');cy.visit('/cart');});expect(1).toBe(1); gives fixtures=[]/unknown=[] and parity-candidate. Noninline beforeEach(seedHelper) at 455-457 also vanishes without case uncertainty.
7. behavior_legacy_discovery.go:466 still adds conditional-hook fixtures after a file-level hook-in-dynamic-scope unknown; if(flag){beforeEach(()=>cy.task('seed','A'));} then a matching case receives parity-candidate with no case unknown.
8. behavior_legacy_discovery.go:637 truncates precondition Text at 240 bytes while SHA256 binds full text: a literal 300-character URL gives SHA256 != Digest(Text) and loses visited-URL matching.
9. behavior_legacy_crosswalk.go:53 accepts {} and minimal schema-zero tests with missing mapping review/annotation. A copied tuple yields parity-candidate; default fixture tests themselves use this missing evidence.

DCP-V1-060..069 witnesses cover small happy-path fixtures but miss the above. Focused internal doccorpus TestLegacy|TestBehavior|TestAFUV1BehaviorProviderV1BytesUnchanged passed (146.423s); CLI Docs|Corpus|Help verification pending at filing. Source model/compiler/encoding unchanged relative to base. Native task created for confirmed bugs, not acceptance or completion.
title: GH #811 review: legacy discovery silently loses assertions/preconditions and admits unsupported parity candidates

acceptanceCriteria: Completed-test navigation buffers are released after writing; a repeated closed-test harness shows bounded retained heap independent of suite length.
Retry replacement, second-page refusal, context close and golden-byte tests still pass.
body: Confirmed during issue #814 round-2 review, HEAD 52a09ef16d8b43723b6f4e2bfe89f031a414d052. Installed Core 1.0.0-rc.3 build407, Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build407. navigation-events.cjs:97 stores every test state; :165-169 flush deletes only contexts, while tests retains all event arrays after output. Synthetic Node --expose-gc harness using createRecorder, one page per test, 30 closed tests with 512 unique URLs each (about 2060 bytes), serialized valid files below 4 MiB, measured +32911400 heap bytes after GC while recorder remained installed. Expected completed tests release large buffers; actual worker memory grows with all completed navigations and can exhaust memory in long suites despite individual bounds. Dispose buffers after final flush, preserving retry/multi-page refusal metadata. Reproduction used only built-ins and a disposable output directory; no source changes.
title: Navigation-events producer retains completed-test event buffers for the entire worker

acceptanceCriteria: A Codex review run launched with codex exec -s read-only from a linked worktree cannot create or mutate tickets in the primary checkout's native Tasks journal, or the limitation is documented with the supported confinement.
The repository's Codex review route (docs or skill) states how a review-only run is kept from writing tickets, and a reproduction shows no new ticket after a read-only review.
body: Observed 2026-10-11 across five Codex review runs (codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -s read-only, run from linked worktrees under /private/tmp/claude-501): the reviewer created native tickets V1-1245, V1-1247, V1-1248, V1-1249, V1-1250, V1-1251, V1-1252, V1-1253, V1-1254 and V1-1255 in the primary checkout's store (journal under the primary .git/taskman) even though the orchestrator and lanes never wrote them. The issue #814 lane's round-2 log shows  and  output for V1-1252 and V1-1255. Expected: a read-only review cannot mutate the shared native queue. Actual: the sandbox flag does not confine corvint-tasks writes (the journal lives outside the worktree, possibly reachable through a non-filesystem path or a writable-root default), so review findings appear as unrequested tickets that need deduplication. Installed Tasks build407. Workaround in use: review prompts now say not to run ticket or task-store commands. Suspected rather than confirmed: the exact write path that escapes the read-only sandbox has not been isolated.
title: Codex read-only review runs still create tickets in the primary native Tasks store

acceptanceCriteria: A build-log entry retains the STR-V0-013 parity report for `corvint test` against both earlier drivers. Every difference is explained or fixed.
20 PRs merge through the queue on the `corvint test` CI call site with complete forward rows and no AFP-V0-030 trip. This is counted under the epoch that V1-0040 advanced.
A build-log entry records median and p90 PR wall time and runner-minutes per merged PR, before and after the switch. Unavailable hosted measurements stay `NOT_OBSERVED`.

Session Test Runner V0 delivery moves from experimental to delivered in the spec header, docs/specs/README.md and docs/specs/INDEX.json, citing that evidence. If a kill criterion fires instead, the evidence and the rollback are recorded.

Balanced placement is decided separately. It is promoted locally only with at least a 20% lower p90 slowest-shard wall time against universe placement over the same frozen pairs and shard count. In CI it is promoted only after an accepted AFP-V0-028 amendment and an executed p90 comparison over 20 PRs. Otherwise it is recorded as unpromoted or removed.
body: Follow-up to V1-0040. This covers the Session Test Runner V0 promotion bar in docs/specs/session-test-runner-v0.md (Acceptance evidence: promotion and kill criteria). V1-0040 closes when the spec, slices 1 to 3 and the call-site switch merge; it leaves `corvint test` experimental. This ticket collects the post-switch evidence that promotion needs, and applies the kill criteria if they fire: an unexplained parity difference that cannot be fixed, or a queue MISS caused by the runner rather than the selector. Computed placement estimates never count as observed timing. Owner priority on 2026-10-11: work on this as soon as possible.
title: test runner: promote `corvint test` from experimental on its STR-V0 promotion evidence (V1-0040 follow-up)

acceptanceCriteria: A discrimination witness whose `mutants` exceeds `bounds.maxMutants`, or whose survivors are inconsistent with `survived`, fails `invalid-field` in the native reader and the portable consumer.

Repro: a cem/0.3 map hunk with `discriminates: {mutants:1000000, killed:1000000, survived:0, survivors:[], bounds:{maxHunks:1,maxMutants:1,wallTimeSeconds:1}, state:"discriminates"}` on a one-line hunk.
