acceptanceCriteria: `corvint-cem-anchor/1` pointers carry base, patchSha256 and targetTree; `pointerState` recomputes base..REV and returns `scope-mismatch` when the map does not describe REV; `/0` pointers stay readable.
`cem provenance --notes-tip OID` reports `rollback` when OID is not an ancestor of the live refs/notes/corvint tip.
Tests: anchoring map(A) onto a sibling commit yields scope-mismatch; resetting the notes ref yields rollback; `verified` implies the anchored patch equals base..REV.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Repro: `cem anchor --map M --commit REV` where M is HEAD's map and REV is a sibling commit with the same parent; `cem provenance` reports `verified`. internal/gitnotes/anchor.go attaches HEAD's committed pointer to any REV; provenance.go `pointerState` checks path, blob and digest only. Second repro: reset refs/notes/corvint to its parent; the anchor is reported absent, not rolled back. Proposed CEM-V1-067 (pointer `corvint-cem-anchor/1` with base, patchSha256, targetTree; `scope-mismatch`; `--notes-tip` with `rollback`). Both paths also refuse cem/1.0 because they call wire.ParseMap (see the cem/v2 statement ticket). Version: 1.0.0-rc.3 build 407.
title: cem anchor/provenance: a pointer is `verified` for any commit it was attached to, and a reset notes ref reads as absent rather than rolled back

acceptanceCriteria: score.go reports cited-not-gold rate at path and span level alongside miss; a scripted cite-every-suggestion agent loses on that metric in a test.
A registration file format is specified and the report refuses a run whose registration commit is newer than its first lane (extends CRT-V0-010).

The treatment arm definition is the shipped profile's artifact, not the all-unknown cem/0.1 worklist; the spec records that any run before decision 0523 P2 has a baseline is invalid as outcome evidence.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. tools/cem-trial/score.go `scoreLane` computes `Miss` over meta.Gold only; a lane that cites every file reaches miss 0 at no cost and the seeded arm hands out up to 8 suggestions per file. select.go/gold.go record secondary span gold that no scorer reads. Decision 0523 P4. Expected: precision (cited-not-gold rate at path and span level) is scored, and a registration file committed before selection fixes hypotheses, primary metric, alpha, n, scorer sha256, model, effort and partition. Running the trial itself is post-rc.3 and owner-commissioned.
title: cem-trial: the scorer counts recall over gold paths only, never cited-not-gold, and the recorded secondary span gold is never scored

acceptanceCriteria: Native and portable consumers emit byte-identical tier and `citation` members for every public case; a rubber-stamp map and a careful map of the same 24-hunk patch both ACCEPT with different integers (kill criterion K2).
Fixture: AGENTS.md split into 20 disjoint spans, one per hunk, still reports specificity 0.
Fixture: a hunk adding `x // `CEM-SM-007`` against a span mentioning CEM-SM-0070 is `cited`; a hunk adding only that comment is `annotation`.
The baseline report over the 591 committed maps is retained in a build-log entry with the measured tier distribution.
docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md gains CEM-V1-060..062 with the fixtures as acceptance evidence; REQUIREMENTS.tsv regenerated.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-060..062. Per hunk exactly one tier: held, mechanical-proved, anchored, cited, unknown, plus an `annotation` flag. `anchored` is derived from base blob, target blob and canonical patch only, kinds `id` (ASCII requirement ID defined by the cited span with the `- `ID`:` prefix) and `path`; the Go-only `symbol` kind is a recorded limit. The result gains hunksByClass, distinctEvidence, ordered evidenceFanOut, maxFanOut, samePathCitations, concentratedHunks, and the cyclic-shift `invariant`/`specificity` pair. No value is pass/fail. No wire change. Earliest proof: the report over the 591 committed maps is the first deliverable (expected about 0 held, about half invariant). Related: V1-0195 (hunk-anchored review projection).
title: cem/1.0 P0: consumer-computed support tiers, integer `citation` block and cyclic-shift specificity null in verify/status/report and the portable consumer

acceptanceCriteria: StableCriterion accepts a plain Git blob span criterion with no Tasks fields; the Tasks fields are an optional, closed extension object that is validated when present.
A public stable case with no Tasks fields verifies identically on native and portable consumers; an existing Tasks-bound case keeps its result.
cem-stable-v1.md records CEM-V1-063 and the pilot-kit path produces a cem/1.0 map on a non-Corvint repository in a documented, timed walkthrough.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-063. A criterion is any committed Git blob span holding acceptance text (issue template, spec, ADR, .taskman ticket). claimTicketSha256, captureSha256 and snapshotHead* in internal/cem/wire/stable.go move to an optional extension. A cem/1.0 map MUST verify with no Corvint Tasks store present. Kill criterion K4: a stranger produces and verifies a map on a non-Corvint repository within one engineer-day.
title: cem/1.0 P1: provider-neutral criterion; Tasks digests become an optional extension (must land before the V1-0595 freeze)

acceptanceCriteria: Wire and both verifiers accept the two authentication forms and refuse any other; the single-valued constant is gone from stable.go and the portable mirror.
Tests: a map that includes its own public key as an artifact stays below VERIFIED; a valid signature over a different gitTree is refused; a valid signature leaves executionAtCommit at NOT_OBSERVED.
cem-stable-v1.md records CEM-V1-064; protocol/cem-1.0 gains the cases; V1-0595 freeze notes cite this ticket as landed.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-064. `authentication` is `{"method":"none"}` or `{"method":"dsse-ed25519","keyid":K,"envelopeSha256":E}`; E names a `receipt-attestation` artifact holding an in-toto Statement whose subjects are the receipt digest, the runner-plan digest and the target gitTree. The axis rises above NOT_OBSERVED only when `--trusted-keys FILE` supplied by the consumer names K; a key carried by the map stays UNTRUSTED_KEY; a valid signature never raises executionAtCommit. Signed production stays an operator step (FPK-V0-036) and is a recorded limit. Freezing the current single-valued constant in V1-0595 would make authenticated receipts inexpressible in 1.0.
title: cem/1.0 P1: receipt `authentication` becomes a verifiable DSSE slot with a consumer-supplied trust root (must land before the V1-0595 freeze)

acceptanceCriteria: `prove --attest-cem-v2` produces a DSSE envelope whose subjects include every artifact; verification refuses an artifact or --target that is not a subject.
Test: swapping one receipt file for another valid receipt under the same path with a re-signed map and the old envelope is refused.
All 54 public stable cases give identical verdictSha256 on native and portable consumers; a case with drift records out of order changes the digest.
cem-stable-v1.md and decisions 0354/0365 are amended in the same change.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-065 and CEM-V1-066. New predicate URI per FPK-V0-033; subjects are the stable map and every artifacts[] entry; predicate adds target {gitCommit, gitTree} beside base and patch. CEMStatementV1 and cem anchor call wire.ParseMap, which refuses cem/1.0 (CEM-V1-018); ParseMap routes the stable spec to ParseStable for attestation and anchoring. The verification result splits `verdict` from `environment` (runtime.goVersion, repository envelope) and publishes verdictSha256 over canonical verdict; later re-verification appends a record keyed by (mapSha256, target). Kill criterion K6: native and portable verdictSha256 differ on any public case.
title: cem/1.0 P1: `cem/v2` in-toto statement over map, artifacts and target; stable routing in attest/anchor; verdict/environment split with `verdictSha256`

acceptanceCriteria: `cem verify` reports `held` only after its own re-execution observes a classified failure of a named test with the hunk reverted; two fixtures (revert breaks compilation; the test also fails without the revert) yield `not-run`.
The dogfood producer offers a cite-the-guarding-test step and the next 30 dogfood changes record the held share in a build-log entry against K1.
Non-Go runners are recorded as limits in the release notes; no runner is reported qualified by this ticket.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-068 and CEM-V1-069. A supported basis may name test IDs; the consumer reverse-applies that one hunk at target and runs only those tests under the fixed go-test runner profile. `held` requires a classified test failure the consumer itself observed; compile, skip or infrastructure failure is `not-run`; a producer-written witness never counts. Today 0 of 8,008 supported non-test Go hunks cite a _test.go file and TCQ-V0-057 selects only hunks that already cite one, so the producer needs a cite-the-guarding-test step or the tier never fires. Every runner other than go test is a recorded limit. Kill criteria K1 (fewer than 25% held over the next 30 dogfood changes drops the headline), K3 (audited held witnesses) and K5 (latency).
title: cem/1.0 P2: hunk-revert falsifier `held` for `go test`, and a producer step that cites the guarding test

docs/CHANGE-EVIDENCE-MAP.md positioning section carries the section 6 MUST NOT list and the kill criteria.

No rc.3 artifact advertises any of these as delivered.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Items decision 0523 defers past rc.3: a per-basis rank against K deterministic null spans seeded by patchSha256 with a BH-corrected per-hunk fraction (needs a labelled held-out set from another repository); optional author anchor offsets on the wire, only if P0 precision against human labels warrants it; a frozen mutant-operator table so discriminate counts are recomputable, and pinning the coverprofile as a Git blob by OID plus sha256 (both need cases in the 0.3 packet); the preregistered reviewer trial run (about 180 pairs for 80% power) after kill criterion K1 has a baseline, owner-commissioned.

acceptanceCriteria: A frozen replay of this task (or an equivalent spec-routed implementation task) carries cmd/corvint/affected.go, tools/gate-affected-select and the Makefile, or the packet names each as withheld with its reason.
The change passes the existing context evaluation gates with no regression on the frozen held-out set.
body: Observed 2026-10-11 by the V1-0040 slice-1 lane. Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 407), `corvint context --task` (201-char task, limit 25) at tree fab866738 (base 136dfa483). The task was to implement the Session Test Runner (`corvint test`, docs/specs/session-test-runner-v0.md). Expected: the packet carries the code the change necessarily edits or reuses: cmd/corvint/affected.go (compileAffectedGraph, shared with the new verb), tools/gate-affected-select (AFP-V0-012 attribution, moved into internal/gateselect) and the Makefile go-test recipe (STR-V0-006 typing). Actual: 25 results dominated by lexical rows (ci.yml, ci-test-slices, cishards, conformance/cli-parity-v0/manifest.go, a CEM sidecar, a benchmark run JSON). None of the three files was included, and 6184 code rows were withheld by the result limit. Answerability was `no-specific-terms`, so the packet did signal weak grounding. This is a suspected recall gap for spec-routed implementation tasks, not a confirmed bug. Evidence: scratchpad context.txt of session 23782259 (not retained in the repository).
title: context: STR slice-1 packet missed the affected command, gate-affected-select and the Makefile that the change had to edit

acceptanceCriteria: Root help regains at least 256 bytes of headroom under its bound, or CCF-V1-009 is amended by an accepted decision.

body: Observed 2026-10-11 by the V1-0040 slice-1 lane (branch claude/v1-0040-impl). Actual: the next verb added to root help must trim other text, or the bound must change. Options: group verbs under a shorter summary with `corvint help <verb>` for detail; or a reviewed CCF-V1-009 amendment raising or restructuring the bound.
title: cli: root help is at its 4096-byte CCF-V1-009 bound with 0 bytes of headroom after the `test` verb

acceptanceCriteria: Document whether canonical in-repository instruction symlinks are deliberately unsupported, with safe direct canonical-file fallback.
If support is accepted, separately specify containment, immutable target binding and out-of-root/cycle refusal before implementing.
body: Observed capability gap, not a confirmed security bug. VanillaTwisted canonically uses AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md. Core build 456, source f0d0e6106d8f7ffeaac46339ba274df3aafc712f, darwin/arm64. body: Source: V1-1262 lane (decision 0523 P0), 2026-10-12, corvint at origin/main f0d0e6106. Cause: internal/dogfoodflow/check.go `agree` requires byte-identical stdout/stderr/status of `cem status` from the base-commit verifier and the tree verifier; the lane added the additive `citation` member to the canonical verification object, so the base verifier (which predates it) can never agree. Expected: a documented transition for a change whose own output differs by construction. Actual: the change cannot be checked or sealed at its own base; the workaround taken in V1-1262 is to gate emission behind an opt-in `--citation` flag so default output stays frozen. Consequence for decision 0525: the dogfood producer cutover to cem/1.0 (V1-1276) and the stable-result freeze (V1-1265) change verifier output by construction and will hit the same refusal; `corvint dogfood finish` already records the analogous no-base-independence case (LCP-V0-014). body: Source: decision 0523 P0 baseline over the 593 committed cem/0.2 maps at origin/main f0d0e6106 (docs/build-log/2026-10-12-cem-citation-baseline-593-maps.md, evidence under docs/build-log/evidence/v1-1262/). Observed: 180 of 592 citation blocks are invariant (every hunk cites the same evidence set); 171 of those are the `chore: bind change evidence` / `chore: seal change evidence` maps the dogfood loop writes for itself, each citing one span for every hunk; 45 maps have negative specificity (umbrella citations that a cyclic shift of the hunk order matches as well as the real plan) and 17 maps have evidence fan-out >= 100. Cause: `make dogfood-change` takes a flat DOGFOOD_CITATIONS TSV (ORDINAL, path, lines, class) and the bind/seal rounds reuse one spec span for every hunk, so the producer writes maps that the cem/1.0 consumer-computed tiers grade as cited/invariant by construction. Expected after the decision 0525 cutover (V1-1276): the producer emits one citation per hunk from the change's own evidence (spec section, test, decision) and the self-referential bind/seal maps are recognised as their own class so they do not dominate every tier metric. Actual: a careful change and a rubber-stamp change look the same at the producer, which is the exact failure cem/1.0 exists to expose. Scope: producer and dogfood loop only; the consumer tiers (CEM-V1-080..082) do not change.
title: dogfood producer: per-hunk citations and a distinct class for self-referential bind/seal maps

body: Source: review of CEM 1.0 fit for the Corvint and corvint-tasks use cases, 2026-10-12, orchestrating session for decision 0523/0525. Observed: corvint-tasks does not consume CEM maps today; internal/taskman imports internal/cem/wire only for the generic JSON value type, and docs/specs/tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md refuses to delegate completion authority to opaque cem/1.0-experimental.1 references. Decision 0523 P1 (CEM-V1-083) makes the criterion provider-neutral (any committed blob span) and a cem/1.0 map MUST verify with no Tasks store present, so the only existing link (CEM-V1-002 native ticket binding) becomes an optional extension. Consequence: after rc.3 a ticket's native completion and the change's sealed cem/1.0 verdict are two unconnected proofs of the same change. Expected: a Tasks gate can require the sealed verdict (verdictSha256 plus the consumer-computed citation block, CEM-V1-080..082/086) as evidence, for example `every hunk under the ticket's effects.touchPaths is at least anchored` or `held hunks >= N once V1-1266 lands`, with the verdict bytes pinned in the gate result and re-verifiable by either independent consumer. Non-goals: Tasks never raises a tier, never trusts a producer-written field, and completion authority stays with the native store (TCB-V0-006). Open question for the spec: whether the gate reads the committed map from the primary checkout at the attempt's snapshot head or receives the verdict as an attached-evidence receipt.

body: Observed 2026-10-12 while building V1-1273 (tools/cem-stable-regen --check) on origin/main 2c81d1f3c and 1058de51f. protocol/cem-1.0/stable/manifest.json (cem-stable-protocol-manifest/1, 16 files) records REPOSITORY-ENVELOPE.cells.json as sha256 c3eed8b83713... / 302453 bytes and REPOSITORY-ENVELOPE.md as 9c35b7a5e681... / 9705 bytes, but the committed files are 6b3828ac703b... / 302947 bytes and dd33dcaf9362... / 10003 bytes. Both files and the manifest were last changed in the same commit fc5588948 (Integrate CEM stable repository and process envelope), so the manifest was sealed before the final bytes of those two files. The other 14 entries match. Reproduction: for each entry in manifest.json files[], compare sha256 and byte length of the named file. Expected: every entry matches. Actual: two mismatches. No consumer test currently verifies the stable manifest entries, so the defect was invisible. cem-stable-regen --check deliberately verifies only the RESULT.schema.json entry of this manifest (see tools/cem-stable-regen/main.go check()) and its first regeneration re-binds only that entry; once this manifest is repaired, widen the check to every entry. Fix: re-bind both entries (and any repair note the stable packet requires), document the repair in docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md traceability, then remove the only-schema restriction in cem-stable-regen check() and rebind.
title: cem/1.0 stable manifest.json: entries for REPOSITORY-ENVELOPE.cells.json and REPOSITORY-ENVELOPE.md are stale since fc5588948

body: Findings from the V1-1273 proof run (2026-10-12, throwaway worktree on PR #821 head merged with origin/main, both P0 patches, `citation` regenerated after artifactChecks). Use them when V1-1265 lands the member. (1) Values: 54 cases come from the native capture (CEM_STABLE_REGEN_CAPTURE on go1.27.2); cases 21 and 22 (go1.24.13-only) need --values: case 21 = the native ComputeCitation block (produced on go1.27.2 with the binding check bypassed), case 22 = null. Envelope cells: 19 of 29 derive from captured cases; 10 need --cell-values (4 sha256 ACCEPT cells = the native ordinary-sha256 value; 6 early repository refusals = null). (2) Consumers pinning the closed 21-key shape that must become 22 in the same change: cmd/corvint/cem_stable_test.go:17; internal/cem/cli/stable_test.go:28; internal/cem/cli/stable_read_test.go:221; internal/cem/cli/stable_report_test.go:44; internal/cemcandidate/stable_test.go:113; interop/cem01-go/stable_repository_test.go:123; internal/cem/verify/stable_repository_test.go:333-334 (the requireS0EResult constant). interop/cem01-go/citation_test.go:470 (TestCEMV1082StableResultKeepsSealedShape) asserts 21 keys and a null citation and must be rewritten. (3) Consumer disagreement: interop TestStableCanonicalFullResults differs on key `citation` for cases 08, 09, 10, 11, 13, 50, 51, 53, 54: native carries a citation block on late cancellations/refusals, portable emits null. Per CEM-V1-091 this is a consumer defect to resolve (decide which side is the contract, probably null on any non-ACCEPT outcome) before regeneration, never by editing captured values. (4) V1-1265 must also add the `provenance` member and the closed producer-only-members list (chore bind/seal class for V1-1281); each is one more cem-stable-regen run, so plan the key count accordingly. acceptanceCriteria: ALGORITHMS.md states the stage and precedence for unresolved hunk basis, missing criterion link, duplicated unknown link IDs and duplicated artifacts.
Native and portable consumers return the same stage and code for each of the four mutations, proven by a shared sealed case or paired tests in internal/cem/verify and interop/cem01-go.
Existing sealed S0E cases and protocol/cem-1.0/maps results are unchanged.
body: Found 2026-10-12 by the independent review of V1-1263 (branch claude/v1-1263-neutral-criterion from origin/main 19779517f) and confirmed by reading both consumers; runtime reproduction NOT_RUN. The native stable consumer (internal/cem/wire/stable.go ParseStable + validateStableGraph) and the portable consumer (interop/cem01-go/cem.go decodeStable + validateStableReferences) return different stage/code pairs for four cem/1.0 map mutations that no sealed S0E case covers. They predate V1-1263 and affect Tasks-form and plain-form maps alike. (1) A hunk basis entry naming an evidence ID that is not in change.evidence: native refuses at stage wire via validateReferences (stable.go ~line 139, code invalid-field); portable refuses at stage references with unresolved-reference (cem.go ~line 4017). (2) A map whose criterion has no criterionLinks entry: native returns reference-coherence from the usedCriteria/ids count (stable.go ~line 399); portable returns unresolved-reference from the linkedCriteria/criteria count (cem.go ~line 4001). (3) A link whose hunkIds repeats an unknown ID: native checks each ID for existence as it walks and returns unresolved-reference first (stable.go ~line 363); portable completes the duplicate scan first and returns duplicate-reference (cem.go ~line 3975). (4) A duplicated artifact path or digest: native returns duplicate-reference (stable.go ~line 428); portable returns artifact-role-closure (cem.go ~line 4047). Expected: CEM-V1-083 and the stable contract require identical results from both consumers for the same inputs. Actual: four divergent refusal codes. Fix: decide the canonical stage and precedence per case in protocol/cem-1.0/stable/ALGORITHMS.md, align the consumer that deviates, and add the four mutations as sealed refusal cases (a public case under protocol/cem-1.0/stable/ or S0E via tools/cem-stable-regen) so parity is tested rather than assumed. Interop cem01-go/stable_neutral_test.go only mutates the criterion and its link ID.
title: cem/1.0 consumers diverge on four refusal codes: hunk-basis stage, missing link, duplicated unknown link IDs, duplicated artifacts

acceptanceCriteria: Decide and record in docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md whether an argument-stage refusal (stage arguments, code invalid-arguments, including a bad --trusted-keys file) is REJECT with accept:false or UNSUPPORTED with accept:null, and make the native CLI (internal/cem/cli/stable.go Refuse arguments/invalid-arguments) and both portable commands (interop/cem01-go/stable_repository.go and cem.go failStable with operational invalid-arguments) emit the same outcome and accept value.

body: Observed 2026-10-12 by the independent Codex review of the V1-1264 branch (CEM-V1-084 receipt authentication). For the same argument-stage refusal the native stable CLI returns outcome REJECT with accept:false (internal/cem/cli/stable.go, r.Refuse("arguments","invalid-arguments",false)), while both portable commands return outcome UNSUPPORTED with accept:null (interop/cem01-go/stable_repository.go executeStableCanonicalCLI and cem.go, failStable(&r,"arguments",operational("invalid-arguments"),false)). The divergence predates V1-1264: the existing missing or relative --map and --repository refusals use the same calls on origin/main 84c331fca. V1-1264 mirrored each consumer's existing convention for a bad --trusted-keys file rather than changing the argument stage. Reproduce: run corvint cem verify-stable and the portable verify-stable and canonical commands with --trusted-keys pointing at an absolute file holding {"profile":"corvint-trusted-keys/1","keys":[]} and compare the JSON outcome and accept members. Expected under the CEM-V1-084 parity sentence: the same result. Actual: REJECT/false versus UNSUPPORTED/null. Suspected contract gap, not a confirmed verifier defect: the parity requirement may only intend the stages after arguments.

body: Observed 2026-10-12 with corvint-tasks build 402 on queue:corvint:main. acceptanceCriteria: The Codex review prompt in the lane common charter and the codex-cli review skill forbid corvint-tasks mutations and name receipt audit as the check.
Decide whether corvint-tasks gains a read-only environment marker; if yes, every mutation refuses with one closed code when it is set and a focused test covers it.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 on queue:corvint:main. The V1-1305 builder ran the one-round Codex review as `codex exec -s read-only ... </dev/null` from its plain clone under /private/tmp. The review nevertheless executed `corvint-tasks ticket attach-evidence` against V1-1305 and the write succeeded: receipt 000000004563.json, request-id v11305-review-invalid-ocm-shape-20261012, actor russelllewis role OWNER, ticket revision 1 -> 2. The Codex sandbox only guards the filesystem of the review cwd; corvint-tasks resolves the journal under the primary checkout .git/taskman and the local-operator actor binding is recorded, not authenticated (decision 0003). Consequence: reviewer-written evidence is indistinguishable from builder or owner evidence, which weakens the reviewer independence the lane protocol relies on, and an unexpected revision bump can make a later expected-revision mutation by the builder refuse STALE_TICKET. Options: (a) the review prompt and skill state that the reviewer must not run corvint-tasks mutations and the orchestrator checks receipt audit for reviewer-attributed writes; (b) corvint-tasks honours an environment marker such as CORVINT_TASKS_READ_ONLY=1 that refuses every mutation with one closed code so a sandboxed reviewer cannot write; (c) attach-evidence records a reviewer role distinct from OWNER. Not a corvint-tasks defect; filed as a protocol gap.
title: Review lanes: a read-only Codex review can still write Tasks journal evidence (attach-evidence on V1-1305)

# Review of 40c67a604b9235edf982b0fd05068dfe16348a4c..efc6dcff3e55e159d112c2835ed1c4f0b9748bf8

All confirmed cases report BOUNDED with unknown=[] while omitting a reachable test. Each includes a normal direct control test to avoid NO_SELECTABLE_TEST masking the missing dependent. Repros are retained in review_soundness_test.go and invoked via overlay.json, with no edits to repository code.

1. P1: java/java.go:408-415 qualifiedReferences requires a contiguous dotted string of at least three segments. `new p.Core()` and `new com . ex . core . Core()` / `new com.ex.core./*comment*/Core()` miss the dirty Core.java edge from a test in q. Two segments follow JAT-V0-003 literally but are an unguarded spec soundness gap; whitespace/comment cases also violate its semantic reference rule.
2. P1: java/java.go:45-47,319-326 reflection markers require punctuation adjacency. `ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader().loadClass ("com.ex.core.Core").getDeclaredConstructor ().newInstance ();` yields neither an edge nor UnboundedReads. JAT-V0-007 requires the triggers regardless of Java whitespace/comments.
3. P1: java/java.go:227-228,253-264 and lex.go:138-144 literal Class.forName binary names do not resolve nested types. Outer.java declares Outer.Inner but `Class.forName("p.Outer$Inner")` is accepted as bounded, matches no type and does not trigger reflection. JAT-V0-003 requires the declaring file.
4. P1: java/lex.go:24-25,55-61 lexes raw bytes without Java Unicode-escape preprocessing and only ends // comments at LF. `// comment \u000a @Test void t(){new Core();}` loses executable code. CR-only `// comment\rclass MissedTest {@Test void t(){new Core();}}` does too. Both compile, yield no frontier, and erase the test signal/edge.
5. P2: java/java.go:429-432 annotation discovery requires contiguous @Name text. `@ Test void t(){new Core();}` (also @/*comment*/Test) compiles but the file is classified as a source despite a test location. JAT-V0-002 test signal is missed.
6. P1: java/java.go:340-346 requires local runner signals and never propagates inherited test discovery. `public abstract class Base {@Test public void t(){new Core();}}` plus `public class MissedTest extends Base {}` selects Base.java, omits runnable MissedTest.java, and reports BOUNDED. JAT-V0-002 itself lacks an inherited-discovery frontier; false selection of abstract Base does not provide a runnable check.
7. P1: java/java.go:215-219 a wildcard import into any observed package skips unresolved-name handling. `import com.ex.core.*; ... @Test void t(){new Generated().callCore();}` omits the test for dirty Core.java when an annotation processor supplies `Generated { public void callCore(){new Core();}}`. A single import of Generated correctly widens, but the wildcard neither sets java:unresolved-import nor an edge. This contradicts the generated-source safety claim under JAT-V0-006.
8. P1: java/kotlin.go:18-26 and kotlin/java.go:21-29 parse package headers from raw source. Kotlin `/*license*/ package p` followed by `class Bridge {fun run()=Core()}` misses java:kotlin-dependent on p/Core.java. A q.BridgeTest importing only Bridge and calling run is excluded for dirty Core.java. The inverse Java `/*license*/ package p; ... new Core()` misses kotlin:java-dependent for dirty p/Core.kt. The normal language scanners strip comments, but these new frontier scanners do not. JAT-V0-008 violated.
9. P1: kotlin/java.go:76,80-82 derives incorrect JVM names. p/core.kt is recorded as coreKt although its JVM facade is CoreKt; Java `import p.CoreKt; ... CoreKt.value()` does not set kotlin:java-dependent. `@file:kotlin.jvm.JvmName("Api")` and spaced `@file:JvmName ("Api")` also fail the exact-substring custom-facade lookup. A Kotlin direct control test permits a BOUNDED plan that excludes the Java test when the Kotlin file changes. JAT-V0-008 violated.

Verification: installed Java and Kotlin package tests pass; Kotlin real-repository ground truth skipped because its env var is unset. Shared TestSeam and TestComposedGraph checks pass. Isolated Go selection repros confirm the above omissions; Java cases compiled with installed OpenJDK 17 and a stub Test annotation (syntax validation, not JUnit runner qualification). No determinism defect observed. No full repository gate run for this read-only review.

Official semantic references: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se17/html/jls-3.html ; https://kotlinlang.org/docs/java-to-kotlin-interop.html ; https://docs.junit.org/6.1.3/writing-tests/test-classes-and-methods.html

The same tree passed go-product-shard (7) on the PR branch run (CI claude/v1-1278-s3-retire-packets, 09:09Z) and the PR touches no Go source under internal/liveverify (it retires packets and docs). Re-queued at 11:08Z (run 38388116872).

Expected: a performance budget test either runs under a load guard (skip or widen when the runner is contended, as the tasks-store timing tests in V1-1324 propose) or measures a ratio against a calibrated baseline on the same host, so a 2% miss on a shared runner does not evict a merge-queue entry.
Actual: a hard 100ms p95 budget measured on whatever runner the shard lands on; the margin is p50 91ms, so ordinary contention crosses it.

Version: origin/main d72617c46 + PR #854 head 5fcbf06bb. Related: V1-1324 (tasks-store timing tests under load).
title: internal/liveverify/affected: TestIncrementalSelectionMeetsTheLiveBudget fails on a loaded CI runner (p95 102ms vs 100ms budget)

acceptanceCriteria: A docs/build-log-only change binds without a spec intent and the sealed map carries class `record`; `tools/cem-citation-baseline` reports `record` rows apart from `change`; the DCW spec names the class and the baseline registration (0527) states whether record maps are excluded from the authored arm.
body:
Observed friction. PR beamfall/corvint#855 added only a build-log entry and three evidence files. `dogfood change` refused the build-log entry as intent (ocm-prepare invalid-requirements-section: the intent must be a spec with exactly one `## Requirements` heading) and refused a uniform plan (DCW-V0-048), so the bind cited DCW-V0-052, -053, -055 and -056 one span per hunk by convention, not because the hunks implement those requirements. The same pattern applies to every docs-only record change (S1..S3 build-log entries, baseline records). These citations are exactly the shape the V1-1336/V1-1278 baselines measure as 'no better than a grep bot' (authored excess 1.94%, kill under 0527): the recipe manufactures weak citations.

Expected: a third citation class beside `change` and `chore` (DCW-V0-048/049), e.g. `record`, for a change whose paths are all under docs/build-log/ (and its evidence/ subtree) or .agent-evidence/: the map binds the hunks to the build-log entry (or to the decision it records) with relation `evidence`, no spec span required, and the baseline tool reports the class separately so record maps stop diluting the authored arm.
Actual: record changes must cite spec spans; builders choose spans mechanically.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: dogfood: an evidence-record change (build-log entry + evidence files) has no requirement to cite; add a `record` citation class instead of forcing spec spans

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-check reports linked/unlinked over the requirement IDs the bound change cites or traces, with a test that a lane adding N traced requirements reports linked=N; or the OCM coverage members are removed from the SUMMARY and the OCM spec is amended in the same change.
body:
Observed on every lane this week (PR #855: `dogfood-check: SUMMARY cem=accepted hunks=4 supported=4 ... ocm=ready-for-review requirements=56 linked=0 unlinked=56` then `dogfood-check: PASS`). Each lane adds requirements and tests that trace them (REQUIREMENTS.tsv rows, test names per ID), yet the OCM line reports zero linked requirements for the whole intent spec and the check passes regardless.

Expected: either the linker counts the requirement IDs that the change's citations and traceability rows actually reference (so a lane that adds CEM-V1-226..229 shows linked=4 of the IDs it touched, not 0 of 56), or the line is removed from the SUMMARY and the spec stops describing it as coverage. A number that is always zero and never gates is noise that trains readers to ignore the summary.
Actual: linked=0 on passing lanes; nothing consumes the value.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: dogfood-check: `requirements=56 linked=0 unlinked=56` still passes; the OCM intent coverage line carries no signal

acceptanceCriteria: Two lanes adding requirements to the same spec merge without conflicts outside the requirement list itself; docs/SPEC-DRIVEN-DEVELOPMENT.md names where intent-status history lives; `make spec-requirements` regenerates every derived row a lane previously hand-edited.
body:
Observed friction across the rc.3 lanes (V1-1276, V1-1277, V1-1278 S1..S3, V1-1281, V1-1336; memory of 2026-10-12: #831 went DIRTY against #829). Each lane appends to the same four shared-insertion points in a spec: the intent-status line in the header, the Agent digest, docs/specs/INDEX.json and README.md rows, and the generated REQUIREMENTS.tsv. Two lanes on one spec file conflict every time, and the resolution rule ('keep both sections, append the branch's tail, regenerate the TSV') is folklore held in agent memory, not in the SDD contract. Requirement ID ranges are reserved by chat (V1-1009 covers the ID collision itself; this ticket is the surrounding header state).

Expected: (a) the intent-status history moves to the build-log (one line per acceptance, already the decision-0423 shape) and the spec header keeps only the current status; (b) the Agent digest and INDEX/README rows are generated from the spec body by `make spec-requirements` like REQUIREMENTS.tsv, so a lane never hand-edits them; (c) REQUIREMENTS.tsv is not committed but checked (generated in CI from the staged specs), or is split per spec so two lanes touching different specs cannot conflict.
Actual: four hand-maintained insertion points per spec, conflicts on every concurrent lane, resolution rules outside the contract.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: specs: intent-status tails, Agent digest lines and REQUIREMENTS.tsv regeneration conflict on every parallel lane; move per-lane state out of the shared spec header

acceptanceCriteria: The SDD contract names the acceptance mode for requirements written under a standing approval, REQUIREMENTS.tsv (or the spec header) carries it, and one audit command lists requirements never read back by the owner.
body:
Open question, not a defect. docs/SPEC-DRIVEN-DEVELOPMENT.md defines `accepted` as 'explicitly approved by the repository owner' and product invariant 8 says generated or inferred documentation can propose intent but cannot accept it. Since the owner's standing auto-accept of lane requirements on 2026-10-11, every requirement a lane writes becomes `accepted` in the same PR that implements it (CEM-V1-140..232, DCW-V0-048..056, this week alone), so the status no longer separates owner-reviewed intent from agent-authored intent, and the authority ladder's top rung is filled by the lane that is also filling rungs 3 and 4.

Expected: either (a) a distinct intent status (`accepted-standing` or `auto-accepted`) that names the standing-approval record and the date, promotable to `accepted` only by an owner read-back, with REQUIREMENTS.tsv carrying the mode so an audit can list every requirement the owner never read; or (b) a periodic owner acceptance batch (the build-log already has 'Owner acceptances' entries) that converts auto-accepted rows, with a gate that refuses `validated` delivery status on an auto-accepted requirement.
Actual: `accepted` is written by the lane; no row distinguishes the two.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: governance: the standing auto-accept of lane requirements (since 2026-10-11) makes `accepted` intent status undiscriminating; record the acceptance mode in the status

acceptanceCriteria: One command takes a committed branch plus a citation plan from BASE to a sealed, checked tree; its tests cover each existing refusal stopping the loop; docs/DOGFOOD.md §4 names it as the default path.
body:
Observed cost. Every lane this week ran the same sequence by hand: pass-0 `dogfood change` to learn hunk IDs, write cites.tsv, `/bin/rm -f .corvint/change.cem.json`, rerun with DOGFOOD_CITATIONS, commit 'chore: bind change evidence', rerun, `make dogfood-check`, `make dogfood-seal`, push. Each step has its own refusal class (invalid-requirements-section, citation-plan-not-provided, citation-plan-uniform, record-index-failed 'commit the sidecar', DIRTY_WORKTREE) and the recovery for each is held in agent memory, not in the tool. A lane spends roughly a third of its wall clock on this loop and the Codex round; the recipe is identical every time.

Expected: a single command (or `make dogfood-finish BASE=<sha> CITATIONS=<tsv>`) that runs the loop end to end, stops at the first refusal with the existing `fix:` line, makes the bind and seal commits itself, and leaves the pushed state for the PR; the per-step commands stay for repair. Keep every NOT_PRODUCED reason visible in one report.
Actual: six manual steps, each with a memorised recovery.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: dogfood: one `corvint dogfood finish-lane` recipe (citations → bind commit → recheck → seal → push) to replace the six-step manual bind loop every lane repeats

acceptanceCriteria: A focused test reproduces a plan row whose BASE span is outside every hunk but whose text recurs in an added region, and asserts the refusal's fix line states the cause.
The DCW spec documents the cause wording under the cite-span-not-stable reason.
The existing refusal code and exit status are unchanged.
body: Observed 2026-10-13 on lane V1-1303 (branch claude/v1-1303-stable-sidecar-reuse, base 94a7d3dc53e1314e761bc306dda80d338d2e2ed6, PR beamfall/corvint#856), Core build from origin/main. The first citation plan was refused `cem-cite NOT_PRODUCED cite-span-not-stable` on row 7, span docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md:1413:1415. Those BASE lines sit outside every diff hunk, but their text (`Acceptance evidence:` and a table header) is repeated by the new section the change adds, so the stability check treated the span as edited. Expected: the fix line names the reason (for example that the span's content also occurs inside a changed region, or that the span moved) and the nearest stable alternative. Actual: the refusal names only the row and span, so the builder had to find a unique line by trial (citing requirement lines 1331..1401 worked). Relation to DCW-V0-019/DCW-V0-046 to be confirmed by the implementer.
title: dogfood change: cite-span-not-stable should say why a span outside every hunk counts as edited

body: Observed 2026-10-13 on lane V1-1303 (PR beamfall/corvint#856). docs/specs/local-completion-policy-v0.md cites internal/localcompletion/types.go line 157 and lifecycle.go lines 456 to 607 without a pinned commit, and line-citations-check verifies them against the working tree. acceptanceCriteria: A local check fails, naming package and path, when a test file in a declared package names a repository path literal outside that package's read-scope entries, and passes on the current tree.
The check runs in the local doc-gate list used by lanes and in CI before the confined shard runs.
The V1-1340 case (internal/cem/verify reading protocol/cem-1.0/stable/tamper-matrix/ with the entry removed) is a fixture that the check catches.
body: Observed 2026-10-13 (lane V1-1340, PR beamfall/corvint#859): a lane added protocol/cem-1.0/stable/tamper-matrix/ and a test in internal/cem/verify (a package declared in .corvint/test-read-scopes.json) that reads it. Local runs are unconfined and passed; the hosted go-product-shard run under the Landlock wrapper failed with a content-looking message ("manifest entry ... does not match the case file") because the read returned EACCES. The affected literal-reader rule (AFP-V0-021) already extracts repository path literals from test sources per package. Proposal: a local check (make target or part of unbounded-readers-check) that, for every declared package, compares the path literals its test files name against the declared read scope and fails naming the undeclared path, so the gap is caught before push. Related: V1-0633 (run the confined wrapper locally) and V1-1298 (selection fan-out on a scopes edit). Not a defect in the wrapper; the declaration grammar and enforcement behaved as specified.
title: test read scopes: fail locally when a declared package reads a repository path outside its declaration

acceptanceCriteria: A test reproduces a pending redo held across several heartbeat calls on a live attempt and shows the heartbeat either completes the pending redo itself or returns within a documented bound shorter than the heartbeat TTL.
GitHub beamfall/corvint#860 questions 1 and 2 are answered in the spec text and the PR body.

While heartbeats are refused REDO_PENDING the attempt is not reaped or fenced on liveness grounds (TTL honoured or extended), proven by a test, or the result states explicitly (retryAfter / liveness-honoured field) whether liveness is preserved; the Tasks spec and help document which writer completes a pending redo and the caller contract.
body: Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#860 (2026-10-13). `corvint-tasks attempt heartbeat` returned ERROR [REDO_PENDING] (retryable) on 5 consecutive calls 360 s apart (~18 min) on a native canonical-writer queue (writeBarrier NONE, ~37k receipts, 2-4 live attempts, no dispatcher). A caller treating three misses as lost (600 s TTL) fenced and killed a healthy 36-minute command. A later claim succeeded within ~6 min and queue status showed no pending redo. Expected: REDO_PENDING resolves within a bounded documented time shorter than the heartbeat TTL (e.g. the heartbeat writer completes the redo), or the result tells the caller how long to wait and whether liveness is honoured. Questions: what leaves a redo pending and which writer completes it; is the heartbeat TTL extended while heartbeats are refused. Code: internal/tasks (journal, snapshot/probe.go, cli). Related completed: V1-0648, V1-1126, V1-0309, V1-0780.
title: corvint-tasks attempt heartbeat refused REDO_PENDING for ~18 min fences a live attempt (GitHub #860)

acceptanceCriteria: Each listed command either settles a pending receipt under the writer lock or is documented as a read that cannot, with a test reproducing a held-pending receipt per command class.
The Tasks spec states which commands settle a pending redo; help text agrees.
body: Follow-up from PR beamfall/corvint#861 (V1-1352, CAL-V0-222/223). That PR makes leaseCommand (internal/tasks/cli/lease.go) proceed past a pending receipt so the store lease writer settles it under the lock. The builder observed that barrier, policy, import, cutover, escalation and `attempt run`'s initial probe still return the snapshot.Probe REDO_PENDING error as-is at their pre-write probe, so a receipt left pending by a writer killed between receipt link-in and head.json rename (§5.2 C2) refuses them until a ticket mutation settles it. Also recorded by Codex: health and pool cleanup do not carry the redo warning. Suspected defect by code inspection (not reproduced live).
title: corvint-tasks barrier/policy/import/cutover/escalation and attempt run initial probe still refuse REDO_PENDING before the store writer settles it (follow-up to GitHub #860)

body: Observed 2026-10-13 in lane V1-1345 (PR beamfall/corvint#862, commit 33e01d0a1). Codex review flagged that the new OCM coverage reader called git diff / git grep through an unbounded reader. The fix capped it at 16 MiB (overflow prints NOT_OBSERVED), but the cap had to live in internal/dogfoodflow/ocm_coverage.go because flow.git in internal/dogfoodflow/flow.go buffers git output with no limit and flow.go was outside that lane's scope. acceptanceCriteria: a decision or TCB-V0 amendment states how a merged-forward lane satisfies the cem-verdict gate at the commit complete --commit pins (merge-aware candidate rule or an explicit quiescent-main requirement)
one real native completion through the cem-verdict gate is recorded with its receipt audit (V1-1283 criterion 4) under the chosen rule
touchPaths without trailing slashes are either normalized to prefix keys for the predicate or refused with a named reason
body: Observed 2026-10-13 from the V1-1283 continuation (PR beamfall/corvint#863, head 0de6d5ab8). TCB-V0-015 substitutes {attempt.candidateCommit} with the gate worktree HEAD, and the verdict gate (internal/taskman/cem_verdict_gate.go) refuses sealed-tree-mismatch unless the candidate's tree differs from the sealed map's target (the bind commit) only by the sidecar rename. Native completion (`complete --commit <merge sha>`) requires the submitted tree to be the merge commit tree. When main moved between the lane BASE and the merge, or when a post-seal commit exists, the merge tree differs from the seal tree, so the gate refuses on exactly the commit completion needs. Every lane closed out today (V1-1303, V1-1340, V1-1345) had a moved main. Criterion 4 of V1-1283 (one real completion through the gate) therefore needs either a lane whose merge commit tree equals its seal tree (PR head = seal commit and no intervening merges) or a gate rule that accepts a merge of the seal commit into base whose non-sidecar delta against base is exactly the seal commit's delta. Expected: decide and specify which (TCB-V0 amendment), with the refusal name kept for a genuinely altered tree. Actual: no gate-compatible completion path for the ordinary merge-forward lane. Also: V1-1283's own touchPaths lack trailing slashes so they govern no hunk under touched-anchored (see the lane report); the predicate vocabulary may need a prefix rule.
title: cem-verdict gate: candidate must be the seal commit, but native completion pins the merge commit, so the gate can only grant on a quiescent main

acceptanceCriteria: make spec-acceptance-audit reports UNPARSED_STANDING 0 on the merged tree
the standing count equals the previous standing count plus the moved markers and the owner/unrecorded counts are otherwise unchanged

body: Observed 2026-10-13 in lane V1-1346+V1-1347 (PR beamfall/corvint#864). SRG-V0-009..010 parse the acceptance mode from the leading parenthetical of a requirement's definition line. `make spec-acceptance-audit` on BASE 523fa4ce6 reports UNPARSED_STANDING for 52 requirements in 5 specs whose standing marker sits at the end of the line; they are counted as `unrecorded` and NOT_PROMOTABLE cannot see them. Expected: the markers sit in the leading parenthetical (same wording), the audit reports 0 UNPARSED_STANDING and the standing count rises by 52. Actual: 52 UNPARSED_STANDING rows. Prose-only change; REQUIREMENTS.tsv columns 5-6 regenerate via make spec-requirements. Run the audit (`make spec-acceptance-audit`) to list the exact rows; do not alter requirement text or IDs.
title: specs: move the 52 trailing standing-acceptance markers in 5 specs to the leading parenthetical so the acceptance audit counts them

acceptanceCriteria: interop/cem01-go qualifies a linux process-containment implementation (or an explicitly bounded linux route) so verify-stable-canonical returns ACCEPT/REJECT on linux with the same verdictSha256 as native
TestTCBV0016GateVerdictRunsBothConsumers runs (not skipped) on the linux CI shard and passes
docs/specs/tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md and cem-stable-v1.md record the qualified hosts for the portable leg
body: Confirmed on 2026-10-13. interop/cem01-go qualifies process containment only in stable_process_darwin.go; stable_process_other.go answers unsupported-process-containment, so verify-stable-canonical reports outcome UNSUPPORTED on linux. The taskman cem-verdict gate (TCB-V0-016/017, PR beamfall/corvint#863) treats that as verifier-disagreement and REFUSES, which is the specified behaviour but means the gate can only GRANT on darwin. Reproduction: PR #863 CI run 38463640466, go-product-shard (0), TestTCBV0016GateVerdictRunsBothConsumers: native ACCEPT verdictSha256 14ac383d..., portable UNSUPPORTED verdictSha256 5de4c58a..., citationSha256 null. Expected: the portable consumer recomputes the same verdict on linux. Actual: UNSUPPORTED. Interim: commit d30f894fa skips the real-consumer test NOT_RUN off darwin; internal/taskman keeps the stand-in consumer on linux. The live policy v9 cem-verdict entry is required:false and the owner runs gates on darwin, so no queue impact yet.
title: cem-verdict gate cross-check: interop/cem01-go verify-stable-canonical is darwin-only, so the real-consumer leg cannot run on linux CI or any linux Tasks host

acceptanceCriteria: Decision recorded (spec tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md) on whether the verdict predicate domain is a distinct closed input from the claim scope, with the rejected alternative
A ticket can declare its full write set as effects.touchPaths and still run cem-verdict touched-anchored over a narrower governed path list
V1-1348's closeout evidence is re-read against the chosen contract and the build-log entry names any re-run needed
body: Friction observed on 2026-10-13 while preparing V1-1348 for criterion 4 of V1-1283. The cem-verdict gate (policy v9, {claim.touchPaths} placeholder, TCB-V0-015) evaluates predicate touched-anchored over the claim-era effects.touchPaths. Only generated spec projection hunks (docs/specs/README.md, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, sometimes INDEX.json) reach tier anchored; ordinary cited hunks are tier cited and fail tier-below-anchored. To make the gate GRANT, V1-1348's effects were declared as exactly docs/specs/README.md and docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv, which is narrower than the paths the lane actually edits, and the real paths then have to be widened after claim (claim with DECLARED effects ignores --scope, see V1-1321). The same field therefore carries two meanings: the Tasks resource reservation (should be the full write set) and the verdict predicate domain (should be the paths whose evidence must be anchored). Expected: a separate, closed predicate input (e.g. a per-gate touchPaths or a ticket requirement-evidence path list) so the claim scope can stay truthful. Actual: one field, two consumers, and the narrower one wins. Related: V1-1356 (candidate must be the seal commit).
title: Ticket effects.touchPaths serves both the claim scope and the cem-verdict predicate, forcing a narrow declaration to make touched-anchored pass

acceptanceCriteria: A merge_group run of ci.yml whose commit's tree a completed successful pull_request run of this workflow already tested in full (records for every shard of the current count) skips only the root Go race invocation and retains the ci-reuse decision with the reused run id; any mismatch, listing failure, failed, partial, narrowed or differently-sharded run stays FULL.

AFP-V0-026 is amended and a new AFP-V0 requirement records the queue reuse with its limits; tools/ci-reuse-plan tests cover the admitted merge_group case and each refusal; the workflow shard-count test still binds REUSE_SHARDS to the matrix.
One hosted merge_group run after the change is retained showing REUSE with the pull-request run id, or the first observation is recorded as NOT_OBSERVED with the reason.
body: Owner request 2026-10-13: PRs wait serially because every merge runs the full 8-shard race matrix three times (pull_request run ~25 min, merge_group run ~20 min, main push ~9-20 min), and the beamfall org is on the free plan (20 concurrent hosted jobs; one CI run holds 13), so raising the ruleset's max_entries_to_build cannot add parallelism until per-run cost drops. AFP-V0-024 already lets a main push reuse a passed pull_request run of the identical tree; AFP-V0-026 keeps the merge_group run FULL and reuse off for it. When the queue entry is the first on an unmoved main, the queue commit is merge(main, PR head) with the same two parents as the pull-request merge ref the PR run tested, so the trees are identical by construction and the identity binds the workflow file, the Go pin and every tracked path. Expected: the merge_group run's docs-plan reuse step runs for merge_group too, admits only a completed successful pull_request run of ci.yml whose head_sha is the queue commit's second parent and that retained ci-tested-tree-TREE-full-S-of-N records for every shard with TREE = the queue commit's tree; then the race invocation is omitted (static, interop, doc, artifact checks still run, go-product aggregates as in REUSE). A later entry whose tree includes a preceding entry differs and runs FULL. Pairs with V1-0760 (the main push reuses the queue run of the same commit, which needs merge_group shards to write the tested-tree record). Limit: AFP-V0-029 shadow rows (V1-0811) must take a REUSE queue run's outcomes from the reused pull_request run.
title: ci: a merge-queue run reuses the identical-tree pull-request result instead of repeating the race shards

acceptanceCriteria: Either the driver runs sharded with active test slices (focused test over a slices fixture) or V1-1315's cutover retires it and this ticket is closed as superseded with the merge named.
While unresolved, the ci.yml comment beside CORVINT_PR_TOOL_SOURCE states that the pin must stay empty while test-slices.json is non-empty.
body: Observed 2026-10-13 while planning the AFP-V0-029 shadow campaign (owner request: run only the needed tests). tools/corvint-pr-tests/main.go execute() calls refuseSlices(universe, shards) for every sharded run (`test-level slices are active (AFP-V0-041); the package-level driver refuses sharded execution`, exit 2). .github/cishards/test-slices.json has been non-empty since revision 3b428343 (internal/tasks/store named slices), so setting CORVINT_PR_TOOL_SOURCE in .github/workflows/ci.yml today would take the driver branch of the Go tests step on every PR shard and fail all eight shards; the shadow `corvint test --dry-run` step shares that pin. Expected: a pinned driver either executes the slices it refuses (whole packages first, then each slice, as the full branch does) or the shadow can be activated independently of the driver. Workaround chosen by lane CI-ROWS: a separate CORVINT_TEST_SHADOW_SOURCE pin that builds only cmd/corvint, keeping the driver inert. Resolution candidates: (a) teach the driver AFP-V0-041 slices (needed only if the driver remains the CI executor), or (b) retire the driver at the V1-1315 cutover to `corvint test` and close this as superseded. Related: V1-1315, V1-0811, V1-0812, decision 0488.
title: ci: corvint-pr-tests refuses sharded execution while AFP-V0-041 test slices are active, so CORVINT_PR_TOOL_SOURCE cannot be set

acceptanceCriteria: The stack-snapshot assertion in internal/contextindex/taskcontext_cancel_test.go no longer fails on a goroutine that has already closed its ready channel but not yet exited; `go test -count=200 -run TestTaskContextCancellationNeverReturnsAPacket ./internal/contextindex/` passes locally.
The product guarantee stays tested: no history or recency work runs after TaskContext returns, and a deliberately broken join still fails the test.
Record the hosted run id and the fix in the PR body; no spec change unless the test contract text in docs names the stack check.
body: Observed 2026-10-13 on hosted CI run 38476173623 (pull_request, PR beamfall/corvint#867 head 302f258fadd17989eebb12bdbb8aaeff34e15901, go-product-shard (7)), a PR that changes only .github/workflows/ci.yml, tools/ci-reuse-plan and docs. internal/contextindex TestTaskContextCancellationNeverReturnsAPacket/recency-on/lexical-term failed with `taskcontext_cancel_test.go:51: startContextRecency.func still running after TaskContext returned`; every other stage in both recency modes passed in the same run. Cause (inferred from source): recency.go startContextRecency runs `defer close(recency.ready); recency.read()` in a goroutine, and TaskContext's join awaits `ready`. The close happens inside the deferred call, so the goroutine's frame `startContextRecency.func1` can still appear in runtime.Stack for a few microseconds after await returns, although no further work runs. assertTaskContextReadersJoined takes one stack snapshot and fails on that transient frame. Expected: the assertion tolerates the goroutine's exit window (bounded poll of runtime.Stack, e.g. up to 100ms) or the reader signals completion as the goroutine's final statement in a way the test can observe deterministically; the product guarantee (no work after join) is unchanged. Actual: a false-positive FAIL costs a full go-product-shard rerun (~25 min) and blocks merge-queue throughput. Recovery used: `gh run rerun --failed`.
title: Flaky: TestTaskContextCancellationNeverReturnsAPacket sees startContextRecency.func after await returned

acceptanceCriteria: The cause is determined from the observer teardown order (zombie before reap versus a real survivor) and recorded in the ticket or a build-log entry
TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption distinguishes a reap-pending descendant from a surviving one, with a bounded wait, and passes 20 consecutive -race runs on hosted ubuntu
If a real leak is found, the observer kills its descendants before returning from an interrupted observation and a regression test covers it
body: Suspected flake, not a confirmed defect. Hosted CI run 38494366263 (PR beamfall/corvint#870, go-product-shard (6), ubuntu-24.04, go test -race -p 1 under test-confine) failed internal/appflows TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption: `observer_unix_test.go:83: descendant 64508 survived interruption` and `descendant 64515 survived interruption` (0.64s). The AFP-V0-047 outcomes rerun of the whole package passed at once (ci-outcomes-pull_request-6: rerun.state RAN, internal/appflows pass), and the PR touches no internal/appflows path. Expected: after cancel() returns through done, no observer descendant answers syscall.Kill(pid, 0). Actual: both descendants still answered. Inference (unverified): kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie until it is reaped, and the test checks immediately after the observation returns, so a descendant still in teardown or awaiting reap reads as survived; a bounded poll (for example up to 2s until Kill returns ESRCH) or reaping before the check would separate a real leak from the race. Reproduction: rerun the package under -race on a loaded ubuntu runner; local darwin runs did not reproduce in this session. Version: origin/main 5163d1ed4 plus PR #870 head c6fe57654.
title: Suspected flake: TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption reports descendants that survived interruption on hosted ubuntu (PR #870 shard 6)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec amendment (requirement IDs, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence, rollback) defines the declared string-keyed registry dialect and its configuration; lane requirements are accepted under the owner's standing auto-accept of 2026-10-11.
A change to one registered builder selects only the tests that pass its literal key, plus every caller with a non-literal key, which are flagged as unknowns; keys are never dropped silently.
A change to the registry file itself still selects every caller of the accessor.
The receipt shows the registry line and the call-site line for each selected test; focused and hostile tests plus sealed change evidence; GitHub #871 closed by the merged PR.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#871 (2026-10-14). impact on a builder module registered in an exported object literal (e.g. registry.ts `'ctx:club_with_two_courses': new ClubWithTwoCourses()`) returns only the changed path, registry.ts as a reverse import and unknowns dynamic-dispatch-unresolved, and no tests, because every spec reaches the registry through a data-provider fixture that takes a string key (createTestData('ctx:...')). Import closure then selects nothing (unsafe) or every spec (152/152 in the reporter's case, where one spec uses the key). Proposal: a narrow declared dialect: registry = exported object literal whose values are `new X()` or `X` of an imported binding -> key->module edges; call sites = literal string argument to an adopter-declared accessor -> test->key edges; impact on the module returns tests using its key with evidence lines for the registry entry and the call site; fail closed: a non-literal key at any accessor call site or a computed registry key is an unknown and widens selection to every caller of that accessor; configuration in a profile entry naming the registry export and accessor methods.
title: impact: resolve literal string-keyed registries (key -> module) to the tests that pass the key (GitHub #871)

acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec amendment (requirement IDs, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence, rollback) defines the application-marker declaration and the four classifications in the owning test-validity contract; lane requirements are accepted under the owner's standing auto-accept of 2026-10-11.
A control run whose target step passes and which carries no application marker is reported NOT-APPLIED, never as a pass or fail of the control, and the strength axis abstains for that control.
The report lists inert controls separately, and repeated NOT-APPLIED for the same control across revisions is flagged as a control defect.
Focused and hostile tests plus a real Playwright control run (or a bounded NOT_RUN reason) and sealed change evidence; GitHub #872 closed by the merged PR.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#872 (2026-10-14). A hand-authored negative control (e.g. a page.route handler that drops one item from a POST body, guarded by shape checks that fall back via route.fallback() and record an annotation when it fires) can be inert: when the real request has a different shape the guard always falls back, the perturbation never happens, the row assertion passes and the control run is green, which reads as 'control did not break the test' (a false strength claim or confusing non-result). The reporter caught one inert control across two revisions only with their own checker comparing 'row step passed' against 'applied annotation present'. Proposal: make 'the control took effect' a first-class axis: a control declares an application marker (annotation type or provider event); each control run is classified APPLIED-FAILED (valid control), APPLIED-EARLY-FAIL (an earlier step failed first), APPLIED-PASSED (assertion too weak) or NOT-APPLIED (inert), and NOT-APPLIED is never credited as strength or weakness; repeated NOT-APPLIED for the same control across revisions is flagged as a control defect; optionally record the observed request shape (keys only, no values) when a guarded handler falls back.
title: test-validity: report inert negative controls as NOT-APPLIED instead of crediting a passing control run (GitHub #872)

acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce first: a test builds an EvidenceReceipt through the real producer in which one attempt ends infrastructure-failed (for example a hook timeout under load) with HookProcess.StdoutSHA256 set and Receipt nil, and records whether VerifyReceipt refuses it. If the producer cannot emit that shape, retain the evidence and close this ticket as not a defect.

If confirmed: VerifyReceipt accepts a well-formed infrastructure-failed attempt whose retained stdout does not decode to a hook receipt, still binding the raw stdout bytes to StdoutSHA256, and still refuses KILLED or SURVIVED attempts without a decoded receipt.
Hostile tests show that a forged nil-Receipt attempt cannot carry a KILLED or SURVIVED verdict, and that a tampered raw-stdout byte still fails verification.
Spec text in the owning BBF spec states the infrastructure-failed attempt rule; focused tests, -race, and sealed change evidence are retained.
body: Suspected defect (not yet reproduced), reported by the V1-1366 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#875) on 2026-10-14 and read by the orchestrator at origin/main 92c298a6e. In internal/behaviorfalsify/receipt.go, VerifyReceipt (func at line 253) skips only attempts whose HookProcess.StdoutSHA256 is empty. Every attempt with retained stdout must have a raw attempt whose HookBytes decode to a HookReceipt with reflect.DeepEqual(a.Receipt, &hook) (line 303), and whose hook.Artifacts must equal a.RetainedArtifacts and declare the native SHA. An attempt that failed for infrastructure reasons but still retained stdout carries a nil Receipt, so DeepEqual(nil, &hook) is false and the whole receipt is refused as invalid. The lane observed that under host load (load average about 60) the live receipts it produced did not verify. Expected: an infrastructure-failed attempt is verifiable as such, with its stdout digest bound, and does not invalidate the receipt. Actual (as reported): the receipt is refused. Unconfirmed: whether the real producer emits stdout-plus-nil-Receipt attempts, and whether that was the actual cause of the observed refusals. Corvint main at 92c298a6e; host go1.27.2; darwin.
title: behaviorfalsify: suspected VerifyReceipt refusal of an infrastructure-failed attempt with retained stdout and nil Receipt

acceptanceCriteria: Decide and record (spec amendment or build-log decision) whether nested member order is normative; if it is, CEM-V1-109 is amended to state it.
If normative: one consumer is aligned, and a sealed vector compares the full rendered result bytes from both consumers, including nested drift, hunks and references.
If not normative: the packet text states that consumers must not depend on nested order, and a test shows the digest is independent of it.

body: Found by the V1-1333 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#879, seal 9eb1815c0) on 2026-10-14 while sealing protocol/cem-1.0/stable/citation-vectors. The native verifier (internal/cem) and the portable consumer (interop/cem01-go) agree on top-level result member order, on citation block bytes and on verdictSha256. They emit the nested members of drift, hunks and references in different orders. CEM-V1-109 (proposed in #879) states that nested order is not fixed, so the vectors compare only the digest and citation bytes. Two independent consumers whose rendered output differs byte-for-byte below the top level weaken the packet's 'reproduce byte for byte' claim and invite consumer-specific parsers. Related but distinct: V1-1289 (refusal-code divergence).
title: cem/1.0 consumers emit nested drift, hunks and references members in different orders

acceptanceCriteria: corpusindex.Open and doccorpus.ParseArtifact allocation no longer depends on the json/v2 pooled-encoder state: TotalAlloc across GOMAXPROCS=1, default and GOGC=10 runs varies by less than 10% (numbers retained), measured with the V1-0587 phase bracket

body: Found by the V1-0587 lane (PR #895, build log docs/build-log/2026-10-14-v1-0587-corpus-alloc-ceiling.md; darwin/arm64, Go 1.27.2). corpusindex.Open (about 658 MB of a 768 MB ordinary run) and doccorpus.ParseArtifact (110 to 270 MB) marshal the 30 to 35 MB corpus or index several times. Measured: one json/v2 Marshal of the 29.8 MB corpus costs 190,565,456 bytes (61 mallocs) on a cold pooled encoder versus 29,818,880 bytes (1 malloc) warm, and TotalAlloc moves in exact steps of that 160,746,576-byte difference. Whether the encoder is warm depends on GC count, the per-P pool slot and race-mode Put drops, so allocation varies with GOMAXPROCS, GOGC and -race: ordinary default 767.7 to 957.3 MB; GOGC=10 reached 1,115,746,416 bytes (over the 1 GiB test ceiling); hosted linux/amd64 race runs 1.09 to 1.41 GB. Expected: allocation roughly proportional to output size and stable across runtime settings. acceptanceCriteria: readRefsContext returns ctx.Err() whenever the context is done and the read ended in an error (e.g. prefer ctx.Err() in the done case when r.err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil), keeping the V1-1155 no-leak guarantees.

body: Observed 2026-10-15 on PR #920 CI (run 38761994872, job 116515913771, go-product-shard 7, linux): TestCompileRefsReadHonoursContext/V1-1155_cancellation_cleanup_survives_delayed_callback_dispatch failed with 'iteration 55 error=file already closed' (changes_test.go:388). PR #920 does not touch internal/upgradechanges. Cause (inferred from origin/main internal/upgradechanges/changes.go:648-701): on cancel, the AfterFunc callback closes the open descriptor; io.ReadAll then returns os.ErrClosed and the goroutine sends it on done. The final select has both done and ctx.Done ready and Go picks randomly, so the done case returns the close error instead of ctx.Err(). Expected: a cancelled read always returns context.Canceled. Actual: about 1 in a few hundred iterations returns 'file already closed'.
title: upgradechanges readRefsContext: cancellation can return 'file already closed' instead of context.Canceled (CI flake in TestCompileRefsReadHonoursContext)

acceptanceCriteria: the #945 repro (require() entry) selects the spec passing its key or widens every caller with registry-key-unresolved; it never returns no test rows
a test reproduces the fail-open case on BASE and passes after the fix; one mutation restoring the fail-open path fails it
non-go-impact-v0 states the rule and the issue is closed with the fixing PR
body: GitHub #945 (owner, build main-253d634, rc.3). With --language-profile non-go-syntax-v0 and a declared string-key-registry/0 registry, a module reached only through require() inside a registry entry arrow gets only the path row and dynamic-dispatch-unresolved: no reverse-import, no test rows, no registry-key-unresolved. Selection fails open, contrary to NGI-V0-010; the dynamic import() form already fails closed (registry-key-unresolved, callers widened at 600). Expected: when a declared registry has any unresolved entry, registry-key-unresolved and the widening apply to every JS/TS changed path, as registry-export-unresolved already does; a require() inside an entry is a module reference the reverse-import rules can see. Repro fixture in the issue. Code: internal/contextindex/registry_dialect.go.
title: impact: registry module reached only by a lazy require() in an entry selects no tests and emits no registry-key-unresolved (GitHub #945)

acceptanceCriteria: each listed lazy entry form resolves key -> module and selects only the specs passing that key, with a test per form
a non-exported const registry named by the declaration and read through a declared accessor resolves, or the spec records why it stays refused
NGI-V0 rows amended or added (new IDs checked for collisions); the issue is closed with the PR
body: GitHub #946 (owner, feature request on the #871 dialect, V1-1365). NGI-V0-008 accepts only X, ns.X, new X(), new ns.X() of a static import, so lazy entries are registry-key-unresolved (import()) or invisible (require(), see #945), and a non-exported const registry read through an exported accessor is refused. Request: an arrow entry whose body is new (require(S).X)(), new (require(S).default)(), require(S).X, or import(S).then(...) with S a closed string literal is an edge to S under the existing reverse-import rules; optionally accept a non-exported const registry when the declaration names it. Motivation: lazy registries cut median spec import closure ~270 -> ~175 files in one real suite.
title: impact: string-key-registry dialect resolves lazy loader entries (require()/import() inside an arrow) and accessor-read non-exported registries (GitHub #946)

acceptanceCriteria: the #947 repro selects only tests/alpha.spec.ts for src/contexts/alpha.ts with accessor-key-nonliteral count 0
shadowed, let/var-bound, reassigned or template-with-substitution identifiers stay non-literal, with tests
NGI-V0 rule recorded; the issue is closed with the PR
body: GitHub #947 (owner, feature request on the #871 dialect, V1-1365). createTestData(SCENARIO_CONTEXT) with const SCENARIO_CONTEXT = 'ctx:delta' at top level of the same spec is accessor-key-nonliteral, which widens every caller at 600 for every key; in one real suite ~60 of 165 non-inline calls use this form, so the dialect never narrows there. Multi-line and generic-call literals already resolve. Request: when the first argument is an identifier bound by a top-level const NAME = '<closed literal>' (or substitution-free template) in the same file with no reassignment possible, treat it as that literal key. Imported consts are out of scope.
title: impact: string-key-registry dialect reads a same-file top-level const string as a literal accessor key (GitHub #947)

acceptanceCriteria: the Playwright producer retains registered route patterns with per-test hit counts (or records NOT_PRODUCED when it cannot)

body: GitHub #948 (owner, build main-253d634). A page.route handler registered for a resource the app fetches server-side never runs, so the test passes on unmocked data while readers assume the mock fixes the input; in the reported case it hid an order-dependent assertion. The test-validity-v0 conformance vectors have no stub/route code today; #872 (V1-1366) covers inert negative controls only. Request: an optional producer-side record of each registered route pattern and its per-test hit count (behaviour-events / navigation-events producers could carry it), and a test-validity finding (e.g. stub-never-matched) for a passing test whose stub had zero hits, naming the pattern and the registration line. Stubs registered only on a control path stay out of scope.
title: test-validity: report a request stub (Playwright page.route/context.route) that never matched during a passing run (GitHub #948)

The owner pre-approved raising the full-gate timeout (2026-10-15), but the store policy cannot express it: internal/tasks/intent/policy.go bounds gate timeoutSeconds by wire.MaxGateTimeoutSecs = 120*60 (internal/tasks/wire/limits.go:105). Expected: a gate timeout bound large enough for the full gate on a loaded host, kept inside the lease/heartbeat and detach bounds (attempt_run maxRunTimeoutSeconds = MaxLeaseMinutes*60-130). Actual: 7200 s hard cap; every full-gate ticket (V1-0252..0255, V1-0414, V1-0150, V1-0285) stalls while lanes run.

acceptanceCriteria: a documented operator path produces a consistent store snapshot while writers may be active (or refuses with a named quiesce requirement), with a test

body: Observed 2026-10-16, corvint-tasks build 558, during the V1-1459 lane (qualify CAL-V0-017 on a copied store). (2) A fresh copy: every read refused UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM because head.primaryWorktree is /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint, differing from the copy's path ('repository relocation is unsupported in this preview'). Expected: an operator can produce a consistent, isolated copy of a store for off-path qualification or recovery drills (quiesced export/snapshot plus an explicit relocate/rebind step), without editing head.json. Actual: no supported path; V1-1459's acceptance criteria cannot be met as written.
