acceptanceCriteria: ticket create reports an existing open ticket with identical title, body and acceptance criteria (warning or refusal with an explicit override), with a test
the behaviour is specified in the Tasks spec
body: Observed 2026-10-16 (build 558). V1-1282 (created 2026-10-12T02:30:34Z) and V1-1283 (15 s later) have byte-identical title, body, acceptanceCriteria and dependencies; V1-1283 was delivered and completed, V1-1282 stayed OPEN in the v1-0 milestone until a lane spent ~50 min re-auditing it, then it was archived as a duplicate. Likely a retried create with a fresh --request-id. Expected: create warns or refuses (named code, override flag) when an open ticket has identical title+body+acceptanceCriteria, or search exposes a content digest so filers can deduplicate cheaply. Actual: silent duplicate.
title: corvint-tasks ticket create accepts a content-identical ticket under a new ID (V1-1282 duplicated V1-1283)

acceptanceCriteria: batch-check over a branch that merged main containing an unsealed main-side commit either passes with that commit reported as main-admitted, or the carry convention is changed so such commits are sealed; test reproduces the 13e1b26d8 case
docs/DOGFOOD.md states which BASE a merged-forward lane uses and how main-side commits are treated
body: Observed 2026-10-16 in the #941 merge-forward lane (head a9a779e7a). `dogfood-batch-check` from a fresh clone against the lane BASE 257bea097 (merge-base with main) failed unbound-commits for 13e1b26d8 'Carry Tasks policy v11 (full-gate reusable) to main' (parent 85ba6321a), a commit on origin/main with no sealed CEM (policy-carry PRs ship without one by convention). Against BASE=f81114713 (the merge's main parent) the check passed (constituents=4, commits=14). Every lane that merges current main and checks against its original base will hit this. Related but distinct: V1-1208 (retroactive bindings). Expected: either main-side commits already admitted to main are not re-required by a branch's batch-check, or policy-carry commits carry a sealed CEM (or a recorded exemption class). Actual: unbound-commits refusal for a commit the branch did not author.
title: dogfood-batch-check fails unbound-commits on any branch that merges main past the unsealed policy-carry commit 13e1b26d8

acceptanceCriteria: the failure path reads the child output only after Wait returns or through a synchronized writer
a forced failure of the test under -race reports no data race (one mutation proving the check bites)
body: Residual from the V1-1353 lane (PR #950, merge-base 883caa3d2, 2026-10-16). Under go test -race on internal/tasks/store, when TestPSRForegroundSignals takes its failure path, internal/tasks/store/pool_sweep_test.go:137 reads the child process output buffer while the os/exec copier goroutine is still writing it; the race detector reports it. Related: V1-1000 (the same test fails under load); this ticket is the race in the failure-reporting path, distinct from the load failure. Expected: the test waits for the command (or uses a synchronized buffer) before reading output. Actual: unsynchronized read, -race report.
title: tests: data race in TestPSRForegroundSignals failure path (pool_sweep_test.go:137 reads the child output buffer while os/exec still writes it)

acceptanceCriteria: the qualification procedure (DOGFOOD/SELF-DEVELOPMENT or the packet README) requires retaining result digests and the per-case table in the build-log entry at run time
the S0E packet runner prints a retained-evidence summary (digests, case outcomes, toolchain, host) suitable for pasting, with a test
body: Residual from the V1-0650 lane (PR #951, 2026-10-16). The 2026-10-02 S0E packet runs (Go 1.24.13 cases 21-22, Linux arm64 54/56) wrote their result JSON under /private/tmp; on 2026-10-16 only two empty cache directories remained and no go1.24.13 toolchain was on disk, so V1-0650 AC1/AC2 rest on the ticket body and build-log prose, not retained artifacts. title: Qualification runs write result JSON only under /private/tmp; lanes lose the artifacts that AC evidence cites

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-batch-check accepts a merge whose only non-derivable path is a declared generated file reproduced byte-identically by its declared generator at the merge tree, with a test; or docs/DOGFOOD.md documents the pre-push recipe and dogfood-change warns before push
a hostile test: a hand-edited generated file at a merge still fails merge-resolution-unbound
body: Observed 2026-10-16 on PR #952 (V1-1460, head 028f6f3f9, BASE b1ee552b3). The lane merged origin/main after #941 landed; the only conflict was the generated docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv, resolved with `make spec-requirements`. dogfood-batch-check from a fresh clone failed merge-resolution-unbound count=1 at the merge (git cannot re-derive the file from the two parents). The suggested repair (redo the merge with -X ours/theirs and commit the regeneration as its own sealed change) rewrites a pushed branch, so the orchestrator had to open a replacement PR. This recurs whenever two lanes add requirement rows (#927, #952). Expected: either batch-check recognizes a generated file whose content equals the generator's output at the merge tree (declared generator, e.g. make spec-requirements) as a derivable resolution, or the lane charter/DOGFOOD documents the -X theirs + separate regeneration recipe at merge time so the failure is caught before push. Actual: unbound, repair needs a new branch.
title: dogfood-batch-check: a merge of main whose only conflict is a generated file (REQUIREMENTS.tsv) is merge-resolution-unbound; the only repair rewrites the pushed branch

acceptanceCriteria: every store-mutating command accepts --lock-wait with the same semantics and bounds as claim, or the Tasks spec names each exception and why
help text and a table-driven test cover the flag on each mutating command
body: Observed 2026-10-16 (build 558). With ~15 orchestrator closeouts running at once, claims hit LOCK_TIMEOUT on taskman.prepare.lock (30 s preparation acquisition, e.g. PR #941's V1-1331 claim). claim, release, renew, submit and attempt heartbeat accept --lock-wait SECONDS; complete, widen, gate run, ticket create, ticket refine, ticket note set, ticket archive and policy update reject it ('unknown flag --lock-wait'), so a supervisor must wrap them in its own retry loop with fresh request IDs. Related: V1-1130 (pool acquire), V1-1150 (pool sweep/reap decision).
title: corvint-tasks: --lock-wait missing on complete, widen, gate run, ticket create/refine/note set/archive and policy update

acceptanceCriteria: the owner decides whether ARTIFACT-V0-008 covers every workflow (with a declared per-job exception list) or stays ci.yml-only; the decision is recorded
if widened: the check covers all .github/workflows/*.yml, the nightly-failure-signal exception is declared, and a mutation (workflow-level issues: write) fails it
body: Residual from the V1-1114 lane (PR #954). The new nightly-failure-signal job in .github/workflows/release-gates.yml is the only job holding issues: write; its permissions are pinned by TestSOPV0013WorkflowBinding, but script/check-ci-least-privilege.sh (ARTIFACT-V0-008) covers ci.yml only, so release-gates.yml and other workflows have no general least-privilege check. Widening the check amends accepted ARTIFACT-V0-008, so it needs an owner decision.
title: Question: extend the CI least-privilege check (ARTIFACT-V0-008) beyond ci.yml to release-gates.yml with a per-job exception list?

title: Suspected: portable legacy verify-stable refuses corvint-sized repositories with unsupported-resource-limit while verify-stable-canonical accepts them

Not covered: (1) routes registered on contexts created with browser.newContext() (only the fixture page/context are wrapped); (2) page.routeWebSocket; (3) routeFromHAR is not separately qualified; (4) when no attempt in a receipt has a corvint-route-stubs record (producer not installed) the routeStubs member is omitted to keep legacy bytes identical, which the spec defines as NOT_PRODUCED, but no per-test explicit reason is emitted. Owner decision bundled here: carrying the record on the /0-/3 external receipt profiles needs a new profile revision. Control-path stubs (#872) stay out of scope.

acceptanceCriteria: Precondition recorded first: V1-1337's prospective run reads 'improve' (authored excess lower bound above 2.5% and above the grep bot); if it reads 'kill' or 'inconclusive', this ticket closes with a recorded decision not to pursue that cites that run.

A labelled held-out set of (hunk, basis) support pairs from at least one non-Corvint repository is committed with its labelling protocol, labeller identity and partition before any rank statistic is computed on it.

Per-basis rank against K deterministic null spans seeded by patchSha256 and the BH-corrected per-hunk fraction at a stated q are computed on the held-out set, with K chosen so the minimum p-value 1/(K+1) is below the BH threshold for the set size, and compared with human labels (precision and recall of BH discoveries).

Outcome recorded in a build-log entry: either proposed CEM-V1 requirements for a consumer report axis (byte-identical across native and portable consumers, no verdict) or a decision not to pursue with the measured precision.
body: Source: docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md ("Seeded K-null permutation rank is post-rc.3 pending a held-out set"; decision 0523 P0 ships the deterministic cyclic-shift null instead), V1-1268, and the V1-1268 disposition (docs/build-log/2026-10-16-cem-post-rc3-disposition.md, origin/main a0b4c4108). Item: per-basis specificity rank against K deterministic null spans seeded by patchSha256, with a BH-corrected per-hunk fraction, as a consumer report axis. Measurement that sets the gate: tools/cem-citation-baseline already runs a seeded derangement null (DCW-V0-053, N=200 per map, seed patchSha256); on the post-S3 corpus (docs/build-log/2026-10-13-v1-1278-post-s3-citation-baseline.md) authored excess is 1.94% [1.53%, 2.34%] against 67.1% for the grep bot; a per-hunk rank keeps per-observation null information the pooled excess discards, but whether it tracks real support needs labels. The item needs (a) V1-1337 to show authored citations beat mechanical producers and (b) external labelled data this repository cannot supply. No rc.3 artifact advertises it (grep recorded in the disposition entry).
title: cem/1.0: per-basis specificity rank against seeded null spans with a BH per-hunk fraction, gated on V1-1337 and a labelled held-out set

acceptanceCriteria: each of the three shapes has a fixture that either selects the reached test or widens with a named reason
a shape that changes accepted NGI-V0-008 behaviour is recorded as an owner decision before it lands

shape (1), an accessor inside a template-literal ${...}, also has a corvint tests setup-select fixture with a TSA-V0 trace row, because setup-select and impact share registryCallSites (registry_dialect.go:642) (absorbs archived duplicate V1-1717)

Each may select fewer tests than a change reaches (fail-open, invariant 2): (1) an accessor call inside a template-literal substitution `${registry[key]()}` is invisible to the reader; (2) writes to the registry object after its declaration (registry.k = ..., Object.assign) are not observed; (3) under accepted NGI-V0-008, eager `new X(args)` entry arguments can reference other modules that are not followed. Suspected, not reproduced as live selection misses. Expected: each either resolves or widens with a named reason.
title: Suspected impact fail-opens in the JS/TS registry reader: accessor in a template substitution, registry writes after declaration, eager new X(args) reaching other modules

acceptanceCriteria: spec and code agree on the languages registry-export-unresolved covers, with a Ruby fixture pinning the choice

acceptanceCriteria: a line shift in a file cited from docs/RELEASE-NOTES-*.md fails make line-citations-check locally, proven by a mutation
DCG-V0-001's document set in the spec matches the checked set

Expected: the local doc gate reports the drift. Fix options: add release-notes files to the DCG-V0-001 document set, or a check that every `path:a-b@hash` anchor in tracked docs still resolves. Related but distinct: V1-0237 (BUILD-LOG citation shifts).
title: line-citations-check does not cover docs/RELEASE-NOTES-*.md: a cited-file line shift passes every local doc gate and fails only in CI

acceptanceCriteria: reproduce on a quiet host and under load with retained timings, or record that it does not reproduce
the handoff deadline or the exec environment cause is identified, and the test passes 3/3 under load ~60 without relaxing the cancellation assertion
body: Observed by the V1-1023/1024 lane (PR #962, head e8f97a3cf, 2026-10-16) on darwin, load 65-84, go1.27.x: `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=3 -run TestTrustedNavCancellation ./internal/doccompiler/` failed 3/3 in 10.2 s with "timed out waiting for PID handoff at .../grandchild.pid: no such file or directory". The branch does not touch internal/doccompiler. The same script shape run by hand from a temp dir wrote the PID file promptly. Suspected: the 3 s handoff deadline under load, or an exec-environment/sandbox difference. Not reproduced on a quiet host. Suspected defect, not confirmed. Related load class: V1-1446, V1-1353's load flakes.
title: tests (suspected): internal/doccompiler TestTrustedNavCancellation times out on PID handoff under load

the package finishes inside its budget at load ~60, or the slowest tests are split/parallelized with the measurement retained; no assertion weakened

The guard lane (#961) also could not finish the whole package inside its window. Same load class as V1-1446 (tools/corvint-pr-tests). Suspected, not confirmed on a quiet host.
title: tests (suspected): internal/dogfoodflow package exceeds the 30m package timeout under load ~68

acceptanceCriteria: a run killed at the per-run limit reports a detail that names the timeout and the limit
a regression test pins the detail; a mutation that drops it fails the test
body: Found by the V1-0547 spike (PR #963, head a8d56d3be, 2026-10-16). When the mutation runner kills a run at its per-run limit, the witness detail reads `run ended without a verdict` (the V1-0651 generic form). Expected: a detail naming the per-run timeout and its limit, so the operator can tell a timeout from a sandbox denial or a crash. Reproduction: the V1-0547 test at a 5 m wall time on a loaded host (lane log agent-spikes/0547-mut-5m-default.log under the session scratchpad). Related: V1-0651 (completed; named sandbox-exec denials), V1-0547.
title: mutate: a per-run timeout kill is reported as "run ended without a verdict" instead of naming the timeout

acceptanceCriteria: the cold build is excluded from (or separately budgeted outside) the per-mutant limit, with retained cold/warm timings
a regression shows a loaded host no longer produces a not-run on the first mutant solely from the cold build
body: Found by the V1-0547 spike (PR #963, 2026-10-16). The per-run limit is wall time / (maxMutants+1), and each discrimination request starts with an empty build cache, so its first `go test` builds cold: 74.5 s cold vs 6.5 s warm at load ~60. The old 42.9 s per-run limit killed that run before a verdict. #963 fixed the test's budget; the product still charges the cold build to one mutant's run. Expected: the cold build is either done once before the per-run budget starts or budgeted separately, with the cost reported.
title: mutate: the per-run limit also covers the request's first cold build, so loaded runs time out before any test executes

acceptanceCriteria: a preflight detects the enclosing-sandbox refusal once and the request reports it as one supported-limit reason
no mutant ever runs unsandboxed; a test pins both
body: Found by the V1-0547 spike (PR #963, 2026-10-16). HostSandbox only looks up /usr/bin/sandbox-exec. Inside a nested `codex sandbox -P :workspace`, sandbox-exec exits 71 and every run reports `mutate: sandbox unavailable: the host refused to apply the sandbox-exec profile` (TCQ-V0-059 / V1-0651 supported limit). Expected: a single preflight that detects the nested refusal up front and reports one not-run reason, instead of spending each run on it. Enforcement must not be relaxed.
title: mutate: HostSandbox has no nesting check, so an enclosing sandbox's refusal surfaces only as per-run not-runs

acceptanceCriteria: TestCALV0232 duration measured on a quiet host and at load ~60 with retained numbers
either fixed to finish well inside budget under load or closed as a duplicate of the measured cause

acceptanceCriteria: the fixture controls os.TempDir() on every supported GOOS, or the Unix-only scope is recorded in CEM-V1-240
body: Recorded by the #961 Codex round (P3, 2026-10-16). CEM-V1-240's refusal now compares by file identity, which also fixes Windows cross-drive paths, but the fixture sets only TMPDIR, which does not control os.TempDir() on Windows (TMP/TEMP/USERPROFILE). Latent because the stable verifier refuses non-Unix hosts. Expected: either the fixture sets the Windows variables or the spec records the Unix-only scope.
title: tests: the TMPDIR-only refusal fixture does not control os.TempDir() on Windows (latent)

acceptanceCriteria: the owner chooses (a) or (b) and the decision is recorded
the chosen option is implemented with a regression (b) or documented in docs/DOGFOOD.md (a)
body: From the V1-0493 spike (PR #963, 2026-10-16). After `dogfood-seal`, `status` offers `verify`, which clears the terminal record and leads to a finish that cannot succeed; the worktree stays held until `cancel`, which records non-success over a completion that did succeed. Options: (a) document that the enrolled workflow ends at the bind commit and a sealed worktree needs a fresh worktree for the next enrollment; (b) add a sealed-terminal state with a `workflow-sealed` no-action reason, admitted only for a same-blob rename of the bound CEM, amending accepted LCP-V0-002, 003 and 020. (b) amends accepted requirements, so it is outside the standing auto-accept and needs the owner.
title: Question: should a sealed dogfood enrollment end at the bind commit (a) or gain a sealed-terminal state (b)?

acceptanceCriteria: witnessResolves rejects a DEPENDENCY_PATH whose consecutive Via units are not graph edges
a forged-edge fixture case fails before the change and passes after; a mutation dropping the edge check fails it

body: From GitHub beamfall/corvint#967 (2026-10-16). On a real queue (~42,000 receipts, ~600 MB state, ~15 concurrent writers) writers wait up to 3.5 min and fail LOCK_TIMEOUT at ~150/h; every timeout names the preparation gate (taskman.prepare.lock), never the writer lock. Over 12 h the gate made no progress for >=45 s while writers queued on 120 occasions (172 min, 24% of wall time). Fast-route heartbeat/renew hold 0.47-0.70 s; complete-route verbs (pool acquire/prepare/observe/release/cleanup/recover, reap, widen, submit, complete) run the complete audit from receipt 1 inside the gate, refusals included, landing a median 42-52 s after the previous commit; 73% of writes are heartbeat/renew queued behind them. Code refs at 05be582: internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:323 (gate held across writer route and prepareLease; audit 153-176; handoff scan 263-266); writer_route.go:159-168; journal/audit.go:296; store/lease.go:66-98,218-225 (inline reap via complete route); pool_commands.go:274; store/writer_checkpoint.go:374,387-427 (>=512 receipts: caller-side complete audit abandoned on SNAPSHOT_MOVED); journal/writer_checkpoint.go:40,522 (4,096-receipt cliff), 48-50; cli/lease.go:69-73 (reap has no --lock-wait). Also observed locally by the orchestrator on 2026-10-16: repeated LOCK_TIMEOUT on taskman.prepare.lock during claim/submit/ticket create with ~5 concurrent closeouts. Proposed (issue order): 1 no complete-history work while holding the gate (serve pool/reap/widen from the writer checkpoint or prepare optimistically outside the gate; decide refusals from the checkpoint first); 2 incremental single-owner checkpoint refresh tolerating appends, remove the WriterFullBound cliff; 3 bound per-write payload/history (receipts carry deltas or refs, no unchanged post-images); 4 isolate liveness writes from complete-route transactions; 5 operability (--lock-wait on reap, report the gate holder in status/doctor, opt-in --timing). Related: V1-0916 (writer refresh audit in caller), V1-1468 (--lock-wait gaps), V1-1150 (reap/sweep --lock-wait), V1-0803 (SNAPSHOT_MOVED questions), closed GitHub #494, #545.
title: corvint-tasks: lease writes serialize behind a preparation gate held during complete-history audits, so ~15 writers hit LOCK_TIMEOUT ~150/h (GitHub #967)

body: Observed 2026-10-16 08:42 (orchestrator, Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 0, Claude Code Stop and UserPromptSubmit hooks in /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint): the hooks repeatedly fail open with corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-deadline. The notice says the usual causes are a large uncommitted set or heavy load and that it 'did not measure either', then tells the user to run git status. Measured at the same time: `git status --short` returned 4,820 paths in 0.37 s real, and the load average was 64.57/96.45/69.59 (5 builder lanes plus closeout gates). So the cause was host load, not the dirty set, but the user cannot tell that from the notice and may be steered toward committing or stashing load-bearing state. Expected: the fallback reports cheap measurements it already has or can take within its budget (elapsed time per phase, the 1-minute load average where available, the dirty path count when the status probe finished), and names the dominant cause. Actual: two unmeasured guesses. This is the same failure class as V1-1120/V1-1422/V1-1280 (all completed); fail-open is correct, so this is a diagnosis gap, not a correctness bug.
title: Hooks: dogfood-event-deadline fallback should report the measured cause (host load, dirty path count) instead of naming two guesses

acceptanceCriteria: An accepted spec defines the hunk classes, the exact equivalence test for NON_SEMANTIC, and the UNCLASSIFIED fallback.
For Go files, a hunk that changes only comments or whitespace is reported NON_SEMANTIC; any token change outside comments (including build tags and //go: directives) is not.
Unsupported languages, parse failures and generated files are reported UNCLASSIFIED with a reason, never NON_SEMANTIC.
The reviewer report shows the class per hunk; tests cover comment-only, directive-change, mixed and unparsable fixtures.
body: Idea source: Anthropic engineering post 'Redesigning source control' (anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control), reviewed 2026-10-16. Idea only; no text copied. Scion's approval rules distinguish comment-only changes from sensitive logic changes, and reviewers concentrate on change intent. Corvint's reviewer report and CEM give every hunk the same review weight; there is no deterministic class for comment-only, whitespace-only or doc-string-only hunks. Idea: a deterministic, language-aware (Go first) hunk classifier that marks a hunk NON_SEMANTIC only when the parsed AST/token stream outside comments is byte-identical between base and head, recorded in the reviewer report (and, if accepted, as a CEM field) with an explanation. Missing parser support or any ambiguity yields UNCLASSIFIED, never NON_SEMANTIC (invariant 2). Project-owned authority decides what a class permits; the classifier itself grants no approval (invariant 3). Related: V1-0195 hunk-anchored review projection, V1-0820 project-owned reviewer rubric. Needs a spec (requirements, failure modes, rollback) before implementation.
title: cem report: classify comment-only and other non-semantic hunks so review effort and approval rules can differ by change class

acceptanceCriteria: Each spec governing affected ranges, CEM base/head ranges and Tasks claim bases states whether it assumes a first-parent/trunk-based history.

body: Idea source: Anthropic engineering post 'Redesigning source control' (anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control), reviewed 2026-10-16. Idea only; no text copied. Scion stores each changeset relative to its first parent and states that this assumes trunk-based development. Corvint makes the same assumption implicitly: `corvint affected --base`, CEM base..head ranges, AFP qualification counting first-parent commits on main (V1-0039), and the Tasks recovery that re-claims at `merge^1` after a merged-forward branch. None of the governing specs states the assumption or what happens on a non-linear base (octopus merge, merge from a side branch, base not an ancestor of head). Idea: one sentence-level statement in each governing spec plus the documented refusal or uncertainty when the assumption fails.
title: docs: state the first-parent / trunk-based history assumption behind affected --base, CEM ranges and Tasks re-claim at merge^1

body: Source: GitHub trending review 2026-10-16 (idea only; nothing was adopted or measured). Prior art: mksglu/context-mode captures structured events through PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hooks (file edits, user corrections, tool calls the user denied, error then fix sequences, blockers, environment changes), snapshots them at PreCompact, and restores a bounded digest at SessionStart. Corvint today re-pins authority at compaction (V1-0094, kernel/CKN-V0) and plans ticket-level resume context (V1-0472) and checkpoint handoff qualification (V1-0473), but nothing retains the session's own working state, such as rejected approaches and user corrections, across compaction. Constraints: invariant 4 (reads do not mutate; any new ledger needs its own bounded private writer spec in the SOL-V0 family and must never feed ranking, evidence or authority); invariant 5 (secret screening before retention); invariant 7 (no database service; context-mode uses SQLite FTS5, so Corvint would need an append-only bounded file). Overlap check: V1-0472, V1-0473, V1-0094 cover adjacent but distinct scope.
title: Idea: hook-captured session working state that survives compaction (decisions, rejected approaches, error-to-fix pairs)

acceptanceCriteria: Spike defines which quantities are directly countable from existing local ledgers (packet bytes, planned versus unplanned reads, surprise) and which need a counterfactual, marking the latter NOT_OBSERVED.

body: Source: GitHub trending review 2026-10-16 (idea only; nothing was adopted or measured). Prior art: xerj-org/xerj ships `xerj gain`, which reports what the tool saved, described as counted rather than estimated, and context-mode ships `ctx_stats`, which covers data avoided and cache hits. Corvint retains self-observations (`corvint observations`) and has cost gates in harness trials (V1-0369, V1-0742, V1-0777), but an operator has no direct report of what Corvint packets displaced in a real session: packet bytes delivered versus files the agent would otherwise read, and the files it read anyway (reads / unplanned-reads ledger). The report must abstain where a counterfactual cannot be observed, rather than invent a savings figure (invariant 2).
title: Idea: counted per-session context-savings report (bytes and tokens avoided, measured not estimated)

acceptanceCriteria: Spike defines the input shapes (host transcript formats), the friction classes it detects, and the secret-screen and byte bounds.

body: Source: GitHub trending review 2026-10-16 (idea only; nothing was adopted or measured). Prior art: obra/superpowers ships a 'figure out what went wrong' skill that reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report. The owner's standing instruction asks agents to file friction, bugs and missing capabilities automatically, yet filing depends on the agent noticing at the time. A post-mortem pass over a finished Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode transcript could propose deduplicated agent-memory tickets: Corvint fallbacks such as dogfood-event-deadline, refused Tasks mutations, repeated failed commands, and packet misses that the agent then grepped for. Each proposal carries transcript line citations and is secret-screened. Proposals only; filing stays an explicit Tasks mutation. Transcripts are untrusted model and host output, per V1-0712.
title: Idea: transcript post-mortem that turns a misbehaving agent session into evidence-cited tickets

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#982 (2026-10-16). One real queue over 18 days: heartbeat 16,925 receipts/172 MB, renew 9,249/88 MB, of 627 MB total store; 61% of receipts and 67% of receipt bytes are liveness, each with its own request file. No retention/compaction/prune path exists; hand deletion breaks the hash chain (JOURNAL_FORKED). Complete audits replay from receipt 1, so lock hold and LOCK_TIMEOUT scale with journal size (#967 / V1-1494). Related: V1-0887 (heartbeats and renews must cost O(1), GitHub #642). Proposed options in the issue: (1) liveness in a fenced lease table outside the audited journal; (2) coalesce superseded liveness on segment seal with a verifiable dropped-range hash; (3) retention policy with default unchanged; (4) drop per-receipt request copies for liveness verbs after commit. Sequence after V1-1494 (same packages).

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#984 (2026-10-16, one real program at 253d634). The work-state command's interpreter was removed from the host; every tick logged `alert work state command: fork/exec ...: no such file or directory` (22 alerts in ~20 min), but `dispatch status` (20 KB) has no provider-health field and nothing was escalated. During the window a no-progress cooldown was charged to a ticket (1 of 4 before parking). Recovery was immediate when the interpreter returned. body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#994. roster.go sorts matching candidates ascending by role priority, so the lowest value wins; Role.Priority in internal/tasks/dispatch/config.go:208 does not say so and config validation (config.go:524) does not warn. Repro: broad role worker priority 50 match states [work]; specific role special priority 92 match idGlob T-001[0-4] states [work]; T-0011 launches under worker with no warning. Fix: document lower-wins on Role.Priority, the config reference and the dispatch spec; emit a deterministic warning at config validation and in dispatch status when a role with narrowing (idGlob etc.) is always beaten by a role whose match is a superset with a lower priority value (conservative superset check, no false positives); optionally show the winning role per ticket. Ordering semantics must not change.
title: dispatch: role priority is lower-wins but undocumented; a narrower role can be silently shadowed by a broader lower-value role (#994)

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded decision chooses the remedy (per-spec sharding, uncommitted derived index with CI check, or another) with its effect on spec-requirements-check, specindex tests and agent read routes.

body: Observed 2026-10-16 on beamfall/corvint#961 (V1-1449 et al.): added to the merge queue five times (13:12, 14:41, 18:03, 19:55 UTC) and removed each time without a single merge_group CI run (13:12:02 -> 13:12:17; 19:55 -> 20:13:27 when main moved). git merge-tree against origin/main shows the textual conflict in docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv every time another PR adding requirements lands first; on the same afternoon #985, #991 and #993 went DIRTY the same way (INDEX.json, README.md, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, plus delivery-status lines in docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md), and GitHub disarmed their auto-merge. Each repair costs a merge commit, a regeneration, a push and a full CI run while Actions runs ~2 concurrent runs. Expected: two PRs that add requirements to different specs (or different sections) merge in either order without a textual conflict in generated files. Actual: any two spec-touching PRs conflict on the generated files. Options to evaluate: shard the generated index per spec (one generated file per spec), stop committing derived files and check them in CI only, or make rows order/line-stable so appends from different specs land on different lines. Spec delivery-status lines that every lane appends to are a second, smaller hotspot.

acceptanceCriteria: A call that outlives its caller still commits exactly once.
Repeated attach calls are idempotent.

body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1005 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Under load claim/pool acquire can outlive the host's per-tool-call limit (~120 s); the caller cannot tell whether the mutation committed. Proposal: --detach starts the mutation in its own process session under the request id and returns a handle; --attach/--wait N returns CLAIMED, PENDING or the verbatim refusal; same holder+request id never starts a second mutation. See beamfall/corvint#1005 for the full problem, current workaround and proposal.
title: corvint-tasks: claim / pool acquire --detach and --attach so a slow mutation survives the caller's tool-call timeout (issue #1005)

acceptanceCriteria: A worker that makes no queue calls for several lease periods keeps its attempt.
An idle or hung worker is not kept alive past maxIdleSeconds.
A fenced attempt stops renewal without error spam.
Renewal is skipped when the lease already covers the interval.
dispatch status shows keeper state per worker.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1006 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. A dispatched session can go many minutes without a queue verb; its lease expires and the attempt is fenced or reaped. Proposal: per-role dispatch option keepLease {intervalSeconds, leaseMinutes, maxIdleSeconds}; renew only for live, non-idle workers at the same generation, only when due; log renew/stop events. Related: V1-1313 (renew vs heartbeat), V1-0625 (holder liveness). See beamfall/corvint#1006 for the full problem, current workaround and proposal.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch: keep the lease of a live dispatched worker's attempt fresh (keepLease) (issue #1006)

acceptanceCriteria: The estimate and its age appear in dispatch status.

Proposal: per-role context {warnTokens, handoffTokens, hardTokens}; the dispatcher reads usage from recognised host event streams, exposes warn/handoff notices to the worker, and past hard releases the attempt with a clean HANDOFF and stops the worker. See beamfall/corvint#1007 for the full problem, current workaround and proposal.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch: per-role context-size warn/handoff/hard thresholds for running sessions (issue #1007)

acceptanceCriteria: Crash or reap frees slots without operator action.

body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1008 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Pools' quarantine/health/confirm-safe cycle is overhead for a scarce stateless resource (host CPU/browser capacity). Proposal: a named slots resource of capacity N; holders acquire 1..N bound to an attempt or run, released explicitly or on attempt end/reap, no quarantine; exclusive request blocks new shared grants; per-class reservation; waiters ordered by ticket priority. Related: V1-0785 (HELD pool waitlist), V1-0786. See beamfall/corvint#1008 for the full problem, current workaround and proposal.
title: corvint-tasks: lightweight shared-capacity slots resource kind with exclusive requests and class reservation (issue #1008)

body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1009 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. title: corvint-tasks pool sweep: optional memberConfig prepare step after cleanup and health, before the member is freed (issue #1009)

acceptanceCriteria: With a 45k-receipt journal, a writer committing every few seconds and 8 concurrent acquirers, every acquire completes within a documented bound (e.g. under 2 minutes).
CPU per waiting acquirer does not scale with the number of retries.
A test reproduces the starvation with a synthetic journal and a background writer and passes after the fix.
Spec records the bound and the admission/audit-reuse rule with requirement IDs.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1010 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17), observed on 1.0.0-rc.3 (main 8cd20e9). With a ~45,000-receipt journal, a 4-member all-FREE pool, a running dispatch and up to 8 concurrent pool acquire processes, acquires lived 2-42 minutes at 30-98% CPU while other writers committed (queue status ~0.2s, head.json advancing). Profile: leaseCommand -> store.Lease -> leaseOnce -> leaseWrite -> prepareLease -> journal.Reader.AuditForWriteObserved -> audit -> walk. Cause (suspected): the pool verb family stays on the complete route (a5827b719, 92000b394); each attempt re-walks the whole journal and is retried if any other write lands during the walk, so a long audit rarely wins under a steady write rate. Starvation, not deadlock. Suggested fixes: fair admission after audit, audit-once-per-head with incremental suffix audit, coalesced acquires, or a retryable result reporting retries and audit duration. See the issue for details.
title: pool acquire starves 10-40 min on a large journal: complete-route audit redone on every retry (issue #1010)
