If the streaming timeout classification is wrong rather than the test, the fix keeps git-timeout only for a real deadline and the parity test covers it.
body: Suspected load flake (not yet reproduced in isolation). Observed in the V1-0414 full-gate run 2026-10-17 04:55-08:55 UTC (attempt e9a499d1, tree ddccd4d2, main 69c6cac03, Go 1.27.2, darwin, host load 30-60), gate output evidence sha256 b190b8be302c8bac1153c92130e70b79a5f24d595857715664eb0bf964693255. internal/cem/gitrun: stream_unix_test.go:38 'stream=git-timeout: Git operation timed out buffered=git-exit-failure: Git exited unsuccessfully: doom' (parity/exit expected matching codes; the streaming path classified a plain exit as timeout); stream_unix_test.go:84 'open .../grandchild: no such file or directory' in the cancellation subtest (the grandchild never wrote its marker before cancellation). Package FAIL in 7.7s. Expected: parity and descendant-containment hold regardless of host load, or the tests bound their timing assumptions. Actual: both fail under load.
title: gitrun stream tests fail under host load: TestRunStreamProcessFailureParity/exit and TestRunStreamContainsDescendants/cancellation

acceptanceCriteria: Under a synthetic CPU load both tests either pass or the run reports an explicit budget-exhausted verdict that the tests accept as a distinct outcome; never "ended without a verdict".
The baseline/mutation budget is documented and test-overridable.
body: Suspected load flake. Observed in the V1-0414 full-gate run 2026-10-17 (attempt e9a499d1, tree ddccd4d2, main 69c6cac03, Go 1.27.2, darwin, load 30-60), gate output evidence sha256 b190b8be302c8bac1153c92130e70b79a5f24d595857715664eb0bf964693255. internal/liveverify/mutate: mutate_test.go:199 and :267 'Run: mutate: run ended without a verdict' after ~35s each; siblings in the same run report verdict=UNSUPPORTED 'baseline tests fail before mutation' at ~32s, which suggests a fixed run budget is exhausted by baseline go test under load. Package FAIL in 341.7s. Expected: the run reaches a verdict or returns an explicit timeout/UNKNOWN verdict, and the tests do not depend on host speed. Actual: no verdict.
title: liveverify/mutate tests end without a verdict under host load (TestRunKillsAMutantAndLeavesTheRootUntouched, TestRunReportsNoMutantsForADeclarationOnlyFile)

acceptanceCriteria: #1021-1: for a set of tests and a revision pair, a read lists each test as reusable or must-run with the reason.
#1021-2: any change to a fingerprint input makes the result must-run.
#1021-3: a missing or unqualified prior result fails closed as must-run.
#1021-4: the redundancy report gives minutes re-run versus reusable, split into exact and same-file-content matches.
#1021-5: both outputs are read-only and bounded, with a compact summary form.
#1024-1: a change to a cited or shared-code path returns STALE and names the path.
#1024-2: only changes outside the declared reach return FRESH.
#1024-3: a resolution error is a distinct outcome, never FRESH.
#1024-4: shared-code patterns are configured in the repository, not hard-coded.
#1024-5: the freshness result can serve as an additional reuse condition for passing-result reuse.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1021 and #1024 (filed 2026-10-17 by the owner). #1021: record a fingerprint (application revision, test-suite revision, test-file digest, config digest, selected project) with each retained passing result; a read lists selected tests as reusable or must-run with a reason; a redundancy report gives test-minutes by category and the share that re-ran an already-passing test (exact versus same-file-content matches). #1024: 'evidence fresh OLD NEW' over a declared reach (cited files plus repository-configured shared-code patterns) returns FRESH, STALE naming the deciding paths, or a distinct resolution-error outcome; usable as an extra reuse condition for #1021. Read-only, bounded, compact summary form.
title: Passing-result reuse at an identical fingerprint, redundancy report, and rebase evidence freshness (GitHub #1021, #1024)

acceptanceCriteria: Every listed file appears in exactly one shard.
The same inputs give the same partition and digest.
Weights are the median of the last K retained full runs; K is configurable.
Files with no history use the median weight and are flagged.
Invalid or missing history falls back to a complete round-robin, and the fallback is reported.
The output feeds the existing sharded stability and compare flow, which fails closed on a missing shard.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1022 (owner, 2026-10-17). Fixed or directory shards finish far apart. Proposal: a planner such as 'tests shards --count N' takes the listed test files plus retained run durations, assigns longest-first to the lightest shard using the median of the last K retained full runs, gives unknown files the median weight (flagged), records a partition digest, and falls back to complete round-robin (reported) on invalid or missing history. Output feeds the existing sharded stability/compare flow, which fails closed on a missing shard.
title: tests shards: duration-balanced deterministic shard partition from retained run history (GitHub #1022)

acceptanceCriteria: Each group contains tickets with pairwise-disjoint changed paths, apart from declared shared paths.
A dry chained merge confirms each group, and a conflict splits the group.
The repository gains no objects and no refs.
The maximum group size is configurable.
An unresolvable candidate is reported and left ungrouped.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1023 (owner, 2026-10-17). Several tickets are often ready for a final run on the same scarce environment. Proposal: a read-only 'plan batches' verb that groups candidate tickets by pairwise-disjoint changed paths (apart from declared shared paths), confirms each group with a dry chained merge that adds no objects or refs to the repository, splits a group on conflict, has a configurable maximum group size, and reports unresolvable candidates ungrouped. Groups can share one pool allocation and run.
title: Tasks plan batches: group ready tickets with disjoint changes, confirmed by a dry chained merge (GitHub #1023)

acceptanceCriteria: Each miss reports its kind, the value and the test location.
Dynamic or templated values count as prefixes.
Known false-positive classes (catch-all routes, patterns inside regular expressions) are labelled.
The check is name-level only and says so.
Output is bounded and the check is read-only.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1025 (owner, 2026-10-17). Tests can name a route, selector or mocked endpoint that exists nowhere in the application; a stub that never matches reaches the real backend or waits, and a selector with no source always times out, found only after a slow run. Proposal: 'tests refs-check' reports routes, selectors and mocked endpoint segments referenced by tests but absent from application source, reusing the existing application-map extraction of routes and selectors.
title: tests refs-check: static name-level check that test routes, selectors and mocked endpoints exist in the app (GitHub #1025)

acceptanceCriteria: Under a synthetic writer-contention test, a timed-out attached run exits 124 or 127, never 1/MALFORMED.
The envelope carries one run item whenever the command was started.
A deadline-exceeded store write maps to a documented retryable code (for example LOCK_TIMEOUT), not MALFORMED.
The outcome write is retried within the cleanup bound before giving up.
V1-1558: claim --detach ceiling expiry or SIGINT reports the same documented stable code, not MALFORMED.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1026 (owner, 2026-10-17), confirmed by the owner's reproduction on main 55abb815: `corvint-tasks run --attempt ID --generation G --timeout 40 -- sleep 300` (attached) under heavy writer contention returned exit 1, envelope ERROR, codes [MALFORMED], warning 'context deadline exceeded', items [] after ~150 s; also with --timeout 3. The child group was reaped but no run outcome is recorded on the attempt. A normal exit on the same attempt returned 3/EXIT. The attempt-runner spec reserves 124 for timeout and 127 for outcome-not-recorded; MALFORMED/1 is for pre-launch refusals. Same class as V1-1558 (claim --detach ceiling/SIGINT -> MALFORMED 'context deadline exceeded'); fix both by mapping a deadline-exceeded or cancelled store write to a documented retryable code and never reporting MALFORMED after launch. Expected: timeout exits 124; failed outcome write exits 127 with the write's code; the outcome write is retried within the cleanup bound.
title: run: a timed-out attached run exits 1 MALFORMED 'context deadline exceeded' under store contention instead of 124/127 (GitHub #1026)

acceptanceCriteria: A measured plan can carry test slices for a package so that no single package sets the shard floor, and the plan digest still covers the whole listed universe exactly once.
A recorded local wall-clock comparison of measured against universe placement on this repository decides promotion against the 20% bar; until then measured placement stays experimental.
body: Residual from V1-1579 (PR beamfall/corvint#1027, head b2ed935f0, 2026-10-17). Measured placement (STR-V0-050..054) partitions whole packages and does not apply AFP-V0-041 test slices, so internal/tasks/store alone sets the floor (live plan: 339 packages, 8 shards, shards 1-7 about 824s, shard 0 = internal/tasks/store alone at 896s). Promotion of measured placement also still needs the local 20% wall-clock bar against universe placement that balanced placement has; no wall-clock comparison was run.
title: corvint test shards: measured placement should carry AFP-V0-041 test slices and meet the promotion wall-clock bar (V1-1579 follow-up)

acceptanceCriteria: ci-shard-costs refresh retains each measured table as a dated, bounded artifact that corvint test shards --durations can read directly.
Retention is bounded (count or age) and the reader refuses a malformed table with a named code.
body: Residual from V1-1579 (PR beamfall/corvint#1027, 2026-10-17). corvint test shards takes the median of the last K retained corvint-ci-package-costs/0 tables; today those come only from the git history of package-costs.json (6 tables at the time), so K is bounded by commit history and a table cannot be retained without a commit.
title: ci-shard-costs refresh should retain dated cost tables instead of relying on package-costs.json git history (V1-1579 follow-up)

acceptanceCriteria: A pool declares any subset of the five operations, and an undeclared one is refused with a typed reason.
An operation in an illegal member state is refused with a typed reason, and nothing runs.
Each run records operation, request id, exit class and output digest; `pool status` shows the last receipt per operation.
The same request id replays the recorded outcome and never runs twice.
A failed retarget or reset leaves the member QUARANTINED with the operation named in the reason.
Timeouts kill the whole process group, and output is bounded as for existing commands.
Pools that do not use the new fields behave as before.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1028 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A pool member that is a disposable test environment needs more than health/cleanup/safeReuse/prepare. It must be built from a pinned source, refreshed without losing data, reset to a clean template, moved to another allowed source, and torn down. The queue knows none of this; it only knows FREE, QUARANTINED and HELD. It cannot tell which operations a member has had, cannot refuse an operation while another holder is active, and cannot show what a member currently serves. Current workaround A separate CLI keeps a private marker per environment, and wrapper scripts decide which operation to run after each release. The queue sees only opaque commands, so a failed rebuild leaves the member in an unknown state that scripts must probe. Proposal Extend memberConfig with optional named operations `provision`, `refresh`, `reset`, `retarget` and `teardown`, using the existing command shape See beamfall/corvint#1028 for the full text.
title: pool: typed member lifecycle operations (provision, refresh, reset, retarget, teardown) with recorded outcomes (issue #1028)

acceptanceCriteria: A source outside the allow-list is refused at acquire with a typed reason.
A member whose observed identity differs from the default cannot become FREE; it stays QUARANTINED with SOURCE_DRIFT and both pairs.
A failing or malformed identity command never frees the member.
`pool status` shows each member's observed identity and observation time.
Removing a pair from the allow-list does not strand a live allocation; the guard applies at release.
Pools without `allowedSources` behave as before.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1029 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A pool member may serve different revisions of the application under test, and a holder may legitimately move one member to a non-default revision for a task. Nothing records which revision a member serves, which revisions are allowed, or that a released member is still on a non-default revision. The next holder silently gets a different environment. Current workaround A sweep script hard-codes the approved revision/tree pairs and a default, reads an identity report from the environment, and moves the member back before confirming it safe. Anyone who skips the script can free a drifted member. Proposal Pool config gains `allowedSources` (revision/tree pairs) and `defaultSource`. A member declares an `identity` command that reports the served pair as JSON. `pool acquire --source <pair>` accepts only allowed pairs and records the target. `confirm-safe` and release to FREE require t See beamfall/corvint#1029 for the full text.
title: pool: per-member source identity, an approved-source allow-list, and a drift guard before a member is freed (issue #1029)

acceptanceCriteria: Specs that reference a seed directly or through a registry key get exactly those setup files.
A computed lookup, unknown key, missing path or empty spec list yields ALL with a typed reason.
A hub file that lists every seed is not followed and does not widen the result.
Comment-only mentions are ignored.
The output records the revision and a digest of the inputs read.
The result can be passed to the test provider so a run executes only those setup files.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1030 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Browser suites often have setup projects that seed shared data. Running all of them before every run wastes time, and under load a seed the specs never read can fail and abort the run. Current workaround A script follows imports and string keys from the spec files to the data contexts they read, and passes the resulting setup files to the test config. It falls back to all on a computed lookup, an unknown key, or a hub file that lists every scenario. Proposal `corvint tests setup-select --specs <paths>` (and an MCP tool) returns the setup files the specs transitively depend on. It reuses the string-key registry dialect of impact analysis, returns an explicit ALL with a reason when it cannot resolve something, and binds the result to the revision. See beamfall/corvint#1030 for the full text.
title: tests: select only the setup/seed files a run needs, failing closed to all (issue #1030)

acceptanceCriteria: A repeated call returns the same path and branch without creating a second worktree.
The branch name derives only from the ticket id and the declared pattern.
A dirty existing worktree is reported, never reset.
The result includes the repository identity and head revision.
Paths outside the declared repository root are refused.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1031 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Agents that work on a second repository (for example a docs repository) repeatedly stop because no authorized worktree exists for their ticket. The queue binds attempts to its own repository but does not create or reuse a per-ticket worktree elsewhere. Current workaround A script creates or reuses a worktree for the ticket on a ticket-named branch from a base head and prints the path. Proposal A program-level declaration `worktrees: {repository, base, branchPattern}` and `corvint-tasks worktree ensure <ticket>`, which creates or reuses the worktree idempotently, refuses when the base is not a clean ancestor, and records the worktree head when the attempt is released or completed. See beamfall/corvint#1031 for the full text.
title: tasks: ensure a per-ticket worktree on a ticket-named branch in a declared repository (issue #1031)

acceptanceCriteria: Each pattern has a rule id, a fixture that triggers it and one that does not.
By default only findings on lines added or changed since the base are reported; --all-lines reports all.
An inline annotation with a reason suppresses exactly the named rule there and is echoed in the report; one without a reason suppresses nothing.
Output is deterministic JSON; exit codes are 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 error.
Preflight can require a clean lint for the same tree.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1032 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Reviewers keep returning browser tests for the same mechanical reasons, all visible in source before any run: no assertion; assertions only on visibility or URL; assertions inside an if/else or try/catch guarded by a visibility or count check; catch handlers that swallow wait errors; fixed sleeps or network-idle waits; tautological assertions; positional, CSS-class or xpath selectors; skip/only markers without a reason. Each costs a run plus a review round. Current workaround A local AST script runs before review and reports findings only on lines changed against the base revision. Proposal `corvint tests lint --base REV [--all-lines] [--json]` over changed test and page-object files, with a closed rule set, stable rule ids, file:line findings and a non-zero exit on findings. A structured inline annotation with a reason justifies one rule at that line. Usable as a preflight check See beamfall/corvint#1032 for the full text.
title: tests lint: static check of test source for non-asserting, conditional, swallowing and timing-dependent patterns (issue #1032)

acceptanceCriteria: A failure counts as known only if it failed in the full run and the isolated re-run, and its evidence is re-read at diff time; missing or passing evidence un-excuses it.
Full-run-only failures are listed as suspected flakes and never excused.
Tests in --own files fail the gate even if known.
The receipt lists new, known, fixed and flaky sets with counts and is bound to the baseline revision.
A baseline older than a configurable bound relative to the branch point is reported as stale.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1033 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A directory or suite run on an integration branch fails for tests that were already failing before the change. Authors are refused for failures they did not cause, or the failures are excused in prose. Current workaround Each failure is compared with an old full-run baseline. When the baseline predates the branch, a separate known-failures list is kept: the failing tests are re-run in isolation, and only those failing in both runs are listed. Failures seen only in the full run are reported as load or order flakes and never excused. Entries stay valid only while their cited run still shows the failure. Tests in the change's own files must pass outright. Proposal `corvint tests baseline record --rev REV` runs the suite, re-runs failures in isolation and stores the both-fail set with evidence run ids. `corvint tests baseline diff RUN... --own PATH...` exits non-zero on any new failu See beamfall/corvint#1033 for the full text.
title: run gate: block only on failures not in a revision-pinned baseline, with evidence-backed known-failure entries (issue #1033)

acceptanceCriteria: Findings name the path, the commit and the missing element (marker, listing, run citation).
Merge conflicts confined to configured generated files are not findings.
The split leaves the final tree byte-identical, keeps author, date and message, and prints the old head.
It refuses the unsafe states, and lists only the notes listing and run citation as manual follow-ups.
A mismatch between expected and actual head aborts without changes.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1034 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Changes to shared test infrastructure (helpers, config, fixtures, setup, dependency manifests) affect every test. Policy requires them in separately labelled commits, listed in the ticket notes, with a cited passing affected-run. Authors repeatedly mix them into feature commits, and reviews spend hours reporting it. Current workaround A script checks that the change merges cleanly, that shared-path changes appear only in commits with a marker prefix, that each is listed in a notes section, and that a passing run is cited. A second script rewrites the branch so each mixed commit becomes a shared-only commit followed by the rest, keeping the final tree, authors and later commits, and refuses dirty trees, detached HEAD, merges in range and a live agent session. Proposal `corvint changes check-shared --base REV` with configurable shared-path globs and generated-file exemptions, and ` See beamfall/corvint#1034 for the full text.
title: shared-path change policy: separate labelled commits that cite an affected run, plus mechanical commit splitting (issue #1034)

acceptanceCriteria: Pairs are reported with the shared assertion lines and score; frequent lines are excluded by a cutoff.
Gate mode considers only pairs involving the branch's added or changed tests.
A distinct-from decision with a reason resolves a pair; one without a reason does not.
Marking an obligation covered-by another test resolves the pair.
Output states that pairs are candidates, not verdicts.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1035 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Different authors write tests proving the same behaviour in different words and files, so titles and descriptions miss the duplication. Current workaround Normalized assertion lines are extracted per test. Pairs across files that share at least two lines above a Jaccard threshold are flagged, ignoring lines that appear in many tests. A branch gate compares the tests it adds or changes against the base and fails until each pair has a decision: a reasoned distinct-from note, or removal with the obligation marked covered-by the other test. Proposal `corvint tests duplicates [--ref REV] [--gate TICKET]`. See beamfall/corvint#1035 for the full text.
title: tests duplicates: detect duplicate tests by assertion-set similarity, with recorded distinct-from decisions (issue #1035)

acceptanceCriteria: A defect can be referenced from a ticket and an expected-fail annotation; a reference to an unknown or not-a-bug id is a preflight finding.
An environment-category defect does not satisfy a blocked-by-defect obligation.
Updates are append-only and safe under concurrency.
The register can be excluded from published or backed-up artefacts by configuration.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1036 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Agents find product faults while writing tests but must not fix product code under their ticket. Findings end up scattered in notes, and a blocked obligation cannot distinguish a real product defect from a fixable environment fault. Current workaround An append-only, locked JSONL ledger of defects (id, location, evidence reference, severity, status suspected/confirmed/not-a-bug/duplicate-of, category product or environment), where later lines override earlier ones, plus a rendered summary and a harvest of untriaged mentions from notes. Audits refuse an environment defect as the reason an obligation is blocked. Proposal `corvint defects add|update|list|harvest`, referenceable from obligations and expected-fail annotations. See beamfall/corvint#1036 for the full text.
title: defects: register for suspected product and environment faults found during test work (issue #1036)

acceptanceCriteria: Identical inputs replay the stored report and say so.
Any change to a tree, an untracked file or the check implementation misses the cache.
--fresh bypasses the cache.
Entries are bounded by count or age.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1037 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Agents run the same static checks repeatedly across many sessions over trees that have not changed, hundreds of times a day. Current workaround A wrapper keyed on the hash of both trees, the uncommitted diff, untracked files and the check scripts replays the stored report, with --fresh to bypass. Proposal Let any preflight or reference check opt into a result cache keyed on tree identities, working-tree diff and the check implementation digest. See beamfall/corvint#1037 for the full text.
title: preflight: content-keyed cache for static pre-run checks (issue #1037)

acceptanceCriteria: With the setting absent, behaviour is unchanged.
Three short sessions hold the next launch; one longer session resets the streak.
The hold appears in `dispatch status` and the event log with its reason.
Running workers are never stopped.
The finding names the ticket, count, median duration and first-seen time.
The setting hot-reloads.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1038 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A ticket can be relaunched over and over by sessions that each end within minutes, recording a little progress or exiting cleanly. Each pays the full start-up cost for little work. Backoff applies only after runs without progress, so churn that counts as progress is never throttled. Current workaround A work-state script holds a ticket for 60 minutes when its last 3 sessions each ended in under 20 minutes. A doctor script flags 3 or more sessions under 4 minutes within 30 minutes, and 6 or more launches in 2 hours with a median under 10 minutes. Proposal Role or global `shortSessions {seconds, count, holdSeconds}`: after `count` consecutive finished sessions of one ticket shorter than `seconds`, new launches for it wait `holdSeconds` from the last end. Running sessions are never touched. Emit an event, show it in `dispatch status`, and add a doctor finding SESSION_CHURN. See beamfall/corvint#1038 for the full text.
title: dispatch: cooldown and doctor finding for repeated short sessions on one ticket (issue #1038)

acceptanceCriteria: With 1 free member and 3 matching tickets, one session launches.
A launched worker that has not yet claimed counts against room until it claims or ends.
Roles without a pool requirement are unaffected.
Status shows each waiting ticket's reason and the computed room.
A stale worker record is ignored.
Higher-priority tickets launch first.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1039 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem When several tickets need a member of a small pool, the dispatcher can launch more sessions than there are free members. One claims a member; the rest start up, poll and fail to acquire, each paying full start-up cost and context. Current workaround A work-state script counts FREE members, subtracts sessions launched but not yet holding a member, holds the excess tickets, and orders waiting tickets so review and critical work go first. Proposal For a role with a pool requirement, compute room = free members minus launched-but-unclaimed workers, and launch at most that many per tick in priority order. Per-role opt-out. Report `pool-wait` as the reason in status and events. See beamfall/corvint#1039 for the full text.
title: dispatch: launch pool-requiring roles only up to the number of free pool members (issue #1039)

acceptanceCriteria: A simulated suspend gap is recorded once.
Idle and wall caps do not fire because of the gap.
Lease expiry during the gap does not reap a live worker.
`dispatch status` shows the last gap.
Without gaps, behaviour is unchanged.
Keep-awake is off by default and documented as not preventing lid-close sleep.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1040 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem When the host suspends (lid closed, maintenance sleep) wall-clock timers keep counting: leases expire, idle or wall caps fire, and sleeping workers look hung, so work stalls or is killed on wake for no real reason. Nothing reports the suspend. Current workaround A doctor script reads kernel sleep/wake times and flags recent sleep; context tools subtract slept time; supervisor shells hold an idle-sleep assertion, which does not stop lid-close sleep. Proposal Detect suspend gaps (a large jump between wall and monotonic time across ticks) and record a `host-slept` event with its duration. Exclude the gap from idle and wall accounting, and give live leases a one-time extension bounded by the gap. Add a doctor finding. Optionally, `service install --keep-awake` holds an idle-sleep assertion while the service runs. See beamfall/corvint#1040 for the full text.
title: host sleep awareness for leases, idle and wall-clock caps (issue #1040)

acceptanceCriteria: A command holding the lock beyond the threshold yields a finding naming pid, command and age.
No completions within the window, with ready tickets and idle workers, yields a finding; an empty queue yields none.
Findings clear on their own when the condition ends.
Detection is read-only.
Thresholds are settable, and the defaults are documented.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1041 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Queue slowness has distinct causes that today need hand-written plugins: a process holding the store or preparation lock for a long time (others fail LOCK_TIMEOUT), queue commands running for a minute or more, no completion for many hours, and file-handle exhaustion. Plugins cannot see lock holders. Current workaround A script walks the process list for long-running queue commands, checks which holds the lock file, compares the last completion time with now, and compares the open-file table with its limit. Proposal Native findings QUEUE_LOCK_HELD (holder pid, command, age), SLOW_QUEUE_COMMAND, NO_COMPLETIONS (window configurable, default 2 h while ready tickets exist) and FD_PRESSURE, with configurable thresholds. See beamfall/corvint#1041 for the full text.
title: doctor: built-in findings for queue lock holders, slow queue commands, completion stalls and file-handle pressure (issue #1041)

acceptanceCriteria: A failed hook is reported, and the result says the switch still happened.
Rollback restores the previous binary and service state.
Live attempts are adopted or the update waits, per the existing compatibility rules.
The result lists hook outputs and retry counts.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1042 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem After the binary changes, host-adapter qualification bound to the exact binary is stale and the running dispatcher still uses the old build. `apply` neither restarts the dispatcher nor triggers requalification. Current workaround A script waits for no live attempts, stops the dispatcher, switches symlinks, re-runs adapter qualification up to three times (flaky under load), and restarts the supervisor. Proposal `apply --restart-service PROGRAM` drains the service, switches and resumes on the new build. `--post-switch CMD` hooks run with bounded timeouts and retries, recorded in the update result. Roll back automatically if the service does not start. See beamfall/corvint#1042 for the full text.
title: update apply: restart the service and run post-switch hooks (issue #1042)

acceptanceCriteria: Workers launched before the drain can read the signal.
A claim during the drain is refused or returns the notice.
The signal disappears when the drain is lifted.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1043 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem When a service drain starts, live workers do not know. They keep starting long commands and hold up the drain. Current workaround Tools the agent calls constantly print a warning on stderr while a stop file exists, and a context-budget tool answers 'hand off now' in drain mode. Proposal While desired is DRAINING, expose a documented signal to workers (a file path named in their environment, plus a short notice appended to `corvint-tasks` output) telling them to finish current work, release and end. Share the mechanism with the context-size notice in #1007. See beamfall/corvint#1043 for the full text.
title: dispatch: tell live workers that a drain is pending (issue #1043)

acceptanceCriteria: The command runs once per change, not per tick.
A failing hook becomes a finding and never blocks the dispatcher.
It is bounded by a timeout and an output cap.
An identical finding set never notifies twice.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1044 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem The only way to be told that findings changed is a polling script that diffs the summary and sends a desktop notification. Current workaround A loop runs every 15 minutes, builds an issue list from status and doctor output, and notifies only when the list changes. Proposal A `notify {command, minIntervalSeconds}` setting in doctor or service config runs an adopter-supplied argv with the new finding summary on stdin, only when the finding set changes, under the plugin sandbox rules. See beamfall/corvint#1044 for the full text.
title: doctor/service: notify hook when the finding set changes (issue #1044)

acceptanceCriteria: A note containing a listed value is refused with SECRET_DETECTED.
The refusal contains no part of the value.
Personal-data classes are opt-in.
The screen applies to ticket notes, know-how and obligation text.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1045 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem The secret screen catches credential-shaped text but not literal values already known to be secret (for example values in local environment files), nor emails, phone numbers or card-like numbers. Agent-written shared notes can leak both. Current workaround A scrubber loads the values from local environment files and rejects any note containing one, plus regular expressions for personal-data classes. Proposal Policy `knowHow.screen {denyValuesFile, classes: [email, phone, card]}`. Values are compared, never echoed or stored; a refusal names the class, not the value. See beamfall/corvint#1045 for the full text.
title: know-how screen: adopter-declared secret values and opt-in personal-data classes (issue #1045)

acceptanceCriteria: A moved ref refreshes the tree and index before the next answer.
A dirty tree is never modified, and responses flag the stale binding.
A missing ref is a typed error.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1046 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem An MCP server rooted at a worktree answers for whatever revision that worktree holds. Keeping agents on the integration branch head needs an external sync and reindex. Current workaround A script detaches the worktree at the branch head when it is clean and runs `index --if-stale`, leaving a dirty worktree alone and logging it. Proposal `corvint-mcp --follow-ref REF` on a dedicated detached worktree: refresh and reindex on a clean tree when the ref moves, report DIRTY instead of changing a dirty tree, and echo the resolved commit in every response. See beamfall/corvint#1046 for the full text.
title: corvint-mcp: follow a branch head on a dedicated worktree (issue #1046)

acceptanceCriteria: Each finding derives only from the recognised host event format.
Unrecognised output yields no finding.
Thresholds are configurable.
Findings cite the evidence file and line range.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1047 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Sessions can end uselessly in ways the queue cannot see: a model request retried repeatedly with no completion, repeated provider errors, or a first tool call refused (wrong worktree or attempt id) so no work happens. Current workaround A script scans each worker's stdout for 3 or more step starts without a finish, 3 or more provider errors in an hour, and refusals before any work. Proposal Using the existing host usage-format parsers, add findings HOST_RETRY_STORM, HOST_ERRORS and EARLY_REFUSAL with counts and the worker id. See beamfall/corvint#1047 for the full text.
title: doctor: session-outcome findings from host event output (issue #1047)

acceptanceCriteria: The refusal is typed and names the signature and count.
A changed input digest clears it.
A declared remediation clears it once, with an audit record.
Disabled by default.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1048 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A test or run that failed with the same normalised error is queued again with no relevant change, consuming a scarce resource each time. Current workaround A runner keeps a signature per failing item; after two identical failures it refuses to claim a resource until the ticket notes declare a fix. Proposal A failure-signature ledger in `preflight` and `run-batch`: refuse after N identical signatures at the same input digest unless a remediation reference is declared. See beamfall/corvint#1048 for the full text.
title: preflight/run-batch: refuse re-running an identical failure signature at unchanged inputs (issue #1048)

acceptanceCriteria: A test shows no real-repository object file mtime changes after plan batches, or the spec records evidence that the change is harmless under TM-V0-008.
NTP-V0-022's known-limit text is updated to match.
body: V1-1580 (PR #1049) `corvint-tasks plan batches` runs a chained `git merge-tree --write-tree` with a throw-away GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY and the repo objects as an alternate. When a merge recreates an object that already exists, Git freshens that object's file mtime in the real repository. Content, object count and refs are unchanged; NTP-V0-022 records this as a known limit. Either prevent the freshen or prove the mtime change is harmless to the TM-V0-008 read contract and to gc/prune.
title: plan batches: dry merge-tree refreshes mtimes of pre-existing objects in the real repository (V1-1580 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A live run on this repository's queue is retained, showing proposed groups and their actual merge outcome.
Promotion is recorded in the spec and a build-log entry, or the verb stays experimental with a recorded reason.
body: V1-1580 delivered `corvint-tasks plan batches` as experimental NTP-V0 work. No GP or live qualification exercises it on a real queue. Promote only with measured evidence on this repository's queue: groups proposed and whether they merged cleanly.
title: plan batches (NTP-V0-020..025): promotion from experimental via a live qualification (V1-1580 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: With a declared progress signal, a hand-off whose fingerprint changed is not a no-progress generation for loop detection, backoff or NO_PROGRESS_HANDOFF.
A hand-off with an unchanged fingerprint and no candidate, gate or review still counts as no progress.
Without the declaration, behaviour is unchanged.
Findings and holds name the signal that judged them.
The declared signal is recorded as loop evidence, so the decision can be audited.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1050 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Loop detection (`loopDetection`, CAL-V0-102), the dispatcher's no-progress backoff, and the doctor kinds NO_PROGRESS_HANDOFF, REPEAT_REFUSAL and SETUP_ONLY_PROOF all judge progress by queue artefacts: a new candidate tree, a gate result, or a review. Many adopters make real progress between hand-offs without producing any of those mid-work. They commit to a working branch, record witnessed obligations, or advance a run plan, and submit a candidate only at the end. For such a program: - NO_PROGRESS_HANDOFF fires on nearly every active ticket. One ticket showed 31 consecutive hand-offs while it was steadily progressing. - Enabling `loopDetection` would hold almost every ticket LOOP_DETECTED, each needing an owner `ticket reopen`, and the opt-in cannot be undone on that store. The adopter therefore keeps its own stall rule and its own doctor detectors, which duplicates these feature See beamfall/corvint#1050 for the full text.
title: Loop detection, backoff and no-progress doctor kinds: accept an adopter-declared progress signal (issue #1050)

acceptanceCriteria: corvint test receipts record a per-unit fingerprint (revision-bound inputs).
runs reusable classifies corvint test units with the same fail-closed rules as Playwright reports.
Tests cover EXACT_PASS and a fingerprint mismatch.
body: V1-1578 (PR #1051) added `corvint runs reusable|fresh` for Playwright reports keyed by test identity + testRevision. `corvint test` (STR-V0) receipts carry no per-unit fingerprint, so its results can never be REUSABLE.
title: corvint test (STR-V0) receipts: per-unit fingerprint so runs reuse covers corvint test results (V1-1578 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A retained fixture from a real Playwright run declaring testRevision.
A live run shows at least one REUSABLE classification and one MUST_RUN with reason, retained as evidence.
body: V1-1578's live qualification found every test MUST_RUN IDENTITY_INPUT_MISSING because the retained 1.61.1 reports predate testRevision. Reuse has not been shown on a real report carrying it; no runner was installed in the lane.
title: runs reusable: qualify against a real Playwright report that declares testRevision (V1-1578 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A report from another root resolves when testRootPath is declared.
Without it the result stays UNRESOLVED with a typed reason.
body: `corvint runs fresh` resolves test files relative to the local checkout; a report produced on another host (different absolute root) cannot be mapped without a declared testRootPath, so freshness is UNRESOLVED.
title: runs fresh: reports produced on another machine need testRootPath to locate test files (V1-1578 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: The README row matches the spec's requirement range and specindex agreement test passes.
body: The PWR-V0 row in docs/specs/README.md still says requirements 001..010, stale before V1-1578 added 033..040.
title: docs/specs/README.md PWR-V0 row lists 001..010; spec now runs to PWR-V0-040 (V1-1578 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: --shard-plan naming a FIFO is refused promptly with a typed error.
A test proves the refusal without blocking.
Regular plan files read as before.
body: Found by the V1-1579 repair lane (PR #1027, head ba1026b88). The shard input reads now use readBoundedFile (O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW, regular-file check, bound+1 read), but ReadShardPlan via decodeStrictBounded still uses plain os.Open, so `--shard-plan` naming a FIFO blocks indefinitely. Expected: refuse non-regular files without blocking, as STR-V0-050 now requires for the other inputs.
title: corvint test --shard-plan: ReadShardPlan opens with plain os.Open, so a FIFO path blocks (V1-1579 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: Cypress visit/intercept/get references are checked with fixtures.
A configured testIdAttribute is honoured.
Anchored regexes are evaluated against map routes; unanchored ones stay labelled.
A retained run on an adopter-scale suite, with promotion recorded or declined with reason.
body: V1-1581 (PR #1052) added `corvint flows appmap refs` (AMAP-V0-090..099), experimental. Residuals: (1) Cypress cy.visit/cy.intercept/cy.get references and a configured Playwright testIdAttribute are not read; (2) unanchored regular expressions are treated as labelled path prefixes, not evaluated; (3) no qualification against a real adopter-scale Playwright suite; promotion out of experimental needs that evidence.
title: flows appmap refs: Cypress references, Playwright testIdAttribute, anchored regex evaluation, adopter-scale qualification (V1-1581 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: A read-only command lists OPEN tickets cited by merged commits/PR merge bodies on the integration ref, with the citing commit and the blocking closeout step.
Partial delivery is not inferred as complete: the report never completes a ticket and labels findings as candidates.
A fixture covers: cited+gate-failed, cited+no attempt, umbrella PR citing several tickets, and an uncited ticket (not listed).
body: Observed 2026-10-17: a read-only audit of 37 of 76 suspected delivered-but-open tickets confirmed 22 delivered on origin/main (e.g. V1-0252..0255 via #202/#205/#206/#904, V1-0414, V1-0811), 13 partial, 2 not delivered. Causes seen: completion is a separate post-merge native write that no merge triggers; closeout waiters die on CIFAIL/session end and merge events are not delivered (auto-merge completion did not wake the session); `complete` is refused when a required gate (full-gate) failed under host load (V1-0414 GATE_FAILED) and the ticket stays open by design; work landed under umbrella/closeout PRs or GitHub issue numbers, not the ticket ID; builders and reviewers may not run corvint-tasks, so the orchestrator is the only closer. A 2026-10-14 audit found the same class (memory batch-similar-tickets). Expected: the store reports, without mutating, OPEN tickets whose ID or linked issue appears in a merged commit/PR on the integration branch, with the pending closeout step (gate failed, no attempt, not submitted), so closeout debt is visible instead of discovered by audits.
title: corvint-tasks: detect delivered-but-open tickets (merged PRs/commits citing an OPEN ticket) and queue their closeout

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-finish emits per-phase timings to its log.
The dominant phase is identified and either sped up or made resumable, with a retained before/after measurement on a docs-only change.
A docs-only lane finish runs under 600 s on a loaded host, or the remaining limit is recorded.
body: Observed 2026-10-17 (corvint origin/main 072a306f1, Go 1.27.2, host load about 60): in two builder lanes (evidence PR #1053 and the #1052 fix lane), `make dogfood-finish` ran longer than the 600 s Bash tool limit. The harness moved it to the background, and the agent parked without reporting. Expected: finish completes well under 10 minutes, or reports progress and phase timings so that a caller can bound it. Actual: one opaque step, over 600 s. Workaround: the lane charter now says to wait in the foreground.
title: make dogfood-finish routinely exceeds the 600 s agent tool timeout under host load 40-60, so builder lanes get backgrounded and park

acceptanceCriteria: With 47k receipts and 3-5 heartbeat/renew/claim writes per minute, acquire calls bounded at 150 s each reach ACQUIRED while a member is FREE, measured with the opt-in load harness or a retained host run.

Either (a) a tail made only of heartbeat/renew receipts is accepted against the audited head, with a spec requirement proving those receipts cannot change pool membership or allocation, or (b) progress survives across bounded calls without a cross-process shared base that breaks PSR-V0-051, or a recorded design decision says why not.
A PENDING result reports retries and audit duration (the #1010 'report the wait' suggestion), or that is explicitly declined.
Tamper tests in the style of PSR-V0-053 still refuse.
body:
GitHub #1010 comment (2026-10-17 14:51Z, reporter build 55abb815, which predates the V1-1560 fix merged in 072a306f1): over 4 hours with about 47,000 receipts there were 11 ACQUIRED and 146 PENDING at the client wrapper's 150 s wait, while one member stayed FREE. Writers ran at about 3-5 fast-route writes per minute (dispatcher keepLease with 13 workers at a 300 s heartbeat, plus claims and notes).

Gap in V1-1560 (PSR-V0-050..057): the resume base lives only in one command's memory (PSR-V0-051). The first resume needs one early-stopped complete attempt plus a prefix walk, which PSR-V0-055 extrapolates to about 3 minutes at 45k receipts and load 60. A client that bounds each call to 150 s and starts a new process each time therefore never reaches a resumed round.

The reporter proposes an interim: commit against the audited head when the receipts since that head are only heartbeat or renew receipts, which cannot change pool membership or allocation.

Expected: a bounded acquire call at 45k receipts completes, or returns a retryable result that lets the next call make progress. Related: V1-1569 (45k qualification), V1-1570 (store file count).
title: pool acquire: bounded client calls (150 s) exit before the first resume base exists, so the V1-1560 resume never helps them; heartbeat/renew-only tails could commit against the audited head (GitHub #1010 follow-up)

acceptanceCriteria: A spec (domain spec, not the leases spec) defines one retention story: prefix-seal or fresh-store, with its audit root, chain-hash continuity, terminal-only eligibility, and a rollback via archive restore.

The implemented path drops a verified, all-terminal prefix (or migrates to a fresh store) and the audit runs from the checkpoint; tamper tests on the archived prefix and on the retained checkpoint refuse.
A measured before/after on a synthetic store of at least 40k receipts shows complete-route audit time and store bytes, retained in the build log.
doctor reports journal size and growth rate with a threshold finding.
receipt compact help states what it reclaims (liveness bodies only) and points to the retention path.
body: GitHub #1055, a follow-up to #982, V1-1508 and V1-1511. On one long-running queue: 47,136 receipts, 493 MB, 19 days old; 84% are TRANSITION receipts averaging about 9 KB. `receipt compact --dry-run` elides 8,848 receipts, shrinking 424.7 MB to 382.2 MB (about 10%). Most of the store is the history of settled tickets and attempts, which can never change again. Every complete-route audit and every cold start still walks it, and that feeds the pool-acquire starvation behind #1010 and V1-1617. The reporter's asks: (1) a supported way to drop an archived, verified prefix whose tickets are all terminal from the live store, keeping its chain hash and checkpoint and auditing from that checkpoint onward (archive export/verify/restore already exist); or (2) a documented fresh-store-from-snapshot path that carries forward only live tickets, leases and policy and keeps the old store read-only; (3) doctor reports journal size and growth rate with a threshold warning; (4) `receipt compact` help states the typical share it can reclaim. The store format is one-way after compaction, so the reporter wants a single documented retention story. This changes store authority and audit roots, so spec it first; the one-way migration needs a documented rollback (a retained archive plus restore).
title: corvint-tasks journal retention: retire settled ticket/attempt history from the live journal (sealed verified prefix or fresh store from snapshot), doctor size/growth warning, compact help expectations (GitHub #1055)

acceptanceCriteria: A refused complete leaves an observable, bounded journal fact and closeout-debt reports COMPLETE_REFUSED with the refusal code, with a test.
HELD and DRAFT tickets cited by merged commits are reported with their status, or their exclusion is specified with reason.
The TCD spec is amended and the read-only proof still passes.
body: V1-1615 (PR #1058) added the read-only `corvint-tasks ticket closeout-debt` verb (TCD-V0-001..010). Residuals: (1) a refused `complete` writes no journal record, so the verb cannot report COMPLETE_REFUSED and shows GATES_PASSED_COMPLETE_PENDING instead; (2) HELD and DRAFT tickets cited by merged work are out of scope.
title: closeout-debt: observe refused complete attempts and cover HELD/DRAFT tickets (V1-1615 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: A reviewed .corvint/shared-paths.json is committed and `corvint changes` enforces it on this repo, with a test.
The update service contract is bound to the corvint-tasks service (launchd/systemd) with a live check, or the binding is declined with reason.
rollback stops and restarts the bound service under the same live-attempt guard, with a test.
body: PR #1059 delivered SPC-V0-001..008 (shared-path change policy) and UPD-V0-011..014 (corvint-update service coordination). Residuals: (1) the repository ships no `.corvint/shared-paths.json` policy, so the check has nothing to enforce here; (2) service control is a generic `PROGRAM status|stop|start|live-attempts` contract and is not bound to launchd, systemd or the corvint-tasks service (V1-0697); (3) `corvint-update rollback` does not drive the service. UPD-V0-011..014 tests failed locally under load at the version-smoke step ('descendant snapshot unavailable'); CI decides.
title: shared-path policy file and update-service binding (V1-1591/1599 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: The darwin lock holder is identified exactly or labelled approximate in the finding, with a test.
The lsof probe stays within its bound at load 60+ or degrades to a narrower probe, measured.
A Linux run (CI or VM) retains live /proc probe evidence.
The notify hook runs after the cache lock is released, with a test.
Host coverage gaps for EARLY_REFUSAL/HOST_RETRY_STORM are closed or declared in the spec.
body: PR #1060 delivered TQD-V0-020..024/026..033. Residuals: (1) darwin approximates the lock holder by the longest-running opener; (2) the darwin lsof probe often exceeds its 5 s bound under load, so doctor warns and produces no finding; (3) Linux /proc probes are covered only by parser fixtures; (4) the notify hook runs while holding the cache lock; (5) EARLY_REFUSAL cannot fire for opencode and HOST_RETRY_STORM cannot fire for claude-code; (6) no cross-run scan cache; (7) the LiveFormats change means an in-place replacement of an older build needs a drain.
title: doctor: exact darwin lock holder, lsof bound under load, live Linux probe evidence, notify outside the cache lock (V1-1598 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: Sweep runs the bounded identity probe on guarded members and quarantines on drift, with a test.
Replay of confirm-safe is shown not to rerun the identity command (or its rerun is specified), with a test.
body: PR #1061 (PSR-V0-081..086) makes member identity and safeReuse mutually exclusive, so `pool sweep` never meets an identity-guarded member and never probes identity. Whether a replayed confirm-safe reruns the identity command is NOT_OBSERVED.
title: pool sweep: probe member identity when identity and safeReuse coexist (V1-1586 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: Decision 0375's RELEASE-NOTES citations are anchored so an insertion above them does not break line-citations-check, verified by an insertion test.
body: Lanes that insert release notes above docs/RELEASE-NOTES.md line ~351 shift the two line citations in decision 0375, failing line-citations-check (seen in #1061). Expected: a citation anchor stable under insertions above it.
title: decision 0375 RELEASE-NOTES line citations break whenever release notes are inserted above them

acceptanceCriteria: A retained live Playwright full and isolated run exercises baseline record/diff and the gate's baseline filter.
A measured before/after count of repeated identical failing runs is retained, or the claim is withdrawn.
body: PR #1062 delivered TOL-V0-047..054 and PWR-V0-041..045 with fixture tests only. NOT_RUN: live Playwright full and isolated runs, and a measured reduction in repeated runs. `runs baseline record` reads kept reports and does not run the suite (recorded deviation).
title: Qualify preflight cache, failure-signature refusal and runs baseline on live Playwright runs (V1-1590/1594/1605 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: Owner decision recorded: STR-V0-011 amendment text accepted, or V1-1609 declined/archived with reason.
body: V1-1609 asks for per-unit fingerprints and `runs reusable` classification of `corvint test` units from receipts. STR-V0-011 (decision 0524) forbids receipts feeding selection or ranking, enforced by TestSTRV0011ReceiptsHaveNoOtherReader. The run/preflight lane (#1062) left V1-1609 undelivered. Question for the owner: amend STR-V0-011 to allow a reuse-only reader, or decline V1-1609.
title: V1-1609 needs an owner amendment of STR-V0-011 before receipts can feed `runs reusable` unit classification

acceptanceCriteria: A 47k-receipt run with per-round timing confirms or refutes the no-resume-flag hypothesis; the result is retained.
A non-detached pool acquire reaches ACQUIRED within 150 s at 47k receipts with a journal head moving every minute, with CAL-V0-116 rewritten-prefix detection intact (negative test).
PENDING answers or doctor split complete versus prefix walks with elapsed time and restart counts.
The ATR spec documents the PENDING progress member or cites PSR-V0-112.
body: GitHub #1063. V1-1617 (PR #1069) delivered: detached acquire progress (PSR-V0-112), compact help cost note (PSR-V0-114), resume after compaction (PSR-V0-115). Remaining: (1) starting the audit from a writer checkpoint was declined there because the CAL-V0-264 writer route drops CAL-V0-116 rewritten-prefix detection; orchestrator decision 2026-10-17: keep CAL-V0-116 detection, so fix speed via root cause and a faster prefix walk instead. (2) Unconfirmed hypothesis from the 1617 lane: one failed resume-base build sets a command-wide no-resume flag, so the remaining rounds of 16 each run a complete audit. (3) Linear extrapolation (not measured): 155-282 s first audit at 47k receipts, so a non-detached 150 s call cannot succeed. (4) The PENDING progress member is documented only in PSR, not ATR.
title: pool acquire stays CPU-bound for 38+ min re-walking a moving journal (GitHub #1063)

acceptanceCriteria: The orchestration procedure (lane charter or orchestrator guidance) caps concurrently running Go-test-heavy lanes by measured host pressure (default at most 3-4 on this host); docs-only lanes may exceed it.
The cap reuses the existing host-pressure signal (V1-0694 level) or documents why it cannot.
A retained before/after measurement over at least one batch shows median load average and focused-test duration with the cap applied.
body: Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. Lanes dispatched with the Claude Code Agent tool do not go through the corvint-tasks dispatch host-pressure throttle (V1-0694, V1-0862, V1-0891), so nothing caps them by host load. Observed: 2,462 uptime samples in lane output had load median 59.95, p90 79.84, max 245.84 on 12 cores. Memory compressor held about 18 GB; 9.0M swapouts; disk 96% full. Focused `go test -run` averaged 1.8 min over 1,962 runs, and several lanes spent hours deflaking tests that flake under load (V1-1532, V1-1495, V1-1392). Expected: lane concurrency follows host capacity. Actual: a fixed cap of 5 then 7 lanes, set by owner instruction, regardless of load. That load caused the slowdowns is an inference from the timings, not a controlled measurement.
title: Orchestrator lanes bypass the host-pressure throttle: 7 concurrent Claude Code lanes kept a 12-core host at load average 60 for 77 h

acceptanceCriteria: A repository script (or documented wrapper) admits `go test` / `go build ./...` through a host-wide counting lock with a configurable limit and bounded `-p`.
Lane charters use the wrapper for every heavy Go command.
Measured: with 5 concurrent lanes, a representative focused package test's wall time is within 1.5x of its quiet-host time, or the remaining gap is recorded.
body: Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. Lanes ran go test 2,464 times for 90.9 h total; there were 166 go test commands over 10 min (28.2 h). Each lane runs `go test -count=1` independently, so 5-7 lanes overlap Go builds and test binaries on 12 cores. Expected: heavy test and build commands across lanes are admitted through one host-wide counting lock (about 2 heavy runs at once, `-p` bounded per run), so each run finishes in its quiet-host time. Related: V1-1550/V1-1573 capacity slots cover Tasks pool acquire, not ad-hoc lane test commands.
title: Concurrent lanes need a shared host test semaphore so go test runs queue instead of thrashing

acceptanceCriteria: Lane charters supply BASE, outcome, verify file and citation plan up front, and run the post-commit dogfood change/check/seal once, after the last edit, through the finish-lane recipe.
A missing input is refused before any expensive work starts, naming every missing input at once.
Measured over the next batch: dogfood-change invocations per lane median at most 2, with the counts retained.
Freeze source, intent and citation plan after implementation/citation review; a content change invalidates only evidence allowed by its actual binding rules, never silently carries stale results.

The closeout coordinator enforces bounded scope and executes independent checks concurrently only when their state/lock contracts permit, with interruption cleanup and retained per-check results. Compare complete-run command count, repeated checks and wall time on representative scoped changes; preserve every required gate and report missing cost telemetry as NOT_OBSERVED.
body:
Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. Over 206 lanes: dogfood-change ran 855 times (27.9 h, avg 2.0 min), dogfood-check 226 (7.9 h), dogfood-seal 179 (4.5 h). Per-lane dogfood-change count: median 4, tail 17-19. Refusals seen in outputs: `dogfood-change: FAIL not-complete` (58), missing DOGFOOD_OUTCOME/DOGFOOD_VERIFY_FILE (13), `BASE is required` (19). Lanes made 116 edits after their first commit, each forcing a re-bind. 60% of lane time (207 h of 345 h) came after the first commit, 67.5 h of it dogfood. The single finish-lane recipe (V1-1348) exists but lanes are not held to running it once at the terminal boundary. Related: V1-1616 (finish-lane over 600 s).

Owner required these closeout optimizations for 1.0 on 2026-10-30. During V1-1894 the real tests took roughly 38-100 seconds per run, while serial manual preparation, repeated evidence work and broadening the active task delayed delivery. Finish implementation and citation review before freezing the candidate; run final checks once per valid input binding, rerun only invalidated checks, and schedule independent work concurrently only when shared locks/state permit. Preserve one builder/independent review, exact-head bindings and required gates; no inference that short logs equal lower billed cost. Current transcript/evidence /private/tmp/v1-1894/.
title: Lanes rerun dogfood-change 4-19 times each; 855 runs cost 28 h where the protocol needs about 2 per lane

acceptanceCriteria: The dogfood wrappers reuse a previously built current-tree corvint binary when a recorded input key (build-input tree digest, VERSION, Go version) matches and those paths are clean, and rebuild otherwise; DCW-V0-022 current-tree identity is preserved and the spec is updated in the same change.

body: Evidence: owner-requested performance search on 2026-10-17. Measured with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 615, corvint-tasks build 615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host at load average 80-84 (wall times are inflated by load; CPU times are the stable signal). Lanes ran dogfood-change 855 times, check 226, seal 179 and finish 152; at the 16 s warm floor that is at least 6 h of lane time spent relinking an unchanged binary. Expected: the wrapper reuses the previously built binary when the build inputs are unchanged (for example keyed by the Git tree digest of the build inputs plus go.sum, VERSION and GOVERSION, with a clean-worktree check for those paths), and rebuilds otherwise. Distinct from V1-1629, which reduces how often lanes run dogfood at all.
title: dogfood wrappers rebuild cmd/corvint on every invocation: 16 s warm, 57 s cold, about 1,400 lane invocations

acceptanceCriteria: When `corvint context` (and other snapshot readers) runs without a usable snapshot, its output names that it did a full build and how long it took, and suggests `corvint index`; read-only behaviour is unchanged.

sourceImports skips files that cannot contain an import before running the regex, with byte-identical index output (test retained) and the measured build-time change recorded.
body: Evidence: owner-requested performance search on 2026-10-17. Measured with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 615, corvint-tasks build 615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host at load average 80-84 (wall times are inflated by load; CPU times are the stable signal). Lane counts come from orchestrator session 03e2afac subagent transcripts (206 lanes). `corvint context` reads a snapshot only when `corvint index` wrote one and never writes one itself (cmd/corvint/taskcontext.go). In a fresh clone or worktree every call does a full in-memory build: measured 22.76 s wall, 7.25 s user, 813-840 MB max RSS at origin/main c92ee0015 with no snapshot, versus 5.82 s wall, 0.43 s user in the primary checkout with a snapshot of its tree. Lane transcripts show 46 `corvint context` calls but only 6 `corvint index` calls, so most lane context calls paid the full build (transcript p50 16.0 s). CPU profile of the no-snapshot call: compileSources 30%, tokeniseSource/buildTermTable 15%, sourceImports regexp.FindAllStringSubmatchIndex 14.5% (an import regex run over every source; a cheap byte prefilter could skip most files), buildSymbolWindows 12%, worktreePin 10%. Snapshots are now 138-163 MB per tree with a recorded 37.8 s build (V1-0328 still says 63 MB). Related: V1-0418 (dirty-worktree overlay).
title: corvint context rebuilds the whole index on every call in a checkout without a snapshot: 22.8 s and 813 MB versus 5.8 s

acceptanceCriteria: One generator invocation produces REQUIREMENTS.tsv, INDEX.json and README.md from a single read of the staged specs, with byte-identical outputs to the current three-pass generator (test retained).
Blob reads are pipelined through one cat-file batch process rather than one synchronous request per file; the SRG-V0-001 Git-index-only rule is unchanged.
Measured: `make spec-requirements` and `make spec-requirements-check` wall and CPU before and after on the same host, retained.
body: Evidence: owner-requested performance search on 2026-10-17. Measured with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 615, corvint-tasks build 615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host at load average 80-84 (wall times are inflated by load; CPU times are the stable signal). Lane counts come from orchestrator session 03e2afac subagent transcripts (206 lanes). SPEC_GENERATE in the Makefile runs script/gen-spec-requirements.sh three times (tsv, --index, --readme). Each run reads all 207 tracked docs/specs files through a `git cat-file --batch` co-process, but writes one request and waits for its reply before the next, so a pass makes 207 sequential round trips. Measured at load 82: the three passes took 9.83 s, 11.31 s and 12.66 s wall for 0.8-0.9 s user each; a full `make spec-requirements` took 52.71 s wall for 4.55 s CPU. Lanes ran `make spec-requirements` 188 times (1.59 h, p50 25.9 s) plus spec-requirements-check (p50 41.4 s), which runs the same three passes before `go test ./internal/specindex`. Expected: one pass reads each blob once and emits all three outputs, and batch requests are pipelined (write all paths, then read the replies in order) so wall time tracks CPU. Related: V1-1525 (generated file conflicts between lanes), V1-0515.
title: make spec-requirements takes 34-52 s for about 3 s of CPU: three full passes, each with 207 synchronous cat-file round trips
