acceptanceCriteria: Policy accepts ticketBudget.overrides[] with exactly one selector (ticket, label or kind) and sessionsPerDay and/or tokensPerDay; malformed or ambiguous entries refuse with a stable code.
Precedence is defined and tested: ticket over label over kind over the default; ties among labels resolve deterministically.
The same rolling-window and exhaustion rules apply per effective limit.
dispatch status and the budget report show each ticket's effective limit, the selector that set it, and the hold reason.
Without overrides behaviour and output are unchanged.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1066 (2026-10-17), follow-up to #652/V1-0937. ticketBudget (CAL-V0-155) is one uniform {sessionsPerDay, tokensPerDay} for every ticket; observed queues need a productive ticket at ~56 sessions/day while stuck tickets need 6-8. Operators keep an external per-ticket cap file and wrapper, which duplicates budget logic and is invisible to dispatch status. Ask: ticketBudget.overrides[] keyed by ticket id and/or label or kind, same rolling-window and exhaustion rules; dispatch status shows the effective limit and why a ticket is held. New requirements go to the dispatch domain spec (ATR-V0 or its successor), not CAL-V0.
title: dispatch ticketBudget: per-ticket and per-label overrides with effective limit and hold reason in dispatch status (issue #1066)

acceptanceCriteria: An operator-run qualification verb checks a supplied json-reporter document against the existing fixture checks and records the version in a store-local allow-list with retained evidence; failures refuse with a stable code.
A ticket or policy can declare a local test repository; witness commit resolution and the TOL-V0-012 spec check run there.
A Playwright 1.64 json report from a separate test repository credits a row whose test passed at retry 0.
Refusal codes are unchanged for unqualified versions and undeclared repositories.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1070 (2026-10-17). (1) The qualified Playwright version allow-list is empty, so every real json-reporter document is refused UNSUPPORTED_VERSION (TOL-V0-009); an adopter on 1.64 has no qualification path. (2) The witness commit and the spec containing the obligation id (TOL-V0-012) must resolve in the task-store repository, so a layout with tests in a separate repository cannot witness. Proposal: an operator verb that runs the existing fixture checks on a supplied retained report and appends the version to a store-local allow-list with evidence (or minor/patch qualification by passing fixture); a ticket- or policy-declared test repository where TOL-V0-012 is checked.
title: ticket obligations witness: adopter qualification path for newer Playwright versions and witness commits resolved in a declared test repository (issue #1070)

acceptanceCriteria: Alias limit raised to 128 bytes, and the refusal names the limit.
plan accepts witnessed rows as explicit rerun entries, does not require non-core rows, and excludes BLOCKED/DEFECT unless listed.
An optional PARTIAL (or per-step progress) state exists and never counts as witnessed.
Witness events accept optional bounded provenance fields testCommit, environmentTree and evidenceRef plus the test title; show reports them per witness.
A 110-row ledger with 78-character ids seeds; a plan listing witnessed regression rows and omitting non-core rows passes.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1071 (2026-10-17). Migrating a real per-ticket obligation ledger hits: (1) alias cap 64 bytes (TOL-V0-034..036) refuses 60 of 4,562 ids, e.g. a 78-char id MALFORMED without the limit in the message; (2) plan refuses ALREADY_CLOSED for intentionally listed witnessed regression rows and UNASSIGNED for optional non-core rows; (3) BLOCKED and DEFECT rows count as open for planning; (4) no PARTIAL state for rows with some steps witnessed; (5) a witness lacks test-repository commit, environment tree, evidence ref and test title. Related: V1-1199 (aliases in plan documents), #1070.
title: ticket obligations migration blockers: alias length, plan rerun/non-core/BLOCKED semantics, PARTIAL state, witness provenance (issue #1071)

acceptanceCriteria: store.Mutate (notes, ticket writes, evidence, obligation witness), attempt heartbeat, release and every read verb resume from a verified checkpoint and validate only receipts after it, with the same refusals as a full audit for any prefix tampering the checkpoint binds (spec requirement + negative tests).
The checkpoint is refreshed under the existing writer lock by whoever extends it; concurrent processes share it instead of each redoing the prefix.
A retained measurement on a >=47k-receipt store with the head moving every 30 s: note write and heartbeat < 1 s, read < 0.5 s, CPU scales with receipts since the checkpoint, not total length.
--timing (or the existing audit-mode output) reports FULL vs CHECKPOINT_PLUS_TAIL on mutation verbs.
Full-audit fallback when the checkpoint is absent, stale, or fails its binding is retained and tested.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1072 (2026-10-17, owner-prioritised). On a ~47,700-receipt (455 MB) store, `ticket note set` takes 47 s wall / 45 s user, CPU-bound in cli.noteCommand -> submitMutation -> store.Mutate -> mutateLocked -> journal.Reader.auditForMutation -> audit -> walk (Reader.step/validateRecord, wire parser, checkHostile, snapshot.ReceiptRestorer.Next restoring elided receipts). Reads after any head move pay the same walk (ticket show >51 s, queue status 14 s vs 0.1-0.2 s at an unmoved head). Five live attempts' heartbeats ran 0:38-2:21 each at 65-125% CPU; total ~640% CPU in corvint-tasks. The read path already has a retained checkpoint (journal.Checkpoint, CHECKPOINT_PLUS_TAIL in cli/lease.go readCheckpoint) and lease writes have verified-cache reuse, but auditForMutation calls audit(nil, requestID, lim, false) with no checkpoint. Broader than #1063 (V1-1626, pool acquire). Related: #1055 (V1-1618 journal retention), #1010, V1-1617/#1069.
title: Tasks store: every store.Mutate write and checkpoint-missing read re-audits the whole journal from receipt 1 (45 s CPU per note write at 47k receipts) (issue #1072)

acceptanceCriteria: corvint-update check --allow-network --component core completes with a release relation (installed vs available) on the reporter host, or the observation bound is configurable or robust to slow first launch/loaded hosts while still failing closed on genuinely unobservable snapshots.
A regression test covers a version smoke whose descendant snapshot exceeds the old bound but completes within the new/configured bound.
body: SUSPECTED defect (not confirmed; looks like a timing bound, not a version mismatch). Observed 2026-10-17, macOS Darwin 25.6.0. Command: corvint-update check --allow-network --component core. Output: {"component":"core","freshness":"UNKNOWN","action":"check",...,"publisherIdentity":"NOT_VERIFIED"} then: version smoke failed: descendant snapshots were unavailable for 6.079s, beyond the 5s observation bound. Installed core: Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 615). The same check with --component tasks worked (installed build 615, available tasks-dev-20260929.2 build 202, relation LOCAL_NEWER, apply refused as downgrade). Expected: core check reports installed vs available release and relation. Actual: freshness UNKNOWN because the installed-binary version smoke exceeded its 5s observation bound (possibly slow first launch or host load). Related, distinct: V1-1368 (completed; 1s descendantSnapshotTimeout failed on loaded host, passed on retry) and V1-0568 (open; descendant snapshot unavailable in desktop sandbox). Not yet checked: whether a retry passes.
title: corvint-update check --component core: version smoke fails with descendant snapshots unavailable 6.079s beyond the 5s observation bound (suspected defect)

acceptanceCriteria: A deadline overrun in the dogfood-change impact step yields a visible NOT_OBSERVED/abstention or one bounded retry instead of exit 2.
The deadline value and any override are documented and tested.
A test reproduces the overrun with an injected slow git.
body: Observed 2026-10-17 in lane gh-tasks3 (PR #1076), load 55-95 on 12 cores: coordination-time-impact exited 2 'Git repository index exceeded its deadline' on ~20 of 22 tries; the diff-tree --find-copies-harder took 13-33 s against the hard-coded 30 s gitDeadline (internal/contextindex/git.go:26), which has no override. dogfood-change does not retry and the exit is not an admitted abstention, so each miss cost a ~20 min rerun. Expected: a bounded deadline-overrun degrades to a recorded abstention/NOT_OBSERVED or a single bounded retry, or the deadline is configurable within a recorded bound.
title: dogfood-change: contextindex 30s gitDeadline exits 2 under host load with no retry or admitted abstention

acceptanceCriteria: A measurement on a >=8k receipt store shows whether non-publishing refreshes recur per write.
If confirmed: backoff or reason trace with a regression test; if not, close with the evidence.
body: Inferred from code by the V1-1650 lane (PR #1075), not measured: once head is >=512 past FullSeq every writer-route write schedules a full refresh after unlock; a refresh that publishes nothing (intent-only divergence, cleanup, unsettled move, lock failure, supersession, newer checkpoint) leaves FullSeq behind, so the next write pays again until the 4096 bound. Expected: bounded backoff or a recorded reason so persistent non-publication does not reintroduce per-write full audits (the #1072 symptom).
title: suspected: refreshWriterCheckpoint can re-run a complete audit on every write when a refresh publishes nothing

acceptanceCriteria: Each item is delivered, or declined with a recorded reason.
Repeated retire/compact/export on a sealed store is tested.
Owner decision recorded on the non-terminal carry rule.
body: V1-1618 (PR #1074, JRT-V0-001..014) residuals: (1) export, compaction and import refuse on a sealed store and CLI archive restore is unimplemented, so retire is one-shot; (2) a sealed store has no checkpoint route, ReviewFold refolds from S each tick; (3) handoff policies, review submissions, artifacts and admits before S are not seeded, so a later receipt naming one refuses, and replaying a retired request ID returns UNSUPPORTED; (4) a consistently forged seal is detectable only against the archive; (5) non-terminal tickets are carried by value in the seal, owner may prefer an all-terminal rule; (6) REDO_PENDING refusal untested, seal not charged to capacity; (7) doctor journal key additive to TQD-V0-001 field list. Review-round findings are handled in the #1074 fix round, not here.
title: journal retention follow-ups: retire is one-shot, sealed store has no checkpoint route, pre-seal objects not seeded (V1-1618 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: Items 1-4 delivered with tests or declined with reason.
Item 5 recorded against the verb-freeze decision.
body: PR #1076 residuals: (1) ticket worktree head is not recorded on release or completion (V1-1588); (2) defects harvest from Playwright or CI reports is not implemented (V1-1593); (3) CLI pre-parse know-how screen ignores declared values, screening only at apply time (V1-1602); (4) reusing a ticket branch no longer descending from base only warns; (5) verbs live in corvint-tasks not Core because of the verb freeze.
title: ticket worktrees / defect register / know-how screen follow-ups (V1-1588/1593/1602 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: The probe runs outside the writer lock and its result is revalidated under it.

`Name ||= ...` is treated as a local definition.
Local definitions later in the file shadow references in earlier qualified reopens, or the limit is recorded as a spec failure mode.
Each case has a TestRubyAutoload* regression test.
body: Residuals from the PR #1088 review fixes (V1-1674, NGI-V0-017/018, internal/contextindex/ruby_autoload.go). Conservative (they add reports, never hide them): (1) `A::B = ...` and `::X = ...` are counted as references, not definitions; (2) a qualified class/module reopen sees only local definitions earlier in the file; (3) `Name ||= ...` is not a definition. Expected: each defines the constant in its lexical namespace and shadows the autoloaded one, like plain `Name =`.
title: Ruby autoload impact: qualified/rooted constant assignments, ||= and later local definitions mis-classified (V1-1674 residuals)

acceptanceCriteria: A CLI fixture provides a scope deriver (or the equivalent seam) so `claim --next` runs NextClaimTicket end to end.
A CLI test asserts that `plan --pool` preview and `claim --next` select the same ticket with waiters present.
body: Gap from the PR #1087 review round (V1-0785, PSR-V0-132). internal/tasks/cli fixtures have no scope deriver, so the NextClaimTicket path that `claim --next` takes cannot be exercised through the public CLI; agreement with `plan --pool` holds only by construction (shared claimNextInput) and a transaction-level test. A divergence in CLI wiring (Now/Barrier inputs) would go undetected.
title: tests: CLI fixtures run without a scope deriver, so claim --next (NextClaimTicket) is unobservable end to end

acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic test reproduces or rules out the stale-starting-child race after a kept LOCK_TIMEOUT relaunch.
If reproduced, the relaunch yields a single coherent result (or a named refusal), never an exit 1 without a result; the ATR spec records the failure mode.
body: Suspected, not confirmed. Residual from the V1-1671 fix (PR #1095, ATR-V0-095, internal/tasks/cli/lease_detach.go). When a launcher died before recording its child (ATR-V0-021), that stale starting child can take the `running` lock after the new launcher moves result.json and relaunches without the ATR-V0-027 liveness check. The store replay keeps the mutation exactly once, but the new child exits 1 without a result, so the attach reports a failure with no result document. No test covers it.
title: SUSPECTED: detach relaunch after a kept LOCK_TIMEOUT can race a stale starting child (ATR-V0-021 hazard after ATR-V0-095)

acceptanceCriteria: A test with a registry key read only inside a template substitution either selects the setup or fails closed to ALL.
If confirmed, the fix is traced to a TSA-V0 requirement.
body: Suspected, inferred and not tested. Residual from V1-1698 (PR #1096). The new shared-constant path in internal/contextindex/setup_shared.go re-lexes template ${} substitutions, but the registry-key path (registryCallSites, setup_select.go/registry_dialect.go) does not appear to, so a registry key read only inside `${REGISTRY.key}` may be missed while the result still reports selected (fail-open).
title: SUSPECTED: setup-select registry-key path misses key reads inside template ${} substitutions

acceptanceCriteria: A paging or --max-commits option reads a range larger than the bound in deterministic parts, each naming its continuation.
The bound or deadline is derived from, or documented against, a measured rate, with the measurement recorded.
body: Residual from V1-1699 (PR #1096, UCL1142-V0-008). The bound was measured at about 20 s for 512 commits on the lane host, so a slower host can still hit the 30 s deadline and refuse with changes-timeout. Wide ranges get only a refusal and no way to read them in parts.
title: changes: 512-commit bound is not a time guarantee; add paging or --max-commits for wide upgrade ranges

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint affected` (or the focused local check list) includes GOOS=windows go vet for touched packages, matching the CI step.
A regression fixture where a test uses a helper from a unix-only file is flagged locally before push.
body: Recurring class: V1-1092 (dispatch prompt_fragments_test.go used unix-only testConfig) and again PR #1089 on 2026-10-18 (internal/tasks/store/lease_bounded_audit_test.go uses newResumeFixture, moving and rewriteReceiptKeepingStamps from a unix-constrained file), each found only by CI job "Windows vet including test files (AFP-V0-042)", which costs a CI round and blocks merge. Neither `corvint affected` plans nor the lane doc-gate list run cross-OS vet locally.
title: Lanes miss Windows-only vet failures until CI: add GOOS=windows vet to the focused/affected local check

acceptanceCriteria: A shared bound/limit helper (or documented contract) in internal/contextindex makes bound exhaustion return a typed unresolved reason that callers must propagate to ALL/uncertainty.
A table-driven test drives every analyzer bound (depth, hop, nesting, template depth, source size) one past its limit and asserts no `selected`/certain result.
A negative-cache rule: in-progress recursion markers are never stored as permanent negative results (regression test with an export cycle).
Spec requirement recorded in the governing contextindex/TSA spec.
body: Recurring class across reviews: PR #1096 Codex (2026-10-18) found 7 P1 fail-opens in internal/contextindex/setup_shared.go (re-export hop bound, template depth bound, cycle marker cached as negative, export * as, require/dynamic import, namespace values, declaring-module reads); PR #1088 Codex found an unenforced Ruby nesting bound; V1-1478 and V1-1717 track similar JS/TS registry fail-opens. Each analyzer hand-rolls its bounds, and hitting one returns the same result as a genuine negative. This breaks product invariant 2 (missing evidence yields uncertainty, never invented certainty). Related: V1-1478, V1-1717.
title: contextindex analyzers need one fail-closed bound contract: every exhausted bound or unsupported form must emit an unresolved reason, never a silent selected

acceptanceCriteria: The launch-lock wait is bounded by the same command deadline as the running-lock wait and the await.
A test with two concurrent --detach launchers of one record shows --wait 0 returns within a small bound with a named outcome.
body: Residual from V1-1671 review fix (PR #1095, head 143979ca2). leaseDetachLaunch calls lockLeaseDetach(leaseDetachLockName, leaseDetachLockBound) before the single command deadline applies, so a concurrent --detach of the same record can block up to 10 s even with --wait 0. A launcher that now waits on the running lock (up to min(10 s, its --wait)) lengthens that hold. Expected: --wait 0 returns immediately even under launcher contention; --wait N returns within N plus scheduling slack. Recorded as a failure mode in the amended ATR-V0-095 text.
title: tasks lease --detach: launch-lock wait (up to 10 s) runs outside the caller --wait bound under concurrent launchers (ATR-V0-024)

acceptanceCriteria: corvint-tasks doctor lists each active attempt whose branch is missing base shared-path commits older than a threshold, naming the ticket and oldest commit.
A claim result includes a notice when the claimed base is missing shared-path commits present on main.
Both are read-only and covered by tests.
body: Residual from V1-1710 (PR #1097, GitHub #1092). `corvint changes behind --format doctor-plugin` emits SHARED_BASE_BEHIND for one branch, but nothing discovers live ticket worktrees and runs it, and a claim result never mentions shared-path commits the branch lacks. Expected: corvint-tasks doctor (or dispatch) enumerates active attempts/worktrees and flags stale ones; claim reports missing shared commits at claim time.
title: corvint-tasks doctor/claim: detect live ticket worktrees missing base shared-path commits (built-in, not only the doctor-plugin output)

acceptanceCriteria: Age is computed from the first-parent commit on base that introduced the change.
Output records the base ref and its last-observed time (e.g. FETCH_HEAD mtime) so a stale base is visible.
body: Residual from V1-1710 (PR #1097). Age of the oldest missing shared commit is its committer time, so a commit authored long ago but merged recently looks stale immediately, and the command never fetches, so a stale origin/main understates what is missing. Both are recorded as failure modes in SPC-V0. Expected: age measured from arrival on the base (first-parent merge time), and output states the base ref observation time.
title: changes behind: age uses committer time, not arrival on base; stale remote-tracking base understates missing commits

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood prepare output lists the modified paths that are not citable, or a plan-check verb validates a citation plan against the diff without binding.
All refused rows are reported in one pass with their reason codes.
Measured over a batch: first-attempt bind refusals for citation rules drop to 0.
body: Friction observed 2026-10-18: 3 of 4 lanes this batch (PR #1090, #1095, #1098) had their first dogfood-finish refused because the citation plan cited a file or span the change modifies (cite-span-not-stable, cite-self-modified-authority under CEM-V1-114). Each refusal costs a full prepare/bind cycle (minutes, plus a lane retry budget of 2). The rule is only discovered at bind time. Expected: prepare (or a cheap `cem cite --check-plan`) emits the set of citable paths (unmodified by BASE..HEAD) and validates a draft plan before the expensive bind, naming every bad row at once.
title: dogfood prepare should list citable sources up front; lanes lose a bind attempt to cite-self-modified-authority / cite-span-not-stable

acceptanceCriteria: The lane finish path (or an installable pre-push hook) runs make windows-vet when Go inputs changed and refuses on failure.
A test shows a unix-only helper reference is refused before push.
body: Residual from V1-1719 (PR #1098, AFP-V0-054). `corvint affected` lists `conditional make windows-vet` and AGENTS.md mentions it, but no pre-push hook, finish-lane recipe or local gate runs it, so an agent that skips the advisory still burns a CI round (V1-1092, PR #1089 class). Expected: the lane finish recipe (dogfood-finish or batch-check) or an opt-in pre-push hook runs it when .go/go.mod/go.sum change.
title: make windows-vet is advisory only: nothing runs it before push, so Windows vet failures still reach CI

acceptanceCriteria: A test with a shallow clone whose merge base is beyond the shallow boundary shows changes behind/check-shared refuse or report a named reason instead of a wrong clean result.
A test where the merge base is within the boundary passes with the same result as a full clone.
body: Residual from V1-1710 review fix (PR #1097, head 3d173f824). The dry merge now runs git merge-tree in a temporary bare repository with the real object store as an alternate and GIT_SHALLOW_FILE passed through. The shallow passthrough was checked by hand only, and that check could not distinguish shallow from non-shallow because the depth-2 clone still reached the merge base.
title: sharedpath dry merge: no maintained test for the temporary-GIT_DIR probe in a shallow clone (GIT_SHALLOW_FILE passthrough)

acceptanceCriteria: An opt-in flag or policy member copies built-in merge attributes and rename config into the probe; external merge/filter drivers are never honoured.
A test shows merge=union resolves where the default reports conflict, and a custom driver still never runs.
body: Residual from V1-1710 review fix (PR #1097). To stay read-only, the dry merge now runs with no repository config or attributes, so built-in attribute drivers (merge=union, merge=binary, -merge) and rename settings are ignored; it can report a conflict the repository would resolve (recorded in SPC-V0-003 as a conservative approximation). Expected: an opt-in mode that copies only built-in-driver attributes and rename config into the probe, never external drivers.
title: sharedpath dry merge: optionally honour built-in .gitattributes merge settings (union, binary) and rename config safely

acceptanceCriteria: A destructured or method parameter shadowing an imported shared constant is not counted as a read
A later-scope shadow does not force ALL
Regression tests in internal/contextindex cover each form
body: Residual from PR #1096 review fix (V1-1698). Simple parameter/declaration shadowing is handled, but destructured and method parameters and later uses of a shadowed name in the same scope still over-select or return ALL. Conservative (no fail-open) but noisy.
title: tests setup-select shared-constant reads lack lexical scope analysis: later-shadowed names over-select or force ALL

acceptanceCriteria: A fixture exceeding 4096 lookups yields unresolved (not not-a-constant) and is not cached
Test fails if the bound is removed
body: Residual from PR #1096 (V1-1698): the hop bound (8) and template depth bound (8) have tests; the 4096 total-lookup bound returns unresolved but has no dedicated test.
title: Add a regression test for the 4096-lookup bound in shared-constant setup resolution

acceptanceCriteria: Imported JSON module top-level keys resolve as constant keys
Unparseable JSON fails closed (ALL with a named reason)
body: Residual from PR #1096 (V1-1698): a setup reading keys from an imported .json module is not recognised as a shared-constant read, so a JSON key change cannot narrow selection.
title: tests setup-select does not treat JSON module exports as shared constants

acceptanceCriteria: Count of ALL outcomes attributable to open setups on the frozen eval corpus is recorded
If above an agreed threshold, a narrowing ticket is filed
body: Residual from PR #1096 (V1-1698): any setup reading through an unresolved import is recorded as open and forces ALL for every change reaching a shared read. Safe but possibly noisy; frequency on real repositories is NOT_OBSERVED.
title: Measure how often unresolved-import open setups force ALL in tests setup-select

acceptanceCriteria: A check (CI or merge-queue) refuses a PR whose analyzer schema number equals main's while the pinned hash differs
Docs name the recovery (rebump to next number)
body: Observed 2026-10-18: PR #1088 (V1-1674) and PR #1096 (V1-1698) both bump the analyzer schema to corvint-analyzer/122 with different pinned hashes. Whichever merges second fails its schema pin test in the merge queue or silently reuses a number for different analyzer content. No check reserves or detects colliding schema numbers across open branches.
title: Concurrent PRs bumping corvint-analyzer schema to the same number are not detected before merge

acceptanceCriteria: A spec section (amending docs/specs/change-compiled-e2e-v0.md or a new spec) states the prover's intent, numbered requirements, non-goals, failure modes and rollback, with the owner's kill/pivot decision of 2026-10-18 as authority.

`corvint-test e2e prove` (or its successor) runs an existing hosted Playwright test, selected by name or file, at base and head with the test tree held at head, and reports the CCE-V0-009/016..018 verdict ladder without compiling anything.
A behaviour-removal control (omitted-event, V1-1679) kills the F1 static-overlay falsifier, and a no-op diff does not score as useful (V1-1713).
A rerun on actualbudget/actual's 4 fixes that shipped hosted e2e tests (3234be04d, c65884a27, eb28966d6, bc9bba67f) records per-change verdicts, minutes and usefulness in a build-log entry.
body: Owner decision 2026-10-18 after the V1-1677 spike (docs/build-log/2026-10-18-cce-spike-v1-1677.md): kill V0 compilation and pivot to a discrimination prover over hosted tests. The spike found 0/10 fixes useful, because the map, the impact hop and the oracle form each failed. 4/10 of those fixes shipped a hosted e2e test, and those tests use getByRole, toBeVisible and other forms that V0 cannot emit. The prover takes hosted tests as given and proves whether they discriminate the change, reusing the delivered prove machinery: BBF controls, the CCE-V0-021 environment block (V1-1681, beamfall/corvint#1091), and receipts. Its known holes from the falsifiers: F1 static text reads DISCRIMINATES (sha256:d6e205fb...), and F2 no-op reads PRESERVES (sha256:5647a092...).
title: CCE pivot: discrimination prover over existing hosted Playwright tests (no compilation)

acceptanceCriteria: make dogfood-finish (or dogfood-change prepare) runs spec-requirements-check when the diff touches docs/specs/** and refuses with the make spec-requirements recovery
Regression test: a fixture spec edit without regeneration is refused before bind
body: Observed 2026-10-18 on PR #1097 (V1-1710): review-fix commit 6ea521b95 edited docs/specs/shared-path-change-policy-v0.md without regenerating docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv. make dogfood-finish bound and sealed it, the lane pushed, and CI doc-gates spec-requirements-check failed (line 3487 stale), costing a CI round and a repair lane. Expected: a stale generated requirements index is refused locally before bind/seal.
title: dogfood bind/seal accepts a spec edit whose REQUIREMENTS.tsv was not regenerated; stale index first caught in CI

acceptanceCriteria: A supported landing watcher classifies CI failures against a declared flake list and reruns within a cap
Bot merge-queue ejection is re-queued within a cap; human dequeue is never overridden
Every unrecoverable state produces an escalation event the owning session receives
body: Observed 2026-10-18: detached per-PR waiters exited on any non-infra CI failure (known flake TestPSRV0111) without notifying the session, and kept polling with auto-merge off after github-merge-queue ejected #1085/#1094. Six PRs sat 06:00-10:40Z until the owner asked. Interim fix in the orchestrator scratch tooling: known-flake rerun (max 3 attempts), bot-ejection re-arm (max 2), and an alerts file tailed by a session-tracked Monitor. Product gap: Corvint/Tasks has no supported PR-landing supervisor that classifies failures (flake vs real), re-queues after bot ejection, and escalates to the owning session.
title: Orchestrator PR waiters exit silently on CI failure and never re-arm after merge-queue ejection

acceptanceCriteria: The test reports go list's stderr (exec.ExitError.Stderr) on failure.
The cause is identified from a failing CI log, and either the read scope or the invocation is fixed, or the ticket records it under the V1-0849 flake umbrella with the evidence.
body: Suspected (not confirmed) flake. cmd/corvint-test/main_test.go:115 runs exec.Command("go","list","-deps","../corvint").Output() and on error calls t.Fatal(err), which discards stderr. In CI run 39092839754 job 117573437918 (beamfall/corvint#1086, docs-only on top of claude/cce-e2e-companion-1665, go-product-shard (0), Landlock-confined per .corvint/test-read-scopes.json, ubuntu, 2026-10-18) it failed in 0.09s with only 'main_test.go:117: exit status 1'. The same test with identical code and read scopes passed in run 39093442555 (beamfall/corvint#1081). Expected: pass, or a failure that names the go list error. Actual: opaque intermittent failure. Cause unknown; candidates are Landlock denying a path go list reads (GOROOT, GOMODCACHE, GOENV) or a concurrent build-cache condition.
title: Suspected flake: TestCCEV0015CoreBoundary fails with a bare 'exit status 1' from go list -deps

acceptanceCriteria: Positive test on route R fails with 403 while two rejection-only tests on R pass with 403: both reported ANCHOR-FAILED and not credited
Same run with the positive test passing: both ANCHORED
Rejection-only test with no success on its route in the run: UNANCHORED warning, cleared by a declared positive sibling
Missing route/actor evidence yields uncertainty, never ANCHORED
Spec requirements, traceability and regression tests added
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1099. A test asserting only a rejection (4xx, error code, denied UI state) can pass for the wrong reason (e.g. a tenant feature flag off makes every request 403) and test-validity credits it as a witness. Add an anchor axis: rejection-only tests are ANCHORED when the same run has a success on the same method+route template for the same actor/fixture, UNANCHORED when none exists (warning, clearable by declaring a positive sibling), ANCHOR-FAILED when the declared/observed positive sibling failed in the same run (blocks crediting). Owning spec: docs/specs/mcp-test-validity-profile-v0.md (or the provider result contract it cites).
title: test-validity: classify rejection-only witnesses ANCHORED / UNANCHORED / ANCHOR-FAILED against same-route successes (GitHub #1099)

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded fixture or reporter produces the request-outcomes record from observed responses and decisive assertions, without author declarations.
Vitest and Go test sessions are either covered or each has a recorded NOT_APPLICABLE reason.
Tests show an undeclared rejection-only Playwright test classified from observed data.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1737 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1101, head d102a537a, LPCV-V0-080..083). Expected: a Playwright fixture records responses and classifies the decisive expect calls into the request-outcomes record automatically. Actual: only author-declared annotations exist; Corvint observes neither responses nor assertions, so an undeclared rejection-only test gets NOT_PRODUCED instead of a verdict. The TypeScript mirror, Vitest and Go test sessions have no equivalent producer.
title: test-validity: rejection anchors depend on author-declared corvint-request-outcomes; no fixture observes responses or decisive assertions

acceptanceCriteria: A spec amendment defines an anchor key for request-less rejections, or records the limit as a documented abstention.
Tests cover a UI-state rejection with and without a positive sibling.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1737 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1101, head d102a537a, LPCV-V0-080..083). Expected: rejection witnesses asserted on UI state or an error code (no HTTP request) can be anchored against a positive sibling. Actual: the anchor key is (actor, method, route), so these always give UNKNOWN.
title: test-validity: UI-state and error-code rejections without a request stay UNKNOWN for rejection anchoring

acceptanceCriteria: One named consumer withholds credit on blocksCredit with a test.
An external profile revision (or a recorded decision not to) lets profiled receipts carry the record.
The over-blocking trade-off is recorded in the spec.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1737 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1101, head d102a537a, LPCV-V0-080..083). Expected: an ANCHOR-FAILED verdict with blocksCredit=true withholds witness credit in a consumer (doccorpus witnesses, CEM verification evidence). Actual: blocksCredit is only reported; profiled receipts (including the doccorpus witnesses) refuse the record with external-profile-has-request-outcomes until an external profile revision. Also note over-blocking by design: an unrelated failure of the positive sibling blocks credit.
title: test-validity: no consumer reads rejectionAnchor.blocksCredit; profiled receipts cannot carry request-outcomes

acceptanceCriteria: Selection over a bound application repository uses an impact graph pinned to that repository's commit.
Tests show an indirect application change narrowing, and an unresolved one still selecting the full suite.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1675 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1102, head f58754780, AFU-V1-067..072); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-V1-1675-e2e-separate-repository.md Limits. Expected: a change in an application-repo file that reaches a linked application file only through imports narrows selection like a same-repo change. Actual: it is e2e-unmapped-change and selects the full relevant suite (safe but coarse; AFU-V1-070 non-goal).
title: affected e2e-safe: no impact graph over a bound application repository, so indirect application changes select the full suite

acceptanceCriteria: flows export round-trips qualified link targets with a test.
Docs maintenance resolves a qualified target in its bound repository or reports a named unbound reason, never 'absent'.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1675 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1102, head f58754780, AFU-V1-067..072); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-V1-1675-e2e-separate-repository.md Limits. Expected: flows export emits links whose targets are qualified ID:PATH, and docs maintenance resolves them in their repository. Actual: export.go skips them and docs maintenance records them as absent root inputs (both recorded spec non-goals).
title: flows export and docs maintenance drop or mis-resolve repository-qualified link targets (ID:PATH)

acceptanceCriteria: A retained live receipt from a real two-repository project with narrowed and fallback cases.
Any divergence from fixtures filed as its own ticket.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1675 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1102, head f58754780, AFU-V1-067..072); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-V1-1675-e2e-separate-repository.md Limits. Expected: one retained live run against a real two-repository project (test repo plus app repo) shows narrowed and full-suite selections matching the deterministic fixtures. Actual: NOT_RUN; only fixtures exist.
title: Live qualification of e2e-safe selection across a real separate test repository and application repository

acceptanceCriteria: A retained live Playwright 1.64 report qualifies through qualify-version.
Any shape divergence from the synthetic fixture is fixed or filed.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1648 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1103, head 49b927b3d, TOL-V0-060..067); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1648-witness-qualification.md Limits/Evidence. Expected: a real Playwright 1.64 json-reporter report of the TOLQ-1..9 fixture qualifies via `ticket obligations qualify-version`. Actual: only a synthetic report in the 1.61.1 shape was checked (TestTOLV0065); browsers were not available to the lane.
title: Run the obligation qualification fixture under a live Playwright 1.64 json reporter

acceptanceCriteria: qualify-version takes the store mutation lock around read-modify-write.
A concurrency test shows two qualifications both retained.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1648 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1103, head 49b927b3d, TOL-V0-060..067); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1648-witness-qualification.md Limits/Evidence. Expected: concurrent qualify-version runs serialize and both versions persist in taskman-obligation-qualifications.json. Actual: atomic rename without the store lock, so a concurrent writer can drop the other's entry (obligation_qualify.go).
title: obligations qualify-version writes the qualification allow-list without the store lock (last writer wins)

acceptanceCriteria: Each verb accepts --test-repository with the TOL-V0 undeclared-name refusal.
Tests cover a separate test repository for each.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1648 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1103, head 49b927b3d, TOL-V0-060..067); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1648-witness-qualification.md Limits/Evidence. Expected: run-batch, preflight and qualify-version can target a declared obligations.testRepositories entry like witness. Actual: they run only in the store worktree.
title: run-batch, preflight and qualify-version lack --test-repository parity with witness

acceptanceCriteria: A run-batch test with a store-local qualified version passes and an unqualified one refuses UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1648 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1103, head 49b927b3d, TOL-V0-060..067); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1648-witness-qualification.md Limits/Evidence. Expected: a run-batch test proves a locally qualified (unshipped) Playwright version is accepted. Actual: covered only through the shared admittedVersionsAt helper.
title: Add a direct run-batch test for a version admitted only by the store-local qualification allow-list

acceptanceCriteria: A declared operation by the current holder on its ALLOCATED member runs once and records a receipt; a non-holder is refused.
Tests cover holder, non-holder and replay.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1585 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1104, head 2215d54aa, PSR-V0-160..167); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1585-pool-member-lifecycle.md. GitHub #1028 stays open for these. Expected: the allocation holder can run declared operations (e.g. refresh, reset) on its own ALLOCATED member with a recorded receipt. Actual: operations start only from FREE or QUARANTINED, so a holder must release first.
title: pool operate: the holder of an ALLOCATED member cannot run lifecycle operations (refresh/reset on a held member)

acceptanceCriteria: Decision recorded: either a policy-gated auto-return with its safety evidence, or the current rule kept with rationale.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1585 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1104, head 2215d54aa, PSR-V0-160..167); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1585-pool-member-lifecycle.md. GitHub #1028 stays open for these. Expected (open question): a declared, verified reset/retarget could return the member to FREE without a separate confirm-safe. Actual: it stays QUARANTINED by design (PSR-V0 safety rule). Decide whether a verified-reset policy should be allowed.
title: pool operate: a passed reset/retarget from QUARANTINED needs an explicit confirm-safe to return to FREE

acceptanceCriteria: Receipt retention is bounded (last N per member/operation) or moved out of pools.json, with a test at 256 members.
A full-size pool still accepts acquire/release.
body: Found 2026-10-18 by the V1-1585 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#1104, head 2215d54aa, PSR-V0-160..167); recorded in docs/build-log/2026-10-18-v1-1585-pool-member-lifecycle.md. GitHub #1028 stays open for these. Expected: operation receipts are bounded or compacted so a full pool cannot wedge pool writes. Actual: retained receipts grow pools.json toward 1 MiB; writes then refuse LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
title: pools.json can reach its 1 MiB bound at 256 members x 5 operation receipts, then every pool write is refused LIMIT_EXCEEDED

acceptanceCriteria: Spec requirements in the Playwright provider / test-validity spec covering external-origin listing, blocking-vs-incidental classification, the validity finding, pass/fail correlation, the allow-list, and UNKNOWN when network evidence is absent

Fixture-driven tests: a CDN module dependency yields the finding with origin, resource type and first test; an allow-listed origin does not; beacon-only traffic is incidental; a pass/fail pair at one revision names the differing external request
Receipt or report output shows the external-origin list, and the build log records non-goals and limits
body: GitHub issue #1106. A browser test's outcome can depend on resources outside the test environment (an import-map module from a public CDN, analytics or survey scripts, third-party APIs). Observed: 3 of 6 runs at nearly the same revision failed in bulk; the CDN module returned 200, issued no follow-up requests and rendered nothing. The receipt gave no sign of the external dependence. Requested: (1) from run traces or network logs, list requests to origins outside the declared test environment (the app under test plus declared mocks) and classify each as blocking (script/module/awaited XHR or fetch) or incidental (beacons); (2) a validity finding when assertions depend on a page whose blocking resources came from an undeclared external origin, naming the origin, the resource type and the first affected test; (3) correlation of pass/fail splits at the same revision with the external requests that differed between runs (status, timing, missing follow-ups); (4) a project allow-list of external origins accepted as deterministic. Missing network evidence must produce UNKNOWN, never a clean verdict. Related: V1-1737 (#1099, PR #1101), which touches the same jstestprovider request-outcome code.
title: Test validity: report run dependence on undeclared external origins (live CDN modules, third-party scripts) (#1106)

acceptanceCriteria: Spec requirements in corvint-tasks-attempt-runner-v0 for active delivery, hard-stop salvage, and the context-exhausted repeat state with a configurable count, including per-host support and UNKNOWN when delivery is unsupported

Tests: a worker that never calls a dispatcher verb receives the warn and handoff notices through the delivery path (fake host); a hard-stopped attempt's salvaged note can be read by the next attempt; N consecutive hard stops of one role on one ticket raise the alert and state, and N-1 do not
Build log records the host mechanisms used, limits, and a NOT_RUN live qualification, cross-referenced to V1-1563
body: GitHub issue #1109, follow-up to #1007 (V1-1549). Context thresholds are exposed only passively, through a level file and notices on dispatcher verb output, so review-type workers that only read files never see warnTokens or handoffTokens. Observed: 6 consecutive sessions of one review role on two tickets in about 90 minutes hard-stopped with no verdict, each relaunch re-read the same inputs, and the last session's concrete findings were discarded. Requested: (1) active delivery of warn and handoff notices into the session through the host message or hook mechanism (for example a pre-tool hook or user-turn injection), so the notice arrives on the next turn whatever tool the worker calls; (2) at hardTokens, salvage the last assistant message(s) and any files under the attempt's evidence path into a handoff note on the attempt, readable by the next attempt; (3) after N consecutive hard stops (configurable) of one role on one ticket, report a distinct context-exhausted state with an alert instead of a plain no-progress run. Hosts without a delivery mechanism must report delivery as UNKNOWN/unsupported, never claim it. Related: V1-1563 (live qualification of the estimate and hard stop).
title: dispatch: deliver context warnings into the session, salvage output at the hard stop, alert on repeated hard stops (#1109)

acceptanceCriteria: TSA-V0 requirements for a one-shot-ui-state-assertion rule (direct reads and reads through a resolved page-object method) and an advisory exact-text cross-variant rule, each with suppression semantics and a fixture that triggers it and one that does not (web-first toBeVisible/toHaveCount, expect.poll)
An unresolved helper body yields an UNKNOWN finding rather than silence; the depth of helper-following is bounded and stated
A cross-variant split at the same revision (playwright runs compare or a run receipt) names the exact-text locator as a likely cause; with no multi-project evidence the rule reports NOT_PRODUCED
Focused tests pass, and the build log records the limits and that no live qualification was run
body: GitHub issue #1114. Browser tests assert a single non-retrying read of UI state, for example expect(await locator.isVisible()).toBe(true) or expect(await locator.count()).toBe(3). The read happens once, so a slower renderer, loaded environment or cold cache fails the test even though the state appears a moment later. Web-first matchers (toBeVisible, toHaveCount) would wait for it. Observed: one test passed on one front-end implementation of a screen and failed on another. The cause was a one-shot isVisible() read hidden in a page-object helper and asserted with toBe(true). Test validity reported nothing, and diagnosis needed a trace. Related case: getByText(name, {exact:true}) can never match when one implementation renders extra inline content in the element, such as a badge span. Requested: (1) an advisory lint rule for expect(await X) where X is a UI-state read (isVisible/isHidden/isEnabled/isChecked/isEditable/count/textContent/innerText/inputValue), directly or through a page-object method whose body returns one. Following the method body is the useful part. (2) Best effort: when one test's pass/fail splits by project or variant at the same revision, report it and name any exact-text locator it uses as a likely cause. Both are advisory, can be suppressed with corvint-lint-allow plus a reason, and appear in the run receipt next to the failure they explain. Natural home: internal/testsource/lint.go (TSA-V0, rules no-assertion..skip-only-without-reason, delivered by V1-1589). A page-object method that can't be resolved must be reported as UNKNOWN, never as clean.
title: tests lint: one-shot UI-state assertions through page-object helpers, and exact-text locators behind cross-variant pass/fail splits (#1114)

acceptanceCriteria: Spec requirements (test-validity or appmap domain spec) for actor-role resolution, request-to-ability resolution, inherited rule-set evaluation, the ACTOR-UNAUTHORIZED finding fields, the rejection-assertion exemption, and UNKNOWN for each unresolved link

A first slice that works on a synthetic fixture (JS fixture factory with role:, Rails-style routes plus CanCanCan-style ability rules with inheritance, or a declared project-owned role/ability table if source parsing is out of scope), reproducing the issue's assistant/manager repro as a finding, an authorized pair as clean, and a 403-asserting test as exempt
Finding names the granting rule file:line, the lowest sufficient role and the alternative fixtures; unresolvable inputs yield UNKNOWN with reason
Build log records the supported frameworks, non-goals (other auth libraries, runtime policy) and that no live qualification was run
body: GitHub issue #1115. A browser test logs in as a fixture-seeded user (for example role assistant) and sends a write request (PUT /api/widgets/:id) whose controller action authorizes an ability (authorize! :update, Widget) that only a higher role (manager, which inherits from assistant) holds. Nothing flags it before the run; it shows up as a 403 after a full lane run, and the fix (pick or seed a higher-role user) is found by reading authorization rules by hand. Requested: for each request a test sends under a logged-in fixture actor, (1) resolve the actor role from the fixture builder (a literal role: passed to the user factory, or the factory default); (2) resolve the route to controller#action and the ability it checks; (3) check the role's rule set, including inherited rule sets; (4) report ACTOR-UNAUTHORIZED with role, ability, the granting rule file:line, the lowest role that has the ability, and other fixtures that seed such a role. Advisory, or skipped, when the test deliberately asserts a rejection (401/403/422; see the rejection-anchor work in V1-1737/PR #1101). Today internal/appmap only carries front-end screen permissions (router.go); nothing parses back-end authorization rules, fixture roles or server routes. Any link that can't be resolved (dynamic role, non-literal ability, unknown route) must be reported as UNKNOWN with its reason, never as authorized.
title: test-validity: flag fixture actors whose role is not authorized for the request the test sends (ACTOR-UNAUTHORIZED) (#1115)

acceptanceCriteria: caller_deadline waits on the caller context's Done channel, with no fixed sleep; the test passes 200x under -count=200 -race locally
If the bridge classification changes, MCPV0-038 wording and decision 0533 references are updated in the same change; otherwise the build log states the product code was unchanged
Nightly release-gates passes on main and issue #1116 is closed after a scheduled run passes (release owner)
body: GitHub issue #1116 (nightly release-gates on main at 0fce98369, run 39121848489, macos-15 full-gate). The only failure is internal/mcp/bridge/git_timeout_test.go:100: index refusal = repository-probe-timeout, want cancelled. The caller_deadline case creates context.WithTimeout(50ms), then sleeps 60ms inside build, and expects the bridge to see the ended caller context. A timerCtx's Err() is set only when its timer callback runs, and on a loaded runner that callback can lag past the sleep, so the bridge sees a live context and classifies the index deadline as repository-probe-timeout. Expected: deterministic. Fix the test to wait on <-ctx.Done() (passing ctx into end) instead of sleeping. Also check whether the bridge classification should treat a passed ctx.Deadline() as ended (product behavior per MCPV0-038 / decision 0533); change it only if the spec says so.
title: Nightly full-gate red: TestMCPV0038IndexDeadlineHasDistinctCode/caller_deadline races the context timer (#1116)

acceptanceCriteria: A failing-test run receipt carries the advisory test-source findings anchored to that test, with rule id, file:line and the named replacement

The issue asked that advisory findings such as one-shot-ui-state-assertion and exact-text-cross-variant appear in the run receipt beside a failing test, so the agent reading a failure sees that the assertion is a one-shot UI read or an exact-text cross-variant mismatch. V1-1769 delivered them only in `corvint tests lint` output, because the run receipt had no small hook. Expected: a run receipt for a failing test lists the advisory lint findings anchored to that test (rule, location, replacement) with their resolution state, and reports NOT_PRODUCED with a reason when lint did not run at the revision. Advisory findings must not change exit status (TSA-V0-016).

Cancelled CI runs do not start a control-plane run, or the job exits in under 10 s without a runner-heavy step; AFP-V0-016/047 wording updated if behavior changes

body: Observed 2026-10-18 ~14:30Z: 13 queued `CI control plane` workflow_run runs on main (e.g. 39132313716), each 3 jobs, behind the same ~2 runner capacity as PR and merge_group CI. .github/workflows/ci-control-plane.yml triggers on every CI `completed` event, so cancelling a superseded run (the batching default cancels constituent runs) still spawns a control-plane run, and ci:batched constituent PRs each spawn one even though they will never merge on their own head. Expected: control-plane work does not grow with cancelled/superseded runs; one run per head, skipped for cancelled conclusions where no status is needed, with a concurrency group per head SHA (cancel-in-progress) so a burst collapses. The forward-rows job still records one row per completed run (AFP-V0-047) or records why a cancelled run has none. Needs the .github consent / ci-control-plane post from the owner.
title: CI control plane runs once per completed CI run (including cancelled and ci:batched ones) and queues 13+ deep on the shared runners

acceptanceCriteria: A finding whose helper chain crosses a changed span is in changed-line scope and names the changed helper file:line
A fixture test covers a helper-only change in the same file and in an imported module
UNKNOWN findings from the same unresolved helper are grouped (one finding listing call sites) or the spec records why not
body: Residual of V1-1769 (PR #1119, GitHub #1114), recorded in the TSA failure modes. Changed-line scoping uses the assertion/locator span at the call site. If a diff changes only the helper body (e.g. a page-object helper switches to `isVisible()` or adds `exact: true`), the calling `expect(await helper())` findings stay out of scope and are not reported for that change. Expected: a finding whose resolution path passes through a changed helper span is in scope, naming the changed helper location. Related: on split tests each call of an unresolved helper gives one UNKNOWN line, which can be noisy; consider grouping UNKNOWNs per helper.
title: tests lint: a change only inside a helper's definition does not bring calling one-shot/exact-text findings into changed-line scope (residual of V1-1769)

acceptanceCriteria: Root cause of the silent miss is identified from the probe code (internal/tasks/cli doctor probes) and cited.

A probe that cannot observe the holder emits the TQD-V0-021 'probe incomplete' warning instead of returning an empty holder set, or the holder is reliably found; covered by a deterministic test with an injected probe result.
TestTQDV0021_RealProbes passes 50/50 under -race -count=50 on Linux with parallel load, with the result retained.
body: Suspected defect (one CI observation, not reproduced locally). Merge-queue run 39133588433 (PR #1081 group, base 950f30c3e) failed go-product-shard (5): internal/tasks/cli TestTQDV0021_RealProbes at doctor_ops_test.go:284. The doctor reported SLOW_QUEUE_COMMAND for the prepare-lock helper pid but NO QUEUE_LOCK_HELD finding for the flock holder of taskman.lock, and warnings were empty. The test only tolerates a missed finding when the probe emits 'probe incomplete' (TQD-V0-021), so a silent miss fails the test and ejected #1081 from the merge queue (removed_from_merge_queue 14:57Z), costing a full queue cycle; the same PR's own CI passed, so it is intermittent. Expected: the lock-opener probe either reports the holder or warns that it is incomplete; it never silently returns no holder. Actual: silent miss on a loaded Linux runner (likely the lock-holder probe racing /proc/locks or lsof output, or a probe timeout not mapped to the incomplete warning).
title: doctor real lock probe misses a held queue lock with no 'probe incomplete' warning (TestTQDV0021_RealProbes flake ejected #1081)

acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether MTV-V0-007 covers the transitive dependency closure of the MCP tool path or only its own sources, and the decision is recorded.

If transitive: the guard computes go list -deps for ./internal/mcp/testvaliditybridge and fails on net, net/*, os/exec reached from the tool path, with an explicit, reviewed allowlist for any accepted standard-library edges; the current offending edges are listed with their import chains.
If direct-only stays: the spec text says so explicitly, so it is clear the transitive closure is unchecked.
body: Question, not a confirmed bug. TestToolPathImportsNoNetworkOrProcessPackage (internal/mcp/testvaliditybridge) parses only the production .go files of the bridge and internal/testvaliditydoc and rejects direct net, net/*, os/exec and unsafe syscall imports. MTV-V0-007 (docs/specs/mcp-test-validity-profile-v0.md:93-97) is worded for 'the tool path's own production sources', so the direct-only check matches its text. But the batch #1120 integrator observed on 2026-10-18 that internal/testvaliditydoc already pulls in net and os/exec through its dependencies (go list -deps), so the no-network/no-process property the requirement protects is not actually established for the MCP tool path. Also found: batch #1120 had to move #1112's external-origin parser into internal/testvaliditydoc/externalorigins after the direct-import guard caught it, so any similar helper placed one package deeper would pass unnoticed.
title: MTV-V0-007 import guard checks only direct imports; the MCP test-validity tool path already reaches net and os/exec transitively

acceptanceCriteria: After a no-progress session on a ticket, the next session's prompt carries a bounded carry-over block holding the prior final-message tail and end reason, labelled untrusted prior-session output; a test proves the block's presence, its bound and its label
Per-role configuration covers on/off, maximum size and number of prior sessions, with defaults recorded in the owning spec under new numbered requirements
Carry-over sessions are distinguishable in dispatch events so progress rates with and without carry-over can be compared; a test covers the event field
No carry-over is injected after a session that recorded progress, or for a different ticket
body: GitHub issue #1122. When a worker session exits at the context handoff threshold with no recorded progress, the dispatcher records its final assistant message in the finished event, but the next session on the same ticket starts from the same prompt without it, rediscovers the same plan and exits again (observed: 13 of 16 no-progress sessions in one program ended at handoff before any edit; three consecutive sessions on one ticket repeated the plan until the stall hold parked it). Expected: a bounded, untrusted carry-over block (tail of the prior final message plus the end reason: handoff threshold, hard stop, tool-call cap) is injected into the next session's prompt for that ticket. Related #1109 (hard-stop salvage), now in batch #1120.
title: dispatch: carry a no-progress session's final message into the next session on the same ticket (#1122)

acceptanceCriteria: internal/testvalidity reports ISOLATED-IN-SERIAL for an isolated test under a describe.configure({mode:'serial'}) ancestor and under test.describe.serial, naming the ancestor file:line; synthetic fixtures cover both forms and a non-serial negative
A test without an isolation annotation under a serial suite is not reported (negative fixture)

body: GitHub issue #1123. A test annotated isolated (own seed/session) can sit inside a describe configured with mode serial (or test.describe.serial). A failure of an earlier serial test skips it, so a targeted witness run reports skipped and proves nothing. Expected: a test-validity rule ISOLATED-IN-SERIAL reports any test carrying an isolation annotation (or creating its own fixture data and session) under a serial ancestor, naming the serial ancestor's file:line and suggesting moving the test out or dropping serial mode. Optional: runner summary distinguishes skipped-because-earlier-serial-test-failed from a plain skip, naming the failing test.
title: test-validity: flag isolated tests nested in a serial suite, ISOLATED-IN-SERIAL (#1123)

acceptanceCriteria: internal/testvalidity reports an invalid-severity finding for expect { <name> } when <name> is a subject or let invoked in an enclosing before or let! of the same or an outer group, naming that before/let! file:line; synthetic spec fixtures cover subject, named subject, let, and a negative where the before is in a sibling group

body: GitHub issue #1124. In RSpec, expect { subject } returns the memoized value when an enclosing before (or let!) already invoked subject, so change/raise_error/have_received block expectations are vacuous and not_to change always passes. Observed in a real suite: four examples bound as requirement proof all passed while exercising nothing. internal/testvalidity has no Ruby/RSpec rule today (only JS/Playwright and Go families), so this needs a Ruby spec reader scoped to describe/context nesting, subject/let/let!/before declarations and expect-block bodies. Expected: an invalid-severity finding naming the memoizing before/let! file:line, exposed in the test-validity verdict so callers can refuse the example as proof. Related optional ask: expectations whose target lines had zero coverage in that example's run (needs per-example coverage input).
title: test-validity: flag RSpec block expectations on a subject/let already memoized by an outer before (#1124)

acceptanceCriteria: receipt compact --help states the elided-receipt restore cost for complete audit walks and names the fast route that avoids it

title: receipt compact help: state that complete audit walks over elided receipts cost more (#1063 ask 4)

acceptanceCriteria: an ort-ours merge that drops the other side's conflict hunks is reported per file and hunk, not just as an aggregate count

body: Observed 2026-10-18 on claude/sta-ci-1697 (PR beamfall/corvint#1100). A hand-resolved main merge is refused with merge-resolution-unbound, and the known recovery is `git merge -X ours` plus a separately bound fix commit. Merge 8a420f0d2 (-X ours of origin/main 70a21da5d) silently dropped main's side in five files: docs/specs/README.md row, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, docs/decisions/README.md 0543 row, two Makefile .PHONY names (windows-vet, lane-scripts-test; no check catches this), and internal/contextindex/analyzer_schema_test.go audit pins (caught only by TestAnalyzerSchemaInputs). dogfood-batch-check still PASSED (derivation=ort-ours, note conflict-side-dropped merges=19). Only a manual replay as a plain merge found the losses; they were repaired in c3cce7994. Expected: batch-check (or the recovery it names) surfaces each dropped conflict side as an unknown or a refusal, listing the files and hunks, and the recommended recovery does not lose the other side silently (e.g. bind a hand resolution as its own derivation, or require a replay diff of dropped hunks).
title: dogfood-batch-check accepts -X ours merges that silently drop the other side's hunks; the merge-resolution-unbound recovery steers agents into it

acceptanceCriteria: Multi-line secret forms (PEM blocks, a token split by a newline) are redacted in the salvage and carry-over records, with synthetic fixtures

body: The screen reused by V1-1763 hard-stop salvage and the V1-1782 carry-over (PR #1126) redacts secrets only within single lines. Expected: a credential that a model's final message wraps across lines (e.g. a long token broken by a newline, or a PEM block) is redacted before it is stored or injected into the next prompt. Actual: only whole-line matches are screened; documented as a failure mode in the ATR spec. Suspected-defect class: confirmed limitation, not observed in the wild.

acceptanceCriteria: A carry-over record is invalidated durably (e.g. a progress marker or revision check on load) so a restart after a failed removal offers no carry-over, covered by a restart test with an injected removal failure
body: ATR-V0-111 (PR #1126) removes the carry-over record when a session makes progress; if that removal fails, an in-memory stale flag suppresses it, but the flag is lost on dispatcher restart, so the left-over record can be offered once to the next session despite the progress (violating V1-1782 AC4 across restarts). Expected: no carry-over is offered after a progress session, across restarts. Actual: one stale offer possible; documented as an ATR failure mode.
title: Dispatch carry-over: a failed record removal after a progress session is forgotten across a dispatcher restart (residual of PR #1126)

body: GitHub #1140. A spec helper that declares a block parameter (&block, or yield/block_given?) and passes a literal block to an assertion (assert_no_*, assert_*_difference, expect { }, perform_enqueued_jobs, ...) whose body only references the block (bare `block`, `block.itself`) instead of calling it (`block.call`, `yield`, `instance_exec(&block)`), or never calls the block on any path, makes every example using it vacuous. test-validity does not flag this today. Same family as MEMOIZED-BLOCK-EXPECTATION (TSA-V0-049..051, internal/testsource/validity_rspec.go, internal/testvalidity/source_rules.go). Add rule BLOCK-NOT-CALLED (severity invalid) to the RSpec reader with new TSA-V0 requirements in docs/specs/test-source-analysis-v0.md. Report the helper definition and every example in the same file that calls it. `&block` forwarded straight to the assertion (`assert_no_enqueued_jobs(&block)`) must not be flagged. Abstention follows TSA-V0-050.
title: test-validity: BLOCK-NOT-CALLED rule for RSpec helpers that pass a block to an assertion without calling it (GitHub #1140)

Observed against Core built from origin/main at 19b2f18b6, 2026-10-18.

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatched session killed mid-run leaves no orphaned pool allocation: the dispatcher releases it on attempt end (test)
`dispatch status` shows held allocations per attempt (test)
Existing waiter ordering (grace, then priority, then arrival) is preserved (test)
Spec requirements added in PSR/ATR with traces; focused internal/tasks/dispatch and cli tests pass
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1147 (owner, 2026-10-18). A ticket whose session needs a pool member must currently acquire it from inside the session. If the worker ends (context limit, crash, budget stop) while that acquire is in flight, the allocation is abandoned and stays allocated or quarantined until a sweep. Expected: for a ticket that declares a pool requirement, the dispatcher acquires the member before launch, hands the allocation to the session (env or handoff file), and releases it when the attempt ends, whatever the session did. Related, not duplicated: V1-1573 (acquire at claim time, a follow-up of capacity slots) and V1-0800 (requiresPool omitted). New requirements belong in the pool-safe-reuse (PSR) or attempt-runner (ATR) spec, not the leases spec, which is over its bound.
title: dispatch: acquire and hold the pool member for a session that needs one; release it on attempt end (GitHub #1147)

acceptanceCriteria: Every configured host type has a context-warning delivery path; none reports UNSUPPORTED when the host config declares the host-neutral path (test)
`dispatch salvage --attempt A` writes the secret-screened handoff note for a running or externally stopped attempt (test)
`launched` and `stopped` events record whether warnings and salvage ran (test)
ATR requirements added with traces; focused dispatch tests pass
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1148 (owner, 2026-10-18). In-session context warnings and hard-stop salvage work for only one host type; other hosts (for example a run/CLI wrapper) report contextDelivery UNSUPPORTED. Salvage runs only on a native hard stop, so a program-side supervisor that stops a session earlier gets no handoff note. Ask: (1) a host-neutral delivery path declared in host config (for example a polled file, or a stdin/notification hook); (2) `dispatch salvage --attempt A` that a supervisor can trigger on demand. Related: V1-1768 (opencode plugin, no-tool-call sessions, candidate hand-off notes) and V1-1792 (line-based salvage screening). Add requirements in ATR.
title: dispatch: host-neutral context-warning delivery and an on-demand salvage command (GitHub #1148)

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatch config with ticketBudget overrides and no default limit validates (test)

Expected: a config with only `overrides` validates; unmatched tickets are never held by the budget; status lists only the override scopes. An explicit `unlimited` default may be accepted instead. The ticketBudget contract lives in the leases spec around line 4325; amend that requirement in place without adding new requirement IDs to the leases spec.
title: dispatch: ticketBudget overrides without a mandatory default limit (GitHub #1149)

body: Found 2026-10-18 closing V1-1694/1695/1665/1697 (PR #1100/#1117 deliveries), Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 634. Extends V1-1760, which covers the root (dogfood binds code hunks only 'cited'). Every original sealed map for those four tickets refuses tier-below-anchored (V1-1694: base e1c349d21 seal 39407f669, 27 of 29 hunks cited). The workaround of an anchored build-log addendum (V1-1694: base b26edd021 seal e0a5521cf) refuses CEM_VERDICT_PREDICATE_FAILED no-governed-hunk because claim.verdictPaths come from touchPaths, which exclude docs/build-log/. V1-1681 passed only because its touchPaths include docs/build-log/. Each refusal charges an attempt, and the four tickets are now RETRY_EXHAUSTED with no supported closeout path. Evidence: .git/taskman/evidence/a2ce090096008915089786cfdca7e4f4ed55e5e73a89af3b1d4929e1cf371949; dry-run with `corvint cem gate-verdict` reproduces it exactly. Actual: no route; the gate failure spends retries.

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint affected --base <607-path range>` output is byte-identical before and after on this repository and the existing affected/gateselect tests pass

A benchmark or recorded measurement for both packages is retained with the change
body:
Measured 2026-10-18 on origin/main 6ceee260b (Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 668, darwin, load ~6), scratch clone, CPU profile from an overlay build.

`corvint affected --base HEAD~20` (607 dirty paths) takes 6.2 s single-threaded. 70% of samples are in Graph.readers -> namersWith -> namesAny: for every dirty path, every unit, every PathToken it calls runCache.of (map hash + memequal: 2.78 s of 4.35 s) and then namesPathRuns, which recomputes the loop-invariant strings.HasPrefix(value,"/") / strings.Contains(value,"..") per run (0.67 s). HEAD~5 (119 paths): 1.71 s, readers ~1.0 s.

Prototype (scratch overlay, not committed): precompute each unit's token runs once per readers() call into a [][]tokenRun indexed by graph.order and hoist the file-name-only flag into it. Result: 6.20 s -> 1.77 s on 607 paths with byte-identical JSON output (cmp), 1.71 -> 1.62 s on 119 paths. readers then costs 0.8 s.

Further step: internal/gateselect already has pathMatcher (inverted component index over all dirty paths, readers.go:637) for the bound-lines path, but Select still calls index.attribute -> readers -> namesPath per dirty path (0.66 s of 5.1 s CPU in `corvint test --base HEAD~5 --dry-run`), re-running componentRuns and strings.Split per call over every holder. Both affected.readers and gateselect.attribute can evaluate all dirty paths per token at once through a pathMatcher-style index; the ascending path indices keep the smallest-naming-dirty-path witness rule. Note the two namesPath copies differ (affected applies the V1-0290 file-name-only rule for lone components; gateselect's does not), so a shared matcher must keep each relation.
title: affected and gateselect: path-literal reader matching is O(dirty x units x tokens) with a map lookup per step; 607-path affected takes 6.2 s, 1.8 s with precomputed runs

CPU profile: compileAffectedGraph -> golang.observeDirectories/readSourceFile ~0.75-0.97 s, and testFillPlan -> gateselect.Select -> indexRepository (filepath.WalkDir + reads) ~0.9 s. Both walk and read the same Go sources in the same process. Investigate whether gateselect can take the source bytes/tokens the affected graph already read (or a shared per-invocation source cache keyed by path+blob), without changing either selection. Excluded: the reader-matching cost itself (separate ticket on path-literal matching).
title: corvint test scans the repository twice: the affected Go graph and gateselect.indexRepository each read every source (~0.8-1.0 s each per call)

acceptanceCriteria: An over-bound range refuses with identical output without decoding the snapshot (test or measurement retained)

body: Measured 2026-10-18 on origin/main 6ceee260b (build 668): `corvint impact --base <HEAD~20>` returns unsupported-impact-range ("impact range exceeds the 100-path bound") after 0.4 s CPU / up to 1.3 s wall and ~430 MB RSS, most of it LoadSnapshot/gob decode plus git status. The range's path count is known from the diff alone. Expected: count the range paths and refuse before loading the snapshot, with the same refusal bytes. Agents and hooks that call impact on long-lived branches pay this on every refusal.
