acceptanceCriteria: Nested includes and cross-file overrides resolve in Ruby evaluation order (later definition wins, customization block after shared body) with fixtures for each; anything still ambiguous abstains; abstention-rate change measured on the V1-1877 suite.
body: Residual of V1-1866/V1-1867 review fixes (PR #1166 head 4aaef55de). To remove false INELIGIBLE verdicts, the reader now abstains (RB-HELPER-UNRESOLVED) when a helper's candidate definitions span files (customization-block override of a shared-file helper) or come through a nested include_context/include_examples inside a shared group. Correct but lossy: real suites often layer shared contexts.
title: RSpec helper resolution: resolve nested shared-context includes and cross-file customization overrides instead of abstaining

acceptanceCriteria: For a new test linked to a legacy test (crosswalk or explicit reference), setup on each side is extracted from committed blobs into a normalised shape (entity kind, count per kind, explicitly set attributes) for at least RSpec FactoryBot create/create_list/build plus YAML fixtures and one JS/TS API/factory setup form; other forms abstain naming the side and line.
Differences in kinds, counts and explicitly set attributes are reported, ordered by whether an asserted value reads them; an N vs M child-count difference reports both counts and the asserting lines.
An explicit attribute on one side left at its default on the other is reported; a group-aggregate assertion (total/all/sum across a group) with a single-member seed is reported on both sides.

Incomplete extraction is advisory and names which side was not analysed; parity is never reported when either side was not analysed; identical normalised shapes give no finding (each pinned by a fixture test).
Requirements in test-source-analysis-v0.md using TSA-V0-100..109 only, with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; Closes #1167.
body: GitHub #1167. When a new test claims to preserve a legacy test's behaviour, test-validity compares assertions but not preconditions: a migrated test can seed a different world (child counts, association shapes, explicitly set vs defaulted attributes, single-member groups behind aggregate claims) and still pass, overstating parity. Link source: the existing legacy crosswalk (documentation-corpus-v1, internal/doccorpus/behavior_legacy_crosswalk.go) or an explicit new>legacy reference. Requested: an advisory-capable SEED-PARITY-DIVERGES check over normalised setup (entity kinds, counts per kind, explicitly set attributes).
title: GH #1167: test-validity: compare a new test's setup against its linked legacy test's fixture (SEED-PARITY-DIVERGES)

acceptanceCriteria: For each resource a test creates and deletes in teardown (after/afterEach/after(:each)/ensure/fixture finalizers in at least RSpec and one JS/TS framework), the actions performed on it are listed with lines; actions known to create dependents come from a bound source or a closed, versioned, revision-pinned side-effect declaration (action -> dependent kind, cascade flags); unknown actions keep the finding advisory and say so.

A known dependent-producing action followed by a parent delete with no dependent cleanup, or cleanup that deletes the parent before the dependent, is reported with the action line and the delete line; no finding when dependents are removed first or the parent delete is declared to cascade.

Recorded run outcomes: a prior receipt row whose teardown delete returned a conflict/validation status (e.g. 409/422) is attached to the finding with status and dependent kind when known; receipts that do not bind to the test's blob abstain.
Never claims a teardown is safe when the side-effect graph is incomplete; each rule pinned by fixture tests.
Requirements in test-source-analysis-v0.md using TSA-V0-110..119 only, with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; Closes #1168.
body: GitHub #1168. E2E tests that create a parent and delete it in teardown fail at cleanup (409/422 from FK or in-use guards) when the system under test created dependents as a side effect (confirmations, audit entries, notifications, ledger lines) that cleanup never removes. Nothing flags the risk before the run. Requested: TEARDOWN-DEPENDENT-LEFTOVER using the source dependency graph or recorded run outcomes, advisory when the side-effect graph is incomplete.
title: GH #1168: test-validity: flag teardown that deletes a parent while side-effect dependents remain (TEARDOWN-DEPENDENT-LEFTOVER)

acceptanceCriteria: A review-stage claim gets a packet built from native records: delta base = newest ancestor commit with a passed review, diff limited to test and fixture paths, the last returned review's items each marked touched/untouched by the delta, obligations the delta touches (changed test identities, cited lines), and a saved partial checkpoint for the same commit.

The packet has a byte cap; content beyond it is listed as exact source ranges to read on demand, never dropped silently; a several-round ticket fixture stays under the cap and names every returned item.
With no passed ancestor the packet falls back to the full diff and says so; the packet is placed in the dispatched session prompt and the full record is not read by default.
Requirements in the owning domain spec (dispatch/external-reviews/obligation ledger, not the full leases spec); focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; build-log entry; Closes #1169.
body: GitHub #1169. Review-stage sessions get the whole ticket history; after a few rounds reviewers hit the context limit before a verdict, hand off, and restart (largest source of no-progress review sessions). An adopter packet builder cut packets to ~10-12 KB. Requested: dispatch/tasks build a bounded review packet: delta base (newest passed-review ancestor) and diff limited to test/fixture paths; last returned items with touched/untouched status; touched obligations only; any partial checkpoint for the same commit; a size cap that names omitted source ranges.
title: GH #1169: dispatch: bounded review packet for review-stage claims (delta since last passed review, returned items, touched obligations, capped with named ranges)

acceptanceCriteria: A closed verdict schema (correct|partial|wrong, stubRisk none|boundary|on-path, reason, reviewer) is recorded per (obligation, test example) with reviewer independence checked against the existing exclude-authors record; unknown values are refused.
A configurable agreement policy (default: all K agree correct and none on-path) credits the witness; two agreeing reviewers with no on-path risk credit it.
One partial or one on-path verdict yields HELD with every verdict and reason and the disagreeing axis shown.

Changing the test file blob or cited lines marks verdicts stale and un-credits until re-reviewed; requirements in corvint-tasks-obligation-ledger-v0.md; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; build-log entry; Closes #1170.
body: GitHub #1170. Crediting an existing test as an obligation witness needs blind independent reviewer judgement; the merge logic (all agree correct, nobody says on-path stub) lives outside Corvint, so held candidates and reasons are invisible. Requested: obligations witness accepts K verdicts per (obligation, example): correct|partial|wrong, stub risk none|boundary|on-path, reason, reviewer identity independent of the author (reuse exclude-authors); credit only when the configured agreement policy holds; held rows keep every verdict and reason with the disagreeing axis; verdicts go stale when the test file or cited lines change.
title: GH #1170: obligations witness: credit existing-test witnesses on K independent reviewer verdicts with an agreement policy; keep held verdicts

acceptanceCriteria: STUB-ON-PATH: a stub on a first-party symbol whose return value flows to an asserted value is reported with stubbed symbol, action line and assertion line (RSpec and Jest/Vitest at least); stubs on external boundaries (HTTP clients, third-party SDKs, clock, queues) are not reported.

STUB-NEVER-INVOKED: a stub in the example or its hooks on a method a bound passing run with call recording never invoked is reported; without a run, it is advisory only when static analysis finds no call path from the action; incomplete analysis abstains.
Requirements in test-source-analysis-v0.md (lane-assigned TSA range) with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; build-log entry; Closes #1171.
body: GitHub #1171. Beyond DESCRIBED-CLASS-STUBBED, reviewers find (1) stubs of first-party collaborators between the action and the asserted value, so the assertion checks the stub, and (2) stubs on methods the exercised path never calls (wrong receiver, renamed method). Requested STUB-ON-PATH (first-party stub/double/receive/mockReturnValue whose value flows into an asserted value; external boundaries excluded) and STUB-NEVER-INVOKED (from recorded call data, advisory from static no-call-path).
title: GH #1171: test-validity: flag first-party collaborator stubs on the action-to-assertion path (STUB-ON-PATH) and stubs never invoked (STUB-NEVER-INVOKED)

acceptanceCriteria: tests reports each test-looking file that no configured runner selects under its default configuration as TEST-FILE-UNSELECTED with a reason: no-runner-for-framework, outside-include, excluded (naming the pattern), suffix-mismatch.

Selected files are not reported; runner configs the reader cannot parse abstain rather than report; requirements in the owning test-selection spec; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; build-log entry; Closes #1172.
body: GitHub #1172. Files that look like tests (framework imports, test-definition calls, directory convention) but no configured runner selects (no runner for the framework, outside include globs, explicitly excluded, suffix mismatch) look like coverage in inventories/crosswalks and get cited as evidence though they never run.
title: GH #1172: tests: report test files no configured runner selects (TEST-FILE-UNSELECTED) and keep them out of witness credit

acceptanceCriteria: A component spec that queries a DOM node it created itself with no render of the subject is reported with the assertion line and value origin.

body: GitHub #1173. Passing tests that assert on a value the test produced itself: a component spec querying DOM it built instead of rendering the subject; an enqueue expectation checking arguments the test enqueued itself; a fixture compared to itself after an action that never touched it. Requested: a data-flow check tracing the asserted actual value; report when its sources are only test-local literals/fixtures/built structures unreachable from the subject call or render; advisory when the trace is incomplete.

acceptanceCriteria: Every compiled route of the supported router dialects resolves its handler; a resource declaration generating a create route for a controller with no create action is reported with the declaration line, the resolved handler and the missing action.

acceptanceCriteria: Given an obligation or cited source lines, each cited branch lists reaching tests grouped by boundary (unit, request, e2e) with an explicit 'none at <boundary>' entry.

acceptanceCriteria: Preregistered request set, target repo and kill threshold recorded before mining

body:
Owner goal 2026-10-18: know every page, page object, link, data setup and step in a site, gathered from its tests, so that 'show me how to do X' builds an e2e test that demonstrates it with confidence.

Existing pieces (read-only inventory 2026-10-18, origin/main 6ceee260b):
- AMAP screen graph: three literal router dialects; React JSX Routes reads 0 screens (V1-1712).
- ANL edges.
- TestFile Gotos, Selectors and Methods: Playwright only.
- AFU flow intents: authored, not mined.
- AMSP `flows appmap plan --draft`: term match over declared flows; emits test.fixme with TODO assertions.
- CCE-V0 compiled e2e: killed after V1-1677 (0/10 useful), pivot V1-1733.

Gaps: no extraction of data setup (test.extend fixtures, beforeEach, storageState, page.route mocks, API seeding); no mining of existing tests into anchored step sequences; page-object resolution is shallow (V1-1236); no how-to query over mined tests; no run-to-prove path for a composed test.

Spike design (Playwright only, one real repo whose router AMAP resolves): mine each hosted test into anchored records: setup facts, ordered goto, page-object calls, fill and click actions, and the real assertions. Rank whole tests and their prefixes lexically against the request. Emit a runnable spec composed only of mined, anchored statements, with the source test's real assertions, abstaining with named UNKNOWNs otherwise. Run it through corvint-test/PWP and bind a receipt so the answer reads VERIFIED@REV. Confidence means a receipt at the revision, not model confidence; mined steps stay learned evidence under project authority (invariants 1-3, 8). Browser and Node stay in companions (invariant 7).

Preregistered measure: N owner-written 'how do I X' requests with known answers. Report: share answered vs abstained; composed tests passing at head and failing on a seeded mutant (CCE-V0-009); zero unanchored statements; byte-identical reruns. Kill if under 40% of requests are answered with a passing, discriminating test.
title: Spike: test-mined how-to knowledge: mine steps, page objects and data setup from hosted Playwright tests, compose and prove a how-to e2e

acceptanceCriteria:
A blocker can record a typed condition: commit ancestor of ; path

exists at ; symbol defined at . Free text remains allowed.

When the deployment ref or source changes, open typed blockers are re-evaluated at the first status read; satisfied ones show UNBLOCKED (condition met at <ref>) in status and doctor, and the item routes back to its work stage or to the operator per policy. A blocker 'commit X ancestor of DEPLOY' flips in the first status read after DEPLOY moves to a descendant of X.
doctor lists free-text blockers that name a sha or path whose condition is already met at the deployment ref.
doctor reports role prompts/operator notes that pin base B once DEPLOY is a strict descendant of B.
Unresolvable refs or symbols stay blocked with an explicit UNKNOWN reason, never silently unblocked.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1177. Blockers on tickets/obligations/rows are free text ('do not queue until commit X is deployed'); when the artifact ships into the deployed commit nothing re-evaluates them. Observed in one day: ~28 sessions ran on a ticket without queueing after X was deployed; a dozen 'no mock for S' items stayed blocked after a stand-in shipped; a role prompt pinned a base three deployments old; 'needs observer O' items stayed blocked two days after O shipped.
title: GH #1177: machine-checkable blocker conditions that re-evaluate when the deployment ref moves (ancestor/path/symbol), plus doctor for stale free-text blockers and pinned bases

acceptanceCriteria: A side whose setup calls an unresolved first-party helper (defined in the suite, not a recognised factory form) is followed to its factory calls when statically resolvable, otherwise the side is SEED-PARITY-NOT-ANALYSED naming the helper and line.
Fixture: two tests with identical visible factory calls but different helper-seeded records no longer report parity.
body: Residual from V1-1883 (PR #1178, TSA-V0-107 failure modes). `corvint tests validity --legacy` reads FactoryBot/fixtures/JS create/build forms only; a side that seeds through a helper such as make_order(...) is not seen, so 'parity' can be reported although the helper's records differ. Invariant 2: missing evidence must abstain.
title: Seed parity reports parity over setup helpers it cannot see (make_order-style helpers without a setup word)

acceptanceCriteria: let_it_be and let!/let seeding, include_context/shared_context bodies (same-file and resolvable cross-file), and factory definitions with associations/traits are read into the seed shape, with counts of implicit associated records.
Measured on one real Rails suite: share of linked pairs analysed before vs after; unresolved forms still abstain.
body: Residual from V1-1883 (PR #1178, spec non-goals). let_it_be, shared_context/include_context and factory definitions/associations (implicit associated records) give not-analysed or are not read, so most real Rails suites abstain.
title: Seed parity: read let_it_be, shared contexts and factory definitions/associations so real suites stop abstaining

acceptanceCriteria: A static check (doc-gate or go-static step) fails when a non-test file under internal/ or cmd/ ends in a GOOS/GOARCH suffix (_js.go, _wasm.go, ...) without an explicit opt-in list, naming the file and suggesting _jsts.go.
The lane charter/SELF-DEVELOPMENT notes name the pitfall.
body: Residual from V1-1883: a new internal/testsource/*_js.go file silently compiled only for GOOS=js; second lane after V1-1858. No guard or lane guidance exists.
title: Go filenames ending _js.go are GOOS=js-only: lanes adding JS/TS analysers hit it twice (V1-1858, V1-1883)

acceptanceCriteria: Dependents are derived from model associations (dependent: options), foreign keys and after_create/after_commit callbacks where statically resolvable, with provenance 'derived' distinct from 'declared'; unresolved sources keep findings advisory.
Actions carry instance identity where the test binds one (variable or let name), so deleting one dependent instance does not clear others of the same kind.
Fixture tests for both, plus one real Rails app measurement.
body: Residual from V1-1884 (PR #1179, TSA-V0-110..119). Only the corvint-side-effect-declaration/0 file feeds the graph; ActiveRecord associations (has_many dependent:), foreign keys in schema.rb/migrations and callbacks are not read, so undeclared dependents are never found. There is also no instance-level identity: one dependent delete clears every action of that kind.
title: Teardown dependents: derive the side-effect graph from the system under test (models, associations, schema/migrations) instead of the declaration only

acceptanceCriteria: Each listed form is read or keeps an explicit advisory reason naming it; receiver- and factory-derived kinds bind to declared kinds.
Same-group hook order follows the framework's documented order.
Ruby provider receipts join on the committed blob digest like JS; request routes map to kinds through the route table when resolvable.
Measured: share of findings advisory on one real suite before vs after.
body: Residual from V1-1884 (PR #1179). Unread forms only mark findings advisory, so most real suites stay advisory: helper files, shared contexts, fixture finalizers and beforeAll/afterAll resources are not read; a kind is not taken from a receiver (record.destroy) or factory argument (create(:order)); order.status-style paren-less Ruby calls read as attributes; same-group hooks are treated as unknown order although RSpec/Jest define it; Ruby provider receipts abstain (receipt-not-js) and request routes do not map to kinds.
title: Teardown dependents: read helpers, shared contexts, fixture finalizers, before/afterAll resources, receiver/factory-derived kinds and paren-less Ruby calls

acceptanceCriteria: obligations reports NO-TEST-BOUNDARY for an open/blocked obligation whose cited locations all sit in repositories with no runnable test provider, or that cites no tracked code; it lists the repositories checked and each one's test inventory.

A scope-change command sets the in-scope/core flag only with a recorded decision (who, when, why, evidence ref) kept in obligation history and shown in status; it refuses without one. Completion rates count in-scope obligations only and list out-of-scope ones separately with their decision.
When a test provider later appears for such a repository, the out-of-scope obligations are listed as re-scope candidates.
Fixture tests for all three acceptance cases from the issue; requirements in the owning obligations spec; Closes #1180.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1180. Obligations implemented entirely outside any repository with a runnable test provider (warehouse SQL, BI model filters) stay core and blocked forever, depress completion rates and get re-triaged repeatedly.
title: GH #1180: obligations NO-TEST-BOUNDARY detector and owner-gated in-scope/core decisions

acceptanceCriteria: doctor reports RUNNABLE-HELD-IDLE for a ticket whose work state names runnable work needing a pool member (queued batch or final run), excluded by an admission or focus rule, while the matching pool has free members for N ticks; it names the ticket, the excluding rule, the age of the work and the free members.

An optional policy lets run-only stages (no author session) bypass author-capacity admission when members are free; with it on, the work dispatches to a free member without entering the author window.
No finding when no member is free or the work needs an author session; fixture tests for each; Closes #1181.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1181. Runnable batches (including a final qualification whose obligations were all witnessed) sat queued >10 days behind focus/priority/author-capacity admission rules while 3 of 4 pool members were idle.
title: GH #1181: doctor RUNNABLE-HELD-IDLE - run-only work held by an admission/focus rule while pool members are free

acceptanceCriteria: `obligations worklist` derives items from recorded review shortfalls with: obligation, verdict (partial/held), missing clause/assertion, cited test file and line, reviewer stub-risk notes, review age.

Excluded: obligations whose newest record is an unreviewed witness candidate; obligations blocked on a capability Corvint knows is missing; obligations without falsifiable text (listed separately as 'needs obligation text').
Ranking is configurable (e.g. priority tickets, then nearest completion); `next` returns the head item plus up to K items citing the same test file.
Acceptance cases from the issue pinned by fixture tests; Closes #1182.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1182. Partial review verdicts name the missing clause, file and reason, but live as free text; workers cannot get a ranked list of the cheapest remaining examples.
title: GH #1182: obligations worklist - ranked, file-batched queue from reviewed partial witnesses

acceptanceCriteria: doctor reports ROLE-QUEUE-DEEP per role when the count of tickets whose work state matches the role exceeds its cap for N ticks, with depth, cap, oldest wait and whether global/pressure caps allow a raise.
Optional policy: a role may declare capMax and scale between cap and capMax while its queue is deep and pressure is calm, returning to cap when the queue drains; never above global or pressure caps.
Fixture tests for both acceptance cases; Closes #1183.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1183. A no-run review role capped at 2 had 10 tickets waiting, each also holding a scarce downstream run resource, while host pressure was calm; nothing surfaced it.
title: GH #1183: doctor ROLE-QUEUE-DEEP and optional role capMax scaling under calm pressure

acceptanceCriteria: The RSpec and Jest/Vitest live providers can record, per example, which declared stubs/mocks were invoked (count), bound to the committed blob digest.
STUB-NEVER-INVOKED gains a run-based form from that receipt; without a receipt it stays the static advisory form.
body: Residual from V1-1887 (PR #1184, TSA-V0-125 residual). STUB-NEVER-INVOKED ships static-only because no provider receipt records stub invocations.
title: Run-based STUB-NEVER-INVOKED: call-recording receipts for RSpec and Jest/Vitest stubs

acceptanceCriteria: receive_messages, receive_message_chain, jest.fn() assigned onto objects and jest.mock module factories are read as stubs.
On-path reachability follows resolvable first-party imports/requires to a bounded depth; unresolved hops keep the trace incomplete (no finding).
Fixture tests for each shape and one cross-module case.
body: Residual from V1-1887 (PR #1184 build log). Tracing stays inside one example, so stubs reached through imports are never on-path; several stub shapes are ignored and give no finding.
title: STUB-ON-PATH: cross-module reachability and unread stub shapes (receive_messages, receive_message_chain, jest.fn() assignments, jest.mock factories)

acceptanceCriteria: A JS/TS Playwright reader resolves fixture scopes (test default, worker via {scope:'worker'}) and reports advisory CLEANUP-HANDLE-OUTLIVED when a closure registered on a longer-scoped fixture/registry (or afterAll/worker teardown) captures a binding from a shorter-scoped fixture; the finding cites both fixture declarations and the registration line and names the fix (own context in cleanup scope, or cleanup before the short fixture tears down).
Unresolvable scopes, dynamic registries or indirect captures abstain with a named reason; no finding is reported as certain without both scopes resolved from committed source.

A run receipt or manifest that records cleanup as unverified or failed yields a distinct outcome (e.g. PASSED_CLEANUP_FAILED) that selection and witness credit treat as not clean evidence (fail closed), even when every test passed; absence of a cleanup record stays NOT_OBSERVED, not clean.
Spec requirements in docs/specs/test-source-analysis-v0.md (new IDs, traceability rows) with positive, negative and abstain fixture tests for each rule; Closes #1185.
body: GitHub #1185. A cleanup task registered on a worker/suite-scoped registry captures a test-scoped handle (APIRequestContext, page, browser context); at worker shutdown the handle is disposed, every delete fails, tests still pass, and leftovers accumulate. The run manifest records cleanup.verified=false but nothing gates on it. Related: V1-1884/#1168 (teardown order), V1-1900 (data-setup cleanup model).
title: test-validity: CLEANUP-HANDLE-OUTLIVED for cleanup closures capturing a shorter-lived fixture handle, and fail closed on recorded cleanup failure (#1185)

acceptanceCriteria: Every containment decision site is inventoried; each accepts ANCESTOR, or EQUIVALENT <sha> when `git cherry <source> <commit>` (patch-id) finds an equivalent commit, recording the equivalent SHA so provenance stays auditable; strict-ancestry-only sites that must stay strict are named with the reason.

A read-only query `source contains <rev> <commit...>` reports per commit ANCESTOR | EQUIVALENT <sha> | ABSENT, and distinguishes ABSENT-patch-differs (a commit with the same subject/change-id exists but its patch differs, e.g. conflict-resolved rebase) from plainly absent; it writes nothing.
Bounded: the patch-id scan has a named commit/byte bound; exceeding it yields UNKNOWN, never ABSENT or EQUIVALENT.
Spec requirements with tests for rebase, cherry-pick, conflict-resolved rebase, merge-only and bound-exceeded cases; Closes #1186.
body: GitHub #1186. Source-containment checks (pool --source provenance, prerequisite/commit-integrated checks, release candidates) use strict merge-base --is-ancestor. A rebased or cherry-picked commit whose content is present is reported missing; workers then repeatedly request fenced repins to older sources, burning sessions on already-deployed code.
title: Source containment: accept patch-equivalent (rebased/cherry-picked) commits as CONTAINED_EQUIVALENT and add read-only `source contains` (#1186)

acceptanceCriteria: commitBinding is OBSERVED when the hand-off checkpoint commit resolves in the store repository, with a test
packet history offers a deterministic cursor/offset beyond 200 events and names the truncation, with a test
body: Residual from #1189 (V1-1885/1886, ERG-V0-017..021). The review packet's hand-off note checkpoint always reports commitBinding NOT_OBSERVED even when the checkpoint commit is reachable, and packet history truncates at 200 events with no cursor, so long-lived tickets lose earlier review context silently beyond the truncation marker.
title: Review packet: hand-off checkpoint commitBinding always NOT_OBSERVED and packet history capped at 200 events with no paging

acceptanceCriteria: staleness is computed against the candidate revision named by the witness request, with a regression test where HEAD and candidate differ
the staleness basis is recorded in the witness output
body: Residual from #1189 (TOL-V0-073..078). Reviewed-witness crediting computes review staleness only at read time and against the store HEAD, not the candidate revision under review, so a verdict can be counted fresh for a candidate it never saw, or stale for one it did.
title: Review staleness is read-time only and judged at store HEAD instead of the candidate revision

acceptanceCriteria: unsorted --reason input is either canonicalized or refused with a code naming byte order, with a test
body: Residual from #1189. `corvint-tasks gate record --reason a --reason b` refuses when reasons are not byte-sorted; callers must pre-sort. Either canonicalize (sort+dedupe) or return a refusal that names the required order.
title: gate record --reason refuses unsorted reasons instead of canonicalizing or naming the order rule

acceptanceCriteria: a focused unit test pins author derivation including alias/same-author exclusion
a focused test pins ReviewPacket framing bytes/fields
body: Residual from #1189. The reviewed-witness author derivation (TOL-V0-075) is only covered indirectly and ReviewPacket framing (ERG-V0-017..021 envelope) has no direct test.
title: Direct tests for reviewed-witness author derivation and ReviewPacket framing

acceptanceCriteria: non-literal whole exports abstain with runner-config-key-dynamic or a named reason, with a test
Mocha hidden-path matching follows segment-exact semantics, with a test
body: Residual from #1187 (V1-1888, TSA-V0-141/142). A runner config whose whole export is not an object literal (e.g. `module.exports = require('./base')`) is read as runner defaults instead of abstaining, and Mocha's hidden-file exclusion is approximated per pattern: any pattern with a literal `.` segment may match any hidden path.
title: Unselected-test runner config: non-literal whole exports read as defaults; Mocha hidden-file rule approximated per pattern

acceptanceCriteria: crosswalk and witness import exclude or mark runner-unselected files, with tests
body: Residual from #1187 (V1-1888). The new unselected test file report (TSA-V0-141/142) is not yet consumed by the doc-corpus crosswalk or the Playwright witness import, so files no runner selects can still be credited as executable evidence.
title: Consume the unselected-test-files report in the doc-corpus crosswalk and Playwright witness import

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-batch-check prints the per-constituent reason code (unsupported-object-alternates) and a fix line
a test covers an alternates-backed clone
body: Observed 2026-10-19 on batch claude/batch-1019a (clone made with git clone --reference): `cem status` returns unsupported-object-alternates for every constituent, but dogfood-batch-check surfaces only `state=unsupported`, so the operator cannot tell the cause is the clone layout rather than the CEM. Expected: the batch check prints the underlying reason code and the fix (use git clone --no-local or repack -a and remove alternates).
title: dogfood-batch-check reports constituents in an alternates-backed clone only as state=unsupported, hiding unsupported-object-alternates

acceptanceCriteria: a read-only finding lists OPEN tickets whose cited requirement IDs or ticket IDs appear in merged first-parent commits, naming the commit
no finding for tickets without such evidence; abstains when history is unavailable
body: Observed 2026-10-19: V1-1192 and V1-1194 stayed OPEN although their requirements landed on main in PR #1060 (b9cfe9618); V1-1879 stayed OPEN after #1176 merged. Finding them took manual git log -S and grep. A doctor/audit finding that links ticket requirement IDs or 'GH #N' titles to merged commits on the default branch would surface delivered-but-open work for closeout.
title: Tasks: report OPEN tickets whose delivering change already merged (delivered-but-open audit)

acceptanceCriteria: batch-check and dogfood-finish refusals for a non-compiling base print the build error excerpt and a fix line
DOGFOOD.md documents the recovery for non-composing constituents
a test covers the refusal output
body: Observed 2026-10-19 on batch-1019b (#1178,#1179,#1184,#1187,#1188): constituents had Go name collisions (rubyName, rubyAssertion) and a main signature change, so every merges-only tip failed to build. dogfood-finish refused base-corvint-build-failed (script/dogfood-finish.sh:85-88, dogfood-check.sh:49-52 build ./cmd/corvint from BASE), and dogfood-batch-check refused current-tree-corvint-build-failed with no fix line. The batch-check advice (-X merges plus a sealed resolution change) is a dead end in this case. Expected: batch-check names the failing package/build error and points to the supported recovery (fix collisions on constituent branches, or a documented resolution path), and DOGFOOD.md documents it.
title: dogfood batch: resolution change cannot be sealed when constituents only compile together after a fix; batch-check refusal gives no fix hint

acceptanceCriteria: each listed form is flagged with its line, with a fixture per form
a justified annotation suppresses the finding with the reason retained
with a run receipt the observed single value is proposed; without one, no proposal
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1191. Flag assertions that accept any of several distinct values for a status/enum/outcome field: toContain on a literal array, || inside expect, oneOf matchers, regex alternation over status codes, and 'X or Y' wording in behaviour-contract expected values. Cite the line; propose the single value when a passing run receipt records it; honour an explicit justification annotation.
title: GH #1191: test-validity EITHER-OR-OUTCOME - assertions accepting several distinct status/enum outcomes

acceptanceCriteria: static finding with line and nearest stubbed value, fixture-backed
run receipt with 5xx plus unstubbed outbound call classifies ENV-UNSTUBBED-CALL naming the call
missing stub table or server log abstains with a named reason
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1192. Static: given the environment stub table (request matchers the mock layer answers), report test inputs reaching a stubbed integration with values no matcher covers, as UNSTUBBED-OUTBOUND-INPUT with the test line and nearest stubbed value. Run-time: when a run receipt records a 5xx whose server log shows an outbound call to an unstubbed host/path, classify ENV-UNSTUBBED-CALL (not product/test failure) and name the call. Absent stub table or server log abstains.
title: GH #1192: UNSTUBBED-OUTBOUND-INPUT static finding and ENV-UNSTUBBED-CALL run classification

acceptanceCriteria: run receipt with both operands empty yields VACUOUS-EMPTY-EQUALITY and the run is not credited as a witness
static unseeded-collection count assertion flagged with a suggested precondition; seeded fixture not flagged
drifted row citation reported against the pinned commit; absent operands or commit abstain
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1193. Run-time: when a run receipt captures assertion operands, flag an equality/count assertion whose both sides are empty or zero as VACUOUS-EMPTY-EQUALITY for that run, and do not count the run as a witness for the bound row. Static: flag count/equality assertions against a collection the bound fixture does not seed, suggesting a non-empty precondition. Related: report row citations (file:line) that no longer point at the cited symbol at the row's pinned commit.
title: GH #1193: VACUOUS-EMPTY-EQUALITY - equality/count assertions passing on empty collections, plus row citation line drift

acceptanceCriteria: click-submit step that triggers a create request and only asserts a dialog closed is reported

acceptanceCriteria: A timeout with no matching request in the server log is reported as request-never-sent with the earlier 4xx on the same page.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1197. (2) Static: role-based locators (e.g. role=alert) targeting a component's error/notification output must match a role the component's markup renders; report mismatch with component path. Abstain when logs or markup are unresolved.
title: GH #1197: RESPONSE-WAIT diagnosis - request never sent vs slow response, and role locators the component never renders

acceptanceCriteria: A corpus build refusal for a bound or anchor violation names the offending path and line (and the bound), not only the error class.
corvint docs corpus build on Corvint's own docs scope at origin/main either succeeds under corvint-corpus-input/2, or the remaining refusals are recorded as intended exclusions with their paths.
Focused doccorpus tests cover the located refusal message.
body: Found while measuring V1-1982 (2026-10-19). At origin/main 547d26417cc9f559a77ab2fdc95721e1043a544c with Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676: `corvint docs corpus manifest --scope docs` (rc 0) then `corvint docs corpus build --manifest <m>` refuses `corpus-refused: native paragraph bound exceeded` under corvint-corpus-input/1, and `corpus-refused: vacuous or oversized anchor` with the schema set to corvint-corpus-input/2. Neither error names a file or line, so the author cannot find the offending page in a scope of hundreds of docs. Corvint therefore cannot build a corpus of its own documentation (dogfood gap for the docs corpus/MCP server). Also: --manifest refuses an absolute path, which is surprising for a scratch manifest. Expected: a located refusal; actual: an unlocated one. Suspected defect for the self-build part (the content may genuinely exceed bounds); confirmed friction for the unlocated message.
title: docs corpus build refusals (paragraph bound, vacuous or oversized anchor) do not name the file, and Corvint's own docs scope cannot be built

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture corpus with 10,000 pinned inputs: build, `docs corpus query`, and each `corvint-corpus-mcp` tool succeed; the reported Git operation count per read is <= a small constant (e.g. <= 16) independent of input count.
Fixture with 2,000 non-indexed text inputs (html/erb/json) in one scope: `docs corpus manifest` and `docs corpus build` succeed.
A corpus that exceeds a documented capacity limit fails in < 1 s with a typed capacity code naming the limit (never `internal-error`).
Freshness still reports `stale` when one of the 10,000 inputs changes (regression guard for the batched path).
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1240 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). Every documentation-corpus read revalidates each pinned input with one Git tree lookup, charged against a fixed 1,024-operation budget (`gitrun.NewDefaultBudget`). A corpus with more than ~1,024 pinned inputs therefore cannot be read at all: every CLI query and every `corvint-corpus-mcp` tool call fails with `git-budget-exceeded`, after a long rebuild. The same per-input charging applies at build and at `docs corpus manifest`: every input the source index does not load as text (for example `.html`, `.erb`, `.scss`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.rake`, `.properties`, template files) costs one tree lookup plus one blob read, so a scope with several hundred such files exceeds the budget at build time.  The budget is a per-verification constant, not scaled to the manifest, and the result is surfaced as `internal-error` rather than a typed capacity refusal.
title: Corpus reads and builds fail with git-budget-exceeded past ~1,024 pinned inputs; batch freshness/blob reads and type capacity refusals (GitHub #1240)

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture repository with 20,000 tracked files: `docs corpus manifest --schema 2 --scope a --scope b` produces one /2 manifest with both scopes and 20,000 inputs, and `docs corpus build` accepts it.
The refusal for a scope above the /2 bound reports the bound and actual count.
/1 behaviour (default) is unchanged.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1241 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). `corvint docs corpus manifest --scope PATH` refuses any scope that contains more than 4,096 tracked files (`empty or oversized scope`) and always writes a `corvint-corpus-input/1` manifest with a single scope. The `corvint-corpus-input/2` build path accepts up to 100,000 records, so a producer with a medium repository must split the tree into many small scopes, run the command once per scope, and merge the manifests by hand into a /2 manifest.
title: docs corpus manifest: emit /2 manifests with multiple scopes and the /2 bound (GitHub #1241)

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture with two repositories: a claim anchored in repository B builds, appears in `docs_search`/`docs_get` with `repository = B` and B's revision, and goes `stale` when the file changes in B (not in A).
An anchor naming an undeclared repository is still refused.
Single-repository manifests are byte-identical to today.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1243 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). A documentation corpus anchors exactly one repository. Every provider anchor must carry `repository == manifest.repository.id`, and every scope revision must resolve to that same repository identity. Documentation that describes a system spread over several repositories (an application, a shared library, a separate end-to-end test repository) can only be imported by copying the other repositories' files under path prefixes into one scratch repository. The anchors then lose their real repository identity and revision, freshness is checked against the wrong history, and downstream consumers cannot map a citation back to the real file. `/2` behaviour contracts already list other repositories, but only to record a `repository-evidence-unavailable` gap.
title: Corpus anchors into additional declared repositories at their own pinned revisions (GitHub #1243)

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture provider with one supplied gap, one status, one case link: build admits all three; `import_parity` counts them; `docs_gaps --id p:flow:a` returns the supplied gap marked `supplied`; the case link suppresses `missing-manual-cases`.
5,000 observations in a `/2` manifest build successfully.
Supplied gaps/status never raise trust (remain `generated` / attributed).
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1244 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). `corvint-corpus-adoption-provider/1` admits subjects, claims, relations, journeys, observations and a fixed set of typed details (`claim_kind`, `flow`, `paragraph`, `test_link`, `coverage`, `ticket`, `intent_comparison`). Several common documentation-corpus families have no typed home and are lost at export:  1. Producer-supplied gaps. `Artifact.Gaps` is compiler-computed only; `ProviderRecord` has no gaps field, so curated gap ledgers (with kind, reason, owner disposition) cannot be imported. 2. Readiness / proof status per subject (e.g. `blocked`, `ready`, `proven` with a reason and the evidence ids it rests on). There is no status detail; forcing it into untyped claims makes it unqueryable by `docs_gaps`/`docs_coverage`. 3. Manual test case <-> subject links. Legacy cases are searched from a separate export file outside the corpus; there is no relation type or detail joining a case id to a flow/endpoint subject, so `docs_gaps` cannot use them (`missing-manual-cases` is driven only by journeys). 4. Test-run receipts beyond the test-validity document format, and observations are capped at 4,096 per corpus even for `/2` manifests.
title: Adoption providers: typed supplied gaps, status detail, manual-case links, /2 observation bound (GitHub #1244)

acceptanceCriteria: The reproduction above: the gap clears (or is replaced by a weaker, distinct gap such as `asserting-e2e-tests-unauthenticated-review`).
A test asserts the *absence* of `missing-asserting-e2e-tests` for a fixture that satisfies the documented rule (today the suite only asserts its presence).
A relation with `join_confidence: "inferred"` or `role: "related"` still yields the gap.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1245 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). `docs_gaps` emits `missing-asserting-e2e-tests` for a flow unless one of its relations has an exact, asserting `test_link` whose evidence `Trust == "reviewed"`. But provider evidence that declares `trust: "reviewed"` is always rewritten during import to `Trust = "generated"` with `ReportedTrust = "reviewed"`, and no other code path sets `Trust = "reviewed"` on a relation. The clearing condition is unreachable, so every flow in every corpus reports `missing-asserting-e2e-tests`, regardless of how well it is tested. (Found by source reading; consistent with every flow in a 159-flow corpus reporting the gap.)
title: missing-asserting-e2e-tests gap can never clear: requires trust reviewed which import rewrites to generated (GitHub #1245)

acceptanceCriteria: `id: "C12345"` returns exactly that case; unknown id returns `none-found`.
Query `"how do I cancel a paid booking"` in ranked mode returns the case above first.
Existing all-token behaviour unchanged when `match: "all"` (default or explicit, documented).
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1246 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). `corvint.docs_search_cases` (and `docs corpus search-cases`) matches a case only if every query token is a prefix of some word in the title, path, preconditions or steps. Natural-language questions ("how is a booking cancelled after payment") therefore return `none-found` because function words never all appear. The case id is not a searched field, so a known case id (e.g. `C12345`) cannot be retrieved, and there is no id parameter. Results are unranked (first N in file order).
title: docs_search_cases: id lookup and ranked any-word search (GitHub #1246)

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture flow with 8 sections: `section: "B"` returns only B's paragraphs; payload <= 1/4 of the unfiltered call.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1247 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). `corvint.docs_flow` returns, for one flow id, the flow subject plus every claim, every relation on the flow, every joined test-knowledge record, and every paragraph of every section. On a medium corpus, five sampled `docs_flow` calls returned ~19x the characters of a reference server answering the same flow-detail calls, which costs agent context and latency.
title: docs_flow: section and record-kind filters to bound the payload (GitHub #1247)

acceptanceCriteria: The first indexed call on an over-bound corpus refuses in under 50 ms at the #1254 shape (~100k records), naming the bound and a count or lower bound.
Within-bound corpora still answer byte-identically.
body: V1-1995 (PR #1264, DCP-V1-193..197) memoizes the query index or its refusal per opened artifact, so later calls answer in under 50 ms, but the first index-backed call still derives the whole index before refusing. #1254 asked the refusal to arrive in under 50 ms. A cheap lower bound on postings/key bytes computed before term extraction could refuse earlier.
title: Indexed corpus tools still pay one full index derivation (~0.5 s) before the first over-bound refusal (GitHub #1254 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A benchmark at 100k records with long claims shows index derivation allocation reduced materially (target under 1 GiB) with identical index output.
body: Observed by the V1-1995 lane (PR #1264) while scaling query-index bounds: deriving the query index allocates per-claim EvidenceTerms slices totalling about 5.4 GiB at 100k records with long claims. Measured in the lane's capacity test, not on a live corpus.
title: Per-claim EvidenceTerms allocation reaches 5.4 GiB at 100k records with long claims

acceptanceCriteria: `docs corpus build` refuses, with the same typed code, every condition that would make the index derivation refuse at query time, or the spec names the ones it cannot pre-check.
body: V1-1995 (PR #1264, DCP-V1-196) makes `docs corpus build` refuse an artifact whose query index would exceed the capacity bound, but other index derivation refusals are still discovered only when a tool first queries the artifact.
title: docs corpus build only pre-checks index capacity; other query-index refusals still surface at query time

acceptanceCriteria: corpusrepublish and flowdocs builds refuse an over-bound index with the DCP-V1-196 code, with a test each.
body: V1-1995 (PR #1264) added a build-time index capacity check (BuildAdmitted) used by `docs corpus build`; corpus builds through corpusrepublish and flowdocs do not call it, so they can still produce an artifact whose indexed tools refuse every call.
title: corpusrepublish and flowdocs corpus builds bypass the BuildAdmitted index-capacity check

acceptanceCriteria: A supplied test_run receipt and a test-validity record for the same test either share one typed representation or the spec defines how they relate, and docs_coverage counts them once.
Existing corpora stay byte-identical or the change is called out with its migration.
body: Residual of V1-1993 (PR #1267, DCP-V1-210..211). Adoption providers can now supply a typed `test_run` claim detail (origin supplied), counted as claim/test_run and supplied_test_run:OUTCOME coverage rows. It is separate from the existing test-validity format, so the corpus has two shapes for test-run evidence with no defined reconciliation.
title: Reconcile supplied test_run receipts with the test-validity format

acceptanceCriteria: Playwright 1.64.0 is qualified by a retained live run (or refused with a documented local qualification procedure), traced to new PWP-V0 requirements
A version refusal writes a typed refusal JSON naming the qualified versions to stdout instead of a 0-byte document
Focused jstestprovider tests pass and fail without the fix
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1263: corvint-js-test-provider e2e --external-server --runner-version=1.64.0 refuses with external-playwright-version-unqualified (qualifiedPlaywrightVersion in internal/jstestprovider/external.go admits only 1.60.0/1.63.0) and leaves a 0-byte stdout document. Expected: 1.64.0 qualified via live run per playwright-external-provider-v0, and a typed refusal document on stdout naming qualified versions.

acceptanceCriteria: Retained live runs (or recorded unavailable observations) for Playwright 1.64.0 on profiles /1 and /2, on Node 24, with system Chrome, and on Linux
Each newly qualified tuple is admitted only by its own PWP-V0 requirement and live evidence
body: Residual from V1-2005 / PR #1269 (#1263): Playwright 1.64.0 is qualified only for /0 and /3 on Darwin arm64 Node v22.23.2 with bundled browsers. Unqualified: /1, /2, Node 24, system Chrome, Linux. The consuming repository's checkout was not observed.
title: Qualify Playwright 1.64.0 external provider on /1, /2, Node 24, system Chrome and Linux

acceptanceCriteria: Root cause of the 'observer descendants never started' failure identified (deadline vs runner load, or the observer exiting before spawning)
The test's startup wait is bounded by a load-tolerant deadline or the observer's own readiness signal, and the fix is proven under -race with CPU contention
body: Suspected flake (not confirmed bug): TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption (internal/appflows/observer_unix_test.go:74) failed on hosted ubuntu in run 39357611388 job 118416710971 (batch PR #1268, shard 4, 2026-10-20T02:19Z) with 'observer descendants never started' after 10.55s. Failed jobs rerun.
title: Suspected flake: TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption reports 'observer descendants never started' on hosted ubuntu (PR #1268 shard 4)

acceptanceCriteria: docs/CAPABILITIES.md is an agent-facing catalog covering every `corvint` top-level command listed by `corvint help`, every shipped cmd/* binary, and every corvint-mcp / corvint-docs-mcp / corvint-test-validity-mcp tool profile: what question it answers, when to use it, minimal invocation, output profile, maturity (stable/experimental/internal), abstain/refusal behaviour, and owning spec.
A drift check (make target wired into the existing doc-gates list) fails when a command, binary or MCP tool is added or removed without a catalog row, and is proven to fail on a synthetic omission.

AGENTS.md, docs/AGENT-ROUTES.md, docs/README.md, README.md and the shipped agent skills (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi) route to the catalog; stale capability claims found while doing so are corrected (absorbs V1-0130, V1-1271, V1-1821).
Owning spec requirements, traceability and a build-log entry are recorded.
body: Owner request 2026-10-20: make sure Corvint's capabilities are properly documented so agents can fully understand what it can do. Today capability knowledge is spread across `corvint help`, 55 cmd binaries, MCP tool profiles, per-host skills, docs/AGENT-ROUTES.md and spec Agent digests; no single agent-facing catalog exists and nothing prevents drift (e.g. V1-1271 Codex skill says non-Go impact unsupported; V1-0130 PORTFOLIO omits verbs).
title: docs: agent-facing capability catalog for every command, binary and MCP tool, with a drift gate

acceptanceCriteria: Done by #1278 (V1-2006, PWP-V0-035..038): the 1.64.0 tuples are admitted, including Node v24.11.1 for /0 and /3, and an e2e refusal exits 3 with one stderr line (#1275).
Receipts and freshness admit from ONE shared exact-tuple table (exact Node patch, runner version, browser source, per decision 0448); freshness on Playwright 1.64.0 is admitted only with a live run.
A refusal document names the failing tuple field (node, runner or browser source) and the admitted values.
Node major/minor ranges (the #1270 request) stay unadmitted unless the owner amends decision 0448; until then #1270 is answered with Refs, not Closes.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1270: the receipt (internal/jstestprovider external.go qualifiedNodeVersion) and freshness (freshness.go Node v22.23.3 + runner 1.63.0) pins are exact patch versions that exclude each other; Node 24 LTS and Playwright 1.64.0 can never qualify. #1275: admission refusals share the exit status of run failures and write nothing on stderr. Folded into the V1-2006 lane (PWP-V0 range).
title: JS test provider: one declared runtime tuple set for receipts and freshness, plus a distinct admission-refusal exit code (GitHub #1270, #1275)

acceptanceCriteria: path:line and path[ids] selectors are accepted, recorded as the selection, and each selector reports an outcome including matched-no-example.
Under --exec-prefix the document records Ruby, Bundler and image/container digest observed inside the prefix, or an explicit unknown.
Each example records its shared-example origin file and line when defined in a shared example.
Spec requirements, fail-without-fix tests and a build-log entry are recorded; a real Ruby/container run is evidence or NOT_RUN.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1271: corvint-ruby-test-provider rspec --spec accepts files/dirs only, records no container runtime identity under --exec-prefix (Git observed on host only), and gives no shared-example origin. Owning spec LPCV-V0 (live-proof-carrying-verification-v0, LPCV-V0-090..095 RSpec provider).
title: Ruby test provider: example-level selectors, in-prefix runtime identity and shared-example origin (GitHub #1271)

acceptanceCriteria: A declared-isolation profile takes server identity (URL + revision/digest) and a pinned reset/health hook, verifies identity before and after each control, resets between controls, and reports infrastructure_failed (never killed) on drift or reset failure; the receipt records the declared isolation.

A runner-neutral control profile takes a pinned perturbation hook under the same plan-approval and containment rules, reruns selected examples through a non-browser provider, and reports the six closed statuses.
At least the Go provider is wired end to end; Ruby wiring follows #1271 or is a recorded residual.
Spec requirements, fail-without-fix tests and a build-log entry are recorded.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1273: BBF-V0-004 only runs controls in a disposable workspace, so adopters testing against a long-lived local app server get no assertion strength. #1274: negative controls are browser-only; Ruby/Go provider examples stay NOT_MEASURED. Owning spec browser-behavior-falsification-v0 (BBF-V0). #1274's Ruby binding depends on #1271 example selection.
title: Falsification: declared-isolation shared-server profile and runner-neutral negative controls for non-browser providers (GitHub #1273, #1274)

acceptanceCriteria: Interrupting corvint-tasks gate run (SIGINT/SIGTERM, supervisor timeout) is reproduced and its retained output observed: whether partial gate stdout/stderr and the attempt record survive is recorded as evidence.
If partial output is lost, gate run retains a bounded transcript and an interrupted outcome on interruption, with a test proving it.
Spec requirement, test and build-log entry are recorded, or the observation closes the ticket with evidence that retention already works.
body: Decision 0544 closes CORE-FINISH-INTERRUPTED-TRANSCRIPT-PRESERVATION-1 as obsolete (Core managed finish no longer runs gates after the ADR-0227 cutover). The successor question for Corvint Tasks is NOT_OBSERVED: does corvint-tasks gate run retain the gate transcript and an interrupted outcome when the run is interrupted?
title: Tasks gate run: observe and retain the gate transcript on interruption (successor to CORE-FINISH-INTERRUPTED-TRANSCRIPT-PRESERVATION-1)

acceptanceCriteria: A Corvint-shipped RSpec formatter (or documented formatter option) emits shared_group_inclusion_backtrace and the provider records the including file:line instead of not-reported
A real RSpec run (rspec gem installed) proves it, with a fail-without-fix test
Stock-formatter runs still record not-reported
body: V1-2010 (PR #1282, LPCV-V0-133) records shared-example provenance as not-reported on stock runs because the stock RSpec JSON formatter omits shared_group_inclusion_backtrace. GitHub #1271 item 3 stays partly unmet. Version: branch claude/ruby-provider-examples-2010 at 39600b79d.
title: Ruby provider: record RSpec shared-example provenance with a formatter that emits shared_group_inclusion_backtrace

acceptanceCriteria: A live docker-prefixed run qualifies the probe: container id is the run's container, or is recorded unknown when it cannot be proven
Image digest is recorded from host-side observation when available, unknown otherwise
Retained live receipt plus a test
body: V1-2010 (PR #1282, LPCV-V0-132) always records the image digest as unknown (not observable from inside the prefix) and records the probe's own container id, which need not be the run's container. NOT_RUN: real docker prefix. GitHub #1271 item 2 partly unmet.
title: Ruby provider: live container qualification of the runtime probe (image digest, run container identity)

acceptanceCriteria: Root cause identified from a retained 1.64.0 trace
Either the derivation handles 1.64.0 traces (12/12 live) or 1.64.0 stays unqualified for negation with a spec row saying so
Test covering the 1.64.0 trace shape
body: V1-1022/1024 live qualification (PR #1280, head d8ed9839c) ran the step-negation cases on Playwright 1.64.0: 7/12 refused step-fault-underivable. Suspected cause: 1.64 trace-format change (SUSPECTED, not confirmed). Expected: step faults derivable as on the qualified tuples.

Spec qualification table lists the Linux tuple or records it as unqualified
body: V1-1022/1024 (PR #1280) qualified only darwin/arm64; no Linux Playwright tuple was run, so Linux CI hosts abstain.

acceptanceCriteria: Profile identifies the slow tests
Package runs under 300 s on the same host without dropping coverage, or the slow cases move behind a documented long-test tag

title: internal/tasks/cli tests take ~701 s

Repaired runner receipts compose on one bound source with a test

title: CEM chain: current versus historical Tasks authority and runner-repair composition on one bound source

title: QUESTION: V1-0632 criterion 2 'preserve 0.x bytes' superseded by decision 0525

Synthetic-omission tests for each

acceptanceCriteria: Comment corrected
Every corvint-mcp profile has a golden tool-list test that fails on an added or removed tool

title: corvint-mcp: flows profile comment says four tools where five are served; only 2 of 4 profiles have goldens

OpenSpec skill metadata version bumped with its content, host-package-versions check passes
Pi routing decided and recorded

Parity test over native and portable outputs

Two-process concurrent anchor test: exactly one wins, the loser is refused, nothing overwritten

Mutation test for the new coverage

acceptanceCriteria: A Ruby provider profile binding exists in internal/behaviorfalsify with BBF requirement rows
Negative controls run for the Ruby provider and fail closed on an unsupported receipt profile
#1274 is commented or closed with the evidence

GitHub #1274 asks for runner-neutral negative controls across providers; the Ruby provider binding was left out because V1-2010 (Ruby provider examples, PR #1282) is not on main yet.
