Application markers observed under the provider are recorded in that receipt
Tests prove a missing or mismatched marker reads INCOMPLETE, not complete
body: Found by the V1-2011 lane (PR #1285, head 17e98b009, BBF-V0-019..028). The provider plan is executed without its own retained evidence receipt, and application markers (what the provider actually started) are not recorded under the provider. Expected: each provider plan step emits a receipt that names the plan digest and the observed application markers so a reviewer can confirm the plan that ran. Actual: only the overall falsification receipt is retained.
title: Falsification: evidence receipts for provider plans and application markers under the provider

acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce or refute the check/exec gap with a test that swaps the toolchain after verification
If confirmed, execute the verified bytes and prove the swap is refused
Record the outcome in the BBF spec
body: Found by the V1-2011 lane (PR #1285, head 17e98b009, BBF-V0-019..028). Suspected defect, not confirmed: the Go toolchain is digest-checked and then executed from its original location, so a replacement between the check and exec would run an unverified binary (TOCTOU). Expected: execute exactly the bytes that were verified (copy to a private dir, or open+verify the fd). Actual (per lane report): runs in place.
title: Suspected: falsification Go toolchain runs in place, leaving a gap between digest check and execution

acceptanceCriteria: The receipt distinguishes independently observed from hook-reported server identity
A forged hook identity cannot produce a complete verdict
Spec row plus test
body: Found by the V1-2011 lane (PR #1285, head 17e98b009, BBF-V0-019..028). The declared-isolation shared-server profile records server identity as reported by the caller's hook; Corvint does not check it independently. Expected: the receipt either independently observes the server identity (pid/port/binary digest) or labels the identity as hook-reported and unverified. Actual: hook-reported identity flows into the receipt without that label.
title: Falsification: verify shared-server identity independently instead of trusting the caller's hook report

acceptanceCriteria: CHANGE-EVIDENCE-MAP.md states the K1 outcome with a link to the V1-1266 build log
line-citations-check passes
body: Found by the V1-1266 lane (PR #1286, head 6e7387505). docs/CHANGE-EVIDENCE-MAP.md:70 still lists the K1 kill criterion for hunk-revert held verdicts as pending. V1-1266 measured it: 0 held of 3,790 hunks over 350 maps after #944 (build log 2026-10-20-V1-1266-hunk-revert-falsifier.md). Expected: the map doc states the K1 outcome and links the build log.
title: docs: CHANGE-EVIDENCE-MAP.md lists K1 without its measured kill outcome

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-change runs the guarding-test search by default (or records why it cannot)
K1 re-tallied over the next 30 Go-code changes with held counts per hunk
Retire or keep decision recorded from that tally
body: Found by the V1-1266 lane (PR #1286, head 6e7387505). K1 fired (0 held) but none of the sampled test-claim citations came from --guarding-tests; internal/dogfoodflow reports guarding-tests-not-run without running it. Decision (orchestrator, under the 2026-10-05 delegation): keep --hunk-revert and --guarding-tests as opt-in steps, not retired, and re-measure K1 once dogfood-change runs the guarding-test search by default. Expected: a fresh 30-change window after that switch.
title: Re-measure K1 after dogfood-change runs the guarding-test search automatically

acceptanceCriteria: Test interrupts gate run with INT, TERM and HUP and asserts the partial transcript is retained
The gate result records the interruption explicitly (not PASS, not silently absent)
Same check for run --attempt or a recorded NOT_RUN reason
body: Decision 0544 item 4 closed CORE-FINISH-INTERRUPTED-TRANSCRIPT-PRESERVATION-1 as obsolete (script/roadmap.sh deleted by ADR-0227) and moved the open question here: whether corvint-tasks gate run (and run --attempt) retains the gate's output/transcript and a recorded outcome after a supervised INT, TERM or HUP. Currently NOT_OBSERVED. Expected: an interrupted gate leaves its partial transcript and an explicit interrupted gate result, never a silently lost transcript.
title: Does corvint-tasks gate run keep the gate transcript when interrupted by INT/TERM/HUP?

acceptanceCriteria: Each refusal class (inexact sidecar, failing OCM, retired 0.x map) records the verifier stage reached and either a partial result or a NOT_RUN reason
Tests cover each class
body: Found by the V1-0632 gap 1 lane (PR #1287, CEM-V1-293). corvint-dashboard-snapshot cem-stable refuses these inputs but cannot retain a verifier result, because the verifier is not reached or not run. Expected: each refusal names which verification step was reached and keeps the partial verifier result or an explicit NOT_RUN reason. Actual: the refusal carries only the code and the input digests.
title: dashboard cem-stable refusal keeps no verifier result when the sidecar is inexact, the OCM fails or the map is a retired 0.x map

acceptanceCriteria: The enrollment format carries the artifact bytes, or a content-addressed reference, for cem/1.0 capsules
The closure admits a capsule built in another worktree; a test proves it
body: Found by the V1-0632 gap 1 lane (PR #1287). A capsule enrollment for a cem/1.0 map names its artifacts by digest, but the enrollment format cannot carry the artifact bytes, so a capsule built elsewhere cannot be closed without the producing worktree. Expected: an enrollment either carries the bounded artifact bytes or names a content-addressed source the closure can read. Actual: the closure needs the artifacts present locally.
title: local-authority enrollment format does not carry artifact bytes for stable CEM capsules

acceptanceCriteria: A real cem/1.0 enrollment completes the protected flow, or onlyCodecPackage is narrowed with a decision
A live enrollment run on a real map is retained as evidence
body: Found by the V1-0632 gap 1 lane (PR #1287). The protected local-authority command requires a codec-only target tree (onlyCodecPackage), so a real repository's stable enrollment cannot run the full protected flow; the full enrollment was NOT_RUN for V1-0632 gap 1. Expected: a real cem/1.0 enrollment can run the protected flow, or the requirement is narrowed with a recorded reason. Actual: it refuses any tree that is not codec-only.
title: protected capsule command onlyCodecPackage check blocks real cem/1.0 enrollments

acceptanceCriteria: test-read-scopes-check (or a sibling) fails when a declared package's non-test module dependencies are not covered by its read scope, at least for packages whose tests run go list
Proven on a synthetic omission that reproduces the #1288 case
The test failure message includes go list's stderr, not a bare exit status
body: Batch PR #1288 (CI run 39376177909, go-product-shard 3): TestGitNotesFetchesNothing failed with a bare 'gitnotes_test.go:296: exit status 1' from 'go list -deps .'. The cause: #1279 (V1-1292) made internal/gitnotes import internal/cem/verify, which pulls in internal/cem/sim, and neither directory was in the package's .corvint/test-read-scopes.json entry. Under Landlock, go list cannot read them. 'make test-read-scopes-check' passed locally, and the test passes locally without confinement. Fixed in batch commit 3d220661a by adding both directories. V1-1736 (TestCCEV0015CoreBoundary, bare exit status 1 from go list -deps) is probably the same class. Expected: the check fails when a declared package's non-standard transitive imports fall outside its read scope, or when a declared package's test shells out to go list. Actual: the check does not compare scopes with the import graph.
title: test-read-scopes-check misses transitive module deps that go list -deps needs under Landlock

acceptanceCriteria: ticket show and ticket blockers report the effective required gate set, including policy-mandated gates, matching what complete enforces
A regression test with a ticket whose own requiredGates omit a policy-mandated gate shows that gate in both read outputs and in complete's MISSING_GATE refusal
body: Observed 2026-10-20 with corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.676: ticket show and ticket blockers for V1-0254 report requiredGates ["full-gate"] and for V1-1114 report []. After a passing full-gate (about 2.5 h), complete refused MISSING_GATE with 'gate focused-docs has no result' for all eight tickets. A closeout driven by the reported requiredGates therefore fails at the last step; when the caller then releases, the passing gate result is stranded on a cancelled attempt (V1-0253, 2026-10-20). Expected: the read surfaces report the effective gate set (ticket gates plus policy-mandated gates) that complete will enforce, or complete names the policy source. Related but distinct: V1-1874 (approval grants revealed one at a time).
title: corvint-tasks: ticket show/blockers report requiredGates without the policy-mandated focused-docs gate that complete demands

acceptanceCriteria: A combined per-example record keyed by a stable example identity carries the run outcome, the test-validity verdict and the source revision/blob both used.
The join is refused with a typed code when the receipt and verdict revisions differ.
Spec requirements and tests cover a shifted-line case and a shared-group example.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1291 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. A consumer that accepts a passing test as evidence needs two facts about the same example: it ran and passed (provider receipt), and its assertions are meaningful (test-validity verdict). Today these are separate documents with no shared key, so consumers must join them by file:line heuristics. That breaks when lines shift or an example comes from a shared group. Ask: emit (or allow requesting) a combined record per selected example, keyed by a stable example identity, with the run outcome, the validity verdict and the source revision/blob both were computed on. Refuse the join when the revisions differ. See beamfall/corvint#1291 for the full text.
title: Join an example-level test receipt to its test-validity verdict in one record (issue #1291)

acceptanceCriteria: Callers can pass requirement IDs per selector (flag or mapping file) for Ruby and JS selected examples.
The receipt echoes each ID beside the example outcome, marked caller-asserted, never inferred.
Spec requirements and tests cover malformed and unknown selectors.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1292 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. Consumers map tests to external requirement or row identifiers. For JS tests this is done via titles/steps; for selected Ruby examples there is no channel, so the mapping lives outside the receipt and must be re-validated separately. Ask: let the caller pass requirement IDs per selector (e.g. `--select path[id]=REQ-1,REQ-2` or a mapping file). Echo them in the receipt next to each example's outcome, so a receipt alone shows which requirement each passing example witnessed. Mark them caller-asserted, not inferred. See beamfall/corvint#1292 for the full text.
title: Carry caller-supplied requirement IDs through selected-example receipts (issue #1292)

acceptanceCriteria: Test validity analyses Jest TypeScript test files on the same verdict axes as the existing JS provider, or the spec names each axis that cannot apply and why.
Fixture tests cover skipped, assertion-free and never-executed assertions in Jest.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1293 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. Test validity analyses Playwright and Ruby tests, but Jest (TypeScript) tests return an advisory 'not analysed' result. Repositories with Jest unit or integration suites therefore cannot get the same assertion-strength judgement (skipped tests, assertion-free tests, assertions that never execute) for those tests, and consumers must treat them as unreviewed. Ask: support Jest test files in test validity with the same verdict axes as the existing JS provider, or document which axes cannot apply. See beamfall/corvint#1293 for the full text.
title: Test validity: analyse TypeScript/Jest tests (issue #1293)

acceptanceCriteria: When a changed file is a test-support module, affected reports the statically importing test files as a narrowed candidate set, still labelled as a fallback.
The plan reports changed symbols so callers can see additive-only changes.
Dynamic resolution in one sub-project does not drop narrowing for statically resolved sub-projects.
Tests cover each case; the fallback stays fail-closed.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1294 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. When a change touches a widely imported test-support module (a shared fixture/registry file), `affected` selects 0 units and falls back to FULL_RELEVANT_SUITE with scope UNKNOWN. That is fail-closed and correct, but it makes every shared-support change cost a full suite. In one case discovery also refused because a sub-project resolves dependencies dynamically. Ask: - When the changed file is a test-support module, compute the importing test files from the static import graph and report them as a narrowed candidate set, still labelled as a fallback. - Report which symbols changed, so callers can see whether only additive exports changed. - When dynamic resolution blocks discovery in one sub-project, keep the narrowing for the sub-projects that resolve statically. See beamfall/corvint#1294 for the full text.
title: affected: narrow selection by import graph when a shared fixture module changes (issue #1294)

acceptanceCriteria: impact and test-validity JSON receipts carry a producer object with version, build and commit, with a stated value when a field is unknown.
Release installs report a non-zero build in --version, or the spec states why build 0 is correct and how consumers identify the build.
Spec requirements and tests cover a dev build and a release-stamped build.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1300 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** `corvint impact` and `corvint test-validity` JSON name no producer version, build or commit. `corvint --version` prints `Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 0)` for an installed release build, so a consumer that must label each derived item with the producing build has to infer it from the install directory name. **Wanted.** A `producer` object in every receipt (`version`, `build`, `commit`), and a non-zero build in `--version` for release installs. **Why.** Consumers that cache or cite receipts cannot tell which build produced them, and cross-build comparisons are unverifiable. See beamfall/corvint#1300 for the full text.
title: Machine-readable receipts carry no producer build identity (issue #1300)

acceptanceCriteria: Either corvint affected accepts an explicit changed-path list at HEAD with the existing fallback vocabulary, or impact receipts state the reverse-import closure depth and that the list is not a closed selection.
A READY receipt never implies a complete test selection it does not have.
Spec requirements and tests cover a two-hop importer case.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1301 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** `corvint impact PATH...` returns one-hop syntax evidence (the changed path and its direct reverse importers, including test files). Tests reached through a second hop (a test importing a module that imports the changed path) are absent, while the receipt still reports `state: READY`, no unknowns and no uncertainty. `corvint affected` produces a selection plan but only from the dirty worktree, a `--base` commit range, or a `--snapshot` receipt; there is no mode taking an arbitrary list of changed paths at the captured revision. **Wanted.** Either `corvint affected --paths PATH...` (plan for these paths at HEAD, with the same fallback vocabulary such as `FULL_RELEVANT_SUITE`), or an explicit field on impact receipts stating the closure depth and that the result is not a closed test selection (for example `selection_closed: false`, `reverse_import_depth: 1`). **Why.** A consum See beamfall/corvint#1301 for the full text.
title: No path-list mode for a closed affected-test selection (issue #1301)

acceptanceCriteria: Every corvint-test-validity/0 test projection carries a repository-relative file, line and titlePath where the provider knows them, and an explicit absent marker otherwise.
Tests cover RSpec and Playwright projections, including a shared-group example.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1302 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** Each `tests[]` entry in `corvint-test-validity/0` has `id`, `name`, `package`, `state` and the projection axes, but no `file`, `line` or `titlePath`. Joining a verdict to a spec file needs a substring match on `id`/`name`, which is format-dependent (RSpec ids are `./spec/x_spec.rb[1:2]`; Playwright ids are opaque). **Wanted.** `file` (repository-relative), `line` and `titlePath` on every test projection. See beamfall/corvint#1302 for the full text.
title: Test-validity projections have no structured test location (issue #1302)

acceptanceCriteria: A read-only static test-validity mode projects the hygiene axis from source for Playwright and RSpec files without a retained run.
Execution and strength axes stay NOT_OBSERVED in static mode; the mode writes nothing.
Spec requirements and tests cover skipped, focused, fixme and assertion-free tests.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1303 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** `corvint test-validity --discover` returns `tests: []` with `abstention.reason: no-retained-evidence` unless a provider run was retained under `.corvint/test-evidence`. Static facts that need no run (skipped / focused / fixme tests, tests with no assertion or expectation calls) are therefore unavailable for a whole suite. **Wanted.** A read-only static mode (for example `test-validity --static [PATH...]`) projecting the hygiene axis from source for Playwright and RSpec files, with execution and strength left `NOT_OBSERVED`. See beamfall/corvint#1303 for the full text.
title: No static test-hygiene projection without a retained run (issue #1303)

acceptanceCriteria: A machine-readable impact capability listing names suffixes with rules, suffixes admitted without rules, and per-call limits; or impact reports unadmitted paths as unanalysed instead of refusing the call.
The listing is derived from the same table the admission code uses, with a test that they agree.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1304 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** Which paths `corvint impact` accepts depends on the immutable index: some suffixes get reverse-import rules (Go/Ruby/JS/TS), other indexed suffixes (for example `.json`) are accepted with a missing-rule uncertainty, and unindexed suffixes return `unsupported-impact-path-suffix` for the whole call. The only description is prose in `--help`, so a consumer must hard-code its own suffix list to avoid a whole-call refusal. **Wanted.** A machine-readable capability listing (for example `corvint impact --capabilities --json`) naming suffixes with rules, suffixes admitted without rules, and the per-call limits (path count, `--limit` range); or an option to report unadmitted paths in the receipt as `unanalysed` instead of refusing the call. See beamfall/corvint#1304 for the full text.
title: No machine-readable list of admitted impact path suffixes (issue #1304)

acceptanceCriteria: Reading projectDir or layout.projectDirectory in a build script no longer marks the layout mapped; only an assignment that remaps a project directory does.
A fixture with rootProject.projectDir reads yields a runnable :module:testDebugUnitTest (or test) task; a fixture with a real remapping keeps the unresolved frontier.
The owning KAT-V0 requirement is traced to the new tests.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). internal/liveverify/affected/kotlin/kotlin.go:180 sets layout.projectMapped when the build text merely contains "projectDir" (for example rootProject.projectDir or layout.projectDirectory), and testTarget then returns task "unknown". On beamfall-android (app-mobile/build.gradle.kts:239,380) and beamfall-android-ui (build.gradle.kts:20, kit/build.gradle.kts:158,355) every unit becomes kotlin:jvm:<module>:unknown:... with build-target-unresolved and test-address-unresolved frontiers, so no Gradle test address is runnable. Expected: only an actual project-directory remapping (projectDir = ... / project(...).projectDir = ... assignment in settings) marks the layout mapped.
title: affected/kotlin: projectMapped substring test on "projectDir" turns every Gradle test task into "unknown" in ordinary Android builds

acceptanceCriteria: Paths inside a recognised Tasks store projection (.taskman/) are classified as non-source task state, with a stated reason, and do not make affected scope UNKNOWN unless a test reads them.
Impact freshness reports them separately rather than degrading source freshness.
Tests cover a repo with a dirty .taskman projection and a test that reads a .taskman file.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). In ~/projects/core-history (Tasks store queue:core:main), `corvint affected --base` reported 866 unknowns, 820 of them UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH under .taskman/, and impact reported mixed freshness over 43 .taskman paths. Every repo that adopts Corvint Tasks carries a dirty projection most of the time, so affected never yields a closed selection there. Related: V1-1524 (hook deadline at ~1,270 dirty .taskman paths), V1-1766 (.taskman/policy.json basename readers).
title: affected/impact: Tasks store projection paths (.taskman/**) count as unowned dirty paths, so scope is always UNKNOWN in repos that use Corvint Tasks

acceptanceCriteria: A spec (or a section of an existing affected spec) owns the Python adapter with numbered requirements, non-goals, failure modes and an experimental qualification label.
Existing tests are traced to those requirements; untested requirements are listed as gaps.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). internal/liveverify/affected/python/python.go runs in every affected call, yet nothing under docs/specs cites affected/python, so its claims are unqualified. Beamfall core-history (106 .py) and oscillux depend on it.
title: affected/python is registered in languages.All() but has no owning spec, requirements or qualification state

acceptanceCriteria: affected either follows go.work sibling modules (selecting dependents in the root repo for a sibling change supplied explicitly), or names the supported cross-repository route (e.g. breakage) in the frontier detail.
Tests cover a go.work with an outside-root sibling.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). Beamfall core-history's go.work uses ../beamfall-plugin-* siblings; affected reports frontier go:workspace-module-outside-root and cannot follow changes across the workspace. Related V1-0874 (go.work parser unification).
title: affected/golang: go.work `use ../sibling` modules outside the repository root are an unresolved frontier

acceptanceCriteria: A read-only command emits a machine-readable per-repository setup report with each gap, its evidence and a suggested fix, and writes nothing.
Tests cover a fully set up fixture and one with each gap class.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). Assessing 25 Beamfall repos needed two review agents assembling init/affected/overview output by hand. No verb reports: missing or stale index snapshot, AGENTS/CLAUDE files with no Corvint route, stale host hooks, repositories without a declared gate, and paths ignored only by the global git excludes file (decision 0158). V1-1977's build log records `doctor` as NOT_PRODUCED.
title: Adoption check: one read-only command that reports a repository's Corvint setup gaps (index snapshot, agent-instruction wiring, hooks, ignored-path drift)

acceptanceCriteria: The refusal and the MIXED report name the drifting paths (bounded list) and state that global excludes are not honoured, with the fix (tracked .gitignore or .git/info/exclude).
Tests cover a path ignored only by core.excludesFile.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). Corvint ignores global excludes by design (decision 0158, sanitizedGitEnvironment in internal/genesis/repository.go). In beamfall-apple-ui, beamfall-android-ui and beamfall-windows, .claude/settings.local.json is ignored only via ~/.config/git/ignore, so `overview` refuses with "dirty worktree or status drift" (internal/genesis/guidance.go:111-135) without saying which path or why.
title: overview/affected refuse or report MIXED on paths ignored only by the global git excludes file without naming the path

acceptanceCriteria: A version-catalog change maps to the modules whose build scripts reference the changed aliases, or to all modules with a stated reason.
com.android.test modules yield a typed unit or an explicit typed frontier instead of kotlin:unknown.
Tests cover both.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). In beamfall-android and beamfall-android-ui, gradle/libs.versions.toml is UNOWNED (no build-config edge), and com.android.test modules (benchmark-*, baselineprofile-*) produce kotlin:unknown units.
title: affected/kotlin: model the Gradle version catalog and com.android.test modules

acceptanceCriteria: Either affected/breakage resolves includeBuild and SPM local/revision dependencies to the dependent repo's units, or both are reported as a named cross-repository frontier with the dependency path.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). beamfall-android uses includeBuild(../beamfall-android-ui) and beamfall-apple pins beamfall-apple-ui by SwiftPM revision; breakage covers Go only, so cross-repo obligations are invisible.
title: affected: cross-repository edges for Gradle includeBuild and SwiftPM revision pins

acceptanceCriteria: Each class gets a typed ownership classification (owned by a declared consumer, or explicitly unsupported with a code) instead of a generic unowned path.
Tests cover one path of each class.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). Shader edits in beamfall-visual-shaders and beamfall-apple-ui, SQL migrations in core-history, and .github/workflows/*.py in every plugin repo yield only UNOWNED or UNINDEXED_SOURCE_PATH, never an owned class.
title: Ownership for non-adapter sources: GLSL/Metal shaders, SQL migrations and workflow-embedded scripts report only UNOWNED/UNINDEXED

acceptanceCriteria: A spec records the provider contract and qualification plan for at least one of the three ecosystems, with the others listed as deferred and reasoned.
body: Found by the 2026-10-20 read-only Beamfall setup review (corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676; evidence under the session scratchpad beamfall-review/). Only Go and JS/TS have a live-test provider; Beamfall's Apple, Android and Windows repos have affected units and CEM runner profiles but nothing runs them live under Corvint.
title: Live-test providers for Swift (XCTest/Swift Testing), Gradle/JUnit and .NET (VSTest)

acceptanceCriteria: Every JS/TS test-source reader shares one test-file predicate that admits __tests__ path segments, or the spec records why a reader excludes them.
Tests cover a __tests__ file through lint and test-validity.
body: V1-2041 (PR #1307, TSA-V0-388) made test-validity count JS/TS files under a __tests__ path segment as test files without changing internal/testsource IsTestFile. Lint and the other readers that call IsTestFile still skip those files, so a Jest repository gets validity findings but no lint or other test-source analysis for its __tests__ files.
title: JS/TS lint and other test readers still use IsTestFile, so Jest __tests__ files are skipped outside test-validity

acceptanceCriteria: corvint-js-test-provider runs Jest with a retained run receipt that test-validity consumes for run outcome and freshness, or the spec records Jest as a deferred provider with reasons.
body: After V1-2041, Jest test validity is static only: measured strength, run outcome and freshness are NOT_APPLICABLE because no Jest run receipt exists (TSA-V0-390).
title: Jest run provider: corvint-js-test-provider runs only Vitest and Playwright, so Jest has no run-based validity axes

acceptanceCriteria: Frontiers other than dynamic import taint only the tests whose import closure reaches them, with tests.
Multi-binding declarations yield one changed symbol per bound name, with tests.
The spec records which further runners or plan profiles get narrowing, or why each is deferred; non-module runtime loading is either modelled for at least one class or stays a named frontier.
body: Residuals of V1-2042 (PR #1309, TJAA-V0-030..033; see the spec section 'Advisory fixture narrowing boundary (V1-2042)'). (1) Only playwright-affected/0 gets the advisory narrowed member; affected-plan/0 and other runners/languages get none. (2) Non-module runtime loading (bundler globs, HTML script tags, file reads, worker-shared state) is unmodelled, which is why narrowing stays advisory. (3) Any frontier other than a dynamic import refuses the whole narrowing (NOT_NARROWED GRAPH_FRONTIER) instead of tainting only the tests that reach it. (4) `export const a = 1, b = 2` is keyed by the first name only.
title: Advisory fixture narrowing: extend beyond playwright-affected/0, let non-dynamic frontiers taint only reaching tests, and key multi-binding exports per name

acceptanceCriteria: On at least one live Playwright repository, a recorded sample of fixture-module changes reports how many full-suite failures fall outside the narrowed set, with the commands and revisions retained in a build-log entry.
body: V1-2042 (PR #1309) adds an advisory narrowed test set under FULL_RELEVANT_SUITE but recall was NOT_RUN. Before narrowing can ever leave advisory status, its recall against the full suite's failures needs a measured sample.
title: Measure recall of the V1-2042 advisory narrowed set on a live Playwright repository

acceptanceCriteria: A user-prompt task longer than MaxQueryCharacters produces ranked context from a deterministic bounded query with a named degradation (or, if refusal is kept by spec decision, the refusal names the limit and the observed length), with tests.
The harness spec records the chosen behaviour and keeps oracle parity.
body: Found during Beamfall setup (beamfall/core-history#43, 2026-10-20). core-history's context-packet.sh passes the ticket body as the harness user-prompt task; for long tickets `corvint harness event` returns `invalid-harness-input: task exceeds the bounded query contract` (internal/gokernel/harness.go:256, MaxQueryCharacters=2000 / MaxTaskBytes=16384), so the packet falls back to rank_failed with no ranked context. Expected: an over-long prompt is bounded deterministically (e.g. leading MaxQueryCharacters runes, with a recorded truncation degradation) or the refusal names the limit and observed length so adapters can bound it themselves. Actual: hard refusal with no length detail; real prompts and ticket bodies routinely exceed 2,000 characters. Version: corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676.
title: harness event user-prompt refuses tasks over 2,000 characters instead of truncating or bounding the query, so long ticket text gets no ranked context

acceptanceCriteria: Assignment-position if/unless/case/begin/while/until (and modifier forms stay non-openers) are balanced correctly when indexing support files; the #1312 reproduction returns ELIGIBLE, with a regression test for each row of the issue table.

A support file that still cannot be parsed only abstains inclusions whose shared group could be defined there, and the abstention names that file; unrelated inclusions (group defined in the same spec file) still bind, with a test.
The test-source-analysis spec records the parse-failure isolation rule.
body: GitHub #1312, follow-up to #1308. On main da15cd7dd (1.0.0-rc.3), `corvint tests validity --files 'spec/a_spec.rb:9>same:3'` returns ABSTAINED rspec-shared-group-unbound whenever any file under spec/support/ contains an assignment-position block expression (`b = if … end`, `= case`, `= begin`, `= unless`), even though the shared group is defined in the same spec file. Plain `if` statements, or the same code in a non-support spec file, are ELIGIBLE. Likely the support-file block/end matcher does not count assignment-position keywords as openers, unbalancing the file, and one unparsed support file fails the whole support-group index.
title: RSpec inclusion selectors abstain repo-wide (rspec-shared-group-unbound) when any spec/support file assigns from if/unless/case/begin/while/until (GitHub #1312)

acceptanceCriteria: An owner decision records default-on or keep-opt-in; if default-on, parity fixtures, the divergence register and MTV-V0-005 are updated with tests.
body: PR #1313 (PUB-V0-027..030) adds an opt-in `--producer` member to impact/test-validity receipts. Default-on would change CCF-V1-006 parity bytes, the VSC envelope exactKeys and MTV-V0-005 CLI/MCP equality, so it needs an owner decision, a divergence-register entry and a parity note.
title: Decide whether receipts carry the producer member by default (V1-2043 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: Official release builds stamp the source commit; the producer member reports it, with a test, and PUB-V0-021 is amended.
body: PR #1313: release builds use -buildvcs=false, so the producer member reports commit "unknown" for official archives. A `-X main.commit` stamp needs a PUB-V0-021 amendment.
title: Release archives state the producer commit instead of unknown (V1-2043 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: MCP impact and test-validity can return the same producer member as the CLI, with a parity test.
body: PR #1313 adds the producer member to CLI receipts only; MCP equivalents do not offer it, breaking CLI/MCP parity for that member.
title: MCP impact/test-validity surfaces lack the producer member that the CLI has (V1-2043 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint impact --capabilities` prints the listing outside any Git root, with a test.
The shifted GPK citation is re-anchored to the intended code.
body: PR #1313 GPK-V0-084..086: the impact root check in parse() runs before --capabilities, so the listing fails outside a Git checkout. Also re-anchor the GPK spec citation that was mechanically shifted to cmd/corvint/main.go:463 (`if err != nil {`), likely semantically stale.
title: `corvint impact --capabilities` requires a Git root although it reads no repository (V1-2047 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A worktree whose only dirty paths are Tasks-store projection files reports source freshness clean plus a separate task-state member, in impact, context and hook packets, with tests.
The owning freshness specs record the rule.
body: PR #1314 (AFP-V0-088) projects .taskman/ files as nonSource task state in affected plans, but AC2 was NOT_PRODUCED: gokernel repositoryFromObservation (`mixed`) and internal/worktreeimpact (`mixed-worktree`) still treat projection-only dirt as source dirt, so every context and hook packet degrades in Tasks repositories (core-history, oscillux, Corvint).
title: Impact/context freshness reports Tasks-store (.taskman/) dirt separately instead of degrading to mixed-worktree (V1-2049 AC2 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A generic directory-fragment literal does not count as a reader of every concrete ticket file (or is narrowed with a declared read scope), so a ticket-only Corvint diff projects as nonSource, with a test.
body: PR #1314 measured Corvint 99dac5234: 13 .taskman/ paths all remain unknown because the generic `/tickets/` literal in internal/tasks/transaction is treated as a reader of every ticket file. That widens plans for ticket-only commits.
title: Corvint's own ticket-only diffs stay UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH because internal/tasks/transaction's generic /tickets/ literal matches every ticket file (V1-2049 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: A BOUNDED plan whose diff is entirely nonSource task state selects no Go tests in the fast tier, with a test; other empty-selection cases keep the full-suite fallback.
body: PR #1314: tools/gate-affected-select treats a BOUNDED plan with an empty selection over a non-empty diff (e.g. only .taskman/ task state) as needing the full suite.
title: Fast tier runs the full ./... suite for a BOUNDED plan with empty selection over a non-empty diff (V1-2049 residual)

acceptanceCriteria: When project instructions declare a verify command, affected and impact report it as the mandatory check (project authority outranks inferred commands), with tests for a Makefile-less npm repo.
Inferred commands that the instructions do not declare are labelled as inferred, not mandatory, with a test.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). In beamfall-docs (no Makefile, package.json build), `corvint affected` advises no mandatory check and `corvint impact AGENTS.md` falls back to `git diff --check`; expected `npm run build` from the AGENTS.md **Verify:** line or package.json. In beamfall-web and beamfall-design-system impact lists `npm test` beside `make gate` although AGENTS.md declares only `make gate`.
title: affected/impact ignore a repo's declared verify command: no Makefile -> no mandatory check, and npm test is added beside a declared make gate

acceptanceCriteria: Impact uncertainty for non-Go repositories names the relevant language or a neutral profile, with tests for at least Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript fixtures.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). `corvint impact AGENTS.md` in beamfall-apple, -android, -web and -docs reports reverse-import results as outside the native Go impact profile. The wording should name the actual language/profile (or be language-neutral). Related, narrower: V1-1814 (Ruby autoload).
title: impact uncertainty says 'outside the native Go impact profile' in Swift, Kotlin, TypeScript and docs-only repositories

acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether committed-range paths keep the dirty naming or get a distinct label; if renamed, the wire change follows the affected-plan compatibility rules, with tests.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). Suspected naming issue, not a confirmed bug: when the change is committed and the worktree is clean, `corvint affected --base <sha>` lists the committed paths under `plan.dirty` and reason `UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH`, which reads as working-tree dirt.
title: affected --base on a clean worktree labels committed range paths as plan.dirty / UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH

acceptanceCriteria: The instructions result summary for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md is the document title or declared purpose, independent of section order, with a test.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). After adding a '## Corvint context' section to AGENTS.md, `corvint impact AGENTS.md` summarised the instructions result as 'Before editing, read `corvint context ...`' rather than the document's title/purpose.
title: impact instructions result summary uses the first body line of a section instead of the document title or purpose

acceptanceCriteria: For an instruction-file-only change in a repo whose unbounded readers cannot reach it, affected selects no units or states the concrete read path per unit, with a fixture test.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout A (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). With only AGENTS.md dirty, `corvint affected --base <origin/main>` selected 9 units in each of beamfall-cloud and beamfall-relay, all witness UNBOUNDED_READER (e.g. internal/httpapi, internal/relay at 68s, plus shell tests). Expected: a Markdown instruction-file change selects nothing, or the plan names why each unit can read that file. Related: V1-0999, V1-0038 (inherited os.Getwd class in Corvint itself).
title: affected selects 9 units via UNBOUNDED_READER when only AGENTS.md changed (beamfall-cloud, beamfall-relay)

acceptanceCriteria: affected emits no Go-provider unknown for a repository without Go units, with a test.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout A (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). In oscillux (Rust) and beamfall-linux (C), affected lists `NO_ADVISORY_GO_COMMAND: provider.go.state is EMPTY_SELECTION` as an unknown. Expected: no Go-provider unknown when the repository has no Go units.
title: affected reports NO_ADVISORY_GO_COMMAND (provider.go.state EMPTY_SELECTION) as an unknown in repos with no Go units

acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether instruction files get a recognised affected ownership class; if yes, affected stops listing them as unknowns, with a test.
body: Found during the Beamfall Corvint setup rollout A (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). Every repo reported `UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH: AGENTS.md` as an unknown. Instruction files are a recognised authority class elsewhere (impact returns them as project-instructions); affected could classify them instead of reporting an unknown. Suspected gap, may be by design. Related: V1-2073.
title: affected reports UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md on every instruction-file change

acceptanceCriteria: Per decision 0547 (V1-2078 narrowing): `key: if`, `<< if` and line-start `else if` balance in the shared rubyOpens reader, with a table test per form, and the existing TSA-V0-396 cases still pass.

Ternary-branch openers, keywords inside regex literals and `x = if a.end?` are recorded as TSA-V0-396 reader limits; files with those forms stay unbalanced and block only the shared groups they could define (TSA-V0-397 abstention).
body: Residual from V1-2063 (PR #1315, TSA-V0-396/397). The reader does not count `key: if x`, `<< if x`, ternary-branch openers or line-start `else if x` (which opens a nested block), and counts keywords inside regex literals. Inferred from the regex, not observed: `x = if a.end?` is treated as closed on the same line. Such files stay unbalanced; since TSA-V0-397 they only block the shared groups they could define. Listed as non-goals of TSA-V0-396.
title: RSpec block reader still misses value openers: `key: if`, `<< if`, ternary branches, `else if`, keywords in regex literals, and `x = if a.end?`

acceptanceCriteria: TSA-V0-091 is amended (or cross-referenced) so its meaning matches TSA-V0-397, and the requirement checks pass.
body: Residual from V1-2063 (PR #1315, TSA-V0-396/397). TSA-V0-091's text was not amended when TSA-V0-397 narrowed abstention to the per-group case.
title: TSA-V0-091 says rspec-shared-group-unbound means the whole support set is unbound; since TSA-V0-397 it also covers one unread file that could define the group

acceptanceCriteria: impact's untracked-path refusal names the untracked path, labels the snapshot correctly (working-tree tree vs commit) and states the stage/commit next step, with a test.
body: Found during the Beamfall plugin AGENTS.md rollout (2026-10-20, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676). In a linked worktree of beamfall-plugin-sdk (HEAD 413817a), `corvint --root <wt> impact AGENTS.md` on a newly created, unstaged AGENTS.md returned rc 2 `impact paths are not tracked at revision d687e4d...`. d687e4d is a Git tree object (the worktree snapshot), not a commit, so the message reads as a wrong revision. Expected: the refusal names the path as untracked, identifies the snapshot as the working tree (or HEAD), and says to stage or commit; or impact gives an advisory result for an untracked path. Related: V1-0450 (OpenCode file-change refuses untracked paths).
title: impact on a new untracked file refuses with 'not tracked at revision <tree>' naming a worktree tree hash, not HEAD, and no next step

acceptanceCriteria: A recorded divergence decision, then a machine-readable closure-depth member in impact output or its capability listing, with parity manifest updated and tests.
body: Residual from V1-2044 (PR #1316, AFP-V0-094..096). One-hop depth and 'READY is not a closed test selection' are stated only in help and docs/CAPABILITIES.md because impact bytes are pinned by conformance/cli-parity-v0/manifest.json (CCF-V1-006). Expected: impact receipts or the `impact --capabilities` listing (V1-2047) state the closure depth machine-readably. Needs a divergence decision.

acceptanceCriteria: Each profile either plans a --path list with tests, or keeps a typed, documented refusal decided per profile.
body: Residual from V1-2044 (PR #1316, AFP-V0-094..096). `affected --path` combined with --provider, Playwright, --snapshot or --appmap-impact refuses with invalid-arguments (AFP-V0-094 non-goal). Expected: a listed path can be planned under those profiles.

acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction pins why the OCM linked none; the fix links added requirement IDs from the intent spec, with a test.
body: Residual from V1-2039/V1-2040 (PR #1317, TSA-V0-410..419). The PR #1317 dogfood-check SUMMARY reported `requirements=0 linked=0` though the INTENTS file named docs/specs/test-source-analysis-v0.md and the diff added TSA-V0-410..419. Other lanes (e.g. #1316) report requirements=3 linked=3. Expected: requirements added by the diff in the named spec are linked. Inputs: /private/tmp/cem10-build/erj2039/.
title: dogfood-check OCM links no requirements (requirements=0 linked=0) although the intents file names the governing spec with new TSA-V0 IDs

acceptanceCriteria: Ruby and JS provider receipts carry caller-asserted requirement IDs per selected example, marked caller-asserted and never inferred, with tests.
body: Residual from V1-2039/V1-2040 (PR #1317, TSA-V0-410..419). V1-2040's AC says the receipt echoes each ID beside the example outcome; the lane echoes them only in `corvint-example-join/0` to avoid conflicting with #1311 and V1-2045. Expected: provider receipts carry a caller-asserted requirements field. Follow-up once #1311 and V1-2045 land.
title: Ruby and JS provider receipts cannot carry caller-asserted requirement IDs directly

acceptanceCriteria: example-join maps absolute digest keys to repository-relative paths, and an ambiguous key gets a typed refusal, with tests.
body: Residual from V1-2039/V1-2040 (PR #1317, TSA-V0-410..419). JS receipts key TestFileDigests by absolute path, so a test file outside the repository root, or a digest key matching more than one anchor file, abstains `example-identity-unbound`. Expected: these still join, or a typed refusal names the cause.
title: JS example-join abstains example-identity-unbound when receipt TestFileDigests keys are absolute or ambiguous

acceptanceCriteria: A test with an ignored embedded or testdata file the graph reads makes `affected --path` refuse or report UNKNOWN; no plan is BOUNDED over it.
body: Residual from V1-2044 (PR #1316, AFP-V0-094) review fix. `corvint affected --path` refuses unsupported-affected-mixed-worktree when a listed path or a graph unit source/test is an ignored untracked file, but an ignored file the graph reaches through go:embed, testdata or declared read scopes is not compared, so the plan can still be BOUNDED while it depends on content absent from HEAD. Expected: refuse or widen to UNKNOWN for any ignored file the graph depends on.
title: affected --path ignored-file refusal checks unit sources and tests only, not embeds, testdata or read scopes

acceptanceCriteria: A new CEM profile version represents empty create/delete and mode-only changes with metadata identity and binding; cem/1.0 bytes and its refusal are unchanged; native and portable conformance pass.
body: Deferred from V1-0609 by decision 0546 §4. In 1.0 these diffs are refused with a typed code. After 1.0, define a versioned metadata identity and binding with explicit uncertainty in a new profile version, without changing the frozen cem/1.0 bytes.
title: Represent metadata-only diffs (empty create/delete, mode-only) in a post-1.0 CEM profile

acceptanceCriteria: A repository with more than 5000 support files makes `corvint tests example-join` refuse tests-bound-exceeded with the join's message; test added.
body: Residual from the V1-2039 review fix (PR #1317). The join lists support paths from the tree; above the 5000-entry listing budget it refuses with the older 'test files in all' message rather than the join's typed tests-bound-exceeded refusal. Expected: one typed refusal naming the join bound.
title: example-join over 5000 support files refuses with the tree-listing message instead of tests-bound-exceeded

acceptanceCriteria: Receipts from the Corvint Playwright reporter and RSpec formatter carry a titlePath array; a non-literal title yields a present titlePath in test-validity output, covered by a test.
body: Residual from V1-2045 (PR #1319, LPCV-V0-145..149). Test-validity locations take titlePath from committed source because receipts keep only joined names, so titlePath is absent for non-literal titles (internal/testvaliditydoc/location.go). Expected: the Corvint Playwright reporter and RSpec formatter record titlePath as an array in receipts, and the location projection prefers it.

acceptanceCriteria: A Vitest receipt whose test is declared in committed source yields a present location at the declaration line, or a typed absence only when discovery is ambiguous; covered by a test.
body: Residual from V1-2045 (PR #1319). For unprofiled runners and Vitest the receipt anchor is a failure frame, not the declaration, so location file/line is absent with reason anchor-not-declaration unless source discovery places it (internal/testvaliditydoc/location_discover_test.go). title: Unprofiled and Vitest test-validity anchors are failure frames, so the location is absent with anchor-not-declaration

acceptanceCriteria: A Playwright receipt with rootDir=e2e/ yields repo-relative location paths; a test covers both the bound and unbound cases.
body: Residual from V1-2045 (PR #1319). Stock Playwright reports spec file paths relative to its rootDir; locations are repo-relative only when rootDir is the repository root, otherwise absent with repository-root-unbound. acceptanceCriteria: The MCP bridge exposes the static preview with byte-identical output to the CLI and the same refusals, covered by a parity test; or the spec records MCP static as a non-goal.
body: Residual from V1-2045/2046 (PR #1319, LPCV-V0-150..153). `corvint test-validity --static` is CLI only; the MCP test-validity bridge cannot request the static preview (NOT_PRODUCED). Expected: an MCP parameter with identical bytes and the same option-combination refusals, or a recorded non-goal.
title: MCP test-validity bridge has no --static source-hygiene preview equivalent

acceptanceCriteria: step_facts accepted with the requires fact syntax and bounds; variations differing only in step_facts group into one compatible set and are not duplicates; a key in both requires and step_facts refuses test-plan-invalid-input; TCN spec amended with new requirement IDs; tests cover each rule.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1320. `corvint test-plan consolidate` (TCN-V0-002/007) has one precondition channel, `requires`. A precondition the step installs and removes itself (stubbed 429/5xx/network error, mocked clock, viewport) either splits every variant into its own compatible set (`conflicting-state`; 2 of 3 retry-error variants in a 44-row adopter matrix), is left undeclared, or is smuggled into `action` as a fake element ID. Expected (issue proposal): optional `step_facts` with `requires` syntax and bounds; never a requires conflict or precedence edge; same key in both is `test-plan-invalid-input`; part of the TCN-V0-005 duplicate key; plan output unchanged apart from input_digest. Related limit in the same issue: `--map` and `--tests` share one --root/--revision, so split app/e2e repositories cannot validate anchors and decide reuse in one plan (consider --tests-root/--tests-revision recorded in the header) - track separately if not taken here.
title: test-plan consolidate: declare step-local preconditions (step_facts) so per-step stubs do not split compatible sets

acceptanceCriteria: A Ruby/RSpec row under --mutate yields either per-mutant killed/survived verdicts with retained receipts, or a typed unsupported witness with a reason; never silent absence; covered by tests and the spec.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1321. `corvint prove --mutate` collects hunk spans only for `*.go`/`*.py`, requires `_test.go` mutation groups and dispatches Python on `.py`, so a row citing an RSpec example over a changed `.rb` file gets no mutation witness and callers cannot tell not-attempted from no-mutants. Behavior-falsification perturbs the environment, clones per attempt and keeps no receipts for `survived`, so it is not a substitute. Expected: either hunk-confined .rb mutants run through a declared runner (pinned container command) with killed/survived per mutant and a retained receipt per run, or an explicit `unsupported` mutation witness with a reason for Ruby rows.
title: prove --mutate: Ruby/RSpec rows get no mutation witness; add line-level .rb mutation or an explicit unsupported witness

acceptanceCriteria: --help (global and per subcommand) prints usage and exits 0 without a pin; read-only listing verbs need no pin; the refusal names the missing flags --executable and --executable-sha256; tests cover each.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1327. `corvint-test-runner --help` and `profiles` print `runner refused: independent executable identity required` and exit 1; every subcommand except `runners` requires --executable and --executable-sha256, including help.
title: corvint-test-runner --help and read-only verbs refuse without an executable pin

acceptanceCriteria: An unadmitted receipt carries an opaque profile label or explicit not-admitted state that cannot be mistaken for a runner receipt; spec amended with requirement IDs; tests cover admitted vs opaque.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1328. assemble-stable (cem-stable-plain-assembly/1, no runnerAdmission) accepts any file as runner plan/receipt by SHA-256 only, and labels the emitted receipt record corvint-test-runner-receipt/0 with CALLER_OBSERVED, so an unadmitted file reads as a runner receipt.
title: assemble-stable labels an unadmitted opaque receipt as corvint-test-runner-receipt/0

acceptanceCriteria: status/verify accept a map path outside the repository (or help documents the layout); out-of-tree anchor/verdict-ledger mode delivered or explicitly deferred to a follow-up ticket with the limit recorded; spec amended; tests.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1329. assemble-stable requires its output outside the repository, while cem status/verify --map refuse absolute paths (map path must be repository-relative) and help does not say so; anchor --artifacts and the verdict ledger only work for committed maps.
title: cem status/verify refuse out-of-repository maps that assemble-stable must write outside the repository

acceptanceCriteria: Every hunk the falsifier did not attempt is listed with a closed not-run reason (unsupported language, test-only hunk, ...); spec amended with requirement IDs; tests cover Go and non-Go hunks.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1330. On a map whose only hunk is a Ruby spec file, cem verify --hunk-revert returns hunks: [] only; the falsifier re-executes go test only for non-test Go hunks.
title: cem verify --hunk-revert returns empty hunks for non-Go hunks with no not-run reason

acceptanceCriteria: The cite refusal states the rule (cited base span must survive the change) and, if cheap, nearest stable spans; the prepare refusal names a fix (git repack -a -d and remove objects/info/alternates, or clone without --shared); tests pin the messages.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1331. cem cite --lines on removed lines refuses cite-span-not-stable with no hint of citable spans; cem prepare in a --shared clone refuses unsupported-object-alternates with no suggested fix.
title: cem refusals cite-span-not-stable and unsupported-object-alternates give no fix

acceptanceCriteria: A criterion form binding an external document by repository identity, object ID and span digest (or content digest plus declared locator), verified when that repository is supplied and reported NOT_OBSERVED otherwise; CEM spec amended with requirement IDs; tests.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1332. The plain criterion form requires criterionSha256 to equal the digest of an evidence span in the same repository at base, so requirements kept in a separate repository cannot be bound without copying.
title: cem plain criterion cannot bind a requirement kept in another repository

acceptanceCriteria: Either receipt admission for the Ruby provider document (exec prefix and inclusion lines bound) or --exec-prefix plus path mapping in the runner rspec profile, so a containerised RSpec run yields an admitted receipt identifying each shared-example inclusion; spec amended; tests.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1333. runnerAdmission corvint-test-runner/0 only admits corvint-test-runner documents; its rspec profile cannot run in a container without a path-preserving wrapper; corvint-ruby-test-provider supports --exec-prefix and shared-example inclusion lines but its document is not admitted.
title: No path from the Ruby test provider report to CEM runner receipt admission

acceptanceCriteria: cem <action> --help prints per-action help; corvint-cem-candidate assemble-stable output carries the same top-level ok envelope as cem actions (additive); cem cite on a stable map refuses with a distinct not-a-producer-map code instead of unsupported-spec; spec amended with requirement IDs; tests cover each.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1335. cem <action> --help prints the whole multi-action usage; assemble-stable output lacks the top-level ok member the cem subcommands have; cem cite on an assembled cem/1.0 stable map refuses unsupported-spec although the real cause is that the input is not a producer map.
title: cem: per-action help, one result envelope with ok, and not-a-producer-map refusal for cite

acceptanceCriteria: TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun passes deterministically under host load (run with -count=20 under heavy.sh and with GOMAXPROCS=2 stress); the fix addresses the real race rather than widening a timeout; a scheduled release-gates run passes or the remaining failures are filed.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1116. Scheduled release-gates full-gate on macos-15 at f3ca72248 (run 39416257984) failed only in internal/tasks/cli: TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun returned code 2 Outcome ERROR Codes [SURVIVORS] instead of 128+15 REFUSED with the child killed by group SIGKILL. Same symptom as archived V1-0768 (merged into umbrella V1-0849). Version: origin/main f3ca72248. Expected: SIGTERM to the runner stops the group and reports RunInterrupted. Actual: SURVIVORS under hosted-runner load.
title: Nightly release-gates: TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun reports SURVIVORS on hosted macos-15 (#1116)

acceptanceCriteria: For a cited example, test-validity flags or refuses with a closed code when an asserted value is fully determined by a stub declared in the same example/group on a method reached by the code under test, or when a message-chain stub is asserted only on a prefix; the hint names the stub and the assertion; RSpec fixtures for both patterns plus a negative control; spec amended.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1339. Test-validity reports a cited example ELIGIBLE when a stub on the asserted path decides the outcome: (1) stubbed mutating operation plus a 'state unchanged' assertion; (2) receive_message_chain stub with only a prefix of the chain asserted. Blind review caught both; the tool did not.
title: Test validity: flag assertions made unfalsifiable by a stub on the asserted path

acceptanceCriteria: The assemble-stable result's nextActions name the verify command (cem verify / verify-stable) and the artifact location for the map it produced; test asserts the emitted next action runs and returns ACCEPT on the fixture.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1329 comment (2026-10-20 15:54). After plain assembly there is no supported verify route named: cem prepare nextActions point --artifacts at the repository root and assume a committed producer map; verifying required copying the assembled map into a scratch clone. Related to V1-2097 (PR #1337 makes status/verify accept out-of-repository maps).
title: assemble-stable result names no verify route for the map it produced

acceptanceCriteria: The external map read and externalReportOutput open through a directory handle (os.Root or openat chain) so a swapped parent cannot redirect the read/write; a test swaps a parent directory between check and open and gets a typed refusal.
body: Codex finding (High) on PR beamfall/corvint#1337 (V1-2097): the containment check for the out-of-repository map path and externalReportOutput is pathname-based (publish.OpenRoot keeps a pathname), so a parent-directory swap between check and ReadBounded escapes containment (TOCTOU).
title: cem status/verify external map read: descriptor-bound containment (os.Root/openat)

acceptanceCriteria: RESULT.schema.json (stable and repository-envelope copies) accepts opaque/0 and corvint-test-runner-receipt/0; the sealed chain is re-bound through a recorded regeneration path; a verify result for an unadmitted fixture map validates against the schema.
body: Codex P2 finding on PR beamfall/corvint#1338 (V1-2096, CEM-V1-310..313): stable and sealed repository-envelope RESULT.schema.json copies require references.runnerReceipts[].profile = corvint-test-runner-receipt/0, so the verify result for a new unadmitted map (opaque/0) fails that schema although the verdict is ACCEPT. Fixing needs re-binding the sealed CEM-V1-091 chain; cem-stable-regen has no enum-widening mode.
title: RESULT.schema.json still requires the old runner receipt label for unadmitted maps

acceptanceCriteria: Stubs on a configurable list of flag/config lookup constants/methods are classified separately from collaborator stubs; the validity result carries a 'conditional on flag KEY=VALUE' qualifier with the forced value and, when discoverable, the code default; a warning when forced differs from default; downstream evidence records the condition instead of an unqualified pass; RSpec fixtures plus negative control; spec amended.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1340. A cited example that forces a feature flag through a stub (allow(FlagClient).to receive(:enabled?).with(:rule).and_return(true)) proves behaviour only while the flag is on; test-validity treats it as an ordinary collaborator stub, so a rule disabled by default can be cited as unconditionally proven. Pairs with V1-2104 (#1339) in the stub-classification area.
title: Test validity: surface feature-flag stubs as a condition on the proven behaviour

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint help cem ACTION` and `--help` on verify-stable and gate-verdict print that action's usage only and exit 0; tests cover each.
body: Residual from GitHub beamfall/corvint#1335 (PR #1342, V1-2102, CEM-V1-340): `cem ACTION --help` now prints only that action, but `corvint help cem ACTION`, `cem verify-stable --help` and `cem gate-verdict --help` still lack per-action help. Also the cite-span-not-stable guidance names only the nearest unedited span above and below.
title: cem per-action help is missing for `corvint help cem ACTION`, verify-stable and gate-verdict

acceptanceCriteria: cem prepare (and Tasks criterion export) can emit the external form from a declared external repository; cem status and the console accept --external-repository and report the criterion as verified, rejected or not observed; any result-format change goes through a recorded re-emission; tests and spec.
body: Residual from GitHub beamfall/corvint#1332 (PR #1343, V1-2100, CEM-V1-330..337). The external criterion form is verified only by `cem verify --external-repository NAME=/abs/path`. Gaps: cem prepare and Tasks cannot emit it; cem status and the console take no external repositories; there is no per-criterion NOT_OBSERVED result field (deferred because it changes the frozen result format and needs a CEM-V1-091 re-emission); RESULT.schema criterionBinding covers only the Tasks form.
title: External criterion form: no producer emits it and core read paths take no external repositories

acceptanceCriteria: Each other groupreap Owner caller either opts into RepeatKillWhileLive with a spec amendment, or its spec records why a single signal suffices; a fake-host test per opted-in caller fails with the repeat disabled.
body: Found by the #1116 lane (V1-2103, PR #1344). On Darwin a single process-group SIGKILL can miss a process forked at that moment (3 of 300 stops in a local probe). #1344 adds opt-in groupreap.Primitives.RepeatKillWhileLive for the attempt runner only (ATR-V0-153). The other Owner callers (dispatch reader, CEM Git runner, dogfood aggregate worker, Linux service descendants probe) still send one signal as their specs require, so they can leave a survivor and HOLD or report SURVIVORS. Suspected, not reproduced in those callers.
title: Other groupreap Owner callers send one group SIGKILL and can miss a member forked at the same moment

acceptanceCriteria: internal/testacceptance freshness reads its admitted runner versions from the shared tuple table; acceptance on 1.64.0/v22.23.2 is admitted; the reporter Node pre-filter derives from the table; tests fail on the old literals.
body: Found by the #1270 lane (V1-2009, PR #1345). PWP-V0-050..052 moved the freshness tuple to the shared Go table and added 1.64.0 on Node v22.23.2, but internal/testacceptance/freshness.go:21 still hardcodes runner 1.63.0, so acceptance on 1.64.0 still refuses. The reporter's external Node pre-filter (v22.23.2, v24.11.1) is a fixed list rather than read from the table. Expected: both derive from the shared tuple table.
title: internal/testacceptance freshness still hardcodes Playwright 1.63.0 and the reporter keeps a fixed Node pre-filter

acceptanceCriteria: A merge_group run whose tree equals a passed PR run reuses or skips artifact-integrity, with a retained reuse record naming the PR run and tree.
A tree mismatch or missing record fails closed to the full artifact-integrity job.
Measured queue wall time before and after is retained in a build-log entry.
body: Observed 2026-10-20: merge_group run 39458994189 took 11.4 min. The go-product shards reused the PR results through REUSE and finished in about 30 s, but artifact-integrity ran from scratch for 11.3 min (PR run 39472511845: 12.6 min). That makes it the whole queue critical path. A batch therefore costs about 30 min of PR CI plus 11 min of queue time, and each failed test adds another full 30 min PR cycle. Expected: artifact-integrity in merge_group reuses the PR run result when the merged tree equals the PR-tested tree (the same corvint-ci-reuse/0 binding the shards use), or it runs only when its inputs changed (see V1-1099 job-level predicates). Related: V1-1642 covers the same rerun on the main push. Also open: PR shards still run the full suite because affected narrowing awaits the owner-dispatched AFP-V0-014 qualification campaign and AFP-V0-028/029 shadow admission.
title: Merge queue reruns artifact-integrity (~11 min) on the tree its PR run already passed; it is the queue critical path

acceptanceCriteria: A fixture spec asserting a never-written plain accessor yields the new finding with the asserted reader and exercised method named.
A fixture where the exercised path writes the accessor (direct, self.x=, or via attribute assignment) yields no finding.
A reader that is a DB column, overridden method, or unresolved definition yields uncertainty, not a finding.
Spec requirements in docs/specs/test-source-analysis-v0.md trace to the tests.
body: GitHub #1339 comment (2026-10-20): a third vacuous pattern seen in practice. A spec asserts a plain attr_accessor (e.g. `expect(obj.flag).to be_nil`/`eq(false)`) that the code under test never writes, while the real state lives in a sibling predicate (`flag?`) or another member. The assertion passes regardless of behavior. Not covered by PR #1348 (TSA-V0-430..442: stub-decides-assertion, message-chain prefix, flag-conditional). Expected: test-source analysis reports a closed finding (e.g. RB-ASSERT-TARGET-NEVER-WRITTEN, 'assertion target is never written on the exercised path') when the asserted reader resolves to a plain attr_accessor/attr_reader (no DB column, no override) with no writer reachable from the exercised method in the analysed source, strengthened when a sibling predicate with the same stem exists; unresolvable cases stay uncertain, not findings.
title: RSpec vacuous assertion: asserted reader is a plain accessor the exercised path never writes (#1339 third pattern)

acceptanceCriteria: Naming an unchanged .rb source and 2-3 spec examples returns test-kills-mutant rows with per-mutant verdict (killed/survived/error) and receipt.
Mutants are bounded by the existing caps and confined to the named spans or the executed lines when given.
Spec requirements trace to tests; exported revision never written.
body: GitHub #1354: RSpec mutation runs only in change mode on changed lines, so new or strengthened specs for an UNCHANGED source file get no test-kills-mutant rows (path mode gives history-consistent only). Request: a selector naming a source file, optional line spans, and the examples (file:line, #1271 selection) to judge; keep 12-mutant cap, row/invocation deadlines and per-mutant receipts; optionally restrict mutants to lines the cited examples execute or a caller span so unrelated survivors are not reported as test weakness.
title: prove --mutate: name an unchanged source file (and optional line spans) to mutate against cited RSpec examples (GH #1354 part 1)

acceptanceCriteria: With the containerised RSpec provider declared, a services-dependent suite reaches PASS/FAIL baseline and mutant verdicts instead of UNSUPPORTED.
Each mutant applies in a disposable copy and carries its own admitted container receipt.
Spec requirements trace to tests; host-sandbox path unchanged when no profile is declared.
body: GitHub #1354: mutated RSpec runs only under host sandbox-exec/bwrap with network denied, so suites needing DB/cache services or container-only gems never pass baseline and every row is NOT_RUN/UNSUPPORTED. #1333/PR 1341 added admitted receipts for containerised RSpec runs. Request: mutation rows execute via that container runner path (or any declared runner profile), keeping: exported revision never written, each mutant in a disposable copy, per-run receipt.
title: prove --mutate: run RSpec mutants through the declared containerised runner profile, not only the host sandbox (GH #1354 part 2)

acceptanceCriteria: test-read-scopes-check reports a declared package whose test builds a tracked repository path from filepath.Join string segments (for example "protocol", "cem-1.0", "stable", "neutral-criterion") outside its declared scope
Proven on the cmd/corvint-cem-candidate next_action_test.go shape at d114cc62e, which the check passed
Existing literal-path detection is unchanged
body: Batch PR #1357 (CI run 39496979738, go-product-shard 7): TestCEMV1350PlainAssemblyNextActionVerifiesBundle failed with 'open .../protocol/cem-1.0/stable/neutral-criterion/repository.recipe.json: permission denied'. The test (V1-2105, commit d114cc62e) builds the path with filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(file), "..", "..", "protocol", "cem-1.0", "stable", "neutral-criterion"), and cmd/corvint-cem-candidate declared no read scopes. 'go run ./tools/test-read-scopes-check' printed ok at that commit because it only matches whole path string literals (AFP-V0-023). Fixed for this case in eb36f78f3 by declaring the directory. Expected: the check joins adjacent string-literal arguments of filepath.Join/path.Join (or otherwise resolves runtime.Caller-relative joins) and flags the out-of-scope tracked path. Actual: the check passes and CI fails with a content-looking permission error.
title: test-read-scopes-check misses tracked paths built from filepath.Join string segments

acceptanceCriteria: A lane on a host whose Homebrew Go moved past the pinned patch can still run make go-version-gated targets (windows-vet, gate steps) against the pinned go1.27.2 without manual toolchain work, or gets one refusal naming the exact install command

Makefile go-version requires GOTOOLCHAIN=local go env GOVERSION = go1.27.2, so every local target that depends on it (make windows-vet, build, gate steps) now fails on this host. acceptanceCriteria: A claim, widen or closeout whose diff touches docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv, docs/specs/INDEX.json or docs/specs/README.md does not refuse RESOURCE_COLLISION solely because another live attempt also lists those generated files
The rule is declared once (policy or reservation class), not per lane, and a regression test reproduces the V1-1639 vs V1-0812 collision
Hand-authored paths keep exclusive collision semantics
body: Observed 2026-10-20, corvint-tasks local build. Every spec change regenerates docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv, INDEX.json and README.md (make spec-requirements), so every spec-touching ticket's closeout widen/submit must include them. Tasks treats them as exclusive PATH resources. V1-1639's cem-verdict closeout (widen to base..seal paths) refused RESOURCE_COLLISION because the parked V1-0812 attempt (waiting on an owner CI post) listed the same three generated files; the closeout script then released and the attempt was CANCELLED. Workaround: release V1-0812 and re-claim without the generated files, re-claim V1-1639. Expected: derived files that are regenerated at merge (V1-1525 already makes them merge-regenerated) are shared or exempt reservation resources. Actual: exclusive, blocking unrelated closeouts for as long as any spec lane is parked.
title: Tasks reservations treat generated spec index files as exclusive, so any parked spec lane blocks every other spec ticket's closeout

acceptanceCriteria: A test injects an uncoded filesystem error and an uncoded receipt refusal into finish and observes the emitted code

acceptanceCriteria: A status-only denial example on a mutating request yields an advisory code (e.g. RB-DENIAL-WITHOUT-NO-EFFECT) citing the example line and the mutating call; it is advisory only and never makes the example INELIGIBLE.
The same example with a no-effect assertion (change/count matcher, reload comparison, or not_to have_received on an outbound client) is not flagged; non-mutating denials (GET/HEAD) are not flagged.
Unresolvable request verbs or custom matchers abstain with a named reason instead of flagging; fixture tests pin each case.
Requirement recorded in test-source-analysis-v0.md with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; Closes #1366.
body: GitHub #1366. A denial example (401/403/forbidden/unauthorized status or a framework forbidden matcher such as render_forbidden / have_http_status(:forbidden)) whose action is a mutating request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, or a create/update/destroy entry point) and which has no assertion on persisted state or outbound calls (change/count matcher, reload comparison, not_to have_received on a client) proves refusal but not no-effect. Real case: authorize! :create, build_and_save_record wrote a row before denying; the status-only example stayed green, and adding expect { request }.not_to change(Model, :count) failed 0->1. Requested: an advisory code (e.g. DENIAL-WITHOUT-NO-EFFECT) citing the example line and the mutating call.
title: GH #1366: test-validity (RSpec): flag denial examples that assert only the refusal status on a mutating request

acceptanceCriteria: A regression test runs affected with base == HEAD on a clean checkout of a multi-language fixture and pins a BOUNDED empty plan with no language-frontier unknowns and no mandatory full-suite advice.

body: Observed 2026-10-20 by two pre-1.0 bug lanes (bugs-affected-cmd, bugs-testsource) at lane start: `corvint affected --base 2b0cfce94` in a clean worktree whose HEAD equals the base (empty diff) returned scope UNKNOWN, listing ~23 LANGUAGE_FRONTIER entries (cfamily, dotnet, python, ruby, swift, typescript) plus NO_ADVISORY_GO_COMMAND, and advice that still lists `make gate`/the full test run. An empty diff has no changed path, so no frontier can be reached; the expected plan is a BOUNDED empty selection with no unknowns (or a single explicit EMPTY_DIFF note). Related but distinct: V1-0567 (dogfood empty range), V1-2070 (fast tier on BOUNDED empty selection over a non-empty diff).

acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce in a test: context on a clean checkout reports revision == HEAD commit SHA.

body: Observed 2026-10-20 by the bugs-testsource lane: `corvint context` in a clean lane worktree at commit 2b0cfce94 reported `"revision": "e5bbe7757…"`, a tree hash, rather than the commit. Related: V1-2080 (impact names a worktree tree hash in a refusal). Expected: `revision` is the HEAD commit when the worktree is clean; a dirty/mixed worktree reports the commit plus an explicit worktree-tree field rather than substituting the tree hash.
