acceptanceCriteria: query.go and batch_input.go refuse, with the per-path git-output-exceeded message, a path whose parent tree exceeds MaxTreeBytes, covered by a git mktree fixture test
batched and per-path outputs are byte-equal for that fixture
body:
Residual from the V1-1991 Codex round (bugs-residuals lane, PR 1386, 2026-10-21). The batched symbol-anchor and CEM projection reads now use gitauth.ResolvePathLookups and admit a path only when its per-path LookupTreeEntry cost is within MaxTreeBytes. The earlier V1-1984 ResolvePaths consumers in internal/doccorpus/query.go and batch_input.go still check only the 32 MiB aggregate bound, so a path under a parent tree larger than MaxTreeBytes (for example about 4.25 MiB, built with git mktree) can be answered where the per-path lookup refuses with git-output-exceeded.
Expected: every ResolvePaths consumer keeps per-path admission parity, or the spec records why aggregate admission is sufficient there.
title: doccorpus query and batch input admit ResolvePaths results with only the 32 MiB aggregate bound, not the per-path tree bound

acceptanceCriteria: script/check-line-citations.sh --relocate (or a make target) rewrites citations whose anchored content moved, without changing the hashes, and lists the ones it cannot place
it hashes in process, not with one subprocess per candidate offset; 21 citations finish in under 5 s
--hash on a path that is conflicted or missing from stage 0 exits non-zero with a message naming the unmerged index entry
line-citations-test covers a shifted range, an ambiguous duplicate match and an unstaged conflicted path
body:
Observed 2026-10-21 while merging nine lanes into batch-1021b, and reported by the hosts-mcp-panel lane. Every merge that moves lines in a cited Go file (internal/contextindex/index.go, cmd/corvint/harness.go, help.go) leaves line citations `path:a-b@hash` whose anchor hash is unchanged but whose line numbers are stale. Lanes rerun line-citations-check several times and repin by hand. The orchestrator wrote a scratch relocate script twice (scan +/-60 lines per citation, calling script/check-line-citations.sh --hash once per offset), which took over 3 minutes for 21 citations. It also falsely reported every citation unmatched while the cited file was unstaged in a conflicted merge, because --hash reads the git index (stage 0) and fails on a conflicted path without saying so.
Expected: one command repins every citation whose hash appears at another position in the cited file, in process, and leaves genuinely changed ones for review.
title: line-citations-check: add a --relocate mode that repins shifted citations by hash match

acceptanceCriteria: The literal mask recognises /.../, %r{...} and %r(...) regex literals in an operand position, and does not treat a quote inside them as opening a string
Fixture: `x =~ /'/` followed by `Foo::Bar.call` still extracts Foo::Bar; division `a / b` is unaffected
The RUBY-AFFECTED-V0-043 limit is removed or narrowed, with a test traced to it
body: The Ruby affected scanner masks string literals before it extracts constants. It does not recognise regex literals, so a quote inside one, such as `x =~ /'/`, opens a string that runs to the next quote. Constants referenced inside that span are hidden, which can drop a dependency edge and under-select tests. This is recorded as a limit in RUBY-AFFECTED-V0-043 (batch-affected-appmap-ruby, #1395). It needs the regex-vs-division ambiguity handled the way Ruby's lexer does: after an operator or keyword, `/` starts a regex.
title: Ruby affected literal mask: a quote inside a regex literal (/'/) opens a string and hides later constants

acceptanceCriteria: Measured before/after wall time for closing N merged full-gate tickets (N>=5) retained in a build-log entry.
Reuse is refused when the seal is not an ancestor of the PASS commit or the PASS was not on the declared protected ref; receipt audit verifies ancestry; focused tests cover accept and both refusals.
Spec requirement (CAL-V0 amendment of CAL-V0-240) recorded.
body: Observed 2026-10-21 during the delivered-but-open sweep: 110 verified tickets across 100 distinct seal trees; 18 require full-gate. CAL-V0-240 reuse only matches the identical tree, so each close runs `make gate` (tens of minutes; one started 06:16 at host load 38-62 was still running 8+ minutes later) even though every seal is an ancestor of origin/main whose own merge already passed the full merge-queue gate. Proposal: an operator-declared reuse rule letting a recorded full-gate PASS at a tree whose commit descends from the seal (on the protected branch, via the merge queue) qualify, with reusedFrom naming that commit and receipt audit verifying ancestry; or a batch close that runs the gate once at the tip for a set of merged seals.
title: Tasks: closing already-merged delivered tickets reruns a full `make gate` per seal tree; let a qualifying full-gate PASS at a descendant main tree cover merged seals

acceptanceCriteria: A policy-enabled gate can be satisfied by a recorded green CI run (run id, head sha, conclusion) on a protected intent-branch commit that descends from the attempt candidate, without local execution, and complete accepts it.
Receipt audit verifies the recorded CI source (ancestry from git; run facts as recorded claims) and fails a rewound branch; rollback is a policy flag.
Measured: closing N merged-and-CI-green tickets takes no local make gate runs.
body: Observed 2026-10-21 (build 699): 91 delivered tickets queued for closeout ran close-delivered.sh serially; each required full-gate executed `make gate` locally (1-2 h at load 50-200). After ~80 min only 3 of 91 had completed. Every ticket was already on main via a batch PR whose merge_group/push CI run was green. Owner directed that CI-checked work needs no local gate, so 86 were closed with ticket complete-manual citing a sha256 of a JSON evidence file (lane PR, batch PR, main commit, green CI run URLs); evidence retained in .git/ci-evidence-2026-10-21. complete-manual loses the gate binding and needs per-ticket evidence plumbing. V1-2193 descendant reuse helps only after one local full-gate PASS at a main descendant. Expected: a typed, policy-allowed gate source that records a full-gate PASS from a verified green CI run on a protected-branch commit descending from the candidate (run id, head sha, conclusion), audited like descendant reuse. Actual: COMMAND gates only record local execution or same-tree/descendant local reuse.
title: Gates cannot accept a green merged CI run as evidence: delivered tickets pay a local full-gate each or fall back to complete-manual

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatch-time check (corvint-tasks or a corvint command) reports, for each candidate ticket, whether an open PR, a merged PR or an origin/main commit already references it as delivered

body: Observed 2026-10-21 in orchestrated 1.0 sweep lanes. proc-1021c delivered 1 of 7 assigned tickets, scopes-1021c 1 of 8, and lanes built 3 duplicates of work already in open PRs (affected-1021d rebuilt V1-2053, already in #1421, then reverted it). Causes: (1) dispatch takes no Tasks claim, so nothing shows a ticket is in flight; (2) tickets stay OPEN after their PR merges (see closeout-lag ticket); (3) PR bodies use 'Refs V1-X' for tickets the lane did not deliver, so a text search cannot tell delivered from mentioned. Interim mitigation: a scratch screen script that checks open/merged PR bodies and origin/main commits for strong refs, and a charter rule that 'Refs' is used only for delivered tickets. Version: corvint-tasks local build from origin/main (2026-10-21).
title: Lane dispatch assigns tickets already delivered or in flight in another open PR (~40% of 1021c/d lane tickets wasted)

acceptanceCriteria: corvint affected (or a documented lane recipe) yields a bounded local subset: changed packages, siblings and direct importers, with the cap and exclusions explicit

Interim mitigation: charter 1021e adds affected-selected siblings and direct importers (cap 15, skip cmd/corvint unless directly changed), and the integrator charter adds a preflight list.
title: Lanes skip tests of sibling packages and direct importers, so batch CI finds deterministic failures (11 of ~24 batches needed 2+ 31-minute runs)

acceptanceCriteria: Batch-integrator procedure (skill or docs) requires one push after all merges and one push per CI failure round

Counted 12 cancelled batch-PR runs on 2026-10-21, about 250 runner-minutes, on a host limited to about 2 concurrent CI runs. Interim mitigation: integrator charter 1021e requires merging all constituents and fixing preflight failures before a single push, and fixing all CI failures in one commit.
title: Incremental pushes to batch PRs cancel in-flight CI: 12 cancelled runs, about 250 runner-minutes wasted on 2026-10-21

title: corvint affected selects 135 packages for a one-package change; emit a tiered direct-dependents subset usable locally

acceptanceCriteria: Profiles before and after on the Corvint repo at recorded host load
Index build wall time is reduced by >=20% with byte-identical snapshot content, or the floor is documented with a profile

body: Lane index-perf-1021i (PR #1458, V1-2239) profiled index build. The os.Root openat walk takes 22% of CPU, GC about 30%, tokenise 13% and goSymbols 8.5%. The gob decode format is itself a floor for snapshot load, even after the mmap path (IDX-SNAP-V0-105). The 10.9 s build figure in V1-2239 did not reproduce. Candidates: a prefix-held directory fd walk, as in journal S6 (open each directory once, then openat the leaf); arena or slab allocation for tokens to cut GC; GOGC tuning for the one-shot build; and a non-gob snapshot encoding behind the format gate (invariant 7).
title: index build: os.Root per-component openat walk (22%) and GC (~30%) dominate index-build CPU

They need per-call (context-carried) budget and prefetch hooks before t.Parallel is safe.
title: doccorpus: DCP-V1-216 bulk equivalence tests dominate package time (217 s, 111 s, 103 s) and cannot run in parallel

acceptanceCriteria: A perf-only contextindex change with byte-identical golden index output does not require a schema version bump

body: Lane idxbuild-1021k (V1-2285) changed only build performance in internal/contextindex; built index content sha256 a5a31c34... identical before and after. TestAnalyzerSchemaInputs / script/analyzer-schema.sh still require a schema bump because every non-test .go file is an analyzer input. Parallel lanes then collide on the schema number (#1445 /137, #1458 /138, #1460 /139, V1-2285 next) and each bump invalidates cached indexes needlessly. acceptanceCriteria: A test kills the producer group mid-git-read and asserts no git child outlives it (or Close waits for them)

acceptanceCriteria: A commit that only mentions an ID in prose yields CITED, not DELIVERED; a closing trailer or a ticket-scoped subject yields DELIVERED.

body: Observed 2026-10-21 (corvint-tasks local build). `ticket delivery-screen <170 ids> --ref origin/main --limit 10000` scanned 8717 commits and reported 154 DELIVERED. That count includes MANUAL/EXTERNAL release tickets such as V1-0019 and V1-0014, whose IDs only appear in commit messages as mentions, and 72 tickets that a single commit merely cites. Without --limit the default 1000-commit scan reported NOT_OBSERVED for tickets cited in older commits, and --limit above 10000 is refused as MALFORMED. Expected: tell a citation that delivers the ticket (a Fixes/Refs trailer or a ticket-scoped subject) apart from a mention, and report CITED rather than DELIVERED for a bare mention; by default, scan back to the store's creation commit, or report the truncation per ticket.
title: ticket delivery-screen counts any commit mention as DELIVERED and truncates at 1000 commits by default

acceptanceCriteria: The issue's static repro selects both specs, or reports a non-BOUNDED scope with a named unknown and no proven exclusion of the second spec.
A three-hop autoload chain is selected or reported as an unknown beyond a documented hop bound.
A namespaced constant and a custom inflection resolve the same way impact resolves them.
A spec referencing no constant that reaches the dirty file is still excluded with NO_DEPENDENCY_PATH_TO_DIRTY_UNIT.
--path, --base and --snapshot modes select the same as worktree mode for the same change.

body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1475 (filed 2026-10-21). impact reports Ruby autoload-convention reverse references, but affected ignores them: a spec that reaches a changed class only through an autoloaded constant is excluded with NO_DEPENDENCY_PATH_TO_DIRTY_UNIT while plan.scope stays BOUNDED and unknown is empty. For Rails-style apps this under-selects silently. impact's dynamic-dispatch-unresolved unknown is also not carried into affected. Preferred fix: use the same autoload roots, inflections and ignore list as impact's ruby_autoload as transitive dependency edges; fallback: non-BOUNDED scope with RUBY_AUTOLOAD_REFERENCES_NOT_IN_GRAPH.
title: GH #1475: affected excludes Ruby specs reached through autoloaded constants while scope stays BOUNDED (fail-open)

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture: primary + 2 additional repositories, >= 8,000 pinned inputs. Second and later calls report `freshness: reused` and freshness_ms < 100 ms while no checkout changes.
Changing one file in one additional repository makes the next call recompute (stale, naming that repository) and later calls reuse again.
Warm p95 < 1 s for `docs_get`/`docs_search` on that fixture.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1487

## Summary
With `additional_repositories` declared in a `corvint-corpus-input/2` manifest, every `corvint-corpus-mcp` tool call recomputes live freshness for all repositories and never reuses it. On a ~100k-record corpus warm calls take ~10 s (freshness ~10 s, query ~70 ms), against ~1.1 s for the same corpus shape anchored in one repository on the previous build. The first call of a session takes ~30 s.

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d (macOS arm64).
- Corpus: adoption-provider shards, 9,068 pinned inputs: primary repository (shards and one case export) plus 4 additional repositories with 7,312 / 1,659 / 84 / 9 pinned inputs. Checkouts are clean, detached at their pinned revisions, 12k / 3k / 0.8k / 0.3k tracked files. ~64k subjects, ~19k claims, ~26k relations, 217 journeys, 4,013 supplied gaps. Artifact 89 MB.

## Reproduction
1. Build the corpus (19.4 s, 1.16 GB RSS).
2. Start `corvint-corpus-mcp --root <primary> --artifact corpus.json --legacy-cases` and send 94 calls across all tools.
3. Read `_meta["corvint/timing"]`.

## Measured
| | value |
|---|---|
| first call | 29.6 s: load 19.2 s + freshness 10.1 s, 36 CPU-s |
| warm calls (86) | `load: reused`, `freshness: computed` on every call; freshness mean 10.0 s (min 8.8 s), verify 0.28 s, query mean 69 ms (max 577 ms); wall mean 9.9 s, p95 13.3 s; 12.9 CPU-s per call |
| peak RSS | 1.39 GB |
| previous build, single repository, same scale | warm mean 1.14 s, freshness ~0.43 s reused |

`internal/doccorpus/query.go` (`liveFreshness`) clears the observation key as soon as an additional repository is checked ("the overlay carries no reusable observation key"), so reuse can never apply.

## Expected
- Freshness reuse works per repository: an observation key per declared checkout (HEAD, status digest), and an unchanged set of keys reuses the previous overlay.
- Warm-call freshness cost does not grow with the number of pinned inputs when no checkout changed.

## Acceptance tests
- Fixture: primary + 2 additional repositories, >= 8,000 pinned inputs. Second and later calls report `freshness: reused` and freshness_ms < 100 ms while no checkout changes.
- Changing one file in one additional repository makes the next call recompute (stale, naming that repository) and later calls reuse again.
- Warm p95 < 1 s for `docs_get`/`docs_search` on that fixture.
title: GH #1487: corpus MCP recomputes freshness on every call with additional repositories (~10 s warm calls)

acceptanceCriteria: Two-citation fixture: changing one cited span marks only that citation `changed`.
`verified_at` is null with a limitation on an unverified corpus.
`docs_gaps {kind}` returns only that kind, with a per-kind total.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1492

## Summary
Gaps between the corpus MCP `trust_envelope` and what a documentation-serving contract needs per response:
1. No `verified_at`: a reader cannot tell when, if ever, content was verified (content_status is always `generated`).
2. Freshness is one value for the whole answer (`fresh`/`stale`/`unknown`). There is no per-citation anchor state (unchanged, moved, changed, gone) and no way to report that the caller's checkout has diverged from the corpus revision.
3. Supplied free text (claim text, gap reasons, subject names) carries no per-field origin marker (e.g. `origin: untrusted` with its length cap) so a consumer cannot keep third-party prose out of an answer structurally.
4. `docs_gaps` cannot filter by gap kind; a "list all gaps of kind K" question returns everything for a subject or the whole corpus.

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d; ~100k-record, 5-repository corpus.

## Reproduction
1. `docs_get` on a subject whose anchored file later changes only in the cited span of one of its two citations.
2. Observe `freshness: stale` for the receipt with no indication which citation changed.
3. `docs_gaps {kind: "k"}` -> `invalid-arguments`.

## Expected
- `trust_envelope.verified_at` (null with a limitation when never verified).
- Each citation carries `anchor_state` (`live moved changed gone unknown`) from the read-time check; the receipt-level freshness is derived from them.
- Optional caller revision input; when it is not a descendant of the corpus revision, report `diverged`.
- Supplied text fields declare `origin` (`source`, `supplied`, `untrusted`) in the receipt.
- `docs_gaps` accepts `kind` (string or list).

## Acceptance tests
- Two-citation fixture: changing one cited span marks only that citation `changed`.
- `verified_at` is null with a limitation on an unverified corpus.
- `docs_gaps {kind}` returns only that kind, with a per-kind total.
title: GH #1492: corpus MCP trust envelope needs verified_at, per-citation anchor state, field origin, docs_gaps kind filter

acceptanceCriteria: After N calls the file holds per-tool counts that sum to N and contains no request string (test greps for each query string).
Disabled by default; enabling it does not change any receipt.
Floor comparison fails when the answered share drops below floor minus tolerance.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1493

## Summary
The corpus MCP records nothing about how it answers over time. A team replacing another documentation server needs per-tool outcome counters (answered, no-match, capability-absent, refused, error) and latency, to set and gate an answer-rate floor, without storing request text. #1480 covers an offline labelled evaluation; this is the runtime counterpart.

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d. Per-call `_meta["corvint/timing"]` exists; no aggregation.

## Expected
- Opt-in flag (e.g. `--outcome-log FILE`) writing aggregate counters only: tool, outcome/miss kind, count, latency histogram, corpus identity, time window. Never arguments, query text, ids or paths.
- A CLI to summarise the file and compare against a stored floor (exit non-zero on regression).

## Acceptance tests
- After N calls the file holds per-tool counts that sum to N and contains no request string (test greps for each query string).
- Disabled by default; enabling it does not change any receipt.
- Floor comparison fails when the answered share drops below floor minus tolerance.
title: GH #1493: opt-in aggregate per-tool outcome counters for the corpus MCP, without request text

acceptanceCriteria: Each new state builds, appears in `docs_get` and is counted per state by `docs_coverage`.
A state outside the vocabulary is still refused.
A qualified `proven` is reported with its qualifier and never counted as unqualified `proven`.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1488

## Summary
The supplied `status` claim detail (DCP-V1-187, from #1244) admits only `blocked`, `ready` and `proven`. A producer's proof/readiness ledger commonly also records partial proof, a subject that cannot be demonstrated through the tested interface, an open discrepancy, an obsolete subject, a not-established outcome, a qualified/provisional outcome, and `unknown`. None of these can be supplied, so most status rows are lost before import.

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d.
- Producer ledger: 203 work-package status rows and 1,862 readiness rows (all `unknown`).

## Reproduction
1. Adoption provider with flow `p:flow:a` and a claim on it with detail `{"status": {"state": "partial", "reason": "two of five criteria proven", "supporting": []}}`.
2. Build -> refused `invalid supplied status`.
3. Same with `unknown`, `not-demonstrable`, `disputed`, `obsolete`.

## Measured
Of 203 work-package rows, 79 map to `blocked`/`proven`; 124 have no state (partial 47, none recorded 38, not-demonstrable 18, qualified/provisional proven 10, other 11). 0 of 1,862 readiness rows (`unknown`) can be supplied.

## Expected
- A larger closed vocabulary, e.g. `blocked ready proven partial not-demonstrable disputed obsolete not-established unknown`, or a closed `state` plus an optional `qualifier` (`provisional`, `classification-only`) so a qualified outcome is not reported as plain `proven`.
- `docs_coverage` counts per state as today; `unknown` stays distinguishable from absence of a status.

## Acceptance tests
- Each new state builds, appears in `docs_get` and is counted per state by `docs_coverage`.
- A state outside the vocabulary is still refused.
- A qualified `proven` is reported with its qualifier and never counted as unqualified `proven`.
title: GH #1488: widen the supplied status vocabulary (partial, unknown, disputed, qualified outcomes)

acceptanceCriteria: A run with all new fields builds and round-trips through `docs_get`.
Unknown values are refused.
A gap targeting a run claim appears in `docs_gaps` for that claim and for its subject.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1489

## Summary
The supplied `test_run` claim detail (DCP-V1-210) carries only `outcome`, `run`, `origin`, `revision` and `at`. Run ledgers used to decide whether a test is trustworthy also record retries, a same-revision flake verdict, cleanup outcome, a control (negative) run outcome and per-axis validity results. These fit only in free text. In addition, supplied gaps must name a subject, so a gap about one run (flaky, stale evidence) has to be attached to the run's parent subject and loses its target.

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d.
- Producer data: 1,993 runs, 9,965 per-run validity rows (5 axes each), 2,274 run-level gaps.

## Reproduction
1. Provider: flow `p:flow:a`; claim `p:run:1` on it with `{"test_run": {"outcome": "passed", "run": "r1", "origin": "supplied", "retries": 2}}` -> refused (unknown field).
2. Supplied gap `{"id": "p:gap:1", "subject": "p:run:1", "kind": "flaky", ...}` -> refused `supplied gap subject missing` (a claim is not a subject).

## Measured
All 1,993 runs import with outcome only; retries, flake verdict, cleanup and control outcome survive only as text; 9,965 validity rows have no home; 2,274 run gaps were re-attached to the flow.

## Expected
- Optional closed fields on `test_run`: `retries` (int >= 0), `flake_verdict` (`stable flaky unqualified unknown`), `cleanup` (`passed failed partial not-run unknown`), `control_outcome` (outcome vocabulary), and `validity: [{axis, status}]` with closed axis and status sets.
- A supplied gap may target a claim id (or a run id declared by a `test_run` detail).
- `docs_coverage` can count runs by flake verdict and cleanup; supplied fields still grant no trust.

## Acceptance tests
- A run with all new fields builds and round-trips through `docs_get`.
- Unknown values are refused.
- A gap targeting a run claim appears in `docs_gaps` for that claim and for its subject.
title: GH #1489: test_run receipts need retries, flake verdict, cleanup, control outcome, validity axes; gaps target a run

acceptanceCriteria: Two revisions of B: anchors at both build; an anchor at the older revision reports that revision in citations.
`docs_locate {path, repository: B}` returns only B's subjects; without `repository`, each result names its repository.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1490

## Summary
Two follow-ups to additional-repository anchors (#1243), found on a 4-repository corpus:
1. A repository can be pinned at only one revision. Records citing an older revision of an already-declared repository cannot be anchored: a second `additional_repositories` entry with the same root commit is refused, and a scope at that revision is attributed to the primary repository.
2. `docs_locate` takes only `path`/`paths`. In a multi-repository corpus the same relative path can exist in several repositories (e.g. `README.md`, `package.json`, `config/x.yml`) and the request cannot say which one is meant.

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d. Primary repository + 4 additional repositories; 102 records cite one repository at an older revision.

## Reproduction
1. Manifest with additional repository B pinned at `revB2`, plus scopes at `revB1` (an ancestor in B) -> refused (`repository identity mismatch` / revision attributed to the primary).
2. Repositories A and B both contain `docs/README.md`, each anchored by a subject. `docs_locate {path: "docs/README.md"}` returns both with no way to restrict to B.

## Measured
82 of 102 older-revision references could be re-pinned because their blob is unchanged; 20 had to be dropped.

## Expected
- An additional repository may declare more than one revision (within the eight-revision bound), each verified in the same checkout's object store; freshness compares only the declared current revision.
- `docs_locate` (and `docs_recommend_tests`) accept an optional `repository` (root-commit id) per path; without it, results group by repository.

## Acceptance tests
- Two revisions of B: anchors at both build; an anchor at the older revision reports that revision in citations.
- `docs_locate {path, repository: B}` returns only B's subjects; without `repository`, each result names its repository.
title: GH #1490: additional repositories pinned at more than one revision; repository qualifier for docs_locate

acceptanceCriteria: Fixture with 3 baseline and 3 target units covering moved, removed and ambiguous: all build; a unit read returns its mapping and readiness.
An unknown outcome or basis is refused; a mapping to a non-inventory subject is refused.
body:
GitHub https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1491

## Summary
There is no typed home for a code-migration ledger: baseline and target inventory units, the mapping between them (unchanged, modified, moved, renamed, copied, added, removed, ambiguous, unresolved, with a basis such as stable id or region hash), and a per-target-unit readiness state with the evidence ids it rests on. `inventory` subjects carry no mapping, and the status detail cannot express `unknown` (see the status vocabulary issue). A reader cannot ask "which documented units of the old revision moved, and is the new location ready".

## Environment
- Build: main-ef2a01d.
- Producer data: one migration run with 3,516 units (baseline and target), 1,872 mappings, 1,862 readiness rows.

## Reproduction
1. Provider with `inventory` subjects `p:unit:old:1` and `p:unit:new:1`.
2. Try to supply a mapping `old:1 -> new:1, outcome moved, basis region_hash` and readiness `new:1: unknown, reason "independent verification missing"`.
3. No relation type or detail accepts either.

## Expected
- A `migration_mapping` relation (or detail) between two inventory subjects with closed `outcome` and `basis` sets, and an optional run id; added/removed as one-sided mappings.
- Readiness via the status detail (with `unknown`), supporting ids pointing at evidence records.
- A read (`docs_get` on a unit, or a `docs_migration` tool gated by a capability) returning the mapping chain and readiness.

## Acceptance tests
- Fixture with 3 baseline and 3 target units covering moved, removed and ambiguous: all build; a unit read returns its mapping and readiness.
- An unknown outcome or basis is refused; a mapping to a non-inventory subject is refused.
title: GH #1491: typed home for a code-migration ledger (unit mappings and per-unit readiness)

acceptanceCriteria: processGroupQuiescentBy (or its caller) treats an exited, unreaped leader whose group has no other live member as quiescent on Linux (for example via the existing /proc held-group proof), so a group that obeys TERM returns before the grace expires.
A focused Linux test (CI or container) shows a TERM-obeying group with a 5 s grace stopping in well under 1 s, and a TERM-ignoring descendant still being SIGKILLed after the grace.
macOS behaviour is unchanged; the owning procgroup requirement records the rule.
body: Observed 2026-10-22 on batch PR #1534 (go-product-shard 4, job 119794317101): TestSourceViewCancellationTerminatesGitProcessGroup with a 1-minute TerminateGrace (V1-2319) took 60.01 s on Linux CI and failed its 25 s bound; on macOS it finishes in milliseconds. Reproduced in golang:1.27.2 Docker: with a 5 s grace the test takes exactly 5.14 s although the shell exits on TERM at once. Cause (inferred from internal/procgroup/process_posix.go cleanupProcessGroupBeforeReap -> processGroupQuiescentBy): the group probe is kill(-pgid, 0), and Linux keeps succeeding while the exited leader is held unreaped as a zombie, so the group never reads quiet until the grace deadline. Production uses the 100 ms default grace, so the cost is 100 ms per cancelled/timed-out child, but any caller with a longer grace pays it in full and the quiescence signal is wrong. The batch fixed only the test (grace lowered to 5 s, commit 3ab77c0b9).
title: procgroup: on Linux every signalled group waits out the full TERM grace because the unreaped leader keeps signal 0 succeeding

acceptanceCriteria: An owner decision accepts or rejects an opt-in goal profile that amends LCP-V0-008; without acceptance the one-continuation rule stays unchanged.
If accepted: continuation is decided only by the claimed ticket's acceptance gate result, never by a model verdict or transcript content, and Stop never runs expensive verification itself.

Hard bounds are enforced and visible: a continuation cap, a no-progress stop after N consecutive unchanged gate results and trees, release on user interruption, and one settlement outcome (COMPLETED, BLOCKED, BUDGET_REACHED) recorded in the ticket's receipts.
body:
Filed 2026-10-22 from a review of openchamber/openchamber (MIT) 'Session Goals'.

OpenChamber turns a prompt into a goal: after each agent turn an independent auditor (a cheap model that sees only the objective and the latest reply) returns continue/done/stuck; it auto-continues, completes with one settlement notification, and stops as BLOCKED only after three consecutive 'stuck' verdicts. Hard stops: token budget, a cap on automatic continuations, and turn errors; an explicit user stop always wins. Per-turn notifications are suppressed while the goal runs.

Corvint today deliberately allows only one bounded remediation continuation at Stop (LCP-V0-008, stop_hook_active releases). The Corvint-shaped version replaces the model auditor with a deterministic one: the claimed ticket's acceptance criteria and required gates (gate run / criterion verification) decide done; the measured signal for 'no progress' is an unchanged gate result plus unchanged committed tree across N consecutive continuations. This also gives lanes a principled bound for the reruns behind V1-1629 (dogfood-change rerun 4-19 times) and V1-1630 (polling loops).

Changing the one-continuation rule is an owner decision; this ticket proposes an explicitly enrolled, opt-in profile, not a default.
title: Tasks goal mode: opt-in bounded continuation until a claimed ticket's acceptance gate passes, with a no-progress stop

acceptanceCriteria: A read-only command takes one base and N candidate refs and emits one comparison record citing each candidate's CEM digest and reviewer report; it mutates no repository or trace state (invariant 4).
Each compared dimension cites its evidence; a candidate lacking a CEM or report shows NOT_PRODUCED for that dimension rather than a score.
No model-authored merge of candidates is in scope; any recommended pick names the evidence that separates the candidates or abstains.
body:
Filed 2026-10-22 from a review of openchamber/openchamber (MIT) 'Multi-run' and 'Fusion'.

OpenChamber runs one prompt on up to five models, each in its own worktree, then leaves comparison to the human (or an LLM 'Fusion' merge). Corvint can do the comparison with evidence instead of taste: for N candidate branches against one base and one ticket, a read-only report of each candidate's acceptance-criterion coverage, witnessed versus unwitnessed hunks, reviewer-report uncertainties and abstentions, affected-test results and diff size. It ranks nothing it cannot cite; missing evidence for a candidate is shown as NOT_PRODUCED, not as a loss.

Useful where lanes or hosts already produce competing attempts (Tasks attempts, maxActiveAttempts) and the owner picks one.
title: Compare candidate changes for one ticket by their evidence: a read-only side-by-side of N candidate branches' CEMs and reviewer reports

acceptanceCriteria: Repository heavy targets (make test/gate/dogfood-change/dogfood-check and the lane test wrapper) run their child processes below interactive scheduling priority (nice 10 or more) by default, with an opt-out variable.

Under a reproduced lane load of at least 3 concurrent package test runs on a 12-core host, 50 consecutive Claude Code user-prompt adapter invocations finish under the 2 s hook limit with no dogfood-event-deadline fallback; timings retained as evidence.
If priority alone does not meet that bound, the adapter's user-prompt path is profiled under load and its remaining load-sensitive work (git probes, snapshot reads) is moved off the synchronous path.
body: 2026-10-22: every UserPromptSubmit hook in the orchestrator session fell back with dogfood-event-deadline while three lanes ran tests (load average 41, rising from 15; 12 cores). Measured at load 25-29 with the installed build 712: `corvint adapter claude-code user-prompt` takes 0.39-0.45 s on this session's enrolled path and 0.41-0.88 s unenrolled, so the hook is fast at idle and fails only when CPU-bound test children starve it of CPU against its fixed 2 s timeout (hooks.json timeout 2). Earlier fixes (V1-0881, V1-1120, V1-1422) cut adapter work but the failure recurs whenever lane load passes about 40. Local mitigation applied the same day: /private/tmp/cem10-build/heavy.sh now runs its command under `nice -n 15` (verified: child nice 15). The repository's own heavy make targets still run at normal priority. Related: V1-1627, V1-1628 (host throttle/semaphore), V1-1496 (fallback cause reporting).
title: Hook adapters still hit dogfood-event-deadline when lane test load starves them of CPU; heavy targets must run below interactive priority

acceptanceCriteria: Measure the 2 s racy-window guard on a coarse-timestamp filesystem (for example FAT/exFAT or an SMB/NFS mount) and record whether a same-second, same-size edit is ever served stale.
Linked worktrees and submodules get a stamp path, or a recorded measurement shows the Git fallback stays within the warm budget for them.
Windows gets a stamp path or a measured, documented fallback cost.
body: Residuals from PR beamfall/corvint#1559 (V1-2434, DCP-V1-314..317). The docs-corpus checkout freshness stamp is file metadata only (size, inode, timestamps). A same-second edit that keeps those is caught only by the 2 s racy-window guard, which is unmeasured on coarse-timestamp and network filesystems. Linked worktrees, submodules, alternates, config includes and non-Darwin/Linux platforms (Windows) always fall back to the slow Git path, so they do not get the warm-call speedup.
title: Docs-corpus freshness stamp: measure racy-window guard on coarse/network filesystems; cover linked worktrees, submodules and Windows

acceptanceCriteria: Every field contributing to pools.json size (identifiers, sweep owners, slots, waiters, receipts, reasons) has a bound such that the computed worst case, including worst-case JSON escaping, is at most 1,048,576 B.
A test builds that worst case and shows it encodes within the bound, and that an oversized fresh input is refused with a typed refusal before any write.
body: Residual of V1-2361 repair (lane tasks-oc-1022, head 668415615, PSR-V0-202). The recover reason cap is now 224 B, derived from a worst-case fixture (256 entries with max configRef, 256 REPORTED identities, 512 receipts) that encodes to 907,069 B with empty reasons. Expected: every reachable pool state stays within the 1 MiB pools.json bound so pool writes cannot be wedged. Actual: three shapes exceed the bound even with empty reasons: identifiers whose characters need JSON escaping, a sweep owner on every entry, or large slots/waiters lists; a probe measured 1,091,418 B, after which such writes are refused LIMIT_EXCEEDED. No reason cap can fix this; it needs per-field or per-entry size bounds.
title: pools.json can exceed its 1 MiB bound with empty reasons: JSON-escaped identifiers, per-entry sweep owners or large slots/waiters lists (probe 1,091,418 B)

acceptanceCriteria: The DCP-V1-303 closed test_run validity axis set gains association with the existing status set; docs/specs/documentation-corpus-v1.md amended in the same change.

body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1571 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

=== #1571 Feature: supplied test_run validity needs an association axis
## Summary
The supplied `test_run` validity axes (DCP-V1-303) are a closed set: `revision environment isolation oracle determinism`. A run ledger that decides whether a test may witness a claim also records an **association** axis: whether the test is bound, at example level, to the behaviour the claim describes (the right example, at the cited revision, exercising the claimed path). That axis has no home, so it survives only as text.

## Environment
- Build: main-2173fd3 (`internal/doccorpus/adoption.go:172`).
- Producer data: 1,993 runs, 9,965 per-run validity rows (5 axes each). Three axes map (`revision`, `isolation`, `oracle`). The fourth (execution) is the run outcome. 1,993 association rows are left as text.

## Reproduction
1. Supply a `test_run` with `"validity": [{"axis": "association", "status": "failed"}]`.
2. The import refuses the record (unknown axis).

## Measured
3,986 axis rows left as text across the 1,993 runs; association is the one with no stand-in.

## Expected
- `association` in the closed axis set, with the existing status set.
- A run whose association status is not `passed` cannot count as a witness for the claim it is linked to.
title: GH #1571: supplied test_run validity needs an association axis

acceptanceCriteria: Optional closed detail shapes for coverage-ledger status per flow, coverage/audit completeness flags per flow, and unresolved concepts per domain attach to their subject and carry the provider trust ceiling.
docs_flow, docs_gaps and docs_coverage serve them; unknown fields are still refused; spec requirements and tests added.
The PR body says Closes #1572.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1572 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

=== #1572 Feature: typed homes for per-subject coverage-ledger status, completeness flags and unresolved concepts
## Summary
Three per-subject record families have no typed home, so a producer can only drop them or flatten them into text:
1. **Coverage-ledger status per flow.** Fields: `scope` (`ui`, `non_ui`), `ledger_status` (`confirmed`, `partial`, `not-browser`), browser-evidence kind, journey count, ordered-step count, verification status and limitations. This does not fit the `blocked/ready/proven` status vocabulary.
2. **Coverage and audit completeness flags per flow.** Fields: `target_status`, `coverage_complete` and `audit_complete` (booleans with a reason), and the source revision and path that back them. These are what stop a consumer from claiming complete coverage too early.
3. **Unresolved concepts per domain.** A concept that is anchored in source and reviewed, but not yet resolved to a UI location or flow. "Known to exist, not yet placed" is a first-class answer and differs from a gap.

## Environment
- Build: main-14dc0e9 measured; main-2173fd3 source read.
- Producer data: 159 coverage-ledger rows, 80 flow completeness rows, 38 unresolved concepts.

## Reproduction
Supply any of the three as a claim detail on the flow or domain subject. The detail is refused (unknown field), or it can only go into claim text.

## Measured
All 277 rows are dropped before import. A journey-coverage question gets a thinner answer than the producer's own server gives (`docs_gaps` returns 4,063 chars against 22,137).

## Expected
Optional closed detail shapes for the three families, attached to their subject, carrying the provider trust ceiling, and served by `docs_flow`, `docs_gaps` and `docs_coverage`.
title: GH #1572: typed homes for per-subject coverage-ledger status, completeness flags and unresolved concepts

acceptanceCriteria: docs_search returns claim hits ranked together with subject hits, each tagged with its record kind (or an opt-in include:[claims]), within existing bounds and trust envelopes.
A test shows a distinctive claim phrase is found by docs_search alone; spec updated.
The PR body says Closes #1573.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1573 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

=== #1573 Feature: docs_search should return claim hits so one call answers a free-text question
## Summary
`docs_search` ranks subjects only. Claim text is reachable only through `docs_claims` with `query` (#1555). A caller asking a plain question therefore has to guess in advance whether the answer is a subject or a claim. With a single search call, every claim question misses.

## Environment
- Build: main-14dc0e9 (no `doccorpus` search change through main-2173fd3).
- Records-only corpus, 13,498 claims, 60,507 subjects.

## Reproduction
1. Take a claim whose text contains a distinctive phrase.
2. `docs_search {query: "<phrase>"}`: the claim is not returned.
3. `docs_claims {query: "<phrase>"}`: the claim is returned.

## Measured
- On a 52-case labelled recall suite: `docs_search` alone passes 21 of 52 (claim cases 0 of 28).
- When the caller routes claim cases to `docs_claims`, the suite passes 40 of 52 (claim cases 19 of 28).
- Expected-id recall across 83 recorded serving calls: 474 of 1,836.

## Expected
- `docs_search` returns claim hits alongside subject hits, each tagged with its record kind and ranked together. Alternatively, an opt-in `include: [claims]` that does the same.
- This lets one call answer a free-text question without the caller routing it.
title: GH #1573: docs_search should return claim hits so one call answers a free-text question

acceptanceCriteria: Optional alternate_ids on a supplied subject: closed list of exact strings, unique within the provider, duplicates refused at import.
docs_get, docs_flow and the path/subject readers resolve an alternate id exactly; the receipt records alias resolution; ambiguous or unknown ids give the typed no-match.
Spec and tests updated; the PR body says Closes #1574.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1574 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
Producers often have their own stable ids for subjects, such as catalog numbers. People and agents use these ids in questions ("show me X-007"). A supplied subject can't carry an alternate id that the readers resolve exactly. `docs_flow` and `docs_get` take only the Corvint subject id. A `docs_search` for the producer id returns a ranked hit list rather than the subject, and only when the id happens to appear in indexed text.

## Environment
- Build: main-14dc0e9 measured; no change in `internal/doccorpus` reader id handling through main-2173fd3.
- Records-only corpus, 60,507 subjects.

## Reproduction
1. Supply a flow subject `p:flow:a` whose producer id is `X-007`.
2. `docs_flow {id: "X-007"}`: refused as an unknown id.
3. `docs_search {query: "X-007"}`: a hit list (about 175,000 chars in the measured case), not the flow.

## Expected
- Optional `alternate_ids` on a supplied subject: a closed list of exact strings, unique within the provider, with a duplicate refused at import.
- `docs_get`, `docs_flow` and the path/subject readers resolve an alternate id exactly to its subject. The receipt records that the id was resolved through an alias.
- An ambiguous or unknown alternate id gives the existing typed `no-match`.
title: GH #1574: supplied subjects need alternate ids that docs_get and docs_flow resolve exactly

acceptanceCriteria: Dynamic-import scanning skips string/template literal contents and type-position import('x') types; a real runtime import() still sets the frontier.
Regression tests reproduce the 469-to-bounded case shape.
PR body says Closes #1575.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1575 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
The TypeScript graph marks a file as containing a dynamic import when its comment-stripped text matches `import\s*\(` (`internal/liveverify/affected/typescript/typescript.go:484`). Two common things that load nothing at runtime also match:
1. **Type-position import types:** `page: import('@playwright/test').Page`. These are erased at compile time.
2. **String literals:** a test title such as `'the server lets an administrator read the import (summary)'`.

Either one sets the `typescript:dynamic-import` frontier. In a Playwright repository every test then reaches a "dynamic" file, so a one-line change to a page-object module widens to the whole suite (`FULL_SUITE_WIDENING`).

## Environment
- Build: main-2173fd3.
- Playwright repository: 469 discovery units, about 420 TypeScript modules.

## Reproduction
1. In a clean Playwright repository, add `const f = (p: import('@playwright/test').Page) => p;` to any test-side module, and commit.
2. Change a page-object module that 11 specs import.
3. `corvint affected --playwright-config playwright.config.ts --playwright-discovery D.json` selects 469 of 469 units (`FULL_SUITE_WIDENING`), with the unknown `typescript:dynamic-import`.
4. Replace the type with an imported type alias and regenerate discovery: the plan becomes `BOUNDED` and selects the 11 importing specs (per project) plus their setup dependencies.
5. The same happens with a string literal containing `import (`.

## Measured
The repository had 10 type-position `import('…')` uses across 6 files, plus one test title containing `import (`. Removing them, together with the config fixes in the companion issue, took the same change from 469 units to 40, with scope `BOUNDED`.

## Expected
- Skip string and template literal contents when scanning for `import(`.
- Do not count an `import(` in a type position (after `:` in an annotation, in `typeof import(…)`, or in a type alias or generic argument) as a runtime import.
- Optionally, name the file and line that set the frontier in the plan's unknown detail, so a caller can find it.
title: GH #1575: affected (TypeScript): type-position import() and string literals count as dynamic imports, widening Playwright selection to the full suite

acceptanceCriteria: process.env reads in non-identity use keys no longer fail the use layer; array trailing commas parse; env-sourced launchOptions.executablePath is an EXECUTION-axis unknown, not identity-unresolved.
Dynamic identity keys still fail closed; tests for each idiom.
PR body says Closes #1576.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1576 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
In `--playwright-config` mode, every project's browser identity reports `playwright:browser-identity-unresolved` ("use.browserName/device is dynamic or unsupported") for three common config idioms. Static selection is then refused for every project:
1. **An environment read in a non-identity `use` option.** Examples: `baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:3000'`, `trace: process.env.X === 'true' ? 'retain-on-failure' : 'on-first-retry'`, and `navigationTimeout: Number.parseInt(process.env.T || '60000')`. Reading `process.env` has no side effects, and these keys are not identity keys, yet any one of them fails the whole global `use` layer.
2. **A trailing comma inside an array literal in an identity option.** `launchOptions: { args: ['--a', '--b',] }` fails; `['--a', '--b']` passes. Formatters add this trailing comma to every multi-line array (Prettier `trailingComma: 'es5'`).
3. **An environment-sourced `launchOptions.executablePath`.** For example, a pinned Chromium path from the environment. This changes which binary runs, not which tests are members, so it fits the EXECUTION axis, like `playwright:external-application-state`.

## Environment
- Build: main-2173fd3 (`internal/liveverify/affected/typescript/playwright.go`, `playwrightUseLayer`).
- Config: five projects, all using `...devices['Desktop Chrome']` or the default browser.

## Reproduction
For each idiom, use a global `use` containing only that item and run `corvint affected --playwright-config playwright.config.ts`:

| Global `use` | browser-identity-unresolved |
|---|---|
| `{ timezoneId: 'America/New_York' }` | 0 |
| `{ baseURL: process.env['HOST'] \|\| 'http://127.0.0.1:3000' }` | 5 (every project) |
| `{ trace: process.env.X === 'true' ? 'a' : 'b' }` | 5 |
| `{ navigationTimeout: Number.parseInt(process.env.T \|\| '60000') }` | 5 |
| `{ launchOptions: { args: ['--a', '--b'] } }` | 0 |
| `{ launchOptions: { args: ['--a', '--b',] } }` | 5 |
| `{ launchOptions: { args: ['--a'], executablePath: process.env.P } }` | 5 |

## Expected
- Accept `process.env` reads (member access, `||`/`??` with a literal, a ternary comparing one to a literal, `Number.parseInt` of those) as pure in non-identity keys.
- Accept trailing commas in array and object literals.
- Report an environment-sourced `executablePath` as an EXECUTION-axis unknown instead of a SELECTION refusal.
title: GH #1576: affected (Playwright): env reads in non-identity use options, trailing commas and env executablePath make every browser identity unresolved

acceptanceCriteria: A const bound to a literal array or ternary of literal arrays resolves to the union of branches for dependencies (conservative superset), in discovery and selection.
Truly dynamic dependencies still refuse; tests added.
PR body says Closes #1577.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1577 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
When a project's `dependencies` is a constant chosen from the environment, two things fail. `affected discovery` refuses the whole listing with `unsupported-playwright-discovery` ("the config's test membership is not static (playwright:project-dependency-unresolved: P dependencies are dynamic)"). Static selection also refuses every project that uses it. An example of the pattern:
```ts
const deps = process.env.LAZY === '1' ? ['global-setup'] : ['setup'];
// projects: [{ name: 'chromium', dependencies: deps }, ...]
```
#1294 asked for statically resolvable sub-projects to keep narrowing when one is dynamic. Here every test project shares the constant, so nothing narrows.

## Environment
- Build: main-2173fd3 (`playwright.go`, `playwrightStringArray` on `dependencies`).

## Reproduction
1. Use a config with three test projects whose `dependencies` reference the constant above.
2. `corvint affected discovery --playwright-config playwright.config.ts --playwright-list list.json` exits 2 with `unsupported-playwright-discovery`.
3. Replace the constant with the literal `['setup']`: discovery succeeds.

## Expected
Either of the following:
- Resolve an identifier bound to a `const` whose initializer is a literal array, or a ternary of literal arrays, to the union of the branches. This is a conservative superset: a test project that might depend on either setup project selects both.
- Or accept caller-declared environment bindings (`--env NAME=VALUE`) for config evaluation and record them in the plan.
title: GH #1577: affected (Playwright): project dependencies from an env-chosen const refuse discovery for every project

body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1578 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
In `--path` mode (no `--playwright-config`), a change to a non-test module under the Playwright test root does two odd things:
1. **The module is reported as a selected Playwright unit.** Unit id `typescript:playwright:<module>.ts`, `testCount: 1`, witness `DIRECT_TEST_CHANGE`, and tiers `tier0=1`.
2. **Simple tsconfig paths are not resolved.** The plan reports `typescript:path-alias-unresolved` for a `tsconfig.json` with `"baseUrl": "."` and `"paths": { "lib/*": ["./lib/*"] }`, and the specs that import the module through that alias are not selected.

The scope is `UNKNOWN`, so this fails closed. But the tier output says one tier-0 unit, which a consumer can misread as "run this one file". Config mode (`--playwright-config`) resolves the same aliases correctly.

## Environment
- Build: main-2173fd3.
- The module is imported by 11 specs, as `import X from 'lib/pages/.../X'`.

## Reproduction
1. `corvint affected --path lib/pages/area/SomePage.ts` in a clean Playwright repository.
2. Selected: 1 unit, the page module itself, with `testCount: 1`. Excluded: 406. Unknowns: `dynamic-import`, `e2e-runtime-dependency`, `executable-config-unresolved`, `path-alias-unresolved`.

## Expected
- `--path` mode classifies only files matched by a runner's test pattern as test units.
- It resolves `baseUrl` and `paths` aliases as config mode does, and selects the importing specs.
title: GH #1578: affected --path: non-test module reported as a selected Playwright unit and tsconfig paths unresolved

acceptanceCriteria: docs_search ranks name/title matches above claim-text-only matches with rarity weighting (e.g. BM25 over name and claim fields); id tie-break only for equal scores.
Optional kind filter; deterministic ordering; tests and spec updated.
PR body says Closes #1579.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1579 (2026-10-22). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
`docs_search` scores a subject by the number of distinct query terms present in its name, id and claim text, plus a bonus for an exact name match. Ties are broken by subject id (`internal/doccorpus/query.go`, `search`). For a one-word query every match scores 1, so results come out in id order, and the kinds that sort first alphabetically fill the first page. There is no weighting by field (a term in the subject's name versus one mention in a long claim), no term-frequency or rarity weighting, and no kind filter.

## Environment
- Build: main-14dc0e9 measured; `search` is unchanged in main-2173fd3.
- Records-only corpus: 60,507 subjects, including 3,728 manual cases and about 29,000 inventory modules.

## Reproduction
1. `docs_search {query: "login", limit: 20}`.
2. Results 1–20 are one use case, then manual cases in id order.
3. The one flow whose name contains "login" (a flow subject, whose id sorts after case and code ids) is at rank 78 of 180.

## Measured
On recorded "which flow covers X" questions, the expected flow and file ids appear in 3 of 20 cases.

## Expected
- Rank a name or title match above a match only in claim text, and weight rarer terms higher (for example BM25 over name and claim fields). Keep the id tie-break only for equal scores.
- Optionally, a `kind` filter (for example `kind: ["flow"]`) so a caller can ask for flows only.
title: GH #1579: docs_search single-term queries come back in id order; add field weighting and kind filter

acceptanceCriteria: A `docs corpus discover-tests --runner playwright|rspec --revision FULL_COMMIT --path PATH` producer emits per-example title path, tags, expectations, navigations/requests, reached helpers/fixtures/shared examples and applicable hooks, each anchored to an exact span, at generated trust.
Unclassifiable syntax is reported as unknown with a reason; output is byte-identical for identical blobs; tests cover both runners.
Spec amended with new requirement IDs; the PR body says Closes #1582.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1582 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
`test_knowledge` records (DCP-V1-086..092) are caller-supplied only. A producer has to read each Playwright or RSpec spec and write down what it checks, which today means a person or a language model reading the file. Most of that record is mechanical: it can be read from the spec's syntax. `discover-legacy` already does this for Jasmine and Mocha/Cypress, and `tests lint` and `tests setup-select` already parse Playwright and RSpec files. There is no producer that emits the mechanical half of a test-knowledge record for current Playwright and RSpec suites.

## Proposal
A `docs corpus discover-tests --runner playwright|rspec --revision FULL_COMMIT --path PATH` producer that emits, per test example, with exact anchors:
- the full title path (describe/context/it, `test.describe`/`test`), tags and annotations;
- each expectation: matcher, negation, the receiver expression text, and the line span;
- each navigation or request the test makes (`goto`, request helpers, routes awaited);
- the page objects, helpers, fixtures and shared examples it reaches by static import or `include_examples`/`it_behaves_like`, with the same unknown reasons `setup-select` uses for computed lookups;
- hooks that apply to it (`before`/`beforeEach` etc.) and whether they contain assertions.

Output is `generated` trust, never `reviewed`: a reviewer still sets the verdict (`bound`, `partial`, `defect`). Anything the tokenizer cannot classify is reported as unknown with a reason, never guessed, matching `discover-legacy`.

## Why
Reviewers then confirm or reject a pre-filled record instead of writing one. Records stay reproducible from the spec blob, and a changed spec yields a changed record without anyone re-reading it.

## Expected
- Deterministic output for identical blobs; every field anchored to a span.
- Example-level identities that `tests example-join` and run receipts can join on (relates to #1571).
title: GH #1582: docs corpus discover-tests: generated test-knowledge records from Playwright and RSpec specs

acceptanceCriteria: Repository-declared extractor profiles emit endpoint, job/event, data entity and UI surface subjects with exact anchors and derived implements/calls relations; unreadable files are gaps with reasons; pinned digested tool output is accepted.
`flows import --format` gains the inventory format; flow job/event relations are checked against declared subjects.
Spec amended with new requirement IDs; tests cover each subject family; the PR body says Closes #1583.
body:
Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1583 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
The corpus has generic subject types for `endpoint`, `data entity` and capability, and flow relations can say a flow `produces` or `consumes` a job or event (DCP-V1-093..099). None of these are source-derived. A producer has to list endpoints, background jobs, events and data entities by hand or by asking a language model to read the code, and the job/event names in flow relations are matched by exact string with nothing to check them against.

These facts are declarative in most web applications and can be read mechanically: a route table, job class declarations and their enqueue sites, event publish/subscribe calls, and the database schema file.

## Proposal
Declared extractor profiles, configured per repository rather than built into Core taxonomy, that emit generic subjects with exact anchors:
- `endpoint`: HTTP method, path pattern, handler symbol, from a route-table file or route declarations;
- job/event subjects: declaration site, every enqueue/publish site, every consumer;
- `data entity`: tables/models and columns from a schema file;
- `UI surface`: routes from a frontend router configuration.

Relations derived from the same evidence (`implements` from endpoint to handler, `calls` from enqueue site to job). A file the profile cannot read is a gap with a reason. A profile that needs a framework's own tooling to evaluate (for example a generated route dump) can accept that tool's output as a pinned, digested input instead of parsing source.

Add a `flows import --format` for this inventory, like the existing `openapi` and `playwright-list` formats, so flow candidates can start from endpoints and UI surfaces.

## Why
Flow relations to jobs and events could then be checked against declared subjects instead of free strings, and endpoint and job inventories stop depending on generated text.
title: GH #1583: docs corpus: source-derived endpoint, job, event, data-entity and UI-surface subjects from declared extractor profiles

acceptanceCriteria: Build extracts code-like mentions from claim text and classifies each resolved-in-span, resolved-elsewhere or unresolved; dangling record references are typed refusals or gaps.

Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1584 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
DCP-V1-004 pins every claim anchor and DCP-V1-005 keeps generated claims at `generated` trust, but nothing checks that a generated claim's text is about its own anchor. A claim can name a method, class, path, route or another subject that does not appear in the cited span or anywhere in the corpus, and it is accepted as long as the anchor itself is structurally valid. That is the most common way a language-model-written claim goes wrong, and it is checkable without understanding the sentence.

## Proposal
A mechanical consistency check over supplied and generated claims at build time:
1. **Mentions.** Extract code-like tokens from claim text (backticked spans, `Class#method`, `Module::Name`, `path/to/file.ext`, HTTP method plus path, identifiers in snake/camel case). Each must occur in a cited span, or resolve to an indexed symbol or subject. Report each one as `resolved-in-span`, `resolved-elsewhere` (with the subject ID) or `unresolved`.
2. **References.** Every subject, flow, test or claim ID a supplied record names must resolve in the corpus inventory; a dangling reference is a typed refusal or gap, not silently kept.
3. A per-claim state (for example `mentions: consistent | partially-unresolved | unresolved`) served with the claim and counted in `docs_gaps` and the coverage floor.
4. An opt-in build flag that refuses a corpus with unresolved mentions above a stated threshold.

This makes no semantic judgment and does not raise trust; it only marks claims that cannot be right.

## Expected
Deterministic token rules documented with the contract, so a producer can run the same check before export.
title: GH #1584: docs corpus: mechanical consistency check of generated claim mentions and references

## Summary
`docs corpus audit-sample` and `audit-report` (DCP-V1-260..268) measure accuracy from a uniform random sample and independent verdicts. Several typical failure patterns of generated documentation are detectable without a reviewer, and nothing reports them or uses them to aim the audit:
- the same or near-same claim text on many subjects (templated filler);
- many claims citing one identical span (anchor clustering), or a claim citing a whole file or a very large span;
- claims whose text shares no code-like token with any cited span;
- uniform sentence shapes across a whole subject family.

## Proposal
1. `docs corpus patterns --artifact CORPUS.json` reporting each pattern with its rule, counts, the claim IDs involved and thresholds, deterministic and bounded like other reads.
2. `audit-sample --stratify patterns` so flagged claims are over-sampled in a stated, reproducible way, and `audit-report` gives accuracy per stratum and a weighted overall figure.
3. Optional build thresholds that refuse a corpus above a stated pattern rate.

## Why
Producers currently write these detectors themselves. In Corvint they would be the same for every adopter, and audits would spend reviewer time where generated text is most likely to be wrong.
title: GH #1586: docs corpus patterns: generated-text failure patterns and stratified audit sampling

Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1587 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
`tested_by` evidence and test-selection joins come from static imports, declared links and supplied test-knowledge records. Nothing turns runtime coverage into evidence. A test's per-example coverage is a mechanical record of which source lines it executed, and it is the cheapest independent check on a declared or generated test-to-source link: if a test never executes a line of the code it is said to cover, the link is wrong.

## Proposal
`flows ingest` (or a `docs corpus` provider) accepting per-test coverage in common formats, each pinned by digest and bound to a run receipt and source revision:
- V8/Istanbul JSON produced per Playwright test (or per test attachment);
- RSpec per-example coverage (Ruby `Coverage` results keyed by example ID);
- LCOV when a run is a single test.

Emit `observed` derivation relations `tested_by` from the executed source subjects to the test example, with the executed line spans, and report declared or supplied links that the coverage contradicts (the test ran and executed none of the linked subject's lines) as a typed conflict. Coverage for a different revision is stale, not joined.

## Relation
This is the evidence that would populate the `association` axis requested in #1571, and it complements `affected --appmap-impact`.
title: GH #1587: Ingest per-test runtime coverage as observed tested_by evidence and contradict declared links

Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1588 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
An agent using Corvint cannot find out what it can do without reading source or long specs. `corvint --help` lists about 50 commands with one-line labels and a spec code (for example `flows  application flows and assertions (AFU-V0)`), and each command's help is detailed but has to be opened one at a time. The specs that explain how the pieces fit are not shipped with the installed build; they have to be fetched from the repository, and the documentation-corpus contract alone is about 2,200 lines.

## What happened in one session
To decide which documentation-pipeline features Corvint already covers, an agent had to:
- read `--help` for `docs`, `docs corpus`, `flows`, `features`, `tests`, `runs`, `witness`, `validate`, `claims` and `gaps` one by one;
- fetch `docs/specs/documentation-corpus-v1.md` through the repository API and grep it for requirement IDs;
- guess the order of a two-step workflow: `affected --playwright-list` is refused, and the working path is `affected discovery --playwright-list`, then `affected --playwright-discovery`;
- search issues by keyword to learn whether a capability existed, which mostly returned nothing.

Each of these is a capability question that the tool itself could answer.

## Proposal
1. **Machine-readable command catalog**: `corvint help --json` (or `corvint catalog`) listing every command and operation with purpose, maturity, owning spec, flags, inputs (with schema IDs), outputs (with schema IDs), exit codes and whether it writes anything.
2. **Task-indexed guide shipped with the install**: a short `AGENTS.md`/`llms.txt` style file under the install root, mapping goals to command sequences (for example "select tests for a change", "build and query a documentation corpus", "prove a test witnesses a change", "check test validity"), each with one runnable example and the expected outputs.
3. **Explicit non-capabilities**: for each area, what Corvint does not do and which issue tracks it, so "not listed" is not mistaken for "not possible".
4. **The same content over MCP**: a `corvint.help` tool or resource on each MCP server, so an agent connected only through MCP can discover capabilities.
5. **Kept true by tests**: the catalog generated from the command registry and checked in CI, so it cannot drift from the binary.

## Why
Agents currently spend most of their effort rediscovering features, miss ones that exist and file requests for things that are already there.
title: GH #1588: Agent-readable capability catalog: corvint help --json, shipped task guide, MCP help

Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1593 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
On main-698ce6c (after #1581), `affected` reports `typescript:dynamic-import` ("shared TypeScript graph frontier") for TypeScript files that contain no `import(` or `require(` at all. The trigger is a regular-expression literal followed later on the line by a string literal containing `/`. Builds main-2173fd3 and main-0b7d59b do not report it for the same tree, so this is a regression from the literal-aware scanner that replaced the `import\s*\(` regex for #1575. Every Playwright selection in an affected repository widens to the full suite again.

## Minimal reproduction
A module in the Playwright graph:

```ts
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
const a = s.replace(/[^x]+/, '').replace('/x', '');
```

| Line 2 | `typescript:dynamic-import` |
|---|---|
| `s.replace(/[^/]+/, '').replace('/x', '')` | yes |
| `s.replace(/[^x]+/, '').replace('/x', '')` | yes |
| `s.replace(/[^\/]+/, '').replace('/x', '')` | yes |
| `s.replace(/[^/]+/, '').replace('x', '')` | no |

It looks like the `/` that opens the regex after `(` is read as division, so `/, '').replace('/` is read as a regex and the rest of the line as an unterminated string. In a real repository four files tripped it, all with `url.replace(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+/, '')` style code. I found them by blanking files and bisecting, because the reason does not name a file.

## Expected
- A regex literal after `(`, `,`, `=`, `:`, `[`, `!`, `&`, `|`, `?`, `{`, `}`, `;`, `return` or at line start is a regex, not division.
- An unclassifiable token is its own reason (for example `typescript:scan-unresolved`), not `dynamic-import`.
- The `detail` of every `typescript:*` frontier reason names the path and line that raised it.
title: GH #1593: affected (TypeScript): regex literal followed by a string containing '/' reported as typescript:dynamic-import

Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1594 (2026-10-23). Owner: fix before 1.0.0-rc.3.

## Summary
Follow-up to #1576 after #1581 (TJAA-V0-035). On main-698ce6c, a real-world Playwright config whose `use` reads environment variables still yields `playwright:browser-identity-unresolved` for every project, and no `playwright:browser-executable-unresolved` appears for its computed `executablePath`. The fix's conditions are met by none of the variants I tried until two unrelated constructs elsewhere in the config were also removed, and the reason gives no location, so finding them took a file-level bisect.

## Found triggers
1. **The word `global` anywhere in the config, including string literals.** The fix turns off on any `globalThis/global/window/self` token. A setup project named `'global-setup'` with `testMatch: 'setup/global-setup.ts'` is the Playwright docs' own convention, and it disables the env-read support. Renaming those strings was required.
2. **`process.env.X ??= value` writes at the top of the config** for keys that are never read by an identity key (for example `TZ`, a run id). These disable it even though no `use` key reads them.

With both removed, comments stripped, and `use` reduced to `baseURL: process.env.HOSTNAME`, identity resolves (0 unknowns). With the real `use` block (`process.env['HOSTNAME'] || '...'`, `process.env.X === 'true' ? 'a' : 'b'`, `Number.parseInt(process.env.X || '60000')`, `executablePath: process.env.X`, and a top-level `require('dotenv').config()`) it still does not, and I could not tell which of these remains the blocker.

## Expected
- The identity check ignores string literals and comments when looking for `global`/`window`/`self` tokens.
- Writes to `process.env` keys that no identity key reads do not disable identity resolution.
- Common default forms in non-identity keys are accepted: `process.env.X || 'literal'`, `process.env.X ?? 'literal'`, `process.env['X']`, `process.env.X === 'lit' ? 'a' : 'b'`, and `Number.parseInt(process.env.X || 'lit')`.
- `browser-identity-unresolved` names the token and line that blocked it.

## Note
Discovery with env-conditional dependencies (#1577) works on this build, and #1575's type-position `import()` handling works. Only the identity half of #1576 is not delivered for this config shape.
title: GH #1594: affected (Playwright): env-read identity support disabled by 'global' strings and unrelated process.env writes

# docs_search ranking after #1580: file lookup regressed (21→10 of 24 labelled cases) and include:[claims] buries claims past rank 200
author: ls-russell-lewis
## Summary
Follow-up to #1579 and #1573 after #1580 (DCP-V1-328, DCP-V1-331). The PR notes that the BM25 weights were not checked against a retrieval evaluation. I ran a caller-labelled `docs corpus eval` suite (52 cases, unchanged case file, same provider inputs, corpus rebuilt per builder) on main-2173fd3 and main-32da877 (re-checked on main-8360815, same result):

| Suite | main-2173fd3 | main-32da877 |
|---|---|---|
| 52 recall cases (file lookup + claim lookup) | 21 pass | 10 pass |
| 64 search cases | 46 pass | 47 pass |

## 1. File lookup regressed without a kind filter
All 11 lost cases are "which file implements X" searches, for example "cancel refreshes occupancy once per tee sheet", where the expected file subject (a `module`) was rank 1 to 3 and is now outside the top 5. Documentation paragraph subjects and inventory subjects now outrank it. With `--kind module` the same queries put the file first again (20 of 24 file cases pass), so the BM25 weighting rather than the data is the cause. Path segments of a module subject seem to get no name-field weight.

## 2. `include: ["claims"]` does not surface claims in practice
For 10 claim-lookup cases, the expected claim was beyond rank 256 in 9 and at rank 202 in the tenth with `docs_search --include claims`. `docs corpus claims --query` returns several of the same claims in its top 7. Claim text weighs 1 and every subject name weighs 3, so the merged list is all subjects at any useful page size. With claims included and file cases filtered by kind, the suite scores 20 of 52: 0 of 28 claim cases.

The dedicated claim query did not regress: routing the same 28 claim cases to `docs_claims` with `query` passes 19 on both main-2173fd3 and main-8360815. So the claim family ranks fine on its own; it is the merge into `docs_search` that buries it.

## Expected
- Path segments of `module`/file subjects count as name terms, or `docs_search` exposes the field weights, so file lookup does not depend on the caller passing `kind`.
- A claim hit can outrank a subject hit when its text is the better match, for example by normalizing scores per family before merging, or by returning the claim family as its own ranked list alongside subjects.
- `docs corpus eval` (or a fixed public fixture suite) runs before ranking changes ship, with the before/after summary in the PR.
title: GH #1597: docs_search ranking: file lookup regressed and include:[claims] buries claims

# Performance: every docs corpus CLI read re-derives the artifact (~25 s, ~1.8 GB each, more than the build); delta paging repeats it per page
author: ls-russell-lewis
## Summary
Every documentation-corpus read from the CLI re-derives the whole artifact before answering (DCP-V1-011). On a corpus of about 166,000 records (95 MB artifact, four additional repositories), one read costs more than building the corpus:

| Operation (main-8360815, CLI) | Wall time | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| `docs corpus build` | 21 s | 1.4 GB |
| `info` | 25 s | 1.8 GB |
| `search --query login --limit 20` | 26 s | 1.8 GB |
| `get --id ...` | 27 s | 1.8 GB |
| `flow --id ...` | 27 s | 2.0 GB |
| `coverage` | 27 s | 2.0 GB |
| `locate --path ...` | 26 s | 1.9 GB |
| `delta --limit 256` (one page) | 20 s | 1.5–2.1 GB |

The same cost on main-14dc0e9 and main-2173fd3 (25–26 s, 1.9–2.1 GB for `info`), so this is not a regression, but it makes the CLI unusable for scripts and for agents that cannot hold an MCP session.

The corpus MCP server pays it once per process: `tools/list` returns in 0.3 s (lazy load), the first tool call takes 27 s and 2.1 GB, and warm calls then take 150–400 ms (840 ms for `docs_search` with `include: ["claims"]`).

**`delta` paging repeats the full cost per page.** A worklist of 166,025 entries at the 256-entry page maximum is about 650 calls of about 20 s each, roughly 3.6 hours to read once.

Host: 10 cores, 32 GB, load average 14–22 during the measurements (other work running). Absolute numbers will be lower on an idle host, but every read costs the same as or more than a build.

## Proposal
1. Let CLI reads reuse a verified state the same way the MCP server does (#1554's stat-stamped freshness): for example a `--freshness-stamp FILE` or a cache keyed by artifact SHA-256, builder and pinned input digests, so a second read of an unchanged artifact skips re-derivation.
2. Let `delta` (and `inventory`) stream the whole result once, for example `--format jsonl` with no page limit or a file output, instead of one full re-derivation per 256 entries.
3. Report where read time goes (re-derivation, index build, query), so callers can tell a slow host from a slow phase.
4. Look at memory: a read peaks at 1.8–2.0 GB for a 95 MB artifact, more than the build itself.
title: GH #1598: docs corpus CLI reads re-derive the artifact every call (~25 s, 1.8 GB)

acceptanceCriteria: A test amends a map to rename an imported ticket's source item and then re-imports; it either updates the mapped ticket or the amendment is refused naming the conflict, and fails on PR #1631's head.

body: Found by the Codex review of PR #1630 (finding 3) and confirmed applicable to PR #1631 by its repair report (head 05ab1ba72). `corvint-tasks import amend-map` (CTS-V0-020/021) accepts changing (queue, BF-1) -> ticket BF-1 into (queue, NEW-1) -> ticket BF-1. The importer still derives the target ticket id from sourceItemId, so a later import builds ticket ...:NEW-1, which the map check refuses: the amendment succeeds but its advertised re-import path is unusable. Expected: either resolve the mapped target before lookup/construction (including references), or refuse a source-item rename for an already imported ticket fail-closed with a named conflict. Actual: amendment commits; re-import refuses.

acceptanceCriteria: A test injects a failing program transition on the WORKTREE_REMOVE write and retries CleanupWorktrees on the same Workflow; no checkout is removed without a durable WORKTREE_REMOVE record, and the test fails on the current code.
