body: From the Codex review of PR #1632 (finding 4), checked against PR #1631 head 05ab1ba72: internal/tasks/store/workflow.go persistFenced sets w.program.Phase before programTransition and reloads the authoritative record only when fenced. After an unfenced failed or ambiguous write (for example the write entering WORKTREE_REMOVE), a retry of CleanupWorktrees on the same Workflow sees a phase that was never committed and can settle/remove a checkout with no durable pending-removal record, or skip settlement that is still required on disk. Expected: after any unsuccessful or ambiguous transition, reload authoritative program state (or keep the phase unchanged) before further effects. Inferred from static review; not reproduced.
title: Program workflow: unfenced persist sets the in-memory phase before the write, so a failed write leaves memory ahead of the store

acceptanceCriteria: A Linux run of TestPSRV0055_PoolAcquireLoad at 45,000 receipts with 8 acquirers shows no ENOSPC failures, with peak inotify watch count retained.
Per-guard inotify watch count is bounded independently of receipt count, with a regression test.
body:
Found by V1-2442 (V1-1569 pool-acquire qualification), WSL2/Linux, Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, sha 0641ad2e0, Go 1.27.2.

Observed: TestPSRV0055_PoolAcquireLoad at 45,000 receipts, 8 acquirers: 122 calls failed with 'no space left on device' (acquire 62, claim 53, pool-release 7) while the disk was 2% used and inodes 1%. At 10,000 receipts / 90 s there were no errors. Host limits: fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288, max_user_instances=128.

Cause (code-read, strongly supported): authority.WatchChanges (change_guard.go:41) visits every path of the store and change_guard_linux.go:33 calls InotifyAddWatch per path, so each live guard holds O(receipts) watches. inotify_add_watch returns ENOSPC when the per-user watch total is reached. About ten concurrent guards over a ~50k-path store exceed 524288. The fd itself is closed (close()), so this is concurrency x store size, not a leak. V1-0906/V1-1225 bounded descriptors only, not watch count.

Expected: change observation on Linux stays within a bounded number of inotify watches per guard (for example watch directories, not every file, or share one watcher), or degrades to a bounded sweep instead of failing the command.
title: Linux Tasks change guard adds one inotify watch per store path; concurrent guards exhaust max_user_watches (ENOSPC) at 45k receipts

acceptanceCriteria: CodeOf(syscall.ENOSPC-wrapping error) returns RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, covered by a unit test.
The pool-acquire harness report keeps a bounded error detail for failed samples.
body:
Found by V1-2442 on WSL2/Linux at sha 0641ad2e0. wire.CodeOf (internal/tasks/wire/codes.go) maps EMFILE/ENFILE to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (CAL-V0-215) and every other untyped error to MALFORMED. The pool-acquire load at 45k receipts returned 122 MALFORMED results whose error text was 'no space left on device' (inotify_add_watch ENOSPC). MALFORMED tells the caller its request was bad; this is host resource exhaustion and may be retryable.

Expected: syscall.ENOSPC (at least from the change guard) is reported as RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with the path and limit named.

Related: the TestPSRV0055_PoolAcquireLoad harness records only wire.CodeOf(err) in Sample.Code (pool_acquire_load_test.go:386) and drops the error text, so the cause needed a patched diagnostic build to find; keeping a bounded Detail would have shown it in the first run.
title: wire.CodeOf reports ENOSPC (inotify watch limit) as MALFORMED instead of RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED

Coverage is also partial: about 573 test files are build-tagged darwin/linux/unix and 223 carry POSIX file-name suffixes, so passing packages ran only their portable subset. The owner must decide whether 1.0 supports Windows (then the refusals become implementation work) or not (then the tickets filed from V1-2441 reduce to test-skip hygiene, the real path bugs, and a documented UNSUPPORTED statement).

Where production code intentionally refuses Windows, its tests fail rather than skip, so a native Windows run cannot tell real defects from expected refusals. Signature families (packages whose first failure carries it): 'no-follow support' from gitstatus/open-no-follow (19 packages, e.g. cmd/corvint 372 hits, internal/contextindex 580, doccorpus, dogfoodflow, gokernel, tracerecordrepo, worktreeimpact, necessity, touchsurprise, rubyprofile, witness, workqueue, tasks/scopes, liveverify/affected, liveverify/parentverify, genesis, doccompiler, mcp/corpusbridge); 'process-platform-unsupported' from internal/procgroup (16: procgroup, benchmarks, benchmarks/dogfood-measure, benchmarks/runner, conformance/cli-parity-v0, companionrelease, extevidence, liveverify/affected/golang, liveverify/mutate, opencodequalification, testacceptance, testsupport, update, tools/compat-trial*, tools/cw-trial; benchmarks/selfuse-batch re-panics); 'unsupported on this platform' (observations, trace, tasks/defects, tasks/supervisor, unplannedread, cmd/corvint-test-runner); publish lock 'cannot be opened' (cem/workflow 86 hits, lrfrepo, conformance/ocm-v0, frontiernextrepo, tools/cem-citation-baseline); 'platform has no qualified safe opening boundary'/UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM (tasks/service, tasks/store, tasks/obligation, tasks/cli dispatch); 'unsupported work source platform' (worksource, cmd/corvint-work-queue); unsupported-watch-platform (docmaintain); file-transport-platform-unsupported (cmd/corvint-postmerge-connect); 'unsupported platform' (cmd/corvint-go-test-provider, liveverify/provider); NOT_RUN 'observed on Darwin and Linux only' (cem/cli, console); 'dispatch is supported only on darwin and linux' (tasks/dispatch); unsupported receipt platform (cmd/corvint-js-test-provider, testvaliditydoc); release gate 'Windows Git descendant containment is unavailable' (releasegate). internal/scopelease TestStaleLockContentionGrantsAtMostOneLease (SCL-V0-008, lease_test.go:363): with 32 goroutines contending for a stale lock, Acquire returns 'scopelease: create lease lock: open ...\.corvint\leases\.lock: Access is denied.' instead of ErrConflict/ErrLockBusy. Expected: an approval-decision event in the exec JSON stream, or a documented stable rollout contract Corvint may read. Actual: only the session file. acceptanceCriteria: The test spawns a leader whose lifetime does not depend on the host /bin/sleep implementation (for example the test binary re-executed with the hostile argv0) and asserts the leader is alive (not state Z) before parsing /proc.
The test passes on a rust-coreutils host (Ubuntu 26.04 / WSL2) and on a GNU-coreutils Linux host, with the run retained.
The parser assertions (comm with spaces/parens, ppid, pgrp) are unchanged.
body: Observed 2026-10-23 on the Windows host under WSL2 Linux (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, go1.27.2, commit 368b80d) during the V1-2323 proof run. In interop/cem01-go, a full go test ./... fails TestStableLinuxProcStatParsesHostileCommandName (stable_process_linux_test.go). Ubuntu 26.04 ships /bin/sleep as the rust-coreutils multicall binary, which dispatches on argv0. It refuses the hostile command name and exits at once, so the test leader is a zombie (state Z) by the time the test reads /proc/<pid>/stat. The parser read ppid and pgrp correctly. The failure comes from the fixture assuming a GNU-coreutils sleep, not from a parser defect. Expected: the test controls its own long-lived leader independent of the host coreutils, for example a re-exec of the test binary under the hostile argv0. Actual: FAIL on rust-coreutils hosts. Evidence: C:\cvq\proof\V1-2323\RESULT.md on the Windows host (sha256 9b0e5ea9310ea59b46a058f9d2cc73c169454601ecc1358e6aecb7c842b69bc0).
title: cem01-go TestStableLinuxProcStatParsesHostileCommandName assumes /bin/sleep accepts a hostile argv0 (fails on Ubuntu 26.04 rust-coreutils)

acceptanceCriteria: The temp filesystem type of the GitHub-hosted go-product shard and of the box runners/offload host is observed and recorded
Either the box runners and heavy.sh offload set TMPDIR to an ext4 directory matching the hosted runner, or the difference is declared where lanes and CI owners read it
body: Observed 2026-10-24 while fixing V1-2554. The Windows-box WSL2 host (Ubuntu 26.04, Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2) mounts /tmp as tmpfs (findmnt -T /tmp) and leaves TMPDIR unset, so every t.TempDir() in heavy.sh offload runs and, by inference, in the self-hosted runners corvint-box-1..8 lives on tmpfs. The GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 shards run their tests from an ext4-backed temp directory (inferred from TestCALV0070 passing there). tmpfs differs from ext4 in at least one way tests assert: a write through a new shared mmap updates no mtime/ctime on tmpfs (probe: /tmp and /dev/shm no, $HOME ext4 yes). V1-2554 fixed that one test with a statfs TMPFS_MAGIC precondition (PSR-V0-226). Expected: the box runners and the offload host either reproduce the hosted runner's temp filesystem (for example TMPDIR on the ext4 root in the runner service env and rt.sh) or the divergence is recorded as a declared host difference, so a box-only failure is not mistaken for a product bug and a hosted-only behaviour is not silently untested once go-product-shard moves to the box. Actual: undeclared divergence; the hosted runner's temp filesystem type is not recorded anywhere.
title: Box test hosts run with /tmp on tmpfs while GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners use ext4: filesystem-dependent tests diverge

Expected: an owner decision whether records admitted by another toolchain of the same derivation are trustworthy enough to reuse (engine is part of the admitted derivation today). Actual: full rebuild, by design.
title: docs corpus build --artifact: decide whether an artifact of an earlier Go toolchain or engine may reuse records

body:
Observed (confirmed bug): scheduled release-gates run 40088201429, job 120855323138 (linux-core, HLQ-V1 step) on main 73f0af89b, host claude-code 2.1.267, adapter corvint@corvint 0.3.6, Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 745. The claude-code tuple FAILs 7/9: discovery 'Stop registers 2 commands, not one'; context/degradation/upgrade 'no SessionStart hook registered'; expansion 'no UserPromptSubmit hook registered'; change/frontier 'discovery did not complete'. cli and codex tuples PASS 9/9.

Cause (from code): 88ba3616e (AHI-190..199, 2026-10-23) added a second Stop command 'corvint adapter claude-code stop-done-list' to integrations/claude-code/plugins/corvint/hooks/hooks.json. conformance/host-lifecycle-v1 readHooks maps each event to exactly one command and errors otherwise, and HLQ-V1-002's discovery predicate says 'every registered hook event runs exactly one command'. Discovery therefore never sets r.hooks, and every later hook case fails with a misleading 'no <event> hook registered'. The host pin (2.1.267 in release-gates.yml since ff1112718, 2026-09-26) did not change; the host's hook discovery is not involved (the harness reads the installed hooks.json, HLQ-V1-004).

Expected: discovery accepts the accepted AHI-191 registration, checks the exact (event, adapter subcommand) set, and the Stop cases run the 'stop' command. Part of GitHub #1551.
title: HLQ-V1 claude-code discovery fails: Stop registers two commands (stop, stop-done-list), every hook case reports no hook registered

acceptanceCriteria: A fixture question naming a one-word subject ranks it first, or the idea is closed with measured evidence that it regresses existing fixtures.

body: DCP-V1-543 (lane claude/gh1665-rank-leftovers, GitHub #1665) ranks a subject in tier named only when its non-prose name has at least two identifier words held contiguously by a question-shaped query. A question naming a one-word subject ("How does Waitlist work?") still ranks by terms alone, so question words can still outrank it. One-word names were excluded because common words would promote too many subjects. Idea: allow a single-word name when it is capitalized in the query or rare by idf, measured on the #1665 fixtures and the #1597 fixture with no frozen outcome change.

acceptanceCriteria: A PID that disappears between enumeration and read is re-checked and dropped as exited; other read errors still fail closed, with tests for both
The collector tests pass 9/9 under a concurrent process-churn loop on the linux/WSL2 box
Spec row amended with the vanished-PID rule, failure modes and rollback
body: Found on the self-hosted box shards of PR #1689 (2026-10-24, WSL2 Ubuntu, go1.27.3, 8 runners on one host). LinuxProcfs* and HostCollectorV2 tests fail with 'final sweep has read failures': the sweep reads /proc/<pid> after the process exited. Repro: passes idle 3/3, fails 9/9 with a /bin/true churn loop in the same PID namespace. Hosted runners rarely see unrelated short-lived processes. Orchestrator decision: a PID that vanished between enumeration and read (ENOENT/ESRCH on its /proc entry, confirmed gone on re-check) is dropped as exited, not counted as a read failure; any other read error still fails the sweep.
title: postmergeproof Linux procfs collectors fail 'final sweep has read failures' when a swept PID exits mid-sweep (shared PID namespace)

acceptanceCriteria: New DCP-V1 requirements define a split-safe parallel or vectorised scan with adversarial tests for strings, escapes and nesting across split points and unchanged refusal order
Warm CLI gaps and flow p50 measured below 170 ms on the DCP-V1-418 fixture on linux/amd64, with peak RSS still within the DCP-V1-430 bound
Existing DCP-V1-410..419 and 430..434 tests pass unchanged
body: Observed 2026-10-24, lane claude/p1-perf-1024 at origin/main 0949876eb, linux/amd64 WSL2 32 threads, DCP-V1-418 fixture (66,752,222-byte artifact). A temporary probe inside decodeArtifactStream showed for 8 warm `docs corpus gaps` reads: sequential scanValue/scanString scan 89-99 ms, worker wait 10-15 ms, chunk concat 6-7 ms, skeleton compare 4-5 ms; index 30 ms, query 12 ms. CPU profile: the scan goroutine is 88 ms CPU per read; more decode workers or a faster deriveClaimTerms cannot shorten it. Result: V1-2477 target 1 (warm flow/gaps p50 < 200 ms) holds on quiet linux with only 6-11 ms margin on gaps (p50 188.7-194.3 ms) and fails on darwin under load (~290 ms). Expected: the boundary scan parallelised or vectorised so warm reads keep a robust margin. Constraint: keep the closed-decoder refusal order (DCP-V1-431) and the byte-equality argument (DCP-V1-414, DCP-V1-419) across chunk splits (a string can span a split point). Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-24-corpus-read-target-and-affected-guide.md (PR from claude/p1-perf-1024). Part of GH #1598 / V1-2477.
title: Docs corpus read: the single-goroutine boundary scan in decodeArtifactStream is the warm-read critical path (89-99 ms of ~185 ms)

acceptanceCriteria: Owner records a decision accepting or rejecting a default affected cache location, with the invariant 4 consequence
If accepted: an AFP-V0 requirement block, invariant 4 amendment, and tests showing the plan is byte-identical with and without the default cache
body: GH #1601 re-test on main-368b80d: warm `corvint affected --cache DIR` met the target (1.8 s vs 8.6 s uncached) but reuse is opt-in, and AFP-V0-390..397 list a default cache location as a non-goal. AFP-V0-431 (lane claude/p1-perf-1024, 2026-10-24) only adds guide advice to pass --cache and batch paths. A default location would make a read command write state, which AGENTS.md invariant 4 forbids unless an accepted spec admits it as a bounded private ledger. Owner decision needed. Candidate design: a cache under the repository's Git common dir or the user cache dir (os.UserCacheDir()/corvint/affected), keyed exactly as --cache is now (executable identity, root, walked-file stat pins), private 0700, one entry per root, with an opt-out flag and doctor visibility; invariant 4 amended to name it. Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-24-corpus-read-target-and-affected-guide.md. Part of GH #1601 / V1-2473.
title: Question: should corvint affected get a default --cache location (opt-in reuse leaves agents at ~9-11 s per --path call)?

acceptanceCriteria: The Pi tasks-host gate-interruption test passes 5 consecutive runs under host load, with REDO_PENDING either avoided or reconciled as pending-operation.
A test covers a native gate run killed after its receipt commit and before the head apply, and shows the adapter outcome is pending-operation.
body: Found by V1-2506 (lane p1-tasks-correct, 2026-10-24, macOS arm64, Go 1.27.2, branch claude/p1-tasks-correct-1024). With CTS-V0-026 the MALFORMED 'unassigned stage slot' refusal after an aborted gate run is gone, but integrations/pi/tasks-host.test.mjs 'PWV actual native gate interruption retains uncertainty' (run from the repo root with CORVINT_TASKS_BIN set) still failed 5 of 12 classified runs under host load. Every failure was a retryable REDO_PENDING with staging empty. Cause: the Pi adapter sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL 100 ms later (integrations/pi/runtime.js:73, process.js:23). When the SIGKILL lands between the receipt commit and the head.json apply, the store is in the designed crash state. Reads wait out the pending window and then refuse REDO_PENDING; they never redo (TM-V0-008, invariant 4). No writer runs before the wrapper's reconciliation reads, so the adapter returns reconciliation-unavailable instead of pending-operation. Expected: an aborted native gate run is reconciled as pending-operation. Options: (a) the Pi adapter gives native writer commands their CAL-V0-319 bounded interrupted-record time before SIGKILL; (b) Pi reconciliation treats REDO_PENDING as pending-operation evidence, or runs a native writer such as reconcile to redo; (c) a native read-through of a pending receipt, which needs an owner decision on invariant 4 and TM-V0-008.
title: Pi adapter: a gate run SIGKILLed after its receipt commit leaves REDO_PENDING, so Pi reconciliation reads fail and the interruption test flakes

A regression test reproduces the 13-path refusal shape and passes after the fix
body: Observed on V1-2322/V1-2323 lane p1-cem (PR #1703, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 746, SEAL adda562c8). The touched-anchored predicate refused tier-below-anchored over all touched paths: 13 paths (6 new artifacts/runner-{plan,receipt}-N.json, new Go files core_stable_readiness.go/_test.go, READINESS.json, tools/cem-release-suites main.go/main_test.go/readiness.test.mjs, core_stable_result_test.go) cannot anchor because CEM-V1-081 anchoring needs a BASE span naming the path (impossible for a new path) or an added requirement-ID definition line (impossible in JSON and receipts). GRANT was only reachable by setting effects.verdictPaths to the 7 anchorable paths, which removes the core implementation from the verdict. Expected: a new file or a committed runner artifact can reach anchored through an admitted basis (e.g. a cited span naming the new path in the same change's spec, or a runner receipt that executed it). Distinct from V1-1840 (no-governed-hunk) and V1-2360 (propose-citations fallback).
title: cem-verdict touched-anchored cannot anchor new files or committed runner artifacts, so verdictPaths must exclude the core change

acceptanceCriteria: make cem-release-gate observes corvint:repository-envelope and cem01-go:repository-envelope as PASSED against the built binaries, or the owner amends READINESS.json with a recorded reason
A test pins that a failing binary envelope run is refused
body: tools/cem-release-suites (PR #1703, V1-2323) runs the sealed repository-envelope suite only at source level; the corvint:repository-envelope and cem01-go:repository-envelope rows are always NOT_RUN because the envelope cells are prose recipes rebuilt in process. READINESS.json requires both rows, so make cem-release-gate refuses release-runner-incomplete on every run (observed 2026-10-24 on darwin/arm64, output sha 00cf64b2…). Expected: an executable binary-level envelope recipe so both release binaries are exercised, or an owner-accepted amendment of the required rows.
title: cem-release-gate reports binary-level repository-envelope rows NOT_RUN, so the release gate can never pass

acceptanceCriteria: A readiness aggregation reads per-platform release-run outputs for one revision and refuses mismatched revisions or binary sets
Both platform rows can be observed PASSED from two runs
A real-lifecycle runner receipt set is produced on linux/amd64 as well
body: StableReleaseReadiness (CEM-V1-601, PR #1703) judges one run, and a run observes only its build platform. READINESS.json requires linux/amd64 and darwin/arm64, so no single run can be ready. There is no aggregation of per-platform release-run outputs bound to the same revision and binary digests. The V1-2322 real lifecycle runner receipts were also produced on darwin/arm64 only; the WSL2 linux/amd64 box was not used for them.
title: cem release readiness: one gate run observes one platform; add a cross-platform aggregation of release runs

acceptanceCriteria: A CI job runs make cem-release-gate on both platforms and its output is retained
Owner ci-control-plane approval is recorded
body: PR #1703 (V1-2323) adds make cem-release-gate (Makefile/script only); lanes may not edit .github. A CI job should build corvint and interop/cem01-go from the same checkout and run make cem-release-gate on linux/amd64 and macOS arm64, failing on nonzero exit. Needs owner ci-control-plane approval.
title: NEEDS-OWNER: wire make cem-release-gate into CI on linux/amd64 and darwin/arm64

A test covers the missing and refused cases

A release candidate can therefore be judged ready without the cem/1.0 stable readiness outcome.
title: releasecandidate ReadinessRecord does not carry the cem/1.0 release-gate outcome

acceptanceCriteria: A failing-first test passes `url.parse(s, true).query` and `dotenv.parse(s)` as test details in a spec and shows whether the closure stays exact.
If it does, the closure stops and names the line; otherwise the ticket closes with the test as evidence.
body: SUSPECTED, not reproduced. Found while fixing GH #1701 (PR #1706, base a681846). playwrightTagNeutralModules (internal/liveverify/affected/typescript/playwright_tag_sources.go:146) treats `url`, `dotenv` and `dotenv/config` as neutral. But `url.parse('/?tag=@x', true).query` and `dotenv.parse('tag=@x')` return an object with a `tag` property, and neither the identifier `tag` nor any playwrightTagIndirection name appears in the code. Expected: a details value built that way cannot leave the tag closure exact. Actual: NOT_OBSERVED, because whether the details-argument rule already refuses a non-literal details value was not checked.
title: Suspected: Playwright tag closure trusts neutral modules (url, dotenv) that can build a `tag` key without a reflective name

acceptanceCriteria: The spec names the binding-provenance rule and the monkeypatch guard before any implementation.
Failing-first tests show a reflective name inside a proven test body leaves the closure exact, and that the same body under a rebound or rewritten `test` still stops.
body: Idea from GH #1701 (PR #1706). Playwright's listing never runs test or hook bodies, so a reflective name such as `Object.entries` or `JSON.parse` inside one cannot change titles or tags. TJAA-V0-090 exempts only a plain JSON.stringify call. Deferring the whole body would need two things: (1) proof that the callee is the @playwright/test `test`/`setup` binding (import provenance, not a name match); (2) a guard against code anywhere in the closure that rewrites `test` members such as `test.describe` or `test.extend` (monkeypatching). Without both, deferral would invent certainty.
title: Idea: defer the Playwright tag-closure reflective rule inside test and hook bodies, given binding provenance

acceptanceCriteria: A static regex testMatch whose match cannot depend on directories above the repository resolves in path mode, with failing-first tests.
An unanchored regex, or one that can reach above the repository root, keeps the testMatch site.
body: Idea from GH #1701 (PR #1706). TJAA-V0-091 resolves only quoted, root-free literal string globs in a project testMatch; a regular-expression testMatch such as /global-setup\.ts/ still raises typescript:executable-config-unresolved at the testMatch line in path mode. Discovery already has playwrightRegexBodyStatic for a static regex subset. Playwright tests a regex against the absolute path, so a regex that is not anchored to a repository-relative suffix depends on the checkout location.
title: Idea: resolve static regular-expression project testMatch in Playwright path mode

acceptanceCriteria: Fallback and refusal records carry a bounded start-error class without changing the stable public message
A test asserts the field for an ETXTBSY and an ENOENT start
body: Observed 2026-10-24 (lane p1-flakes, CI run 40048074466 shard 3): WQO-V0-042 failed with 'immutable acquisition fell back to worktree: error=Git error: cannot start Git'. The cause was ETXTBSY on a wrapper just written by a parallel test (fixed in PR claude/p1-flakes-1024 via internal/execfile), but the public message gave no errno, so the diagnosis took a reproduction. GitFailureDetails(err) already carries StartError/Stderr; only the test now prints it. Expected: the fallback/refusal record names the start error class (ETXTBSY, ENOENT, EACCES) in a bounded diagnostic field while the stable public message bytes stay unchanged. Actual: bare 'cannot start Git'. Version: Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 746 tree 0949876.
title: contextindex: 'Git error: cannot start Git' hides the start errno and stderr from the operator

acceptanceCriteria: Production work captures retain a bounded ADAPTER_FAILED cause reason
The 250 ms drain and 1 s reap bounds are either justified under 4 vCPU load or changed with reasoning recorded
body: Suspected, not confirmed (lane p1-flakes 2026-10-24, V1-2476). cmd/corvint/work_runner.go maps a nonzero adapter exit, 'process residue' after the 1 s reap bound and 'incomplete pipe capture' after the 250 ms post-reap drain bound to ADAPTER_FAILED without recording which; tests assert stderr stays empty. The lane added observeWorkCause so the final-check test names the cause, but a production capture still records a bare code. Under a starved CI host a 250 ms drain bound can expire while the pipe still holds output. Expected: the capture or refusal record retains a bounded cause reason (and the drain/reap bound that expired); the bound itself may need a load-justified value with the reasoning recorded. Actual: ADAPTER_FAILED alone. Reproduction: not reproduced at base under taskset -c 0-3 -race -count=20 (PASS); keep as suspected.
title: work runner: ADAPTER_FAILED causes (nonzero exit, process residue, incomplete pipe capture) are not surfaced in any retained record

acceptanceCriteria: No *_test.go outside internal/execfile writes an executable with os.WriteFile
A repository check refuses a new executable os.WriteFile in tests, listed with the other doc gates
body: Follow-up to PR #1707 (lane p1-flakes, 2026-10-24). internal/execfile.WriteFile holds syscall.ForkLock for reading so a script written and then executed by the test process cannot fail ETXTBSY when a parallel test forks (WQO-V0-093). PR #1707 converted the fixtures in internal/contextindex, cmd/corvint/work_* and conformance/mcp-2026-07-28 only. 22 executable os.WriteFile(..., 0o7xx) test fixtures remain in internal/tasks/store (2), cmd/corvint-test-runner (2), cmd/corvint-go-test-provider (2), cmd/corvint (2, non-work files), tools/corvint-pr-tests, internal/testrunner, internal/tasks/supervisor, internal/tasks/cli and others (grep: os\.WriteFile\([^)]*0(o7[0-7][0-7]|755|700)\) in *_test.go). Each is the same latent flake under -race -p 1 CI shards; a sweep plus an unbounded-readers-style check that refuses new executable os.WriteFile calls in tests would close the class. Reproduction of the mechanism: internal/execfile TestWriteFileExcludesForkInheritance control subtest (about 10 % ETXTBSY on WSL2 Linux).
title: Sweep the 22 remaining write-then-exec test fixtures to execfile.WriteFile and refuse new ones

acceptanceCriteria: Warm CLI docs flow and docs gaps p50 < 170 ms on the DCP-V1-418 fixture on linux/amd64, n=20 interleaved against the base binary, with host load average recorded on a quiet host
Peak RSS within the DCP-V1-430 234 MB bound
Decode results, digest tails and refusals byte-identical to the base (TestDCPV1552ParallelScanMatchesSequential and DCP-V1-410..419, 430..434 tests pass unchanged)
No new on-disk state or format change
body:
Found by lane p1-scan (V1-2571, PR #1708, head 66aa6dc2b, base a68184603), part of V1-2477 target 1 / GitHub #1598.

After DCP-V1-551 moved the split-member boundary scan into parallel segments (claims scan 36.1 -> 8.5 ms in process, darwin load ~5), instrumented phase timings show the main goroutine in decodeArtifactStream blocking on dispatch to saturated decode workers for about 46-62 ms. The workers spend about 170 ms CPU per decode of the DCP-V1-418 fixture on json v2 Unmarshal plus the EncodeTo canonical comparison, and reflect.MakeSlice on the dispatch path (with its page faults) is the next serial cost. Streamed decode only fell 75.7 -> 65.5 ms.

Expected: warm CLI docs flow and docs gaps p50 < 170 ms on linux/amd64 (V1-2571 target). Actual (n=20 interleaved, linux/WSL2 box load 22-26): flow p50 239 -> 258 ms, gaps p50 289 -> 287 ms; darwin load 24-119 within noise. Hosts were saturated by peer lanes, so a quiet-host qualification is also needed.

Levers to evaluate: cheaper canonical check (compare encoded bytes without a full re-encode, or decode straight into preallocated element storage), avoiding per-batch MakeSlice, and fewer allocations in the claim decode. Keep byte-identical results and the DCP-V1-414/419 refusal order; no new on-disk state (that is V1-2572).
title: Docs corpus read: decode-worker CPU (JSON unmarshal + canonical re-encode) and dispatch MakeSlice are the warm-read critical path after the parallel boundary scan

acceptanceCriteria: A run whose test fails because a subprocess executable cannot be found records a named problem (or diagnostic) identifying the undeclared tool, distinct from an ordinary test failure
A focused test pins the behavior; docs for request tools show the git example
body: Observed 2026-10-24, lane p1-cem2, WSL2 linux/amd64 go1.27.3, at commit 27e9d98 (PR #1710). The runner passes no host PATH. A plan for tools/cem-release-suites (tests run git via exec.Command) was admitted, and the run recorded 3 tests FAILED. Only after git was declared in request tools ({"git":{"executable":"/usr/bin/git","sha256":...}}) and --tools was passed on both plan and run did all 7 tests pass. Expected: the receipt names the missing executable as a problem (or plan admission warns about undeclared tools), so that a host-tool gap is not read as a test failure. Actual: plain test FAILED states, with the cause visible only in the test output.
title: corvint-test-runner runs a go test that shells out to git with no PATH, and reports FAILED tests instead of naming the undeclared tool

acceptanceCriteria: Reproduction confirms or refutes path-dependent output
If it is confirmed, the documented build of corvint-test-runner for receipts is -trimpath and reproducible, and a test or recorded check shows equal digests from two roots
body: Suspected, not confirmed. Lane p1-cem2 on 2026-10-24 (WSL2 linux/amd64 go1.27.3) rebuilt corvint-test-runner for each receipt run, and the executable sha256 differed between builds of the same commit in different roots. Inference: the build omits -trimpath, so the embedded paths vary. This makes --executable-sha256 pins unstable across hosts. Reproduce: build cmd/corvint-test-runner at one commit in two different directories and compare the sha256 values.
title: Suspected: corvint-test-runner binaries built for receipts are not byte-reproducible across checkout roots

acceptanceCriteria: The catalog emits each (kind, id, reason) unadmitted row at most once, with a test on the overlay fixture.
The catalog digest change is recorded and CompilerVersion bumped if compile outputs change.
body: Observed 2026-10-24 in lane p1-cce-2 (branch claude/p1-cce2-1024, stacked on PR #1702 head c4ec0f3) while building CCE-V0-111 on the internal/changee2e overlay fixture: the catalog's unadmitted list holds `path:edge:screen:admin:app.home->screen:admin:app.clubs.teesheets` with reason `edge-unproven` three times. Expected: one row per (kind, id, reason), as the catalog digest and obligations reasons are meant to be canonical. Actual: duplicates, likely one per flow step or flow that crosses the edge. Effect: inflated unadmitted counts in catalog/compile reports; no verdict change observed. Reproduce: the vocabulary test fixture (vocabularyRepo in internal/changee2e/vocabulary_test.go) and list Catalog.Unadmitted for KindPath.
title: changee2e catalog repeats one path:edge unadmitted row (edge-unproven) three times

acceptanceCriteria: A before/after TestCALV0263_LeaseGateLoad report at 40k receipts on WSL2, with n and p50/p99, shows widen and reap wall p99 below 2 s with no gate-hold regression.
A test proves that the reused base state is the one the gate re-validates before commit.
body: Observed by lane p1-tasks-latency on 2026-10-24 (branch claude/p1-tasks-latency-1024, base 0949876eb). Platform: WSL2 Ubuntu on the Windows box, Ryzen 9 5950X, go1.27.3. TestCALV0263_LeaseGateLoad at 40k receipts, 15 writers, 120 s runs, both QUALIFIED (load <= 12). Widen wall p50/p99 was 14.3/47.9 s on base and 11.0/11.5 s on head, and reap wall was 13.7/45.9 s on base and 10.8/11.4 s on head. Gate hold p99 was only 63-195 ms. Per-phase timing puts almost all of the wall in SnapshotReadMS (18-48 s), a full base audit of the receipt history in a fresh process before the gate. Heartbeat, renew and claim do not pay it, because their writer route reuses the checkpoint. Expected: widen and reap reuse a verified writer checkpoint or segment seal, so their wall scales with the tail, not the history. Actual: every widen/reap pays a full-history read. Proof reports: /mnt/c/cvq/proof/2026-10-24/p1-tasks-latency/lease-{base,head}-{5,6}.json on the box. Related but distinct: the JSG-V0-011 segmented-store resume ticket (SNAPSHOT_MOVED) and V1-2537 (gate hold).
title: Tasks widen/reap wall is 11-48 s at 40k receipts: the fresh-process base snapshot read runs outside the lease gate

acceptanceCriteria: The TestPSRV0055_PoolAcquireLoad report records the peak inotify watch count per process and summed across processes on Linux, read in-process with no external sampler.
A Linux run at 45,000 receipts and 8 acquirers retains that peak in the build log for V1-2482.
body: V1-2482 acceptance item 1 needs the peak inotify watch count retained for a 45,000-receipt, 8-acquirer Linux run. The harness report (CORVINT_TASKS_POOL_ACQUIRE_LOAD) has only `watch max` in ms. Lanes may not run an external /proc fdinfo sampler, because the lane hook refuses sleep loops. Observed in lane p1-tasks-redo on 2026-10-24 (linux/amd64 WSL2, go1.27.3, commit d8eb9e072 stacked on #1704): the run passed with 0 ENOSPC; peak watches NOT_OBSERVED, derived as about 9 per guard from TestPSRV0222. Expected: each worker process reports its own inotify watches (from /proc/self/fdinfo inotify lines, read at each guard open), and the report carries the per-process and summed peak. Actual: there is no watch count in the report.
title: TestPSRV0055_PoolAcquireLoad does not record the peak inotify watch count, so V1-2482's acceptance cannot be retained from a lane run

acceptanceCriteria: `corvint how GOAL --source DIR` output is byte-identical to `corvint flows appmap how --request GOAL --source DIR` in a CLI test
help, usage and `make capability-catalog` list the alias; spec site-knowledge-howto-v0 records it with a requirement ID and test
body: Stage 6 (V1-1903, PR #1714) ships the how query as `corvint flows appmap how --request GOAL --source DIR` and the corvint.map_knowledge MCP view. The spec's job statement asks "how do I X", but there is no top-level `corvint how` command, so agents must know the nested flows/appmap path. Expected: `corvint how GOAL [--source DIR]` prints the same site-knowledge-how/0 bytes as the nested command (alias, no second implementation), listed in help and the capability catalog. Actual (branch claude/p1-skhb-1024 @ 59c980532): `corvint how` is an unknown command. Observed while delivering V1-1903.
title: Site knowledge: add the top-level `corvint how GOAL` alias for `flows appmap how`

acceptanceCriteria: a live run on a host with the pinned tuple records site-knowledge-proof-evidence/0 for at least one generated draft, retained with host, versions and digests
`corvint-test e2e how-accept --evidence` over that file yields a receipt whose first failing condition (or verdict) is not `infrastructure`, cited in a build-log entry
body: V1-1905 (PR #1714, 623d4b8aa) delivers SKH-V0-163..176 offline: internal/skhproof and `corvint-test e2e how-accept` assess recorded site-knowledge-proof-evidence/0. The live run of SKH-V0-080/082 (repeated runs, validity, mutants, controls) is NEEDS-HOST: neither the lane host nor the WSL2 runner carries the pinned tuple, so every shipped receipt reads `infrastructure` with `live-run-not-recorded`. Related host blocker: V1-2389 (headless-shell 1248 missing). Expected: a recorded evidence file from a live run over the first-adopter fixture, and a receipt that reaches past `infrastructure`.
title: Site knowledge 8: run the acceptance pipeline live under the pinned Playwright 1.64.0 / Node v24.11.1 / headless shell 1248 tuple

acceptanceCriteria: the owning spec (PWP, RVN or AMSP) records the selector/method witness shape with requirement IDs
internal/skhproof verifies a witnessed selector binding in a test and still reads binding-unverified without a witness
body: SKH-V0-089 needs selector and method witnesses from the PWP, RVN and AMSP contracts. Those amendments are not made, so the stage 8 pipeline (V1-1905, PR #1714) reports every selector and method binding as `binding-unverified`, and no generated test can read confidently. This is an owner question on which contract owns the witness and its wire shape, followed by the amendment itself.
title: Site knowledge: amend PWP/RVN/AMSP witnesses so SKH-V0-089 selector and method bindings can verify

acceptanceCriteria: Path mode does not raise executable-config-unresolved for a literal testMatch; any remaining reason names the computed key and line.
A computed index into a fresh local array (split, map, array literal) does not stop the tag closure; failing-first tests from the issue repro.
Spec amended with new TJAA requirement IDs; PR body says Part of #1717.
body: Filed from https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1717 (2026-10-24), follow-up to #1701 (V1-2576) re-tested on main ec41e4e. (1) Path mode flags literal testMatch at playwright.config.ts:120 as typescript:executable-config-unresolved; the site should name the computed dependencies, and path mode should not need dependencies. (2) Tag closure stops at the computed index each.split(';')[index]; a computed index on a fresh local array (split/map/array literal) is tag-free. 303 units stay omission-unverified.
title: GH #1717: affected (Playwright): path mode still flags literal testMatch as executable-config-unresolved; tag closure stops at computed index on a fresh local array

acceptanceCriteria: Query coverage ignores stop/low-IDF words; general search recovers to at least the prior 64-row baseline on the issue corpus or a recorded fixture.
id-slug phrases reach the named/path-phrase tier; single-word matches do not enter the named tier; tests.
Declaration derivation is partial up to a named bound, records dropped counts, and the gap names bound/value/count without an arbitrary file; double compile removed or explained.
PR body says Part of #1665.
body: Filed from the 2026-10-24 17:36 re-test comment on https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/1665 (main ec41e4e): exact-file 22/24, claims 45/52, general search regressed to 59/64. (1) Coverage counts filler words (where, source, implemented); count content words only (stop list or IDF). (2) An id-slug phrase (reservation-cancellation) does not reach the named/path-phrase tier, and the named tier admits one-word matches (V1-2568 residue). (3) Multi-repo declarations (V1-2567 / DCP-V1-549) derive 0 on a large corpus; the gap 'derived declaration bound' names no bound, value or count and attaches to an arbitrary file. Derive up to the bound and record what was dropped (or allow path/kind restriction); the gap names the bound. Build compiles twice (15.1 s vs 10.9 s).
title: GH #1665 re-test: search coverage counts stop words, id-slug phrases miss named tier, multi-repo declarations derive 0 with an unnamed bound

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three omission cases (narrowed receipt inventory, omitted receipt or failed rerun, selection narrower than `corvint affected`) is tried against the native verifier and interop/cem01-go with a reproducible fixture, and the observed verdict is recorded.

If any case yields a clean verdict, a BUG ticket (milestone v1-0, labels agent-memory, bugs, cem) is filed with the reproduction, expected uncertainty or rejection, and the CEM-V1 requirement it violates; this ticket links it.
If every case already produces uncertainty or rejection, the evidence (test names or commands and outputs) is retained on this ticket and it closes as no-defect.
body:
Source: the expert-audited CEM 2.0 proposal of 2026-10-24 (five reviewers, all CONCERNS; revised plan published privately at https://claude.ai/artifact/QhbSmihmftUL6WtKrgMRRB). The proposal is not accepted intent (AGENTS.md invariant 8); the owner filed this split on 2026-10-24: discovery spike and 1.0 inventory-completeness check in v1-0, everything else post-1-0 under one umbrella.

Suspected soundness gap, not a confirmed bug. The supply-chain trust reviewer noted that digest and hash links prove what a map includes, not that nothing was left out. CEM-V1-003/004 already bind a runner receipt's own expected inventory and observed attempts, and incomplete inventory produces uncertainty. The open question is whether the expected inventory is bound to anything the producer does not choose: can a producer (a) pick or rebuild a receipt whose expected inventory excludes a failing test, (b) omit a whole runner receipt or a rerun that FAILED, or (c) select a narrower test set than `corvint affected` would for the same base and target, and still get a clean verdict from the native verifier and interop/cem01-go?
title: CEM 1.0: check whether a map can omit a FAILED run or runner receipt without the verifier noticing

acceptanceCriteria: A pre-registered protocol is committed before any replay result is read: the change set (30-50 changes with a later defect fix, at least one external repository), the baseline, the mutation operators and budget, and the decision rule using owner-set thresholds X (escaped-defect capture over baseline) and Y (false-alarm rate).
The owner sets X and Y in the protocol before the run; until then the ticket stays open with the thresholds named as the blocker.

Results report per change: baseline flag, typed label, whether the later fix touched a flagged unit, false alarms, flagged units, and wall-clock cost; unavailable measurements are NOT_OBSERVED, never estimated.
A build-log entry records the result and an explicit verdict: CONTINUE (CEM 2.0 umbrella proceeds) or KILL (umbrella and children are closed or re-scoped with the evidence cited).
body:
Source: the expert-audited CEM 2.0 proposal of 2026-10-24 (five reviewers, all CONCERNS; revised plan published privately at https://claude.ai/artifact/QhbSmihmftUL6WtKrgMRRB). The proposal is not accepted intent (AGENTS.md invariant 8); the owner filed this split on 2026-10-24: discovery spike and 1.0 inventory-completeness check in v1-0, everything else post-1-0 under one umbrella.

Kill-or-continue experiment for the whole CEM 2.0 thesis, run alongside 1.0 work and shipping nothing. Replay 30-50 historical agent changes that later needed a defect fix (Corvint lanes and at least one external repository). For each changed unit, compute (a) a coverage-diff baseline (changed lines executed by the cited tests) and (b) a prototype typed-discrimination label (discriminated / type-discriminated / weak-test / likely-equivalent / uncovered) from existing `prove --mutate` and `cem verify --hunk-revert` machinery. Measure which approach flags the unit the later fix touched, the false-alarm rate (flagged units with no later defect), flagged units per change, and wall-clock cost per change against the CEM 1.0 dogfood cost.

Related: V1-0836 (three-arm sealed CEM reviewer trial) is the outcome trial that gates any ranking; V1-0573 (criterion-level acceptance experiments).
title: CEM 2.0 discovery replay: does typed per-unit discrimination catch escaped defects a coverage-diff baseline misses?

acceptanceCriteria: Typed held claims are produced for Go changes with every field present or an explicit NOT_PRODUCED(reason).
Fixtures cover an equivalent mutant (likely-equivalent), a revert that breaks the build (type-discriminated), a co-authored test passing at base (not discriminating), and coupled hunks.
Cost per change is measured against the CEM 1.0 dogfood cost and stays at or below it; false-alarm rate is at or below the owner's Y.

Source: the expert-audited CEM 2.0 proposal of 2026-10-24 (five reviewers, all CONCERNS; revised plan published privately at https://claude.ai/artifact/QhbSmihmftUL6WtKrgMRRB). The proposal is not accepted intent (AGENTS.md invariant 8); the owner filed this split on 2026-10-24: discovery spike and 1.0 inventory-completeness check in v1-0, everything else post-1-0 under one umbrella.

Make `held` a structured claim: operator, killing oracle and its provenance, determinism bound (n, epsilon), equivalence screen (Trivial Compiler Equivalence), and coupling set. Labels: discriminated / type-discriminated (revert breaks the build) / weak-test / likely-equivalent / uncovered(reason). Headline names its denominator ('no cited test killed k of N mutants, operators O, bound B'), never 'no test would notice'. A co-authored test discriminates only if it fails at base; only criterion-admitted oracles count. Cost: mutant schemata, subsumption and TCE dedupe, first-kill stop, content-addressed reuse, disclosed sampling; delta debugging over hunk subsets for coupled hunks. Disclosure gate only; any ranking stays advisory until V1-0836's outcome trial admits it. Delivered first on the cem/1.0 wire (phase P1).
title: CEM 2.0 C1: typed discrimination per changed unit with a defined denominator

Source: the expert-audited CEM 2.0 proposal of 2026-10-24 (five reviewers, all CONCERNS; revised plan published privately at https://claude.ai/artifact/QhbSmihmftUL6WtKrgMRRB). The proposal is not accepted intent (AGENTS.md invariant 8); the owner filed this split on 2026-10-24: discovery spike and 1.0 inventory-completeness check in v1-0, everything else post-1-0 under one umbrella.

T1: provenance axis self-reported < signed(keyid) < reproduced < independently-reproduced, orthogonal to the five shipped trust classes plus a new `inherited` class; a same-machine signature is SLSA L1 and never presented as more. T2: reproduction verdicts reproduced / nondeterminism / not-comparable; unreproducible is the honest default outside Go; flake claims carry (n, epsilon). T3: sequence-numbered evidence-ledger tree heads anchored in Git notes, recomputable context packs, verdict binds verifier identity. T4: corvint-trusted-keys/2 with roles, expiry and thresholds; human-review keys need user presence; Tasks ticket authority binds to owner-controlled store provenance. 'Witness' is reserved for independent cosigners.
title: CEM 2.0 T1-T4: reproduction-anchored provenance axis, anti-rollback and corvint-trusted-keys/2

body:
Source: the expert-audited CEM 2.0 proposal of 2026-10-24 (five reviewers, all CONCERNS; revised plan published privately at https://claude.ai/artifact/QhbSmihmftUL6WtKrgMRRB). The proposal is not accepted intent (AGENTS.md invariant 8); the owner filed this split on 2026-10-24: discovery spike and 1.0 inventory-completeness check in v1-0, everything else post-1-0 under one umbrella.

User job: before merging an agent's change, show which changed behaviour no executed check would notice, and what the agent never looked at. Sequence: P0 promote 1.0 / CEM-V1-008 / V1-1629 (existing 1.0 work); S discovery replay (v1-0 spike, kill criterion); P1 C1 on the 1.0 wire; P2 C2 + A1 + A3; P3 C3 + T1-T3; P4 wire, second consumer, A4, A5. North star: escaped-defect capture versus a coverage-diff baseline on held-out external repositories. Guardrails: flagged units per change, false-alarm rate, cost <= 1.0 (target about 5x cheaper), zero invented certainty, incremental == full rebuild. Stop-loss: Entire or Agent Trace add verification fields; Qodo or Copilot ship per-PR mutation; 1.0 gets no adopters; the replay does not beat LLM reviewers. Deferred: behaviour flows, learning stage, non-test witness classes beyond types and fuzz, hermetic execution beyond Go, external transparency log.
title: CEM 2.0 umbrella: the counterfactual receipt (expert-audited proposal, owner intent pending)

acceptanceCriteria: A spec requirement bounds the default affected cache (size or entry cap, or pruning of entries whose root is gone) with failure modes and rollback
Tests prove eviction never changes plan bytes and never touches files outside the cache directory
`corvint affected cache` reports the bound
body: AFP-V0-432 (lane claude/affected-default-cache-1024, V1-2572, GH #1601) makes `corvint affected` keep one graph entry per root under os.UserCacheDir()/corvint/affected. Nothing ever prunes an entry, so every removed lane worktree leaves its entry behind; one entry for this repository is about 4.8 MB (darwin, 2026-10-24), and lanes create hundreds of worktrees. Reproduction: run `corvint --root WT affected --path X` in a worktree, remove the worktree, then `corvint affected cache` still counts the entry and its bytes. Expected: a bounded cache (for example a total-size or entry cap with oldest-first eviction, or pruning of entries whose root no longer exists) that never changes plan bytes. Actual: unbounded growth until the operator deletes the directory. Visibility already exists through `corvint affected cache [--format doctor-plugin]` (AFP-V0-435).
title: affected default cache: entries of deleted roots accumulate with no eviction

acceptanceCriteria: A computed member read or write after a non-null assertion (`x![k]`, `x()![k]`, `x[0]![k]`) stops the Playwright tag closure and names its line
A failing-first test in internal/liveverify/affected/typescript covers the repro
The governing spec (AFP-V0-409/425 or TJAA) records the requirement
body:
Confirmed bug (fail-open), found during GitHub #1717 work (PR #1719), present on origin/main ec41e4e. In internal/liveverify/affected/typescript/playwright_tag_sources.go, playwrightMemberAccessAt treats only an identifier, `)`, `]` or `.` before `[` as a member access, so `details![key]` (TypeScript non-null assertion) is not seen as a computed member access and the tag closure stays exact.

Repro (scratch test, linux/WSL2 via heavy.sh, corvint build at ec41e4e + PR #1719): grepFixture(t, grepRepro) with e2e/plain.spec.ts = "const details: any = { tag: ['@base'] };\nconst key = 't' + 'ag';\ndetails![key].push('@smoke');\ntest('plain', async () => {});\n"; gh1647Omission returns unverified=[] omissions=[].

Expected: the closure stops at line 3 (a computed member access/write can reach a tag array), so the grep omission stays unverified. Actual: verified. Same gap likely applies to playwrightArrayLiteralAt/playwrightFreshArrayAt only indirectly (PR #1719 already refuses `!` as an array-literal start).
title: affected (Playwright): tag closure misses a computed member access after a TypeScript non-null assertion (details![key])

acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction on current main either confirms the stale captured-base label (then a fix binds the packet to live HEAD or reports explicit base drift, with a regression test) or shows it no longer occurs (recorded with the build and command).
body: Split from V1-0418's attached evidence (VT audit 2026-10-11, Core rc.3 build 456). A mixed-worktree `corvint context` query in VanillaTwisted reported captured commit c7e2140 while live HEAD and the receipt history tip were both a9e90f93. Original receipt: /Users/russelllewis/projects/VanillaTwisted/.agent-evidence/obedience-audit-2026-10-11/corvint-context.json (evidence sha256 39e5ff8d...c97 on V1-0418). Expected: the packet either binds to live HEAD or names explicit base drift/freshness. Actual: an older captured base with no drift signal. Status: SUSPECTED, not reproduced on a current build; first step is a reproduction on current main.
title: Suspected: mixed-worktree context packet labels a stale captured base (c7e2140) while live HEAD is a9e90f93

acceptanceCriteria: A corpus over the output byte bound with derived declarations builds in one compile, with a byte-identical result to the two-compile retry, or the spec records why it cannot.
TestDCPV1569DerivationStopsAtTheOutputBound asserts the new compile count.
Build time on a large over-bound fixture is measured before and after.
body: Found in GitHub #1665 (V1-2598, PR #1722, base ec41e4e). DCP-V1-569 retries a compile that the output byte bound refused, deriving the prefix of declarations that fits. The bound is only known after the whole artifact is encoded, so a byte-bound corpus still compiles twice. The reporter saw 15.1 s instead of 10.9 s on a 114 MB, 4-repository corpus against MaxCorpusBytes 128 MiB. A record-bound corpus now compiles once. Expected: one compile, using a running or lower-bound estimate of the encoded size before derivation. Actual: two compiles. Reproduced by TestDCPV1569DerivationStopsAtTheOutputBound, which asserts 2 compiles.
title: docs corpus build: an output-byte-bound corpus compiles twice because the artifact size is known only after the full encode

acceptanceCriteria: A spec requirement with failure modes defines the manifest field, and the field keeps old manifests readable.
A test shows a filtered derivation keeps only the selected declarations and names the excluded ones in one gap.
DerivationVersion and the release notes change only if the default output changes.
body: Option raised in GitHub #1665 (re-test of ec41e4e; V1-2598, PR #1722). Derivation is now bounded: it keeps declarations in manifest input order up to the record and output byte bounds (DCP-V1-568, DCP-V1-569). A large multi-repository corpus therefore keeps a prefix chosen by input order rather than by what the caller needs. Expected: a manifest-declared path or kind filter, for example source paths of chosen repositories or symbols but not tests, that selects which declarations are derived. Excluded inputs are named in a gap. Actual: no caller control.
title: docs corpus build: let the caller restrict declaration derivation by path or kind

acceptanceCriteria: Both RESULT.schema.json copies admit the CEM-V1-083 plain criterion binding form beside the Tasks form, with the CEM-V1-091 chain re-bound through a recorded regeneration path.
TestCEMV1622OpaqueReceiptResultValidates validates the plain-map verify results against the committed schema with no overlay.
body: Found 2026-10-24 on V1-2107 (branch claude/cem-v0596-deps-1024, base ec41e4e9c). Repro: TestCEMV1622OpaqueReceiptResultValidates (internal/cem/verify) marshals the native ACCEPT result for the public neutral-criterion case and validates it with a closed draft 2020-12 test validator against both protocol/cem-1.0/stable/RESULT.schema.json copies. Expected: the result validates (ALGORITHMS.md CEM-V1-020 gives criterion bindings two closed forms, plain = exactly id, criterionIndex, criterionSha256, evidenceId). Actual: $.references.criterionBindings[0]: undeclared member evidenceId (the schema's $defs/criterionBinding is only the Tasks form with additionalProperties false and the eight Tasks members required). This holds for both runner labels, so it is independent of the opaque/0 widening V1-2107 delivered; the V1-2107 lane was scoped not to widen beyond the two runner profiles. The test pins this gap and validates the rest of each result with only $defs/criterionBinding overlaid as anyOf [Tasks form, plain form]. Fix needs a cem-stable-regen mode that can add a oneOf/anyOf branch to a $defs node (the CEM-V1-620 --widen mode only widens string const/enum) and a re-bound CEM-V1-091 chain.
title: RESULT.schema.json criterionBinding lacks the CEM-V1-083 plain form, so every plain (unadmitted) map's verify result fails the schema

acceptanceCriteria: TestCCEV0021ServeTree no longer races a freed port (hold the listener until serve takes over, or retry pick on port-in-use in the test only)
CAL-V0-132 drain wait is bounded by a load-tolerant deadline or the leak check distinguishes slow drain from leak
Both tests pass in 20 repeated runs with -count=20 under heavy.sh concurrent load
body:
PR #1689 head 1c435c88e1, run 40119696525, go-product-shard (6) on self-hosted actions-runner-7 (several runners share one host). Two failures, both passing on GitHub-hosted runners at main:
1. internal/changee2e TestCCEV0021ServeTree: environment_test.go:138 environment-unavailable:port-in-use. freeLoopbackAddr listens on :0 and closes; serveTree then refuses when the port already answers. Another process on the shared host can bind the freed port in between (TOCTOU).
2. internal/tasks/dispatch TestCALV0132_RepeatedLedgerMemberRefuses: reap_test.go:212 V1-0948 worker process groups [2496962] outlived their leaders; the 5 s drain wait in drained() can be too short under host load.
Expected: both pass under concurrent self-hosted shards. Actual: fail once; failed jobs rerun.
title: suspected: CCE-V0-021 port-in-use and CAL-V0-132 group-drain tests flake on the shared self-hosted runner host

acceptanceCriteria: The owner accepts or rejects a versioned liveness-tail store format with a durable watermark, a recovery contract that never deletes or reissues an authority receipt, and no daemon
The design states how a lost renew that shortened a lease fails toward expiry, or excludes renew from the allowance
If accepted, the format change has its own spec requirements, old-store readability or refusal behaviour, and crash-injection tests; if rejected, V1-2203's target is re-scoped
body: Observed 2026-10-24 in lane claude/tasks-heartbeat-durability-1024 (V1-2203, PR #1726, LGL-V0-008 proposed). The owner decision of 2026-10-24 allowed heartbeat and renew receipts to commit without their own fsync, durable with the next synced write or a group sync of at most 1 s, with recovery reading a lost tail heartbeat as an older heartbeat. The lane stopped under the decision's stop clause and shipped only the staging-directory sync skip (LGL-V0-005..007). Why the full allowance is unsafe in the current store: (1) a crash that keeps head.json's advance and loses or tears the unsynced receipt makes audit report JOURNAL_FORKED or MALFORMED, and a lost head advance makes every read refuse REDO_PENDING (TestLGLV0008_LostLivenessTailIsRefusedNotAdopted pins all three); (2) reading such a tail as an older heartbeat needs a durable watermark that tells a liveness tail from an authority tail, which head.json's closed member set cannot carry, so it is a store-format cutover old binaries refuse; (3) recovery would have to delete committed receipts and reissue their sequence numbers; (4) a bounded 1 s group sync needs a periodic process, which product invariant 7 forbids as a daemon; (5) the premise fails for renew: planRenew (internal/tasks/transaction/lease.go) sets ExpiresAt to the renew's recordedAt plus its lease minutes, so a renew can shorten a lease, and losing it leaves the earlier, longer expiry in force (a newer-looking lease, not an older one). Expected: an owner decision on whether to pursue a versioned liveness-tail format (watermark plus recovery contract plus how renew-shortening fails toward expiry), or to accept the remaining heartbeat floor. Actual: no accepted design; V1-2203's 50 ms quiet-host target stays NOT MET (projected 56-59 ms after LGL-V0-005, inference).
title: Tasks: unsynced heartbeat/renew receipts need an owner store-format decision (liveness watermark, receipt-loss recovery, renew shortening)

acceptanceCriteria: The VS Code impact view names evidence_truncated alongside evidence_omitted for a result that carries it.
An extension test covers a result with evidence_truncated and one without.
body: Found in lane claude/analysis-held-1024 (V1-1003). Impact results now carry `evidence_truncated` (rows dropped at the per-result maxEvidence ceiling of 10), separately from `evidence_omitted` (MCPV0-031 display cap). extensions/vscode/src/model.ts:155 renders only evidence_omitted and references_omitted, so a ceiling cut is silently invisible in the extension. Expected: the extension names both counts. Actual: evidence_truncated is ignored. Version: branch claude/analysis-held-1024 at 743e9ca47.
title: VS Code extension does not display impact evidence_truncated counts (MCPV0-112)

acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with an ambiguous slid insertion (git indent heuristic vs plain Myers) is mapped with hunk starts equal to `git diff` output, or the trial alignment accepts an equivalent slide and records it
cem-trial reruns c01-5944eab4fd07 without the alignment refusal
The owning contract (CEM hunk derivation vs CRT alignment) is named in the spec
body: V1-0836 held-out run (2026-10-24, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 0 at /private/tmp/cem-trial-heldout-bin). Task c01-5944eab4fd07 (beamfall 5944eab4fd07, base ddcaac8b90d4) fails all 6 lanes (control, treatment, seeded x2) in tools/cem-trial/main.go:686 alignedHunks: 'map hunk 5 is internal/manifest/manifest.go -117 +117, the presented hunk internal/manifest/manifest.go -116 +116'. The hunk inserts a `{ ID: "continue" ... },` block before an identical-shape `{ ID: "recent"` element, so the insertion can slide by one line; git's indent heuristic places it at 116, Corvint's map at 117. Expected: either the CEM map's hunk ranges match git diff's placement (the presented patch), or alignedHunks/cem prepare tolerate a pure slide of an equivalent hunk. Actual: the pair is invalid in every arm. Suspected defect, not yet confirmed which side owns the contract.
title: cem prepare emits a different hunk start than git for an ambiguous slid insertion, so cem-trial drops the pair in every arm

acceptanceCriteria: A lost control attempt on the live lane is retried (bounded) or the test distinguishes infrastructure loss from a wrong verdict
cce-live passes 5 consecutive runs on hosted macos-15, or the residual rate is recorded
body:
First cce-live run on batch PR #1731 head 34367a343 (run 40129429349, job 120977770853, hosted macos-15, Playwright 1.64.0 tuple passed AFP-V0-435). internal/changee2e TestCCEV0009LivePreserves failed at prove_test.go:376: verdict = INCONCLUSIVE (control-not-killed:control:omitted-event:setup-1), want PRESERVES. That control's status is infrastructure_failed, reason one-or-more-attempts-lost-to-infrastructure; the other three controls were killed and head/base outcomes all passed. Expected: the live test either retries an attempt lost to infrastructure before reading the verdict, or reports the infra loss as a skip/retry rather than a product failure. Actual: one lost attempt fails the CI job. Suspected flake; one observation. Recurrence 2026-10-25: batch PR #1748 head 60dbf9c75 (run 40196868668, job 121179730366, hosted macOS, tuple check passed): TestCCEV0053LiveRecordsCoverage at coverage_record_test.go:130 verdict INCONCLUSIVE (control-not-killed:control:omitted-event:setup-1), attempt reason playwright-infrastructure; main run 40163191708 (bde40f379) also failed cce-live. Same control, different live test, so the fix belongs in the shared live-verdict path, not one test.

Recurrence 3 (2026-10-25): batch #1764 head 2a8448cd3, cce-live run 40202373049 job 121196064040. TestCCEV0053LiveRecordsCoverage verdict INCONCLUSIVE (control-not-killed:control:omitted-event:setup-1), want DISCRIMINATES. Same signature as the #1748 and main failures. Rerun requested.
title: cce-live: TestCCEV0009LivePreserves reads INCONCLUSIVE when one control attempt is lost to infrastructure on hosted macos-15

acceptanceCriteria: A test on a segmented store runs one complete-route write (e.g. widen) and then a pool release; the release resumes (Resumed=1, audits=0) with the same report and store bytes as the complete route
No store-format change or resident process
LGL-V0-011 harness at 47k on a real disk shows release p99 <=2 s after an interleaved widen
body: Found by V1-1702 (PR #1733, head fcba2fa38). The LGL-V0-009 sealed-base resume works only when the writer checkpoint's FullSeq equals the manifest's Through (S). Any write that takes the complete route (widen, reap, Mutate, or any write after the checkpoint is invalidated) retains a checkpoint whose FullSeq is that write's head, past S. The next pool acquire or release then declines quietly: TestLGLV0010_SealedBaseGate/full-seq-past-the-seal shows audits>0 and resumed=0. It keeps paying the complete audit (about 20 s at 47k receipts under load on linux/WSL2, and 35-60 s in the V1-1702 evidence) until a writer-route write or a validated seal rebases the checkpoint to S. Expected: after a complete-route write, the store keeps or re-derives a sealed base, so pool verbs stay at about 1 s. One option is for the complete route to retain a checkpoint with FullSeq=S when the manifest is bound and the walk covered S. Related: V1-2202 (S6 widen/reap) and V1-2592.
title: Tasks: a complete-route write rebases the writer checkpoint FullSeq to its head, so the next pool verb loses the LGL-V0-009 sealed-base resume and pays the 20-60 s complete audit

acceptanceCriteria: A focused test either shows that a tail-removed base blob does not decline the resume, or confirms the decline and the fix removes it while preserving the rewritten-blob refusal
Classification recorded: confirmed or not-a-bug
body: Suspected, not reproduced. Found while reviewing V1-1702 (PR #1733, fcba2fa38). SealedResumeBase and the S6a resume base both stamp the base's evidence and pinned blobs, and PrecheckResume plus the held check re-hash them. If a legitimate tail write between S and head removes or rewrites one of those blobs (for example evidence garbage collection or a pin replacement), the stamp no longer matches and the resume declines to the complete route. That is safe, because a decline is never wrong, but it costs the full audit. Expected: only blobs the resumed state still references are stamped, or the tail walk accounts for blob removals. Actual: unverified. Reproduction needed: a fixture where a tail receipt drops a base blob, followed by a pool release, then check ResumeDeclines.
title: Tasks S6a/LGL-V0-009 (suspected): the resume precheck re-hashes the stamped base blobs, so a tail write that removes or replaces a base evidence/pinned blob may decline a resume that is actually safe

acceptanceCriteria: A test rewrites the bound manifest at a stable head; the lease command refuses on its first round with a non-retryable integrity code
A head that genuinely moves still retries and reports SNAPSHOT_MOVED
body: Pre-existing behaviour observed in V1-1702's TestLGLV0009_SealedBaseDeclinesRewrittenSegment/before/manifest (PR #1733, fcba2fa38). If the manifest the head binds is rewritten in place before a lease command, the head guards fail the manifest digest before any resume is tried. The command retries all of its rounds as if a concurrent writer had moved the snapshot, then refuses SNAPSHOT_MOVED. That is retryable to the caller, but the store is corrupt, not moving. Expected: a manifest digest mismatch at a stable head refuses once with a non-retryable integrity code (CORRUPT or similar), and the retry rounds are not spent. Actual: SNAPSHOT_MOVED after the full retry budget. The store is never written in either case, so this is not a safety bug.
title: Tasks: a sealed-segment manifest rewritten in place (stamps kept) makes the head guards answer SNAPSHOT_MOVED on every retry round instead of a corruption refusal

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the seven cases has a failing-then-passing test in tools/cem-trial
select presents a patch byte-identical to gitauth CanonicalDiff under a hostile git config (diff.noprefix=true)
CRT-V0-016 text updated; build log records that the 2026-10-24 held-out report rescores at bc580295f
body: Codex review (one round, 2026-10-24) of PR #1727 commits f99c64c6c and 3074f8911 in tools/cem-trial. Confirmed by reading: (1) reRegister returns early when prior and current registration share a commit, so two files committed together skip the scorer-only comparison (register.go reRegister). (2) registrationInvalid returns before reRegistrationInvalid when Registration is nil on a non-heldout report, so a stray re_registered block goes unchecked. (3) ReusedFrom stores the manifest digest only, so a scorer-only re-registration with an unchanged manifest cannot tell --reuse lanes from --resume checkpoint lanes. (4) --resume does not restore a checkpoint's re_registered record. (5) reuseSource.merge keeps the first lane per key, so an ineligible --reuse lane shadows an eligible checkpoint lane. (6) reRegister refuses a prior report with never-started pending lanes because unstampedLanes counts them. (7) select.go canonicalDiffArguments omits gitauth CanonicalDiff's config neutralisation (diff.noprefix, attributes, --full-index, prefixes, --end-of-options). None applies to the 2026-10-24 held-out run: its manifests differ (0b9c0958 vs 879d19a2), commits differ, no --resume, prior report fully stamped, and Beamfall/global git config sets no diff.noprefix. Fixing changes the scorer digest, so the held-out report stays rescored at the registered tree bc580295f.
title: cem-trial CRT-V0-016 reuse: Codex round findings (same-commit bypass, nil registration, reuse vs resume provenance, checkpoint ReRegistered drop, lane shadowing, pending lanes, full CanonicalDiff config)

acceptanceCriteria: A computed member read or write on an object-literal receiver (`{ ... }[k]`, `({ ... })[k]` already stops) stops the Playwright tag closure and names its line

The TJAA spec residual for TJAA-V0-095 is updated
body: Confirmed bug (fail-open), found during GitHub #1737 work (branch claude/gh1737-pw-1024, base origin/main b63dd0d520ee). In internal/liveverify/affected/typescript/playwright_tag_sources.go, playwrightMemberAccessAt returns false when the byte before `[` is `}`, so `{ tag: ['@a'] }[k]` is not treated as a member access. Reproduction (scratch test calling playwrightTagTextLiteral, linux/WSL2 go1.27.3): `export function f(k: string) { return { tag: ['@a'] }[k]; }` returns at=0 why="" (exact), while `const o = { tag: ['@a'] }; export function f(k: string) { return o[k]; }` stops with `a computed member access can reach a tag array without naming it`. Expected: both stop and name the line. Care: `}` also ends a block, so `if (x) {}\n[a].forEach(...)` must not regress silently; a conservative stop there is acceptable. Sibling of V1-2611 (non-null `x![k]`). Recorded as a residual in TJAA-V0-095.
title: affected (Playwright): tag closure misses a computed member read on an object-literal receiver ({ ... }[key])

acceptanceCriteria: A spec amendment in docs/specs/typescript-javascript-affected-adapter-v0.md defines the proof rule, failure modes and rollback
Each admitted construct has a positive and a fail-closed negative test in internal/liveverify/affected/typescript

body: GitHub #1737 item 2 asked for a sound, conservative data-flow rule: a construct is ignored only when the analysis proves its value cannot reach a test or describe title, tag or details argument. The lane (branch claude/gh1737-pw-1024) delivered only the fresh-object rule TJAA-V0-095: a plain computed write into a const, unexported, single-declaration fresh object literal whose other uses are `.`-property names, object keys, plain computed write targets, `in` operands, and properties/spreads of object literals nested in a direct `.fulfill(...)` argument; with no `this`/`super` in the closure and no closure-defined `fulfill`. NOT MET and remaining: (1) value-flow through names: `let`/`var` objects, aliases, call arguments other than `.fulfill(...)`, returns, and per-function scoping (a second `const` of the same name in another function rejects today); (2) computed reads and compound writes of a fresh object when the initializer provably holds no tag array (no spread of an unproven source); (3) sinks other than Route.fulfill (route.continue, request.post data, page.evaluate args) with an explicit trust list; (4) callee identity: today any `.fulfill(...)` callee outside the closure is trusted as Playwright Route.fulfill. Every addition must keep invariant 2: unproven stays UNKNOWN with its line.
title: affected (Playwright): general proof that a construct's value cannot reach a test title, tag or details argument (GH #1737 item 2 remainder)

A focused run of internal/localcompletion passes on the box with ~/.gitconfig replaced by a directory (git skips an EACCES global file, so chmod 000 cannot reproduce; a directory reproduces the CI exit 128), with a control git run failing under the same condition
body: Observed on PR #1740 (head 5255887cc), go-product-shard (5), job 121023118539, runner corvint-box-2, 2026-10-25T00:07-00:34Z. internal/localcompletion tests (TestAggregatePublicationNewProcessCrashRecovery, TestAggregatePublicationRefusesForeignOldArtifact, TestAggregateHistoryExactCapacityAndOrphanConflict) fail at storage_test.go:770: `git init -q -b main` exits 128 with `warning: unable to access '/home/russell/.gitconfig': Permission denied` then `fatal: unknown error occurred while reading the configuration files` (108 denials in the log). The same runner ran #1735 shard 2 an hour earlier with 0 denials, so this is intermittent host state, not code. Expected: test git invocations never depend on the runner user's global config (tests should set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/HOME to a temp dir, as gitauth does) and the box's home config stays readable. Suspected causes: a concurrent process rewriting or chmod-ing ~/.gitconfig on the box (heavy.sh WSL jobs share the russell user), or runner-2 service user differing from the home owner. Unconfirmed.
