acceptanceCriteria: Self-hosted jobs no longer replace ~/.gitconfig on start (inode stable across two consecutive job starts, or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL points at a per-job file)
A go-product shard run on the boxes with overlapping jobs shows no `unable to access ... .gitconfig` denials
Workflow change reviewed under ci-control-plane; AFP-V0-421 note updated if the flock is removed
body:
Root cause of V1-2633 and the tasks/store CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE / git exit-128 family in V1-2632 (runs 40141946180, 40144038527, 40144517103). Since 1c435c88e (#1689) each self-hosted job runs four `git config --global` writes under the AFP-V0-421 flock (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~449-460). git writes .gitconfig.lock and renames it over ~/.gitconfig, so the inode changes at every job start even for unchanged values (verified on the box: 23388814 -> 23388815). The test-confine wrapper (AFP-V0-023, .github/testconfine/scopes.go Rules) grants a confined package every sibling of each ancestor of the checkout root as one file rule, and Landlock binds rules to the file object, not the path; a confined probe read the file, then got EACCES on the same path after an unconfined rename over it. The eight corvint-box runners share one account and one home, so any confined package still running when another runner starts a job loses access to /home/russell/.gitconfig: `warning: unable to access ... Permission denied`, `fatal: unknown error occurred while reading the configuration files`, exit 128 (108 denials in job 121023118539; box-6 tasks/store first CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE 23:49:40Z, 50 s after box-1 started a job at 23:48:50Z). Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-25-box-ci-failures.md (PR #1741).

Fix (needs owner ci-control-plane; .github change): give each job its own global configuration instead of rewriting the shared file. In the self-hosted setup step write the four values to `$RUNNER_TEMP/gitconfig` and export `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$RUNNER_TEMP/gitconfig` through `$GITHUB_ENV`; the flock becomes unnecessary. Weaker alternative: run `git config --global` only when `git config --global --get KEY` differs, so an unchanged value never renames the file. PR #1741 lands the code-side hardening (TestMain isolation in localcompletion, tasks/store, mcp/bridge) but 50 more declared packages spawn git in tests (see the sweep ticket), so the workflow fix is the complete cure.
title: NEEDS-OWNER: self-hosted shard jobs must stop rewriting the shared ~/.gitconfig (Landlock grants are inode-pinned)

acceptanceCriteria: Every declared package whose tests spawn git passes with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL set to a directory (one package per go test command)
No test depends on identity or defaults from the account's global configuration
Scan script or list retained in the build-log entry
body:
Follow-up to V1-2633 / PR #1741. A scan of .corvint/test-read-scopes.json packages whose _test.go files call exec.Command("git") found 53 packages; three now isolate GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM in TestMain (internal/localcompletion, internal/tasks/store, internal/mcp/bridge). The remaining 50 (heuristic: no TestMain setting GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL; some may isolate per call) include cmd/corvint-mcp (13 spawns), internal/mcp/corpusbridge (13), internal/cem/gitauth (9), internal/cem/verify (8), internal/doccorpus (5), internal/taskman (4), internal/extevidence (4) and single-spawn packages. On the self-hosted runners any of them fails with git exit 128 whenever another runner starts a job while they run (inode-pinned Landlock grant on ~/.gitconfig, see the NEEDS-OWNER ticket), and on any developer host an unreadable or hostile ~/.gitconfig changes fixture behaviour. Darwin reproduction recipe: run the package with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing at a directory (access passes, open fails, exit 128 like the confined box).

Scope: add the same two os.Setenv lines to each package's TestMain (create one where missing), or a shared test helper if the repo prefers; keep fixtures that set identity explicitly. Dedupe against the workflow fix: if the owner lands per-job GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL first, this sweep remains hygiene, not a CI blocker.
title: Sweep: 50 declared (confined) packages spawn git in tests without global-config isolation

acceptanceCriteria: After 3 identical failed observations on a member, pool status shows a stalled-recovery condition with the count, since and the detail digest/excerpt.
quarantine.since is set to a real timestamp when a member enters QUARANTINED.
With all members stalled, an acquire returns a typed refusal naming the condition instead of waiting or timing out; dispatch stops starting pool-needing attempts and says why.
The verb and condition are spec-backed and documented in corvint_help/docs.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1743. A member that never becomes safe stays QUARANTINED with quarantine.since NOT_OBSERVED, lastHealth/lastCleanup NOT_OBSERVED, and a generic reason; external readiness failures leave no trace (only confirm-safe success is recorded), and dispatch keeps starting attempts. Requested: (1) a verb to record a failed readiness observation per member with a bounded, redacted detail and digest, stored as lastHealth/lastCleanup with result, time and digest; (2) persist quarantine.since; (3) count consecutive identical failures (same detail digest) and raise typed POOL_MEMBER_RECOVERY_STALLED after a threshold or quarantine-age bound, shown in pool status and a pool-level summary; (4) with every member stalled, acquire/dispatch refuses with a typed reason instead of waiting or burning sessions; (5) document it in corvint_help/docs.
title: GH #1743: pool members stuck QUARANTINED fail silently; record failed observations, quarantine.since, stalled-recovery condition, fail-closed acquire

acceptanceCriteria: With every member of a pool stalled, dispatch with a planSelected:true pool role launches no attempt for that pool and reports POOL_MEMBER_RECOVERY_STALLED naming the pool, covered by a CLI test

body: Follow-up to V1-2636 / beamfall/corvint#1744 (GH #1743). Found by the #1744 lane while adding TestPSRV0265_DispatchHoldsStalledPoolLaunchesCLI. The stall hold in internal/tasks/cli/dispatch.go fires only for a pool role that does not match on planSelected. internal/tasks/transaction/plan.go defers a pool ticket when no member is FREE; with every member QUARANTINED the ticket never becomes SELECTED, so a role with match {"planSelected":true} never matches it, it never reaches the pool room, and dispatch emits no pool-wait event and no POOL_MEMBER_RECOVERY_STALLED reason. Expected: the planner deferral (or roster) carries the stalled reason so dispatch says why for planSelected roles too. Actual: silent hold. Version: Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 753 plus #1744 head fffd78aad.
title: Dispatch: a planSelected pool role is held silently when every pool member is stalled; no POOL_MEMBER_RECOVERY_STALLED reason reaches the operator

acceptanceCriteria: An E2E /0 receipt run with an absolute node argv[0] whose version differs from PATH node binds argv[0]'s version, shown by a focused test.

body: Observed 2026-10-25 (lane claude/cce-live-1025, corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 754, base 8200ba7c6). TestNEAV0002ActualBrowserAssessment ran the Playwright runner as argv [/private/tmp/pw-tuple-1064/node-v24.11.1-darwin-arm64/bin/node, cli.js] through the testacceptance worker, whose SafeEnvironment PATH is /opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin. Every run in the report records node_version v22.23.3 (the Homebrew node on PATH). Cause: internal/jstestprovider/runner.go Config.identity sets NodeVersion from nodeVersion(), which runs `node --version` from PATH instead of the runner argv's executable. Expected: the receipt binds the version of the node executable that ran the runner (argv[0] when it is a node binary), or reads unknown. Actual: it binds an unrelated PATH node. The same test also declares RunnerVersion 1.63.0 while the CLI is 1.64.0; /0 binds the declared value without observing it.
title: jstestprovider /0 E2E receipt binds the Node version of PATH node, not the runner's node executable

acceptanceCriteria: A regression test whose fixture has a gitignored, untracked report directory containing a dynamic import shows the affected plan narrows and reports no frontier from that directory.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1750 (version main-8200ba7). `corvint affected --base ... --playwright-config ... --playwright-discovery ...` reads files git ignores and HEAD does not track (a Playwright HTML report under the gitignored /playwright-report/) into the shared TypeScript graph. Their minified bundles produce typescript:dynamic-import and typescript:scan-unresolved frontiers, so the plan is NOT_NARROWED / GRAPH_FRONTIER / FULL_RELEVANT_SUITE even when the range changes one spec. Expected: ignored-and-untracked paths are not graph inputs (consistent with the --path refusal of an ignored file HEAD does not track); if visible, reported as ignored/excluded, never as a frontier. Tracked-but-ignored and untracked-not-ignored files stay fail-closed.
title: GH #1750: affected scans gitignored untracked files (playwright-report/) into the TypeScript graph, so their frontiers force FULL_RELEVANT_SUITE

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1751 (version main-8200ba7). Dirty JSON data files that no test, config, fixture or reporter reads are reported as UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH under playwright:dynamic-source-reachability and the plan falls back to FULL_RELEVANT_SUITE (NOT_TEST_SIDE). Request: a project-owned, checked-in, reviewable declaration of path ownership (glob -> no-runtime-reader, or glob -> owning tests). The receipt records the declaration digest and matched dirty paths; a declaration contradicting observed evidence (static import by a test, named by a config/fixture) is refused fail-closed; unknown/excluded entries name the excluding declaration. Project authority outranks syntax but never invents certainty against observed evidence.
title: GH #1751: affected has no project-owned declaration of dirty paths with no runtime reader; UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH forces the full suite

acceptanceCriteria: An owner-accepted decision on the witness via contract for deep chains (keep, cap, or reference), recorded in affected-plan-v0.

If changed: receipt bytes and warm wall time on the perf-budget Ruby fixture grow linearly in affected units, measured on the quiet WSL2 host, and the perf-budget affected-path target is promoted or re-justified.
body: Observed 2026-10-25 on main 8200ba7c6, WSL2/Linux 32 CPU, quiet host (lane claude/affected-reuse-1025, V1-2473/GH #1601). On the perf-budget Ruby fixture (corvint-perf-budget-fixture/1, 20,001 files, models in one require_relative chain 6,666 deep), `corvint affected --path app/models/model_00001.rb` writes an 823,768,618-byte compact receipt. Warm (graph cache hit) it takes 7.00 s at 4.54 GB peak RSS; --no-cache 13.75 s / 4.21 GB. A CPU profile puts 4.8 of 6.4 s in canonical JSON encoding plus GC. Cause: traverse and testUsersOf in internal/liveverify/affected/select.go copy the parent's Via for every reached unit (`append(append([]string(nil), parent.Via...), dependent)`), so a chain of length n costs O(n^2) memory and output. `via` is wire contract (affected-plan-v0 'full witness chain', ranking uses its length), so shrinking it needs an owner decision: e.g. a parent reference or a capped chain plus a digest in the compact receipt, with --full keeping the full chain. Until then the perf-budget affected-path target (1000 ms, PRB-V0-031) cannot be met on this fixture whatever the graph reuse does; it stays pending. A Rails-shaped tree of the same size with bounded depth is sub-second warm (see build log 2026-10-25-affected-path-reuse). Expected: receipt size and warm time roughly linear in affected units. Actual: quadratic in chain depth.
title: affected receipt grows with the square of a require chain: every selected unit copies its full witness via (824 MB, 7 s warm on the perf fixture)

body: Suspected measurement defect, not confirmed. Observed 2026-10-25 by lane claude/corpus-read-1025 (V1-2477/V1-2571) on the Windows box, WSL2/Linux 32 CPU, go1.27.3, Windows power plan Winhance, governor NOT_EXPOSED_IN_WSL2. Binary origin/main 8200ba7c6, docs corpus flow --id adapter:lib0-1 --timings on the 66.75 MB fixture (~/bench/corpus copy). Quiet samples (idle-check quiet:true, load1 0.26-0.80, Windows CPU 0.4-1.1 %) gave flow median 280.8 ms, p95 311.4 ms (n=11), while untimed reads of the same binary at load1 28-36 ran 240-383 ms and often faster than quiet. Actual: the quiet-host protocol may report a pessimistic number, so p50 targets such as V1-2571's 170 ms are judged against a slower clock than CI or a loaded host. acceptanceCriteria: verifyPinnedRevisions resolves all pinned revisions of one checkout through a single git cat-file batch process, with a test counting process starts.

body: Observed 2026-10-25 by lane claude/corpus-read-1025 (V1-2477). In internal/doccorpus read.go verifyPinnedRevisions runs one goroutine per checkout directory with gitauth.Open, then CommitTree per pinned revision, and each CommitTree starts its own git cat-file --batch -z process. On the 66.75 MB fixture (6 revisions over 5 checkouts) an untimed probe showed gitauth.Open +5-18 ms and trees +10-15 ms per read. After DCR-V1-554 this header verification is off the warm-read critical path (it finishes before the scan ends), so the cost is CPU and process spawns rather than latency; it becomes latency again on corpora with many pinned revisions per checkout or a cold page cache. Expected: one batch reader per checkout resolves every pinned revision of that checkout. Actual: one process per revision. Verification must stay complete and fail closed (DCR-V1-410, DCR-V1-432).
title: Docs corpus pin verification spawns one git cat-file --batch process per pinned revision instead of one per checkout

acceptanceCriteria: A gate GRANT whose hunks are satisfied on runner-input states selection and inventory completeness as NOT_OBSERVED (or the basis refuses a plan narrower than the governed package's tests), shown by a focused internal/taskman test replacing the current CEM-V1-634 pin.
The narrowed-plan and whole-omission cases of TestCEMV1634GateRunnerBasisTrustsTheCitedSelection no longer produce a GRANT without that uncertainty.
docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md records the rule with owner acceptance, CEM-V1-634 is updated, and pinned GRANT documents' reverification impact (TCB-V0-013) is recorded.
body:
Found by V1-2599 (omission soundness spike), Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 754, repository base 8200ba7c6ecc56a03ef58350c1f952b097e04956, branch claude/cem-omission-2599.

Observed: the sealed verdict gate's runner-input basis (CEM-V1-606, `corvint cem gate-verdict`) satisfies a cited hunk when every receipt the link names PASSED and the plan's inputFiles pin the hunk blob. It never compares the plan's selection (request.expectedTests / selectors) with the target's test inventory or with `corvint affected`.
- With a failing selected test in the receipt, or a failed rerun named by the link, the gate refuses `tier-below-anchored`, and the hunk carries reason `runner-not-passed`. This is correct.
- The same change GRANTs once the producer narrows the plan's expectedTests to exclude the failing test, or leaves the failed run out of the map whole (its receipt row, artifact and link digest). Whole omission is byte-identical to a map with no failed run.
- The GRANT document's closed members (candidateTree, citation, code, governed, inputs, map, outcome, paths, portable, profile, reason, sealedMaps, verdict) carry no selection or inventory completeness statement. A clean GRANT therefore carries no uncertainty for a selection the producer chose.

Reproduction: `TestCEMV1634GateRunnerBasisTrustsTheCitedSelection` (internal/taskman/cem_verdict_omission_unix_test.go), which pins the current GRANT. Reader-side context is in interop/cem01-go/testdata/omission/ and the CEM-V1-633 tests. Both stable readers ACCEPT these maps with REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_ONLY and sourceInventoryCompleteness / runnerReceiptSemantics NOT_OBSERVED, so the readers state the limit and the gate does not.

Expected: the gate GRANT records that runner selection and inventory completeness were NOT_OBSERVED (or refuses the runner-input basis when the plan's selection is narrower than the target's tests for the governed package), or the owner records an accepted limit. Unknown inventory must yield uncertainty, never invented certainty.

Violated: CEM-V1-004 (incomplete inventory produces uncertainty), CEM-V1-005 (distinguish selected and executed tests from coverage and discrimination), AGENTS.md product invariant 2.

Not fixed in V1-2599: the fix is a GRANT wire change (a new member, or a new refusal) that changes pinned GRANT documents (TCB-V0-013), so it needs an owner decision. When fixed, update CEM-V1-634 and its test.
title: cem gate-verdict runner-input basis GRANTs a narrowed plan or a whole-omitted failed run with no selection or inventory uncertainty

acceptanceCriteria: A failing-first test shows a generic affected plan with a declared docs path read by a TS test via a string literal either selects that test or refuses the declaration with a named unknown.

body: Found while delivering GitHub #1751 (V1-2646, PR #1758, TJAA-V0-101). AFP-V0-160 moves a dirty path matched by .corvint/documentation-paths.json from UNOWNED_DIRTY_PATH into DECLARED_DOCUMENTATION and selects the tests whose recorded PathTokens/path literals read it. The TypeScript language plugin records neither, so in the generic `corvint affected` plan a TS/JS test that does readFileSync("docs/contracts/_setup.json") is never selected when that declared file changes: the plan can be BOUNDED and exclude the real reader. Expected: a TS test naming a declared path is selected, or the declaration is refused fail-closed as TJAA-V0-101 does for Playwright plans. Actual (inference from code reading, internal/liveverify/affected/documentation.go reader rule plus typescript plugin, not reproduced end to end): the reader is missed. The Playwright plan path is covered by TJAA-V0-101's contradiction check; the generic plan is not.

acceptanceCriteria: A spec records the owner-mapping grammar, its authority, and its failure modes before implementation.

body: GitHub #1751 asked for a project-owned declaration of dirty paths with no runtime reader, optionally with glob-to-owning-tests mapping. PR #1758 (TJAA-V0-101) records the existing AFP-V0-160 file/directory declaration in Playwright plans and refuses it on contradiction, but does not implement glob grammar or a mapping from a declared path pattern to the tests that own it. Non-goal of #1758; filed so it is not lost.

acceptanceCriteria: A Tasks command run from a directory outside the store repository can name the store explicitly, with focused tests and a spec requirement

body: Found while delivering V1-2649 / GitHub #1754 (ATR-V0-340..344, PR #1762, base 8200ba7c6ecc). A dispatch role may now start its worker in a ticket worktree of another repository (role cwd {worktree}). corvint-tasks resolves its store only from its working directory and has no store-root flag or env (corvint-tasks --help, 2026-10-25), so such a worker must run every claim, heartbeat and release as `cd {workRoot} && corvint-tasks ...`. Expected: a bounded way to name the store (for example CORVINT_TASKS_ROOT set by the dispatcher, or a --root flag) so a worker in another repository talks to the right store without changing directory. Actual: commands run from the code worktree find no store or the wrong one. Idea, not a confirmed defect.
title: corvint-tasks: no store-root option, so a dispatched worker started in another repository's worktree must cd to workRoot for every Tasks command

acceptanceCriteria: TestCALV0070_PinnedInventoryMutateParity compares outcomes (reports, errors, store bytes) and does not fail when the ChangeGuard legitimately falls back to the fresh inventory in one run but not the other, or the test isolates the watch from stray events so both runs take the same stages deterministically.

body: CI flake on batch PR #1748 head 60dbf9c75 (run 40196868668, job 121180028842, go-product-shard (4)); the batch does not touch internal/tasks/store. pinned_inventory_test.go:138 step 0: pinned stages [watched audited observed], ordinary [watched audited observed fresh], Err empty in both. observeMutation (mutate.go:340-376) falls back to the fresh inventory whenever watch.Check() reports a change, so the stage list depends on whether a filesystem event (plausibly late delivery from the test's own copyTree restore of the primary worktree just before the run) reaches the watch. That fallback is correct product behaviour; the test asserts the incidental stage sequence. Expected: parity of results, independent of watcher event timing. Actual: intermittent failure.

acceptanceCriteria: A failing-first test: a vitest repository whose test-less helper reads a declared docs path and is imported by one test; the generic plan with that dirty path selects the importing test or names an unknown.
The AFP-V0-021/AFP-V0-160 spec text and the TJAA-V0-102 residual are updated in the same change.
body: Found while delivering TJAA-V0-102 (PR #1768, branch claude/ts-gh1751-1737 at 8948d6fd8, base claude/batch-1025c 5852429b2). TypeScript units now record path literals, so graph.readers selects a unit whose PathTokens name a dirty path. The reader rule (internal/liveverify/affected/readers.go) does not traverse a reader to its dependents (AFP-V0-021), so a non-test helper module such as tests/helpers/contracts.ts that runs readFileSync('docs/contracts/_setup.json') is selected as a reader but contributes no check, and the tests that import it are excluded with NO_DEPENDENCY_PATH_TO_DIRTY_UNIT. Meanwhile documentationPaths still classifies the dirty path as DECLARED_DOCUMENTATION, and its reason says every path-literal reader is selected. Expected: a reader without its own test either selects its importing tests (traverse dependents from a path-literal reader) or raises a named unknown. Actual: scope BOUNDED, with zero checks reaching the reader. Recorded as a TJAA-V0-102 residual. The same shape probably affects Go and shell helper readers (suspected, not reproduced).
title: affected (generic plan): a test-less TypeScript helper that reads a declared documentation path selects no test; its importers are excluded while the path stays DECLARED_DOCUMENTATION

acceptanceCriteria: A test shows a resolved import specifier is not in a unit's PathTokens, while a readFileSync literal is.
The TJAA-V0-102 non-goal is updated; no reader that names a path through a non-import literal is dropped.
body: TJAA-V0-102 (PR #1768, 8948d6fd8) records the path-shaped tokens of every string literal, including import and require specifiers (for example './helper.js'). The generic reader rule matches a non-Go token by component runs and by lone file name (AFP-V0-072), so a dirty path such as docs/helper.js or any other helper.js selects every TS module that imports a same-named relative module, through PATH_LITERAL_READER. This over-selects; it never drops a reader. The import graph already owns specifiers. Expected: static import/export-from/require/dynamic-import specifiers that the TS import graph resolves are excluded from PathTokens. Actual: they are included. A non-goal recorded in TJAA-V0-102. Related: V1-1817 (shell lone-file-name over-selection).
title: affected (TypeScript): import specifiers are recorded as path tokens, so a dirty helper.js file name selects every module that imports any ./helper.js

acceptanceCriteria: A compile performs at most one full artifact encode, or the spec records why a second is required
Artifact bytes stay byte-identical (existing derivation fixture digests unchanged)
Build time on the over-bound fixture measured before and after
body: Version: branch claude/doccorpus-gh1665 at ae0a8c2c4 (PR #1769). internal/doccorpus/compile.go compileOnce calls hashSized(a) (a full deterministic JSON encode into sha256) and then Encode(a) only to check the output bound with the digest set, and the build command encodes the artifact a third time to write it. Expected: one encode whose bytes serve the bound check, the digest and the written output (or a size-only bound check derived from the hashed length plus the digest member). Actual: two full encodes per compile inside compileOnce, four on an over-bound build. Observed while timing V1-2613 (100 files x 700 defs, 128 MiB bound: 12.6 s after pinned reuse, encode is a large remaining share - inference, not profiled).
title: docs corpus: each compile encodes the artifact twice (hashSized then Encode) before the caller encodes it again to write

acceptanceCriteria: A supported public command (or a documented promotion of the assembler) produces a cem/1.0 stable bundle for an existing base..target without writing to the target repository or committing the map; its requirements are numbered in docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md (or a companion spec if CEM-V1 is at its obligation limit) with non-goals, failure modes and rollback.

An end-to-end test runs prepare -> cite -> the new bundle route -> `cem verify-stable` against a read-only fixture repository and gets accept true and a stable verdictSha256 across two runs; the tamper matrix still refuses a modified bundle.

Input-path rules (real paths, symlinked ancestors such as macOS $TMPDIR) are documented in `corvint help` for the route and either accepted after realpath resolution or refused with a typed reason naming the path; a test covers a /var -> /private/var style ancestor.
GitHub issue #1767 receives a reply naming the supported route once it lands.
body:
Reported as GitHub issue #1767 (adopter, build main-8200ba7). Observed at origin/main 3a8d87bb3.

An adopter that may only read the product repository builds cem/1.0 stable maps for already-merged commits with `cem prepare` in a disposable clone, `cem cite`, then `corvint-cem-candidate assemble-stable --experimental` (adding runner plan and receipt as artifacts), then `cem verify-stable --repository R --map M --artifacts DIR --expected-base B --target T`. That verifies (accept true, changeIntegrity VERIFIED, reproducible verdictSha256), but step 3 is an internal experimental binary: `cem export` requires the target to commit the map, and anchor/verdict-ledger have no out-of-tree mode. The assembler's input rules also changed without notice (it now refuses a path with a symlinked ancestor, which on macOS is every path under $TMPDIR).

Expected for RC3, where cem/1.0 is the only CEM: a supported, non-experimental route to produce a stable bundle (map plus declared artifacts) for an existing range without committing the map, verified later by `cem verify-stable`. Actual: only the experimental assembler does it.
title: cem/1.0 RC3: supported out-of-tree stable bundle for an existing base..target without committing the map (GH #1767)

acceptanceCriteria: verdicts() reports met exactly when low > 0 and high >= 0.20 x mean control miss, with a table test at the boundaries (inclusive endpoints).
The two CRT-V0-008 kill readings are emitted (upper bound below 0.10 absolute; seeded_vs_treatment upper bound <= 0.05) with tests.
The first-run report is not rescored or edited; the spec's CRT-V0-008 note that the scorer lags the accepted amendment is removed in the same change.
go test ./tools/cem-trial passes.
body:
The owner accepted the CRT-V0 2026-10-01 amendments on 2026-10-25 (V1-0836 closeout). The amended CRT-V0-008 gate reads: met when the BCa interval's lower bound exceeds 0 and the interval does not exclude the 20% target (0.20 x unrounded mean control miss); kill readings: an upper bound below 0.10 absolute rules out a 20% gain, and a seeded_vs_treatment upper bound at or below 0.05 reads as "the map's evidence adds nothing beyond its worklist".

Observed at origin/main 3a8d87bb3: tools/cem-trial/score.go verdicts() (about line 757) still requires `relative >= relativeGate && low > 0` for met and emits no kill readings; the spec said the scorer keeps the old reading until the amendment is accepted.

Expected: verdicts() implements the amended reading and the kill readings for every compared arm and for seeded_vs_treatment. Actual: pre-amendment reading. The 2026-10-24 held-out report (benchmarks/results/cem-reviewer-trial-first-run.json) is not rescored: both arms' lower bounds are below 0, so neither is met under either reading.
title: cem-trial scorer still prints the pre-amendment CRT-V0-008 gate reading after the owner accepted the 2026-10-01 amendment

acceptanceCriteria: The owner answers in a recorded decision: post-map entries only, or an amended CCE-V0 rule for historical entries against a pinned later map.
The CCE-V0 Shadow evaluation section and V1-1666 reflect the answer.
body: Observed 2026-10-25 (lane cce-shadow-1025). beamfall/core-history committed its first AMAP-V0 appmap.json at 11e8e74b5 (owner merge of core-history#46); there are 0 first-parent changes after it, so a window of post-map merges has 0 of the 30 required entries. The frozen gate's bug-fix entries are historical by definition (fix F, parent P), but BuildCatalog reads the map at each entry's head revision, and every core-history revision before 11e8e74b5 refuses `e2e-map-unavailable: manifest: appmap.json is absent at the evaluated revision`. Applying the later map to earlier trees would make the map a Corvint-chosen overlay rather than project-owned authority at that revision (invariants 3, 8), and the frozen gate values change only by owner decision. Question for the owner: wait for 30 post-map entries (at least 10 bug-fix) on an adopter, or amend CCE-V0 to let a registered window pin one project-owned map revision for historical entries (with how its digest binds and what refuses when an entry's tree does not contain the mapped routers). Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-25-cce-shadow-window-post-appmap.md.
title: CCE shadow: may a window's historical entries compile against a project-owned map committed only at a later revision?

acceptanceCriteria: Owner approves or rejects the rerun policy.
If approved, a failed shard reruns once automatically, the summary names flaky tests, and the flake rate is reported per week.
body: Audit: of 16 batch PR CI runs on 2026-10-24..25, 11 had at least one go-product-shard failure (20/240 shard jobs failed, 8%), mostly known flakes (git exit 128 V1-2633, corpus-http V1-2626, groupreap, CCE-021 V1-2616, tasks/store under load V1-1516). acceptanceCriteria: An inventory derived from code (dispatch switches/registries, not hand lists) covers every subcommand at every depth of corvint and of every cmd/ companion binary that has subcommands, plus every flag and every MCP tool across all MCP servers.
Every inventory node answers --help/-h with its own usage, flags, required inputs and one example, exit 0; a table-driven test proves it for all nodes.

Every node has a machine-readable catalog entry (corvint help --json or a per-binary `help --json` linked from it) and one LLM entry point (docs/CAPABILITIES.md plus a root llms.txt or equivalent) links all of it; shipped Claude/Codex/Gemini/OpenCode skill text points at the catalog.

The drift check fails (with tests proving it on a synthetic new subcommand, flag, binary and MCP tool lacking help or catalog) and runs in required CI; AGENTS.md states the rule for new functionality.
CAP-V0 spec updated (Failure modes gap closed) with traced requirement IDs.
body:
Owner request 2026-10-25: "ensure that llms can easily discover all functionality for corvint and its tooling, and this stays the case as things are further developed". CAP-V0 already gates top-level corvint commands, cmd/ binaries and corvint.* MCP tools, but its own Failure modes say subcommands outside the CAP-V0-007 tables (flows coverage/record, appmap build, switch-only verbs), flags and companion-binary subcommands (corvint-tasks, corvint-test e2e, etc.) are not gated; GH #1784 (V1-2684) is one symptom. Generalize: derive the inventory from the dispatch code at every depth for corvint and every companion binary, require per-node help and a catalog entry, and fail CI on drift.

2026-10-29 retained evidence: Observed Core1.0.0-rc.3.dev build1: corvint ocm link --help omits --expected-base and --target, but invoking its printed shape against a cem/1.0 map refuses expected-base-required. Full corvint help ocm documents both. Retain as command-discoverability evidence; no evidence of missing underlying capability.
SHA256 digests: aba1af0987e2be56585f18f77131e575352f00c035059bbc8840d6f0561cce2c. Operator ATTACH_EVIDENCE is not granted by current policy; retained here as prose evidence only, not a gate, acceptance decision or formal evidence attachment.
title: Every Corvint command, subcommand, companion binary and MCP tool is LLM-discoverable, with a drift gate that keeps it so

acceptanceCriteria: A dispatch `finished` event carries a structured outcome: exitCode, exitSignal, and stopReason (completed | operator-stop | context-limit | lease-expired | crash).

The event also carries facts the dispatcher observes itself: the commit SHAs created in the worker's working directory since launch, whether the attempt was released or handed off, and whether a handoff note was written.
The progress label is derived from those facts, not from the output stream. A signal-stopped session that made a commit is not reported as 'no progress', and a signal stop is named explicitly.
`message` is never filled from a mid-stream tool-output fragment: it uses the worker's last summary, or '(stopped before summary)'.
The finished event schema is documented in the dispatch reference and spec-backed, with tests for the signal-stop-with-commit case.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1799. When a dispatched worker exits on a signal (exit 130/143: operator stop, steward stop at a context limit, lease expiry), the `finished` event's message comes from the tail of the raw output stream, and its keys (at, detail, kind, message, profile, program, role, seq, ticket, worker) carry no structured outcome. In one observed case the session committed two minutes before it was stopped, yet the event said 'no progress'. Stop-loss consumers (hold a ticket after N no-op sessions) must regex free text and get false positives. Related: V1-1844 (warning/salvage fields on finished vs a stopped event), V1-1782 (carry-over of the final message).
title: GH #1799: dispatch finished event for a signal-stopped worker carries a raw stream fragment; add structured outcome (exit, stopReason, commits, handoff) and derive progress from facts

acceptanceCriteria: e2e catalog|obligations|compile|prove accept --repo ALIAS=ROOT and --manifest-repo ALIAS with the same semantics as flows appmap build.
The diff is taken in --root (application) and tests are read from the aliased root at a stated revision recorded in the report.
A two-repo fixture test covers catalog and obligations without a replay harness; spec requirements trace to it.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1802 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1802 corvint-test e2e: no support for an application repository plus a separate test repository (flows appmap build has --repo, CCE does not)
Observed on main-866a7fd (1.0.0-rc.3).

Many adopters keep the application (routers, templates, backend) in one repository and the hosted Playwright suite in another. `flows appmap build` supports that layout (`--repo ALIAS=ROOT`, `--manifest-repo ALIAS`, `tests.repo` in the manifest; AMAP-V0-017..020). `corvint-test e2e catalog|obligations|compile|prove` do not: they accept only `--root`, `--manifest` and revisions, and call the map build for a single root (`internal/changee2e/catalog.go` `appmap.Build(ctx, o.Root, manifest, rev)`). So:

- With `--root` = the test repository, the manifest's routers are not there and an application diff cannot be expressed at all.
- With `--root` = the application repository, the manifest and tests are not there (`e2e-map-unavailable: manifest: appmap.json is absent at the evaluated revision`).

Workaround used: a scratch clone of the application repository in which each change X is replayed as two synthetic commits, base' = X^ tree + the test tree under `e2e/` + a single-root copy of the manifest, and head' = X tree + the same overlay (diff base'..head' is byte-identical to X^..X). It works (catalog 2.3 s, obligations 4-6 s), but it is a hand-built harness, not a product path, and it pins the tests to one revision for both sides.

Expected: `e2e catalog|obligations|compile|prove` accept the same `--repo ALIAS=ROOT` / `--manifest-repo ALIAS` binds as `flows appmap build`, with the diff taken in `--root` (application) and the tests read from the aliased root at a stated revision, recorded in the report.

Why it matters: without it CCE cannot be adopted by a two-repository team without a replay harness, and no shadow window can be run there.

[comments: 0]
title: GH #1802: corvint-test e2e: support application repo plus separate test repo (--repo ALIAS=ROOT / --manifest-repo, as flows appmap build)

acceptanceCriteria: Every changed path is placed or listed under unknown with a reason; the verdict is full-suite-required when any path is neither.
ignored_paths is reserved for an explicit declared exemption.

Regression tests cover a Ruby-only change and a page-object-only change.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1803 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1803 flows appmap impact: non-UI changed paths and unbound page-object changes read no-navigation-impact with zero specs (not fail-closed)
Observed on main-866a7fd (1.0.0-rc.3), map built from 37 `ui-router-states/0` routers in an application repository with the hosted tests in an aliased repository.

`flows appmap impact` does not fail closed in two cases; it reports `verdict: no-navigation-impact` with `spec_files: []` and nothing under `unknown`:

1. **Non-UI changed paths are dropped.** `internal/appmap/impact.go` increments `ignored_paths` for any changed path that is not placed and whose extension is not in `impactUIExtensions`. A real change of 10 Ruby files (models and workers behind a UI screen) read `changed_paths: 10, ignored_paths: 10, verdict: no-navigation-impact`. A synthetic one-line change to one model, and a new Ruby file, each read the same. A server-side change can break any screen; "no navigation impact" is true, but a consumer that selects tests from `spec_files` gets an empty set.
2. **A changed page object that no manifest binding places on a screen selects nothing.** With a single-root map, a one-line change to a page-object file read `no-navigation-impact`, `spec_files: []`, while `corvint affected --path <same file>` on the test repository selects 66 units, 12 of them specs that import that page object.

For contrast, unplaced `.ts` changes do fail closed (`full-suite-required`, unknown `reference-graph-bound`), and a changed spec file selects that spec.

Expected: every changed path is either placed (screens/specs) or listed under `unknown` with a reason, and the verdict is `full-suite-required` whenever any path is neither; `ignored` is reserved for an explicit, declared exemption (as CCE's `reach_exempt`). A changed test-support file (page object, fixture, helper) either resolves through the test import graph to the specs that import it, or reads unknown.

CCE `e2e obligations` on the same inputs correctly reads `UNKNOWN` with `unplaced-path` for every one of these spans, so the two relations disagree on the same diff.

[comments: 0]
title: GH #1803: flows appmap impact: non-UI and unbound page-object changes read no-navigation-impact with zero specs (must fail closed)

### #1804 affected --appmap-impact refuses an impact report from the application repository in a two-repository layout
Observed on main-866a7fd (1.0.0-rc.3).

`corvint affected --base FULL_COMMIT_ID --appmap-impact REPORT` refuses a report built for another repository:

`{"code": "appmap-invalid-query", "error": "the impact report for app admin was not built for --base <test-repo sha> at HEAD <test-repo sha>"}`

In a two-repository layout (application in one repository, hosted Playwright suite in another, map built with `--repo`/`--manifest-repo`), the application change lives in the application repository's history, so `flows appmap impact` must run with `--root` = the application repository. GitHub beamfall/corvint#1805 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1805 flows appmap build: injected state-name enum behind an export-star barrel reads not-read-whole import-chain-bindings
Observed on main-866a7fd (1.0.0-rc.3), `flows appmap build` on an AngularJS application whose routers name states through an injected constant: `$stateProvider.state(StateConstants.ADD_ONS, {...})`.

The constant is registered as `.constant('StateConstants', RoutesConstants)` in one module that imports `RoutesConstants` from `./routes`; `./routes/index.ts` is `export * from './routes.constants'`; `routes.constants.ts` declares `export enum RoutesConstants { CLUB = 'app.club', ... }` with only literal string members (about 200).

With `di_constants` set to the registering file, and again with the registering file plus the `routes` directory, the map reads one unknown `{kind: di-constant, ref: StateConstants, reason: not-read-whole, detail: import-chain-bindings}` and 153 states stay `non-literal-name` (23 screens, 10 resolved, 43%). Expected: either an `export * from` barrel one level behind the import is read when the target module declares the table exactly once and nothing else in scope rebinds it, or the unknown names the hop and binding that failed (`path:line`, binding name) so an adopter can fix the scope.

acceptanceCriteria: A two-root impact mode returns test-repo units affected by an application diff, with explicit UNKNOWN for unbound application paths, never an empty set.
impact can be evaluated at an explicit revision without a working-tree checkout, or refuses typed.
The guarantee (unmapped path -> UNKNOWN or full-suite fallback) is documented in the spec and help.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1808 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1808 impact: no cross-repository closure (application repo -> separate test repo) and no explicit-revision mode
## Problem

In a layout where the application lives in one repository and its browser tests in another, impact analysis cannot answer "which tests in the test repository does this application change affect?":

- `impact` (CLI and MCP) works inside one root. Its reverse closure stops at the repository boundary, so an application diff never reaches the test files that drive it through HTTP/UI.
- `impact` cannot be run at an explicit revision of either repository. An adopter evaluating selection against historical changes, such as replaying past merges or applying synthetic mutants at a pinned revision, must check out each revision and rebuild the index.

Related: #1802 (CCE has no application-repo plus test-repo mode) and #1804 (`affected --appmap-impact` refuses an impact report from the application repository). This issue is about impact analysis itself.

## Request

1. A two-root mode: `impact --app-root A --test-root T --base REV` that returns test-repository units affected by an application-repository diff, with an explicit UNKNOWN (never an empty set) for application paths that have no binding to any test.
2. `--at REV` (or `--revision`) for both roots, reading from an index snapshot of that revision without a working-tree checkout.
3. Document the guarantee: an unmapped application path yields UNKNOWN or a full-suite fallback, never "no tests affected".

[comments: 0]

acceptanceCriteria: An over-bound file becomes a per-path UNKNOWN, or is skipped when it matches a declared generated/vendored pattern; never a whole-run failure.

body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1811 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1811 affected discovery: one over-bound file in the repository walk aborts the whole run (generated bundle), forcing a full-suite fallback
## Problem

`affected discovery` (the Playwright two-step selection) aborts the whole run when one file in the repository walk is larger than its bound:

```
{"code": "unsupported-playwright-discovery", "error": "affected: repository walk exceeds its bound: \"public/frontend/admin/main.js\" is 12666662 bytes", "ok": false}
```

The file is a committed, generated frontend bundle (about 12.6 MB). Nothing the test suite imports reaches it, but because of this one file every selection on that repository falls back to the full suite. The run took 8.9 s before failing.

## Request

1. Treat an over-bound file as an explicit per-path UNKNOWN (or skip it as generated, if it matches a declared generated or vendored pattern), never as a whole-run failure.
2. Let a repository declare generated or vendored paths (bundles, minified assets) that the walk excludes, with the exclusion visible in the plan.
3. Report which bound was hit and how to raise it (flag or config) in the error.
4. Fail closed only for changes that actually touch the unknown path. A change elsewhere should still narrow.

acceptanceCriteria: ticket create --template offers a complete valid payload skeleton with defaults and the queue's native source.
Or omitted nullable keys default to null and source defaults to the native queue.
A MALFORMED reports every missing or invalid key with its expected shape in one error.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1812 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1812 ticket create: template gives no valid skeleton; closed payload refuses omitted nullable keys and source needs an undocumented shape
## Problem

`ticket create --template` describes the fields, but the payload is a closed object that requires every key, nullable ones included. An operator writing a payload from the template hits repeated MALFORMED errors, for example:

```
MALFORMED: /payload: closed object violated (missing keys: owner, order, source, estimateMinutes, supersedes, supersededBy)
```

The template marks these keys `nullable`, but leaving one out is refused, and `source` needs an internal shape (`kind`, `sourceItemId`, `sourceQueueId`, `sourceRevisionSha256`) that the template does not give as a value. Creating one operator ticket took four attempts.

## Request

1. `ticket create --template --skeleton` (or similar) prints a complete, valid payload with defaults (nulls, empty arrays, the queue's native `source`), ready to edit.
2. Or: accept omitted nullable keys as null, and default `source` to the native queue.
3. Report every missing or invalid key in one error, with its expected shape.

[comments: 0]

acceptanceCriteria: pool hold --pool P [--member M] --holder H --lease-minutes N --reason TEXT, plus renew and release, are journaled like allocations and visible in queue status.
Dispatch ordering honours holds; a maximum hold length bounds abandoned holds.
The supported way to run an operator job on a pool member is documented.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1813 (reporter ls-russell-lewis, observed on main-866a7fd 1.0.0-rc.3).

### #1813 pool: no operator hold for a member outside a dispatched session (placeholder ticket plus unrenewed lease today)
## Problem

An operator who needs a pool member (a disposable test environment) for maintenance or evaluation work, outside any dispatched worker session, has no direct way to hold one. The only path is to create a placeholder ticket, claim an attempt on it with `--pool`, and rely on a lease that is renewed only by the dispatcher's keepLease for a supervised session. For a hand-run job, the lease is not renewed, and the claim is tied to a ticket that represents no real work.

## Request

1. `pool hold --pool P [--member M] --holder H --lease-minutes N --reason TEXT` (and `pool renew`, `pool release`), recorded in the journal like any allocation, visible in `queue status`, and honoured by dispatch ordering.
2. Optionally a maximum hold length and an automatic release on holder process exit, so an abandoned hold cannot pin a member.
3. Document the supported way to run an operator job on a pool member.

[comments: 0]

acceptanceCriteria: An OUT_OF_SCOPE claim refusal lists the ticket's declared touch paths, the rejected requested paths, and a nextAction naming the retry.
A requested --scope that is a subset of the declared touch paths is admitted.
ticket show exposes the declared claim scope (effects.touchPaths) at the top level.
Tests cover the refusal payload, subset admission and the show field; the spec is updated in the same change.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1818 (observed on 1.0.0-rc.3).

### claim: OUT_OF_SCOPE refusal names neither the ticket's declared touch paths nor the retry (omit --scope); agents stop instead
## Problem

When a ticket declares `effects.touchPaths` and a claim passes `--scope` with any other path, the claim fails with a bare `FAILED: OUT_OF_SCOPE`. The refusal does not say:
- which paths the ticket declares,
- that omitting `--scope` claims with the ticket's own scope,
- whether the requested path is outside the declaration or just a different spelling of it.

Agents read a bare refusal as a policy denial and stop rather than retry. Measured in one deployment: 8 dispatched sessions over 3 days ended "blocked before work" on this refusal (three tickets, two roles). Each needed an operator diagnosis to find that the fix was simply to drop `--scope`.

## Request

1. The OUT_OF_SCOPE result carries the declared touch paths, the rejected path(s), and a `nextAction` such as "retry without --scope to claim the declared scope".
2. Consider accepting a requested scope that is a subset of the declared touch paths, and refusing only real widening.
3. `ticket show` exposes the declared claim scope next to `claimabilityScope`, so a caller can check it before claiming.
title: GH #1818: claim OUT_OF_SCOPE refusal names neither the declared touch paths nor how to retry

acceptanceCriteria: The dispatcher can re-exec on a new build while live sessions finish under their existing attempt and lease, and new launches use the new build.
Journal/state compatibility between the two builds is checked first; an incompatible pair refuses with a reason and falls back to a drain.
dispatch upgrade --check NEW_BUILD reports whether the switch can be rolling without changing state.
Tests cover a rolling switch with a live attempt and a refused incompatible switch; the spec records the contract and rollback.
body:
GitHub beamfall/corvint#1815 (observed on 1.0.0-rc.3).

### dispatch: every build upgrade needs a full drain (no rolling upgrade); frequent adopters lose hours of launches
## Problem

Moving a running dispatcher to a new Corvint build requires a drain: no new sessions start until every live session has ended, then the dispatcher restarts on the new build. An adopter who takes every main merge (to pick up fixes quickly) pays for that drain each time. Measured over two days: 17 drains, each 6 to 60 minutes, and about 3.5 hours without a single launch on one day. Live sessions that run long (30+ minutes) set the drain length, and anything waiting (reviews, queued runs) stalls behind them.

## Request

1. A rolling upgrade: the dispatcher re-execs on the new build at once. Live sessions keep running and finish under the attempt and lease they already hold, and new launches use the new build. Journal and state compatibility between adjacent builds is checked up front (refuse with a reason when it doesn't hold, and only then fall back to a drain).
2. Or, if a drain is unavoidable: a documented, bounded switch that hands live attempts over (HANDOFF with state preserved) instead of waiting for them to end naturally.
3. A `dispatch upgrade --check NEW_BUILD` that reports whether the switch can be rolling, before an adopter schedules it.
title: GH #1815: dispatch build upgrade needs a full drain; add a rolling upgrade and an upgrade --check

acceptanceCriteria: The decision (fix the tests versus accept system-symlinked ancestors in --detail-file) is recorded with its reason against the pool spec.
The five PSR CLI tests pass on darwin with the default TMPDIR under /var/folders, and on Linux.
A regression test covers a detail file under a symlinked ancestor with the chosen behavior.
body:
Observed in `make gate` at 866a7fd52 (1.0.0-rc.3 candidate) on the darwin host, 2026-10-25; log /private/tmp/rc3-gate-866a7fd5.log around line 47787.

Failing tests in internal/tasks/cli: TestPSRV0265_DispatchHoldsStalledPoolLaunchesCLI, TestPSRV0267_PlanSelectedRoleReportsStalledPoolCLI, TestPSRV0260_PoolObserveStallsQuarantinedMember, TestPSRV0260_PoolObserveFlagsAndState, TestPSRV0263_PoolSummaryWhenEveryMemberStalled. Each `pool observe --detail-file <t.TempDir()>/health.log` returns:

`UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM: /var/folders/.../001/health.log: cannot open: openat var: not a directory`

On macOS /var is a symlink to /private/var, so the no-symlinked-ancestor open refuses every default TMPDIR path. The gate lane called it a flake because the package passed on an isolated rerun, but that rerun ran on WSL Linux, where /var is a real directory, so the rerun proves nothing about darwin. This is the same class as completed V1-0753 and V1-0960 (TMPDIR with a symlinked ancestor).

Expected: either the tests resolve their temp dir (filepath.EvalSymlinks) as the V1-0753/V1-0960 fixes did, or `pool observe --detail-file` accepts an operator-named detail file whose ancestors are system symlinks, as the product contract decides. Blocks a clean rc.3 full gate on darwin.
title: rc.3 gate (darwin): pool observe --detail-file refuses macOS TMPDIR with UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM 'openat var: not a directory'; 5 PSR CLI tests fail

acceptanceCriteria: A decision record states whether, and with what evidence, a package-named extends may leave paths/baseUrl known.
If adopted, a fixture whose extends package declares no paths resolves @playwright/test as external while an undeclared alias stays unresolved.
body: Found in V1-2700 (#1806). AMAP-V0-195 reuses contextindex.WebImportResolver. When the tsconfig that governs a test file extends a package (e.g. @tsconfig/node20/tsconfig.json) that the index does not hold, the resolver reads paths/baseUrl as unknown and returns Unresolved for every bare specifier. The map keeps those unresolved, with detail 'specifier X (config resolution unknown)', so @playwright/test imports turn every join in that subtree UNKNOWN. That is fail-closed and correct, but it may blank adopter maps. Expected: decide whether a known package-only base config (no paths/baseUrl) can be proven safe, e.g. by reading node_modules when tracked or by a declared assertion. Actual: the whole subtree's joins are UNKNOWN. Repro: TestAMAPV0195ResolverRefusalAndComputedLoadStayUnknown.
title: appmap test imports: a package-named tsconfig extends makes every bare test import unresolved

acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether MMR-V0 admits a two-alias corvint.impact call; the decision is recorded in docs/build-log or an MMR-V0 amendment.

If admitted: corvint.impact accepts both aliases, returns the same impact-two-root/0 bytes as the CLI for the same inputs, and a parity test covers it; if not: docs/MCP-SERVER.md names the CLI as the two-root path.
body: Found 2026-10-25 in lane claude/two-repo-layout-1025b (V1-2701, GitHub #1808). CLI `corvint impact --app-root DIR --test-root ALIAS=ROOT` (ANL-V0-064..067) now builds the application map with tests from an aliased root and answers impact-two-root/0. The MCP tool corvint.impact (internal/mcp/bridge/bridge.go callImpact) stays single-root. Expected (coordinator request): the MCP impact path matches the CLI. Actual blocker: multi-root MCP MMR-V0-005 (decision 0441, owner-accepted) says a tool call MUST reach only the repository its `repository` alias names, and MMR-V0-007 binds each call to one repository, so a cross-root impact call needs an owner amendment of MMR-V0 (for example an explicit two-alias argument whose aliases both come from the server's --repo set). Question for the owner: amend MMR-V0 to allow a two-alias impact call, or keep MCP single-root and document the CLI as the two-root path. Recorded as an ANL-V0 non-goal until decided.
title: Should MCP corvint.impact gain a two-root mode matching CLI impact --app-root/--test-root? MMR-V0-005 forbids a call reaching a second repository

acceptanceCriteria: A run with a seeding 500 shows the server exception next to the failing test.

body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1825. When a test failure (or hook failure) includes an HTTP 5xx from the system under test, attach the matching server error record from a run's server error log: match on method + path + time window (and request id when logged); include exception class, message and first application frame; mark environment/fixture when raised from test-support paths; report unmatched 5xx explicitly as server error not found in log; group repeated identical fixture exceptions across runs.
title: GH #1825: attach the server-side exception to a test that failed on an HTTP 5xx from fixture seeding

acceptanceCriteria: Records are current, stale-unconfirmed, retired or UNKNOWN by linked-path change in C..R and revision distance.

A shared staleness evaluator for INGESTED / LOCALLY_OBSERVED UI records: current if no linked screen/template/route path changed in C..R, otherwise stale-unconfirmed, retired after a configured distance. title: GH #1830: shared staleness evaluator for observed UI records by revision distance over linked source paths

Measured in the lane: after AFP-V0-446 removed the 27 testdata sites, LANGUAGE_FRONTIER 107 -> 80 on #1816 and 108-118 -> 81-91 across the last 20 merged ci:batched PRs; the remaining 80 are all plugin-wide sites raised through participants(). On PR #1816 the gateselect closure added 52 Go packages to `corvint test --dry-run` that the plan does not select and that no non-test import path connects to the dirty package; across the last 20 merged ci:batched PRs it added 1-55 packages per PR (0 unsound by `go list -deps`). STR-V0-061 (this lane) makes `corvint test` use SelectStructural (rules (a)-(c) + AFP-V0-023) and take rule (d) from the plan's UNBOUNDED_READER selections, so `corvint test` and `make gate-affected` now differ on rule (d). Expected: one reachability implementation (planner graph) feeds both consumers, or gateselect's closure stops at test-only edges and drops token-holder runs, with TestSelectStructuralLeavesRuleDToThePlan_STRV0061 and TestSTRV0007UniversePlacementEqualsCIPlan as the parity oracles. Spec: docs/specs/session-test-runner-v0.md STR-V0-002/061; docs/specs/affected-plan-v0.md AFP-V0-012.
title: gateselect.Select's rule (d) closure follows test imports and path-token holders transitively and names packages the planner proves unreachable; share one reachability with internal/liveverify/affected

body: Playwright reports pool in corvint runs stability|compare|reusable only on config.metadata.corvintRunIdentity (PWR-V0-002), but nothing produces it and the spec does not define how applicationRevision, configDigest and testFileBlobs are computed. Observed in an adopter: three same-commit full-suite reports gave insufficient 246, deterministic 0, every test IDENTITY_INPUT_MISSING. title: GH #1835 runs: ship a corvintRunIdentity producer, document its rules in PWR-V0, report missing identity once per run

acceptanceCriteria: Either the harness user-prompt receipt's coverage.packet_bytes equals the canonical byte length of the written context member, with a test, or the owning spec states exactly which bytes packet_bytes counts for harness packets and a test pins that definition
body: Observed 2026-10-25 by the V1-2716 lane with the origin/main corvint binary (0245855002c84e45e41e8a63036d48f83df2c4fa) on a small fixture repository with a root AGENTS.md: `corvint --root R harness event --host opencode --host-version 2.1.3 --surface plugin --adapter-version 0.7.19 --event user-prompt --input -` with input {sessionIdSha256, task:"repair the parser"} returns context.coverage.packet_bytes=951 while the written context member canonicalizes to 1004 bytes (state OUT_OF_SCOPE, 0 results); removing any single member (request 881, mode 989, schema_version 985, state 981, verification 968 ...) does not reproduce 951, so the count appears to be taken before several harness members are added. acceptanceCriteria: On a PR and main push with all CI-observable rows PASSED and only independent-external-consumer NOT_OBSERVED, cem-release-readiness succeeds, and its summary plus a warning annotation name the row and V1-0014.

body: Owner-approved 2026-10-25. Today .github/workflows/cem-release-gate.yml job cem-release-readiness exits 3 on every PR and main push because the independent-external-consumer row (V1-0014) is NOT_OBSERVED, which no CI host can observe. That makes the check permanently red and hides real regressions in CI-observable rows. Change: the PR/main job fails only when a CI-observable row is not PASSED; the external-consumer row is reported NOT_OBSERVED in the step summary and as a ::warning:: annotation naming V1-0014. The release path (aggregate readiness used for tag/promote) stays strict and still refuses while that row is unobserved. Amend AFP-V0-432 in the same change.
title: cem-release-readiness on PRs/main fails only on CI-observable rows; external-consumer row is a visible known blocker

acceptanceCriteria: A real-shape Playwright 1.64 trace fixture with string stacks call ids is accepted by observe --records and binds code locations to its actions in a focused test.

body:
Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1852 (2026-10-25), main 4a94b88f9, 30 trace zips from @playwright/test 1.64.0 chromium (trace on, dom+aria snapshots, sources true).

Observed: `flows appmap observe --records` refuses 30 of 30 real trace zips with appmap-invalid-query "trace zip stacks entry is not a stacks document". internal/appmap/uirecords.go decodes each stacks pair as [int, frames] and keys the action as call@<int>; real N-trace.stacks entries carry the string call id (e.g. "wcuw@676"), so the first pair fails and the whole trace is refused. One malformed stacks entry discards the whole trace.

Expected: string call ids are accepted and matched to the action callId with the entry prefix; the integer form keeps working; a malformed stacks entry marks stacks unavailable for that entry (trace-without-stacks) and the trace still yields screens, transitions and endpoints. A real-shape fixture covers the Playwright 1.64 layout.

Version: corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 760). Multi-context zips are V1-1202.
title: GH #1852: flows appmap observe --records refuses every real Playwright 1.64 trace because stacks call ids are strings

Measured on batch 1025i CI run 40246146353 (2026-10-25, 8 self-hosted go-product shards, go test -json Elapsed). The 347 packages took 15,757 s of test time. The 20 slowest top-level tests take about 3,950 s, which is 25% of the total, and each one alone is longer than most packages:

- 418 s internal/tasks/store TestLGLV0009_SealedBaseDeclinesRewrittenSegment
- 276 s internal/doccorpus TestDCPV1216LegacyDiscoveryGitOpsIndependentOfPathCount
- 217 s internal/tasks/store TestLGLV0009_SealedBaseDeclinesChangedState
- 207 s cmd/corvint TestPackSnapshotReadsWithoutChangingAByteOnTwentyTasks
- 204 s internal/doccorpus TestDCRV1552ParallelScanMatchesSequential
- 199 s internal/docviews TestVerifyRejectsCanonicalBundleOver64MiB
- 197 s tools/corvint-pr-tests TestAFPV0048ShardedRunExecutesSlices
- 189 s internal/tasks/store TestCALV0089_ProgramWallExpiryEndsContinuation
- 173 s internal/doccorpus/selfcorpus TestCorpusSelfDocumentation
- 170 s internal/tasks/store TestJSGV0020_HarnessRunsBothModes
- 169 s internal/tasks/store TestCALV0044_HandoffPolicyReceiptInterval
- 165 s internal/companionrelease TestCorvintBundledBinariesBuildTwiceIdentically
- 159 s internal/doccorpus TestDCPV1216SymbolAnchorsGitOpsIndependentOfAnchorCount
- 159 s cmd/corvint TestBlobShardsReadOnlyTwentyTaskMatrix
- 153 s internal/doccorpus TestDCPV1091TestKnowledgeQueryExposure
- 151 s internal/doccorpus TestDCPV1216PlaywrightDiscoveryGitOpsIndependentOfPathCount
- 147 s internal/tasks/store TestATRV0297_ReassignRemovesPriorStageWorktrees
- 146 s internal/tasks/store TestLGLV0009_PoolVerbsResumeFromSealedBase
- 146 s internal/tasks/store TestCALV0371_MovedWorktreeKeepsItsRecord

A single test cannot be split across shards, so these set a floor on shard wall time and on every lane run that selects them. Likely causes to check per test: fixture sizes larger than the property needs (64 MiB bundle, twenty-task matrices, path-count scaling sweeps), repeated builds of the same binaries, and serial subtests that could run in parallel. Related, not duplicated: V1-0961 and V1-1108 (internal/tasks/store package time and mutexes), V1-0643 (doccorpus hermetic fixtures), V1-1753 (shard balance), V1-1100 (per-test cost table).
title: tests: the 20 slowest single tests take 25% of CI test time (145-418 s each; LGLV0009 418 s)

acceptanceCriteria: N LookupTreeEntry calls inside one object session spawn at most one git cat-file process, proven by a test that counts spawns
Results stay byte-identical to the current per-call lookup (differential test over the existing gitauth fixtures)
TestDCPV1216SymbolAnchorsGitOpsIndependentOfAnchorCount measured before/after with heavy.sh, target under 60 s on CI with -race, spec sizes unchanged
body: Found in V1-2740 (Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 761, origin/main 4a94b88f9). Repository.lookupTreeEntry (internal/cem/gitauth/object.go:382) opens a fresh streamCommitBatch (commitstream.go:179) for every call, including inside BeginObjectSession, so each lookup pays about 2.1-2.3 ms of process spawn on WSL2. Reproduction: heavy.sh go test -count=1 -run TestDCPV1216SymbolAnchorsGitOpsIndependentOfAnchorCount ./internal/doccorpus takes about 34 s, almost all in the per-path oracle (about 10,000 lookups for the DCP-V1-216 5,000-anchor size); CI run 40246146353 took 159 s under -race. Expected: lookups within one object session reuse one long-lived cat-file --batch process (or the session's tree cache), so N lookups cost one spawn. Actual: one spawn per lookup. Distinct from V1-2657 (one batch per pinned revision in pin verification) and V1-2560 (legacy discovery one op per tree).
title: gitauth LookupTreeEntry spawns one git cat-file batch per call even inside an object session (about 2.2 ms per lookup)

body: Found in V1-2740 (Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 761, origin/main 4a94b88f9). TestCorpusSelfDocumentation (internal/doccorpus/selfcorpus) builds a contextindex over the whole checkout; it takes 13.7 s without -race and 129.4 s with -race on WSL2 heavy.sh, 173 s on CI run 40246146353. A CPU profile shows the top self cost in documentRecord's documentReference.FindAllString (internal/contextindex/parse.go:24, about 7%), the sourceImports regexes (parse.go:721), go/parser and termCounter. Expected: path-reference and import extraction use a linear byte scan (or a cheap prefilter before the regex) so the index build is not regex-bound. Actual: regexp dominates. The whole-checkout build is the property DCP-V1-019 self-documentation proves, so the test itself cannot shrink.
title: contextindex whole-repository build spends most race time in documentReference and sourceImports regexes (selfcorpus 129 s under -race)

body: Found by the #1665 residual lane 2026-10-26 (branch claude/residual-1751-1665, head 9bc2fddee). acceptanceCriteria: Per-declaration encoded size measured before and after on the over-bound fixture and recorded in a build-log entry
Per-declaration cost reduced substantially (target at most half of 1.9 KB) or the spec records why not
Ranking fixtures and declaration recovery tests still pass
body: Measured by the #1665 residual lane 2026-10-26: each derived declaration costs about 1.9 KB in the encoded artifact (about 2.4 KB from the reporter's numbers on beamfall/corvint#1665). With a 114 MB artifact, only about 8-10k of the reporter's 40,601 declarations fit under the 128 MiB output limit, so a derive filter is mandatory. Expected: a much smaller per-declaration encoding so most declarations fit without a filter. Actual: the bound truncates them.
title: docs corpus: each derived declaration costs ~1.9-2.4 KB, so only ~8-10k of 40k fit beside a 114 MB artifact under the 128 MiB bound (GH #1665)

acceptanceCriteria: The spec records the rationale for the corpus artifact bound, which today is unstated
A recorded decision picks option 1, 2, 3 or a combination for #1665-scale corpora, with measured memory (RSS) and size at the reporter's scale
Follow-up implementation tickets are filed or linked (V1-2748 for option 1)
body: MaxCorpusBytes = 128 << 20 (internal/doccorpus/capacity.go:147, DCP-V1-033, added 2026-09-28 in 5ebb216b8) caps the /2 corpus artifact, and the decoder refuses larger input (artifact_decode.go:66, :602). No spec or decision records why 128 MiB; it matches the repo-wide 128 MiB size class, and the whole Artifact is held in memory, so the bound likely protects RSS. Decision 0001 already names the 128 MiB boundary as not meeting the RSS/scale goals and targets a range-read, block-verified immutable format. GH #1665: a 114 MB four-repo corpus keeps only ~8-10k of 40,601 derived declarations. Options: (1) shrink per-declaration encoding (V1-2748), (2) raise the bound (moves the wall; memory grows), (3) move the corpus onto the decision-0001 range-read format (the real fix, the biggest job). Raised by the owner 2026-10-26.
title: docs corpus: decide how large corpora get past the 128 MiB artifact bound (shrink per declaration, raise the bound, or range-read immutable format)

body: Value audit 2026-10-26 (owner: 'If corvint costs more then its pointless'), four-panel read-only audit of V1-2717 runs v2717/v2717b/v2717c in /private/tmp/claude-501/sbp-v2717*/ and ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db; panel data in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/{forensics,retrieval,agent-integration,methodology}/. CONFIRMED: in v2717c-p07-on the agent called the plugin's Code Mode `execute` 6 times and fetched proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org, then edited go.sum 13 times (23 steps vs 8 off; $0.734 vs $0.215, 90% of the rerun's +$0.567 gap). The off arm has no `execute` tool, so the plugin added a network path the harness had denied. Expected: Code Mode honours the host's tool and network denials (no fetch when webfetch is denied), or refuses network by default.
title: OpenCode plugin Code Mode execute reaches the network while the host denies webfetch and websearch

acceptanceCriteria: SessionStart emits dogfood workflow guidance only for repositories enrolled in Corvint dogfood; a foreign-repo fixture shows none.
Claude Code and OpenCode produce the same context selection for the same prompt and revision, or the spec names the intended difference.
