Use this explicit key and root for begin, verify, review and finish' for a foreign repository (~330 tokens per session of pure overhead). Also UserPromptSubmit there returned 15/17 anchors missing and a different profile than OpenCode's frame for the same task.
title: Claude Code SessionStart injects Corvint dogfood workflow argv into repositories that are not Corvint

acceptanceCriteria: The frame abstains when the prompt already names an existing path, when no anchor resolves, or when no row has more than syntax authority; replay on the 10 V2717 prompts shows which abstain.
The injected frame is under 200 tokens when it carries rows (rows plus one-line disclosure).
Rows are distinct files in score order; a same-name declared in 2+ non-test files is demoted absent a path anchor; junk anchors are stripped.
An offline replay over the ContextBench SWE-bench-Pro rows reports, for the frame, P@2 and the share of tasks holding a gold file absent from the rg-idf top 5.
body: Value audit 2026-10-26 (owner: 'If corvint costs more then its pointless'), four-panel read-only audit of V1-2717 runs v2717/v2717b/v2717c in /private/tmp/claude-501/sbp-v2717*/ and ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db; panel data in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/{forensics,retrieval,agent-integration,methodology}/. CONFIRMED (retrieval replay with pinned 0.7.26 binary, byte-identical to the trial probe on 6/6): only 9.5% of frame bytes (68 of ~713 tokens) point at gold files; ~80% is envelope and the prompt-bound disclosure. Frame hit@1 4/8 and file precision 0.41 vs idf-weighted identifier rg hit@1 6/8. Every row is syntax/medium with identical reasons. Agents reached a gold file at step 0-1 in every pair without the frame; on/off steps were equal (84 vs 84) when the frame held gold. Defects: same-name sibling symbols win (p01,p08,p09,p10; evalRankSymbols internal/contextindex/eval_query.go:734-818); one file can fill all 5 rows and rows are not score-ordered (evalConfidentSymbols :1044-1180, p04); READY with 5 irrelevant rows when gold files do not exist yet (p07); BUDGETED drops a frame whose top-2 holds gold (p09); queries carry junk anchors (/app, pr_description, *, ^). Break-even: frame ~$0.005/session vs ~$0.023/turn.
title: Harness context frame: abstain unless it adds signal, cut the envelope, fix row selection

acceptanceCriteria: A trial receipt records the exact injected frame bytes (or digest plus stored file) per session, probed on the base tree.
Receipts carry a per-step ledger (tokens, tool, cost) and grader per-test results.
A checked-in paired-analysis script reports per-pair deltas, bootstrap CI on the cost ratio and McNemar on resolution.
The trial harness has a shell-enabled mode with network still denied.
body: Value audit 2026-10-26 (owner: 'If corvint costs more then its pointless'), four-panel read-only audit of V1-2717 runs v2717/v2717b/v2717c in /private/tmp/claude-501/sbp-v2717*/ and ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db; panel data in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/{forensics,retrieval,agent-integration,methodology}/. CONFIRMED gaps: the V2717 receipts and opencode.db do not persist the injected frame text or ranked packet (the panel had to replay it); frame_probe runs on the agent-edited checkout rather than the base tree; receipts carry no per-step token ledger and no grader per-test output (p05 flips across 3 runs and its failing test is NOT_OBSERVED); the harness denies the shell so test-selection value cannot be exercised; there is no paired-analysis tool (pooled ratio 1.10 [1.01,1.20] was computed ad hoc; same-arm noise ±13-15%, off-arm per-session SD $0.039).
title: Paired agent trials must persist the injected frame, per-step ledger and grader per-test output

acceptanceCriteria: Step 0 (free, offline): run corvint affected on all retained V2717 off-arm patches at base; report per task whether FAIL_TO_PASS tests' units are selected and selected/total package share. Kill if the target is missed in >2/10 or >50% of packages are selected.

Step 1 (owner approval, ~$10-20): shell-on paired run with network denied, file paths stripped from prompts, a ~30-token post-edit 'run: <selected tests>' digest and frame abstention; confirm only if on-arm cost per resolved beats off across two repeats and PASS_TO_PASS breakage falls.
Result recorded as a build-log entry and receipt.
body: Value audit 2026-10-26 (owner: 'If corvint costs more then its pointless'), four-panel read-only audit of V1-2717 runs v2717/v2717b/v2717c in /private/tmp/claude-501/sbp-v2717*/ and ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db; panel data in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/{forensics,retrieval,agent-integration,methodology}/. Verdict of the audit: prompt-time context injection cannot pay on SWE-bench-Pro-shaped tasks (agents localize in 1-2 ops; oracle ceiling 5-8%; frame equals token overhead; pooled cost +10%, no resolve gain). The one untested plausible lever is post-edit verification: `corvint affected` in 0.3-0.9 s selected 3 units including the target for p05, 25 units for p10, nothing for p04 (Python). Literature precedent: TDAD regressions 6.08% -> 1.82%. Also V2716 fusion never reaches the harness frame (cmd/corvint/harness_context.go:86-90, query_widening.go:15-26), so V2716 precision is not an agent-value lever as wired.
title: Does diff-time test selection (affected) pay for a coding agent? Offline replay, then a small shell-on paired run

acceptanceCriteria: runtime.Caller/runtime.Callers/runtime.FuncForPC are not file-read witnesses; a fixture mirroring navidrome log/log.go selects only the edited package's dependents.
The p06 replay selects fewer than half the Go packages.
body: Found by V1-2757 step 0 (2026-10-26): `corvint affected --base SHA` (1.0.0-rc.3 build 765) on base + agent patch for the 10 V2717 SWE-bench Pro pairs; repro scripts and outputs in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/affected-replay/ (run_pair.sh, out/pNN-off/full.json, summary.json). CONFIRMED on navidrome (p06): log/log.go calls runtime.Caller, so every package importing log becomes UNBOUNDED_READER; one edit to persistence/album_repository.go selects 22 of 22 Go packages (witness causes in out/p06-off/full.json). runtime.Caller reads frame metadata (file name strings), not file contents, so it is not a file read. Related over-selection: V1-2708. Pooled replay share 21.7%, but p01 .55, p03 .96, p06 .67, p09 .77.
title: affected: a runtime.Caller call marks every importer an UNBOUNDED_READER, selecting the whole Go module

acceptanceCriteria: A dirty Go package with no tests produces a runnable compile/vet check for it and its in-module dependents.
A go.mod/go.sum change produces an explicit module-level check or a named UNKNOWN, never a silent empty selection.
body: Found by V1-2757 step 0 (2026-10-26): `corvint affected --base SHA` (1.0.0-rc.3 build 765) on base + agent patch for the 10 V2717 SWE-bench Pro pairs; repro scripts and outputs in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/affected-replay/ (run_pair.sh, out/pNN-off/full.json, summary.json). CONFIRMED on flipt (p07): the agent edited internal/cue/validate.go (no test file at base) plus go.mod/go.sum; affected returned EMPTY_SELECTION for Go and emitted no command, selecting only unrelated bats tests. An agent told 'run: <selected tests>' would verify nothing about its change. Expected: a changed package with no tests still gets a compile check (go build / go vet / go test -run '^$' of the package and its dependents), and go.mod/go.sum changes widen to module-level checks.
title: affected: a dirty Go package without tests yields EMPTY_SELECTION and no check, not even build/vet

acceptanceCriteria: affected emits a runnable pytest command (node ids or files) for a selected Python plan on the four replay repos, or names why not.
A fixture test covers the pytest command for a src-layout and a flat-layout project.
body: Found by V1-2757 step 0 (2026-10-26): `corvint affected --base SHA` (1.0.0-rc.3 build 765) on base + agent patch for the 10 V2717 SWE-bench Pro pairs; repro scripts and outputs in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad value-audit/affected-replay/ (run_pair.sh, out/pNN-off/full.json, summary.json). CONFIRMED on ansible (p02, p04), qutebrowser (p03), openlibrary (p09): Python unit selection works (p04 picks target test_play_iterator, 24/1162 units) but advice.checks is empty for every Python pair and the provider state is MODULE_PATH_UNRESOLVED or EMPTY_SELECTION, so no pytest command reaches the agent. This blocks test selection as an agent lever on Python repos.
title: affected: Python selections are PLAN_ONLY with no runnable pytest command

acceptanceCriteria: The ContextBench receipt writer emits precision_answered, abstention_rate, precision_abst0 and a length-matched baseline precision per arm and split, with a regression test on a fixture containing abstained rows.
The owning benchmark spec defines abstention scoring explicitly and future preregistrations cite precision_answered or the length-matched comparison.
Re-running the scorer on the retained v2716f rows reproduces fused .162 vs bm25 .071 precision_answered on the full split.
body: Observed 2026-10-26 in the value-audit rescore of the V1-2716/V0415 ContextBench receipts (per-row data on the Windows box ~/bench/v2716f, 1132 rows, receipt numbers reproduced exactly). The receipt metric scores an abstained/empty answer as precision 1: reported = (1-abst)*prec_answered + abst. bm25:ident full split: abst .246, prec_answered .071, reported .299; Corvint fused: abst .064, prec_answered .162, reported .215. The frozen V1-2716 criterion (fused precision >= 0.25) therefore compares abstention rates, not ranking quality, and Corvint 'failed' while being ~2x more precise on answered rows (+0.083 held-out, +0.091 full; hard subset no-basename-in-prompt AND >=2 gold files: .190 vs .085). A second confound: bm25:ident returns ~20 files and Corvint ~10; truncating bm25 to Corvint's per-row length cuts the margin to +0.032 held-out / +0.044 full. Corvint-flagged OUT_OF_SCOPE rows keep their widening answers in the receipt. Expected: receipts report precision_answered, abstention rate, precision with abstention scored 0, and a length-matched baseline; prereg criteria use those. Scripts: value-audit/contextbench-rescore/rescore.py, rescore_matched.py (session scratchpad 82ebfb6e).
title: ContextBench retrieval receipts score an empty answer as precision 1, hiding answered-row precision and list-length effects

acceptanceCriteria: On the corvint repo, a prompt naming an existing path or requirement ID yields resolution state resolved (regression test with a fixture prompt), and a prompt with no resolvable anchor yields an abstaining envelope of bounded size.
Envelopes omit governance entries the host already loads (AGENTS.md imported by CLAUDE.md) and subagent SessionStart envelopes carry no repeated content; a test pins the byte bound.
The forensics script rerun on transcripts after the change reports resolved/abstained states and the envelope bytes per session, retained as evidence.
body: Observed 2026-10-26 by streaming the newest 200 Claude Code transcripts with a Corvint envelope under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint (15 main sessions, 185 subagents, ~4.5 days; script value-audit/own-repo-forensics/analyze.py, metrics.json, session scratchpad 82ebfb6e). 1601 envelopes (760 SessionStart, 841 UserPromptSubmit), median 844 B, ~2.0 MB total. Every envelope that carried a resolution was state=unresolved (809/809, typically reason anchor-not-found with most anchors missing); none resolved or abstained. governance[] named only AGENTS.md, which CLAUDE.md already loads via @AGENTS.md (read 0/200). Subagent envelopes named nothing else. Paths named only by Corvint were later read 87/1124 (7.7%); paths also named in the prompt 160/232 (69%). First named-file read came at median tool step 100 vs first search at step 2.5; 0/11 sessions read a named file before searching. Expected: anchor resolution resolves real anchors on the project's own repo or the envelope abstains; envelopes drop content the host already loads (AGENTS.md via CLAUDE.md); subagent SessionStart envelopes are omitted or minimal. Related V1-2755 (OpenCode frame abstain/shrink), V1-2754 (SessionStart dogfood argv in foreign repos).
title: Claude Code hook envelopes on the corvint repo never resolve and are almost never used: 100% unresolved, 7.7% of Corvint-only named paths read

acceptanceCriteria: Decide, with the CEM read-path witness either bounded or justified, whether a staged change-evidence file must select its path-literal readers on every PR.
Index or allowlist interop/cem01-go and .github/nightly-signal so they stop forcing FULL scope, or record why they must.
Once the shadow tier/cost rows have collected forward data, report recall and cost for B+R+U against S, with any miss named.
body: Offline analysis of shadow forward rows (2026-10-26; 341 of 557 rows analysed, 30 of 69 failing rows; GitHub artifact downloads hit a rate limit). The current `corvint affected` selection S costs median 0.867 of full (IQR 0.821-0.926). Tier recall over the 30 non-flaky failing rows: B changed packages 19/30 at cost 0.025, C (one hop) 20/30, transitive closure 22/30, C plus read scopes 26/30 at 0.290, and B plus read scopes plus the unbounded-reader set 30/30 (Wilson 0.89-1) at 0.427. S also caught 30/30. Breakdown of S's cost as median shares of full: the unbounded-reader set 0.34 (always selected); other plan witnesses (dependency paths, binary-exec, path literals) 0.26; path-literal readers of `.corvint/changes/*.cem.json`, which 405 of 453 rows carry, 0.15; Go-import frontier 0.008. The 31 rows where S = Full are UNINDEXED_SOURCE_PATH outside the AFP-V0-028 allowlist (29 from interop/cem01-go, 2 from .github/nightly-signal). Evidence: scratchpad value-audit/shadow-traffic/result.json and scripts (session 82ebfb6e). Caveats: the cost table dated 10-25 is applied to rows from 10-14 to 10-26; go list ran at go1.27.3; the flaky rule is the analyst's own. The shadow tier/cost rows (AFP-V0-480..484, PR #1872) will measure this forward.
title: affected over-selects on real CI traffic: median 0.867 of full test cost, while changed packages + read scopes + unbounded-reader set caught 30/30 failing rows at 0.427

acceptanceCriteria: Both tests pass 50/50 runs under go test -count=50 -cpu 1,4 with a parallel load, or their assertions bound the count instead of fixing it
No weakening of the PSRV-V0-224/151 requirement checks
body:
PR beamfall/corvint#1871 run 40341610462 (head 5e661089ed, go-product-shard (4), self-hosted) failed two internal/tasks/store tests although the batch changes no package that store depends on (go list -deps overlap empty).

- TestPSRV0224_ClaimRebindsMovedHeadWithoutJournalAdvance (claim_head_test.go:166): writer route deferred the claim observation 3 times, test wants exactly 2 then the complete route.
- TestPSRV0151_DeclinedResumeChargesNoResumedWalk (lease_bounded_audit_test.go:157): resumed 1 stage; a SNAPSHOT_MOVED invalidation forced a second fast route.

Both assert exact retry/deferral counts that depend on scheduling under parallel load (package took 465 s). Expected: the counts are bounded (at most N) or the race is made deterministic. Actual: intermittent FAIL on a loaded runner. Both pass in the WSL rerun of unrelated packages; store not yet rerun locally under -race/-count stress.
title: Store tests PSRV-V0-224 and PSRV-V0-151 flake on CI: writer-lock deferral and resume-walk counts are timing-sensitive

acceptanceCriteria: A prereg naming arms, sample and a practical-saving threshold (e.g. >=20% lower time to first confirmed failure without worse green latency or CPU) is frozen before any replay.
The three orders are replayed on the same <=20 runs with identical package sets; per-run and pooled times, CPU-seconds and overhead are retained under docs/build-log.
The verdict states whether affected-first beats the naive orders; if not, a follow-up proposes switching CI to the cheaper order.
body: Idea (value audit 2026-10-26). Interim mutation replay, commits 1-6: changed packages only (selector B) caught 12/12 killed mutants at 0.32x the test cost of `corvint affected` (A); A caught 12/12. V1-0716 already orders CI full mode affected-first (V1-0735 and V1-1189 cover surfacing and the order key), but nothing compares that order with naive orders. Proposal: replay a fixed sample of retained CI runs (capped at 20 paired replays) under (1) current affected-first, (2) changed-packages-first then the rest without duplication, (3) changed packages ordered by historical duration/failure rate. All arms run the full required set; ordering only, no skipping. Measure wall-clock time to first CONFIRMED failure, time to green on passing changes, runner CPU-seconds, and selection/index overhead. Do not test 'B passes, skip the rest' here: that needs escape evidence (see the boundary-mutant prereg ticket). Fixing V1-2708 alone may make A approximate B plus overhead. Source: Astra (Codex gpt-6-astra) consultation 2026-10-26, answer retained in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad astra/answer.md; interim mutation replay (prereg 172496b5, amendment 1) in value-audit/mutation-replay.
title: Test ordering trial: does affected-first ordering beat changed-packages-first or duration/failure-history ordering on time to first confirmed failure?

acceptanceCriteria: A new prereg with both cohorts, mutation operators, selection rule, ground-truth scope, statistics and kill/confirm thresholds is hashed before any run.
The pilot reports B-escape rate and A-rescue rate with confidence bounds per cohort, plus a full-suite ground-truth check on an isolated sample.
Result and deviations are recorded as a build-log entry; the verdict says whether corvint affected adds catch value over changed packages.
body: Question (value audit 2026-10-26). The running mutation replay (prereg 172496b5) cannot show value of wider selection: its mutants are mostly caught inside the changed package, ground truth is limited to A's selection, stages stop at the first confirmed kill, 12/12 recall bounds recall only above ~76% (Wilson), mutants cluster by commit, and selector E is seeded with the mutated function. The current replay stays unchanged; this is a NEW preregistration. Design: two frozen cohorts chosen before any selector result is seen: (1) randomly sampled representative changes; (2) a boundary challenge set mutating caller-visible behaviour in changed code: exported return semantics, serialization fields/defaults, interface behaviour, error propagation, side effects; plus historical real regressions where available. Report the B-escape rate separately from A's rescue rate; never pool the enriched cohort into deployment savings without prevalence weighting; check A and pruning omissions with full-suite ground truth on an isolated bounded sample; report uncertainty per commit. Power note: ~60 independent killed cases with zero escapes bounds escape probability near 5% (one-sided 95%). Budget: half a day design, 20-40 runner-hours pilot. Source: Astra (Codex gpt-6-astra) consultation 2026-10-26, answer retained in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad astra/answer.md; interim mutation replay (prereg 172496b5, amendment 1) in value-audit/mutation-replay.
title: Boundary-mutant preregistration: measure how often changed-packages-only selection misses a regression that corvint affected catches

acceptanceCriteria: The harness records active CI runner jobs and host load at each stage start and end, and either waits for an isolation window or marks the stage CONTAMINATED.
An ambiguous kill triggers matched paired clean/mutant reruns; unresolved cases are reported as UNKNOWN.
A re-run of the c5 m1 case under isolation is retained, classifying it as a real kill or a flake.
body: Fix (value audit 2026-10-26). The mutation replay runs on the WSL box that also hosts the 8 self-hosted CI runners; during the replay the runners used ~590% CPU next to the replay's ~570%, and at least one confirmed failure (cmd/corvint TestSourceViewReverifiesHeadBeforeSuccess, c5 m1) looks like a load flake (V1-1302). Load contaminates ground truth and per-test cost. Related: V1-2655 (box benchmarks confounded by the runners; generic quiet-baseline rule). Proposal for the replay harness (and any future selector prereg): run under reserved CPU/memory or exclusive windows with runner jobs paused or capped, record active runner jobs at each stage start/end, and for any ambiguous kill rerun clean and mutant trees in matched pairs under the same conditions, keeping unresolved cases as UNKNOWN rather than kills. Log any protocol change explicitly. Do not change the currently running replay mid-run. Source: Astra (Codex gpt-6-astra) consultation 2026-10-26, answer retained in the 82ebfb6e session scratchpad astra/answer.md; interim mutation replay (prereg 172496b5, amendment 1) in value-audit/mutation-replay.
title: Mutation replay harness: isolate runs from the co-tenant CI runners and resolve ambiguous kills by matched paired reruns

acceptanceCriteria: On the WSL CI runners, a go-product shard that runs corvint work tests writes no corvint-work-run-* or corvint-work-queue-gocache-* entries under /tmp (shown by a before/after listing).
The work run parent stays private (0700, owner-checked) and still ignores ambient TMPDIR unless an explicit, documented override is set; the spec records the rule.
Tests that allocate work run roots use an injected parent and remove it on exit.
body: Observed 2026-10-26 on batch PR #1872, go-product-shard (2), corvint-box-7: ENOSPC writing /tmp/corvint-work-run-1898386825/home/.cache/corvint-work-queue-gocache-1000/... The WSL runners' .env already sets TMPDIR=/var/tmp/corvint-ci/tmp/corvint-box-N on ext4 (718G free), and job processes carry it, but cmd/corvint/work_materialization.go workRunParent returns "/tmp" unless a test-only context key is set, and internal/worksource/git.go also uses a fixed "/tmp" parent. Each run builds a Go cache under its private home inside that root, so concurrent work-queue tests across 8 runners exhaust the 16G RAM-backed /tmp. The fixed parent is deliberate (no ambient TMPDIR; decision 0111 context), so the fix needs an explicit, owner-scoped parent (for example an operator-set variable or a validated private 0700 directory) or tests that inject workRunParentKey with t.TempDir(). Related: V1-2691 (heavy.sh cache on tmpfs), V1-2737 (leaked test temp dirs), V1-2563 (tmpfs vs ext4).
title: corvint work run roots (and their per-run Go cache) are hardcoded to /tmp, so CI jobs fill the WSL runners' 16G tmpfs despite TMPDIR on disk

acceptanceCriteria: With CORVINT_WORK_RUN_PARENT set, corvint work and script/corvint-work-queue create no corvint-work-executable-* or corvint-work-queue.* entries under /tmp (shown by a test or before/after listing).
Without the override, behavior is unchanged and documented in the governing spec.
body: Residual from V1-2768 (lane commit 3b7e2de30, which routes run roots and source scratch through the checked CORVINT_WORK_RUN_PARENT override). Still fixed to /tmp: cmd/corvint/work_executable_binding.go:162 copies the bound binary into /tmp/corvint-work-executable-*, and script/corvint-work-queue's build scratch uses /tmp/corvint-work-queue.*; a subprocess launched with a hand-built environment that drops CORVINT_WORK_RUN_PARENT (the conformance/work-queue-v0 replay CLI) also falls back to /tmp. On the WSL CI runners /tmp is a 16G tmpfs and filled on 2026-10-26 (#1872). Expected: these writers use the same checked parent when set, or a TMPDIR-following test parent in tests.
title: corvint work still writes executable copies (corvint-work-executable-*) and standalone script build scratch (corvint-work-queue.*) under fixed /tmp

acceptanceCriteria: A read-only command reports per-module reached/total screens and lists unreached screens, each count citing its evidence source.
Screens whose existence cannot be established are reported UNKNOWN, not counted as reached or unreached.
A fixture app with partial coverage produces the expected per-module counts in a maintained test.
docs/CAPABILITIES.md and the governing spec describe the report.
body: Adopter report (2026-10-26, active work-project adopter): their app map covers 10 of 23 screens, and they can only learn that by hand. They asked for a per-module report stating how many declared or discovered screens the map reaches and which ones it misses. Expected: a read-only flows/appmap command (and MCP tool) prints, per module, reached/total screens with the unreached screen list and the evidence source for each count (declared routes, observed traces, page objects). Missing evidence must read UNKNOWN, never a reached count. Related: V1-2719 (bind page objects and specs from traces), V1-2697, V1-2659.
title: flows appmap: per-module coverage report ("reached X of Y screens") so adopters see which screens the map does not yet cover

acceptanceCriteria: For each supported non-browser runner, receipts carry per-example identity and outcome (pass/fail/skip) or record an explicit NOT_PRODUCED reason.
A maintained test shows a file with mixed passing and skipped examples yields per-example receipt entries.
The governing spec names which runners have example-level evidence and which abstain.
body: Adopter report (2026-10-26): test-validity evidence is the feature they value most, but for non-browser tests it is recorded at file or package granularity, so a receipt cannot say which individual examples ran, passed, or were skipped. Browser (Playwright) flows already bind individual specs. Expected: supported non-browser runners record per-example outcomes in receipts and selection can cite file:line examples. Related: V1-2200 (bun file:line example selection, one runner), V1-2705 (selection-recall audit).
title: Test evidence: example-level (per test case) receipts for non-browser test runners, not only per-file or per-package

acceptanceCriteria: A stable channel and its promotion bar are documented in the distribution spec.
corvint-update can check and apply the stable channel without picking up developer prereleases.
Release notes for a stable promotion list behavior and flag changes since the previous stable.
body: Adopter report (2026-10-26): adoption churn (frequent prerelease Core/Tasks updates that change behavior or flags) is a named cost for the active work-project adopter. Expected: a documented stable channel that adopters can pin to, updated only after a qualification bar, with corvint-update able to check/apply that channel alone, and release notes that flag behavior changes. Related: V1-0422 (signed archives and package-manager channel), V1-0020/V1-0021 (1.0 release candidate and stable).
title: distribution: an adopter stable channel so adopting projects are not exposed to every prerelease churn

acceptanceCriteria: Root cause identified with a reproduction (e.g. under stress/CPU contention) or recorded evidence.
Quiet mode passes 20 consecutive runs under induced CPU load, or the assertion is bound to the test's recorded qualification with a documented reason.
body: Batch #1872 CI run 40377147321, shard 4 on corvint-box-3 (2026-10-26 ~14:23 EDT, load 40-80, /tmp near full): single_writer_harness_test.go:519 failed with 'quiet reap: 2 audits and 1 resumed over 2 calls, want at least one audit per call and no resume' (126.44 s). The rerun of the same commit passed (168.75 s, ~15:21 EDT). Quiet mode asserts Resumed == 0, but under load the change-time based resumable audit (journal.ResumableAudits) evidently observed a change it treats as resumable. The `ticket create --template` default and the orchestrator's payload template both use coverage INCOMPLETE. The touch paths are not known until a lane has screened the ticket. As a result, the native lifecycle that AGENTS.md and the corvint-first rule prefer is never reachable, and all closeouts use complete-manual. Expected: a supported route to COMPLETE coverage, for example proposing touchPaths from `corvint impact`/`affected` on the delivered diff, or a claim-time widen. Closing through gate run/complete should then become the default.

acceptanceCriteria: a repository whose admitted sources exceed 128 MiB indexes successfully; no unsupported-impact-repository refusal for aggregate size

peak RSS of the index build measured before/after on a synthetic large fixture (for example 500 MiB of admitted sources) and recorded in a build-log entry; no single read buffer scales with repository size

body:
Owner direction 2026-10-27: the 128 MiB aggregate admission bound is a brick wall that would block larger projects; if speed is the worry, optimize how we index instead of refusing.

Cause: internal/contextindex/git.go fetchBlobs reads every admitted blob through ONE `git cat-file --batch` call whose whole output is buffered (gitExpecting(..., maxBatchBytes, ...)) and returned as one map; validateBlobAdmission refuses the repository (unsupported-impact-repository) when sources plus framing exceed maxBatchBytes. The cap protects that single buffer; it is not a product requirement. Corvint's own repository hit it (V1-2880). maxIndexedSources (200,000 files, observe_tree.go) is the same kind of wall.

Direction: (1) fetch blobs in bounded chunks (stream cat-file output per object) so no single buffer scales with the repository; (2) consume blobs incrementally in the index build so peak memory is bounded by chunk size plus derived index, not total source bytes, where the builder allows; (3) drop the aggregate refusal; keep the per-file maxSourceBytes bound and the vendor/generated exclusions; (4) measure and optimize index build time and memory on a large fixture (parallel parse, incremental reuse), and report admitted bytes/files and elapsed time instead of refusing; (5) revisit maxIndexedSources the same way. Keep invariant 7 (one binary, no database service) and the bounded-reader rule: every reader stays bounded per call.
title: Remove the 128 MiB index admission wall: chunked, streamed and faster indexing so large repositories are admitted

The 200-path bound exists for the learning trace (invariant 5, bounded learning); nothing requires the CEM, citations or seal to share it. Proposed: (1) the CEM binds, checks and seals any size; the verifier runs citation checks in budgeted chunks (or a budget scaled to hunk count) instead of one 1,024-op pass, with total cost measured; (2) the local outcome over 200 paths records a complete non-learning aggregate (ALO-V0, aggregate-local-outcome-v0.md, currently proposed/NOT_QUALIFIED) or a bounded learning sample, never a refusal; learning inputs stay bounded and evaluation-gated; (3) intents: lift or scale the 16-intent cap with a stated reason; (4) amend DCW-V0-039/040 and record the decision; per-lane seal + batch-check stays supported. acceptanceCriteria: Owner selects the OIF-V0 promotion route (adopter-repository dogfood, a Corvint-owned intent in a declared form, or a restated bar) and the choice is recorded as a decision or build-log entry.
One real change is dogfooded through ocm prepare --intent-form on the selected route with prepare/status/verify/report transcripts retained, and V1-2885 can then promote OIF-V0.
body: Found by V1-2885 on 2026-10-27 (Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 775, base 98b780811). OIF-V0 promotion needs one real change dogfooded through `corvint ocm prepare --intent-form FORM`. A reader sweep over all 2333 tracked Markdown files (deriveIntent per form) derives nothing Corvint-owned: adr-decisions 0 (all fail invalid-adr-number: no Corvint decision record has `adr: NNNN` front matter), roadmap-acceptance 0 (ROADMAP.md uses `**Accept:**` body lines, not `  - **Acceptance:**`, so missing-requirements; 3 fixture tasks.md fail invalid-ticket-item), openspec-spec 2 / openspec-delta 2 / speckit-spec 1, all under interop/spec-toolchains/fixtures (synthetic conformance intents for a fictional app, not Corvint governing intent). Live CLI: `ocm prepare --intent-form adr-decisions --intent docs/decisions/0541-...md` -> invalid-adr-number; `--intent-form roadmap-acceptance --intent ROADMAP.md` -> missing-requirements. Expected: a real change whose governing intent is project-owned text in a declared form. Actual: none exists in Corvint, and the lane rules forbid inventing one or editing an accepted decision to parse. Owner decision needed on the route: (a) run the promotion dogfood on an adopter repository whose intent already parses (Beamfall: 99 of 215 ADRs derive under adr-decisions), recording it as the OIF-V0 real change; (b) accept a Corvint-owned intent written natively in a declared form (for example a future decision record with ADR front matter, or an OpenSpec/Spec Kit-shaped spec) and dogfood the next change it governs; or (c) restate the promotion bar. The dogfood wrapper also cannot pass a form (OIF-V0 open decision 5), so any route runs OCM manually beside dogfood-change. Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-27-oif-v0-promotion.md.
title: OIF-V0 promotion: no Corvint-owned intent reads under any declared intent form, so a Corvint change cannot be the promotion dogfood

acceptanceCriteria: A keep-alive that survives Windows reboot and ssh session exits, approved by the owner.
A check that reports when the distro has no Windows-side holder.
Reboot test: runners online and idle afterwards without any ssh session.
body: 2026-10-27, PR #1916 run 40578325407: all eight go-product shards failed or were cancelled with 'The runner has received a shutdown signal'. Cause: no wsl.exe/wslhost.exe process on the Windows box kept the Ubuntu distro alive, so WSL terminated the distro whenever the last ssh-launched wsl.exe exited, stopping all eight actions.runner systemd units (VM uptime stayed; distro PIDs restarted at ~190). Something long-lived had held it before (likely among the stuck sessions cleared earlier the same day). Temporary fix: a keep-alive started outside the ssh job object via Win32_Process Create: wsl.exe -d Ubuntu --exec /bin/sleep infinity (pid 35128); it does not survive a Windows reboot. Durable fix needs owner approval for persistent Windows configuration, e.g. a startup scheduled task running the same keep-alive, plus a heavy.sh/runner health check that detects a distro with no holder.
title: WSL self-hosted runners die when no wsl.exe holds the Ubuntu distro open

acceptanceCriteria: Lane charters and dogfood docs direct per-lane inputs (citation plans, intent lists) to a lane-unique directory, never the shared orchestrator scratchpad.

acceptanceCriteria: Measured per-shard breakdown (compile vs test) on a PR run before and after, on the same self-hosted box.
PR go-product wall time cut by at least 40% with the same package set, -race kept, and every package still with one terminal outcome.

Any change to the AFP-V0-014 fixed argv (-p 1) is an owner-approved spec amendment that keeps the historical qualification profile's frozen argv comparable (separate qualification argv or recorded break).
body: 2026-10-27 measurement, green batch run 40544500978 (batch-1027d), eight self-hosted shards on one 32-thread WSL box: shard wall 25-44 min (about 4.2 runner-hours), but summed per-package test time is only 2.67 h over 340 packages (13-29 min per shard). Shard 7: 41m42s in the test step for 13 min of package time, so roughly 28 min goes to compiling. Causes: (1) go test -json -p 1 -count=1 -race (ci.yml ~547, pinned as the AFP-V0-014 qualification argv) builds and runs one package at a time, so each shard uses about one core while 8 shards share 32 threads; (2) the trusted Go build cache is restored only on main pushes and merge-queue entries, so every PR shard compiles the whole -race graph cold; (3) imbalance: internal/tasks/cli alone takes 18.4 min, and 73 tests of at least 60 s sum to 1.98 h (internal/tasks/store dominates). Options: -p >1 on PR runs (keep -p 1 only for the qualification profile), a per-host warm build seed for PR shards (AFP-V0-428 already refreshes one on main), shard by measured time, and split or speed the slowest tasks tests. .github changes need owner ci-control-plane approval.
title: CI go-product shards spend most of their wall time compiling: -p 1 -race with no PR build cache uses ~1 core per shard

acceptanceCriteria: A repeated heavy.sh run of the same package at the same commit compiles warm: the second no-test `go test -run '^$' ./cmd/corvint` offload finishes within 10 s of offload overhead, measured before and after.
Concurrent slots never share a worktree; a slot's tree is reset to exactly HEAD + wip patch + untracked files before each run (no stale files leak between runs), proven by a test or scripted check.
script/heavy.sh serve and the live ~/bench/rt.sh carry the same fix, or the ticket records which one the V1-2862 cutover makes authoritative.
Test semantics unchanged: no -trimpath unless every runtime.Caller/path-reading test is shown unaffected.
body: Measured 2026-10-27 on the WSL offload box (32 threads, load ~24), corvint batch head a7efd7f61. `go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/corvint`: fresh path 14.6 s; same path again 1.6 s; new path with identical content 17.1 s; with -trimpath a new path is warm at 2.3 s. Go adds the package directory to the compile action ID unless -trimpath is set, so a new checkout path misses the shared GOCACHE. The live remote half (/home/russell/bench/rt.sh) runs every command in `git worktree add $HOME/bench/rt/<date-pid>/tree`, and the repo's script/heavy.sh serve half does the same (`wt=$w/heavy-$id`, line ~268). Every heavy.sh test run therefore recompiles the tested package's whole dependency graph: a no-test run of ./cmd/corvint takes 27-39 s end to end versus ~5 s for a small package. heavy-selection.log records ~1,600 go test runs since 2026-10-25; at 15-35 s of avoidable compile each that is an estimated 7-15 h of box time (estimate, not measured per run). Fix direction: run each slot in a stable per-slot worktree path (acquire the slot before checkout, reuse $HOME/bench/rt/slotN/tree with `git checkout --force --detach` + `git clean -fdx`), which keeps test behaviour identical; -trimpath is the alternative but changes runtime.Caller/file paths that some tests read, and V1-2590 notes checkout-root sensitivity. Same root cause likely costs each lane's local `make windows-vet` and corvint builds in per-lane /private/tmp worktrees.
title: heavy.sh offload builds every run in a fresh worktree path, so Go recompiles the whole dependency tree on each test run (build cache keyed by package dir)

acceptanceCriteria: Baseline: `corvint affected` replayed at each of the last >=50 lane changes merged to origin/main (base = the change's first parent) records per change: plan scope (narrow vs UNKNOWN/FULL), selected/unknown/universe counts, selected share of Go packages and of measured test cost, and the unknown/witness kinds that widened it; retained as a benchmarks/results JSON plus build-log entry.

Safety: for the same changes, every test that failed in that change's CI run (or its merge-queue run) is checked against the narrowed selection; any miss is listed with its cause. Narrow rate is only reported alongside the miss count.
Re-measure after each selection fix (V1-2708, V1-2763, V1-2806) on the same change set; a fix counts only if the narrow rate rises with zero new misses.

Gate: a repeatable command (make target or corvint-test subcommand) recomputes the rate on a fixed change set and fails when the narrow rate drops below the recorded floor or any miss appears; wired into the doc-gates or a scheduled job (CI wiring needs owner ci-control-plane approval).
body: Owner 2026-10-27: "hard is the point. it should be able to do hard." Corvint's own repository (Go plus TypeScript/Ruby/.NET integrations, binary-exec and directory-reading tests) is the hard case its test selection must handle, yet `corvint affected` plans on it are almost always UNKNOWN and fall back to the full suite (e.g. aliased-roots change: 112 selected, 101 unknown, 75 of them unrelated TypeScript dynamic imports; heavy-selection.log since 10-25: 539 of 1031 lane runs whole-package). Nothing measures the self-use narrow rate, so regressions in it go unnoticed. Related: V1-2708 (frontier scoping, in progress), V1-2763 (cem.json readers), V1-2806 (whole-package slices), V1-2705 (built-in recall audit, GH #1814), V1-2707 (CI narrowing inert).
title: Self-use narrowing rate: baseline over merged lane changes, safety check against CI outcomes, and a regression gate on this repository

acceptanceCriteria: A 500+ path merged range reaches dogfood check and seal without too-many-obligations, or the refusal is reported up front in seconds with the exact intent narrowing needed

Replay evidence on a real batch range retained in a build-log entry

With the CEM size wall removed, a 583-path replay (98b780811..ed70f3efb, 1,687 hunks, plain clone, 2,609.55 s) produced cem-prepare, cem-cite, 16 OCM prepare/status pairs, cem-status and the local outcome, but ocm-aggregate is NOT_PRODUCED too-many-obligations (1,192 against the 256 aggregate bound) and coordination-time-impact is NOT_PRODUCED context-abstention-invalid (the before binary refuses it at every stage too, so not size-related). dogfood check then fails dogfood-report-drift and the range cannot be sealed. body: Measured by the V1-2883 lane (2026-10-27). acceptanceCriteria: batch-precheck labels each failing finding base-present or introduced and exits nonzero only for introduced ones
The three named base failures are reproduced on origin/main and fixed, or shown absent
Test covering a base-present finding that does not fail the lane
body: Reported by the V1-2883 lane (2026-10-27): batch-precheck failed test-read-scopes-check (internal/liveverify/affected/shell_test.go) and capabilities-check/capability-catalog-check (five unlisted corvint-test flags: --endpoint-source, --openapi, --rails-routes, --remedy-commits, --remedy-summary), all outside the lane's diff (inferred base failures, not rerun at base). acceptanceCriteria: A replay of the V1-2892 change set shows go:build-constraint-variants no longer making plan.scope UNKNOWN when the constrained package's all-variant edges are in the closure.
A focused test covers a reached //go:build package whose variant edges are all modelled, and one whose variant is not, keeping the latter UNKNOWN.
The affected-plan spec records the rule and its rollback.
body:
Observed: all 50 replayed Corvint lane changes carried LANGUAGE_FRONTIER go:build-constraint-variants, so plan.scope was UNKNOWN in 50 of 50. golang.go:354-356 sets the unit frontier on every package with a //go:build file, and select.go frontierUnknowns raises the unit frontier of every reached unit; Corvint's closures (median 0.21 of tested Go packages) always reach one (e.g. process_unix.go). The edges are already a superset of every variant (golang.go:42-45), so selection is sound for the variants the closure covers; the residual uncertainty is only which variant one test run exercises. AFP-V0-028 already lets `corvint test` narrow past it, but the plan scope stays UNKNOWN and CI or other consumers that require BOUNDED never narrow.
Expected: a reached constrained package whose all-variant import edges are in the closure does not by itself make the plan UNKNOWN (or the plan names it as a bounded variant caveat), with the rule written in the affected-plan spec.
Evidence: V1-2892 self-narrow baseline (benchmarks/results/v2892-self-narrow-baseline-2026-10-27.json, docs/build-log/2026-10-27-self-narrow-baseline.md), 50 lane merges from batch PRs #1857..#1901 replayed with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 dev `corvint affected --base M^1` at M.
title: affected: go:build-constraint-variants on any reached package makes every self-use plan UNKNOWN

acceptanceCriteria: A replay of the V1-2892 change set shows shell:foreign-invocation-unmodelled raised on fewer than 50 of 50 plans, with each remaining case explained.
Focused tests cover a script reached only by a literal path reader (no frontier) and one invoked by a computed path (frontier kept).
The NSA spec records the narrowed rule and its rollback.
body:
Observed: all 50 replayed Corvint lane changes carried LANGUAGE_FRONTIER shell:foreign-invocation-unmodelled. shell.go:131-139 (NSA-V0-012) adds it to every non-test shell unit whenever the source universe holds any .go/.ts/... file, so in a mixed-language repository every plan that reaches any shell script is UNKNOWN, regardless of whether any program invokes that script. Expected: the frontier is raised only for shell units a foreign-language program could reach by a computed path (for example scripts no literal-path reader names, or with an explicit declared-invocation escape), so a plan that reaches only literally-named scripts can stay BOUNDED.
Evidence: V1-2892 self-narrow baseline (benchmarks/results/v2892-self-narrow-baseline-2026-10-27.json, docs/build-log/2026-10-27-self-narrow-baseline.md), 50 lane merges from batch PRs #1857..#1901 replayed with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 dev `corvint affected --base M^1` at M.
title: affected: shell:foreign-invocation-unmodelled on every non-test shell unit makes every self-use plan UNKNOWN

acceptanceCriteria: corvint affected over a change to only internal/jstestprovider/qualified-reporter.cjs selects the reading Go package and emits no NO_SELECTABLE_TEST for that path, or the ticket records why the unknown is correct.
A focused test pins the behaviour.
body:
Observed: 2 of 50 replayed lane changes (batch #1892, 5aa176d78844 and 7fc1c7fde53d) carried NO_SELECTABLE_TEST typescript:internal/jstestprovider/qualified-reporter.cjs. The file is a reporter asset shipped by the Go jstestprovider package, so its owning tests are Go tests, not TypeScript ones; the TypeScript plugin claims it and reports no selectable test. Unverified hypothesis: an asset owned by a Go embed or path reader should be attributed to that Go unit and not yield NO_SELECTABLE_TEST. Expected: the plan selects the Go package that embeds or reads the asset and emits no NO_SELECTABLE_TEST for it.
Evidence: V1-2892 self-narrow baseline (benchmarks/results/v2892-self-narrow-baseline-2026-10-27.json, docs/build-log/2026-10-27-self-narrow-baseline.md), 50 lane merges from batch PRs #1857..#1901 replayed with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 dev `corvint affected --base M^1` at M.
title: affected: internal/jstestprovider/qualified-reporter.cjs reports NO_SELECTABLE_TEST though Go code embeds it

acceptanceCriteria: batch-regen regenerates every derived file in one fixed-order target and one commit
batch-precheck runs the drift test union selected over the whole batch diff, as one offload
push of a batch head without a passing precheck receipt for that exact HEAD is refused
replay of the 1026b, 1027d and 1027e batches: each drift failure is caught locally
body: Found 2026-10-27 by the build/test/CI audit (scratch evidence: audit-ci/ runs.jsonl over 1000 ci.yml runs 10-18..10-27; local heavy-*.log). About 9 of 11 merge_group failures and about 6 batch PR runs in 9 days were drift: TestCAPV0019CommittedCatalogMatchesTheBinary x4 (39886843372...), gate-ledger+TestAFUV1024 x3, lrfrepo spec enumeration, TestCoreVerbsEmitTheFrozenProfiles (40341610462, 40593213326), TestAffectedReceiptMembersAreClosedAndByteStable, TestCAPV0047, TestImprovementLoopSpecsEnumerateEveryObligation, companionrelease build tests. DRIFT_TESTS in script/batch-precheck.sh covers only TestAFUV1024 and the CAPV004x range, and precheck was evidently not rerun on the pushed head. Each failure costs 45-80 min plus a requeue. Fix: one `make batch-regen` (spec-requirements, capability-catalog, analyzer bump, use-case receipt repin, line-citation repin, frozen-profile/AFU/receipt-member goldens) committed once; a batch-drift step that runs every golden/receipt/catalog/enumeration test selected over the merged batch diff (cross-lane union); git push of claude/batch-* refuses without a precheck receipt matching HEAD.
title: Batch PRs fail CI on cross-lane drift in goldens, catalogs and spec enumerations that batch-precheck does not run

acceptanceCriteria: the local doc-gate list is derived from ci.yml doc-gates steps and a test fails when they diverge

body: Found 2026-10-27 by the build/test/CI audit (scratch evidence: audit-ci/ runs.jsonl over 1000 ci.yml runs 10-18..10-27; local heavy-*.log). 19 of 45 classified real failed runs (10-24..10-27) were doc-gates: host-package version bump AHI-020 (40586057604), use-case receipt pins, docs gate steps. Each costs a re-push and often a full 176 job-min rerun. Fix: dogfood-closeout and batch-precheck run exactly the CI doc-gates job's step list (generated from ci.yml, so it cannot drift), and auto-apply mechanical repins (host-package bump, receipt repin) before the check. Related: V1-1894, V1-2393.
title: doc-gates fail on about 40% of real failed CI runs: lanes push without the full CI doc-gate list

acceptanceCriteria: queue-entry wall time drops to about the doc-gates duration when REUSE fires

body: Found 2026-10-27 by the build/test/CI audit (scratch evidence: audit-ci/ runs.jsonl over 1000 ci.yml runs 10-18..10-27; local heavy-*.log). With tree REUSE firing on 30/31 merge_group entries since 10-24, the queue critical path is go-static (4-5.8 min) or cce-live (8.7 min, 8 of 31 entries). Push reruns doc-gates (109 x 1.1 min) and cce-live (9 x 8.8 macOS min). Reused go-product-shard jobs still check out, set up Go and build the helper (~786 job-min/9 days). The shadow planner is built 8x per PR run (~31 s each, ~1.1k job-min). Fix: extend tree-keyed REUSE to go-static, go-interop, cce-live and doc-gates; skip shard jobs at job level in DOCS/REUSE mode with go-product accepting skipped; build the shadow planner once in docs-plan. Related: V1-1642, V1-2113, V1-1099.

acceptanceCriteria: one Go build cache per host, documented
post-batch trim keeps each cache under a stated bound

body: Found 2026-10-27 by the build/test/CI audit (scratch evidence: audit-ci/ runs.jsonl over 1000 ci.yml runs 10-18..10-27; local heavy-*.log). Mac: /tmp/corvint-go-build-cache 130 G (CORVINT_GOCACHE), ~/.cache/corvint-go-build-cache 5.3 G (DOGFOOD_GOCACHE, precheck), ~/Library/Caches/go-build 19 G; 78 Gi free; 115 lane/batch dirs in /private/tmp. Box: heavy-offload strips GOCACHE so offloaded go test uses ~/.cache/go-build (214 G) while remote make targets use ~/.cache/corvint-go-build-cache (28 G), so the same packages compile twice. Fix: one cache per host (GOCACHE in ~/bench/go.env; align CORVINT_GOCACHE/DOGFOOD_GOCACHE defaults); run go-cache-trim and scratch-sweep after each batch. Related: V1-2691, V1-1632.

body: Found 2026-10-27 by the build/test/CI audit (scratch evidence: audit-ci/ runs.jsonl over 1000 ci.yml runs 10-18..10-27; local heavy-*.log). /private/tmp/cem10-build/rt-remote.sh is pre-V1-2891 (fresh worktree, mkdir locks), the deployed ~/bench/rt.sh uses flock slot trees, and script/heavy.sh is a third variant. heavy-selection.log records neither rc nor wall time, so offload overhead and slot wait are NOT_OBSERVED (V1-2209 saw 344 s slot wait). Builds refuse when box load >16, and the box runs at 21-30 under lanes, so builds always fall back to the Mac. Fix: rt.sh lives in the repo and installs with a checksum check, printed each run; log rc, wall and phases (pack, ssh, reset, compile, test); HEAVY_FETCH=1 returns changed files for go test; reserve a build slot instead of the load gate. Related: V1-2891, V1-2552.

acceptanceCriteria: a fixture where a Go server change must select a TypeScript e2e spec through a declared runtime edge
without the declaration the TypeScript frontier stays UNKNOWN, never excluded
frozen affected replay shows no recall loss
body: Found 2026-10-27 by the V1-2708 lane (AFP-V0-560, branch claude/frontier-scope-1027, seal baeed9f91) and its Codex review. AFP-V0-560 excludes a plugin's LANGUAGE_FRONTIER when the change reaches it only through terminal witnesses; soundness assumes no hidden edge crosses languages. TypeScript e2e specs depend at runtime on the Go server binary, an edge no plugin models, so a Go server change neither selects those specs nor keeps the TypeScript frontier. Expected: a modelled cross-language runtime edge (declared or inferred) that selects or keeps the frontier. Actual: frontier excluded, specs unselected. body: batch-1028 (2026-10-28, base aa3b6e4f, 19 sealed lanes) ran `make dogfood-batch-check` and failed: unbound-commits count=8 and merge-resolution-unbound count=7. Of the 8: (1) the orchestrator's `make batch-regen` commit, which the batch routine (ASD-V0-033) requires as one direct commit of derived files (INDEX.json, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, analyzer digest, citation repins); (2) a direct repin of two AUTOMATION.md citations whose cited code another lane changed, which line-citations-check requires after merge; (3) six lane commits made after the lane's seal (mutate-transient x3, host-dispatch, flows-docs, cem-completeness; see V1-1773). The 7 merge failures are hand-unions of spec status lines, requirement tables and trace rows that two lanes both appended to, which every multi-lane batch hits. DOGFOOD.md tells the orchestrator to seal each such edit on its own branch, which costs one dogfood-closeout per batch fixup and is not done in practice (V1-2805: no batch has passed since 2026-10-25). Expected: either the check recognises a derived-only commit whose tree equals what `make batch-regen` regenerates from its parent (exempt and reported as a NOTE), and an append-only union of both sides' added lines as a derivable merge (`union` derivation), or the batch tooling ships one command that seals the orchestrator fixup as a constituent with derived citations, so a clean batch is achievable in one step.
