Owner rules from the local wrapper (HEAVY_LOCAL_REASON refusal, load-aware wait, WSL offload, build offload) are present in script/heavy.sh or recorded as deliberate drops.
Cutover happens between batches with no lane running, as LANE-ORCHESTRATION requires; make lane-scripts-test passes.
body: Pipeline audit 2026-10-28 (Codex gpt-6-astra, verified). Lane charters point at /private/tmp/cem10-build/heavy.sh, whose slots are mkdir dirs with dead-PID reclaim (lines ~49-60). docs/LANE-ORCHESTRATION.md:79 records that this prototype can drop a live owner's slot when two waiters reclaim the same dead slot, and that script/heavy.sh (flock, no reclaim step, stable remote worktrees) replaces it. The local wrapper also carries owner rules the repo script may lack (HEAVY_LOCAL_REASON refusal, load wait, build offload).
title: Orchestrator lanes use the /private/tmp/cem10-build/heavy.sh mkdir-slot prototype instead of the versioned flock script/heavy.sh

acceptanceCriteria: A bulk closeout verb runs claim, submit, the ticket's requiredGates and complete for each delivered ticket, binding the lane seal identity and the batch merge evidence.
Tickets whose gates cannot run locally are refused with a named reason, never silently manual-completed.
complete-manual remains available only for explicit manual dispositions; receipt audit distinguishes the two.
body: Pipeline audit 2026-10-28 (verified source): internal/tasks/cli/batch_close.go:18 and :199 write COMPLETE_MANUAL with merge sha and CI URL as evidence. Orchestrator closeout likewise uses complete-manual per ticket. A merged, green batch stands in for per-ticket acceptance; AGENTS.md reserves complete-manual for explicitly evidenced manual dispositions.
title: ticket batch-close writes COMPLETE_MANUAL from merge identity instead of running each ticket's required gates

acceptanceCriteria: batch-precheck steps reuse a prior pass through the existing ledger when every input binding is unchanged, and report the reuse.
The lane charter drops explicit doc-check invocations that closeout already covers on the same inputs.
Measured lane closeout wall time before and after is recorded.
body: Pipeline audit 2026-10-28: Makefile:621 dogfood-closeout runs dogfood-finish then the full batch-precheck (22 checks, ~90 s warm per docs/build-log/2026-10-27-batch-drift-precheck.md:45). With ~20 lanes per batch that is ~30 lane-minutes, and the charter also runs several of the same doc checks explicitly before it. The batch reruns batch-precheck on the composed tree anyway.
title: dogfood-closeout runs the whole batch-precheck in every lane; reuse dependency-bound passes

acceptanceCriteria: A make or corvint target emits a bounded review packet for a batch: merged-range impact, lane overlap advice, constituent CEM reports and unresolved obligations.
The orchestrator batch review prompt includes the packet; the reviewed revision is retained.
body: Pipeline audit 2026-10-28: the one-round Codex batch review gets only the diff range. Corvint already offers impact, review (experimental) and CEM/OCM frontier inspection (docs/SELF-DEVELOPMENT.md:24, :115). Cross-lane interactions are the highest-risk part of a batch and the reviewer gets no evidence about them.
title: Batch review prompt lacks Corvint impact, overlap and constituent CEM evidence

acceptanceCriteria: Doc gates and the CEM release gate reuse a pass bound to the exact tree, with independently validated receipts, on merge_group and push.
No gate is weakened: a tree mismatch or missing receipt runs the gate in full.
Needs owner ci-control-plane approval for the .github change.
body: Pipeline audit 2026-10-28: race results and static/interop results already reuse exact-commit evidence (.github/workflows/ci.yml:127, :1140), but the doc gates and the CEM release gate (2-4 min on both platforms, cem-release-gate.yml:14) run again on merge_group and on push-to-main for an identical tree.
title: CI reruns doc gates and the CEM release gate on PR, merge_group and push for the same tree

acceptanceCriteria: A real local `corvint test --base <sha>` whose plan includes a root go invocation finishes COMPLETE (no unlisted unit) on the Corvint repository with tools/local-authority present.
The nested-module unit is run by its own module invocation or excluded with an explicit, receipt-visible reason; it is never silently dropped.
Regression test covering a root-requiring nested module in the Go universe; governing spec updated in the same change.
body: Found by the V1-2980 lane (2026-10-28), reproduced on installed build 778. tools/local-authority is a nested Go module that requires the root (AFP-V0-582). Its unit go:github.com/Beamfall/corvint/tools/local-authority enters the sessiontest Go universe via graph.UnitIDs() in cmd/corvint/test.go, but root `go list ./...` does not list it, so every real (non dry-run) local `corvint test` with a root go invocation ends INCOMPLETE ("1 unlisted"). Expected: units of a nested module are either run through their own module invocation (as V1-2980's go-module unit does) or excluded from the root universe with a stated reason; a clean run reads COMPLETE.
title: corvint test: tools/local-authority (nested module requiring the root) enters the root Go universe, so every real local run ends INCOMPLETE with 1 unlisted

acceptanceCriteria: Retained span bytes are budgeted before allocation, or overlapping spans share bounded backing storage, in both the native and portable verifiers.
A regression with 64 overlapping near-full spans of one large blob stays under a stated memory bound or is refused with a bounded-resource code.
Both verifiers agree on the outcome (CEM interop parity).
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/cem/verify/verify.go:299-310 copies each span (append([]byte(nil), spanBytes...)); interop/cem01-go/stable_repository.go:998 does the same; internal/cem/gitauth/object.go:595 charges each distinct blob once. Scenario: 64 distinct near-full spans of one 64 MiB blob retain about 4 GiB while the blob budget charges 64 MiB. (A cap on record count or total span bytes was not seen in the cited slices.)
title: CEM verifiers copy every evidence span, so overlapping spans of one blob retain gigabytes

acceptanceCriteria: Covered ranges are kept as intervals and intersected directly with added lines; no per-line expansion over the profile span.
The profile example 1.1,4294967295.2 completes within a small time and memory bound.
Coverage results for ordinary profiles are unchanged.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/cem/coverprofile/coverprofile.go:115 parses lines with ParseUint(...,10,32); internal/cem/workflow/cover.go:149 loops line from StartLine to EndLine inserting into a map with no cancellation. Scenario: 'mode: set' then 'pkg/a.go:1.1,4294967295.2 1 1' causes about 4.3 billion map insertions before the patch intersection.
title: coverprofile admits 32-bit line numbers and cover.go expands every line, so a tiny profile allocates billions of entries

acceptanceCriteria: Each baseline and each reverted run executes on a fresh snapshot of the target with only the intended hunk changed.
A regression test with a sentinel-creating test yields no held verdict for an unrelated hunk.
The hunk-revert spec records the isolation requirement.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/cem/verify/hunkrevert.go:226 (judgeCandidates runs baseline and reverted tests against the same tree) and :282 (only the reverted file is restored). Scenario: a named test creates a sentinel file and passes on first run, fails when the sentinel exists; baseline passes, reverted run fails, so an unrelated hunk gets held. Other fixture or source mutations also persist between candidates.
title: hunk-revert shares one workspace and cached baselines, so test side effects can manufacture a held verdict

acceptanceCriteria: All reads, sweeps, temp creation and replacement in both ledgers go through one validated directory handle (openat-style) or are refused when the directory identity changes.
A test swapping .corvint for a symlink between validation and write leaves the external directory untouched.
Both ledgers share the fix or a common helper.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/observations/observations.go:282-295 does Lstat of .corvint then opens and locks the directory, but removeStaleTemporaries (:688) uses filepath.Glob/os.Remove and replaceLedger uses os.CreateTemp(directory) by pathname; internal/unplannedread/unplannedread.go:436 has the same pattern. Scenario: another process swaps .corvint for a symlink after validation, so temp creation, stale deletion and ledger replacement happen in the external directory (read commands writing outside the repository, violating product invariant 4).
title: observation and unplanned-read ledgers use pathname operations after a directory check, so directory substitution redirects writes outside the repository

acceptanceCriteria: A private-key (and PGP private key) header without a terminator redacts through end of input, or the value is refused.
A regression with a footerless PEM shows no base64 body in the output.
Terminated blocks screen exactly as before.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/secretscreen/secretscreen.go:231-232 has a header-only alternative '-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----' used when no END marker matches; :283 appends text[start:] unmatched. Scenario: a PEM key with the footer missing becomes '[REDACTED]' plus the remaining base64 key material in screened output (consumer internal/diagnostic/bound.go:54).
title: secretscreen redacts only the BEGIN header of an unterminated private-key block and leaks the body

acceptanceCriteria: Ambiguity is resolved against every profile path, including zero-count ones, before counters are examined.
A test with a/pkg/a.go count 0 and b/pkg/a.go count 1 is refused with the ambiguity error.
Unambiguous profiles behave as before.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/cem/workflow/cover.go:141 skips Count==0 blocks so those paths never enter the map; profileLinesFor (:159) checks ambiguity only among remaining paths. Scenario: a/pkg/a.go count 0 and b/pkg/a.go count 1 at the changed line; hunk pkg/a.go is credited coverage from b instead of being refused as ambiguous.
title: coverage path ambiguity disappears when one matching profile file has zero coverage

acceptanceCriteria: survived requires a terminal pass for every eligible test; otherwise the row is skipped or test-not-observed.
Tests cover a skipped and a missing eligible test.
The spec wording and code agree.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/cem/verify/hunkrevert.go:397-415 classifyRevert sets ran=true on any single pass and returns survived. Scenario: baseline has TestA and TestB passing; reverted run passes A but skips or omits B, still yielding survived, though the documented requirement is that all eligible tests pass.
title: hunk-revert reports survived when some eligible tests never pass

acceptanceCriteria: Classification stops after two matches and checks cancellation.
An adversarial repeated-byte case completes within a stated time bound.
Where an exact count is reported (SpanOccurrences) a linear algorithm or a documented cap is used.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/cem/verify/verify.go:461-480 countOverlapping loops bytes.Index and advances one byte per match with no ctx check; interop/cem01-go/cem.go:924 stops after two matches. Scenario: a 1 MiB repeated-byte citation in a changed 2 MiB repeated-byte blob gives about a million overlapping matches each comparing the large needle.
title: native evidence-drift countOverlapping is quadratic and uncancellable; portable verifier stops at two matches

acceptanceCriteria: Field boundaries are scanned once and reused across credential-name checks.
An adversarial scaling test shows near-linear time for repeated credential words.
Screening results are unchanged on existing tests.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence read: internal/secretscreen/prefilter.go:182-200 scan: for each stem occurrence it walks the remaining field bytes (suffix loop) then advances rest by one byte. Scenario: a long 'tokentokentoken...' string without a delimiter makes each occurrence scan the rest of the field, O(n^2) before regex matching.
title: secretscreen prefilter afterCredentialName rescans the field suffix per occurrence (quadratic)

acceptanceCriteria: An unchanged test function that references a changed test function (same package) forces the whole-package reason naming both.
Regression test in cmd/corvint covers the wrapper-test case.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: internal/liveverify/affected/golang/testfunctions.go:41-48 puts Test/Example/Fuzz names only in Tests (not Others); cmd/corvint/test_slices.go:109-110 builds `declared` from file.Others only, and :113-117 checks unchanged-file Uses against `declared`. Scenario: unchanged TestWrapper calls edited TestCommon; TestCommon is not in declared, so only TestCommon enters -run and the wrapper is skipped.
title: test slicing (Go): a changed test function called by an unchanged test function is sliced alone

acceptanceCriteria: The sectioned freshness probe verifies every section (as the pack probe does).
Test corrupts a body section and asserts --if-stale reports stale and rebuilds.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: internal/contextindex/snapshot.go:775-779 probes the sectioned file with loadCompact; snapshot_sectioned.go:83-85 maps loadCompact to {sectionIdentity}, so body sections are never read. Scenario: corrupt the sectioned body while header/identity/gob stay intact; full reads reject it but --if-stale reports fresh and never repairs.
title: index --if-stale: sectioned snapshot probe checks only the identity section

acceptanceCriteria: A changed test file whose import set differs from base (or has a blank/dot import) yields a whole-package slice with a stated reason.
Regression test removes a blank import and asserts the package stays whole.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: testfunctions.go:36-71 handles only FuncDecl and TypeSpec/ValueSpec; ImportSpec never sets SideEffect. cmd/corvint/test_slices.go:102-107 and testBaseSideEffect (:150-175) reuse the same parser, so import changes against base are not compared. Scenario: remove a blank import (DB driver registration) from a_test.go containing TestA; unchanged TestDB now fails but only TestA runs.
title: test slicing (Go): import additions/removals in a changed test file do not force whole-package

acceptanceCriteria: Semicolon-separated import statements yield an edge for every statement.
A test with `import a; import b` is selected when b.py changes.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: python.go:250-262 scans only lines starting with `import `/`from `; parseImportLine (python.go:355-368) cuts each clause at ';' so the second statement is never parsed. Scenario: test_combined.py has `import a; import b`; editing b.py excludes test_combined.py with no frontier flag.
title: affected python: scanImports drops imports after a semicolon (import a; import b)

acceptanceCriteria: Resolving pkg.sub.mod adds edges to every existing ancestor __init__.py unit.
Test: editing pkg/__init__.py selects a test that imports only pkg.sub.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: python.go:166-189 resolve and :192-206 resolveRef return the single longest matching module; no ancestor package initializer edges are added. Scenario: change pkg/__init__.py side effects; a direct `import pkg` test is selected while tests importing pkg.sub (which also run the initializer) are excluded.
title: affected python: importing pkg.sub does not add an edge to ancestor pkg/__init__.py

acceptanceCriteria: An alias claimed by two files records all owners or sets a widening frontier flag; no silent first-wins.
Test with lib/core.py and src/core.py asserts the ambiguity is surfaced and consumers are selected.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: python.go:100-104 `if _, taken := moduleNames[name]; !taken` keeps the first owner of an alias; moduleAliases (:382-392) registers source-root-relative names. Scenario: lib/core.py and src/core.py with PYTHONPATH=src; `import core` binds to lib/core.py, so editing src/core.py omits real consumers.
title: affected python: source-root alias collisions silently keep the first file

acceptanceCriteria: Default execution witness runs with -count=1 (or records cached results explicitly as cached with original binding).
Test: a cached package result cannot yield an executed-pass receipt.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: internal/gotestrun/run.go:126-129 default command is `go test -json` with no -count=1; parseEvents (run.go:~183-205) reads only Action/Package/Test and never records cached output; internal/witness/evidence_go.go:34 binds the document to the current repository observation. Scenario: a cached pass replays as fresh execution evidence after an external service fails.
title: test-run: go test witness runs without -count=1 and discards (cached) results

acceptanceCriteria: Mapped access in pack and sectioned readers (including worker goroutines) converts a mapping fault into a refused-snapshot error.
Test truncates a mapped file mid-read and asserts an error, not a crash.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: internal/contextindex/pack_reader.go:287-296 verifyBlock hashes mapped s.data and verifyAll (:331-345) does so in worker goroutines; snapshot_sectioned.go:526-531 reads sections in a goroutine; debug.SetPanicOnFault/recover exists only at snapshot_decode.go:58-60. Scenario: another process truncates the opened mapped snapshot; the fault terminates the process instead of a cache miss.
title: contextindex: pack and sectioned mapped reads are not guarded against SIGBUS on truncation

acceptanceCriteria: ReadFile refuses a FIFO without blocking (O_NONBLOCK open then fstat, or lstat first).
Test with a writerless FIFO returns an error within a bounded time.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c. Evidence: internal/corpusindex/index.go:126-133 calls os.Open(path) before f.Stat().Mode().IsRegular(); cmd/corvint-corpus-http/main.go:44 calls it with no context. Scenario: --index pointing at a FIFO with no writer blocks startup indefinitely.
title: corpusindex.ReadFile: os.Open on a FIFO blocks before the regular-file check

acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic two-writer test (writer A paused between segment publish and head switch, writer B enters the lease precheck) leaves A's segment and receipts intact and A's seal completes.
Seal settlement runs only while the writer lock is held; unlocked guards observe the marker and report it without deleting anything.
Interrupted-seal recovery (JSG-V0-008) still finishes or undoes a genuinely abandoned seal under the lock.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:618 calls writerGuards with no writer lock; guards.go:77 calls settleSegmentSeal(repo) from it; segment_seal.go:355-364 on head==PriorHead removes the published segment and manifest; segment_seal.go:~179-185 later switches head and drops the original receipts. Scenario: writer A publishes a segment before switching head; writer B's unlocked precheck sees A's live seal marker as interrupted and deletes the segment; A then switches the unchanged head and drops the originals, so both copies are lost.
title: corvint-tasks: unlocked writerGuards settles an active segment seal and can delete both journal copies

acceptanceCriteria: With an ALL barrier present, gate run refuses before spawning the gate program (test asserts the program never starts).
A gate run with a role the lease operation rejects refuses before spawning.
The post-execution recheck is retained for changes that land while the gate ran.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/tasks/store/lease_gate.go:70-90 (GateRun calls reusableRun/runGate with no barrier or role check first); lease_recovery.go:170-173 probeLeaseRecovery returns (false, nil) when writerGuards refuses, so an ALL barrier is swallowed before the run (guards.go:110 is the refusal only reached later in Lease). Scenario: an ALL pause barrier is present, or gate run is invoked with a role the lease operation would refuse (role part not traced to its refusal site); the gate program runs and its external side effects happen, then Lease rejects the record. Barrier part confirmed; role part unverified.
title: corvint-tasks gate run executes the gate command before barrier and role admission

acceptanceCriteria: A hanging git status during the gate observation is terminated when the run context ends or a bounded timeout elapses (test with core.fsmonitor set to a hanging script).
Git observation output is capped and the descendants are cleaned up.
Executable Git config (core.fsmonitor and similar) is disabled for these observations.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/tasks/store/release.go:216-224 gitOutput uses exec.Command(...).Output() with no context and no output cap; lease_gate.go:~400 worktreeTree runs git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all through it on the gate path. Scenario: the repository sets core.fsmonitor to a hanging program (the sanitized env removes global and system config but not repository config); the git status never returns, the gate timeout and SIGTERM cancel only the unused context, and the output is buffered without bound.
title: corvint-tasks gate: pre/post-gate git observation ignores the gate timeout and cancellation and is unbounded

acceptanceCriteria: Two agents with different PATH resolving a bare argv[0] to different executables do not share a reusable PASS (test).
Either the resolved executable path and digest join the reuse key, or a PATH-dependent reusable gate without an explicitly bound search environment is rejected at policy admission.
Documented in the governing Tasks gate spec (TCD-V0-158 area).
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/tasks/store/lease_gate.go:~573-590 gateEnvironmentKey/environmentOf digest only the names declared in def.Env (with values for reusable gates); lease_gate.go:609 uses exec.Command(argv[0],...), which resolves a bare name through the parent process PATH before cmd.Env is applied. Scenario: a reusable gate has argv [verify] and env []; agent A's PATH resolves a passing verify, agent B's PATH resolves a failing one, the environment digest is identical, and A's PASS is reused for B.
title: corvint-tasks reusable gate reuse key omits the PATH that selects the gate executable

acceptanceCriteria: A test cancels the context after stop and before activation; the old service is restarted under a separate bounded cleanup context and the outcome is RESUMED_OLD.
A restart failure is retained in the ServiceOutcome evidence rather than dropped.
Drain-failure restart uses the same cleanup context.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/update/update.go:~484-492 the deferred restore calls svc.start(ctx, ...) with the operation context; procgroup/process.go:303-306 Run returns process-cancelled without spawning when ctx.Err() is set; service.go:~274 drain failure path likewise restarts with the same ctx. Scenario: SIGTERM or the operation deadline arrives after the service was stopped but before activation (including during drain); the old binary stays installed but the previously running service is never restarted.
title: corvint update: cancelled context after service stop prevents restarting the old service

acceptanceCriteria: After stop, quiesce polls status under a deadline and proceeds only on an observed STOPPED; RUNNING at the deadline or UNKNOWN refuses with the destination unchanged and the old service resumed.
The same observation applies before automatic rollback.
A test with a delayed-shutdown control program covers both paths.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/update/service.go:245-251 sets State=STOPPED as soon as the stop verb exits 0 (service.ok checks only exit status, service.go:130-135); no status poll follows. rollbackPermitted (service.go:~292) makes the same assumption. Scenario: a control program's stop returns zero after requesting asynchronous shutdown while status still reports running; the updater marks STOPPED and swaps the binary under a running service, and automatic rollback does the same.
title: corvint update: service shutdown completion is never verified before activation or rollback

acceptanceCriteria: apply refuses a Tasks release whose build-verification.json archiveSha256 differs from the downloaded archive digest, before execution or activation.
check and apply share one validation of the declaration.
Regression test with a mismatched archiveSha256.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/update/update.go:1385-1397 compares only profile, target, build, component and qualification between the internal MANIFEST.json and build-verification.json; update.go:828-834 (the check path) additionally requires m.ArchiveSha256 == the SHA256SUMS archive digest, and no other apply-path site references the report archiveSha256 (grep). Scenario: a report that matches the internal fields but names a different archiveSha256 is rejected by check but accepted by apply, which installs with qualification evidence that does not describe the archive.
title: corvint update apply: Tasks qualification report archiveSha256 is not compared with the downloaded archive

acceptanceCriteria: A release carrying two platform archives passes check and apply on each platform (platform-specific report filenames or a validated per-target collection).
RunTasksArchive publishes the report in the agreed form.
Test covers a release containing both archives and the existing single-platform layout.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c in /private/tmp/batch-1028. Evidence read: internal/companionrelease/tasks_archive.go:15-26 TasksArchiveReport holds one Target, Component and ArchiveSHA256; internal/update/update.go:824-834 and :1317 require the single asset build-verification.json whose Target equals the running platform. Scenario: a release carrying Darwin arm64 and Linux amd64 archives can publish only one report, so whichever platform it does not describe fails qualification in check and apply.
title: Tasks release metadata: one build-verification.json cannot qualify both supported archive platforms

acceptanceCriteria: A Go file with thousands of names in one multiline declaration retains O(B) declaration text, not O(S*B), asserted by an allocation test.
SymbolExtents output and knowHowSymbolTable digests are byte-identical for existing fixtures.
The non-Go next-symbol lookup is O(S log S) or better.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c (batch-1028). Evidence: internal/contextindex/symbol_extent.go:115 emits one symbolExtent per declared name of a spec; symbol_extent.go:86 joins lines[start-1:end] into Content per symbol; internal/tasks/store/know_how_symbols.go:34 hashes each Content. Non-Go path at symbol_extent.go:67 does an all-pairs next-symbol search. Scenario: a multiline var block with S names inside the 1 MiB input cap retains S copies of the B-byte declaration.
title: contextindex SymbolExtents retains the full declaration text once per declared name (Theta(S*B) memory)

acceptanceCriteria: symbolContextText stops joining/decoding at 2000 runes; allocation per symbol is bounded by the cap, asserted by a test on an adversarial single-line file.
Output of symbolContextText is unchanged for existing inputs (parity test).
Identical windows are computed once.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c (batch-1028). Evidence: internal/contextindex/symbolwindows.go:210 symbolContextText strings.Joins the full window then calls truncateRunes; internal/contextindex/parse.go:844 counts every rune then allocates a full []rune before slicing to 2000. buildSymbolWindows (symbolwindows.go:234) does this per symbol. Scenario: thousands of Go names on one line beside a long comment, file under 1,000,000 bytes: each symbol joins and decodes the same large window, Theta(S*B) work and allocation.
title: contextindex symbol windows join and rune-decode the whole window before applying the 2000-rune cap

acceptanceCriteria: A file larger than the ceiling is refused with invalid-obligations-input after reading at most ceiling+1 bytes.
A FIFO or other non-regular file is refused without blocking.
Inputs at or under the ceiling behave as before.
body: Found by the 2026-10-28 astra 1.0 audit; verified at a5cb1804c (batch-1028). Evidence: cmd/corvint/obligations.go:155 readObligationsInput calls os.ReadFile(path) and only then compares len(data) with obligationsInputCeiling. Scenario: --cem or --impact names a multi-gigabyte file (OOM before refusal) or a FIFO (blocks forever); the advertised bounded invalid-obligations-input error is never reached.
title: corvint obligations reads --cem/--impact fully (os.ReadFile) before enforcing its 4 MiB ceiling

acceptanceCriteria: Non-regular files are excluded from automatic discovery and refused at open.
A per-file and aggregate byte cap is enforced, with an explicit refusal naming the file.

body: Found by V1-3060 (macOS cmd/corvint timeout). Since V1-2691 (0d988848c) script/corvint-work-queue keeps its compiler cache at ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/corvint-work-queue-gocache-UID. workChildEnvironment (cmd/corvint/work_materialization.go:103) gives every run HOME=<run root>/home and no XDG_CACHE_HOME, so the cache is per-run and empty: every real `corvint work` capture compiles the whole producer closure from scratch. Before V1-2691 the cache was a shared /tmp/corvint-work-queue-gocache-UID. Evidence (darwin, 12-core): isolated leaf TestWorkFinalCheck.../CommandFailures/nonzero 7.5-7.8 s cold vs 3.85 s with a shared XDG_CACHE_HOME; WorkFinalCheck tops 139-151 s before vs 50-60 s after the V1-3060 test-only prelude fix. Test-side mitigation landed in V1-3060 for the final-check fixtures only; other fixtures that run the real script (work_observe, runner, corpus, adopt, materialization_unix, production_fixture) and the product path still compile cold. Expected: the run-private child environment carries a stable, owner-checked per-user cache root (XDG_CACHE_HOME from the operator or os.UserCacheDir), keeping the script's ownership/mode checks. Related: V1-2691 (OPEN, tmpfs cache), V1-2768 (COMPLETED, /tmp run roots).
title: corvint work captures compile the work-queue producer closure cold: the per-user Go cache sits under the run-private HOME since V1-2691

A narrowed lane PR therefore never qualifies for REUSE, and a grouped entry's tree (stacked on earlier entries) never equals its PR tree, so each queue entry would run the full 8-shard suite (~30 min, measured 30 min on #1957 before V1-3051). Expected: a merge_group entry selects with corvint affected over (queue base main .. entry head), admitted by the same narrowing verdict as PRs, with UNKNOWN falling back to FULL; and REUSE accepts a narrowed PR run when the entry tree equals the PR tree and the selection covers the same range. Related: V1-1102 (group size/capacity question), V1-2902, V1-2113, V1-2941.

acceptanceCriteria: A Linux test shows each scenario's peak_rss_bytes reflects only the measured command (a tiny child reports far less than the harness's own resident set)

body: Suspected defect (unverified root cause). On PR #1976, perf-budget run 40764955655 (uncontended, so judged) failed: index-cold-build, index-warm-build, context-query, lifecycle-hook, affected-go and affected-ts each report peak_rss_bytes=457867264 against ceilings of 256 MiB/128 MiB. The latest perf-budget run on main (40752800429, at c58127c72) records 458928128 in 65 samples but was contended, so it reported not-judged and passed. A byte-identical peak across unrelated commands, including a lifecycle hook, points at measurement, not product memory. Hypothesis: internal/perfbudget/rusage_unix.go reads ProcessState.SysUsage Maxrss, and Go's Linux os/exec starts children with clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK), so the child's high-water RSS can include the harness parent's resident set. perf-budget is not a required check, so merges are not blocked, but every uncontended Go PR run will fail.

body: Codex review (gpt-6.1-sol, 2026-10-28) of the V1-3078 relay (57afc1a2f), verified against source. (1) internal/perfbudget/measure.go:213: on an MCP initialize failure, s.fail never reads the relay report, so a target start error (e.g. /definitely/missing/corpus-mcp) is a scenario failure with exit 1 instead of *StartError with exit 2. (2) relay_linux.go:44/129: fd 3 is inherited without FD_CLOEXEC by the measured command and its descendants, and result() reads to EOF, so a detached child that survives the group sweep blocks the harness, and context cancellation cannot interrupt the read.
title: perf-budget relay: MCP start errors lose StartError classification, and an inherited report fd can block the harness on a detached descendant

internal/tasks/cli wall time on WSL is measured and either reduced or isolated into its own shard.
body: Observed 2026-10-29 on four per-lane PR branches (base 0a04f081337c46ea20159d88fc368c24555ae49c; claude/gh2004-2005, claude/v1-3090, claude/gh2010, claude/gh2006-2009). The focused selection from `corvint test --dry-run` (NARROWED 174-269 units) was run as one `go test -json -p 1 -timeout 30m -count=1 <pkgs>` through the lane heavy.sh WSL offload, whose remote wrapper applies `timeout ${TIMEOUT:-40m}`. All four runs exited 124: 127-142 packages passed, then internal/tasks/cli, which alone takes 1015-1146 s on WSL, was killed unfinished. Each needed a second 17-19 min run of tasks/cli alone. Slow packages seen: cmd/corvint 243-374 s, companionrelease 194 s, appmap 145 s. Expected: a focused selection finishes within the offload cap in one run, e.g. corvint test emits parallel package invocations (-p >1 or sharded invocations split by measured cost), or the offload sizes its timeout from the selection. Actual: serial -p 1 over ~140+ packages exceeds 40 min and the slowest package is killed.
title: Focused corvint test selections exceed the 40-minute heavy.sh remote cap: go test -p 1 serial run reaches internal/tasks/cli last and is killed (rc 124)

acceptanceCriteria: A push to main whose merge-queue run passed narrowed does not rerun all 8 shards in full; live evidence from two consecutive merges with run IDs and shard durations

Spec/requirement updated for the new push reuse rule
body: Observed 2026-10-29 with CORVINT_MQ_NARROWING on. #2015 merge-queue run 40892814639 narrowed (shards ~1 min); push of the identical commit 03df27fec (run 40894001942) ran all 8 shards FULL for 18-25 min. #2016 MQ 40894005317 narrowed to 185 units; push 618b95947 (run 40898318537) ran FULL. #2017 MQ ran FULL (stacked entry), so push 529fa9245 (run 40901066926) reused with ~35 s shards. This is the documented design in ci.yml header (AFP-V0-730..733: a narrowed entry records no tested tree), so MQ narrowing only moves the full run from the queue to the push; per-merge Go shard cost is unchanged. Expected: the push of a commit whose merge-queue run passed a trusted narrowed selection reuses that run (same tree, same selection), or narrows against the last main commit with a full tested-tree record; FULL stays the fallback. Related: V1-2902 (static jobs rerun), V1-1642, V1-2279.
title: CI: a narrowed merge-queue entry records no tested tree, so the main push of the same commit reruns all 8 Go shards in full

Its queue base 618b95947 was the previous queue entry (#2016), not yet on main. Any batch of two or more PRs in the queue therefore runs every entry after the first FULL. Expected: a stacked entry narrows to the trusted selection of main..entry head (union of the in-queue ranges under their PR MET verdicts), or to the range from the previous entry when that entry's record is trusted; FULL stays the fallback. Related: V1-3093 (PR base moved), V1-3064, V1-1102.
title: CI: a merge-queue entry stacked behind an unmerged entry falls back to FULL (queue base is not an ancestor of main)

acceptanceCriteria: release-gates.yml core-n1-replay rows pass on beamfall/corvint with no pre-1.0 tag in the repository, fetching the baseline from corvint-history pinned by OID
The lifecycle N-1 row qualifies against a published predecessor archive verified by SHA-256
The runbook documents the single-root baseline route

Historical acquisition is explicit and pinned by full tag/object or immutable archive identities; it uses disposable storage and leaves candidate Git refs/history unchanged. Existing local-tag mode still works.

Missing/mismatched identities, wrong outer digest, missing asset and failed acquisition refuse visibly. Both the outer published archive digest and internal checksum manifest are checked before predecessor execution; the same verified predecessor remains available to host-lifecycle qualification.

Retain focused acquisition/selector/lifecycle/workflow checks, both real Core baseline replays and a real Linux N-1 install lifecycle tied to the candidate. Independent review and native closeout retain unknowns; no release publication is authorized.
body:
Found minting 1.0.0-rc.3 (2026-10-30). After decision 0587 the new beamfall/corvint has one root commit and no tags. release-gates.yml runs make core-n1-replay CORE_N1_TAG=v1.0.0-rc.1 and v0.8.1, which git-archive a local tag, and the lifecycle predecessor selector needs a prior reachable v* tag (or previous_release_tag/oid naming a tag present in the repo). Pushing the old tags would import the whole pre-1.0 history and defeat the single root. Expected: the gates fetch frozen baselines from beamfall/corvint-history (tag + pinned OID) or from the published release archives, and the lifecycle N-1 can use a published predecessor archive by digest. Actual: those rows cannot pass; rc.3 runs them locally from a scratch clone with tags fetched from the archive.

First-batch audit 2026-10-29: preserve existing local-tag replay and add explicit historical-source acquisition outside candidate Git state. Update the CCF acquisition guidance only; unchanged replay/skip semantics, no new interoperability claim. Lifecycle qualification must consume the published predecessor archive, not substitute a locally source-built predecessor.

Observed 2026-10-30: scheduled Release gates run https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/actions/runs/41059652620 on main 21fea70cb failed exactly here. linux-core step "Fetch the previous release's published linux/amd64 archive (N-1)": `previous-release: no reachable previous release; supply an explicit tag and direct OID`. core-n1-replay-v1.0.0-rc.1 / -v0.8.1: `fatal: not a valid object name: v1.0.0-rc.1` / `v0.8.1`. beamfall/corvint has 0 releases and 0 tags. New blocker for the planned route: beamfall/corvint-history is NOT reachable from account Russe11 (GitHub API 404, `git ls-remote git@github.com:beamfall/corvint-history.git` "Repository not found", absent from `gh repo list beamfall --archived` and repo search). The tags v0.8.1, v1.0.0-rc.1, archive/final still exist in the local ~/projects/corvint checkout. Acquisition from corvint-history is impossible until its location/visibility is confirmed.
title: release-gates.yml cannot pass on the single-root repository: core-n1-replay and the lifecycle predecessor need v* tags that live only in corvint-history

The same widen succeeded immediately after a brief `unpause`, then the barrier was restored.

Expected (suspected defect, not confirmed): an admission barrier stops new admissions; widening the scope of an already admitted live attempt should either be allowed, or the refusal should say that widen counts as admission and name the documented recovery. Separately, claim with --scope rejects paths outside declared effects and tells the agent to claim then widen, so under a paused queue the documented route always needs a second unpause window.

Sequence: enrolled session e30b6dca… finished strict binding at a8eeab8d3 (reports acked, coordination pinned local-outcome.json digest deddbfbb…); then the AC2 one-command `make dogfood-closeout BASE=21fea70c… LANE=1` ran finish-lane (inputs-check, prepare, bind [commit skipped: unchanged map], dogfood-record, check, seal) and sealed to 40776cede. Its dogfood-record step rewrote <gitdir>/corvint/local-outcome.json at 08:30 (new trace 061181c9…, task 'Dogfood change from 21fea70cb1fe to HEAD', digest 624579f1…), and the matching dogfood-report.json references the new digest. Sealed `corvint dogfood finish --session-key e30b…` then refuses `sealed-evidence-drift`: internal/localcompletion/sealed.go validateSealed requires saved.Coordination to be byte-current, and post-seal there is no supported re-coordination (coordinate() would recreate the shared map). Diagnosis: all prior bindings (archived map R100 digest equal), reports and ocm-status are current; only local-outcome.json differs.

Expected: the documented one-command lane closeout and an enrolled local completion compose. Either finish-lane leaves an enrolled session's pinned coordination untouched/coordinates through the enrollment, or sealed continuation accepts a replacement outcome only when it is bound to the exact evidence target/base/admitted set and referenced by a complete dogfood-report at that target, re-pinning it and forcing a new report-set review. Fail closed otherwise.
title: Local completion: the one-command closeout (dogfood-closeout/finish-lane) re-records local-outcome.json before sealing, so the enrolled sealed finish always refuses sealed-evidence-drift

The committed .corvint/changes maps bind to commits from the pre-1.0 history, which the single-root repository (decision 0587) does not contain, and beamfall/corvint-history is currently unreachable (404 over the API). Expected: the corpus binding proof passes in the single-root repo without weakening the CI=true no-skip rule (V1-1334). Actual: the full gate fails. acceptanceCriteria: A JS literal using each JS-only escape (\x, \u{}, \0, \v, backtick, line continuation) is decoded or classified as sensitive, with a test per escape
A trailing-backslash literal fails closed
body: Found 2026-10-30 by the independent security review of the V1-3179 boundary lane (batch claude/batch-1030a, head d92b0a2a5). internal/jstestprovider/sensitive_input_grammar.go:157-180 decodes a JS string literal with JSON rules. JavaScript-only escapes (\x20, \u{..}, \0, \v, escaped backtick, line continuation) or a trailing backslash fail the whole decode, and the classifier then compares the raw text. Inference (not run): 'custom\x20entry' still evades the 'custom entry' match. CodeQL alert 31's case is fixed; this class is not. Older than the lane. Expected: decode the full JS escape grammar, or fail closed (treat undecodable literals as sensitive). Severity Low.
title: jstestprovider: JavaScript-only string escapes make the sensitive-input JSON decode fail, so the classifier compares undecoded text

acceptanceCriteria: Budget accounting uses the escaped byte length; a control-character path test proves the budget holds
body: Found 2026-10-30 by the V1-3179 security review. internal/mcp/corpusbridge/corpusbridge.go:686: `row` adds the raw len(path), but the structured row carries the JSON-escaped path. A path of control characters (up to 1024 bytes, about 6 KB escaped) is under-counted in that half of the budget. Budget accuracy only, not injection. Expected: count the encoded bytes, as the V1-3179 fix already does for the cost via writeJSON. Severity Low.
title: corpusbridge: the row budget counts raw len(path) while the structured row holds the JSON-escaped path

acceptanceCriteria: A manual `make core-n1-replay` on a tree whose only previous release is a prerelease tag replays against that tag, or reports FIRST_RELEASE, matching script/core-n1-source.sh.
A script test covers the prerelease-only case.
body:
CORE_N1_TAG defaults via `git describe --exclude '*-*'`, which skips every prerelease tag. After v1.0.0-rc.3 ships (the first release; owner 2026-10-30) a manual `make core-n1-replay` resolves CORE_N1_TAG to empty and must name the tag. The Release gates workflow passes the tag through script/core-n1-source.sh, so CI is unaffected.

Expected: the default selects the previous published release as core-n1-source.sh does (or delegates to it), including prereleases.
Actual: empty default.

Reported by the V1-3177 lane (wsl-lanes, branch claude/lane-n1-first-release-w1, head 306e0a81c, base b469ab710), 2026-10-30.
title: Makefile CORE_N1_TAG default excludes prerelease tags, so a manual make core-n1-replay resolves to empty once rc.3 is the only release

title: dogfood propose-citations refuses map-unavailable until dogfood change has run, forcing an extra dogfood-change in lanes that commit first

body:
The V1-3177 lane's dogfood-check WARNed tier-below-anchored on 14 hunks, 7 reported unanchorable. New files such as script/core-n1-source.sh have no BASE line, so if the WARN becomes a touched-anchored refusal those hunks can only pass with a runner receipt. Related: V1-3130, V1-2360.

Question: what anchor (self-anchor in the HEAD blob, test receipt, or explicit exemption) should a new file's hunks reach before the gate tightens?

Reported by the V1-3177 lane (wsl-lanes, branch claude/lane-n1-first-release-w1, head 306e0a81c, base b469ab710), 2026-10-30.
title: dogfood-check tier-below-anchored: hunks in newly added files have no BASE line to anchor, so a touched-anchored gate would refuse them without a runner receipt

acceptanceCriteria: A local check fails at d92b0a2a5 naming tools/compat-trial and internal/archivepath, and passes at de68fce5f.
The check runs in batch-precheck on darwin without Landlock (e.g. go list -deps closure against declared scopes for packages that compile repository source).
A test covers adding an out-of-scope import.
body:
PR #5 (batch claude/batch-1030a, head d92b0a2a5) passed `make batch-precheck` on the Mac, then failed CI go-product-shard 0 and 7. V1-3179 made tools/compat-trial/snapshot.go import the new internal/archivepath, and both tools/compat-trial and tools/compat-trial/build-fixtures build that tree from source under the Landlock test-confine wrapper (AFP-V0-023). .corvint/test-read-scopes.json did not grant internal/archivepath/, so the build got `open .../internal/archivepath: permission denied`. Reproduced on wsl-lanes with .github/testconfine and fixed in de68fce5f. `make test-read-scopes-check` passes before and after, because it only scans test-file literals and not the import closure of packages that compile source.

Expected: a local check (test-read-scopes-check or batch-precheck) fails when a scoped package that builds repository source gains a transitive import outside its scope.
Actual: only the Linux CI shard finds it, which costs a full 30-40 min CI round.
title: test-read-scopes-check misses a new transitive import in scoped source-building packages; Landlock denial only surfaces in CI shards

acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-finish/dogfood-closeout refuses before binding when migrate-traces reports stranded_revisions or ignored change.ocm files predate BASE, naming the exact recovery commands

body: Observed 2026-10-30 (lane claude/lane-misc-w2-43ff6c, worktree v1-3060-macos-cmd-corvint-870b46, base b469ab710): the worktree directory was reused from an earlier lane. Ignored .corvint/change.ocm.001.json/.002.json (2026-10-28) and the worktree-local trace store under .git/worktrees/<name>/corvint named commit 337bdce6b (not an ancestor of HEAD). make dogfood-closeout bound successfully, then rebind failed with coordination-time-query: unsupported-query-trace-state and local-outcome: record-failed (local trace store contains unreachable revision). Recovery needed moving the stale ocm files aside and corvint migrate-traces --dry-run then --apply --plan-digest D. Expected: dogfood-change/dogfood-finish detects at start that the local trace store or ignored ocm files predate the current branch (stranded_revisions non-empty) and either names the exact recovery commands in its refusal or retires them safely, before any bind. The current refusal says to restore the commit or run migrate-traces but never says a reused worktree path is the cause. Related: V1-3034 (migrate-traces limit).
title: Reused worktree path inherits a stale worktree-local trace store and ignored .corvint/change.ocm.NNN.json, so dogfood-closeout fails at rebind with unsupported-query-trace-state / record-failed

acceptanceCriteria: The documented lane test recipe (AGENTS.md / docs/DOGFOOD.md or lane charter) fails the step when heavy.sh refuses, even when piped.

Reported in lane closeout notes of batch claude/batch-1030a (base b469ab710), 2026-10-30; exact transcript output was not retained.
title: A heavy.sh refusal is hidden when lanes pipe its output through tail before git commit

acceptanceCriteria: Adding a code to the cemcode registry requires no edit in internal/observations, or a local generator/check reports the drift before push.

PR #7 (V1-3168, lane claude/lane-citation-replace-w1) added the CEM code `hunk-digest-mismatch`. internal/observations keeps its own list `admittedDogfoodErrorCodes`, so `TestDogfoodReasonAdmitsEveryRegisteredCEMCode` failed in CI shard 1 (run 41070773409) with observation-prohibited-content. acceptanceCriteria: Running a corvint built from an older commit inside the Corvint repository with newer cmd/internal changes reports a stale-binary degradation in JSON and text output.
dogfood-change/closeout record or refuse that degradation (test).

The WSL affected-w2 lane found that `~/.local/bin/corvint` on WSL was built on Oct 27. Its `corvint affected` output (90 units, analyzerhtmlcss/jstestprovider hits) differed from a binary built from b469ab710 (49 units), and both V1-3201 and V1-3207 had been filed from the stale output. title: Stale corvint binary on lane hosts silently produces selections and evidence different from current source

acceptanceCriteria: The three tests pass under umask 0002 and 022.
A test still proves a group-writable cache directory is refused.

acceptanceCriteria: On a host with heavy.env, both entry points share one slot set (test).

body:
scripts-w2 lane report 2026-10-30: on wsl-lanes, ~/lanes/heavy.sh uses mkdir slots in ~/bench/rt/.slots (4) shared with rt.sh, while the repo's script/heavy.sh uses flock locks in /tmp/corvint-heavy-1000 (8 slots). Expected: one semaphore per host; script/heavy.sh reads the host's configured slot dir/count.

acceptanceCriteria: A remote lane can run ticket show/search for current tickets without a writable journal.

acceptanceCriteria: A session lane cannot start dogfood-closeout/seal in the background without a refusal naming the foreground recipe.

Expected: the lane brief and/or guard refuse background closeout steps in session lanes too, or closeout stays under the foreground 600 s budget by splitting.

acceptanceCriteria: The refusal names file, line and the literal.

acceptanceCriteria: DOGFOOD.md lists every admitted relation, checked against code.
